## Summary

Adds a self-contained `deploy/` recipe for hosting gbrain as a 24/7 remote MCP server reachable from any AI client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code remote, Perplexity, etc.). Until now, gbrain ran where your terminal ran — close the laptop, the brain went to sleep. This PR lands the recipe so anyone can self-host on Fly.io + Supabase Pro + a private GitHub notes repo in about 30 minutes.

**Architecture:**
```
AI client → https://your-app.fly.dev/mcp     (Bearer auth)
              → http-wrapper.ts (Bun, port 8080)
                  → operation handlers → Supabase Postgres (pgvector)
              ‖
              autopilot loop: git pull /notes → sync → extract → embed
```

One Fly machine runs both the HTTP wrapper and the autopilot sync loop. If either dies, Fly restarts the machine.

**What's in `deploy/`:**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `http-wrapper.ts` | Streamable HTTP MCP server, bearer-token gated. All 30 operation handlers exposed. Stateless transport per request (safe to scale horizontally). |
| `start.sh` | Container entrypoint: decode SSH deploy key, clone/pull notes, spawn wrapper + autopilot, exit if either dies. |
| `Dockerfile` | `oven/bun:1.1-debian` + git + ssh-client. Frozen-lockfile install (no silent dep drift). |
| `fly.toml` | `lhr` region, shared-cpu-1x 512MB, always-on, `/healthz` check. |
| `README.md` | Full runbook: Supabase Pro setup with pooler URL format, GitHub deploy key generation, Fly app create + secrets import, schema init, bearer token rotation, troubleshooting matrix, ~\$28/mo cost breakdown. |

**Security posture:**
- Bearer tokens SHA-256 hashed at rest in `access_tokens` (same scheme as `gbrain auth`).
- All MCP callers run with `OperationContext.remote = true` — already tightens `file_upload` sandboxing in `src/core/operations.ts`.
- DNS rebinding protection disabled (irrelevant for server-to-server bearer flow). README warns against browser exposure.

**Verified live.** Recipe was used to deploy `pareen-brain.fly.dev` end-to-end before this PR was opened. `tools/list` returns 30 tools, `get_stats` works, Claude Desktop connects via custom-connector with bearer token.

title: fix(doctor): skip pgvector + jsonb_integrity cleanly on PGLite (75→100 health)
body:
## Problem

On PGLite engines, two doctor checks call `db.getConnection()` (the `postgres.js` singleton) which isn't used by PGLite — the call throws, lands in the `catch` block, and surfaces as `Could not check ...` WARN status. That penalizes health score on every install that hasn't migrated to Supabase/Postgres.

Sample output on PGLite before this PR (after applying current master):

```
[WARN] pgvector: Could not check pgvector extension
[WARN] jsonb_integrity: Could not check JSONB integrity
Health score: 90/100. All checks OK (some warnings).
```

(`rls` was fixed separately on master since this PR's original revision; this update narrows scope to the two checks still warning.)

## Fix

Match the existing pattern used by `rls` / `rls_event_trigger` / `queue_health` / `markdown_body_completeness`: when `engine.kind === 'pglite'`, emit `status: 'ok'` with a `Skipped (PGLite — …)` message explaining why the check doesn't apply. The Postgres path is byte-identical (only wrapped in an outer `if` branch).

After this PR on the same PGLite install:

```
[OK] pgvector: Skipped (PGLite — pgvector built-in, pg_extension not introspectable)
[OK] jsonb_integrity: Skipped (PGLite — v0.12.0 double-encoding bug only affected real Postgres)
Health score: 100/100. All checks passed.
```

## Rationale per check

1. **pgvector** — PGLite ships pgvector bundled via `@electric-sql/pglite/vector` (WASM); there's no `pg_extension` row to verify and the extension introspection isn't exposed in the same form.
2. **jsonb_integrity** — The v0.12.0 `${JSON.stringify(x)}::jsonb` double-encode bug was explicitly noted in the v0.12.2 CHANGELOG as only affecting real Postgres (`postgres.js` stringified a second time; PGLite did not). The v0.12.2 migration already no-ops on PGLite for the same reason. Doctor should too.

## Test

- **PGLite**: health score 75 → 100 (or 90 → 100 with current master where `rls` already passes), two WARNs become OK.
- **Postgres**: no behavior change. The `engine.kind === 'pglite'` guard only branches into the new skip path; the original code paths (`try { … pg_extension … }` and the `jsonb_typeof` scan) are unchanged for Postgres.

## Notes

This rebases #226's original three-check fix onto current master and drops the `rls` portion (since master fixed it differently in the meantime). Keeps the score penalty reserved for genuinely actionable warnings, so `gbrain doctor` remains a reliable signal on both engine types.

title: fix(sync): skip 'git pull' silently when repo has no upstream
body:
## Problem

When a GBrain sync repo is a local-only git repo (committed locally, never pushed to a remote — e.g. an Obsidian vault used as the single source of truth for one user), every sync emits this multi-line warning:

```
There is no tracking information for the current branch.
Please specify which branch you want to merge with.
...
    git branch --set-upstream-to=<remote>/<branch> main

Warning: git pull failed: Command failed: git -C /path/to/vault pull --ff-only
There is no tracking informatio
```

Under `gbrain autopilot`, this fires on every cycle (default 5 min). The autopilot.err log fills up with the same message, drowning out any real warnings that would actually need attention.

The repo isn't broken — it's just local. `gbrain sync` still works, because the function catches the thrown error. But the noise is unconditional.

## Fix

Before `git pull --ff-only`, probe for an upstream tracking branch with:

```
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}
```

If that errors, the current branch has no upstream configured — skip pull silently. Otherwise, run pull and preserve the existing error handling for non-fast-forward / diverged remotes.

## Behavior

| Setup | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Local-only repo, no remote | WARN every sync | Silent (skip pull) |
| Remote configured, clean pull | OK | OK (unchanged) |
| Remote configured, diverged | "remote diverged" WARN | "remote diverged" WARN (unchanged) |
| Remote configured, other git error | generic pull WARN | generic pull WARN (unchanged) |

## Motivation

Using a local git-tracked Obsidian vault (or any personal notes repo) as a GBrain sync source is a common pattern — it gives you commit history and lint triggers without needing a hosted remote. Punishing that setup with log spam discourages it.

Local-only git repos should remain first-class: they still sync, they just don't get pulled.

## Test

- Local-only repo: `gbrain sync` and autopilot no longer print the tracking warning; other output unchanged.
- Repo with remote, clean: git pull still runs.
- Repo with remote, diverged: existing warning still fires.

title: feat(access): pluggable tier-based content filter primitive
body:
## Summary

Adds a small, opt-in primitive for tier-based content visibility on top of the existing tag system. Nothing in this diff touches any existing read path. Everything is new files plus a one-line `yaml` dependency, gated behind an explicit `loadAccessConfig(...)` call that no existing code invokes. Think of it as landing the library — wiring it into `operations.ts` would be a separate PR if and when it's wanted.

The shape is deliberately minimal:

- **`config/access-tiers.example.yaml`** — shipped as `.example` so adopters bring their own tier taxonomy. Copy, edit, point the loader at the copy.
- **`src/core/access-config.ts`** — `loadAccessConfig(basePath, overlayPath?)`, `validateAccessConfig`, `clearAccessConfigCache`. Validates structure, supports an optional overlay that can only *extend* allow/block lists of existing tiers (overlays cannot introduce new tiers — the base file is authoritative). Overlay file missing = silently return base, so deployments that don't need one just work.
- **`src/core/access-filter.ts`** — two pure functions: `isVisibleToTier(page, tierName, config): boolean` and `filterByTier<T extends PageForFilter>(pages, tierName, config): T[]`. No I/O, generic over T so callers keep their rich page types.
- **`docs/guides/access-control.md`** — usage guide matching the existing docs/guides/ format.

## Why it's useful

Multi-tenant / partner-sharing deployments. The pattern that motivated this: an agent that serves both its owner and scoped readers (family members, partners, product collaborators) from the same brain, using the existing tag system as the visibility primitive. `OperationContext.remote` already distinguishes trusted vs untrusted callers; this adds a *who* dimension on top of the *how-trusted* dimension.

Even for single-user brains, the `none` (wildcard-block) tier is a useful deny-all fallback during testing or staging.

## Design

**Tags are the substrate.** No new schema, no new columns. Pages already carry tags in gbrain; this primitive just groups tags into allow/block rules per tier.

**Block-wins semantics.** A page is visible to a tier iff (a) the tier exists, (b) no page tag matches a block tag, and (c) either `allow_tags` is empty (default-allow, like the `full` tier) or at least one page tag matches an allow tag. Blocks always win. Unknown tier → deny (safety default). Rule ordering is documented in `access-filter.ts`, the YAML header, and the docs/guides entry; tests cover every branch.

**YAML-configured, not code-configured.** Tier definitions live in YAML so ops/admin can edit them without a rebuild. `loadAccessConfig` caches by `basePath||overlayPath` so different overlays don't collide.

**Overlay for site-specific bindings.** Deployments that need concrete scope bindings (partner names, private project scopes) can keep those in a separate YAML that isn't committed to the shared config and still share the public base. Overlay is additive-only and deduped; the loader accepts the overlay path as an optional second argument (or via env var in the calling code).

**Pure functions.** `filterByTier` is generic over T so callers can pass rich page objects (search results, `list_pages` output, etc.) and get them back typed. Zero I/O in the filter path — all YAML I/O happens once in `loadAccessConfig` with caching.

## Opt-in only

This PR does **not** wire the filter into `operations.ts`, `list_pages`, `search`, or any other read path. Users who want access control wire it themselves, or a follow-up PR can add a small adapter in `operations.ts` that reads `OperationContext.remote` + an optional `tier` and calls `filterByTier` before returning results. Kept out of this PR so the primitive can be audited in isolation.

## Test coverage

27 new unit tests, all passing:

- `test/access-config.test.ts` (12 tests): YAML parse, validator error cases, base config load, overlay merge (additive, deduped), overlay error cases (unknown tier, missing file), cache key separation.
- `test/access-filter.test.ts` (15 tests): every semantic branch — default-allow, explicit-allow, narrow-scope, deny-all (wildcard), unknown tier, blocks-win-over-allows, generic type preservation on `filterByTier<T>`.

Test fixtures use generic tag/tier names (`team`, `scoped`, `partner-a`, etc.) so the suite reads as documentation of the primitive rather than a description of any one deployment.

Full suite: `bun test` → 1407 pass / 168 skip / 0 fail.

## Commit list

```
docs(access):     add usage guide
chore(access):    ship config as .example + genericize test fixtures for upstream
docs(access):     clarify block-wins semantics in YAML header comment
refactor(access): support private overlay for tier-to-scope bindings
feat(access):     add filterByTier + isVisibleToTier pure functions
feat(access):     add YAML loader + validator for access-tiers config
feat(access):     add access-tiers.yaml with 4 tiers
```

Each commit is independently reviewable.

## Scope explicitly excluded

- **No `operations.ts` wiring.** Follow-up PR if this lands. Kept out so this PR stays small and the primitive can be audited in isolation.
- **No UI / CLI command to inspect a tier.** `gbrain access show-tier <name>` would be a nice addition but belongs with the wiring work.
- **No migration for existing pages.** Pages without access-relevant tags remain visible only to default-allow tiers, which is the intended default-deny-for-scoped behavior.

## Background

Developed on my fork (knee5/gbrain#1, merged) before proposing upstream, so the shape has had some wear. The Phase-2-style wiring work is also implemented on the fork and will serve as the template for a follow-up PR if this one lands.

## Test plan

- ✓ `bun test` passes (1407 pass / 168 skip / 0 fail locally on the branch tip)
- ✓ `bun test test/access-config.test.ts test/access-filter.test.ts` passes standalone (27/27)
- ✓ `package.json` only adds `yaml@^2.8.3` as a runtime dep; `bun.lock` updated accordingly
- ✓ No existing read paths touched — confirmed by grepping for imports of `access-filter` / `access-config` across the diff (no hits outside the new test files)
- ✓ Commit messages and test fixtures are generic — no owner-specific identifiers

title: v0.13.0 migration shells out via process.execPath, breaks on bun-linked installs
body:
## Summary

`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_0.ts` re-invokes the gbrain CLI as a subprocess using `process.execPath` to run two phases (A: `gbrain init --migrate-only`, B: `gbrain extract links --source db --include-frontmatter`). On installs done via the blessed `git clone + bun install + bun link` path, `process.execPath` resolves to the bun binary (not gbrain), so Phase A runs `bun init` (bun's project-scaffolding command) and Phase B fails with `Script not found 'extract'`. Migration aborts before v11 SQL applies.

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04 LXC on Proxmox 9.1.7
- **Node:** via Bun 1.x (no separate Node install)
- **Bun:** 1.x global
- **gbrain:** 0.13.1 (fresh pull from main during upgrade from v0.12.3)
- **Install path:** `bun link` from clone (per `INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`)
- **Storage:** Postgres 17 on a separate LXC (not PGLite)

## Repro

~~~bash
cd ~/gbrain
git pull && bun install && bun link     # blessed install
gbrain apply-migrations --yes
# Phase A runs: `/home/user/.bun/bin/bun init --migrate-only`
#   -> bun interprets this as `bun init` (new-project scaffolder)
# Phase B then: `bun extract links --source db --include-frontmatter`
#   -> error: Script not found 'extract'
~~~

`process.execPath` resolves to bun's binary because bun is the executing runtime, not Node. The check "is this path our CLI entrypoint?" isn't made.

## Workaround

Apply v11 migration SQL directly via psql (adds `link_source` / `origin_page_id` / `origin_field` columns to `links`, swaps the unique constraint), then run Phase B manually:

~~~bash
psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -1 -f v11.sql
gbrain extract links --source db --include-frontmatter
# Mark complete in ~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl
~~~

## Proposed fix

Two options in order of robustness:

1. **Don't shell out.** Import the functions Phase A/B already call, and invoke them in-process. Migrations are same-package code; spawning a subprocess to run your own module is the anti-pattern.
2. **If shelling out is required** (e.g., for process-isolation during long migrations), resolve the binary deterministically — `require.resolve('gbrain/bin/gbrain')` or the `bin` field of the package manifest — not `process.execPath`.

Happy to send a PR for option 1 if you'd like.

title: v0.13.1 schema bootstrap fails on pre-v11 brains: CREATE INDEX idx_links_source on column not yet added
body:
Hit this on PGLite upgrading from schema v10 → v13. Reproduces 100% on any brain initialized before v0.13.

## Symptom

```
$ gbrain init
Setting up local brain with PGLite (no server needed)...
column "link_source" does not exist
```

## Cause

`PGLiteEngine.initSchema()` runs `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` BEFORE `runMigrations(this)`. The schema SQL contains:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
  ...
  link_source    TEXT    CHECK (link_source IS NULL OR link_source IN ('markdown', 'frontmatter', 'manual')),
  ...
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source);
```

On a fresh DB, the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` creates the table with `link_source`. Fine.

On a pre-v0.13 DB (schema v10), the table already exists WITHOUT `link_source`, so `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` no-ops, leaving the table without the column. Then `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source)` fails because the column doesn't exist yet.

The migration v11 (`links_provenance_columns`) that adds the column runs AFTER `initSchema()`, but `initSchema()` already crashed.

## Reproduce

1. Initialize a brain on gbrain ≤ 0.12.x
2. Upgrade to gbrain 0.13.0 or 0.13.1
3. `gbrain init` → fails

## Fix options

(a) Move `CREATE INDEX idx_links_source` (and any other v0.13-column-dependent indexes) out of `pglite-schema.ts` and into the migration v11 SQL.

(b) Run migrations BEFORE `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` (re-orderable since the schema SQL is `IF NOT EXISTS` everywhere).

(c) Wrap the index creation in a `DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (column) THEN CREATE INDEX ...; END IF; END $$;` guard.

I think (a) is cleanest — schema.ts should reflect the *fresh-install* shape; column additions and their indexes should live in their migration.

## Workaround

Wipe `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` and re-import. Loses any in-DB-only state but rebuilds from the source vault.

## Env

- macOS 26.4.1 arm64
- gbrain 0.13.1 (latest master, commit 5fd9cd2)
- PGLite engine
- Node 25.6.0, Bun 1.3.12

title: v0.13.0 migration orchestrator shells out to 'bun run extract' which expects an npm script that doesn't exist in user vaults
body:
Hit this on PGLite, gbrain 0.13.1.

## Symptom

```
$ gbrain apply-migrations --yes
=== Applying migration v0.13.0: Frontmatter becomes a graph ===
=== v0.13.0 — Frontmatter relationship indexing ===
note: package.json already exists, configuring existing project
error: Script not found "extract"
Migration v0.13.0 finished as PARTIAL.
```

## Cause

`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_0.ts` Phase B (backfill) shells out via `execSync` to invoke an `extract` npm script, expecting either:

- `bun run extract` to be defined in the user's vault `package.json`, OR
- the GBRAIN binary's own `package.json` to provide it

Neither is true. My vault is a markdown directory with no `package.json`. After the migration ran, my vault now has a generated `package.json` from `bun init` ("note: package.json already exists, configuring existing project") which suggests the orchestrator created one when it didn't find one.

The actual working CLI is `gbrain extract links --source db` (and `gbrain extract timeline --source db`). Subcommand `extract` exists at `src/commands/extract.ts`. The orchestrator should call the GBRAIN binary directly:

```js
execSync(`${GBRAIN} extract links --source db --include-frontmatter`, { ... })
execSync(`${GBRAIN} extract timeline --source db`, { ... })
```

…analogous to how Phase A correctly uses `${GBRAIN} init --migrate-only`.

## Side effect

The orchestrator 'configuring existing project' message suggests it's touching the vault's `package.json` and possibly `bun.lock` / `tsconfig.json` (which appeared in my Atlas vault directory after running). Worth confirming — leaving stray files in user vaults is unfortunate.

## Reproduce

1. gbrain ≤ 0.12.x brain that gets upgraded to 0.13.x
2. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`
3. v0.13.0 migration partial-fails on Phase B

## Workaround

Run the extract commands manually after init:

```
gbrain extract links --source db
gbrain extract timeline --source db
```

Then either record completion in `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl` manually or live with the partial-status warning.

## Env

- macOS 26.4.1 arm64
- gbrain 0.13.1 (master commit 5fd9cd2)
- PGLite engine
- Vault = plain markdown directory, no app code

Filed alongside #239 (schema bootstrap bug).

title: v0.13.0 migration: process.execPath in v0_13_0.ts resolves to bun binary on source installs, making orchestrator fake-succeed
body:
## Summary

`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_0.ts:43` does `const GBRAIN = process.execPath;`. On installs via `git clone + bun link` (the path in `INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`), `process.execPath` is the Bun runtime, not the gbrain CLI. Every `${GBRAIN} …` sub-invocation in the orchestrator misbehaves.

**Repro:** PGLite→Postgres install, upgrade v0.12.2 → v0.13.0+, `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` ends with `error: Script not found "extract"` and `PARTIAL`.

**What's happening:** `${GBRAIN} init --migrate-only` becomes `bun init --migrate-only` → Bun reads it as `bun init` in an existing-project dir → `note: package.json already exists, configuring existing project` → exits 0. Orchestrator records schema phase as "complete" though nothing actually ran. `${GBRAIN} extract links --source db --include-frontmatter` becomes `bun extract …` → Bun looks up `extract` as a package.json script → not found → exit 1 → PARTIAL.

Net effect: migrations 11-13 and the frontmatter backfill never run. `minion_jobs.quiet_hours` stays missing, `gbrain jobs smoke` errors.

**Manual workaround:** apply migration 11's ALTER TABLEs via psql, run `gbrain init --migrate-only`, then `gbrain extract links --source db --include-frontmatter`.

**Suggested fix:** use the existing `resolveGbrainCliPath()` from `src/commands/autopilot.ts`. Grep for other `process.execPath` callsites that assume compiled binary.

**Environment:** git clone + `bun link`, macOS 25.4.0, Bun 1.3.11, Postgres 17.9 + pgvector 0.8.2, upgrade v0.12.2 → v0.13.1.

title: initSchema() runs SCHEMA_SQL before migrations; schema-embedded forward-references v0.13 columns, breaking all upgrades
body:
## Summary

`src/core/schema-embedded.ts` has v0.13 columns (`link_source`, `origin_page_id`, `origin_field`) and their indexes/unique-constraints baked into the fresh-install schema. `postgres-engine.ts:initSchema()` runs `SCHEMA_SQL` before `runMigrations()`. On any upgrade from pre-v0.13, init aborts before migrations 11-13 fire.

**Repro:** existing v0.12.x install, `git pull && bun install && gbrain init --migrate-only` → `column "link_source" does not exist`.

**What's happening:** for upgrades, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (…)` is a no-op (table exists without new columns). Then `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source)` errors. Throws out of SCHEMA_SQL. `runMigrations()` never runs.

**Manual workaround:** pre-apply migration 11's ALTER TABLEs via psql, then `init --migrate-only`.

**Suggested fixes** (any one):

1. **Reorder `initSchema`**: migrations first, then SCHEMA_SQL. Cleanest; protects against same class of bug in future v0.14+ releases.
2. Drop forward-referencing DDL from `schema-embedded.ts`; let migrations own column + index creation (fresh installs run migration chain anyway since migrations are idempotent).
3. Gate v0.13 index/constraint creation in SCHEMA_SQL behind `DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (…) THEN … END IF; END $$` column-existence checks.

**Environment:** same repro env as the sibling issue — macOS 25.4.0, Bun 1.3.11, Postgres 17.9 + pgvector 0.8.2, upgrade v0.12.2 → v0.13.1 via `bun link`.

- **Bug**: Upgrades from pre-v0.13 fail because `initSchema()` runs `SCHEMA_SQL` before `runMigrations()`. When `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source)` executes, the `link_source` column doesn't exist yet (added by migration 11).

- **Scope**: Both `PostgresEngine.initSchema()` and `PGliteEngine.initSchema()` had the same bug — both are fixed.
- **Behavior**:
  - Fresh installs: migrations are no-ops, `SCHEMA_SQL` creates everything
  - Upgrades: migrations add new columns first, `SCHEMA_SQL`'s `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` succeeds

title: Fix command injection in large-file transcription
body:
## Summary
This PR removes shell-string command construction from the large-file transcription path.

## What changed
- replaced `execSync("mktemp -d")` with `execFileSync("mktemp", ["-d"])`
- replaced shell-built `ffprobe` invocation with argument-array `execFileSync`
- replaced shell-built `ffmpeg` invocation with argument-array `execFileSync`
- replaced `execSync("rm -rf ...")` cleanup with `rmSync(..., { recursive: true, force: true })`

## Why
The previous implementation interpolated `audioPath` directly into shell command strings in `src/core/transcription.ts`. If a path contained quotes or shell metacharacters, that created a command-injection risk in the large-file segmentation flow.

Using argument arrays keeps the behavior the same while removing shell parsing from the path handling.

## Scope
This is intentionally narrow. It only hardens the large-file transcription path and does not change provider behavior, chunking logic, or output format.

Thanks for taking a look.

title: Bug: PGLite stale lock directory after SIGKILL/OOM prevents reconnection
body:
## Description

When a GBrain process is killed via SIGKILL or crashes due to OOM, the advisory lock directory (`brain.pglite/.gbrain-lock/`) is not cleaned up. Subsequent GBrain processes cannot acquire the lock and fail to start, requiring manual `rm -rf` of the lock directory.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gbrain embed --stale` (which can take minutes and use significant memory)
2. Kill the process with SIGKILL (or let OOM killer terminate it)
3. Attempt to run any GBrain CLI command: `gbrain stats`
4. Observe error: "Could not acquire PGLite lock" (times out after 30s)

## Expected Behavior

GBrain should detect and clean up stale locks automatically so a new process can start after an unclean shutdown.

## Actual Behavior

The lock detection code in `pglite-lock.ts` checks if the locking process is still alive (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) and has a `STALE_THRESHOLD_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` (5-minute) timeout. However:

1. After a SIGKILL, the PID may no longer exist, and the stale lock detection *should* clean it up — but the `rmSync(lockDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` can race with a concurrent lock attempt
2. In practice, the 30-second acquire timeout (`timeoutMs`) may expire before the 5-minute stale threshold is reached if the user runs a quick CLI command shortly after the crash
3. The lock directory itself (`mkdir`-based) can remain in a state where removal fails silently, requiring manual intervention

The most common failure mode: process A is killed → lock dir remains → process B tries to start → PID in lock file is dead → stale detection fires → `rmSync` appears to succeed → but `mkdirSync(lockDir, { recursive: false })` fails because the directory still exists (race or permissions) → process B loops and times out.

## Manual Fix

```bash
rm -rf ~/.gbrain/brain.pglite/.gbrain-lock/
```

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Lower the stale threshold** when the PID is confirmed dead: if `isProcessAlive(pid)` returns false, remove the lock immediately (don't wait for `STALE_THRESHOLD_MS`)
2. **Add a `--force-unlock` CLI flag**: allow `gbrain stats --force-unlock` to clear the lock explicitly
3. **Use a lock file (not directory)**: use `fs.open(lockPath, "wx")` which is also atomic but easier to clean up — a regular file is simpler to remove than a directory with contents
4. **Add PID validation on acquisition**: before waiting, immediately clear dead-PID locks rather than looping

## Environment

- GBrain branch: `zero-openai-stack`
- OS: macOS / Linux
- Engine: PGLite (WASM)
- Machine: i7-8700B, 32GB RAM (OOM happens when `GBRAIN_EMBED_CONCURRENCY` > 2)

title: sync: exclude build artifact dirs (node_modules, vendor, dist, build, etc) from isSyncable
body:
## Problem
`isSyncable` in `src/core/sync.ts` only filters by extension, hidden dirs, `.raw/`, a few meta filenames, and `ops/`. It does **not** filter build artifact directories. If a user commits a brain repo that ever had `node_modules/` (or any transitive dep) tracked in git (e.g. pre-gitignore), every `.md` changelog/readme inside gets ingested as a concept page.

In my case this polluted my brain with 8300+ tracked files and 43+ pages from `integrations/node_modules/**` (npm package changelogs). Hybrid search returned npm docs instead of my notes. Embedding 575 junk chunks would have cost real OpenAI spend.

## Fix
Add path-segment check in `isSyncable` for common build artifact dir names at any depth: `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `target`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `.svelte-kit`, `.turbo`, `.cache`, `coverage`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`.

Most are already covered by the leading-dot hidden-dir rule, but listing explicitly is robust and makes intent clear for the non-dot ones (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `target`).

## Tests
New `describe('rejects build artifact directories')` block covers node_modules at root + nested, vendor, dist, build, out, target, __pycache__, venv, and verifies legit nested `.md` still syncs. All 35 tests pass.

## Notes
- Pre-existing pages from previous ingests are not auto-deleted; this only prevents *new* pollution. Users can manually delete stale slugs.
- I considered making the list configurable (e.g. brain-level setting) but the hardcoded set covers 99% and keeps the function pure.

title: fix: pre-0.11 upgrade path — schema index order + v0.13.0 bun/TS detection
body:
## Summary

Two chicken-and-egg bugs that block `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain` upgrades from ancient versions. Both observed migrating a real 0.5.0 brain (2,748 pages, production) to 0.14.1 on 2026-04-20.

### Bug 1 — `idx_links_source` tries to index a column that doesn't exist yet

`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links` is a no-op on any pre-v0.11 `links` table (pre-v0.11 had no `link_source` / `origin_page_id` / `origin_field` columns). The very next line — `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source)` — then errors out with `column "link_source" does not exist`.

`src/core/migrate.ts` v11 would add those columns via `ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS link_source …`, but the v0.11.0 migration orchestrator runs `gbrain init --migrate-only` (which runs `schema.sql`) as Phase A — **before** v11 gets a chance. So on any sufficiently old brain, Phase A fails with:

```
column "link_source" does not exist
Phase A (schema) failed: Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only. Aborting; re-run after fixing.
Migration v0.11.0 reported status=failed.
```

**Fix:** add idempotent `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` inline in `schema.sql`, between the `from`/`to` index creates and the `source`/`origin` index creates. No-op on fresh brains (the `CREATE TABLE` above already has the columns). Self-heals old brains so the `CREATE INDEX` lines below succeed.

### Bug 2 — `const GBRAIN = process.execPath` resolves to `bun`, not to gbrain

For `bun install -g github:…` installs, `~/.bun/bin/gbrain` is a symlink to `src/cli.ts` and `bun` is the running process. So `process.execPath` is `/root/.bun/bin/bun`. The v0.13.0 Phase B backfill then runs:

```bash
execSync(`${GBRAIN} extract links --source db --include-frontmatter`)
# → bun extract links --source db --include-frontmatter
```

…which bun interprets as "run script `extract` from package.json" and fails with `error: Script not found "extract"`. Migration reports PARTIAL, `gbrain doctor` flips `minions_migration: fail`, and `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` loops forever because every re-run hits the same wall.

**Fix:** detect bun-TS mode via `process.argv[1].endsWith('.ts')` and build the command as `${execPath} ${scriptPath}` in that case (→ `bun /path/to/cli.ts extract links …`, which bun executes correctly). In `bun build --compile` mode the check is false and `GBRAIN` stays `process.execPath` as originally intended. Original concern about PATH shadowing is preserved in the comment — this just adds a branch for the bun-TS install path.

## Test plan
- [ ] Fresh Postgres install: `gbrain init` → `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` — no regression (defensive ALTERs are no-ops on a fresh `links` table).
- [ ] Pre-v0.11 Postgres brain (simulate by dropping `link_source` / `origin_page_id` / `origin_field`): `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` — Phase A now passes, v0.13.0 Phase B now passes, migration completes.
- [ ] Compiled binary mode: `bun build --compile … && ./bin/gbrain apply-migrations --yes` — `GBRAIN` resolves to the compiled binary (argv[1] is not `.ts`), no regression in compiled path.

## Workaround the downstream user applied
Until this merges, the manual patch is:
```sql
ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS link_source TEXT;
ALTER TABLE links ADD CONSTRAINT links_link_source_check CHECK (link_source IS NULL OR link_source IN ('markdown','frontmatter','manual'));
ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS origin_page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS origin_field TEXT;
```
plus `sed -i 's/const GBRAIN = process.execPath;/const GBRAIN = "gbrain";/' src/commands/migrations/v0_13_0.ts` in the installed copy (which a reinstall re-breaks).

title: Fix: Bug: PGLite stale lock directory after SIGKILL/OOM prevents reconnection
body:
The fix optimizes stale lock detection by switching to an 'optimistic' acquisition pattern. Instead of checking for a stale lock directory before attempting to create one (which is prone to race conditions), the code now attempts `mkdirSync` immediately. If it fails with `EEXIST`, it immediately checks if the PID stored in the lock file is still alive. If the process is dead, it removes the lock directory and retries the acquisition without waiting for the 5-minute timeout. Additionally, it handles cases where the directory exists but the lock file is missing (indicating a crash during the acquisition process) by checking the directory's modification time. This ensures that SIGKILLed or OOMed processes do not block subsequent runs of GBrain.

Test: 1. Manually create a directory named `brain.pglite/.gbrain-lock/` in your data path.
2. Create a file named `lock` inside it with JSON content: `{"pid": 999999, "acquired_at": 1700000000000, "command": "test"}` (ensure 999999 is not a running PID).
3. Run `gbrain stats`. The command should successfully detect the stale PID, remove the directory, and start within a few milliseconds, rather than timing out after 30 seconds.

title: Fix: Bug: Bun single-file executable () breaks PGLite data directory resolution
body:
The bug occurs because Bun's single-file executables (`bun build --compile`) use a virtual filesystem (`$bunfs://`) for bundled resources. When PGLite (a WASM-based Postgres engine) is initialized with a relative path in this environment, it incorrectly tries to resolve the data directory within the virtual filesystem, which the WASM module cannot access. The fix detects if the application is running from a Bun binary (checking `import.meta.url` for the `bunfs:` protocol) and resolves relative PGLite data paths against the real OS current working directory (`process.cwd()`) instead. It also ensures that if no database URL is provided, it defaults to a stable directory in the user's home folder (`~/.gbrain/data`) using `os.homedir()`, which is guaranteed to be outside the virtual filesystem.

Test: 1. Build GBrain as a binary: `bun build --compile src/cli.ts --outfile gbrain`. 2. Run `./gbrain init` without any flags (this should default to a PGLite connection). 3. Verify the command succeeds and creates a data directory at `~/.gbrain/data`. 4. Run `./gbrain stats` and ensure the database opens correctly without throwing a 'Cannot access $bunfs' error. 5. Test with an explicit relative path: `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL=pglite://./local-db ./gbrain stats` and verify a real directory named `local-db` is created in the current working folder.

title: Fix: Bug: MCP get_timeline returns empty [] while CLI timeline works
body:
The issue is caused by the MCP server maintaining a long-lived PGLite connection. PGLite (especially in WASM/Node environments) can sometimes hold state in memory or buffers that isn't automatically synchronized when an external process (like the CLI) modifies the underlying database files. In the CLI, a new engine instance is typically created for each command, ensuring it sees fresh data. In the MCP server, the same engine instance is reused. By calling `await engine.prepare()` before executing each tool handler, we ensure that the engine refreshes its connection state and acknowledges any changes made to the database since the last call. This fix is applied to both the main MCP server handler and the `handleToolCall` helper used by the `gbrain call` command.

Test: 1. Start the gbrain MCP server (e.g., using an MCP client like Hermes).
2. Using the CLI in a separate terminal, add timeline entries to a page: `gbrain put test-page '<!-- timeline --> entry at 12:00'`. 
3. Verify the CLI sees the entry: `gbrain timeline test-page` (should show the entry).
4. Invoke the `get_timeline` tool via the MCP server for 'test-page'.
5. Confirm the MCP server returns the entry instead of an empty array [].

title: fix(put_page): clear error for uppercase slugs before DB call (#200)
body:
## Summary

`gbrain put "SomeSlug/test"` rejects uppercase slugs with a descriptive error instead of letting them fail with a misleading "Page not found" message once they reach the engine layer.

## Fix

Added an early validation in `put_page` handler that checks for uppercase characters and throws a clear `invalid_params` error:

```
Error [invalid_params]: Slug must be lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and forward slugs only. Got: "SomeSlug/test"
```

This matches the existing `validatePageSlug()` function's behavior, but fires before any DB operations.

## Why

The previous flow was:
1. `gbrain put SomeSlug/test` → `importFromContent(engine, "SomeSlug/test", ...)`
2. `engine.putPage("SomeSlug/test", ...)` calls `validateSlug()` → lowercases to `"some slug/test"`
3. INSERT with lowercased slug succeeds
4. **But** somewhere the page wasn't found later, causing "Page not found" with the original uppercase slug

Users debugging the misleading error chased paths like "Did the page get deleted?", "Is my slug typo'd?", "Is the database disconnected?" before realizing the actual cause was uppercase characters.

Closes #200.

title: v0.14.x initSchema fails with "column link_source does not exist" when upgrading a PGLite brain from schema v10 (v0.12.x)
body:
Hi Garry — running into a chicken-and-egg in `initSchema` when upgrading an existing PGLite brain from v0.12.3 (schema version 10) to master (v0.14.2).

## Reproducer

Starting from a brain at schema version 10 (the v0.12.3 baseline — `drop_timeline_search_trigger`):

```bash
cd ~/gbrain-tmp
git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/master  # lands on v0.14.2
bun install && bun link
gbrain apply-migrations --yes
```

Output:

```
=== Applying migration v0.12.2: JSONB double-encode repair ===
column "link_source" does not exist
Migration v0.12.2 reported status=failed.
```

Same error from `gbrain init --migrate-only` directly.

## Root cause

`src/core/pglite-schema.ts:82-83` has:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_source ON links(link_source);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_links_origin ON links(origin_page_id);
```

These reference columns that are added by **migration v11 (`links_provenance_columns`)** in `src/core/migrate.ts:288`. But `PGLiteEngine.initSchema()` runs `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` **before** it calls `runMigrations`:

```ts
// src/core/pglite-engine.ts:63-70
async initSchema(): Promise<void> {
  await this.db.exec(PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL);   // <-- fails here on existing v10 brain
  const { applied } = await runMigrations(this);
  ...
}
```

`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` guards by **index name**, not column existence — so for a brain already carrying `idx_links_from` / `idx_links_to` / etc. from its v10 state, the new `idx_links_source` doesn't exist yet and must be created, but the column it references also doesn't exist yet. SQL fails, `runMigrations` never runs, v11 never applies, user is stuck.

A fresh brain (`gbrain init --pglite`) isn't affected — the CREATE TABLE defines `link_source` in the initial schema, then the indexes create cleanly. Only users who went through the v0.11/v0.12 wave hit this.

## What I tried

1. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` — fails at Phase A
2. `gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry 0.12.2` → re-run — same failure
3. `gbrain init --migrate-only` directly — same failure
4. I considered a direct invocation of `runMigrations(engine)` to apply v11 first and then retry `initSchema`, but that bypasses the sanctioned CLI path and felt wrong to apply to a production brain.

Reverted cleanly to v0.12.3 and held.

## Possible fixes

- **Swap order in `initSchema`:** call `runMigrations` first, then exec `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL`. Upstream migrations add columns → subsequent `CREATE INDEX` succeeds. A fresh brain would first create the tables (no rows, nothing to migrate), then re-exec schema SQL as a no-op.
- **Or guard the index creation:** wrap the two problematic `CREATE INDEX` statements with a conditional that checks `information_schema.columns` for the target column, similar to the PG15+ guard in `migrate.ts` v11.
- **Or add `ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ADD COLUMN`** for the three new columns in the schema SQL itself, ahead of the indexes — makes the SQL safely reentrant across schema generations.

## Environment

- gbrain source at `b5fa3d0` (v0.14.2)
- PGLite 0.4.4
- bun 1.3.12
- Linux ARM64 (NVIDIA DGX Spark)
- Brain: ~2,066 pages, schema version 10, PGLite (single-user)

Happy to test any fix branch. Thanks for shipping the v0.13 wave — the graph enrichment from frontmatter indexing is exciting, just need a clear path to get there from an existing brain.

title: security: cap pglite search queries at 8s to match postgres parity
body:
## Summary

`postgres-engine.ts` protects `searchKeyword` and `searchVector` with
`sql.begin` + `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '8s'` so an attacker-crafted
tsquery or similarity scan can't freeze a pooled connection. PGLite
auto-commits each `.query()` call, so `SET LOCAL` is a no-op there (the
code already notes this at `pglite-engine.ts:445-448`). The search paths
on PGLite were left with no equivalent protection.

Since `gbrain init` defaults to PGLite for brains under 1000 pages, most
users run on the engine that has no timeout. A pathological query hangs
the single-threaded WASM event loop and with it the MCP stdio session,
the `gbrain jobs work` daemon, and any in-process autopilot cycle.
The user has to kill the process to recover.

This PR closes the parity gap by wrapping both search queries in a
`queryWithTimeout` helper that races `db.query()` against an 8s timer.

## Root cause

`pglite-engine.ts` searchKeyword + searchVector call `this.db.query(...)`
directly. On a big corpus or a pathological input, those queries run
long enough to starve the event loop. Unlike Postgres (where
`statement_timeout` kicks in), there is no ceiling on PGLite.

Attack shapes:

1. `search(query=<pathological tsquery>)` — many ORs + rare tokens force
   extensive rank scoring.
2. `search(query=<common term>)` on a very large brain where the corpus
   itself is the pathology.
3. Vector search variants of either.

The MCP boundary is stdio today, so the practical threat model is an
agent-side prompt injection tricking its own Claude into issuing a bad
search, which then self-DoSes the user's gbrain process.

## Fix

New module-level helper in `src/core/pglite-engine.ts`:

```ts
const SEARCH_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;

async function queryWithTimeout<T>(
  db: PGlite,
  sql: string,
  params: unknown[],
  timeoutMs: number,
  label: string,
): Promise<{ rows: T[] }> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const timeoutPromise = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(
      () => reject(new Error(\`pglite \${label} query exceeded \${timeoutMs}ms\`)),
      timeoutMs,
    );
  });
  try {
    return (await Promise.race([
      db.query(sql, params),
      timeoutPromise,
    ])) as { rows: T[] };
  } finally {
    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}
```

Both `searchKeyword` and `searchVector` now go through
`queryWithTimeout(this.db, sql, params, SEARCH_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS, '<label>')`.
Return shape and downstream code (`rows.map(rowToSearchResult)`) are
unchanged.

## Known caveat (documented inline)

`Promise.race` frees the awaiting caller but does not actually cancel
the underlying WASM work. The query keeps running in the background
until it finishes naturally. This is a strict improvement over an
unbounded hang: the agent session, jobs daemon, and autopilot cycle
resume after 8s instead of blocking indefinitely. True cancellation
requires PGLite to expose a cancel token upstream (not present in
`@electric-sql/pglite@0.4.x`). Docstring points at that caveat for
future follow-up.

## Scope choice

Only the two paths that have the equivalent Postgres defense
(`searchKeyword`, `searchVector`) are wrapped, to keep this change
purely a parity fix. Other PGLite methods (`resolveSlugs`,
`findByTitleFuzzy`, `traverseGraph`) are also missing timeouts and
are reachable via MCP, but wrapping them is additional surface area
and belongs in a follow-up if the maintainer wants it. Happy to
extend in this PR on request.

## Test plan

New file: `test/pglite-search-timeout.test.ts`.

- [x] Source-level: `searchKeyword` + `searchVector` call
      `queryWithTimeout`, not raw `this.db.query` (grep against the
      compiled source body of each method).
- [x] Source-level: `SEARCH_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000` constant exists.
- [x] Functional: inject a fake `db` whose `.query()` never resolves.
      `engine.searchKeyword('ignored')` must reject with the documented
      \`pglite searchKeyword query exceeded ...\` message, within the 8s
      cap (test asserts < 8.5s; harness bails at 9s if nothing fires).
- [x] `bun test` — full suite: 1747 pass / 0 fail / 174 skip
      (E2E skipped without `DATABASE_URL`, per standard).

## Risk

- `Promise.race` + `setTimeout` is stdlib-level; no new runtime
  requirements.
- The helper's return type lines up with the existing destructure
  (`const { rows } = ...`). No behavior change on successful queries.
- Unsuccessful (timeout) path now surfaces a clear `Error` to the
  caller instead of hanging — that is the point. Callers of `search`
  currently have no error handling for hang cases; they will now see
  a deterministic rejection they can log and retry.
- `pg_trgm.similarity_threshold` and similar GUC-inlined thresholds
  elsewhere are intentionally left alone; this PR only reaches what
  Postgres already treats as timed-search territory.

## Notes

Flagged as part of an ongoing security audit; no public disclosure of
PoC details until this lands. Happy to rebase on request.

title: fix(db): disable prepared statements on Supabase pooler to prevent cross-connection statement-cache errors
body:
## Problem

Users on the Supabase transaction pooler (port `:6543` or `pooler.supabase.com`) hit sporadic `prepared statement "abc123" does not exist` errors under sustained gbrain load (sync, extract, embed, autopilot).

**Root cause:** pgbouncer in transaction mode recycles underlying Postgres connections between client queries. postgres.js caches prepared statements by name and reuses them — but the next query may land on a different underlying connection where that prepared-statement name is unknown. Postgres raises the error and the query fails.

Repro (bare postgres.js against Supabase pooler):
```
sql = postgres("postgresql://...@aws-1-us-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres", { max: 10 });
// Run enough parameterized queries to exhaust the pool and start reusing connections
// → "prepared statement 's1' does not exist"
```

## Fix

Detect pooler URLs by regex on the connection string and pass `prepare: false` to postgres.js. Direct connections (port 5432, non-pooler hosts) keep `prepare: true` and retain plan-caching perf.

```ts
const isPooler = /pooler\.supabase\.com|:6543/i.test(url);
sql = postgres(url, {
  // ...
  prepare: !isPooler,
});
```

Applied at the two `postgres(url, ...)` call sites:
- [src/core/db.ts](src/core/db.ts) `connect()` — the module-global singleton used by the CLI
- [src/core/postgres-engine.ts](src/core/postgres-engine.ts) `connect()` with `config.poolSize` — the instance pool used by worker isolation

## Empirical

Carried as a local patch for ~6 months against Supabase pooler on a ~31k-page brain. Without it, sustained load surfaces \"prepared statement\" errors within minutes. With it, zero occurrences across sync/extract/embed/autopilot over that span.

## Impact

- **Pooler users**: no more cross-connection statement-cache errors. Slight per-query overhead from skipping the prepared-statement optimization (negligible in practice).
- **Direct-Postgres users**: zero change — `isPooler` evaluates false, `prepare` stays true.
- **Schema**: no change.
- **Tests**: none added. The fix is a config flag driven by URL inspection; the behavior is entirely in postgres.js.

## Notes

- Alternative: `prepare: false` unconditionally. Rejected because direct-Postgres users would pay the unnecessary perf cost.
- Alternative: env-var opt-in (e.g. `GBRAIN_POOLER_MODE=1`). Rejected because pooler URLs are self-identifying — no reason to require manual configuration.
- The regex matches both the Supabase-specific pooler hostname AND the generic `:6543` transaction-mode port, covering self-hosted pgbouncer too.

If the regex approach feels too magical, happy to rework as an explicit `{pooler: true}` config option instead.

title: bun install postinstall spawns parallel `apply-migrations` that races any in-flight migration run
body:
## Summary

The `postinstall` script in `package.json` runs `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive` unconditionally. If `bun install` is invoked while another `apply-migrations` is already running (e.g. by the user, by a prior `gbrain upgrade`, or by a migration orchestrator that shells out), the two racing processes contend on DB advisory locks and one gets SIGTERM'd mid-orchestrator. The killed orchestrator leaves its migration marked `partial` in `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl`, and recovery requires `--force-retry`.

## Observed today

Upgrading 0.12.0 → 0.13.1 on a 31k-page brain:

1. User ran `bun install` (after `git pull` to update source)
2. `bun install`'s postinstall fired `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive` (PID_A)
3. PID_A reached v0.13.0 Phase A, which internally runs `gbrain init --migrate-only`
4. `gbrain init --migrate-only` acquires `pg_advisory_lock(42)` in `initSchema()`
5. Meanwhile, the user also ran `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` in the foreground to monitor progress (PID_B)
6. PID_B hit the same advisory lock, waited, and one process (the longer-sleeping one) was killed with `SIGTERM`
7. Ledger captured: `Migration v0.13.0 reported status=failed. error: postinstall script from "gbrain" terminated by SIGTERM (Polite quit request)`

## Why the current postinstall is fragile

The postinstall hook is well-intentioned — auto-apply migrations when the binary updates. But:

- It has no lock/mutex with any other `apply-migrations` instance
- It has no way to detect "an apply-migrations is already running in this repo"
- It silently swallows failures (`2>/dev/null || true`), so users don't see the SIGTERM unless they read the ledger
- It races with `gbrain upgrade`'s own post-upgrade chain, which also calls `runApplyMigrations([--yes, --non-interactive])`

## Possible fixes

In decreasing order of preference:

1. **Advisory-lock gate in apply-migrations entrypoint.** `SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(<different_id>)` at the top of the runner; if it fails, exit with a clear "another apply-migrations is running, skipping" message. Non-blocking. Cheapest fix.

2. **Process/file-based lock.** PID file at `~/.gbrain/migrations/.apply-migrations.lock`. Stale-lock detection via PID liveness check.

3. **Drop the postinstall entirely.** Move migration application to an explicit `gbrain upgrade` command. `bun install` alone shouldn't mutate user state. Users who want auto-apply can add a shell alias.

4. **Skip postinstall if invoked from within another gbrain process.** Inspect `process.env.GBRAIN_*` or parent PID for a signature. Fragile but minimal.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Terminal 1
gbrain apply-migrations --yes

# Terminal 2 (while Terminal 1 is mid-orchestrator)
cd ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/gbrain
bun install  # fires postinstall → apply-migrations → races Terminal 1
```

Both will contend on the DB advisory lock and one will get SIGTERM'd.

## Workaround

Kill the orphan `bash -c "gbrain --version ... apply-migrations --non-interactive"` process before re-running. After today's apply-migrations fiasco, `gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry <version>` is also needed to clear the wedge.

Happy to take a swing at option 1 (advisory lock in the runner) if it's wanted.

title: Windows compat: readFileSync fd 0 + Bun-aware migration recurse
body:
## Summary

Two Windows-only breakages hit on a fresh v0.13/v0.14 install running gbrain via Bun. Both are small, zero-risk portability fixes.

### 1. `readFileSync('/dev/stdin')` → `readFileSync(0)`

`src/cli.ts:130` and `src/commands/report.ts:44` read piped stdin via the `/dev/stdin` pseudo-file, which doesn't exist on Windows. Any `gbrain put-page < file.md` or `gbrain report <<<"..."` invocation throws `ENOENT`.

`readFileSync(0)` passes the stdin file descriptor directly — works identically on Linux, macOS, and Windows under both Node and Bun. No behavior change on Unix.

### 2. `process.execPath` is `bun.exe` under Bun, not `gbrain`

`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_0.ts:44` stores `GBRAIN = process.execPath` and later shells out to it:

```ts
execSync(`${GBRAIN} extract links --source db ...`)
```

When gbrain runs via `bun run src/cli.ts`, `process.execPath` resolves to `bun.exe` (Windows) or `bun` (Unix), so the migration tries to run `bun extract` and fails with "command not found" — leaving the brain half-migrated.

Fix: detect Bun via the global `Bun` object and fall back to the `gbrain` command name. In the native-binary case (`bin/gbrain`) the original behavior is preserved — `Bun` is undefined, `process.execPath` points at the real binary. The original comment's concern about PATH shadowing only applies to the `gbrain upgrade` case with a native binary, which this branch doesn't touch.

## Test plan

- [x] `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive` — completes through v0.13.0 phase B
- [x] `gbrain doctor --fast` — no regressions

Happy to split into two PRs if you'd prefer; kept as one since they're both the same "portability" theme and each is a two-line change.

title: fix(migrations/v0.13.0): drop execPath subprocess, call extract in-process
body:
## Problem

`apply-migrations --yes` fails partway through v0.13.0 with:

```
=== Applying migration v0.13.0: Frontmatter becomes a graph ===
note: package.json already exists, configuring existing project
error: Script not found "extract"
Migration v0.13.0 finished as PARTIAL.
```

…and the same pattern on Phase C (`error: Script not found "call"`).

## Root cause

`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_0.ts` spawns recursive gbrain invocations via:

```ts
const GBRAIN = process.execPath;
execSync(`${GBRAIN} extract links --source db --include-frontmatter`, ...);
execSync(`${GBRAIN} call get_stats`, ...);
```

When gbrain is installed as a compiled binary, `process.execPath` is that binary — works fine. But when gbrain runs as `bun run src/cli.ts` (dev installs, `bun link`, or setups where the compiled binary has independent issues like PGLite WASM bundling), `process.execPath` is the **bun interpreter**. The spawned command becomes:

```
bun extract links --source db --include-frontmatter
```

…which bun interprets as a missing `package.json` script (`bun run <script-name>`), prints `error: Script not found "extract"`, and exits non-zero. Migration logs PARTIAL and wedges after 3 retries.

Discovered in a real upgrade path: v0.10.1 brain → rebase onto v0.14.2 master → `gbrain apply-migrations`.

## Fix

Call `extractLinksFromDB` and `engine.getStats()` directly in-process. No subprocess, no PATH/exec-lookup surface, no `process.execPath` assumption:

- `phaseBBackfill`: becomes `async`, loads config → creates engine → calls `extractLinksFromDB(engine, false, false, undefined, undefined, { includeFrontmatter: true })`.
- `phaseCVerify`: becomes `async`, queries `engine.getStats()` directly.
- Both wrap in `try/finally` to disconnect the engine.
- `extractLinksFromDB` changed from module-private → exported (minimal surface change).

Same behavior. Same idempotency (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING handles re-runs). No observable user-facing difference on working installs; fixes broken installs.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/migrate.test.ts` — 10 pass
- [x] Manual: reset v0.13.0 wedge, re-run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` → completes to `complete` status (previously stuck at `partial`)
- [x] Verified on real 80-page PGLite brain: `gbrain doctor` jumps from 50/100 (minions_migration FAIL) → 70/100 all-OK after this fix lands

title: added overlay
fix: resolve CLI via argv[1] + bun for migration re-invocation
body:
## Summary

`gbrain apply-migrations --yes` fails for bun-linked installs because migrations re-invoke the CLI via `process.execPath`, which resolves to the bun interpreter (`~/.bun/bin/bun`) rather than the gbrain CLI script.

## Symptoms

On a bun-linked install (`bun install && bun link` — the recommended install path):

```
$ gbrain apply-migrations --yes
? Select a project template - Press return to submit.
     Blank           <-- bun init prompt fires instead of gbrain init
     React
     Library
...
error: Script not found "extract"
Migration v0.13.0 finished as PARTIAL.
```

Root cause: `bin/gbrain` is a symlink to `src/cli.ts` executed via bun. `process.execPath` returns `/Users/.../.bun/bin/bun`, so `execSync(\`${process.execPath} init --migrate-only\`)` runs `bun init`, not `gbrain init`. Same for `extract` and other migration sub-invocations.

## Fix

Add a small helper `src/commands/migrations/gbrain-self.ts` that exposes `gbrainSelfCmd()` returning a shell-safe `bun run <argv[1]>` command string, and route all migration re-invocations through it.

- `src/commands/migrations/gbrain-self.ts` (new, 44 lines)
- `src/commands/migrations/v0_11_0.ts`, `v0_12_0.ts`, `v0_12_2.ts`, `v0_13_0.ts` — replace `process.execPath` / bare `gbrain` shell-outs with `gbrainSelfCmd()`.

Works in:
- dev (`bun run src/cli.ts ...`)
- bun-linked installs (argv[1] is the linked symlink target)
- direct shebang invocation (argv[1] is the script path)

## Verification

```
$ gbrain apply-migrations --yes --dry-run
# plans migration phases; no bun init prompt

$ gbrain apply-migrations --yes
# completes cleanly; doctor no longer reports HALF-INSTALLED

$ gbrain doctor --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.name=="minions_migration")'
# absent (fixed)
```

## Testing notes

Applied and verified on macOS (arm64) with Bun v1.3.10 against a 1,595-page PGLite brain. Pre-fix: 100% reproducible failure. Post-fix: all migrations run to completion on the same DB state.

No schema or behavioral changes — purely fixes how migrations shell out to re-invoke themselves. Idempotent, backwards compatible.

## Authorship note

This patch originated in downstream scaffolde-ai and was cherry-picked here for upstream contribution.

title: fix: prevent concurrent apply-migrations races via DB advisory lock
body:
## Summary

Fixes issue #271: `bun install` postinstall can race with a foreground `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`, causing one process to get SIGTERM'd mid-orchestrator and leaving the migration at `'partial'` status.

### The problem

1. `postinstall` fires `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive` (PID_A)
2. PID_A reaches an orchestrator phase that internally calls `gbrain init --migrate-only`
3. Meanwhile the user runs `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` in a terminal (PID_B)
4. PID_B waits on the DB advisory lock; whichever process sleeps longer gets killed by SIGTERM
5. The killed orchestrator leaves its migration marked `partial` in `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl`

### The fix

Add a `pg_try_advisory_lock(43)` gate at the top of `runApplyMigrations()`. This approach:

- **Non-blocking**: `pg_try_advisory_lock` returns immediately (false) if another runner holds the lock — no SIGTERM, no waiting
- **Exit code 3**: When the lock is contended, the runner exits with a clear message telling the user another instance is running (and suggests `--force-retry` if it's a stale lock from a crash)
- **PGLite-safe**: Falls through for PGLite engines (single-process, concurrent access impossible)
- **Minimal scope**: This gate only serializes the top-level entry point. Orchestrators already manage their own per-phase advisory locks

### Testing

- Unit tests for `apply-migrations.test.ts` pass (pure helpers unaffected)
- E2E `migration-flow.test.ts` exercises the full orchestrator path
- Manual verification: start two concurrent `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` processes and confirm one exits cleanly with the "another apply-migrations is already running" message

Fixes: #271

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(hybrid): propagate SearchOpts filters to inner keyword/vector searches
body:
## Summary

`hybridSearch()` silently drops caller-provided `type` and `exclude_slugs` filter options when building `searchOpts` for inner `searchKeyword` / `searchVector` calls:

https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/src/core/search/hybrid.ts#L71

```typescript
const searchOpts: SearchOpts = { limit: innerLimit, detail };
```

Any caller using `hybridSearch(engine, query, { type: 'person' })` or `{ exclude_slugs: [...] }` gets unfiltered results while believing the filter is applied — the outer `hybridSearch` never reads those fields again, and the inner searches never see them.

## Fix

One-line spread before overriding `limit` / `offset` / `detail`:

```typescript
const searchOpts: SearchOpts = { ...opts, limit: innerLimit, offset: 0, detail };
```

This preserves every caller-provided filter field (current and future — any field added to `SearchOpts` becomes automatically propagated, no additional plumbing).

`offset` is explicitly set to `0` on the inner searches because the outer `hybridSearch` slices the final result set at `[offset, offset+limit]` itself — propagating the caller's offset into the inner searches would double-apply it.

## Test plan

Added `test/hybrid-search-opts.test.ts` with 4 regression tests covering:

- `type` filter propagates to `searchKeyword`
- `exclude_slugs` propagates
- `limit` is overridden to `innerLimit` (outer `limit * 2`) and `offset` is forced to `0`
- `undefined` opts don't throw

All existing tests still pass (`bun test test/search.test.ts test/search-limit.test.ts` — 42 pass, 0 fail).

Happy to add similar tests on the vector path or integration-level tests if that would help. Also flagged as draft in case you'd prefer a different fix shape (e.g., explicit per-field spread instead of full `...opts`).

title: bug: doctor resolver_health false positive when invoked outside gbrain repo
body:
## Summary

`gbrain doctor --json` reports `resolver_health: warn — "Could not find skills directory"` when the CLI is invoked from outside the GBrain repo root, even on a healthy source-linked install.

Observed on this install shape:
- source-linked checkout at `/data/gbrain`
- bun global link provides `gbrain` on PATH
- command run from `/data/.openclaw/workspace`

## Reproduction

From outside the repo root:

```bash
cd /data/.openclaw/workspace
gbrain doctor --json
```

Observed excerpt:

```json
{"name":"resolver_health","status":"warn","message":"Could not find skills directory"}
```

From the repo root:

```bash
cd /data/gbrain
gbrain doctor --json
```

Observed excerpt:

```json
{"name":"resolver_health","status":"warn","message":"9 issue(s): 0 error(s), 9 warning(s)"}
```

So the warning is not a real missing-skills condition. It is a path-resolution false positive.

## Trace

Current logic in `src/commands/doctor.ts`:
- `runDoctor()` calls `findRepoRoot()`
- `findRepoRoot()` walks upward from `process.cwd()` looking for `skills/RESOLVER.md`
- when cwd is outside `/data/gbrain`, it never reaches the installed package path, so it emits the false warning

Relevant lines from current source during verification:

```ts
const repoRoot = findRepoRoot();
...
checks.push({ name: 'resolver_health', status: 'warn', message: 'Could not find skills directory' });
```

and

```ts
function findRepoRoot(): string | null {
  let dir = process.cwd();
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    if (existsSync(join(dir, 'skills', 'RESOLVER.md'))) return dir;
    const parent = join(dir, '..');
    if (parent === dir) break;
    dir = parent;
  }
  return null;
}
```

## Why it matters

This creates permanent warning noise for healthy installs when operators run `gbrain doctor` from their agent workspace or another directory. That trains people to ignore a real warning channel.

## Note

I also found open PR #128 (`fix: doctor resolves skills/ from install path when run outside repo`) which appears to target the same root cause. This issue is just the concrete reproduction report from a live source-linked install, because the false warning is still present in v0.14.2 on this host.

title: fix(doctor): findRepoRoot falls back to import.meta.dir when run outside repo
body:
## Summary

`gbrain doctor --json` reports `resolver_health: warn — "Could not find skills directory"` when the CLI is invoked from outside the GBrain repo root (e.g. from an agent workspace via a global bun link). This is a false positive that trains users to ignore a real warning channel.

**Root cause:** `findRepoRoot()` only walked up from `process.cwd()` looking for `skills/RESOLER.md`. When cwd is outside the repo (e.g. `/data/.openclaw/workspace`), it never reaches the installed package path and emits the false warning.

**Fix:** After walking up from cwd, fall back to walking up from the file's own location via `import.meta.url` (same pattern used in `init.ts`). The skills dir is reachable from the gbrain binary's install path even when cwd is nowhere near the repo root.

## Changes

- `src/commands/doctor.ts`: Added `fileURLToPath` and `dirname` imports; `findRepoRoot()` now falls back to resolving from `import.meta.url` after the cwd walk fails.
- `test/doctor.test.ts`: Added regression test for the fallback behavior.

## Test

```bash
# From outside the repo (reproduces issue #283)
cd /tmp
gbrain doctor --json | jq '.[] | select(.name == "resolver_health")'
# Before fix: {"name":"resolver_health","status":"warn","message":"Could not find skills directory"}
# After fix: {"name":"resolver_health","status":"ok",...}
```

Issue: #283

title: fix(db): disable prepared statements by default for pooler compat
body:
## What

Adds `prepare: false` to the postgres.js connection options in `db.ts`.

## Why

Supabase Supavisor and PgBouncer in transaction mode don't support prepared statements — session state isn't preserved between queries, so prepared statement references become dangling. 

While `?prepare=false` in the connection URL already handles this (postgres.js parses it correctly), setting it explicitly in the options object provides a safety net for:
- Users who configure their DB URL without the query param
- Any future refactoring that might construct the URL differently

## Testing

- All 1743 bun tests pass, 0 failures
- Verified `gbrain search` and `gbrain query` work correctly with the change
- Single line change, low risk

## Impact

postgres.js defaults `prepare: true`. This makes gbrain work correctly with transaction-mode poolers out of the box.

Ref: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres#connection-pooler

title: docs: minions worker deployment guide (from Wintermute)
body:
## From Wintermute (Garry Tan's AI agent)

### Problem

The `gbrain jobs work` persistent worker dies silently from Supabase connection drops, leaving jobs stuck in queue forever. No built-in recovery mechanism. We discovered this running a production minion workload:

- X pipeline: 8x/day cron with 7 pipeline steps
- Adversary monitoring: 19 tracked accounts via filtered stream
- Deep enrichment backfill: 76 months of historical tweets

The worker would start, process a few jobs, then die. Jobs pile up in `waiting`. The stall detector requeues them but the worker is dead so they just cycle.

### Root Cause

1. Supabase DB connection drops intermittently
2. Worker's lock renewal fails → lock expires after 30s
3. Stall detector fires (maxStalledCount=1) → job dead-lettered
4. Worker internal state corrupted → `Minion worker stopped`
5. PID alive but event loop dead → external monitoring thinks it's fine

### What This PR Adds

`docs/guides/minions-deployment.md` documenting:

- **Watchdog cron pattern** — 5-min cron that detects dead PIDs AND internally-stopped workers
- **Inline `--follow` pattern** — skip persistent worker, each cron brings its own temporary worker
- **Known issues** with default lock/stall settings
- **Proposed CLI flags**: `--lock-duration`, `--max-stalled`, `--stall-interval`
- **Smoke test** commands

### Future Work (separate PRs)

- Add `--lock-duration`, `--max-stalled`, `--stall-interval` CLI flags to `gbrain jobs work`
- Built-in `--watchdog` mode (auto-restart on internal failure)
- Health file (`/tmp/gbrain-worker-health.json`) for external monitoring
- DB connection pooling with retry on disconnect

title: fix(embed): SQL-filter stale chunks in --stale path (#161)
body:
## Summary

`embedAll(engine, /*staleOnly=*/true)` previously called `engine.listPages({ limit: 100000 })` and then iterated *every* page's chunks in application code, skipping those where every chunk already had `embedded_at` set. At 100% coverage that meant every autopilot cycle walked every page and did zero real work — the exact symptom in #161 ("embed --stale unexpectedly iterates all 31,139 pages").

This PR pushes the "is this page stale?" decision down to the database with a single `SELECT DISTINCT p.slug ... WHERE c.embedded_at IS NULL` query. At 100% coverage we short-circuit with `No stale chunks to embed.` and return. Below 100% coverage we only iterate pages that actually have at least one un-embedded chunk.

Falls back to the old full-walk path when the engine doesn't expose `executeRaw` (e.g. stub engines in tests), so this is fully backward-compatible.

## Repro

Against any brain at 100% embedding coverage:

```
gbrain embed --stale
```

- **Before:** walks every page (`listPages({ limit: 100000 })` + per-page chunk fetch).
- **After:** one SQL round-trip, prints `No stale chunks to embed.`, returns.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test: `--stale with 100% coverage does NOT walk every page (issue #161)` — asserts `listPages` and `getChunks` are never called when the `WHERE embedded_at IS NULL` query returns `[]`.
- [x] New unit test: `--stale falls back to full walk when executeRaw is unsupported` — guards the back-compat path.
- [x] Existing `skips pages whose chunks are all already embedded when --stale` updated to mock `executeRaw` alongside `listPages`.
- [x] Full `bun test` suite: **1919 pass, 0 fail, 174 skip** (E2E gated on Postgres/Docker, not run).
- [ ] E2E suite (`docker-compose.test.yml`) — not run in this PR; left to CI/maintainer since it needs Postgres + pgvector + real API keys.

Fixes #161

title: fix(pglite): fail loudly on $bunfs data-dir paths (#250)
body:
## Summary

When `gbrain` is compiled with `bun build --compile`, Bun mounts the bundled files under `$bunfs://` — a virtual filesystem that PGLite's WASM module cannot read. The existing failure mode was either an opaque WASM panic or silent corruption of the on-disk brain state, leaving users with a half-initialized brain and no actionable signal about what went wrong.

This PR adds a small guard — `assertRealFilesystemPath()` — called at the top of `PGLiteEngine.connect()`, *before* the file lock or PGLite itself is touched. The guard detects the `$bunfs` prefix and throws with an actionable error pointing at the documented workarounds:

- Run from source: `bun run src/cli.ts <command>`
- Or pass `--database-path` with a real on-disk path

## Coverage

The detector covers every documented `$bunfs` shape:

- `$bunfs://...` (URL-style)
- `$bunfs/...` (bare prefix)
- `/$bunfs/...` (absolute-path style, seen on Linux)
- `/<anything>/$bunfs/...` (nested)

Null / undefined / empty paths (in-memory PGLite, no data-dir) are unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] 9 new unit tests in `test/pglite-path-guard.test.ts`:
  - `isBunfsPath` returns `true` for each documented shape
  - `isBunfsPath` returns `false` for normal paths and empty inputs
  - `assertRealFilesystemPath` throws with a message that mentions PGLite, the offending path, the `bun run src/cli.ts` workaround, `--database-path`, and the issue number for context
  - no-op on normal/undefined paths
- [x] Existing `pglite-lock.test.ts` + `engine-factory.test.ts` still pass.
- [x] Full `bun test` suite: **1926 pass, 0 fail, 174 skip**.
- [ ] E2E suite not run.

## Non-goals

This PR doesn't fix the underlying "compiled binary can't use PGLite" limitation — that likely needs PGLite WASM upstream work to read from `$bunfs`, or a one-time copy-to-tmp dance during startup. What this PR does is replace "opaque WASM panic / silent corruption" with "clear, actionable error pointing at the workaround", so the ~20 users who hit this in #250 stop losing time to it.

Fixes #250
