title: v0.22.8 perf: doctor integrity batch-load + multi-source correctness
body:
## Summary

`gbrain doctor` was timing out at 60s on Postgres+PgBouncer deployments because the integrity check called `getPage()` 500 times sequentially through transaction-mode pooling. This PR replaces the sequential loop with a single SQL query (~6s wall-clock) and adds the correctness work to make that single query equivalent to the sequential path on every supported case.

**Performance**
- Doctor integrity sample: 60s+ timeout → ~6s on Postgres + PgBouncer
- Round-trips: ~500 sequential `getPage()` calls → 1 batch SQL query

**Correctness** (codex catch — see Review trail)
- Multi-source brains (UNIQUE(source_id, slug) since v0.18.0) now scan each slug once via `SELECT DISTINCT ON (slug)` instead of overcounting per source row
- Batch path explicitly gated to Postgres via `engine.kind` so PGLite never enters
- Silent `catch{}` narrowed to `GBRAIN_DEBUG`-gated `console.error` so real Postgres errors (deadlock, connection drop, SQL bug) are diagnosable

**Infrastructure**
- Skillpack lockfile Linux ext4 fix (sub-millisecond `mtimeMs` precision was causing intermittent CI flakes)

## Test Coverage

New `test/e2e/integrity-batch.test.ts` — four parity cases against real Postgres:

```
[+] test/e2e/integrity-batch.test.ts (E2E, Postgres-only, skip on missing DATABASE_URL)
  ├── dedup        — multi-source duplicate slugs scan once (codex catch regression guard)
  ├── hits         — bareHits + externalHits match between batch and sequential
  ├── validate     — validate:false (boolean) page skipped on both paths
  └── topPages     — ordering matches between paths

[+] test/skillpack-install.test.ts — added 1 regression case for Linux fs-timestamp
    negative-age (utimesSync(+10ms) deterministically reproduces the bug)
```

## Verification Results

- `bun test test/integrity.test.ts` — 29 pass, 0 fail (PGLite suite)
- `bun test test/skillpack-install.test.ts` — 27 pass, 0 fail
- `DATABASE_URL=... bun test test/e2e/integrity-batch.test.ts` — 4 pass, 0 fail (real Postgres)
- `bun build --compile --outfile /tmp/gbrain-test src/cli.ts` — clean build

## Pre-Landing Review

`/plan-eng-review` walked four findings; all addressed in this PR:
- source_id dedup regression → `SELECT DISTINCT ON (slug)` (commit `0450c99`)
- no test coverage for batch path → 4 parity E2E tests (commit `1f22b89`)
- silent `catch{}` swallows DB errors → `GBRAIN_DEBUG`-gated `console.error` + `engine.kind` gate (commit `0450c99`)
- validate filter divergence → intentionally left as-is (boolean is the documented contract; stringly-typed handled by lint, not scan)

## Plan Completion

All planned work landed:
- [x] DISTINCT ON SQL fix
- [x] engine.kind gate
- [x] Debug-gated catch log
- [x] Inline comments for non-obvious WHY
- [x] E2E parity tests (dedup, hits, validate, topPages)
- [x] CLAUDE.md inventory updates
- [x] CHANGELOG v0.22.8 entry (perf-first headline, 3-row numbers table, "To take advantage" block)
- [x] VERSION 0.22.8

## Review trail

The original perf commit (`60203df`) was reviewed via `/plan-eng-review` + `/codex review`. **Codex flagged a `source_id` dedup regression**: the batch SQL scanned raw `(source_id, slug)` rows while the sequential path scanned unique slugs via `engine.getAllSlugs()` (which returns `Set<string>`). On multi-source brains, the batch path overcounted bare-tweet hits and exhausted the 500-page sample budget on duplicates. Single-source users were unaffected.

This PR addresses all four findings from the eng-review walk (see Pre-Landing Review section above). Validate-filter divergence is documented inline at the SQL line so future maintainers see the intent.

The skillpack lockfile fix in `08dd9bf` is unrelated to the doctor work — surfaced when CI flaked on Linux ext4 while testing the perf commit. Bundled into this PR because it's a small focused fix that gates the same CI lane.

Migration `v24` (`rls_backfill_missing_tables`, introduced in v0.18.1) fails on PGLite installs because it unconditionally runs `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on tables that only exist in the Postgres schema (`subagent_messages`, `access_tokens`, `mcp_request_log`, `subagent_tool_executions`, `subagent_rate_leases`, etc.). PGLite's `pglite-schema.ts` deliberately omits these tables (comment at top: "No access_tokens / mcp_request_log (local-only, no remote auth)").

Other migrations that are Postgres-only correctly guard with `if (engine.kind === 'pglite') return;` (see v23 `files_source_id_page_id_ledger`). v24 is missing that gate.

## Environment

- gbrain `0.20.4` (commit `11abb24`)
- PGLite engine (`~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`)
- Node 24.14.1 / macOS 24.6.0

## Reproduction

Any PGLite install reaching schema v23 will hit this on the next `initSchema()` / `gbrain init --migrate-only`:

```
  [24] rls_backfill_missing_tables...
error: relation "subagent_messages" does not exist
  severity: ERROR
  code: 42P01
  where: 'SQL statement "ALTER TABLE subagent_messages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY"
          PL/pgSQL function inline_code_block line 23 at SQL statement'
```

## Suggested fix

Add an engine gate at the top of the v24 handler, matching the pattern already used in v23:

```ts
// src/core/migrate.ts around line 748 (v24 entry)
{
  version: 24,
  name: 'rls_backfill_missing_tables',
  sql: '',
  handler: async (engine) => {
    if (engine.kind === 'pglite') return;
    // ... existing RLS backfill SQL
  },
},
```

PGLite is single-process / single-user with no PostgREST exposure, so there's nothing to backfill — a no-op is the correct behavior (already documented in the RLS doctor check: `[OK] rls: Skipped (PGLite — no PostgREST exposure, RLS not applicable)`).

## Workaround

For anyone else hitting this before the fix ships, mark v24 done manually:

```js
// requires @electric-sql/pglite loaded with extensions: { vector, pg_trgm }
await db.query(
  "INSERT INTO config (key, value) VALUES ('version', '24') ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value"
);
```

## Related observation (separate issue, flagging for context)

While debugging this, I also hit a second issue on the same install: `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` in `pglite-schema.ts:63` runs `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id)` before the migration loop runs. On a mid-migration install (pre-v21 where `pages.source_id` doesn't exist yet), `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages` is a no-op against the old schema and the bare CREATE INDEX fails before migrations get a chance to add the column. Our DB was wedged at schema v4 since Apr 22 for this reason. Happy to file separately if helpful.

title: PGLite initSchema fails on mid-migration installs — source_id index created before column exists
body:
## Summary

`PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` in `src/core/pglite-schema.ts` runs `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id)` (line 63) every time `initSchema()` is called. The migration loop that adds `pages.source_id` (migration v21) runs **after** this. On a mid-migration install (any DB that predates v21), the sequence is:

1. `initSchema()` → `db.exec(PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL)`
2. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (...)` → no-op (pages already exists from schema v4)
3. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id)` → **fails with `column \"source_id\" does not exist`**
4. Migrations never run.

The implicit assumption is that the schema SQL is only executed against either a fresh DB (where `CREATE TABLE` just created `pages` with `source_id`) or an already-current DB (where the column was added by a prior migration run). Any install caught between those two states is wedged.

## Impact

A PGLite install at schema v4 was stuck wedged for 3 days across `gbrain apply-migrations` runs (v0.11.0, v0.12.0, v0.12.2 all recorded as `partial` in `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl`). Each failure in `upgrade-errors.jsonl` is a terse `column \"source_id\" does not exist` with no hint that the schema SQL itself is the culprit — all the data-migration orchestrators point at their own schema phase, which just shells out to `gbrain init --migrate-only` and gets the same error.

In our case, the nightly `gbrain sync` launchd job ran successfully enough to mask the wedge (sync skips non-fatally on individual-file errors), so it wasn't obvious until we tried to upgrade the gbrain version.

## Environment

- gbrain `0.20.4` (commit `11abb24`)
- Wedged from schema v4; the failing path affects any install that hasn't already applied migration v21 before picking up a version of the schema SQL that includes the `idx_pages_source_id` line.
- PGLite engine (`~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`)
- Node 24.14.1 / macOS 24.6.0

## Reproduction

Starting state: PGLite DB at schema v4 (i.e. any install from before v21 was introduced).

```
$ npx gbrain init --migrate-only
column \"source_id\" does not exist
```

No stack, no hint at the offending SQL statement, no recovery suggestion. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` produces the same error wrapped by the data-migration orchestrator:

```
Migration v0.12.2 is WEDGED (3+ consecutive partials with no completion).
Check ~/.gbrain/upgrade-errors.jsonl for the last failure reasons, fix the underlying issue, then run:
  gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry 0.12.2
```

`--force-retry` does not help because the underlying schema SQL keeps failing.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/core/pglite-engine.ts:86
async initSchema(): Promise<void> {
  await this.db.exec(PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL);   // ← line 63 of schema fails here
  const { applied } = await runMigrations(this);  // ← never reached
}
```

```sql
-- src/core/pglite-schema.ts line 63 (inside PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
```

The `CREATE INDEX` cannot be guarded by a column-level `IF NOT EXISTS`; Postgres does not support that. The table-level `IF NOT EXISTS` on the preceding `CREATE TABLE` hides the fact that the column isn't actually there.

## Suggested fixes

A few options, in increasing order of invasiveness:

**Option 1 — Gate the index creation on the column.** Wrap just the `source_id` index (and any other v18.0-added columns the schema SQL references) in a `DO $$ ... IF EXISTS ... END $$` block:

```sql
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
     WHERE table_name = 'pages' AND column_name = 'source_id'
  ) THEN
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
  END IF;
END $$;
```

Minimal change, preserves the \"schema SQL is always safe to re-run\" property. Once migration v21 runs on the next `initSchema()` call and adds the column, the next `initSchema()` will create the index.

**Option 2 — Move the index into migration v21 alongside the column add.** v21 already creates the index in its pglite branch (`pglite-schema.ts` line 40-41 of the `sqlFor.pglite` block). If the schema SQL trusts migrations to own v18.0-added columns entirely, the schema SQL can stop trying to create indexes on them. Cleaner separation of concerns — \"schema SQL owns the latest shape, migrations own the evolution,\" but doesn't overlap.

**Option 3 — Defer `initSchema()`'s schema SQL pass until migrations complete.** Run migrations first, then the schema SQL (which should be idempotent against the post-migration shape). Biggest change but also the most robust — it removes the ordering dependency entirely.

Happy to send a PR for option 1 if that'd help.

## Workaround

For anyone else hitting this before the fix ships, bypass `initSchema()` entirely and call `runMigrations()` directly against the existing engine. Once migrations complete and the column exists, `gbrain init --migrate-only` works normally:

```ts
// migrate-bypass.mts
import { PGLiteEngine } from 'gbrain/pglite-engine';
import { runMigrations } from './node_modules/gbrain/src/core/migrate.ts';

const engine = new PGLiteEngine();
await engine.connect({
  database_path: \`\${process.env.HOME}/.gbrain/brain.pglite\`,
  engine: 'pglite',
});
try {
  const { applied, current } = await runMigrations(engine);
  console.log(\`Applied \${applied} migration(s). Schema now at v\${current}.\`);
} finally {
  await engine.disconnect();
}
```

Run with `npx tsx migrate-bypass.mts`. (Separate caveat: migration v24 also fails on PGLite for a different reason — see #395.)

## Related

- #395 — v24 `rls_backfill_missing_tables` fails on PGLite (missing `engine.kind` gate). These two issues compound: even after working around this one by bypassing `initSchema()`, v24 still needs manual handling.

title: fix(pglite): guard idx_pages_source_id against pre-v21 brains (upgrade blocker)
body:
## Summary

**Critical upgrade blocker** for existing PGLite brains at schema version 13-20: every attempt to upgrade to v0.18.0+ crashes with `column "source_id" does not exist`, and the v0.18.0 migration goes wedged after 3 consecutive partials.

## Root cause

`initSchema()` runs `pglite-schema.ts` **before** migrations apply, on every connect. The current schema includes:

\`\`\`sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
\`\`\`

On existing brains created before v0.18.0, `pages` exists from an older schema without `source_id`. The `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (...)` above is a no-op (table already exists), so the column stays missing. Then the unguarded `CREATE INDEX` hits the column before migration v21 has a chance to add it — crash.

## Fix

Wrap the index creation in a `DO` block that probes `information_schema.columns` first. Fresh installs enter the branch on first `initSchema` call (because the `CREATE TABLE` just created the column). Existing brains skip the index on first pass, let migration v21 add the column, then get the index on the very next `initSchema` call.

## Reproduction

- Start with any PGLite brain at schema version ≤ 20 (i.e. any brain upgrading from v0.13/v0.14/v0.15/v0.16/v0.17).
- Run \`gbrain apply-migrations --yes\`.
- Observe \`column "source_id" does not exist\` and \`Migration v0.18.0 is WEDGED\` after three retry cycles.

This PR, applied to v0.20.4, unblocks a clean v13 → v24 schema migration on an 80-page PGLite brain in my setup.

## Related memory / context

This is the "PGLite 顺序" failure mode called out in my lessons log from the 2026-04-21 upgrade cycle (see \`lessons_2026-04-21.md\` in our local CLAUDE notes). Keeping it for posterity in case other brains at v14.x attempt the same jump.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced on an 80-page PGLite brain pinned at schema v13 — crashed every upgrade until this fix.
- [x] After fix: \`gbrain init --migrate-only\` applies v14-v24 cleanly, \`gbrain apply-migrations --yes\` completes v0.18.0 through v0.18.1, \`gbrain doctor\` reports \`schema_version: Version 24 (latest: 24)\`.
- [ ] Fresh PGLite install path worth a look from reviewers — I verified manually but don't have an automated test against a brand-new \`~/.gbrain\` directory.

title: fix: harden PGLite upgrade path
body:
## Summary
- guard `idx_pages_source_id` creation in `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` so `initSchema()` stays replay-safe on pre-v21 brains

Older PGLite brains could fail before migrations ran because the latest schema replay tried to create `idx_pages_source_id` before `pages.source_id` existed. After bypassing that, v24 could still fail on PGLite by running Postgres-only `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` statements against tables that do not exist in `pglite-schema.ts`.

title: fix(resolver): support nested slugs with multiple path segments
body:
## Problem

The Step 1 regex validation in `SlugResolver.resolve()` only matches single-slash slugs like `state/scheduled`. Nested slugs like `reference/nodes/hermes` (2+ slashes) fail the check and fall through to Step 3, where they lose the race to fuzzy title matching.

## Root Cause

Regex pattern in `src/core/link-extraction.ts` line 583:

```regex
/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/
```

This only matches single-slash slugs.

## Solution

Changed to:

```regex
/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?:\/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)+$/
```

The fixed pattern allows one or more slash-separated segments.

## Testing

Verified with nested slugs `reference/nodes/hermes` and `state/scheduled/infrastructure-state` in test frontmatter—both now resolve correctly via the fixed Step 1 check.

---

**Verified 2026-05-07** — clean against v0.28.7 (aa04988) on schema v40.
Branch is 1 commit ahead of origin/master (merge-base aa04988). No rebase needed.
Single-file change in `src/core/link-extraction.ts`; regex fix confirmed in source.

title: fix: unblock initSchema upgrades on pre-source-id brains
body:
## Summary

`initSchema()` currently applies the embedded latest schema before numbered migrations run. On existing brains that predate `pages.source_id`, that can fail before `runMigrations()` ever gets a chance to add the column.

This PR makes the upgrade path explicit in both engines:

- detect legacy brains where `pages.source_id` is still missing
- run `runMigrations()` first in that case
- then apply the embedded schema
- then do the normal post-schema migration pass

Fresh installs and already-upgraded brains keep the current path.

## Why this shape

There are already a few open issues around the same failure mode (#366, #378, #396, #375). A schema-level guard on one specific index helps, but the broader problem is ordering: the latest schema blob is allowed to reference columns that only appear in later numbered migrations.

This keeps the fix tight and local to `initSchema()` while unblocking older brains without changing the steady-state behavior for modern installs.

## Reproduction / observed failure

On my local upgrade from `0.14.2` to `0.20.4` (Postgres / Supabase via PgBouncer), `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` initially failed with:

```text
column "source_id" does not exist
```

Root cause: `src/core/postgres-engine.ts` ran `SCHEMA_SQL` first, and the embedded schema now references `pages(source_id)` before older brains have received that column through the numbered migration chain.

## Validation

- [x] Reproduced on a real Postgres-backed brain upgrading from `0.14.2` to `0.20.4`
- [x] After this fix, the schema chain was able to advance to `24/24`
- [x] `gbrain doctor` returned schema green / RLS green after upgrade
- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [ ] I did not have a legacy PGLite brain handy to replay end-to-end locally, but mirrored the same fix there because the failure mode reported in #396 is the same ordering bug in `PGLiteEngine.initSchema()`

## Related

- Closes #366
- Addresses #378
- Addresses #396
- Addresses #375

If you prefer the narrower schema-guard approach for PGLite, I’m happy to trim this down further, but in my testing the engine-level ordering fix was the cleanest way to make old brains survive the jump.

title: fix: propagate AbortSignal to runCycle + worker force-eviction safety net
body:
## Problem

When a Minions worker evicts a timed-out autopilot-cycle job, the `runCycle` function inside the handler **ignores the abort and continues running all remaining phases**. The worker marks the job as evicted and moves on, but the zombie handler keeps executing — holding the event loop, monopolizing CPU, and (critically) **holding the Postgres cycle lock** so no new cycle can acquire it.

**Observed failure mode on a production brain (54K+ pages):**

1. Autopilot-cycle starts. Extract phase takes 600s+ on large brains.
2. Job hits the 600s wall-clock timeout. Worker fires `AbortController.abort()`.
3. `runCycle` has no abort check between phases → **keeps running** through extract → embed → orphans.
4. Worker force-evicts the job from `inFlight` after 30s grace period to unblock the slot.
5. But the zombie handler is still alive in the process, holding the cycle lock.
6. Worker picks up the *next* queued autopilot-cycle → `runCycle` tries to acquire lock → **lock is still held by the zombie** → returns `skipped: cycle_already_running`.
7. This repeats every 5 minutes until the zombie finishes or the lock's 30-min TTL expires.
8. Meanwhile 20-35 autopilot-cycle jobs queue up, all returning "skipped."

The worker's SIGTERM handler also couldn't terminate the process because the zombie handler held the event loop — requiring SIGKILL.

**This is the companion fix to #417 (incremental extract).** #417 eliminates the *cause* (extract taking 600s+), this PR adds the *safety net* (abort signal propagation) so that even if a future phase is slow, the cycle bails promptly instead of wedging the worker.

## Error Log

Worker log showing timeout, abort ignored, and force-eviction:

```
[extract.timeline_fs] 54461/54461 (100%) done
Timeline: created 0 entries from 54461 pages
[cycle.extract] done
[cycle.embed] start
Job 1290 (autopilot-cycle) hit per-job timeout (600000ms), aborting
Job 1290 (autopilot-cycle) did not exit within 30s of abort. Force-evicting
from inFlight to unblock worker. The handler is still running but the worker
will claim new jobs.
```

The worker emitted the abort, but `runCycle` had no `checkAborted()` calls — it just kept going into the embed phase. After force-eviction, the worker log went silent (no new jobs picked up despite 20+ in the queue), confirming the zombie handler was blocking the event loop.

Job showing the stale lock blocking subsequent cycles:

```
Job #1461: autopilot-cycle (COMPLETED)
  Started: 2026-04-25T12:10:03.708Z
  Finished: 2026-04-25T12:13:09.645Z
  Result: {"status":"skipped","reason":"cycle_already_running"}
```

186s wall clock to discover the lock was held — the cycle lock check itself was slow because it had to wait for a Postgres round-trip and the lock row's TTL comparison.

Postgres lock row left behind by the killed worker:

```sql
SELECT * FROM gbrain_cycle_locks;
-- id: gbrain-cycle
-- holder_pid: 1065070  (dead process)
-- acquired_at: 2026-04-25T00:32:04.576Z
-- ttl_expires_at: 2026-04-25T01:02:04.576Z
-- is_live: true  (TTL hadn't expired yet)
```

## What We Tried

1. **SIGTERM on the worker** — did not work. The zombie handler from the force-evicted job held the event loop. The worker process ignored SIGTERM entirely. Had to escalate to SIGKILL.

2. **SIGKILL on the worker + supervisor restart** — killed the process, but the Postgres cycle lock persisted with a 30-min TTL. New worker started, new cycles all returned "skipped: cycle_already_running."

3. **Manual lock deletion** — `DELETE FROM gbrain_cycle_locks WHERE id = 'gbrain-cycle'`. Unblocked new cycles immediately. But this is a manual intervention, not a fix.

4. **Checked if the worker's force-eviction was supposed to clean up** — it wasn't. The force-eviction only removes the job from the worker's `inFlight` set. It does NOT release the cycle lock because the lock is held inside `runCycle`, which is still running as a zombie.

5. **Added `checkAborted()` between phases (this PR)** — cooperative abort. Between each phase, check if `signal.aborted` is true. If so, throw immediately. The `finally` block in `runCycle` releases the cycle lock on any exit path (normal, error, or abort). This means a timed-out job will bail at the next phase boundary AND release the lock.

**Hotfix:** Deployed the `checkAborted` + `signal` propagation directly to the production instance. This PR is the clean version with tests.

## Solution

### 1. Propagate AbortSignal into `runCycle` (`src/core/cycle.ts`)

Add a `signal?: AbortSignal` option to `CycleOpts`. Between each phase, call `checkAborted(signal)` — if the signal has fired, throw immediately instead of proceeding to the next phase.

```typescript
function checkAborted(signal?: AbortSignal): void {
  if (signal?.aborted) {
    const reason = signal.reason instanceof Error
      ? signal.reason.message
      : String(signal.reason || 'aborted');
    throw new Error(`[cycle] aborted between phases: ${reason}`);
  }
}
```

### 2. Pass job.signal from the worker handler (`src/commands/jobs.ts`)

The autopilot-cycle handler already receives the job object from the worker. The worker attaches an `AbortController` to each job. Wire `job.signal` into `runCycle`:

```typescript
const report = await runCycle(engine, {
  brainDir: repoPath,
  pull: true,
  signal: job.signal,  // new
  yieldBetweenPhases: async () => { ... },
});
```

### 3. Force-eviction safety net (`src/core/minions/worker.ts`)

When the worker evicts a stalled job from `inFlight`, log a clear warning. The handler may still be running (Node has no way to kill a running async function), but the worker can at least claim new jobs.

### Behavior matrix

| Phase state when abort fires | Result |
|------------------------------|--------|
| Between phases (yield point) | `checkAborted` throws → cycle returns `failed` report → lock released |
| Mid-phase (e.g., deep in embed) | Current phase runs to completion, then `checkAborted` fires before next phase |
| Phase already finished | No effect (cycle was going to end anyway) |

The abort is **cooperative** — it can't interrupt a phase mid-execution (that would require threads). But it prevents the cascade: instead of running 3 more phases after timeout, the cycle bails at the next phase boundary.

## Results

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Phases run after timeout | All remaining (3-4) | 0 (bails at next boundary) |
| Lock held after worker kill | 30 min (TTL) | Released on abort throw |
| Worker recovery after stuck job | Required SIGKILL | Automatic (abort + eviction) |
| Queue starvation duration | 30+ min per incident | < 1 phase duration |

## Testing

- `test/cycle-abort.test.ts` — 3 tests: signal propagation, mid-cycle abort, no-signal backward compat
- `test/e2e/worker-abort-recovery.test.ts` — end-to-end: worker timeout → abort → cycle stops → worker recovers → next job runs
- `test/minions.test.ts` — regression tests for force-eviction behavior
- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- Production hotfix deployed and stable for 12+ hours

## Related

- Companion to #417 (incremental extract). #417 eliminates the cause (extract taking 600s+); this PR adds the safety net so any slow future phase can't wedge the worker.

title: fix(doctor): graph_coverage hint references the actual extract commands
body:
## Summary

`gbrain doctor`'s `graph_coverage` warning currently suggests two commands that don't exist:

```
[WARN] graph_coverage: Entity link coverage 0%, timeline 0%. Run: gbrain link-extract && gbrain timeline-extract
```

```
$ gbrain link-extract
Unknown command: link-extract
$ gbrain timeline-extract
Unknown command: timeline-extract
```

The actual subcommands are `gbrain extract links` and `gbrain extract timeline` (or `gbrain extract all` to do both), defined in [src/commands/extract.ts](src/commands/extract.ts).

This is the moment the user is trying to learn the tool, so a wrong hint here is high-friction. Fix is a one-line string change in [src/commands/doctor.ts:508](src/commands/doctor.ts#L508).

## Also in this PR

A stale doc comment in [src/core/link-extraction.ts:5-6](src/core/link-extraction.ts#L5) referenced `src/commands/link-extract.ts` and `src/commands/timeline-extract.ts` — both were consolidated into `src/commands/extract.ts` some time ago. Updated the comment to point at the current file.

## Repro

```bash
gbrain doctor
# warning prints "Run: gbrain link-extract && gbrain timeline-extract"
gbrain link-extract        # Unknown command
gbrain extract links       # works
```

## After

```
[WARN] graph_coverage: Entity link coverage 0%, timeline 0%. Run: gbrain extract links && gbrain extract timeline
```

## Notes

- Hit this on a fresh upgrade from v0.14.2 → v0.20.4. Whole upgrade landed cleanly otherwise — really nice work on the dream/runCycle primitive and the supervisor.
- Tested locally: `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean, `bun test` no regressions.

title: fix: connection resilience for minion supervisor + worker
body:
## Problem

The minion supervisor's worker processes die when PgBouncer rotates connections or Supabase bounces the pooler. The executeRaw() calls throw 'password authentication failed' or 'connection terminated', the worker crashes, and while the supervisor respawns it, the queue goes stale because:

1. The supervisor's own health check DB connection also dies silently
2. Logs don't distinguish OOM kills (SIGKILL) from connection deaths (exit code 1)  
3. The postgres-engine has no reconnect logic — once the pool is poisoned, every query fails until process restart

## Fixes

### 1. PostgresEngine: executeRaw retry on connection errors
- Added isConnectionError() detector for 13 known Postgres/PgBouncer error patterns
- executeRaw() catches connection-class errors, calls reconnect() (tears down pool, creates fresh one), retries query exactly once
- Concurrent reconnect guard prevents thundering herd

### 2. Supervisor: health check failure tracking + auto-reconnect  
- Tracks consecutiveHealthFailures counter (resets on success)
- After 3 consecutive failures: emits health_warn with reason=db_connection_degraded
- Attempts engine.reconnect() if available; emits db_reconnected on success

### 3. Supervisor: worker exit classification
- worker_exited events now include likely_cause field (oom_or_external_kill, graceful_shutdown, runtime_error, clean_exit, unknown)

## Tests
23 new tests: connection error pattern matching, exit classification, reconnect guard, retry-once, health failure tracking. All existing tests + typecheck pass.

title: fix(embed): server-side staleness filter — fixes 270x egress amplification
body:
## Problem

`gbrain embed --stale` (used by autopilot every cycle and recommended by `gbrain doctor`) walks every page in the brain even when 0 chunks need embedding. On a 1.5K-page / 8K-chunk Supabase-backed brain that is 100% embedded, a single invocation pulls **~76 MB** from Postgres (the `pages` table + every chunk's `vector(1536)` `embedding` column) and discards all of it after a client-side `.filter(c => !c.embedded_at)`. With autopilot firing this every 5–10 minutes, plus a 2-hour cron also running `embed --stale`, this compounds to **20–80 GB/day** of pure-waste egress. We hit Supabase's 5 GB free-tier bandwidth ceiling at 102 GB used (2058% over) twice in one week (2026-04-19 and again on 2026-04-24).

Relevant lines in master (`v0.20.4`, commit `11abb24`):

- `src/commands/embed.ts:223` — `const pages = await engine.listPages({ limit: 100000 });` — pulls every page row
- `src/commands/embed.ts:237` — `const chunks = await engine.getChunks(page.slug);` — pulls every chunk including the 1536-dim embedding vector
- `src/commands/embed.ts:238-240` — `staleOnly ? chunks.filter(c => !c.embedded_at) : chunks` — filter runs client-side, after the bytes have already crossed the wire

`rowToChunk` (`src/core/utils.ts`) defaults `includeEmbedding=false`, which means the embedding bytes are received and immediately dropped in TypeScript. Pure waste.

## Fix

Two new `BrainEngine` methods, identical implementations on Postgres + PGLite:

- `countStaleChunks(): Promise<number>` — single `SELECT count(*) FROM content_chunks WHERE embedding IS NULL`. ~50 bytes wire. Pre-flight short-circuit for `embed --stale`.
- `listStaleChunks(): Promise<StaleChunkRow[]>` — `SELECT slug, chunk_index, chunk_text, chunk_source, model, token_count FROM content_chunks JOIN pages WHERE embedding IS NULL ORDER BY p.id, chunk_index LIMIT 100000`. Excludes the (always-NULL on stale rows) embedding column. Per-row ~1.5 KB instead of ~8 KB.

`embedAll` is forked into two paths:
- `staleOnly === true` → new `embedAllStale` using the SQL-side filter. Pre-flight count short-circuits when 0 stale.
- `staleOnly === false` (i.e. `--all`) → existing behavior verbatim. The user explicitly asked for re-embed-everything.

Staleness predicate is `embedding IS NULL`, not `embedded_at IS NULL`, because the bulk-import path could previously leave `embedded_at` populated while `embedding` was NULL (see consistency fix below). `embedding IS NULL` is the truth source for "this chunk needs an embedding."

## Wire-cost impact

| State | Before | After | Reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 stale chunks (autopilot common case) | ~76 MB | ~50 bytes | ~1,500,000× |
| 100 stale across 10 pages (post-rotation) | ~76 MB | ~150 KB | ~500× |
| 8K stale across 1.5K pages (cold start) | ~76 MB | ~12 MB | ~6× |

## Functional contract preserved

The fix preserves the existing contract — every chunk where the embedding is missing still gets embedded; nothing is skipped; non-stale chunks on partially-stale pages are NOT lost. Code-flow proof:

1. `embed --stale`'s only side effect is "for every chunk where the embedding is NULL, call `embedBatch` and write back via `upsertChunks` with the new embedding (and `embedded_at = now()`)". Verified by reading `src/commands/embed.ts:216-308`.
2. New chunks for new pages are **never** introduced by `embedAll`. They're added by `importFromContent` (`src/core/import-file.ts:99-154`) which chunks AND embeds inline before the DB transaction commits — verified by tracing `gbrain sync`, `gbrain import`, and MCP `put_page` paths. `embed --stale`'s only role is the defensive sweep for chunks that lack an embedding.
3. The new path preserves non-stale chunks on partially-stale pages: it re-fetches the full chunk set for each stale slug and passes it to `upsertChunks`, with `embedding: undefined` for non-stale chunks (which the engine's existing `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.embedding, content_chunks.embedding)` clause leaves untouched).

## Bonus consistency fix in `upsertChunks`

While tracing the staleness predicate, found a quiet bookkeeping bug in both `postgres-engine.ts` and `pglite-engine.ts`: when `chunk_text` changes and no new embedding is supplied, the existing CASE clause correctly clears `embedding` to NULL — but `embedded_at` was set via `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.embedded_at, content_chunks.embedded_at)` which kept the old timestamp. That left rows with `embedding IS NULL` but `embedded_at IS NOT NULL` — making any staleness predicate on `embedded_at` silently miss them.

Fixed at write time: when text changes and no new embedding is supplied, both columns reset to NULL together. This is why the new staleness predicate uses `embedding IS NULL` (truth source today, even on databases written before this fix) and the consistency fix keeps both columns honest going forward.

## Migration impact

None. No schema changes, no DB migration, no backfill, no config file changes. `embedded_at` and `embedding` have been on `content_chunks` since v1 of the schema (`src/schema.sql:79-94`); no version of gbrain in the wild lacks them.

## Risk / things to look at in review

- **`upsertChunks` re-fetch on partially-stale pages:** the new path re-fetches `getChunks(slug)` per slug so it can preserve non-stale chunks through the upsert. This costs one extra round-trip per stale slug. On a typical post-rotation case (10 stale slugs × ~5 KB existing chunks-without-embedding each = ~50 KB) this is negligible compared to the savings. Could be eliminated in a follow-up by adding a `partialUpdate: boolean` flag to `upsertChunks` that skips the implicit DELETE step.
- **Behavioral change for `--stale` callers when count==0:** the previous code emitted "Embedded 0 chunks across N pages"; the new code emits "Embedded 0 chunks (0 stale found)". Searching the repo confirms only `test/embed.test.ts` matched the old wording; updated.
- **`--all` path is byte-identical to before** — explicit regression test added.
- **`listStaleChunks` LIMIT 100000:** identical to the existing `listPages({ limit: 100000 })` cap. Brains with >100K stale chunks (extremely rare; would only happen post-mass-rotation or post-restore-without-embeddings) won't be fully drained on a single call but will converge over multiple runs since each run embeds and clears 100K. Pagination param can be added later if needed.

## Tests

Added to `test/embed.test.ts` (4 new):
- `zero stale chunks: countStaleChunks short-circuits, listPages never called` — proves the egress fix.
- `N stale chunks across M pages: only stale slugs re-fetched, exact stale set embedded, non-stale chunks preserved` — proves correctness + the merge logic doesn't wipe fresh chunks (this is the regression risk).
- `--stale dry-run: counts stale via countStaleChunks, reports via listStaleChunks, no embedBatch or upsertChunks`.
- `--all (non-stale) path is byte-identical: walks listPages and embeds every chunk` — regression guard for backwards compat.

Updated existing `--stale` tests to mock `countStaleChunks` + `listStaleChunks` for the new path. Test counts: 11 pass / 0 fail in `test/embed.test.ts`. Full suite: 2422 pass; one pre-existing flake in `test/e2e/minions-shell-pglite.test.ts` (mock module ordering issue) confirmed present on stock master before this PR.

## Reference

Empirical incident: Supabase 102 GB used / 5 GB free-tier ceiling = 2058% on 2026-04-24. Same bandwidth pattern as 2026-04-19. Three independent investigations (manual code read, GPT-via-Codex audit, clean-room subagent) converged on the same bug + same fix.

title: ci: Tier 1 runs all 20 E2E files; fix three test fragilities
body:
Hi! I've been running `bun run test:e2e` end-to-end locally against a Docker test container while working on a fork, and surfaced three classes of fixable bugs that don't show up in the current CI workflow because Tier 1 only runs 2 of the 20 E2E files. This PR fixes all of them.

## Summary of changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` | Tier 1 now runs every `test/e2e/*.test.ts` via `bun run test:e2e` (was 2 files). `GBRAIN_ALLOW_SHELL_JOBS=1` added so `minions-shell.test.ts` can register its handler. |
| `test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts` | Fix `init --non-interactive without URL` (Bun .env auto-load) + fix `v24 self-heals` (stale version literal). |
| `test/init-migrate-only.test.ts` | Same Bun .env auto-load fix. |
| `test/skillpack-check.test.ts` | Same Bun .env auto-load fix. |
| `.env.testing.example` | Added `GBRAIN_ALLOW_SHELL_JOBS=1` with explanation. |

## The bugs

### 1. Tier 1 ran 2 of 20 E2E files

`.github/workflows/e2e.yml` listed only `mechanical.test.ts + mcp.test.ts`. The other 18 mechanical files (cycle.test.ts, sync.test.ts, upgrade.test.ts, minions-shell.test.ts, etc.) were never exercised in CI. **Result: green CI was a partial gate.** Switching to `bun run test:e2e` (which iterates every `test/e2e/*.test.ts` via `scripts/run-e2e.sh`) makes CI = local; new E2E files added later get picked up automatically.

`GBRAIN_ALLOW_SHELL_JOBS=1` added to the Tier 1 env because `test/e2e/minions-shell.test.ts` needs it (the shell handler refuses to register otherwise). Safe in the CI runner against the ephemeral postgres service.

### 2. Bun .env auto-load defeats env-deletion tests

Three test files (mechanical, init-migrate-only, skillpack-check) delete `DATABASE_URL` from the spawned subprocess env to test "no config" paths. But Bun auto-loads `.env` from cwd, and the spawn used `cwd: project_root`. Result: the deleted env vars get re-injected from project `.env`, defeating the test. **CI passes** because CI runners have no `.env` at project root. **Local runs fail** on every developer machine that has a `.env`.

Fix: spawn with `cwd: '/tmp'` (no `.env` there) and pass `src/cli.ts` as an absolute path so script resolution is cwd-independent. The bug-fix pattern is the same in all three files.

### 3. `v24 self-heals` test asserts exact version literal `'24'`

After rolling schema version back to 23 and re-triggering initSchema, the test asserts the resulting version is exactly `'24'`. That's correct when v24 is the latest migration, but the next time anyone adds v25, the rollback-and-replay advances to LATEST_VERSION (>=25), not 24. The literal is a time bomb.

Fix: assert `version >= 24`. The intent ("v24 ran cleanly without 42P01") is preserved; the assertion is robust to any future migration.

### 4. `.env.testing.example` missing `GBRAIN_ALLOW_SHELL_JOBS`

`test/e2e/minions-shell.test.ts` requires `GBRAIN_ALLOW_SHELL_JOBS=1` to even register the handler. Without it the test silently fails because the worker rejects the job as "shell handler disabled." Adding to `.env.testing.example` with an explanatory comment so contributors don't trip on it.

## Validation

- `bun test test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts test/init-migrate-only.test.ts test/skillpack-check.test.ts`: **87/87 pass**
- Diff is 49 insertions / 8 deletions across 5 files; no algorithm changes, all test infrastructure / CI workflow.

## Why these went undetected for so long

The CI workflow shape masked them. With Tier 1 running just 2 files, files like minions-shell.test.ts were never executed by CI, so the missing `GBRAIN_ALLOW_SHELL_JOBS` flag never produced a failing run. Similarly, the .env auto-load fragility doesn't fire in CI environments because they lack `.env`. The fix that stops this entire class of bug is the workflow change to run all 20 files; the others are downstream cleanups that get the new tests to actually pass.

Happy to split into separate PRs if you'd prefer per-bug review. Or merge all together — your call.

title: feat: Shippable Standard quality framework — 6-gate enforcement for shipping changes
body:
## Summary

Introduces a 6-gate quality framework that runs as `bun run preship` to enforce the contract CLAUDE.md "Pre-ship requirements" already documents but doesn't execute. Catches a class of bugs that escape current review (missing schema_version, empty catches, re-promotion duplicates, silent multi-minute ops, etc.).

This is companion to a separate test/CI fix PR I'm also opening. **That one should land first** — this PR's E2E stage assumes Tier 1 has a healthy test surface, which the companion fixes.

## The 6 gates

| # | Gate | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **CONTRACT** | schema_version on public types, edge cases documented, named constants for caps/limits |
| 2 | **IDEMPOTENCY** | mutating ops are duplicate-safe across reruns |
| 3 | **OBSERVABILITY** | bulk ops report progress, errors are structured, no empty catches |
| 4 | **INTEGRATION** | composes into existing primitives (BrainEngine, runCycle, Minions, progress.ts), no engine bypass |
| 5 | **PROOF** | tested on real production-shape data, not just unit fixtures |
| 6 | **SCOPE** | docstrings match actual behavior, claims about security/performance honestly bounded |

`quality/criteria.md` is the source of truth. The runner (`scripts/check-shippable.sh`) handles the gates that reduce to deterministic checks (multi-line empty-catch detection via awk, missing schema_version on `Report` types, raw SQL outside engine implementations); `skills/pre-ship-check/SKILL.md` is the agent skill that handles the judgment-based gates (PROOF, SCOPE, architectural INTEGRATION).

## What ships

- `quality/criteria.md` — the 6-gate spec
- `scripts/check-shippable.sh` — bash 3.2-compatible static gate runner with **line-level diff awareness** (only flags lines ADDED in current diff, not pre-existing content in modified files) and **upstream-byte-identical exemption** (downstream forks inherit upstream's quality)
- `scripts/preship-e2e.sh` — E2E runner. Auto-sources `.env.testing`. Three paths: existing `DATABASE_URL`, Docker auto-spin (ports 5434-5437), skip-loud. Refuses Supabase URLs (E2E truncates tables)
- `skills/pre-ship-check/SKILL.md` — the agent skill that walks the gates
- `package.json` — `bun run preship` (full chain), `preship:gate-only` (fast)

## Why this matters

- **Shippable code is a property of the codebase, not a property of any single agent's discipline.** CLAUDE.md says "agents should run E2E before shipping." That's documentation; this PR makes it executable.
- The static gate alone has caught real bugs in development on a fork: a re-promotion bug from naive `compiled_truth` concatenation; missing `schema_version` on a Report type; empty catch swallowing per-page errors. All three would have shipped without the gate.
- The framework's own diff passes its own gate (self-checking).

## Override flags

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GBRAIN_SHIPPABLE_FULL_FILE=1` | Flag every issue in changed files, not just newly-added lines (audit mode for cleaning inherited debt) |
| `GBRAIN_NO_UPSTREAM_EXEMPT=1` | Disable upstream-byte-identical exemption (for upstream-bound PRs where you DO want to clean inherited patterns before submitting) |
| `GBRAIN_PRESHIP_SKIP_E2E=1` | Skip E2E (cosmetic-only PRs) |
| `GBRAIN_PRESHIP_REQUIRE_E2E=1` | Fail-loud when E2E can't run (CI environments) |

## Validation

- [x] Self-check on this PR's diff: 0 blocking, 0 warnings
- [x] `bun run preship:gate-only`: clean
- [x] The chain works end-to-end against a Postgres test container in author's local dev environment

## Notes

- The line-level diff awareness uses `git diff --unified=0` and parses hunk bodies line-by-line (NOT the hunk header counts, which include context lines). This means the gate doesn't bark on pre-existing patterns in files you happen to touch — important for files like `src/core/cycle.ts` that have long-standing intentional empty catches.
- The upstream-byte-identical exemption is dormant on this repo (`upstream/master` ref doesn't exist on `garrytan/gbrain`) but useful for downstream forks. Doesn't add complexity; harmless on the upstream itself.
- 806 insertions / 0 deletions: pure addition. No existing code modified.

Happy to discuss naming (Shippable Standard? Quality Gate? something else?) and the framework's location (`/quality/` vs alternative).

title: feat: dream-cycle — episodic-to-semantic promotion as runCycle phase 7
body:
## Summary

Adds nightly promotion of recurring timeline patterns to `compiled_truth`. Composes into `runCycle` as **phase 7 of 7** (`phase: 'promotion'`). Two callers reach the engine: the new `gbrain dream-cycle` CLI for manual one-off runs with custom config knobs, and `runCycle`'s own pipeline for autopilot/scheduled runs.

This is the largest of three companion PRs. **Recommended to land #410 (CI fixes) and #411 (Shippable Standard) first** for review-load reasons; technically each is independent.

## Why this is interesting

The dream-cycle "the agent runs while I sleep, the brain wakes up smarter" intent already lives in CLAUDE.md and the existing `gbrain dream` command. This PR completes the loop: `dream` does maintenance (lint/sync/extract/embed/orphans); `dream-cycle` does **synthesis** (consolidating recurring patterns from the timeline into compiled_truth). Both phases live in `runCycle`, so autopilot picks up promotion automatically.

## Algorithm

**Deterministic + cached embeddings.** Phase 1 of the algorithm has zero LLM calls; the only model interaction is embedding generation, which is cached.

1. `collectEvidence` walks pages (capped at `MAX_PAGES_TO_SCAN=500`), pulls last `evidenceWindowDays` of timeline entries, normalizes summaries.
2. Embeds unique normalized texts via cached lookup. New text → `embedBatch` → cache → return. Existing text → cache hit. A 1500-summary brain stays sub-cent on `text-embedding-3-large` after the first run.
3. Clusters via cosine similarity union-find. Default threshold 0.85, configurable via `PromotionConfig.similarityThreshold`. Two summaries that mean the same thing ("ai concierge launch prep" vs "ai concierge ready to launch") cluster together. Cluster's most-recent member text becomes the canonical pattern.
4. Falls back to exact-text grouping if embedding API fails OR if v25 migration hasn't been applied yet.

**Idempotency** via `dream_cycle_promotions` (v26): SHA256(cluster_id || target_slug) primary key. `applyPromotions` checks before writing; `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is belt-and-braces against concurrent races. A re-run with identical clusters produces zero duplicate writes.

## What ships

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `src/core/promotion.ts` | 735 (new) | Promotion engine: clustering, scoring, application, fallbacks |
| `src/commands/dream-cycle.ts` | 106 (new) | CLI runner for manual one-off promotion runs |
| `src/core/cycle.ts` | +119 | Wires `'promotion'` into `CyclePhase` / `ALL_PHASES` / `NEEDS_LOCK_PHASES` + `runPhasePromotion` + Phase 7 dispatch + `patterns_promoted` total |
| `src/core/migrate.ts` | +99 | v25 (`timeline_summary_embeddings`), v26 (`dream_cycle_promotions`), v27 (RLS for both) |
| `src/cli.ts` | +11 | `dream-cycle` command in `CLI_ONLY` set |
| `test/promotion.test.ts` | 294 (new) | 28 tests: normalization, scoring, cosine similarity, clustering, ranking, candidate scoring |
| `test/autopilot.test.ts` | 46 (new) | 9 tests for `shouldRunDreamCycle` rate-limit |
| `test/e2e/cycle.test.ts` | +7 | Phase count assertion: `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(6)` (was hardcoded `6`) |

**1417 insertions / 6 deletions across 8 files.** No existing functionality changed; only additions and one robustness fix to the cycle phase-count assertion.

## Security: sensitive-text filter is honestly bounded

`looksLikePhoneOrIdShape` is a 5-pattern regex filter (phone, SSN, ID shapes, "patient X" phrasing, MM/DD/YYYY dates). The function name + module comment explicitly state what it is and isn't:

- **What it IS**: best-effort defense-in-depth against the most-obvious leaks of phone/SSN/ID into `compiled_truth`
- **What it is NOT**: a PHI detector, a HIPAA control, a PII detector

Real PHI redaction needs named-entity recognition (Microsoft Presidio, healthcare NLP) and a model trained on medical text. The function is preserved as `looksLikePhi` (deprecated alias) for backward compatibility but the honest name is what the new code uses.

## Schema migrations (all idempotent, additive)

| v | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 25 | `timeline_summary_embeddings` | Cache table for embeddings + ivfflat cosine_ops index |
| 26 | `dream_cycle_promotions` | Idempotency key table + indexes on target_slug, cluster_id, promoted_at |
| 27 | `rls_for_dream_cycle_tables` | `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on both new tables. Same gating pattern as v24's RLS backfill. Internal cycle-state tables should not be readable by the Supabase anon key |

## Validation

- [x] **43/43 tests pass** across promotion.test.ts (28), autopilot.test.ts (9), and cycle.test.ts E2E (6)
- [x] Typecheck clean
- [x] **Real-data validation**: live dry-run on production-shape brain data correctly merged near-duplicate meeting summaries (e.g. three variations of "AI concierge launch on April 27" → cluster of size 3)
- [x] Migration v25/v26/v27 applied successfully on test container, verified RLS check now reports all internal tables enabled

## Notes for reviewers

- Threshold tuning (default 0.85 cosine, 3-recurrence, 14-day window) was set by intuition not by evaluation. On real brain data with mostly-one-off meeting summaries, the defaults produce zero promotables — the clustering correctly merges similar text but the recurrence threshold is too strict for that workload. **Tuning is a separate algorithmic concern**; this PR delivers the mechanism, not the optimal defaults.
- The first-slug targeting in `applyPromotions` (always promote the cluster to its first slug) is acknowledged as iteration-order-dependent. A future improvement could pick the most-cited target or split promotion across all cluster members.
- Pure addition: no existing public APIs changed, no existing tests rewritten, no behavior altered for users not invoking `dream-cycle` or running runCycle's `promotion` phase.

Open to algorithmic feedback — particularly on default thresholds, the clustering algorithm choice, and whether you'd prefer the integration shape to look different.

title: MCP serve: stdin=/dev/null causes lock contention after gateway restart
body:
## Problem

When OpenClaw gateway restarts, it spawns a new `gbrain serve` MCP server process via the MCP config. However, the stdin of the new process is connected to /dev/null instead of a proper stdio pipe. This causes:

1. The serve process becomes unresponsive (stdin is /dev/null)
2. It still holds the PGLite database lock
3. Subsequent CLI commands (sync, etc.) timeout waiting for the lock

## Reproduction

1. Start gateway with gbrain MCP server configured
2. Restart gateway (SIGUSR1 or restart command)
3. Observe multiple `gbrain serve` processes - the older one(s) have stdin=/dev/null
4. gbrain sync fails with "Timed out waiting for PGLite lock"

## Root Cause

The MCP server spawn mechanism in OpenClaw does not properly handle stdio for long-running server processes. When gateway restarts, it starts a new serve process but the old one does not get cleaned up properly and stdin gets redirected to /dev/null.

## Workaround

A singleton wrapper script can detect and kill stale processes.

## Environment

- gbrain: latest from git
- Platform: Linux (Docker container)
- Database: PGLite at ~/.gbrain/brain.pglite
- OpenClaw: v2026.4.23
