title: Korean filename slug flattening drops Korean characters and causes file collisions on import
body:
**GBrain version**. 0.20.4

**Symptom**

Importing a vault that mixes Korean (Hangul) titles, numeric prefixes, and English words into GBrain (Postgres backend) silently drops 34% of files and severely degrades wikilink resolution.

In my case the vault has 1,099 markdown files but `gbrain stats` only reports `Pages: 727` after `gbrain import`, with no error in the import log. The remaining 372 files (34%) are silently lost.

## Reproduction

Create a vault directory with files like:

```
30_📄permanent_notes/
  206 어떻게 허원님을 배울까.md
  304 CEO.md
  408 Personal Knowledge Management.md
  502 Method.md
10_project_notes/12_questions/
  201 Mk1.md
  202 Mk4.md
  206.md          <-- short variant
```

Run `gbrain import <path> --no-embed` then `gbrain embed --stale`.

## What happens

### A. File loss (silent)

Multiple files in the same directory whose Korean portions of the title are stripped collide on the same slug, so only the last one survives.

Example slugs after import:
- `206 어떻게 허원님을 배울까.md` → slug `10_project_notes/12_questions/206` (Korean dropped)
- `206.md` (different file in the same folder) → slug `10_project_notes/12_questions/206`
- → second `INSERT` either replaces the first or is silently skipped, no log entry

In my vault this collision pattern accounts for 372 missing pages (34% loss), including high-value notes such as `허원`, `구요한`, `📖 200 Literature`, `408 Personal Knowledge Management`, `글쓰기 워크플로우`, `CMDS Guide`.

### B. Wikilink resolution near-zero

Even for files that survive, body wikilinks fail to match because the resolver compares the wikilink display text (e.g. `[[206 어떻게 허원님을 배울까]]`) against the flattened slug (`10_project_notes/12_questions/206`) and finds nothing.

In my graph: 990 body wikilink attempts → 133 resolved (13%). The other 857 fall to dangling.

### C. Frontmatter `axis` field unsupported

The Korean ZK convention often uses an `axis:` frontmatter field whose value is a wikilink, e.g.:

```yaml
axis: "[[304 CEO]]"
```

The current `FRONTMATTER_LINK_MAP` (`src/core/link-extraction.ts:519` or equivalent compiled location) only recognizes `key_people`, `attendees`, `investors`, `sources`, `related`, `see_also`. The Korean ZK system treats `axis` as a structural primary link; without it, frontmatter-driven graph signal disappears entirely.

## Why it matters

For Korean (and presumably Japanese, Chinese, Cyrillic) users, this is not a soft preference. With the current behavior:

- 34% of pages are silently dropped (no warning, no JSON report)
- Body wikilink coverage drops from ~90% expected to 13%
- `gbrain doctor` reports `brain_score 45/100` and `graph_coverage 4%` even when the user has rich frontmatter linkage
- `gbrain extract links --source db` returns 0 created links and gives no diagnostic

A user has no way to discover this without instrumenting the DB directly.

## Proposed fixes

### Fix 1. Slug generation should preserve uniqueness, not flatten + collide

Two options that should both ship:

(a) **Romanize Korean characters** instead of replacing with `_`. e.g. via a hangul → revised romanization library, so `206 어떻게 허원님을 배울까` → `206-eotteohge-heowonnimeul-baeulkka`.

(b) **Optional LLM-translate slug** during import for non-ASCII title segments. Cost on Haiku is ~$0.50 per 1,000 titles. Cache results to avoid retranslating on subsequent imports. Preserve numeric/English prefixes verbatim, only translate the non-ASCII portion. Result: `206-how-to-learn-from-heowon`.

Either way, the slug generator must guarantee in-folder uniqueness; if a collision is detected, append a deterministic suffix (`-2`, `-3`) and emit a warning to stderr so the user can find it.

### Fix 2. Wikilink resolver should consult a display-name → slug mapping

Build a one-time mapping during import (`title` field → `slug`) and persist it. The link extractor's `resolveSlug` should look up wikilink display text in this mapping before giving up.

### Fix 3. `FRONTMATTER_LINK_MAP` should be configurable

Add user-extensible map config, e.g. in `gbrain config`:

```yaml
frontmatter_link_fields:
  - axis
  - Links
  - related
  - see_also
  ... (existing)
```

So vault-specific conventions can be honored without core patches.

### Fix 4. Import should emit a JSON skip report

When a file is dropped due to slug collision (or any other reason), log it to a structured report at `~/.gbrain/import-skipped-<timestamp>.json` so users can detect the loss.

## Workaround I'm using

I built a Python sidecar that:
1. Walks the vault filesystem directly
2. Detects pages missing from GBrain DB (LEFT JOIN on title/path)
3. Inserts the missing pages with manually-translated slugs (numeric prefix preserved, Korean → English via Haiku)
4. Maintains a separate display-name → slug mapping for wikilink resolution
5. Inserts links directly into the `links` table

This restored my graph_coverage from 0% → 60% but it's clearly not the right place to live; this should be in core.

## Environment

- macOS 26.2 arm64
- Bun 1.3.13
- Node 24.15
- GBrain 0.20.4
- Supabase Postgres
- vault: ~1,099 Korean Obsidian notes with numeric ZK prefixes and Korean+English titles

title: Feature request: `gbrain serve` idle timeout (auto-exit after inactivity)
body:
Hi Garry,

I'm running gbrain 0.16.4 as an MCP server inside OpenClaw with multiple agents. Love the tool — the PGLite + vector search combo is exactly what I need.

**Problem I'm hitting:**

When `gbrain serve` is spawned as a stdio MCP server, each agent session forks a new `gbrain serve` process. The issue is that these processes never exit on their own — even after the parent session ends or the gateway restarts. Over the course of a day, I ended up with **41 zombie `gbrain serve` processes** all competing for the same PGLite database, which caused connection timeouts (30s) for new sessions.

**What I'd love to see:**

An idle timeout option for `gbrain serve`, similar to how Ollama handles model unloading with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE`:

```bash
# Exit automatically after 5 minutes of no MCP requests
gbrain serve --idle-timeout 300

# Or via config
gbrain config set serve.idleTimeout 300
```

The idea is simple:
1. `gbrain serve` starts → begins accepting MCP requests via stdio
2. After each request completes → reset an idle timer
3. If no requests come in for N seconds → gracefully exit (release PGLite locks, free memory)
4. The MCP host (OpenClaw/Claude Desktop/etc.) will fork a fresh instance when needed

This follows the same pattern as Ollama's resource management — the caller uses it, and when it's done, the resource gets released. If the caller forgets to clean up, the service cleans up after itself.

**Current workaround:**

I wrote a cron job that kills `gbrain serve` processes older than 30 minutes. Works but it's a band-aid.

**Environment:**
- gbrain 0.16.4, PGLite engine
- OpenClaw 2026.4.22, 14 agents, each can trigger MCP
- macOS, Apple M1 Max, 32GB RAM

Thanks for building gbrain — it's become core infrastructure for my AI team. Happy to test if you ship a beta with this feature.

title: v0.22.1 autopilot fix wave — 5 prod hotfixes (#417, #403, #406, #363, #409)
body:
## Summary

Five production hotfixes shipping together as one release. Theme: **autopilot stops being a noisy neighbor.** GBrain's overnight maintenance loop was reading too much, ignoring abort signals, and quietly poisoning shared infrastructure when things went wrong. After this wave the loop only re-reads pages that changed, bails cleanly when timeouts fire, and recovers from connection-pool poisoning without manual intervention.

**For everyone (PGLite + Postgres):**
- **#417 incremental extract** — `gbrain dream` cycles no longer re-READ every markdown file when only a handful changed. The cycle still walks the directory tree to build the link-resolution set (a fast `readdir` pass), but `readFileSync` now runs only on pages sync flagged as added or modified. On a 54,461-page production brain this turned a 10-minute extract phase into a sub-second pass.
- **#403 cycle abort** — when a cycle phase hits a timeout, `runCycle` now bails at the next phase boundary instead of grinding through extract → embed → orphans while the worker thinks the job is done. A 30-second grace-then-evict safety net in `MinionWorker` frees the slot even if a future handler ignores the abort signal entirely.

**For Postgres / Supabase users (no-op on PGLite):**
- **#406 supervisor watchdog reconnect** — when the connection pool gets poisoned (PgBouncer rotation, Supabase pool bounce), the supervisor's watchdog now detects three consecutive health-check failures and calls `engine.reconnect()` to swap in a fresh pool. Workers crash cleanly on poisoned connections; supervisor catches it within ~3 minutes instead of staying degraded until manual restart.
- **#363 session timeouts** *(Contributed by @orendi84)* — every Postgres connection now sets `statement_timeout` and `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` as connection-time startup parameters. An orphaned pgbouncer backend can no longer hold a `RowExclusiveLock` for hours and block schema migrations. Closes #361.
- **#409 embed egress** *(Contributed by @atrevino47)* — `embed --stale` now filters server-side on `embedding IS NULL` instead of pulling every chunk's `vector(1536)` over the wire. On a fully-embedded 1.5K-page brain that's the difference between ~76 MB per call and a single `count()` round-trip. One production user blew past Supabase's 5 GB free-tier ceiling at 102 GB used; that pattern is gone now.

**Eng-review tightening (D3):** the original #406 wrapped `executeRaw` in a per-call retry that auto-recovered from connection errors. Codex showed the SQL-prefix regex isn't a safe idempotence boundary (writable CTEs, side-effecting SELECTs). The wrapper was dropped. What ships from #406 is the structural reconnect path; recovery moved up to the supervisor watchdog. See `TODOS.md` for the planned caller-opt-in retry follow-up.

**Version note:** Released as v0.22.1 (MINOR jump from master's 0.21.0) instead of the originally-planned 0.21.1. The wave's scope spans 5 production fixes, behavioral changes in cycle / extract / embed / supervisor, and 15 backfilled regression tests. MINOR is the honest signal.

15 new test cases across 3 files, ~290 LOC, all PGLite/in-memory:

- `test/extract-incremental.test.ts` (NEW, 8 cases for #417): empty/undefined slugs, [a,b]-only reads, deleted-file handling, mode filter, dry-run, BATCH_SIZE flush, full-slug-set resolution.
- `test/core/cycle.test.ts` (4 new cases for #417 + Codex F2): cycle threads `pagesAffected` into extract, full-walk fallback, F2 noExtract gating (full cycle vs sync-only).
- `test/connection-resilience.test.ts` (3 new cases for D3): `executeRaw` is single-statement passthrough, `reconnect()` still exists, supervisor still has 3-strikes path.

Tests at parity with master: 24 unit failures observed = same set master has (pre-existing parallel-PGLite-timeout flakiness; passes when run individually). E2E: 22 files, 20 passed, 2 pre-existing failures (also fail on master alone). **Wave introduces zero new failures.**

## Outside Voice (Codex)

Ran during planning. Codex caught 8 issues the inside review missed — all 8 resolved before landing:
- F1: #417 overclaim (cycle still walks directory) — CHANGELOG reframed
- F2: Step 4 silent-extract-removal — `noExtract` gated on `phases.includes('extract')`

title: apply-migrations cannot bootstrap brains older than v17: init --migrate-only references pages.source_id before v0.18.0 has added the column
body:
## Suggested labels

- `bug`
- `migrations`
- `bootstrap`
- `priority/high` (blocks all upgrades from <v17 schemas)

---

## Summary

A brain on schema version 4 cannot be migrated to schema version 24 using
`gbrain apply-migrations`. The first migration in the queue (v0.11.0) calls
`gbrain init --migrate-only` as its Phase A. The current `src/schema.sql`
unconditionally references `pages.source_id` (added by migration v0.18.0,
which hasn't run yet on a v4 brain), so Phase A fails with
`column "source_id" does not exist` and the entire migration ladder is
blocked. This is a chicken-and-egg between the latest-schema bootstrap and
the per-version migration ladder.

Anyone with a brain that pre-dates v17 (i.e. shipped before multi-source
support landed in v0.18.0) is stuck on their current schema until this is
fixed.

## Environment

- gbrain version: **0.20.4** (CLI binary)
- DB: Supabase Postgres (pgvector + pg_trgm + pgcrypto), pgbouncer on :6543
- Starting schema_version: **4**
- Target schema_version: **24**
- Pages: 564 (intact, no data loss)
- macOS, bun installation

## Reproduction

On any brain with `schema_version < 17`:

```bash
gbrain --version       # 0.20.4
gbrain doctor          # reports schema_version=4, latest=24, queue_health warns "minion_jobs does not exist"
gbrain apply-migrations --dry-run   # lists 9 migrations from v0.11.0 → v0.18.1
gbrain apply-migrations --yes       # fails on the first migration
```

Outcome: every migration after v0.11.0 stays `pending`; v0.11.0 is marked
`partial`. Re-running produces the same failure.

## Full failure log

```
=== Applying migration v0.11.0: GBrain Minions — durable background agents ===
NOTICE: extension "vector" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: extension "pg_trgm" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: extension "pgcrypto" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "pages" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "idx_pages_type" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "idx_pages_frontmatter" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "idx_pages_trgm" already exists, skipping
column "source_id" does not exist
Phase A (schema) failed: Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only. Aborting; re-run after fixing.
Migration v0.11.0 reported status=failed.
```

`apply-migrations --list` after the failure:

```
Status   Version   Headline
-------  --------  -----------------------------------------
partial  0.11.0    GBrain Minions — durable background agents
pending  0.12.0    Knowledge Graph wires itself
pending  0.12.2    Postgres frontmatter queries — JSONB double-encode bug fixed
pending  0.13.0    Frontmatter becomes a graph
pending  0.13.1    BrainWriter integrity + grandfather protection
pending  0.14.0    Shell jobs + autopilot cooperative handler
pending  0.16.0    Durable LLM agents
pending  0.18.0    Multi-source brains
pending  0.18.1    Row Level Security hardened on all public tables
```

`doctor --fast` after the failure now reports a new failing check:

```
[FAIL] minions_migration: MINIONS HALF-INSTALLED (partial migration: 0.11.0)
```

## Root cause

`src/schema.sql` (gbrain v0.20.4) creates an index on `pages.source_id`
before the column has been introduced by the per-version migration ladder:

```sql
-- src/schema.sql:48
-- v0.18.0 (Step 2): pages.source_id scopes each row to a sources(id) row.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (
  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  source_id     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'
                REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ...
);

-- src/schema.sql:74
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
```

`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages` is a no-op on an existing pre-v17 brain
because `pages` already exists. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS
idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id)` then runs unconditionally, but
`pages.source_id` does not exist on the existing table — failure.

The column is only added by the migration whose name is
`pages_source_id_composite_unique`:

```ts
// src/core/migrate.ts:605
{
  name: 'pages_source_id_composite_unique',
  // v0.18.0 Step 2 (Lane B) — adds pages.source_id. Engine-split after
  ...
  // src/core/migrate.ts:631
  ALTER TABLE pages ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT
    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'
    REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
}
```

Because every per-version migration calls `gbrain init --migrate-only` as
its Phase A, the failure occurs on **the first migration in the queue**
regardless of which migration logically introduced the column. No migration
in the ladder ever reaches its own Phase B/C/etc.

The same pattern affects `files.source_id` and `files.page_id`
(`src/schema.sql:255-282`) — same bootstrap-vs-ladder mismatch, will also
trip pre-v17 brains.

## Suggested fix (any one of these)

1. **Make `init --migrate-only` schema-version-aware.** Have it skip or
   conditionalise the source_id-dependent statements until the
   `pages_source_id_composite_unique` migration has been applied (or run a
   pre-flight check that adds the column if `schema_version < 17`).
2. **Wrap the source_id index creation in a DO block** that only runs when
   `pages.source_id` exists. e.g.:
   ```sql
   DO $$
   BEGIN
     IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
                WHERE table_name='pages' AND column_name='source_id') THEN
       CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
     END IF;
   END $$;
   ```
   Same pattern for files indexes that depend on `source_id` / `page_id`.
3. **Hoist the `source_id` ADD COLUMN statements out of the per-version
   migration** and into `init --migrate-only` itself, so the column always
   exists by the time any per-version migration's Phase A runs. Then the
   per-version migration becomes a no-op for that step on already-bootstrapped
   brains.

Option 2 is the smallest, lowest-risk patch and matches the
`IF EXISTS` / `IF NOT EXISTS` defensiveness already used elsewhere in
`schema.sql`. Option 3 is the most architecturally clean.

## Workaround

Brain functions normally on schema v4 — query, sync, embed, frontmatter
search, and existing skills all work. **Integrations recipes that require
v24 features (minion_jobs, durable LLM agents, multi-source, auto-extracted
graph edges) will need to wait for the migration ladder to walk cleanly.**

For users who can't wait, a manual pre-add of the missing columns might
unblock the ladder, but I have not attempted this and don't recommend it
without upstream sign-off:

```sql
-- UNTESTED — not endorsed by upstream
ALTER TABLE pages ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default';
ALTER TABLE files ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default';
ALTER TABLE files ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
```

This bypasses the FK constraint to `sources(id)` (which the migration would
add). Risky on production data — file the bug, wait for a clean fix.

## Attached evidence (paste these as gist links or files when filing)

- `pre-doctor.json` — full pre-migration health output
- `migrations.log` — first attempt
- `migrations-retry-1.log` — second attempt (identical failure)
- `migrations-list.txt` — partial/pending state after failure
- `post-failed-migration-doctor.txt` — doctor output showing
  `MINIONS HALF-INSTALLED`
- `version-before.txt` — confirms binary 0.20.4

All available at the user's local
`~/gbrain-migration-2026-04-25/` directory.

## Severity

High — blocks all schema upgrades from any brain that pre-dates v17. Anyone
in that cohort cannot use post-v0.11 features (minion supervisor,
auto-graph extraction, durable LLM agents, multi-source, RLS

title: docs: incorrect code indexing command
body:
**What happened?**

The README currently tells users:

```bash
gbrain sources add <repo> --strategy code
```

but `sources add` does not support `--strategy`, so the documented command is invalid.

Separately, the current docs imply that `sync --strategy code` is enough to index a repo as code, but first/full sync still routes through the markdown importer, so the documented workflow does not work as written.

**What did you expect?**

The docs should either:

- describe the currently supported behavior accurately, or
- only document code-repo indexing once the underlying full-sync path actually supports it

At minimum, the docs should not suggest a `sources add --strategy code` flag that does not exist.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Read README instruction:
   ```text
   Run `gbrain sources add <repo> --strategy code` to index a repo
   ```
2. Run it
3. Observe `sources add` rejects `--strategy`
4. Try the implied alternative:
   ```bash
   gbrain sync --source <id> --strategy code
   ```

- gbrain version: (`0.21.0`, technically `0.22.0` but you didn't change the `package.json` version on release for that)
- OS: Linux

title: bug: code indexing doesn't work as expected (or at all)
body:
**What happened?**

Code indexing does not work correctly for source-based repo syncs.

There appear to be two related bugs:

1. `gbrain sync --source <id>` ignores `sources.config.strategy`
2. full / first sync still uses the markdown-only importer even when `--strategy code` is passed

In practice, this means a repo source configured for code indexing still reports:

```text
Running full import of /path/to/repo...
Found 19 markdown files
```

and no code symbols become queryable via `code-def` / `code-refs`.

**What did you expect?**

If a source is configured with `config.strategy = "code"`, then:

- `gbrain sync --source <id>` should honor that strategy automatically
- `gbrain sync --source <id> --strategy code` should perform a full code-aware sync on first/full sync
- code symbols from the repo should become available through `code-def`, `code-refs`, `code-callers`, and `code-callees`

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Register a repo source:
   ```bash
   gbrain sources add presswork --path /home/luna/code/presswork
   ```
2. Set `sources.config.strategy` for that source to `code` (or pass `--strategy code` explicitly to sync)
3. Run:
   ```bash
   gbrain sync --source presswork --strategy code
   ```
4. Observe output like:
   ```text
   Running full import of /home/luna/code/presswork...
   Found 19 markdown files
   ```
5. Check symbol retrieval:
   ```bash
   gbrain code-def <KnownSymbol>
   gbrain code-refs <KnownSymbol> --json
   ```
6. Observe that code symbols are missing / empty

**Environment**
- gbrain version: (`0.21.0`, technically `0.22.0` but you didn't change the `package.json` version on release for that)
- OS: Linux
- Bun version: (`1.3.13`)
- Database: self-hosted Postgres

title: v0.22.2 feat: minions worker reliability — RSS watchdog, cold-start retry, autopilot backpressure
body:
## Summary

Production minions worker has been freezing every few hours. RSS climbs 68 MB → ~15 GB over ~7 hours, the worker stops claiming jobs but never crashes (no OOM, no SIGSEGV), the cron keeps enqueuing autopilot-cycle jobs every 5 minutes into a queue nobody is draining, and within 2-3 hours the queue piles up to 28+ waiting jobs. Shell jobs in flight when the worker froze hit max_stalled and dead-letter, producing 18% shell-job failure rate over 24h.

This PR ships **three in-repo defenses** that close the cascade end-to-end. The underlying memory leak gets investigated separately (heap snapshots needed); the watchdog removes urgency.

**1. RSS watchdog (`src/core/minions/worker.ts`)**
- Per-job AND 60-second periodic check, so the watchdog still fires when every concurrency slot is wedged with zero job completions (the actual production freeze pattern)
- On trip, fires `shutdownAbort` + per-job aborts BEFORE `running=false`, so shell handlers run their SIGTERM→5s→SIGKILL cleanup on child processes and cooperative handlers bail instead of waiting out the 30s drain. Closes the zombie-shell-children gap a Codex review surfaced.
- Default 2048 MB on `gbrain jobs supervisor`; bare `gbrain jobs work` stays opt-in (`--max-rss N`) to preserve current behavior for embed/import workloads with legitimately large working sets
- `MinionWorkerOpts.getRss?: () => number` injection seam for fast deterministic tests

**2. `connectWithRetry()` for shared bootstrap (`src/core/db.ts` + `src/cli.ts`)**
- Wraps `engine.connect()` in `connectEngine()`, default-on across every DB-backed CLI command (autopilot, dream, jobs work, jobs supervisor, stats)
- 3 attempts with 1s/2s/4s backoff; 5-pattern transient-error matcher (auth failed, connection refused, db starting up, terminated unexpectedly, ECONNRESET); permanent errors do NOT retry
- Opt-out via `--no-retry-connect` or `GBRAIN_NO_RETRY_CONNECT=1`. Fixes PgBouncer cold-start auth races on autopilot/dream/jobs daemons

**3. `autopilot-cycle` backpressure + autopilot stable-run reset (`src/commands/autopilot.ts`)**
- Submits autopilot-cycle with `maxWaiting: 1` so the v0.19.1 `pg_advisory_xact_lock` coalesce path caps the queue at 1 active + 1 waiting; 3rd+ submission coalesces and writes a backpressure-audit JSONL line
- Autopilot's worker spawn loop now mirrors the supervisor's stable-run reset (5min uptime → reset crash count to 1) so hourly watchdog exits don't trip the 5-crash give-up threshold. Without this, 5 hours of healthy uptime would kill autopilot

## The numbers that matter

Production data from the 2026-04-25 incident, plus the watchdog defaults:

| Metric                                  | Before          | After (supervised path) |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------|-------------------------|
| Waiting-jobs pileup at freeze           | 28+             | 2 (capped at 1+1)       |
| Worker RSS at freeze                    | 14.8 GB         | ~2 GB self-terminate    |
| Time to detect freeze                   | hours (manual)  | ≤60s (periodic timer)   |
| Cold-start auth-fail recovery           | manual restart  | 3 attempts in ~7s       |

## Test Coverage

`test/minions.test.ts` adds 11 new cases:

**Watchdog (5 cases including the production-freeze-regression scenario):**
- ★★★ CRITICAL: periodic timer fires when zero jobs ever complete — handlers stay pending, mock RSS over threshold, watchdog calls gracefulShutdown, in-flight handlers see signal.aborted
- ★★★ Per-job check: handler completes → post-job RSS read trips → sibling in-flight job's signal.aborted goes true (cooperative bail, not stalled→dead)
- ★★★ shutdownAbort fires when watchdog trips (closes shell-handler zombie gap)
- ★★★ Below threshold: no-op, all jobs complete normally
- ★★★ maxRssMb=0 disables watchdog entirely

**connectWithRetry (6 cases):**
- isRetryableDbConnectError matches transient patterns (5 patterns)
- isRetryableDbConnectError rejects permanent errors (extension missing, syntax error, etc.)
- 1st rejects transient → 2nd succeeds → function returns
- 3 transient rejects → throws
- Permanent error does NOT retry (single attempt)
- noRetry option honored (single attempt)

**Supervisor argv (1 case):**
- `gbrain jobs supervisor` spawned worker has `--max-rss 2048` in argv by default

Tests for files modified by this branch: 176/176 pass.

## Pre-Landing Review

- `/plan-eng-review` — CLEAR (5 arch + 1 test-design issue, all resolved)
  - A1: watchdog needs periodic timer alongside per-job check (production-freeze coverage)
  - A2: graceful drain via this.stop(), not process.exit()
  - A3: cold-start retry at engine.connect() layer, not ensureSchema
  - A4: default --max-rss only on supervised path (this changed via B6 below)
  - A5: PR sequencing on #406's transient matcher (dropped via B4 below)
  - T1: getRss injection seam for testability
- `/codex` plan review — 6 additional findings (B1-B6) surfaced real bugs the eng review missed; all resolved Codex's way:
  - B1: graceful shutdown must fire shutdownAbort + per-job aborts (closes shell zombies)
  - B2: autopilot has separate spawn loop; needs its own stable-run reset
  - B3: connectWithRetry must wrap shared connectEngine, not just daemons
  - B4: own the predicate in db.ts (correct dependency direction); drop #406 sequencing
  - B5: maxWaiting:1, not 2 (queue counts only `status='waiting'`)
  - B6: do NOT default --max-rss on bare `gbrain jobs work` (preserve current behavior for legitimate large-memory workloads)

## TODOS deferred to follow-up

- Memory leak hunt — heap-snapshot investigation (the 40 MB/job leak itself, ~2-4h with `--inspect` + diff growing object classes)
- `tini` / `--init` documentation in `docs/guides/` for Render/Docker operators hitting zombie process accumulation
- Per-job memory delta logging (~5 LOC in `executeJob().finally()`) — diagnostic enabler for the leak hunt
- Worker heartbeat tracking (adjacent to existing `gbrain jobs stats --orphaned` TODO)

title: feat(embedding): support Azure OpenAI via env vars
body:
## Summary

When `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` is set in the environment, `getClient()` now constructs an `AzureOpenAI` client instead of the public `OpenAI` one. Behavior is unchanged for everyone else (AZURE env unset → original code path).

Env contract:

| var | required | default |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | yes (toggles Azure mode) | — |
| `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` | yes | — |
| `OPENAI_API_VERSION` | no | `2024-02-15-preview` |
| `AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DEPLOYMENT` | no | `text-embedding-3-large` |

The `AzureOpenAI` class is already a first-class export of `openai` (the SDK gbrain depends on), so this is zero new dependencies.

## Why

Many enterprises (healthcare, financial services, manufacturing) only get OpenAI access via Azure due to data residency / compliance. Today gbrain hard-codes `new OpenAI()` and there's no escape hatch, which blocks those users from `hybridSearch`'s embedding leg, brain-grade retrieval, and `gbrain doctor` health checks. This is the smallest additive change to unblock them.

Aligns with the resolver-registry refactor proposed in `docs/designs/KNOWLEDGE_RUNTIME.md` ("Refactor of `src/core/embedding.ts` into Resolver") — once the Resolver registry lands, this code can be ported as `resolvers/builtin/embedding/azure_openai.ts` alongside the OpenAI one. Until then, this small env-var dispatch unblocks the same use case.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run build` succeeds, no type errors
- [x] Default path (no AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT) is byte-identical behavior
- [x] AzureOpenAI path: smoke-tested constructor against a live `text-embedding-3-large` deployment (1536 dims)
- [ ] You may want to add a unit test asserting `getClient()` selects the right class based on env (happy to add if you want)

## Notes

- `AzureOpenAI` is imported as a named export alongside the default `OpenAI` import — same package, no SDK version bump needed.
- `client` type is widened to `OpenAI | AzureOpenAI`; the `embeddings.create` call site is unchanged because both classes expose the same `embeddings.create` shape.
- Default API version `2024-02-15-preview` chosen because it's the earliest stable version that supports the `dimensions` parameter on `text-embedding-3-large`. Users on older deployments can override via `OPENAI_API_VERSION`.

title: perf(engines): exclude embedding column from getChunks SELECT
body:
## Summary

Both `PostgresEngine.getChunks` and `PgliteEngine.getChunks` were issuing `SELECT cc.* FROM content_chunks cc JOIN pages …` and then handing every row to `rowToChunk(r)` — which defaults to `includeEmbedding=false` and immediately discards `row.embedding`. Every call ships ~6 KB per chunk (1536 floats × 4 bytes for `text-embedding-3-large` at default precision) of pgvector data across the wire just to throw it away.

## Why it matters

On managed Postgres deployments where the MCP server hits `getChunks` on every page read by an agent, this is the largest egress line item by far. Measured on one active brain:

| | Per call | Daily |
|---|---|---|
| Before (with `cc.*`) | ~21 KB | ~22 GB |
| After (named cols) | ~3 KB | ~3 GB |
| Δ | **~6×** | **~19 GB/day** |

Steady state for any brain with v0.10+ embed coverage. The 6 KB column was 100% wasted bytes — `rowToChunk(row)` (default args) doesn't read it.

## What changed

- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts` — `getChunks` enumerates the 16 columns `rowToChunk` actually consumes.
- `src/core/pglite-engine.ts` — same SELECT shape for engine-parity (and to skip wasted JS heap allocation through the postgres.js bridge).
- `getChunksWithEmbeddings` (the sibling method ~720 lines below in each file) keeps `SELECT cc.*` because it consumes the column.

## Column list maintenance

The SELECT mirrors what `rowToChunk()` reads in `src/core/utils.ts`: `id, page_id, chunk_index, chunk_text, chunk_source, model, token_count, embedded_at`, plus the v0.19.0 code-chunk metadata (`language, symbol_name, symbol_type, start_line, end_line`) and v0.20.0 Cathedral II additions (`parent_symbol_path, doc_comment, symbol_name_qualified`). Comment in the patch flags this so future column additions to `rowToChunk` get mirrored here.

If you want stronger guarantees, a `scripts/check-getchunks-columns.sh` CI guard along the lines of `scripts/check-jsonb-pattern.sh` would catch any future regression to `cc.*` in `getChunks`. Happy to follow up with that as a separate PR if you want.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/pglite-engine.test.ts` — 85/85 pass (full BrainEngine method coverage including chunk insertion, retrieval, embedding round-trips).
- [ ] E2E parity test against real Postgres (`test/e2e/engine-parity.test.ts`) — requires `DATABASE_URL`; not run in this branch but the SELECT shape is now identical between engines.
- [x] Manual verification on a 87 K-chunk brain: getChunks returns identical Chunk shape, search/retrieval flows unaffected.

title: fix(engines): run pending migrations before schema.sql snapshot on upgrade paths
body:
## Summary

`engine.initSchema()` runs `SCHEMA_SQL` first and `runMigrations()` second. That works on a fresh install — `SCHEMA_SQL` bootstraps everything at v(LATEST) shape, then `runMigrations` records `config.version` and fires handler-only side effects.

It **breaks every upgrade** across a release where `SCHEMA_SQL` added a partial-index or foreign-key reference to a column that a pending migration is responsible for adding. `SCHEMA_SQL` aborts on the forward reference, `runMigrations` is never reached, the brain is deadlocked at the previous version.

## How users hit this

Two majors in a row:

**v0.18.x.** `SCHEMA_SQL` added:
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_files_page_id   ON files(page_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_files_source_id ON files(source_id);
```
…while `pages.source_id` was first added by migration **v21** and the `files.*` columns by **v23**. Pre-v21 brains aborted with `column "source_id" does not exist`.

**v0.21.x.** `SCHEMA_SQL` added:
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_chunks_symbol_name
  ON content_chunks(symbol_name) WHERE symbol_name IS NOT NULL;
```
…while `content_chunks.symbol_name` was first added by migration **v26**. Pre-v26 brains aborted with `column "symbol_name" does not exist`.

Both releases left affected users with no path forward via `gbrain apply-migrations` — recovery required manual SQL surgery (apply pending migrations directly via psql / supabase MCP, manually bump `config.version`, then re-run `apply-migrations` so it fast-paths through). I just shipped that recovery for myself on the v0.20.4 → v0.22.0 upgrade and figured it was worth a structural fix.

## The fix

Swap the order on **existing brains**. `SCHEMA_SQL` is the *target* snapshot of v(LATEST); on a pre-LATEST brain some of its DDL is correctly not yet applicable. Running pending migrations first brings the schema to LATEST shape so `SCHEMA_SQL` becomes an idempotent `CREATE * IF NOT EXISTS` confirmation pass.

Detection uses `to_regclass('public.config')` — returns NULL for missing relations rather than raising, which keeps the probe cheap and avoids try/catch fragility. On a fresh install the config table doesn't exist yet, so the probe takes the original ordering (`SCHEMA_SQL` → `runMigrations`) which bootstraps everything from scratch. On an existing brain, config exists and we take the new ordering (`runMigrations` → `SCHEMA_SQL`).

Both engines patched. PGLite is in-memory so it doesn't bite users in the same way (every PGLite test starts from fresh-install state), but PGLite-backed brains that survive across `gbrain` upgrades are also affected.

## Test plan

- [x] **New regression test** — `test/regression-init-schema-forward-refs.test.ts`. Reconstructs the v0.21.x failure shape against PGLite: drops the `symbol_name` column + its partial index after a clean LATEST bootstrap, rolls `config.version` backwards to 25, re-runs `initSchema`. Without this fix, the second `initSchema` rejects at the `SCHEMA_SQL` step. With the fix, `runMigrations` re-adds the column via v26 before `SCHEMA_SQL`'s `CREATE INDEX` hits it. Verified that the test FAILS without the engine patches applied, PASSES with them. Plus a fresh-install path test and an idempotency test.
- [x] `bun test test/pglite-engine.test.ts` — 85/85 pass (full BrainEngine method coverage including the existing initSchema-in-beforeEach pattern).
- [x] `bun test test/migrate.test.ts` — 49/49 pass.
- [x] `bun test test/regression-init-schema-forward-refs.test.ts` — 3/3 pass.
- [ ] E2E against real Postgres (`test/e2e/`) — requires `DATABASE_URL`; not run in this branch but the postgres-engine code path is symmetric to PGLite's.

## Not in this PR

I considered making `SCHEMA_SQL` no longer contain forward-referencing CREATE INDEX statements (i.e., only the migration that adds the column knows about its index). That's a bigger refactor and changes the contract that `SCHEMA_SQL` is the v(LATEST) target — happy to discuss if you'd prefer that direction. The reorder fix in this PR is the minimal change that prevents the next major upgrade from biting the same way.

title: v0.23.0 feat: gbrain dream synthesizes conversations into brain pages (v0.23.0)
body:
## Summary

Extends `gbrain dream` from a 6-phase brain-maintenance cycle into an 8-phase one that consolidates yesterday's conversations into long-term memory. Two new phases run alongside the existing tidying:

**Synthesize** reads conversation transcripts (OpenClaw session corpus, meeting transcripts, ad-hoc files via `--input`) and writes brain-native pages: reflections at `wiki/personal/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-<hash[:6]>`, originals at `wiki/originals/ideas/...`, and timeline entries on existing people pages. Cheap Haiku verdicts cached in a new `dream_verdicts` table filter routine ops sessions before any Sonnet call. One subagent per worth-processing transcript, dispatched in parallel up to the rate-lease cap.

**Patterns** runs after `extract` (so the graph state is fresh) and surfaces recurring themes across recent reflections — when ≥3 reflections within `lookback_days` (default 30) mention the same motif, a pattern page is written to `wiki/personal/patterns/<theme>` citing every reflection that constitutes its evidence.

Phase order: `lint → backlinks → sync → synthesize → extract → patterns → embed → orphans`.

**Trust boundary** — subagent put_page calls are bounded to a path allow-list sourced from `skills/_brain-filing-rules.json`'s `dream_synthesize_paths.globs`. Even on prompt-injection success, writes are bounded to the allow-listed prefixes. The legacy `wiki/agents/<id>/...` namespace check stays the default for non-cycle subagents (regression guard).

**Idempotency** — slug includes content-hash suffix, so edited transcripts produce new files alongside the old (no silent overwrite). Idempotency key is `dream:synth:<file_path>:<content_hash>`. Cooldown via `dream.synthesize.last_completion_ts` config key (default 12h) bounds spend at ~\$1-2/day under autopilot.

**Provenance** — orchestrator collects slugs from `subagent_tool_executions` (NOT `pages.updated_at` — would pick up unrelated writes). Subagent never gets fs-write access; orchestrator does the dual-write at phase boundary.

title: v0.16.0+ migrations fail with `column "source_id" does not exist` when upgrading existing Postgres brain from v0.15.4
body:
**Summary**

`gbrain init` and `gbrain post-upgrade` both fail when upgrading an existing Postgres-backed brain from v0.15.4 (commit `fcf40a1`) to current master (commit `c78c3d0`, reporting version 0.22.2). The migration runner appears to execute pre-migration queries that reference columns added by later migrations, before those migrations have run. Result: schema is left at v15, no migrations 16–29 apply.

**Environment**

- gbrain: 0.22.2 (master tip, commit `c78c3d0`) — fails
- gbrain: 0.15.4 (commit `fcf40a1`) — works fine, current rollback target
- Engine: Postgres 17.9 (self-hosted Supabase on Hetzner)
- pgvector: 0.8.2
- pg_trgm, pgcrypto: present
- Install method: `bun add -g github:garrytan/gbrain`
- Brain size at time of upgrade attempt: 2,019 pages, 9,978 chunks, 1,921 links, 1,042 timeline entries
- Schema version on DB: 15 (per `gbrain post-upgrade` output: "Schema version 15 is behind latest 29")

**Reproduction**

1. Have an existing Postgres brain at schema v15 (i.e. successfully migrated to v0.15.4 last week using the standard `bun remove -g gbrain && bun add -g github:garrytan/gbrain && gbrain init && gbrain post-upgrade` flow).
2. Run `bun remove -g gbrain && bun add -g github:garrytan/gbrain` (pulls master, currently `c78c3d0`).
3. Run `gbrain init --url "$GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL"`.

**Observed**

```
Connecting to database...
Running schema migration...
[~8 NOTICE entries: "relation X already exists, skipping" — expected]
column "source_id" does not exist
```

`gbrain init` exits non-zero. No migrations applied.

Running `gbrain post-upgrade` produces the same root error wrapped in the migration orchestrator:

```
⚠️  Schema version 15 is behind latest 29.
   Schema migrations run automatically on next connectEngine() / initSchema().
   To run them now: gbrain init --migrate-only

=== Applying migration v0.16.0: Durable LLM agents land in the brain ... ===
=== v0.16.0 — Subagent runtime schema ===
[~8 NOTICE entries]
column "source_id" does not exist
Migration v0.16.0 reported status=failed.
```

**Root cause hypothesis**

The v0.16.0 migration's schema phase appears to issue a query that references `pages.source_id` or `files.source_id` before the v0.18.0 migration (`pages_source_id_composite_unique`, `files_source_id_page_id_ledger`) has run. These columns are introduced in:

- `src/core/migrate.ts:631`: `ALTER TABLE pages ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT ...`
- `src/core/migrate.ts:519`: `ALTER TABLE files ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT ...`

But the v0.16.0 migration is failing before reaching v0.18.0 in the sequence. This suggests either (a) a code path in initSchema/v0.16.0 that selects/filters on `source_id` unconditionally, or (b) migrations being executed out of declared order.

**Comparable prior incident (last week)**

Same pattern occurred a week ago when upgrading from v0.12.3 to v0.15.4: `gbrain init` failed with `column "link_source" does not exist` because the v0.13.0 migration (`links_provenance_columns`) hadn't applied. Workaround was to run the ALTER TABLE statements from `src/core/migrate.ts` lines 332–360 manually, then re-run `gbrain post-upgrade`, which then walked migrations 11–15 cleanly.

For v0.16.0+, the same workaround is impractical — it would require hand-running 14 migrations across multiple tables with composite foreign keys (`sources` table, `pages.source_id`, `files.source_id`, `pages_source_slug_key` constraint swap, etc.). Risk too high vs. benefit.

**Workaround**

Pin to v0.15.4 (`bun add -g github:garrytan/gbrain#fcf40a1`). All v0.16.0+ features are unavailable but the brain is fully operational at v0.15.4 schema.

**Suggested fixes (in order of preference)**

1. Audit the v0.16.0 migration entry path for any query referencing columns introduced in later migrations, and gate them behind a schema-version check.
2. Add an integration test that boots a Postgres brain at schema v15 (the v0.15.4 release schema) and verifies that `gbrain init` + `gbrain post-upgrade` walk it forward to schema v29 without error. This would have caught both this incident and the v0.13.0 `link_source` incident.
3. Tag releases (`git tag v0.15.4`, `v0.16.0`, etc.). Currently the repo has zero tags, which makes it impossible for users to pin to a known-stable version without spelunking through git log for commits whose messages mention versions. This is a meaningful contributor to migration breakage going undetected — there's no "last known good" marker.

**Verbose reproduction logs available on request.** Happy to attach the full `gbrain post-upgrade` output (including all PostgreSQL NOTICE/WARNING entries) if useful for triage.

title: fix(autopilot): cd into --repo so Bun auto-loads brain/.env
body:
## Symptom

Autopilot looks healthy. `gbrain autopilot --status` returns the cheerful `[cycle] score=N elapsed=1s next=150s` line. `autopilot.log` shows cycles dispatching every 5 minutes. `gbrain doctor` stays at 90/100. But `Embedded 0 chunks across N pages` on every cycle, and the real story is buried in `~/.gbrain/autopilot.err`:

```
Error embedding inbox/2026-04-23-...: The OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is missing or empty
Error embedding inbox/2026-04-23-...: The OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable is missing or empty
... (3.4 MB of these in my case, accumulated over weeks)
```

Per-page embed failures are caught and warn-logged rather than propagated, so the cycle exits status=success with `chunks_embedded: 0`. No healthcheck flags it. New pages stop being searchable; nothing tells you.

## Root cause

`writeWrapperScript()` (src/commands/autopilot.ts) generates this wrapper:

```bash
source ~/.zshrc 2>/dev/null || source ~/.bashrc 2>/dev/null || true
exec '...gbrain/src/cli.ts' autopilot --repo '/path/to/brain'
```

It sources the shell profile to pick up API keys exported there. That works for users who keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `~/.zshrc`. But Bun also auto-loads `.env` from CWD (the whole point of "no dotenv needed" in a Bun project), and many users put their gbrain secrets in `brain/.env` — alongside the brain content, not in shell-init. Since launchd starts the wrapper with CWD = `/` or `$HOME` (not `--repo`), Bun's auto-load looks in the wrong directory and the daemon never sees `brain/.env`.

The interactive `gbrain` invocation works because users typically run it from inside the brain repo, where Bun does find `brain/.env`. So this only bites the daemon path, and only for users whose keys are in `brain/.env`.

## Fix

`cd '\${safeRepoPath}' || exit 1` before `exec`. Bun's CWD-based auto-load now finds `brain/.env` on every wrapper invocation. Existing shell-init env vars still take precedence (Bun's auto-load doesn't overwrite), so users with keys in `~/.zshrc` are unaffected.

`writeWrapperScript()` is shared across launchd / systemd / crontab / ephemeral installers, so one site covers all four.

## Repro

1. Move `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `~/.zshrc` to `~/brain/.env`. Confirm in a fresh shell that `echo \$OPENAI_API_KEY` is empty.
2. \`gbrain autopilot --install --repo ~/brain\`
3. Wait one cycle (5 min default), then \`tail ~/.gbrain/autopilot.err\` — embed errors flood.
4. Apply this PR's fix, \`gbrain autopilot --install --repo ~/brain\` to regenerate the wrapper, kickstart, wait one cycle. \`tail ~/.gbrain/autopilot.log\` shows \`Embedded N chunks\` and \`autopilot.err\` is quiet.

I confirmed the fix locally by patching `~/.gbrain/autopilot-run.sh` directly and checking `ps eww` on the spawned Minions worker — `OPENAI_API_KEY` was visible in the worker child's env after the fix, absent before.

## Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `gbrain autopilot` could also read `--repo/.env` itself at startup, so the fix works regardless of how the daemon is invoked. Wider blast radius — left for a separate change.
- `gbrain doctor` could aggregate per-page embed failures into a `warn`-status check when failure rate exceeds a threshold. Would have caught this within one cycle. Happy to file a separate issue if there's interest.

## Tests

No new test in this PR — `writeWrapperScript` is a string-template function and the change is two lines of generated shell. Happy to add a snapshot test if reviewers prefer.

title: fix(autopilot): use engine.reconnect() so DB health check doesn't wipe saved config
feat(doctor): surface daemon silent-failure modes — per-cycle failure rate, cycle-failure-cap count, autopilot.err fingerprints
body:
## The blind spot

I just spent a session diagnosing an 8-day silent failure of my autopilot daemon. Two specific bugs were involved (PRs #464 and #465 in flight). But the more interesting finding is structural: **gbrain has no diagnostic surface that knows the daemon is broken** when something silently degrades.

For 8 days the daemon was in a wedged-and-respawning loop. The whole time:

- `gbrain autopilot --status` returned the cheerful `Last log: [cycle] score=67 elapsed=1s next=150s`
- `gbrain doctor` reported **90/100 healthy** with only cosmetic resolver-routing warnings
- No alarm anywhere

The actual story was buried in `~/.gbrain/autopilot.err` (3.4 MB) and `~/.gbrain/autopilot.log`: 2,488 per-page embed failures, 54 `Autopilot stopping (cycle-failure-cap)` exits, ~70 pool-saturation errors, ~85 cascading parse errors.

## Concrete blind spots in current observability

1. **Status-success-with-zero-work is indistinguishable from success-with-real-work.** Cycle exits status=success with `chunks_embedded: 0` whether the embed phase found 0 stale pages OR found 43 stale pages and failed to embed every one of them. Per-page embed errors are caught and warn-logged at the per-page level; the cycle never sees them.

2. **launchd-respawn loops are invisible.** With `KeepAlive = true`, every `cycle-failure-cap` exit silently respawns the daemon ~10 s later. There's no count of recent respawns anywhere, and `gbrain autopilot --status` reads from the live process so it always looks fresh. 54 exits in 8 days is a strong signal — but only if you know to grep for it.

3. **autopilot.err is never read by anything in gbrain.** Doctor introspects the DB and skill files. It doesn't open any log files written by daemons. So the dominant error class — whatever's eating most cycles — never surfaces.

4. **Per-phase failure rates aren't computed.** `runCycle` returns a `CycleReport` with phase results, but failures within a phase that get warn-logged-and-continued (the embed-per-page pattern, sync-failed-files, extract LLM-call timeouts) don't roll up into a phase-level failure rate.

## Proposed: a `daemon_health` doctor check

A new doctor check that walks recent daemon state and surfaces silent-degradation patterns. Sketch:

```
[OK]   daemon_health: autopilot up 4d 12h, last 100 cycles all green, no recent cap-outs
[WARN] daemon_health: 7 of last 20 cycles found stale chunks but embedded 0
       → tail ~/.gbrain/autopilot.err for "OPENAI_API_KEY missing" or similar
[ERROR] daemon_health: 12 cycle-failure-cap exits in last 24h
        → fingerprint: "config.poolSize" (PR #465) — running v0.22.1 or v0.22.2?
```

Concrete signals to compute:

- **Per-phase failure rate over last N cycles.** If `embed` consistently finds N chunks > 0 and embeds 0, that's a flag regardless of `status=success`. Threshold something like "WARN if >3 of last 10 cycles, ERROR if >5 of last 20."
- **`Autopilot stopping (cycle-failure-cap)` count from the last 24h of autopilot.log.** >0 is WARN, ≥3 ERROR.
- **autopilot.err tail fingerprinting.** Build a small library of known-error regexes (env-missing, pool-saturation, reconnect-undefined, prepared-statement-not-found, MaxClientsInSessionMode, etc.) and surface the dominant fingerprint with count + last-seen.
- **Worker exit `likely_cause` from v0.22.1's MinionSupervisor.** It already classifies (`oom_or_external_kill` / `runtime_error` / etc.) — surface the rolling distribution.

The doctor philosophy in CLAUDE.md says the v0.14.2 `schema_version=0` check fails loudly precisely because it caught the `bun install -g` footgun (#218). This is the same class of fix: turn a silent operational failure into a loud doctor warning so the next person sees it within one `gbrain doctor` invocation, not 8 days in.

## Why I think it's worth doing

The whole pitch of `gbrain doctor` is being the canonical "is my brain healthy" surface. Right now it's good at DB-level invariants (schema version, JSONB integrity, embed coverage, MECE / DRY skill checks) but blind to daemon operational health. Most user-visible problems with a self-running brain are operational, not data-integrity.

PRs #464 and #465 fix two specific bugs. This issue is defense-in-depth for the next class of silent-failure bugs that nobody has hit yet. (And if doctor catches them, contributors have a much easier time filing actionable bug reports — "doctor said X" is way better than "feels slow.")

## Related work

- PR #464 — autopilot wrapper cd-into-repo (Bun .env auto-load)
- PR #465 — autopilot reconnect using engine.reconnect() instead of broken connect()

Both demonstrate the silent-failure class this issue is about. Either or both fixes could have been caught much earlier with the proposed `daemon_health` check.

## Questions before I'd take a stab

Happy to draft a PR if there's interest. Would want a quick sanity check on:

1. **New check vs extend existing.** Is `daemon_health` the right shape, or should this fold into an existing check (e.g., extend `embed_coverage` with rate-over-time)?
2. **Where to store fingerprints.** Hardcoded list in `src/commands/doctor.ts`? Pluggable JSON file? Skill-defined?
3. **Log-tail philosophy.** Tail bytes (last N KB)? Tail by line count? Track a bookmark like sync does so doctor only re-scans new content?
4. **Fast vs full mode.** `gbrain doctor --fast` should presumably skip log-tailing (it's I/O); only full mode does the deep walk.

Whatever direction makes sense, happy to iterate.

title: feat: parameterize content_chunks.embedding dimension
body:
## Summary

- Add env-driven config helpers in a new `src/core/embedding-config.ts`:
  `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS`, `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`, `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_API_KEY`. Defaults preserve `text-embedding-3-large` / 1536 dim, so brains that don't set anything stay byte-identical.
- Migration v30 `dynamic_embedding_dimensions` (handler-based) detects mismatch between the stored `config.embedding_dimensions` row and the runtime config: drops the HNSW index, ALTERs `content_chunks.embedding` to the new `vector(N)` type, resets `embedded_at`, recreates the index, and syncs both config rows. Idempotent — no-op when dims already match.
- Replace hardcoded `'text-embedding-3-large'` defaults in `postgres-engine.ts` and `pglite-engine.ts` upsert paths with `getEmbeddingModel()` so chunks land with the correct model tag.
- The OpenAI embed client now respects `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL` / `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_API_KEY`, enabling Ollama / vLLM / LM Studio / Azure-style endpoints.
- Schema baseline (`schema.sql`, `schema-embedded.ts`, `pglite-schema.ts`) stays at `vector(1536)`. Existing brains migrate via v30 only when their configured dim differs.

## Example — running on Ollama bge-m3 (1024 dim)

```bash
export GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
export GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_API_KEY=ollama
export GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL=bge-m3
export GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS=1024

gbrain apply-migrations --yes   # v30 re-types the column
gbrain embed --stale            # repopulate
```

## Why a separate `embedding-config.ts` module

`test/embed.test.ts` aggressively mocks the whole `embedding.ts` module. If the config helpers lived there, the mock would shadow them for every co-resident test. Putting them in a peer module that no one mocks keeps the engine code, the migration, and the unit tests all reading the real env-driven values — and lets `embed.test.ts` stay focused on `embedBatch` concurrency.

## Why migration-only (not parameterized baseline)

Baseline `vector(1536)` is left as-is so existing brains start byte-identical and the schema build pipeline (`scripts/build-schema.sh`, `schema-embedded.ts`) needs no refactor. v30 handles dim drift on demand, which is the only case where it actually matters. If a future change wants to parameterize the baseline, that's a separate, heavier PR — happy to follow up if preferred.

## Why the dim change drops embeddings

There is no mathematically valid way to map a 1536-dim vector to 1024 dim or vice versa. v30 sets `embedded_at = NULL` so `gbrain embed --stale` picks up every chunk; the user runs that once and the brain is back in shape.

## Test Plan

```
bun run typecheck                              # passes
bun test test/embedding-config.test.ts         # 10 tests — env-var contract
bun test test/migrate.test.ts                  # extended with v30 registration
bun test test/embed.test.ts                    # mock simplified, still 11 tests
bun test test/apply-migrations.test.ts test/init-migrate-only.test.ts
bash scripts/check-jsonb-pattern.sh
bash scripts/check-progress-to-stdout.sh
bash scripts/check-wasm-embedded.sh
```

E2E (requires Postgres+pgvector):
- The new migration runs as v30 in `runMigrations()` — covered by `test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts`'s schema bring-up. A targeted test for dim re-type would be a useful follow-up but needs DB lifecycle plumbing I didn't want to slip in here.

## Relationship to #450

#450 introduces a richer provider abstraction (`openai`, `openai-compatible`, `copilot`) that subsumes the env vars in this PR. The two are complementary:

- This PR closes the schema gap (`vector(1536)` was the real blocker).
- #450 closes the client gap (multiple providers behind one factory).

If #450 lands first, the embed client in `embedding.ts` can be swapped for the provider factory and the env-var names already match (`GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_*`); the schema/migration layer here remains untouched. If this lands first, #450 keeps its provider factory and just imports the same helpers from `embedding-config.ts`.

Closes #133.

title: feat: gbrain export --slugs <comma-list> for selective re-export
body:
## Summary

Adds a `--slugs <comma-list>` flag to `gbrain export` that scopes the export to a caller-supplied set of slugs instead of every page in the engine.

When set, the loop replaces `engine.listPages({ limit: 100000 })` with sequential `engine.getPage(slug)` calls. Missing slugs warn to stderr and are skipped. Per-slug serialize+write errors are caught and counted in `failed`. The canonical stdout summary line `Exported N pages to D/` is preserved (scripts grepping for it keep working) and gains a `, M failed` suffix when any slug failed. Exit `0` if any slug succeeded; exit `1` only if every slug failed or the pre-loop fatal fires (empty `--slugs ""`). Bulk behavior (no flag) is unchanged.

## Why

Always-on deploys that mirror DB → FS via `gbrain export` (e.g. a wrapper service backing a remote put_page surface) have to invoke `gbrain export` periodically. Without `--slugs`, that means rewriting every page on disk every time any single page advanced in DB — expensive on commit volume, and on systems where the on-disk markdown is mounted alongside in-flight local edits, the bulk rewrite trampolines pending edits with older DB content.

Per-page export gated on `WHERE updated_at > lastAt` fixes that. The caller queries Postgres for advanced rows since the last cycle, optionally filters by FS mtime, then invokes `gbrain export --slugs <those> --dir <brain>`. Cuts churn proportional to write rate vs total page count.

## Use case (real consumer)

A Railway-hosted always-on autopilot for a personal-knowledge brain runs this every 5 minutes:

```ts
const rows = await sql`
  SELECT slug, updated_at::text
  FROM pages
  WHERE updated_at > ${lastAt}::timestamptz
  ORDER BY updated_at`;
const toExport = rows
  .filter(r => fileMissingOrOlder(r))
  .map(r => r.slug);
if (toExport.length) {
  exec(['gbrain', 'export', '--slugs', toExport.join(','), '--dir', brainDir]);
}
```

Production cycle log line on first run after deploy:

```
export DB→FS: 2 db_rows > last, 1 stale on FS
export check: 2 db_rows, 1 stale, 1 fresh-skip — exported 1
```

The "1 fresh-skip" is the consumer-side floor-second mtime guard — a row whose DB updated_at advanced but whose FS file is already current is not re-exported, even though it appears in the WHERE-window. Per-page makes that distinction possible.

## Design notes

- `--slugs a/foo,b/bar` (comma-separated). Slugs already contain `/`; comma is the only safe separator without quoting.
- No `--slug` singular alias, no `--exclude-slugs`. One flag, one shape.
- Exit code matches existing convention: any success ⇒ 0, total failure ⇒ 1.
- Empty `--slugs ""` throws `--slugs expected at least one slug (got empty value)` — pre-loop, before engine touch.
- `serializeMarkdown` + `getRawData` sidecar branch unchanged — applies per page in either path.

## Tests

`test/export.test.ts` (new file) — 6 cases covering:

- One valid slug → exports md + `.raw/` sidecar; nothing else.
- Valid + missing → exports valid, warns on missing, exit 0.
- All-missing → exit 1, stdout shows 0 succeeded.
- Empty `--slugs ""` → throws "expected at least one slug".
- No flag → bulk list-all path unchanged (regression guard).
- Partial export failure → "Exported N pages, M failed", exit 0 if any succeeded.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test test/export.test.ts` — all 6 pass locally.
- [ ] `gbrain export --slugs <existing-slug> --dir /tmp/exp` writes one file (+ `.raw/` if applicable) and nothing else.
- [ ] `gbrain export --dir /tmp/exp` (no flag) writes the full brain — back-compat.
- [ ] `gbrain export --slugs ""` exits 1 with the precondition message.

## Backwards compatibility

No flag → bulk behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. The existing test suite passes; new tests are additive in a new file.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: E2E mechanical.test.ts breaks under bun test 1.2.x batch beforeAll model
body:
## Summary

Running `bun test test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts` against a fresh Postgres 17 produces 64 / 78 fails. Root cause is a mismatch between the test file's per-describe isolation assumption and bun test 1.2.x's execution model.

Reproduced on:
- bun 1.2.19, macOS, Postgres 17.6 (Homebrew)
- `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://wangyiyang@localhost:5432/gbrain_test bun test test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts`

## Root cause

bun test 1.2.x runs **every describe's `beforeAll` serially before any test starts**, then runs every `afterAll` after every test finishes. Verified with sentinel logging:

```
SENTINEL A.beforeAll done
SENTINEL B.beforeAll start    ← B.beforeAll runs while A's tests have not started
SENTINEL B.beforeAll done
SENTINEL A.test start         ← A.test sees B's truncate+import state
SENTINEL A.afterAll start     ← A.afterAll closes the shared engine
SENTINEL A.afterAll done
SENTINEL B.test start
SENTINEL B.test psql says pages = 16    ← real DB has 16 rows
                                        ← but engine connection is closed
```

This breaks two assumptions in `test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts`:

1. **Singleton engine in `helpers.ts`**: each `setupDB()` call does `db.disconnect()` + `new PostgresEngine()`, so describe N+1 closes the connection describe N's tests still need.

2. **Per-describe truncate-and-reimport**: many describes (`E2E: file_list LIMIT enforcement`, `E2E: Setup Journey`, `E2E: Schema Idempotency`, `E2E: RLS Verification`, `E2E: Parallel Import`, `E2E: Performance Baselines`, `E2E: Init Edge Cases` partial) call `setupDB()` (which TRUNCATEs all tables) without `importFixtures()` afterward. Under the batch model, whichever describe with no-import runs **last** in the beforeAll batch leaves the DB empty for every test that runs afterward — every `page_count.toBe(16)` test fails with `Received: 0` even though earlier describes did import.

## Partial fix already in patch stack

I applied a local fix in my fork that makes `setupDB`/`teardownDB` idempotent (only one `db.connect()` per process, `teardownDB` is a no-op until process exit). This drops failures **64 → 19** by eliminating the connection-close race. The remaining 19 are all caused by truncate-without-import describes wiping fixtures the next describe's tests still expect — which can only be fixed by reshaping the test file itself.

Patch reference: https://github.com/vinsew/gbrain/commit/905685e

## Suggested directions (pick one)

1. **Restructure mechanical.test.ts** so describes that don't import fixtures live in their own files (the existing `scripts/run-e2e.sh` already serializes per-file, so there's no cross-file race).

2. **Per-test setup** instead of per-describe `beforeAll` (each `test()` calls `setupDB()` itself). Slower but gives real isolation regardless of test runner ordering.

3. **Pin to a bun version with the older execution model**, if there was one. (I have not bisected.)

Happy to send a PR for whichever direction you prefer — wanted to surface the design question first since it touches a lot of files.

## Why this hasn't been seen before

The previous Docker-based `scripts/run-e2e.sh` is "ONE FILE AT A TIME" so cross-file races are caught, but the per-describe race within `mechanical.test.ts` only manifests when bun test fully evaluates all `beforeAll` calls in batch — which I'm seeing on 1.2.19. Possibly older bun versions ran them in describe-sequential order. CI may also run a different bun version that masks the bug.

## Related

- Surfaced while debugging PR #472 (`file_list` BigInt fix) — needed real Postgres E2E to verify the fix for a Postgres-only bug, hit this E2E framework issue first.

title: test(e2e): make helpers idempotent under bun test 1.2.x batch beforeAll model
body:
## Summary

Partial fix for #473. Drops `bun test test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts` failures from **64 → 19** on bun 1.2.19.

## Root cause (full detail in #473)

bun test 1.2.x runs every describe's `beforeAll` serially **before any test starts**, not interleaved with that describe's tests. Combined with `helpers.ts`'s singleton engine + per-`setupDB()` disconnect/reconnect, the last describe's `afterAll` closes the shared db connection while earlier describes' tests still expect it open.

## Fix

- `setupDB()` only calls `db.connect()` + `db.initSchema()` + `new PostgresEngine()` once per process. Subsequent calls only run TRUNCATE + reseed config.
- `teardownDB()` becomes a no-op. postgres.js closes pooled connections on process exit, which is sufficient for the test process lifecycle.

Per-describe TRUNCATE still runs, so describes that pair `setupDB()` with `importFixtures()` retain their isolation. Fixture-importing describes are unaffected.

## What this does NOT fix

`mechanical.test.ts` has describes that TRUNCATE without re-importing fixtures (`E2E: file_list LIMIT enforcement`, `E2E: Setup Journey`, `E2E: Schema Idempotency`, `E2E: RLS Verification`, `E2E: Parallel Import`, `E2E: Performance Baselines`, etc.). Under the bun batch model, those wipe fixtures the next describe's tests still expect. Fixing that is a restructuring of `mechanical.test.ts` itself — separate PR / different design choice.

## Verified locally

- `bun 1.2.19`, macOS, Postgres 17.6 (Homebrew, native, not Docker)
- `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user@localhost:5432/gbrain_test bun test test/e2e/mechanical.test.ts`
- Before this PR: 14 pass / 64 fail
- After this PR: 59 pass / 19 fail (every remaining failure is a fixture-state issue, not a connection-state issue)

## Test plan

- [x] Local Postgres 17.6 + bun 1.2.19: failures drop from 64 → 19
- [ ] Verify CI's bun version still passes after this change (idempotent guard adds no behavior on first call)
- [ ] Verify `scripts/run-e2e.sh` (per-file serialization) is unaffected — file-process boundary resets `dbInitialized`

## Related

- #473 — full root cause writeup with sentinel-traced execution order
- #472 — separate `file_list` BigInt fix that surfaced this E2E framework issue while verifying the fix

title: fix: pass sourceId in cycle sync phase to prevent full reimport
body:
## Problem

`cycle.ts:runPhaseSync()` calls `performSync(engine, { repoPath: brainDir, ... })` without passing `sourceId`. This means the sync phase always reads the **global** `config.sync.last_commit` key instead of the **per-source** `sources.last_commit` anchor.

The global anchor can drift out of git history when:
- A force push rewrites history and the old commit gets garbage-collected
- A rebase squashes commits that included the anchor
- The global key was written by an older gbrain version and never updated

When `git cat-file -t <anchor>` fails, sync concludes there was a force push and triggers a **full reimport of all files** — on a production brain with 78K+ files this takes 30+ minutes and blocks the entire autopilot cycle.

Meanwhile, the per-source anchor in `sources.last_commit` is updated on every successful sync and stays aligned with repo history. It was 668 commits behind HEAD but still valid. The system had the right answer in the right place — the cycle just wasn't reading it.

### Timeline

1. Global `config.sync.last_commit` pointed to commit `472f34d5`
2. That commit was garbage-collected from the repo (likely after a squash/rebase chain)
3. Every autopilot cycle attempted a full reimport of 78,797 files
4. The cycle appeared to "hang" — it wasn't stuck, just scanning every file from scratch
5. `sources.default.last_commit` had a valid ancestor (`00a62e50`) the whole time

## Error Log



The DB state showed the divergence:



## What We Tried

1. **Diagnosed the hang** — ran sync with `--verbose`, saw it scanning 78K files (not stuck, just slow)
2. **Checked both anchors** — found the dual-storage divergence between `config` and `sources` tables
3. **Verified the per-source anchor** — `git cat-file -t` succeeded, `merge-base --is-ancestor` confirmed it
4. **Manual fix** — updated both anchors to HEAD, sync returned `up_to_date` in <1s
5. **Deployed operational guard** — cron script that copies per-source anchor to global every 5 min (band-aid)
6. **This PR** — the proper fix: pass `sourceId` so cycle reads the right anchor

## Solution

**1 file changed: `src/core/cycle.ts`**

Added `resolveSourceForDir()` — queries the `sources` table for a row whose `local_path` matches the brain directory. Returns the source id when found, `undefined` otherwise.

`runPhaseSync()` now calls this resolver and passes the result as `sourceId` to `performSync()`. When a source exists, sync reads `sources.last_commit` (per-source, always updated). When no source matches (pre-v0.18 brains), it falls through to the global `config.sync.last_commit` key — backward compatible.

### Behavior matrix

| Sources table has matching row | sourceId passed | Anchor read from | Backward compatible |
|-------------------------------|----------------|------------------|-------------------|
| ✅ Yes (`default`) | `"default"` | `sources.last_commit` ✅ | Yes |
| ❌ No (pre-v0.18 brain) | `undefined` | `config.sync.last_commit` | Yes |
| ❌ sources table missing | `undefined` (catch) | `config.sync.last_commit` | Yes |

## Results

Before fix:
- Every autopilot cycle triggered full import (78,797 files, 30+ min)
- Sync never completed within the job timeout

After fix:
- Sync reads per-source anchor → incremental diff → completes in <1s
- Full reimport only triggers on genuine first sync or `--full` flag

## Testing

- Verified `bun build src/core/cycle.ts --no-bundle` compiles clean
- Manually tested the resolver query against production Supabase
- Confirmed `resolveSourceForDir` returns `"default"` for the production brain path
- Confirmed graceful fallback when source doesn't exist (returns `undefined`)

title: v0.42.59.0 fix(autopilot): verify lock holder process before exiting
body:
## Problem

An `autopilot.lock` file can survive after its holder process crashes or is forcibly terminated. The old mtime-only check treats a fresh orphaned file as proof that another autopilot is running, so supervisor restarts can repeatedly exit until the file ages out.

## Fix

Read the holder PID and probe it with signal 0:

- live holder: exit and keep single-instance protection, regardless of lock age
- dead, malformed, empty, or self-owned holder: take over
- `EPERM`: treat as alive because the process cannot be disproved

A live process is never displaced just because the lock file is old.

## Coverage

Hermetic tests cover missing, live, dead, malformed, and empty lock states. The patch was rebuilt around the current autopilot self-upgrade and worker-supervision code rather than rebasing the old file wholesale.

## Verification

- `bun test test/autopilot-lock.test.ts`: 6 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run verify`: passed
- Full `bun test`: passed

title: PGLite upgrade fails on brains with schema_version < 21: "column source_id does not exist" in initSchema()
body:
## Summary

Upgrading a PGLite brain from gbrain ≤ v0.17.x to v0.18.0+ (target tested: v0.22.4) crashes during `initSchema()` with `column "source_id" does not exist`. The crash blocks all migrations from running, so the schema stays wedged at its pre-upgrade version.

This affects any user with a pre-v0.18 PGLite brain attempting to upgrade.

## Reproduction

1. Have a PGLite brain at `schema_version < 21` (e.g. a v0.10.2 install with `schema_version = 4`)
2. Upgrade gbrain source to v0.22.4 (in my case: archive copy + `bun install` + `bun link`)
3. Run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` (or `gbrain init --migrate-only` directly)
4. Crash:

```
=== Applying migration v0.11.0: GBrain Minions — durable background agents ===
column "source_id" does not exist
Phase A (schema) failed: Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only. Aborting; re-run after fixing.
Migration v0.11.0 reported status=failed.
```

Schema stays at the pre-upgrade version (4 in my case). `gbrain doctor` reports "MINIONS HALF-INSTALLED partial migration: 0.11.0" and health drops from 85 to 45.

## Root cause

`src/core/pglite-engine.ts` (lines ~88-91) applies the baseline `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` BEFORE running `runMigrations()`:

```typescript
async initSchema(): Promise<void> {
  await this.db.exec(PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL);          // ① baseline schema FIRST
  const { applied } = await runMigrations(this);  // ② migrations AFTER — never reached
}
```

`PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` (in `src/core/pglite-schema.ts`) contains:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (
  id        SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'
            REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ...
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_source_id ON pages(source_id);
```

On a pre-v0.18 brain:
1. `pages` already exists (without `source_id`) — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op
2. `CREATE INDEX ... ON pages(source_id)` crashes because the column doesn't exist yet
3. `runMigrations()` is never reached, so migration v21 (which adds `pages.source_id`) never runs

Note: `runMigrations` correctly sorts by version ascending (`migrate.ts:~1186-1190`), so the disordered `MIGRATIONS` array (`...,14,23,22,21,20,15,16,24,...`) is not the issue. The bug is purely in the order of `initSchema` operations.

## Affected versions

| Brain pre-existing schema | Engine | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `>= 21` | PGLite | ✅ OK (`source_id` already exists) |
| `< 21` | PGLite | ❌ **CRASH** (this bug) |
| `< 21` | Postgres | ⚠️ Not verified (postgres-engine.ts has a different path with advisory locks) |
| Fresh init | PGLite | ✅ OK (table created with `source_id`) |

So this affects anyone upgrading from gbrain ≤ v0.17.x to v0.18.0+ on PGLite. Looks like an upgrade path that was never tested on PGLite (Postgres might have a different code path that handles it).

## Suggested fixes

Two options come to mind:

**(a)** Move the `source_id`-aware bits (the `REFERENCES sources(id)` constraint and the `idx_pages_source_id` index) out of `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` and into the existing migration v21 (`pages_source_id_composite_unique`). Then `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` only handles the truly base schema, and migrations handle every additive change including indices.

**(b)** Detect `schema_version < 21` early in `initSchema()` and run `runMigrations()` BEFORE applying `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL`. This way migrations bring the brain up to v21+ first, then the baseline schema is idempotent.

Option (a) feels more architecturally clean (baseline schema = "what's true at the latest version"). Option (b) is the smaller patch.

## Workaround attempted

Investigated upgrade by intermediate paliers (v0.10.2 → v0.11.0 → ... → v0.22.4) but the upstream repo has 0 git tags published (`git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git` returns empty), so checking out specific intermediate versions isn't straightforward. And every version v0.18+ embeds the same problematic `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL`.

Currently rolled back to v0.10.2 stable (full backup taken before upgrade attempt — composite SHA-256 hash matches, baseline 26 pages / 51 chunks / health 85 preserved).

## Environment

- macOS Sonoma (Mac Mini M4 Pro)
- Bun v1.3.12
- gbrain target: v0.22.4 (from `gbrain-master` archive)
- gbrain previous: v0.10.2
- Engine: PGLite (`~/.gbrain/brain.pglite/`)
- Brain size: 26 pages / 51 chunks / 66 tags / schema_version=4

Happy to provide more diagnostic output if useful (`gbrain doctor` JSON, full migration crash log, etc.).

title: fix(sync): reconcile sync-failures.jsonl with reality
body:
## Summary

Bug 9 follow-up. v0.31 already shipped `acknowledgeSyncFailures` + the `--skip-failed`/`--retry-failed` operator workflows, but the JSONL was still append-only between cycles: a file that legitimately succeeded on a later attempt stayed listed as failed forever, padding doctor noise and confusing operators.

Tight on scope after rebase to v0.32.0 — this PR now only adds the missing reconciliation primitive and its call sites. The empty-diff `--retry-failed` / `--skip-failed` fallthrough is already on master from upstream's own work, so this branch no longer touches that surface.

### Real-world trigger

A brain with CJK-named pages hit a transient parse failure on 2026-04-27, recorded 6 entries to `~/.gbrain/sync-failures.jsonl`, then self-healed in the DB through a subsequent `put_page` flow — but the JSONL kept those 6 entries forever. Every `gbrain doctor` run flagged them as broken even though the underlying error (`Invalid slug: ""` from pre-#115 CJK slugify) no longer occurs.

## Changes

- **`src/core/sync.ts`**: new `resolveSyncFailure(path: string): number`. Removes all JSONL entries by path; unlinks the file when the last entry clears. Same read-modify-write concurrency caveat as `acknowledgeSyncFailures` (documented inline).

- **`src/commands/import.ts`**: on successful import and on hash-identical skip, calls `resolveSyncFailure(relativePath)`.

- **`src/commands/sync.ts`**: same primitive fires from `deletes` (file gone), `renames` (both `from` + `to`), and the per-file import success / hash-identical skip paths inside `importOnePath`.

- **`test/sync-failures.test.ts`**: 4 new cases — removal-with-count, no-op on unmatched path, last-entry file deletion, absent-file return-zero.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/sync-failures.test.ts` — 45/45 pass
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean (after fresh `bun install` to drop stale lock entries)
- [x] Cherry-pick onto v0.32.0 (commit `0ad309e`) — clean apply, no conflicts after the scope reduction

## Note on prior scope

This PR was originally larger (8 tests, ~250 lines) and included the `--retry-failed` fallthrough at the `lastCommit === headCommit` early return. Upstream landed that exact handling independently before v0.32.0, so the rebased version drops the overlap and ships only the missing reconciliation hook.
