title: fix: bridge shared provider env into gbrain CLI
body:
## Summary

Make `gbrain` work correctly when it is launched from Hermes workflows but provider credentials live in Hermes' env file.

The failure mode was not that users simply forgot to set `OPENAI_API_KEY`. In this topology there are two local tools with two config homes:

- Hermes stores provider credentials in `${HERMES_HOME:-~/.hermes}/.env`
- gbrain reads from its own config/env home, `${GBRAIN_HOME:-~}/.gbrain/`

When Hermes or cron launched `gbrain`, the shell process did not necessarily export the provider keys, and gbrain did not know how to consult Hermes' env file. That made embedding/AI gateway calls fail with errors such as:

```text
OpenAI embedding requires OPENAI_API_KEY.
```

This PR adds a narrow provider-env connector instead of requiring duplicated secrets or changing `loadConfig()` semantics.

## What changed

- Add CLI bootstrap `loadSharedProviderEnvFiles()`:
  - loads gbrain's own `~/.gbrain/.env` first
  - then loads shared provider credentials from `${HERMES_HOME:-~/.hermes}/.env`
  - preserves explicit process env precedence
- Restrict Hermes env imports to provider-related keys only, so unrelated Hermes secrets are not copied into gbrain's process.
- Keep `loadConfig()` pure/read-only. Env-file loading remains a CLI startup side effect, not a config-reader side effect.
- Pass config-file OpenAI/Anthropic credentials into gateway env as fallback when process env does not already contain them.
- Add regression tests for:
  - dotenv parsing and env precedence
  - `loadConfig()` remaining read-only even when env files exist
  - Hermes provider env fallback
  - excluding unrelated Hermes secrets such as gateway/messaging tokens

## Precedence

The connector uses this order:

```text
process.env > ~/.gbrain/.env > ${HERMES_HOME:-~/.hermes}/.env
```

Rationale:

1. `process.env` remains the operator escape hatch for one-off overrides and CI.
2. `~/.gbrain/.env` remains gbrain's native/local configuration source.
3. Hermes' env file is a fallback for embedded/Hermes-launched gbrain workflows where provider keys are already configured in Hermes.

## Security / privacy

- No provider key values are logged or exposed.
- Hermes env loading is allowlisted to AI provider variables used by gbrain recipes.
- Hermes-only credentials, gateway tokens, and unrelated secrets are not imported.
- Existing privacy checks pass.

## Validation

Required repo gate:

```text
bun run verify
```

Targeted regression tests:

```text
bun test test/ai/config-no-env-mutation.test.ts test/ai/gbrain-env-file.test.ts test/cli-multimodal-integration.test.ts
```

Runtime validation of the actual topology:

- temporarily made `~/.gbrain/.env` absent
- ran gbrain from this branch with only `HERMES_HOME` pointing at Hermes' config home
- confirmed `providers explain --json` detected OpenAI and Anthropic provider keys via Hermes env
- confirmed `gbrain embed --slugs projects/auto-research/multiplayer-research-game-context` did not fail with provider-key errors
- confirmed `gbrain features --auto-fix` completed without the original `OPENAI_API_KEY` failure

No secret values were printed during validation.

title: git pull/clone always fails: --no-recurse-submodules placed before subcommand in GIT_SSRF_FLAGS
body:
## Summary

`pullRepo` and `cloneRepo` in `src/core/git-remote.ts` always fail with `error: unknown option: --no-recurse-submodules` (exit 129) because `--no-recurse-submodules` is included in `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS` (line 29-34) and spliced **before** the subcommand. That flag is only valid as a `clone`/`pull`/`fetch` subcommand option, not a top-level git flag.

The error is masked at runtime because:

1. The error message is sliced to 100 chars in `src/commands/sync.ts:405` (`msg.slice(0, 100)`), which truncates before reaching the actual `unknown option` error.
2. `performSync` catches the failure and prints a `Warning:` then proceeds with local state, so `gbrain sync` reports `Already up to date.` regardless. The pull never actually runs.

Net effect: every `gbrain sync` against a remote-backed brain silently no-ops on the pull phase. Anyone pushing to the same brain from a second machine never has their changes pulled down.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Set up any brain repo with a remote
gbrain sync
# Output:
#   [gbrain phase] sync.git_pull error 11ms (git pull failed in <path>: Command failed: git -C <path> -c http.f
#   Warning: git pull failed: git pull failed in <path>: Command failed: git -C <path> -c http.followRedirects=
#   Already up to date.
```

Run gbrain's exact invocation manually to see the underlying error:

```bash
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GCM_INTERACTIVE=never GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/false SSH_ASKPASS=/bin/false \
  git -C <repo> \
    -c http.followRedirects=false -c protocol.file.allow=never -c protocol.ext.allow=never \
    --no-recurse-submodules pull --ff-only

# unknown option: --no-recurse-submodules
# (exit 129)
```

Move `--no-recurse-submodules` after `pull` (i.e. as a subcommand option) and it works:

```bash
git -C <repo> -c http.followRedirects=false ... pull --ff-only --no-recurse-submodules
# Already up to date.
```

## Suggested fix

Split `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS` into top-level (`-c` flags) and subcommand-level (`--no-recurse-submodules`) sets:

```ts
export const GIT_SSRF_FLAGS = [
  '-c', 'http.followRedirects=false',
  '-c', 'protocol.file.allow=never',
  '-c', 'protocol.ext.allow=never',
] as const;

export const GIT_SSRF_SUBCMD_FLAGS = [
  '--no-recurse-submodules',
] as const;
```

Then update both call sites to append the subcommand flags after the subcommand:

```ts
// pullRepo (line 182):
const args = ['-C', repoPath, ...GIT_SSRF_FLAGS, 'pull', '--ff-only', ...GIT_SSRF_SUBCMD_FLAGS];

// cloneRepo (line 156):
const args = [...GIT_SSRF_FLAGS, 'clone', ...GIT_SSRF_SUBCMD_FLAGS];
```

Also worth fixing: the 100-char truncation in `src/commands/sync.ts:405` hid the actual error message during debugging. Consider raising the limit or printing the underlying `Error.message` separately when verbose logging is on.

## Environment

- `gbrain` v0.31.3
- macOS 25.3.0 (arm64)
- `git --version` 2.x (Homebrew / Apple)
- bun runtime

title: Fix git submodule flag placement
body: # Fix git submodule flag placement Closes #813. ## Summary - Split SSRF hardening into top-level git config flags and git subcommand flags. - Keep `-c http.followRedirects=false`, `protocol.file.allow=never`, and `protocol.ext.allow=never` before `clone` / `pull`. - Move `--no-recurse-submodules` after the `clone` / `pull` subcommand, where git accepts it. - Add regression assertions for the exact fake-git argv shape for both `cloneRepo` and `pullRepo`. ## Why `--no-recurse-submodules` is not a valid top-level `git` option. With the previous argv shape, both clone and pull could fail before reaching the subcommand: ```text git --no-recurse-submodules clone ... git -C repo --no-recurse-submodules pull ... ``` The new shape keeps the same SSRF defense but places the submodule flag at the subcommand level: ```text git clone --no-recurse-submodules ... git -C repo pull --ff-only --no-recurse-submodules ``` ## Validation - `/private/tmp/kage-oss/bun-runtime/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun test test/git-remote.test.ts` — 37 pass, 0 fail. - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` - `git --no-recurse-submodules clone` fails with `unknown option`, confirming the old top-level placement is invalid. - `git clone --no-recurse-submodules` reaches clone usage, confirming the flag is accepted after the subcommand. - `git -C /private/tmp/kage-oss/git-flag-check --no-recurse-submodules pull --ff-only` fails with `unknown option`. - `git -C /private/tmp/kage-oss/git-flag-check pull --ff-only --no-recurse-submodules` reaches pull's normal no-upstream error, confirming the flag is accepted after `pull`. --- Need help on this PR? title: v0.31.4.1 still fails on schema-v10 origin Postgres brains: v0.13.0 migration references files.page_id before column exists
body:
## Summary

`v0.31.4.1` still fails to upgrade legacy schema-v10 origin Postgres brains. The forward-reference bootstrap fixes from #776 (lane 1: #740/#741 covering v39–v41) and the `mcp_request_log.agent_name` work referenced when closing #695/#657 do not cover the **v0.13.0** failure point. Migration v0.13.0 ("Frontmatter becomes a graph") trips on `column "page_id" does not exist` on the `files` table before the column has been added.

This appears to be the same class as #366 (v0.13.x → v0.18.1, closed as duplicate of #695) and #451 (pre-v17 bootstrap, also closed via #695), but neither was actually patched for the entry point at v0.12 → v0.13.

## Environment

- `gbrain --version` → **`0.31.4.1`** (master at `943e7b9`, post #815)
- Engine: **PostgreSQL** (Supabase-hosted)
- Brain age: schema v10 → 49 (39 versions behind)
- Brain content: ~12,200 pages, ~30,000 chunks, 100% embed coverage. Brain is fully queryable on the v0.12.2 CLI; queries continue to work on `0.31.4.1` as long as migrations don't run.
- macOS 14, Node.js via Bun

## Repro

```sh
cd ~/gbrain
git pull   # master at 943e7b9
bun install
# the postinstall (`gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive`) fires automatically and fails as below
gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive
```

## Trace (relevant excerpt)

```
⚠️  Schema version 10 is behind latest 49.
   Schema migrations run automatically on next connectEngine() / initSchema().
   To run them now: gbrain init --migrate-only

Migration v0.12.0 is WEDGED (3+ consecutive partials with no completion).
Check ~/.gbrain/upgrade-errors.jsonl for the last failure reasons, fix the underlying
issue, then run:
  gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry 0.12.0
Then re-run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`.

=== Applying migration v0.13.0: Frontmatter becomes a graph — company, investors,
attendees now create typed edges automatically ===

=== v0.13.0 — Frontmatter relationship indexing ===

NOTICE: extension "vector" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: extension "pg_trgm" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: extension "pgcrypto" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "sources" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "pages" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "idx_pages_type" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "idx_pages_frontmatter" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: relation "files" already exists, skipping
NOTICE: column "storage_url" of relation "files" does not exist, skipping
NOTICE: relation "idx_files_page" already exists, skipping

column "page_id" does not exist
Migration v0.13.0 reported status=failed.
```

The `idx_files_page` "already exists" notice is the smoking gun: the schema replay creates an index on `files(page_id)` before migration v0.13.0 has added the `page_id` column. Same class of forward-reference bootstrap bug as #366 / #695, just at a much earlier table/column pair.

The hinted `~/.gbrain/upgrade-errors.jsonl` does not exist on this install — that file is never written. (Minor side bug: the wedge-recovery hint should either point to a path that exists or stop suggesting it.)

## Why the v0.31.4.1 fix wave didn't help here

PR #776's upgrade-path lane covered:
- #741 — bootstrap forward-references for **v39–v41** (modality, emotional_weight, effective_date, effective_date_source, import_filename, salience_touched_at)
- #740 — three v0.30.0 issues (image-decoder deps, UNSAFE_TRANSACTION on pooled connections, missing `connect()` in v0.29.1 Phase B+C)
- mcp_request_log.agent_name forward-ref (referenced when closing #695)

None of these touch the **v0.13.0 → files.page_id** path. The same chicken-and-egg pattern lives much earlier in the migration chain than the fixes have reached.

## Side bug: postinstall auto-attempts migration

The npm/bun `postinstall` script runs `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive` automatically. On a wedged brain this means every `bun install` attempts the migration, fails, and bumps the wedge counter — without the operator opting in. Suggest either gating this behind a `GBRAIN_AUTO_MIGRATE=1` env var or running `gbrain doctor` first and skipping if a migration is already wedged.

## Asks

1. Should this reopen #366 or land as a fresh issue covering the schema-v10 → v0.13.0 entry point specifically?
2. Is there a recommended manual `ALTER TABLE files ADD COLUMN page_id …` shape that would let the v0.13.0 migration proceed on Postgres engines, or is the cleaner path to extend `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` to cover this column too?
3. Confirm whether the wipe-and-reimport escape hatch is still the recommended fallback for brains this old.

Happy to test patches against this exact brain.

title: Fix whoami over stdio MCP
body: # Fix whoami over stdio MCP Closes #713. ## Summary - Thread a lightweight `transport` label through MCP dispatch. - Mark stdio MCP calls as `transport: 'stdio'` and HTTP MCP calls as `transport: 'http'`. - Make `whoami` return the local shape for stdio MCP, where the caller is a local pipe without per-token auth. - Preserve the fail-closed `unknown_transport` behavior for ambiguous non-stdio remote contexts. ## Why Stdio MCP is intentionally `remote: true` for data access filtering, but it does not have OAuth or legacy token auth. `whoami` treated `remote: true` plus missing `ctx.auth` as a transport bug, so Claude Code / stdio clients saw `unknown_transport` even though other tools worked. This keeps the trust boundary intact: - `remote: false` local CLI still reports `{ transport: 'local', scopes: [] }`. - `transport: 'stdio'` also reports the local shape because it is a local pipe. - OAuth / legacy HTTP callers still report their auth identity. - Unknown remote callers without auth still fail closed. ## Validation - `/private/tmp/kage-oss/bun-runtime/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun test test/whoami.test.ts` — 10 pass, 0 fail. - `/private/tmp/kage-oss/bun-runtime/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun run typecheck` - `git diff --check` --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(mcp): extract_facts entity_hints array schema missing items field (rejected by OpenAI strict validator)
body:
## Repro

OpenAI's strict JSON-schema validator (used by `gpt-5.5` / `gpt-5-codex` and any client that runs `tools/list` through the official OpenAI tool-schema validator) rejects the entire MCP tool list with:

```
LLM request rejected: Invalid schema for function 'gbrain__extract_facts': In context=('properties', 'entity_hints'), array schema missing items.
```

When this fires, **every** gbrain MCP tool becomes unavailable to that agent — not just `extract_facts` — because the strict validator rejects the whole tool list when any single tool def fails validation.

## Root cause

`src/core/operations.ts:2396` declares `entity_hints` as a JSON-schema `array` without an `items` field:

```ts
entity_hints: { type: 'array', description: 'Existing canonical entity slugs the agent has already resolved. Helps the extractor pick the right slug.' },
```

Per JSON Schema (and OpenAI's strict-mode validator), an `array` MUST declare what its items are. The handler at line 2421 already treats the value as `string[]`:

```ts
entityHints: Array.isArray(p.entity_hints) ? (p.entity_hints as string[]) : undefined,
```

so the right `items` schema is `{ type: 'string' }`.

The `ParamDef` type already supports this — `src/core/operations.ts:198` has `items?: ParamDef`, and the only other array-typed MCP param in the file (`pages_updated` at line 1692) sets it correctly:

```ts
pages_updated: { type: 'array', required: true, items: { type: 'string' } },
```

`buildToolDefs` in `src/mcp/tool-defs.ts` already passes `items` through to the emitted JSON schema when present, so this is purely a missing-field bug at the operation declaration site.

## Fix

```diff
-    entity_hints: { type: 'array', description: 'Existing canonical entity slugs the agent has already resolved. Helps the extractor pick the right slug.' },
+    entity_hints: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Existing canonical entity slugs the agent has already resolved. Helps the extractor pick the right slug.' },
```

## Scope check (other array params)

I scanned `src/core/operations.ts` and `src/mcp/` for `type: 'array'` props missing `items:` and found only this one in MCP-exposed tool definitions. The only other hit (`candidates: { type: 'array' }` in `src/core/resolvers/builtin/x-api/handle-to-tweet.ts:102`) is an internal resolver `outputSchema` that doesn't go through `buildToolDefs`, so it doesn't reach OpenAI's tool validator — but it's still technically invalid JSON Schema and worth fixing if you want a clean sweep. I'm leaving that one out of this issue to keep scope tight; happy to file separately if useful.

## Verified

I patched our pinned install (commit 9c60b3a, v0.31.3) on a live pod, restarted the MCP server, ran `tools/list`, and confirmed:
- The emitted `extract_facts.inputSchema.properties.entity_hints` now has `"items": {"type": "string"}`.
- All 61 gbrain tools pass a recursive "every `type: array` has `items`" check.
- OpenAI strict-validator rejection no longer reproduces.

Happy to send a PR if helpful — just wanted to surface this with the analysis first since it's a one-character-class change.

title: MCP tool `extract_facts` has invalid JSON schema — array `entity_hints` missing items spec, fails OpenAI strict tool validation (HTTP 400)
body:
## Summary

When `gbrain serve` is connected as an MCP server to a client that uses OpenAI-compatible strict tool validation (Hermes Agent via OpenRouter → OpenAI/Azure in my case), every inference call fails with HTTP 400 because the `extract_facts` tool declares an array parameter (`entity_hints`) without specifying `items`.

## Error

Invalid schema for function 'mcp_gbrain_extract_facts': In context=('properties', 'entity_hints'), array schema missing items.

Provider returns:
{
"type": "invalid_request_error",
"param": "tools[20].parameters",
"code": "invalid_function_parameters"
}

## Environment

- gbrain version: 0.31.0
- Install path: `git clone + bun link`
- macOS: [your version, run `sw_vers -productVersion` to fill in]
- MCP client: Hermes Agent (Nous Research), latest as of 2026-05-10
- LLM provider in client: OpenRouter → openai/gpt-4.1-mini (Azure backend)

## Repro

1. Run `gbrain serve` in stdio mode
2. Connect from an MCP client that surfaces all gbrain tools to an OpenAI-compatible strict-mode endpoint
3. Send any user prompt → HTTP 400 from provider

## Workaround

Exclude the tool client-side:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  gbrain:
    command: gbrain
    args: [serve]
    tools:
      exclude: [extract_facts]
```

Works fine after that. Other gbrain tools function correctly via MCP.

## Suggested fix

In the tool schema declaration for `extract_facts`, add `items` to the `entity_hints` array. Something like:

```json
"entity_hints": {
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string" }
}
```

Any other array parameters in the MCP tool surface should get the same audit since OpenAI's strict validation rejects all arrays without `items`.

Happy to help test a fix.

title: v0.30.3 fix(engine): thread sourceId through import; stop misfiling pages to default
body: ## Summary **Multi-source sync stopped misfiling pages to `source_id='default'`.** Every page synced via the incremental path landed at `(default, slug)` because `importFromContent` never passed sourceId to `tx.putPage`. When the same slug already existed in another source, the mid-transaction duplicate-slug state exploded scalar-subquery patterns in `addLink`/`getTags`/`removeTag`/etc. with "more than one row returned by a subquery used as an expression". The trigger error was a red herring — Postgres NOTICEs about `to_tsvector` skipping >2047-char tokens drowned out the real failure site. **Headline numbers** (production brain at start of investigation): - 7 files failed every `sync --all` since 2026-05-05 (DESIGN.md, TODOS.md, WORKFLOW.md, EMAIL_GUIDE.md, agent-workflow.md, repo-harness.md, LINT_GUARDRAILS_TRIAGE.md) - 41 pages silently misfiled in `source_id='default'` instead of `brain`/`goodoff`/`treply` - 0 of these failures were caused by user file content **What changed:** ### Engine - New `SourceOpts` + `LinkSourceOpts` types in `src/core/engine.ts` - 13 BrainEngine methods extended with optional source opts: `putPage`, `deletePage`, `upsertChunks`, `getChunks`, `deleteChunks`, `addLink`, `removeLink`, `getLinks`, `getBacklinks`, `addTag`, `removeTag`, `getTags`, `addTimelineEntry`, `createVersion`, `getVersions`, `revertToVersion` - 6 scalar-subquery patterns (`WHERE page_id = (SELECT id FROM pages WHERE slug=$1)`) replaced with `USING pages p WHERE ... p.slug=$1 AND p.source_id=$N` joins — multi-source-safe even if a future code path leaks a row - PostgresEngine + PGLiteEngine both updated for parity ### Import pipeline - `importFromContent`, `importFromFile`, `importCodeFile` accept and thread `sourceId` through every per-slug engine call - `sync.ts` passes `opts.sourceId` to all `importFile` callsites (incremental + full-sync paths — full-sync had the same leak in a separate code path) - `runImport` in `import.ts` plumbs `sourceId` - `reindex-code.ts` plumbs `sourceId` ### Migration - New `gbrain repair-default-source [--dry-run] [--json]` walks every row in `source_id='default'`, matches each slug against configured sources' `local_path` filesystems, and either MOVES the row (rightful source has no `(source, slug)` row) or DELETES it as a duplicate (rightful row already exists from a successful later sync). Ambiguous + orphan rows stay in `default` for manual cleanup. - **Production data already migrated:** 24 moves + 1 duplicate deletion + 21 untouched orphans. Subsequent `sync --source goodoff` and `--full brain` runs both work cleanly and file into the correct source. ### Tests - `test/multi-source-import.test.ts` — 9 regression cases on PGLite in-memory exercising the original failure mode ## Out of scope (intentional, deferred) - `updateSlug` / `rewriteLinks` are not source-aware yet. Used by sync renames; not on the failing path. - MCP `put_page` still routes to `source_id='default'`. Multi-source MCP writes would need a `source_id` param on the operation contract. - `gbrain import ` CLI doesn't expose `--source` yet (the underlying helper accepts it; CLI surface is a follow-up). ## Verification - Production `gbrain sync --source goodoff` now passes 9/9 files (was 2 passing, 7 failing every cycle) - Production `gbrain sync --source brain --full` passes 96/96 files with 0 errors and 0 new leakage to default - Unit tests: 9/9 pass in the new regression suite - Build: `bun build --target=bun src/cli.ts` compiles clean ## Test plan - [x] Run `gbrain repair-default-source --dry-run` to preview - [x] Run `gbrain repair-default-source` to apply - [x] Run `gbrain sync --all --yes` and confirm 0 failures - [x] Spot-check `SELECT source_id, count(*) FROM pages GROUP BY source_id` shows the leak stopped 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(oauth): hide secret hash for token_endpoint_auth_method=none clients
body: ## Summary `GBrainClientsStore.getClient()` returned the stored secret hash for every registered client, even those registered with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none` (PKCE-only). The MCP SDK's `clientAuth.js:45` strict-compares stored secret to the request body whenever `client.client_secret` is truthy — regardless of `token_endpoint_auth_method` — so PKCE-only clients (e.g. Claude Desktop's confidential-client registration) get rejected with `invalid_client` at the token exchange even though OAuth 2.1 says no secret should be required. This 8-line fix returns `client_secret: undefined` when `token_endpoint_auth_method === 'none'`. The stored hash is preserved in the database so a client can switch auth methods later — only what the SDK sees at validation time is affected. ## Repro 1. Register a client with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none` (Claude Desktop's confidential-client OAuth flow does this by default). 2. Hit `/token` with `grant_type=authorization_code` + valid PKCE verifier, no `client_secret`. 3. Before this fix: SDK rejects with `invalid_client` because stored hash != empty body secret. 4. After this fix: SDK sees `client.client_secret = undefined`, skips the secret check, PKCE verification passes. ## Test plan - [x] Reproduced against `gbrain serve --http` on v0.31.10 with Claude Desktop OAuth flow - [x] Confirmed fix lets the same flow complete to a valid bearer token - [ ] Reviewer: re-run `bun test test/oauth.test.ts` — 72 cases pass on the rebased branch 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: feat(search): --source filter on search + query ops (closes #784)
body: ## Summary `SearchOpts.sourceId` existed in the engine type since v0.18 but the engine method bodies (`searchKeyword`, `searchVector`, `searchKeywordChunks`) never extracted it — declared but unused. The issue reporter's brain has 11 sources where wiki recall on infrastructure queries gets drowned by ~76% diary content, and the client-side workaround was a slug allowlist with N+1 filesystem reads. This PR connects the dormant plumbing to a CLI flag. Closes #784. ## What changed **Engine layer (6 methods, identical pattern, mirrors `language` / `symbolKind`):** | File | Method | Change | |---|---|---| | `postgres-engine.ts` | `searchKeyword` | `+ AND p.source_id = $N` | | `postgres-engine.ts` | `searchVector` | same, inside HNSW inner CTE so candidate pool excludes out-of-source rows up front | | `postgres-engine.ts` | `searchKeywordChunks` | same (two-pass anchor primitive) | | `pglite-engine.ts` | `searchKeyword` | appended to `extraFilter` | | `pglite-engine.ts` | `searchKeywordChunks` | same | | `pglite-engine.ts` | `searchVector` | same (inner CTE parity) | **Op layer (`src/core/operations.ts`):** - New `resolveSourceFilter(engine, source)` helper: - Hot-path uses a direct indexed probe — `SELECT id FROM sources WHERE id = $1 AND archived IS NOT TRUE LIMIT 1` — instead of `listSources()` (which runs `countPages(engine, id)` per row, making validation 1 + N queries per call). Cold review caught the N+1 in the first cut. - Error path falls back to `listSources()` to populate an actionable `Available: a, b, c` hint. Slow, but the caller already typed wrong so the slow path is acceptable. - Empty string / null / undefined = no filter (matches the rest of the search-op optional-param shape). - `unknown_source` `OperationError` envelope matches existing `insufficient_scope` / `unknown_operation` so MCP clients get a clean error code. - `search` op: `+ source` param, threads through to `engine.searchKeyword`. - `query` op: `+ source` param, threads to `engine.searchVector` (image branch) AND `hybridSearch` (text branch — `hybridSearch` already accepted `SearchOpts.sourceId` and passes through to its inner `searchKeyword` + `searchVector` calls). ## Behavior change for existing callers `SearchOpts.sourceId` was type-declared but ignored by engine bodies. Any pre-existing caller passing `sourceId` (e.g. `hybridSearch`'s pass-through at `search/hybrid.ts:368`) was a no-op before this PR; after it, the value actually filters. I checked the tree — `two-pass.ts:36` is the only other consumer, and its docstring says "Filter expansion to one source", which is what users expected. ## Tests `test/search-source-filter.test.ts` — 8 cases against PGLite: - `engine.searchKeyword` no `sourceId` crosses sources - `sourceId='wiki'` / `sourceId='diary'` each restrict to that source - `sourceId` pointing at unregistered id returns 0 rows (engine has no validation by design — that's the op layer's job) - search op exposes `source` param of type string - unknown source throws `OperationError('unknown_source', ...)` - registered source resolves through op and filters results - query op exposes the same `source` param Postgres parity not separately tested — engine SQL is symmetric and `test/multi-source-integration.test.ts` already exercises the cross-engine source semantics. Happy to add an `e2e/` variant gated on `DATABASE_URL` if you'd prefer; let me know. Manual smoke against a live Postgres brain: - `gbrain search "anthropic" --source default` → results from `default` only - `gbrain search "anthropic" --source bogus` → `Error [unknown_source]: unknown source 'bogus'. Available: default` - `gbrain query "anthropic" --source default` → results from `default` only ## Pre-flight - `bun run typecheck` ✓ - `bun test test/search.test.ts test/search-lang-symbol-kind.test.ts test/search-limit.test.ts test/multi-source-integration.test.ts test/mcp-tool-defs.test.ts test/search-source-filter.test.ts` → 80/80 pass - Cold review (independent reviewer agent, decorrelated context) → caught the listSources N+1, fixed in 17ee192 - 3 commits: feat + perf fix + inline-marker comment matching project convention ## Notes - The `resolveSourceFilter` helper lives module-private. Open to extracting if a 2nd consumer materializes; for now it only serves `search` + `query`. - Backwards compat: callers passing no `source` get the existing cross-source behavior. `sourceId === ''` treated as no filter (matches `--type ''` / `--lang ''` shape). - HNSW + filter recall: vector-search with a sparse source filter shares the same well-known post-filter trade-off as the existing `--lang` / `--symbol_kind` filters (HNSW inner pool may exhaust if filtered source is < 10% of corpus). Pre-existing class issue, not introduced here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(ai): claude-sonnet-4-6 alias maps to non-existent dated model
body: ## What The anthropic recipe alias `claude-sonnet-4-6` → `claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929` points at a model ID that does not exist at the Anthropic API. Direct curl confirms: | Model ID | Anthropic API response | |-----------------------------------|------------------------------| | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | 200 OK | | `claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929` | 404 not_found_error | | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | 200 OK | | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | 200 OK | ## Impact Most visible for v0.31 facts extraction. `getFactsExtractionModel()` defaults to `'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929'` (`src/core/facts/extract.ts:53`). The gateway recipe rewrites the friendly alias to the dated form, the API rejects it, and the gateway swallows the error. End result: `gbrain call extract_facts` returns `{inserted: 0}` on every input for users who don't override the model. This affects every v0.31+ install on the default model setting. Visible to the user as: "hot memory feature shipped but facts table never gets rows." Same alias path also affects `gbrain providers test --touchpoint chat` which surfaces the 404 as `config error: model: claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929`. ## Fix Replace the dated form with the working alias throughout the recipe (3 occurrences in `expansion.models`, `chat.models`, and as the alias target) and drop the now-redundant alias entry. The haiku alias stays unchanged because its dated form is valid at the API. ## Verification Local, against v0.31.10: - Before: `gbrain providers test --touchpoint chat` → `not_found_error` - After: 200 OK - Before: `gbrain call extract_facts '{turn_text:"..."}'` → `{inserted: 0}` - After: `{inserted: 3, fact_ids: [1,2,3]}` with correct kinds (`event`, `commitment`, `preference`) and entity resolution on a one-paragraph input ## Note No unit test added — the model IDs in this file are config values and the verification is "does Anthropic accept this string", which a unit test can't cleanly assert without hitting the live API. A `providers test` E2E in CI with a fake `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=test` would catch the 404 path generically but is out of scope for this fix. --- Need help on this PR? title: fix: move --no-recurse-submodules after subcommand in GIT_SSRF_FLAGS
body: ## Summary Fixes #813 — every `gbrain sync` silently no-ops the git pull phase because `--no-recurse-submodules` is placed before the subcommand in `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS`. ## Root Cause `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS` mixes top-level `-c` flags with the subcommand-level `--no-recurse-submodules` flag in a single array. Both `cloneRepo` and `pullRepo` spread this array before the subcommand, producing: ``` git -C -c http.followRedirects=false ... --no-recurse-submodules pull --ff-only ``` Git rejects this with `unknown option: --no-recurse-submodules` (exit 129). The error is masked at runtime by 80-char truncation in `src/commands/sync.ts`, so sync reports `Already up to date` while never actually pulling. ## Fix 1. Split `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS` into `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS` (`-c` flags only) and new `GIT_SSRF_SUBCMD_FLAGS` (`--no-recurse-submodules`) 2. Append subcommand flags after the subcommand in both `cloneRepo` and `pullRepo` 3. Bump error message truncation in `sync.ts` from 80/100 to 300 chars so underlying git errors are visible ## Testing Manual verification of the corrected argument order: ```bash # Before (broken): --no-recurse-submodules before pull git -C -c http.followRedirects=false -c protocol.file.allow=never -c protocol.ext.allow=never --no-recurse-submodules pull --ff-only # → error: unknown option: --no-recurse-submodules (exit 129) # After (fixed): --no-recurse-submodules after pull git -C -c http.followRedirects=false -c protocol.file.allow=never -c protocol.ext.allow=never pull --ff-only --no-recurse-submodules # → Already up to date. (works) ``` ## Files Changed - `src/core/git-remote.ts` — Split flag arrays, update cloneRepo + pullRepo call sites - `src/commands/sync.ts` — Increase error message truncation from 80/100 to 300 chars --- Need help on this PR? title: chore: add shareable Kage agent memory
body:
## What is Kage?

Kage is repo-local shared memory for coding agents. It commits the reusable engineering context that usually gets trapped inside one agent session: why a bug happened, which files mattered, what tests proved the fix, and what the next teammate's agent should recall before editing.

I am applying to YC Summer 2026 with Kage, and this PR is meant to show the product in the most concrete way: real open-source issues fixed, then the repo memory from that work shared back so future teammates and agents can reuse it.

This PR demonstrates the handoff: after merge, another contributor can `git pull`, install Kage, and immediately recall the same gbrain bug-fix context, memory graph, code graph, paths, and validation evidence from the committed `.agent_memory` bundle.

## How a teammate uses this after merge

```bash
git pull
npm install -g @kage-core/kage-graph-mcp
kage setup verify-agent --agent codex --project .
kage recall "issue 394 dream --dry-run --json stdout" --project .
kage viewer --project .
```

Claude Code:

```bash
git pull
npm install -g @kage-core/kage-graph-mcp
kage setup verify-agent --agent claude-code --project .
kage recall "mixed-case slug import chunks Page not found" --project .
```

This PR also adds a Kage bootstrap section to `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so compatible agents know to use repo memory automatically before code changes or implementation questions.

## Summary

This PR adds Kage's repo-local `.agent_memory` for the gbrain contribution sprint, plus `.agent_memory/README.md` explaining how the committed memory is shared across teammates.

It includes:

- 12 approved memory packets in `.agent_memory/packets/`
- memory graph artifacts in `.agent_memory/graph/`
- recall indexes in `.agent_memory/indexes/`
- Kage metrics in `.agent_memory/metrics.json`
- structural/code graph artifacts in `.agent_memory/structural/` and `.agent_memory/code_graph/`
- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` bootstrap instructions so agents can use Kage automatically

I sanitized local machine paths before committing: generated metadata uses `project_dir: "."`, and local Bun PATH prefixes were removed from verification strings.

## What was fixed in the sprint

| PR | Issue | Fix | Kage memory captured |
|----|-------|-----|----------------------|
| #818 | #813 | Git submodule flag placement for `code-sync` | `gbrain #813: git submodule flag placement` |
| #821 | #713 | Preserve `whoami` identity through stdio MCP calls | not captured as a packet in this local set |
| #822 | #799 | Make `doctor` skip generated dependency folders | not captured as a packet in this local set |
| #823 | #709 | Add Astro frontmatter/script/style support to code sync | `gbrain #709: Astro files need code sync coverage` |
| #824 | #693 | Keep `doctor --json` stdout/stderr machine-parseable | `gbrain #693: doctor --json should suppress implicit progress` |
| #825 | #485 | Restore positional directory handling for `check-backlinks` | `gbrain #485: check-backlinks positional dir parsing` |
| #826 | #486 | Add npm fallback for `check-update` | `gbrain #486: check-update npm fallback` |
| #827 | #394 | Keep `dream --dry-run --json` stdout clean | `gbrain #394: dream JSON dry runs must not mix human stdout` |
| #828 | #430 | Preserve mixed-case slugs through import and chunk lookup | `gbrain #430: mixed-case slugs must be canonicalized before import writes` |
| #829 | #380 | Support `put --file` and reject unknown shared operation flags | `gbrain #380: put --file should be real and unknown op flags should fail early` |

Also opened #819 for #806 MCP array schema `items`; it is included as memory, but I am not counting it in the ten because an upstream duplicate was already in flight.

## How Kage was used

The working loop was:

1. Ask Kage for issue-specific repo context before editing.
2. Use recalled memory + code graph paths to inspect the right files first.
3. Make the focused fix.
4. Run targeted tests/typecheck/diff check.

body: ## Summary Fixes the v0.31.6 chat-default 404 (`claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929` is a phantom ID; Sonnet 4.6 is dateless) and adds a power-user tier routing surface so users can swap defaults with one config key. Six commits, bisect-friendly. **Bug fix sweep + reverse alias + pricing dedupe.** Replaced `claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929` with `claude-sonnet-4-6` across source/tests/docs. The recipe alias is reversed (broken ID → canonical) so users with stale `models.dream.synthesize` configs keep working. Opus 4.7 pricing corrected from `$15/$75` to `$5/$25` per Anthropic docs (the old number was Opus 4.0). `cross-modal-eval/runner.ts` PRICING now reads from `ANTHROPIC_PRICING` instead of duplicating. PR #830 from `garrytan-agents` was the seed fix — its recipe diff and structural test file are pulled verbatim and credited. **Tier system + async reconfigure + recipe-models merge.** Four-tier classification (utility/reasoning/deep/subagent) routes every internal LLM call. `gbrain config set models.default opus` overrides every tier with one key. `models.tier.` for per-tier overrides. `reconfigureGatewayWithEngine(engine)` is the new async re-stamp seam called after `engine.connect()` so DB-config tier overrides actually take effect. Per-gateway-instance recipe-models merge replaces the earlier plan to soften `assertTouchpoint` wholesale (Codex F4/F5 — too broad). Tests + doctor `subagent_provider` check enforce the Anthropic-only constraint at three layers (submit-time queue guard, tier-resolution fallback, doctor surfacing). **`gbrain models` CLI + silent-no-op regression test.** Read mode prints the routing table with source attribution per row. `gbrain models doctor` fires a 1-token probe to each configured model and classifies failures (model_not_found / auth / rate_limit / network / unknown). New `test/e2e/facts-extract-silent-no-op.test.ts` is THE regression test for the v0.31.6 bug class — wires gateway with the broken model ID, asserts `isAvailable("chat")` is false and `extractFactsFromTurn` returns `[]`, then asserts the reverse alias rescues it. ## Test Coverage Tier system + bug fix coverage is concentrated in 6 test files (85 cases): - `test/anthropic-model-ids.test.ts` (NEW, 6 cases) — recipe-shape guardrails, verbatim cherry-pick of PR #830 - `test/model-config.serial.test.ts` — 10 new tier-system cases (precedence, subagent-Anthropic fallback, alias-chain conflict) - `test/ai/gateway-chat.test.ts` — reverse-alias regression + existing contract tests rewritten for new alias direction - `test/facts-extract-silent-no-op.test.ts` (NEW, 5 cases) — the structural regression test for the bug class - `test/agent-cli.test.ts` — 3 new queue submit-time guard cases - `test/budget-meter.test.ts` — updated for corrected Opus 4.7 pricing Full test suite: 5076 pass / 2 pre-existing flaky failures unrelated to this branch (`BrainRegistry empty-id` depends on absence of `~/.gbrain/config.json`; LongMemEval `warm-create speed gate` races under parallel contention). title: Add shareable Kage agent memory
body:
Hi @garrytan 

## What is Kage?

Kage is repo-local shared memory for coding agents. It commits the reusable engineering context that usually gets trapped inside one agent session: why a bug happened, which files mattered, what tests proved the fix, and what the next teammate's agent should recall before editing.

I am applying to YC Summer 2026 with Kage, and this PR is meant to show the product in the most concrete way: real open-source issues fixed, then the repo memory from that work shared back so future teammates and agents can reuse it.

This PR demonstrates the handoff: after merge, another contributor can `git pull`, install Kage, and immediately recall the same gbrain bug-fix context, memory graph, code graph, paths, and validation evidence from the committed `.agent_memory` bundle.

## Kage links
- Website: https://kage-core.com/
- GitHub: https://github.com/kage-core/Kage
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kage-core/kage-graph-mcp
- Hosted viewer shell: https://kage-core.github.io/Kage/viewer/

## Active PRs from this Kage sprint

- #846 Fix git submodule flag placement
- #847 Fix extract_facts MCP array schema
- #848 Fix whoami over stdio MCP
- #849 Skip generated dirs in frontmatter scan
- #850 Add Astro files to code sync
- #851 Silence doctor progress in JSON mode
- #852 Honor positional check-backlinks directory
- #853 Fall back to npm for check-update
- #854 Keep dream JSON dry runs clean
- #855 Normalize mixed-case slugs during imports
- #856 Support put --file and reject unknown op flags
- #857 Add shareable Kage agent memory

## How a teammate uses this after merge

```bash
git pull
npm install -g @kage-core/kage-graph-mcp
kage setup verify-agent --agent codex --project .
kage recall "issue 394 dream --dry-run --json stdout" --project .
kage viewer --project .
```

Claude Code:

```bash
git pull
npm install -g @kage-core/kage-graph-mcp
kage setup verify-agent --agent claude-code --project .
kage recall "mixed-case slug import chunks Page not found" --project .
```

This PR also adds a Kage bootstrap section to `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so compatible agents know to use repo memory automatically before code changes or implementation questions.

## What this PR adds

This PR adds Kage's repo-local `.agent_memory` for the gbrain contribution sprint, plus `.agent_memory/README.md` explaining how committed memory is shared across teammates.

It includes:

- 12 approved memory packets in `.agent_memory/packets/`
- memory graph artifacts in `.agent_memory/graph/`
- recall indexes in `.agent_memory/indexes/`
- Kage metrics in `.agent_memory/metrics.json`
- structural/code graph artifacts in `.agent_memory/structural/` and `.agent_memory/code_graph/`
- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` bootstrap instructions so agents can use Kage automatically

I sanitized local machine paths before committing: generated metadata uses `project_dir: "."`, and local Bun PATH prefixes were removed from verification strings.

## Issues fixed using Kage

| PR | Issue | What was fixed | How Kage helped |
|----|-------|----------------|-----------------|
| #846 | #813 | Fixed git submodule flag placement for `code-sync` clone/pull operations. | Kage recalled the git remote path and prior branch context, pointing directly at `src/core/git-remote.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, and `test/git-remote.test.ts` instead of re-scanning the repo. |
| #847 | #806 | Added missing `items` schema for MCP array params, specifically `extract_facts.entity_hints`. | Kage memory captured the strict MCP/OpenAI-compatible validator failure and preserved the exact regression: array schemas must declare `items`. |
| #848 | #713 | Preserved `whoami` identity through stdio MCP calls while keeping remote HTTP auth behavior fail-closed. | Kage helped separate local stdio transport from HTTP auth by recalling MCP transport/auth paths and the relevant `whoami` tests. |
| #849 | #799 | Made `doctor` skip generated dependency/build directories during frontmatter scans. | Kage pointed the work at the scanner path and test area instead of treating this as a general doctor problem. |
| #850 | #709 | Added Astro frontmatter/script/style support to code sync, chunking, and code-reference extraction. | Kage recalled that `.astro` needed changes across sync extension allowlists, language detection, link extraction, import-file pseudo paths, and five related test files. |
| #851 | #693 | Kept `doctor --json` machine-parseable by suppressing implicit progress output unless `--progress-json` is explicit. | Kage preserved the distinction between plain JSON mode and explicit progress JSON, plus the unit/e2e test split. |
| #852 | #485 | Restored documented positional directory handling for `check-backlinks check/fix`. | Kage recalled the parser function, expected `--dir` precedence, and `test/backlinks.test.ts` coverage. |
| #853 | #486 | Added npm fallback for `check-update` when GitHub releases has no latest release. | Kage preserved the cause: package installs can have npm versions even when GitHub releases are absent. |
| #854 | #394 | Kept `dream --dry-run --json` stdout clean during embed phase while preserving standalone `gbrain embed` human summaries. | Kage connected `src/commands/embed.ts`, `src/core/cycle.ts`, and `test/dream.test.ts`, preventing an overbroad fix that would silence standalone embed output. |
| #855 | #430 | Preserved mixed-case slugs through import and chunk lookup by canonicalizing before transaction writes and direct chunk upserts. | Kage recalled the issue as a cross-path normalization bug spanning `importFromContent`, PGLite, Postgres, and chunk writes. |
| #856 | #380 | Added real `put --file <path>` support and rejected unknown shared operation flags before DB connection. | Kage recalled the CLI shared-op parser and the need to fail typo flags early, not just add a file-reading code path. |

## How Kage was used

The working loop was:

1. Ask Kage for issue-specific repo context before editing.
2. Use recalled memory + code graph paths to inspect the right files first.
3. Make the focused fix.
4. Run targeted tests/typecheck/diff check.
5. Capture the verified bug-fix learning back into repo-local memory.

```bash
kage recall "issue 394 dream --dry-run --json preamble stdout valid JSON tests" --project .
kage recall "mixed-case slug put_page lowercased slug upsertChunks Page not found" --project .
kage recall "put --file ignored unknown flags should error CLI put command operations tests" --project .
kage recall "Astro code sync coverage" --project .
kage recall "doctor --json progress stderr" --project .
```

### Issue #394: `dream --dry-run --json` clean stdout

Kage surfaced:

- `src/commands/embed.ts`

That changed the fix: the patch silenced embed progress only when dream is emitting structured JSON, rather than globally changing embed output.

### Issue #430: mixed-case slug import/chunks

Kage query:


Kage surfaced:

- `src/core/import-file.ts`

- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts`
- `test/pglite-engine.test.ts`

That made the bug look like a cross-path canonicalization problem, not an import-only issue. The fix normalized slugs before import transaction writes and in direct `upsertChunks` paths.

### Issue #709: Astro code sync coverage

Kage query:

```bash
kage recall "Astro code sync coverage" --project .
```

Kage surfaced the multi-file shape of the change:

That prevented a shallow `.astro` extension-only patch and made the PR cover sync, chunking, references, and tests.

### Issue #380: `put --file` and unknown flags

Kage query:

```bash
kage recall "put --file ignored unknown flags should error CLI put command operations tests" --project .
```

Kage surfaced the shared operation flag parser and `test/cli.test.ts`, so the fix did both parts of the issue: real file input and early rejection of unknown flags before DB work.

title: v0.32.3.0 skill: functional-area-resolver — pattern for compressing routing tables
body:
## Summary

Ship `functional-area-resolver`, a new skill that documents and benchmarks a pattern for compressing agent routing files (AGENTS.md / RESOLVER.md). The pattern replaces per-skill rows with functional-area dispatcher entries that list their sub-skills in `(dispatcher for: ...)` clauses. The LLM reads one area entry and routes to the correct sub-skill.

Empirical result: **a 25KB routing file compresses to 13KB without losing routing accuracy** — proven across Anthropic Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, and Haiku 4.5 with held-out blind fixtures + n=3 seeded repeats. Functional-areas variant beats the verbose baseline by +13 to +17pp on training (lenient scoring) at 48% the size. Reproducible from `evals/functional-area-resolver/baseline-runs/*.jsonl`.

**Skill contribution.** SKILL.md, routing-eval fixtures, wire-up into `skills/RESOLVER.md` + `skills/manifest.json` + `openclaw.plugin.json` so downstream agent forks pick it up via `gbrain skillpack install --update`.

**Eval contribution.** New `evals/functional-area-resolver/` directory (outside `skills/` so the bundler doesn't ship eval infrastructure to downstream installs). TypeScript harness routed through gbrain's gateway with `--model {opus|sonnet|haiku}` flag, strict + lenient scoring side-by-side on every output row, receipt format binding `(model, prompt_template_hash, fixtures_hash, harness_sha, ts)` so future contributors detect schema drift. 45 unit tests for pure functions. Three canonical baseline receipts committed.

**Prior art.** SKILL.md cites three papers grounding the pattern: AnyTool ([arXiv:2402.04253](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04253)) for hierarchical routing, RAG-MCP ([arXiv:2505.03275](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.03275v1)) for token-reduction prior result, Anthropic Agent Skills progressive disclosure for the design pattern. The pattern is positioned as the *static-prompt* analog of runtime hierarchical schemes in the 2024-2025 literature.

## The numbers that matter

Training corpus, n=20 fixtures × 3 seeds, lenient scoring (predicted shares dispatcher area with expected):

| Variant | Opus 4.7 | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 | Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (270 bullet rows) | 81.7% | 86.7% | 73.3% | 25KB |
| **functional-areas** (this pattern) | **100%** | **100%** | **88.3%** | **13KB** |
| resolver-of-resolvers (no dispatcher clause) | 66.7% | 41.7% | 65.0% | 10KB |

The `(dispatcher for: ...)` clause is the load-bearing signal — strip it and Sonnet collapses to 41.7%, exactly the SKILL.md's predicted failure case, now observed.

Held-out (n=5, lenient) saturates at 100% across most cells.

Catches that this review caught included the harness distribution architecture (would have shipped broken in downstream installs), routing-eval gate enforceability, manifest.json sync, plugin version drift, and statistical methodology.

PR #860 started as a fix for `embed --stale` silently defaulting to `source_id='default'` for non-default sources (~22K chunks left unembedded across 5,042 media-corpus pages on production). A scan during eng review surfaced **5 more sites with the same bug pattern**. This PR exterminates the bug class end-to-end:

**Bug-site fixes (5 sites + embed):**
- `embed --stale` / `embed --all` / per-slug embed (PR #860 original)
- `extract` (links + timeline) — `addLinksBatch` / `addTimelineEntriesBatch` now thread `from_source_id` / `to_source_id` / `origin_source_id`. Source-aware link resolution: origin > default > unresolved.
- `extract-takes` — `listAllPageRefs()` replaces the `getAllSlugs()+getPage(slug)` N+1
- `patterns` + `synthesize` reverse-write — refs contract carries `source_id`; per-source disk subdir `.sources/<id>/<slug>.md` for non-default sources; path-traversal guard

title: fix(mcp): seal source-isolation leak on read path (P0)
body: Builds on the baseline commit. Adds the actual enforcement and the auth wire-up that populates AuthInfo.sourceId, so OAuth-authenticated MCP clients can no longer read pages belonging to other sources. Engine layer (the WHERE clauses the previous commit left missing): - core/postgres-engine.ts: searchKeyword / searchKeywordChunks / searchVector now apply `AND pages.source_id = $N` when ctx.sourceId is set - core/search/hybrid.ts: thread opts.sourceId into the searchOpts literal before calling engine.searchKeyword/searchVector. Previously this function rebuilt searchOpts without the field, silently dropping the filter even after the engine learned to honor it. This was the Tier 3 leak (`query` op) that survived the engine-level fix. Auth layer (populates the field): - core/migrate.ts: migration v47 adds oauth_clients.source_id (FK to sources, ON DELETE SET NULL) - core/schema-embedded.ts + core/pglite-schema.ts: same column in the fresh-install schema - core/oauth-provider.ts: verifyAccessToken JOINs oauth_clients and propagates source_id into AuthInfo.sourceId - mcp/http-transport.ts: legacy bearer-token validateToken path also extracts source_id and federated_read claims - commands/serve-http.ts: tokenSourceId reads the formal AuthInfo.sourceId field instead of the previous always-'default' cast Semantics: - oauth_clients.source_id SET → strict isolation, engine WHERE-filters - oauth_clients.source_id NULL → federated/super-reader, no filter (matches stdio CLI behavior — unscoped = full reach) Pre-fix, every OAuth client silently collapsed onto source 'default' because the field was planned but never wired, and the engine ignored the param even when callers passed it. This commit closes both halves. Verified end-to-end against live shared Postgres with three test clients (scoped-empty / scoped-populated / NULL-federated) across all four read surfaces: list_pages, search, query (hybrid), get_page cross-source. --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(operations): add items schema to entity_hints array param
body: ## Summary `extract_facts.entity_hints` is declared as `type: 'array'` but lacks the `items` schema. JSON Schema strictly requires `items` on array types; MCP clients that validate tool definitions (caught downstream by OpenClaw) reject the `extract_facts` tool def at handshake. The fix is a one-liner: add `items: { type: 'string' }`. ## Why this slipped through silently `buildToolDefs` at `src/mcp/tool-defs.ts:24` already guards: `...(v.items ? { items: { type: v.items.type } } : {})`. With no `items` on the op param, the builder simply drops the field from the wire schema, producing a spec-violating tool def. The Anthropic SDK accepts it; strict validators reject it. Hence "works on dev box, fails downstream" pattern. ## Spot-check the rest of the codebase Grepped all `type: 'array'` declarations: - `src/core/operations.ts:1733` `ingest_log.pages_updated` — already has `items: { type: 'string' }` ✓ - `src/core/operations.ts:2443` `extract_facts.entity_hints` — **this PR** - `src/core/resolvers/builtin/x-api/handle-to-tweet.ts:102` `candidates` in `outputSchema` — pure documentation surface (only consumed by `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))` in `commands/resolvers.ts:162`), not wire-validated. Out of scope for this fix. ## Test plan - [x] `bun run typecheck` clean - [x] No behavior change — `entity_hints` was already array-of-strings semantically; the patch only declares it so MCP clients accept it ## Credit Schema mismatch caught by OpenClaw downstream during MCP tool-def validation. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? title: fix(extract_facts): add items schema to entity_hints array param
body: ## Problem The `extract_facts` MCP tool declares `entity_hints` as `type: 'array'` with no `items` definition (`src/core/operations.ts`). Anthropic's API validates JSON Schema at the schema-validation layer before dispatching the request to the model, and rejects array properties that lack `items`. As a result, **any call to `mcp__gbrain__extract_facts` from a Claude client (Claude Code, the Anthropic API directly, etc.) fails with `InputValidationError` before the tool ever runs**. ### Repro ``` $ claude mcp call gbrain__extract_facts '{"turn_text": "..."}' Error: InputValidationError: tools.N.input_schema: entity_hints.items: Field required ``` ## Fix One-line change: declare the array's element type as `string`. This matches the existing pattern used elsewhere in this file (`pages_updated` in the consolidate op) and matches what the implementation already treats them as: ```ts entityHints: Array.isArray(p.entity_hints) ? (p.entity_hints as string[]) : undefined ``` After the patch, the schema validates and the tool dispatches normally. ## Test plan - [x] No code logic change — schema-only correction - [x] `bun test test/serve-http-health.test.ts test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts` — 30/30 pass - [x] `tsc --noEmit` — clean - [ ] Reviewer: invoke `mcp__gbrain__extract_facts` from any Claude client and confirm no `InputValidationError` --- Need help on this PR? title: feat(serve): --bind HOST flag for loopback-only HTTP MCP deployments
body: ## Problem `gbrain serve --http` calls `app.listen(port)` with no host, so Express/Node binds to `0.0.0.0` — every interface on the box. That's the right default behind a reverse proxy or cloud LB, but it's the wrong default when the brain is meant to be consumed only by on-host agents (cron jobs, local Codex sessions, desktop clients tunneling through SSH). Today the only way to lock those deployments down is to patch the source. ## Fix Add a `--bind ` flag that threads through `serve.ts` → `serve-http.ts` → `app.listen(port, host)`: - Default stays `0.0.0.0` to preserve historical behavior. - Operators opt in to loopback-only with `--bind 127.0.0.1` (or `::1` for IPv6). - The startup banner gains a `Bind:` line so the posture is visible in stderr at boot. - `runServeHttp`'s new `bind?` field is optional and defaults to `'0.0.0.0'` inside the function, so any existing programmatic caller continues to work unchanged. ``` $ gbrain serve --http --port 7878 --bind 127.0.0.1 ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ GBrain MCP Server vX.Y.Z ║ ╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣ ║ Bind: 127.0.0.1:7878 ║ ║ Port: 7878 ║ ║ ... ``` ## Test plan - [x] `bun test test/serve-http-health.test.ts test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts` — 30/30 pass - [x] `tsc --noEmit` — clean - [x] Running as a systemd user unit with `--bind 127.0.0.1` for the last several days on a personal node; loopback-only confirmed (`ss -ltn` only shows `127.0.0.1:7878`, no `*:7878`). - [ ] Reviewer: run with no flag and confirm `0.0.0.0` bind (no behavior change vs. main). - [ ] Reviewer: run with `--bind 127.0.0.1` and confirm external interface is not listening. --- Need help on this PR? title: Voyage 2048d provider option is not sent as output_dimension on the wire
body:
## TL;DR

Voyage's OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint only returns the configured vector width when the HTTP request body includes `output_dimension`, but the current GBrain provider-options path gives the AI SDK `output_dimension` directly, which the SDK drops before the request is sent. The result is a quiet schema mismatch for brains initialized at 2048 dimensions: GBrain expects `vector(2048)`, Voyage defaults the response to its provider default, and the first embed fails or stores unusable vectors.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["GBrain config\nembedding_dimensions=2048"] --> B["dimsProviderOptions()"]
  B --> C["AI SDK openai-compatible adapter"]
  C --> D["Voyage HTTP request"]
  D --> E["Voyage response vectors"]

  B -. current .-> X["{ output_dimension: 2048 }"]
  X -. dropped by SDK .-> D

  B --> Y["{ dimensions: 2048 }"]
  Y --> C
  C --> Z["gateway shim rewrites\ndimensions -> output_dimension"]
  Z --> D
```

## Why This Matters

This breaks the exact setup GBrain advertises for modern Voyage recipes: a user can initialize a 2048-dimensional brain successfully, pass schema checks, and still fail at the first real embedding request because the provider never received the dimension instruction.

The bug is especially confusing because upstream already has a Voyage compatibility fetch wrapper that rewrites `dimensions` to `output_dimension`. The missing piece is earlier in the pipeline: the request has to use the SDK-supported key first, otherwise the wrapper never sees anything to rewrite.

## Repro

1. Configure a Voyage 2048-dimensional brain:

```bash
gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model voyage:voyage-4-large --embedding-dimensions 2048
export VOYAGE_API_KEY=...
gbrain providers test --model voyage:voyage-4-large
```

2. Observe the provider request body. Without the fix, `output_dimension` is absent.
3. Voyage returns the provider default vector width instead of 2048.
4. GBrain rejects the vector because the DB schema expects `vector(2048)`.

## Root Cause

`src/core/ai/dims.ts` currently returns this for Voyage models on the OpenAI-compatible adapter:

```ts
{ openaiCompatible: { output_dimension: dims } }
```

The AI SDK OpenAI-compatible adapter forwards `dimensions`; it does not forward arbitrary Voyage-specific `output_dimension` provider options. GBrain's `voyageCompatFetch` already knows how to translate `dimensions` to Voyage's actual wire key, so the resolver should feed the SDK the key it accepts:

```ts
{ openaiCompatible: { dimensions: dims } }
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- `dimsProviderOptions('openai-compatible', 'voyage-4-large', 2048)` returns SDK-compatible `dimensions`.
- The actual HTTP request body sent to Voyage contains `output_dimension: 2048`.
- `encoding_format` remains set so the existing Voyage response shim continues to parse base64 embeddings.
- `voyage-4-nano` participates in the same dimension-output behavior.
- Non-flexible Voyage models still do not receive dimension provider options.

## Agent Implementation Notes

Patch should stay small and provider-specific:

- update `src/core/ai/dims.ts`
- add/adjust tests in `test/ai/gateway.test.ts`
- do not change schema initialization, HNSW policy, provider recipes, or generic OpenAI-compatible behavior in this PR

The important test is a wire-level fetch stub that calls `embed(['dimension probe'])` and asserts the final parsed request body includes `output_dimension: 2048`. A unit assertion on `dimsProviderOptions()` alone is not enough because the failure happens across the SDK boundary.

title: fix: send Voyage output_dimension on embedding requests
body:
## TL;DR

Fixes Voyage 2048-dimensional embeddings by passing `dimensions` into the AI SDK, then letting GBrain's existing Voyage fetch shim translate that to Voyage's real wire field, `output_dimension`. Without this, GBrain can initialize a `vector(2048)` brain but the first Voyage embed request omits the dimension instruction and receives the wrong vector width.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["embedding_dimensions=2048"] --> B["dimsProviderOptions"]
  B --> C["AI SDK openai-compatible"]
  C --> D["voyageCompatFetch"]
  D --> E["Voyage /embeddings"]

  B -->|"SDK key"| C
  C -->|"dimensions"| D
  D -->|"output_dimension"| E
```

## What Changed

- Changes Voyage OpenAI-compatible provider options from `output_dimension` to SDK-forwarded `dimensions`.
- Keeps the existing `voyageCompatFetch` rewrite as the single wire-compatibility point.
- Adds `voyage-4-nano` to the flexible-dimension Voyage model set.
- Adds a wire-level regression test proving the actual Voyage request body contains `output_dimension: 2048`.

## Why This Is The Small Fix

GBrain already has the right architecture: provider dimension knowledge lives in `dims.ts`, and Voyage wire differences live in the gateway fetch wrapper. The bug is just that `dims.ts` was bypassing the SDK contract by passing Voyage's final wire key too early.

This PR keeps the boundary intact:

- `dims.ts`: says "this model needs dimensions"
- AI SDK: receives the supported `dimensions` option
- `voyageCompatFetch`: translates to Voyage's `output_dimension`

## Non-Goals

- No schema changes.
- No HNSW changes.
- No pricing/default-dimension changes.
- No changes to unrelated OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Attempted focused local test: `bun test test/ai/gateway.test.ts`
  - Could not run in the fresh upstream worktree because dependencies are not installed there: `Cannot find package 'ai'`.

title: OAuth authorization_code grant always returns invalid_client (SDK middleware vs hashed secret column)
body:
# Draft GitHub issue — file at github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/new

**To file:** `gh issue create --repo garrytan/gbrain --title "<title>" --body-file <this file's path>`

(Or paste the body via the GitHub web UI. Title suggestion below the rule.)

---

**Title:** `OAuth authorization_code grant always returns invalid_client (SDK middleware vs hashed secret column)`

---

## Summary

`gbrain serve --http` rejects every `authorization_code` exchange with `{"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client_secret"}`, even when the client sends the exact correct plaintext secret. `client_credentials` exchanges with the same client and secret succeed.

Root cause: `GBrainOAuthProvider.getClient()` populates the SDK's `OAuthClientInformationFull.client_secret` field with the SHA-256 hash from the `oauth_clients.client_secret_hash` column. The MCP SDK's `authenticateClient` middleware (used on every grant **except** the custom `client_credentials` handler) does a plaintext string comparison against that field, which never matches the plaintext the client sends.

Reproducible against any confidential client. Affects every OAuth client trying to connect Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, or any other authorization_code + PKCE flow.

## Repro (1 minute)

```bash
# 1. Register a client (gives you a plaintext client_secret).
gbrain auth register-client test-client --grant-types authorization_code,client_credentials,refresh_token --scopes "read write"

# 2. Generate PKCE pair.
VERIFIER=$(python3 -c "import secrets;print(secrets.token_urlsafe(64)[:96])")
CHALLENGE=$(python3 -c "import hashlib,base64,sys;v=sys.argv[1];print(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(v.encode()).digest()).rstrip(b'=').decode())" "$VERIFIER")

# 3. Get an auth code.
curl -s -i "http://localhost:3131/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=$CID&redirect_uri=$REDIRECT&code_challenge=$CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256&state=t&scope=read+write"
# → 302 Location: $REDIRECT?code=gbrain_code_...

# 4. Exchange (fails).
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3131/token \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=authorization_code" \
  --data-urlencode "code=gbrain_code_..." \
  --data-urlencode "redirect_uri=$REDIRECT" \
  --data-urlencode "client_id=$CID" \
  --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CSECRET" \
  --data-urlencode "code_verifier=$VERIFIER"
# → HTTP 400 {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client_secret"}

# 5. But client_credentials with the same secret works.
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3131/token \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  --data-urlencode "client_id=$CID" \
  --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CSECRET"
# → 200 {"access_token":"gbrain_at_...",...}
```

## Root cause (verbatim from source)

`src/core/oauth-provider.ts:133-149` — `getClient` returns the hash in the `client_secret` field:

```ts
async getClient(clientId: string): Promise<OAuthClientInformationFull | undefined> {
  const rows = await this.sql`
    SELECT client_id, client_secret_hash, client_name, redirect_uris,
           grant_types, scope, token_endpoint_auth_method,
           client_id_issued_at, client_secret_expires_at
    FROM oauth_clients WHERE client_id = ${clientId}
  `;
  if (rows.length === 0) return undefined;
  const r = rows[0]!;
  return {
    client_id: r.client_id as string,
    client_secret: r.client_secret_hash as string | undefined,  // ← hash, not plaintext
    ...
  };
}
```

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/.../middleware/clientAuth.js` — does plaintext compare:

```js
if (client.client_secret) {
    if (!client_secret) {
        throw new InvalidClientError('Client secret is required');
    }
    if (client.client_secret !== client_secret) {     // ← hex hash ≠ plaintext, always throws
        throw new InvalidClientError('Invalid client_secret');
    }
    ...
}
```

`client_credentials` is unaffected because gbrain's custom handler at `src/commands/serve-http.ts:261-279` intercepts that grant and hashes the incoming secret before comparing to `client_secret_hash` itself. The bug is exposed only when the SDK's middleware path is reached (everything except `client_credentials`).

## Why this matters

Every authorization_code + PKCE client breaks against a confidential gbrain OAuth client. This is the canonical flow for:
- Claude Desktop's Settings → Connectors
- ChatGPT custom GPT connectors
- Cursor / Windsurf / any browser-OAuth MCP client

Workaround: convert the client to public (`token_endpoint_auth_method='none'`, `client_secret_hash=NULL`) so the SDK middleware skips the check entirely. That's arguably the right posture for MCP clients per the spec, but it shouldn't be the only workable posture — confidential clients should work too, and there's nothing in `gbrain auth register-client`'s docs that tells users to register clients as public for browser-OAuth flows.

## Suggested fixes (any of these, happy to PR)

1. **In gbrain — verify in `getClient`'s caller side.** Add a `verifyClientSecret(clientId, plaintext): Promise<boolean>` method on `GBrainOAuthProvider`, plug it into the SDK via a custom middleware wired before `mcpAuthRouter`, and stop returning the hash in the SDK's `client_secret` field. Cleanest.
2. **In gbrain — return a sentinel in `client_secret`** that signals "compare via custom path." Pass `client_secret: '__verified_externally__'` and override the SDK's middleware to delegate verification to gbrain. Hackier.
3. **Fix the SDK** to call a separate `verifyClientSecret` hook instead of doing direct equality on `client.client_secret`. Probably the right long-term shape but requires a separate PR upstream of gbrain.

## Additional observation (separate but related)

`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` returns 404. Per RFC 9728, when the protected resource is at `<server>/mcp`, the discovery URL should be `<server>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` (resource path appended). Clients fall back to `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (no suffix) which gbrain serves, so it's not blocking, but worth tightening for spec compliance.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.32.0 (master HEAD as of 2026-05-10)
- Postgres engine (Supabase 17.6.1)
- Reproduced on both Bun-on-Linux (Railway deploy) and Bun-on-Windows (local)

title: fix(serve): skip stdin EOF handlers when MCP_STDIO=1
body: ## Bug When `gbrain serve` is spawned by OpenClaw's gateway with `MCP_STDIO=1`, the gateway's `bundle-mcp` layer creates a piped stdin that delivers EOF immediately after the initial JSON-RPC handshake. This triggers premature `engine.disconnect()` and process exit, preventing the MCP server from handling any tool calls. Error seen in gateway logs: ``` failed to start server "gbrain" ... MCP error -32000: Connection closed ``` ## Root cause Two locations listen for stdin `'end'`/`'close'` to trigger graceful shutdown: 1. **`src/mcp/server.ts:startMcpServer()`** — the MCP SDK lifecycle handler 2. **`src/commands/serve.ts:installStdioLifecycle()`** — the parent watchdog (v0.32) Both treat stdin EOF as "client disconnected permanently." With `MCP_STDIO=1`, the pipe EOF fires at handshake completion but the session continues. ## Fix Guard both stdin EOF handlers with `process.env.MCP_STDIO !== '1'`. Signal handlers (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP) and `transport.onclose` remain active so the process still exits cleanly when appropriate. **Files changed:** - `src/mcp/server.ts` — guard stdin handlers - `src/commands/serve.ts` — extend `skipStdinEndShutdown` check - `test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts` — add regression test ## Verification ```bash # Without fix: gbrain exits immediately with "Connection closed" # With fix: gbrain stays alive and handles tool calls MCP_STDIO=1 DATA_DIR=/root/.gbrain bun run src/cli.ts serve ``` All 23 stdio lifecycle tests pass (22 existing + 1 new). --- **Testing**: `bun test test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts` — 23 pass, 0 fail --- Need help on this PR? title: v0.32.4 feat: add sync_freshness check to gbrain doctor
body:
## Summary

Adds a `sync_freshness` health check to `gbrain doctor` that catches the silent failure mode where `gbrain sync` quietly stopped running. Pure staleness probe — reads `sources.last_sync_at` only, no filesystem access. Warns at 24h, fails at 72h. Env-var thresholds. Future-timestamp warning. Source-id-in-message so the printed fix command actually copy-pastes.

Surfaces in both `runDoctor` (local) and `doctorReportRemote` (thin-client over MCP).

## Scope reframed mid-PR

Original PR shipped with a best-effort filesystem-vs-DB page drift detector. `/plan-eng-review` then `/codex` surfaced two P0s the eng review missed:

1. **Trust boundary leak.** `doctorReportRemote` runs inside the HTTP MCP server (`src/commands/serve-http.ts`). Walking DB-supplied `local_path` values from a remotely-callable endpoint leaks filesystem signal — an OAuth `write`-scoped client could mutate `sources.local_path` and probe arbitrary server paths via the timing/count signal.
2. **Future-`last_sync_at` silently fell through as `ok`.** Negative `ageMs` from clock skew or a corrupted DB write skipped both threshold tests. Now warns with "clock skew or corrupted timestamp."

Codex recommended stripping FS drift entirely from `sync_freshness` for v0.32.4 — staleness only. Drift detection belongs in the existing `multi_source_drift` check which already has `GBRAIN_DRIFT_LIMIT` + `GBRAIN_DRIFT_TIMEOUT_MS` guards, and runs only in local trusted `runDoctor`. Drift will resurface in a follow-up PR with slug normalization tests, meta-file allow-list, and bidirectional set-diff.

Plan file: `~/.claude/plans/rippling-crunching-newell.md` (eng review + codex outside voice + final scope decision).

## Test Coverage

12 unit tests in `test/doctor.test.ts` ("v0.32.4 — sync_freshness check" describe block):

- empty sources → ok
- `last_sync_at IS NULL` → fail with "never been synced"
- `>72h ago` → fail with day-rounded "Nd ago"
- exact 72h boundary → warn (strict `>` semantics)
- 24h-72h → warn with hour-rounded "Nh ago"
- exact 24h boundary → ok (strict `>` semantics)
- `<24h` → ok with "N federated source(s) synced recently"
- future `last_sync_at` → warn (clock skew or corrupted timestamp)
- mixed sources (one fail + one warn) → fail with both listed
- `executeRaw` throws → outer-catch warn
- env override `GBRAIN_SYNC_FRESHNESS_FAIL_HOURS=6` → 7h-stale fails
- source.id-in-message regression (named source still uses id for fix command)

## Pre-Landing Review

- `/plan-eng-review` found 7 issues (2 P1, 4 P2, 1 P3). Initial amend scope agreed on `walkBrainRepo` route + slug-set-diff drift.
- `/codex` outside voice surfaced 13 challenges including the 2 P0s above. Strongest argument: strip drift entirely. Accepted.
- Final amend addresses 5 of the 7 eng review findings + both codex P0s in one revised commit set.

Deferred follow-ups (filed as P1+P2 in plan file):
- Resurrect FS drift through `multi_source_drift` with proper guards, LOCAL-DOCTOR-ONLY.
- Slug normalization audit between `walkBrainRepo` and `engine.getAllSlugs()`.

## Test Suite

```
bun run verify    →  PASS  (privacy + jsonb + progress + test-isolation + wasm + admin-build + admin-scope-drift + cli-exec + typecheck)
bun run test      →  4,249 pass, 1 fail (pre-existing perf flake unrelated to PR), 0 skip
```

Single failure: `test/eval-longmemeval.test.ts:194` warm-create p50 perf gate. Got 600ms vs 500ms threshold. Pre-existing, hardware-timing-flaky, zero overlap with this PR (which only touches `doctor.ts`).

## Version

```
VERSION       0.32.0  →  0.32.4
package.json  0.32.0  →  0.32.4
```

## To take advantage of v0.32.4

`gbrain upgrade` ships the binary. No migration, no config:

```bash
gbrain doctor   # look for the new sync_freshness row
```

Customize thresholds if defaults don't fit:
```bash
GBRAIN_SYNC_FRESHNESS_WARN_HOURS=12 gbrain doctor
GBRAIN_SYNC_FRESHNESS_FAIL_HOURS=24 gbrain doctor
```

Thin-client users: `gbrain remote doctor` includes the same check end-to-end through MCP.

title: feat: gbrain-context OpenClaw context engine — deterministic temporal/spatial injection
body: ## What Adds a context engine plugin (`gbrain-context`) that injects structured live context into the system prompt on **every `assemble()` call**. ### Injected context (deterministic, <5ms, zero LLM calls): - **Garry's current local time** — computed from `heartbeat-state.json` timezone, not hardcoded US/Pacific - **Current location** — city + timezone from heartbeat or active flight data - **Home time** — shown when traveling (e.g. `Mon 7:58 AM PT`) - **Active travel** — flight number + route when in transit - **Quiet hours** — detection based on local time + garryAwake flag - **Airport→timezone mapping** — 30+ airports for automatic tz resolution from flights ### Why The compaction-induced "time warp" bug: when sessions compact, the LLM loses track of the user's current time, location, and state. This caused Wintermute to respond to a Sunday night photo as if it were happening Monday morning, and to report Pacific Time when the user was in Toronto. The context engine fixes this **architecturally** — no matter how aggressively context gets compacted, live state is reinjected fresh on every turn. ### Architecture - **`src/core/context-engine.ts`** — Engine implementation. SDK-free, independently testable. Reads `memory/heartbeat-state.json` and `memory/upcoming-flights.json`. - **`src/openclaw-context-engine.ts`** — Plugin entry point. Uses `definePluginEntry` + `api.registerContextEngine()`. - **`ownsCompaction: false`** — Delegates compaction to legacy runtime. Only owns `systemPromptAddition`. ### Enable ```json { "plugins": { "slots": { "contextEngine": "gbrain-context" } } } ``` ## Testing 9 tests, all passing: - Engine info validation - systemPromptAddition injection with Toronto timezone - US/Pacific fallback when no location set - Messages pass-through (unchanged reference) - Ingest no-op - Quiet hours detection - Day-of-week validation - Graceful handling of missing workspace files - Token estimation from message content ``` bun test test/context-engine.test.ts # 9 pass, 0 fail, 20 expect() calls [106ms] ``` --- Need help on this PR?
