(Per #799 reporter on a different project: 869 doctor warnings, all node_modules MISSING_OPEN.)

### After (this PR)

**`gbrain frontmatter validate`:**
```
$ gbrain frontmatter validate /Users/watson/projects/veefriends-kb
OK — 55 file(s) scanned, no frontmatter issues
```

55 files scanned instead of 126 — node_modules/ correctly skipped.

**`gbrain doctor`:**
> 2099 frontmatter issue(s) across 10 source(s)

Drop of 71 (= the vfkb node_modules false-positives now correctly excluded). The remaining 2099 are real MISSING_OPEN cases in registered diary paths, not node_modules.

### Regression check — non-node_modules source still reports real issues

```
$ gbrain frontmatter validate ~/atlas/agents/terminal/memory
Found 7 issue(s) across 7 file(s) (scanned 135)
```

Same count before and after on a source without `node_modules/`.

## Verification

```
$ bun run typecheck
$ tsc --noEmit
(exit 0)

$ bun run verify
OK: no JSON.stringify(x)::jsonb interpolation pattern in src/
OK: max_stalled defaults are 5 in all schema sources
OK: all rowToPage feeder projections include source_id
check-progress-to-stdout: OK (no banned stdout \r patterns)
check-test-isolation: OK (367 non-serial unit files scanned)
[check-wasm-embedded] OK — compiled binary produced real semantic chunks.
[check-admin-scope-drift] ok: 5 scopes match
OK: src/cli.ts is git-tracked as executable (100755)
OK: no direct derived-table writes outside the reconcile layer in src/ + scripts/
(all 11 checks pass)
```

## What was NOT tested

- **`.obsidian` exclusion** wasn't exercised against a real Obsidian vault in this session. Followed the existing pattern from `walkDir():421` which includes `.obsidian` — behavior is identical to that walker.
- **No unit test added** — the existing `test/frontmatter-*.test.ts` files don't have a fixture for "walker recurses into excluded directories." Adding one would require a fixture project with a `node_modules/` shim. Happy to add one if you'd prefer.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Reviewer runs `gbrain frontmatter validate <any-node-project>` pre and post fix; node_modules entries should disappear post-fix
- [ ] Reviewer runs `gbrain doctor` on the same project; `frontmatter_integrity` count should drop by the number of node_modules `.md` files

## Commits

title: gbrain frontmatter validate walks node_modules/, inflating MISSING_OPEN counts in doctor
body:
## Summary

`gbrain frontmatter validate <path>` (and by extension the `frontmatter_integrity` check in `gbrain doctor`) walks every subdirectory under `<path>`, including `node_modules/`, `.git/`, and other non-content directories. This produces large false-positive counts of `MISSING_OPEN` warnings on any source repo that vendors npm packages.

The sibling `gbrain frontmatter generate` walker filters these directories correctly. The two walkers should behave consistently.

## Repro

\`\`\`bash
mkdir test-source && cd test-source
npm init -y && npm i express
gbrain sources add test --path "\$(pwd)"
gbrain doctor 2>&1 | grep frontmatter_integrity
\`\`\`

Expected: 0 issues (no content yet).
Actual: tens to hundreds of \`MISSING_OPEN\` issues, all inside \`node_modules/\`.

I hit this on a real-world setup pointing gbrain at a TypeScript project (Bun + node_modules + a docs/ folder). 7 real content issues got drowned in 226 false positives from npm package READMEs.

## Root cause

Two walkers in [\`src/commands/frontmatter.ts\`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/src/commands/frontmatter.ts):

- **\`generate\` walker** (line ~421) correctly skips:
  \`\`\`ts
  if (entry === '.git' || entry === 'node_modules' || entry === '.obsidian') continue;
  \`\`\`

- **\`validate\` walker** (lines ~243–264) has no such filter. It pushes every directory onto its DFS stack and only filters per-file via \`isSyncable\`, which doesn't reject the \`node_modules\` prefix.

Result: doctor's \`frontmatter_integrity\` check (which uses the validate path) reports inflated counts that operators cannot resolve via \`--fix\` since the files aren't theirs. The warning becomes load-bearing noise that erodes trust in doctor's output.

## Suggested fix

Add the same skip predicate to the validate walker:

\`\`\`ts
for (const name of entries) {
  if (name === '.git' || name === 'node_modules' || name === '.obsidian') continue;
  // ...existing per-entry logic
}
\`\`\`

Both walkers should ideally share a single helper (\`shouldSkipDirEntry(name)\`) to prevent this from drifting again.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.33.0
- Windows 11, Bun 1.3.13
- Postgres engine (Supabase pooler)
- Reproduces against vanilla \`node_modules/\` from \`npm init\`

## Notes

Happy to send a PR for the one-line fix if useful — let me know.

title: fix(recipes/openai): add max_batch_tokens to embedding touchpoint
body: # PR: Add max_batch_tokens to OpenAI recipe ## Problem `src/core/ai/recipes/openai.ts` is the only embedding recipe in the codebase without a `max_batch_tokens` cap. Every other provider declares one (voyage=120K, azure-openai=8K, dashscope=8K, zhipu=8K, minimax=4K). Without `max_batch_tokens`, gbrain's recursive-halving safety net never engages. The batcher dispatches whatever fits in its char-based estimator window — typically ~150K-200K tokens per request — and any page with token-dense content (Discord exports, JSON dumps, code-heavy pages) tips a single request past OpenAI's 1M-token TPM ceiling. Retry storm follows. First-failed request blocks the queue head; subsequent passes hit the same fat page first and never progress. Reproduction: 1. Init brain with Postgres engine. 2. Sync a corpus containing a few discord-full chat exports (~800K chars each). 3. `gbrain embed --stale`. 4. Observe `Rate limit reached ... TPM: Limit 1000000, Used 1000000, Requested 150000` on the same 4-5 pages every pass. ## Fix Add `max_batch_tokens: 100_000` to the OpenAI embedding touchpoint. Why 100K and not 200K-250K (closer to OpenAI's 300K per-request cap): - gbrain's batcher estimates tokens as `chars / 4`. - Token-dense content (markdown+JSON, code blocks, timestamps in Discord/Slack dumps) tokenizes at ~chars/2.7. A 100K estimated batch can be ~150K real tokens. - 100K estimated = ~150K worst-case real, safely under the 300K/request hard cap. - Also gives recursive-halving room to work on outlier pages without thrashing. ## Diff ```diff embedding: { models: ['text-embedding-3-large', 'text-embedding-3-small'], default_dims: 1536, dims_options: [256, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 3072], cost_per_1m_tokens_usd: 0.13, price_last_verified: '2026-04-20', + max_batch_tokens: 100_000, }, ``` ## Tested - Local gbrain install (v0.33.0, Postgres+pgvector) cleared its embedding queue after the patch where 5 prior passes had been stuck. - No regression on small batches — recursive-halving only engages when estimated batch tokens exceed cap. ## Related The doctor warning `recipe "google" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps` is the exact issue this PR fixes for OpenAI. Google recipe should get the same treatment — happy to add that in a follow-up. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith with what you need. - [ ] Let Codesmith autofix CI failures and bot reviews

title: bug: reject partial or mixed-dimension embedding responses before indexing
body:
## TL;DR

GBrain should reject embedding responses unless the provider returns exactly one vector for each input text and every vector matches the configured schema dimensions. Today the gateway only checks the first returned vector's dimensions, so a partial or mixed-dimension provider response can silently misalign chunks, skip rows, or write unsafe embeddings.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["texts[0..N]"] --> B["embedMany"]
  B --> C["provider response"]
  C --> D{"count == N?"}
  D -->|"no"| E["fail before indexing"]
  D -->|"yes"| F{"every vector dim == schema?"}
  F -->|"no"| E
  F -->|"yes"| G["write chunk embeddings"]
```

## Why This Matters

The embedding table is a database contract: chunk row `i` must receive the vector for input text `i`, and that vector must match `content_chunks.embedding vector(N)`. If a provider, proxy, shim, or degraded endpoint returns fewer vectors than requested, GBrain should fail closed before indexing.

This is provider-neutral. It protects OpenAI, Voyage, Gemini, LiteLLM, local servers, and any future OpenAI-compatible provider.

## Root Cause

The current gateway checks only the first returned embedding's dimensions:

```ts
const first = result.embeddings?.[0];
if (first && Array.isArray(first) && first.length !== expectedDims) { ... }
```

That misses two important cases:

1. partial response: 2 input texts, 1 returned vector
2. mixed response: first vector is correct width, later vector is wrong width

## Acceptance Criteria

- If `result.embeddings.length !== texts.length`, throw `AIConfigError` before returning vectors.
- If any returned vector has the wrong dimension, throw `AIConfigError` before returning vectors.
- The error message should make the operator action clear: retry/check provider health for partial responses; migrate/change model for dimension mismatch.
- Add tests for partial response and later-vector dimension mismatch.

## Agent Implementation Notes

Keep this PR small:

- touch `src/core/ai/gateway.ts`
- add focused tests in `test/ai/gateway.test.ts`
- do not change provider recipes, batching, schema, or retry behavior

The fix belongs immediately after `embedMany()` returns and before `recordSubBatchSuccess(recipe)`.

title: fix: reject partial embedding responses
body:
## TL;DR

Fails closed when an embedding provider returns fewer vectors than requested or any returned vector has the wrong dimension. This prevents GBrain from silently misaligning chunk rows with provider output before data reaches `content_chunks.embedding`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant G as GBrain gateway
  participant P as Embedding provider
  participant DB as content_chunks
  G->>P: embedMany([text A, text B])
  P-->>G: [vector A only]
  G--xDB: reject before indexing
```

Closes #925.

## What Changed

- Verifies `result.embeddings` is an array with exactly one vector per input text.
- Verifies every returned vector matches the configured schema dimension, not just the first vector.
- Adds regression tests for partial responses and mixed-dimension responses.

## Why

Embeddings are positional. If two texts go into the provider, two vectors must come back in the same order. A partial response is not a degraded success; it is unsafe to index because downstream code cannot know which chunk was omitted.

Similarly, checking only the first vector lets a mixed-dimension response pass until a later write or query path fails in a less obvious place.

## Non-Goals

- No provider recipe changes.
- No retry-policy changes.
- No schema or migration changes.
- No batching changes.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Attempted focused local test: `bun test test/ai/gateway.test.ts`
  - Could not run in the fresh upstream worktree because dependencies are not installed there: `Cannot find package 'ai'`.
  - GitHub Actions should run the full dependency-backed suite.

## Agent Review Notes

The critical invariant is that `recordSubBatchSuccess(recipe)` is called only after both checks pass:

1. returned vector count equals input text count
2. every returned vector width equals configured `embedding_dimensions`

title: fix: scope v0.32.2 facts migration dirty checks
body: ## TL;DR Fixes a false-failure path in migration `v0.32.2`: Phase B now queries legacy facts first and dirty-checks only the source worktrees it would actually write. A dirty unrelated source no longer blocks a no-op facts migration or a migration whose fenced writes touch another source. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["legacy facts"] --> B{"fenceable groups?"} B -->|"none"| C["complete no-op"] B -->|"yes"| D["collect touched source_ids"] D --> E["dirty-check touched sources only"] E --> F["write fences"] ``` Closes #927. Complements #921 by removing one concrete false-failure case before the CLI error-surface work. ## What Changed - `isLocalPathDirty()` still treats non-git sources as allowed, but now fails closed on unexpected git probe errors. - Phase B reads legacy fact rows before dirty-checking source trees. - Phase B returns complete immediately when there is no legacy work. - Dirty-tree refusal now applies only to source IDs that have fenceable writes in this migration. - Adds regression tests for: - no legacy facts - structurally unfenceable facts - unrelated dirty source - targeted dirty source refusal - unexpected git probe failure ## Why Dirty-tree refusal is a safety guard for filesystem writes. It should fire when the migration is about to mutate a source, not when a registered source happens to be dirty but irrelevant to this migration pass. The old order could wedge a healthy install that had nothing to migrate. ## Non-Goals - Does not change facts schema. - Does not weaken targeted dirty-tree refusal. - Does not change #921's CLI detail rendering; this PR removes a false-failure path but does not redesign migration output. ## Validation - `git diff --check` - Attempted focused local test: `bun test test/migrations-v0_32_2.test.ts` - Could not run in the fresh upstream worktree because dependencies are not installed there: missing `@electric-sql/pglite`. - GitHub Actions should run full dependency-backed validation. --- Need help on this PR? title: bug: embed --stale --source should scope stale chunk queries by source_id
body:
## TL;DR

`gbrain embed --stale --source <id>` should only count, list, read, and write stale chunks for that source. Today the stale fast path accepts `--source` at the CLI level but the SQL stale-count/list queries are global, so multi-source brains can do unnecessary work and same-slug pages can still be routed through the wrong source unless every downstream call is carefully re-scoped.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["multi-source brain"] --> B["default: shared-slug"]
  A --> C["openclaw-support-kb: shared-slug"]
  D["gbrain embed --stale --source openclaw-support-kb"] --> E["count/list stale chunks"]
  E -->|"current: global"| F["sees stale work outside requested source"]
  E -->|"desired: source-scoped"| G["only KB stale chunks"]
  G --> H["getChunks/upsertChunks with source_id=openclaw-support-kb"]
```

## Why This Matters

This is both correctness and cost control:

- **Correctness:** duplicate slugs are valid across sources. Any stale-embed path must treat `(source_id, slug)` as the page identity.
- **Cost:** recurring jobs often want to refresh one source, such as a support KB, without scanning or embedding unrelated user docs.
- **Operator trust:** if a user asks for `--source openclaw-support-kb`, the command should not count or process stale chunks from every source.

## Related Work

This complements existing source-isolation/source-sync issues such as #891 and egress work such as #775. It is narrower than a full sync rewrite: this issue is specifically the stale embedding path.

## Root Cause

`runEmbed()` parses `--source`, but the stale path calls:

```ts
engine.countStaleChunks()
engine.listStaleChunks()
```

without passing a source filter. The engine methods also do not accept source-scoped options yet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BrainEngine.countStaleChunks(opts?: { sourceId?: string })` supports optional source scoping.
- `BrainEngine.listStaleChunks(opts?: { sourceId?: string })` supports optional source scoping.
- Postgres and PGLite implementations filter by `pages.source_id` when `sourceId` is provided.
- Image chunks are not treated as stale text embeddings.
- `embed --stale --source <id>` passes source scope into stale count/list queries.
- Stale rows are grouped by `(source_id, slug)` before `getChunks`/`upsertChunks`.
- Tests prove duplicate slugs do not fall back to `default` and source-scoped stale queries are actually scoped.

## Agent Implementation Notes

Recommended small patch shape:

- update the `BrainEngine` interface method signatures
- update `PostgresEngine.countStaleChunks/listStaleChunks`
- update `PGLiteEngine.countStaleChunks/listStaleChunks`
- update `src/commands/embed.ts` so `embedAllStale()` receives and forwards `sourceId`
- add one focused test file that mocks `embedBatch` and asserts `getChunks`/`upsertChunks` receive the stale row's `source_id`

Do not broaden this PR into all source-isolation fixes. Keep it to stale embedding behavior.

title: fix: scope stale embedding queries by source
body: ## TL;DR Makes `gbrain embed --stale --source ` actually source-scoped from SQL preflight through chunk writes. The stale fast path now counts/lists only stale chunks for the requested source, excludes image rows from text embedding staleness, and groups work by `(source_id, slug)` before calling `getChunks`/`upsertChunks`. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI as embed --stale --source kb participant DB as content_chunks + pages participant Emb as embedBatch CLI->>DB: countStaleChunks({sourceId:"kb"}) CLI->>DB: listStaleChunks({sourceId:"kb"}) CLI->>DB: getChunks(slug,{sourceId:"kb"}) CLI->>Emb: embed stale text chunks CLI->>DB: upsertChunks(slug,chunks,{sourceId:"kb"}) ``` Closes #929. ## What Changed - Adds optional `{ sourceId }` to `BrainEngine.countStaleChunks()` and `BrainEngine.listStaleChunks()`. - Implements source filters in Postgres and PGLite stale chunk queries. - Filters out image-modality rows from text stale embedding checks. - Threads `sourceId` through `embedAllStale()`. - Groups stale rows by composite `(source_id, slug)` identity. - Adds a focused test proving stale rows from `openclaw-support-kb` write back to that source, not `default`. ## Why `--source` should be a cost and correctness boundary. title: feat: add OpenClaw native adapter package
body: ## TL;DR This PR adds an optional OpenClaw-native adapter package for GBrain. The existing root `openclaw.plugin.json` is still useful and stays in place: it is the bundle plugin for skills, MCP, and `gbrain-context`. This new package covers the layer the root bundle does not: OpenClaw-native tools, an OpenClaw CLI command, and the authenticated `/plugins/gbrain/extract` route with timeout, queue, and file-size limits. ```mermaid flowchart LR Root["root openclaw.plugin.json\nskills + MCP + context engine"] --> Host["OpenClaw"] Adapter["plugins/openclaw-gbrain\nnative adapter package"] --> Host Host --> Tools["gbrain_status / search / query"] Host --> Route["/plugins/gbrain/extract"] Route --> Runtime["OpenClaw logged-in model runtime"] Tools --> CLI["local gbrain CLI"] ``` ## Why This Is Better Than Only The Root Plugin The root bundle is good for making GBrain visible to OpenClaw as a knowledge/skill package. It is not enough for OpenClaw-native product use cases because it does not register host tools, does not expose an extraction route, and does not own host-side pressure controls. This adapter adds the missing host-native surface without replacing the root bundle: | Surface | Root `openclaw.plugin.json` | New `plugins/openclaw-gbrain` | | --- | --- | --- | | GBrain skills | yes | no duplicate skill tree | | `gbrain serve` MCP | yes | uses local CLI helpers only | | `gbrain-context` | yes | no duplicate context engine | | OpenClaw-native tools | no | `gbrain_status`, `gbrain_search`, `gbrain_query` | | OpenClaw CLI command | no | `openclaw gbrain status` | | OAuth-backed extraction route | no | `/plugins/gbrain/extract` | | Rate/queue/file limits | no | plugin-level timeout, queue, interval, and file-size guards | So the root plugin remains the default bundle. This package is the optional adapter for OpenClaw installs that need native tools and host-owned extraction. ## What Changed - Adds `plugins/openclaw-gbrain/` with: - `openclaw.plugin.json` - `package.json` - `README.md` - `index.js` - Registers: - `gbrain_status` - `gbrain_search` - `gbrain_query` - `openclaw gbrain status` - authenticated `/plugins/gbrain/extract` - Adds extraction pressure controls: - `maxConcurrentExtractions` - `extractionQueueLimit` - `extractionQueueTimeoutMs` - `minExtractionIntervalMs` - `maxExtractionFileBytes` - Keeps spawned command env behavior explicit: - optional `~/.gbrain/gbrain.env` fills missing values - runtime/OpenClaw env wins over file env - `$HOME/.bun/bin` is prepended for LaunchAgent-style PATHs - Adds a static contract test for the plugin boundary. - Documents the adapter in the README next to the MCP/OpenClaw setup section. - Regenerates `llms-full.txt` after README changes. ## Boundaries - This does not remove or replace root `openclaw.plugin.json`. - This does not move OpenClaw-specific extraction into GBrain core. - This does not embed a second GBrain runtime. - This does not accept arbitrary command strings; command paths are configurable, arguments are built internally. - This does not add user-supplied model API-key fields to the extraction payload. - The extraction route is host-owned and requires OpenClaw gateway auth. ## Validation Ran in `/Volumes/LEXAR/repos/gbrain-upstream-prs/openclaw-plugin`: - `bun install --frozen-lockfile` - `bun run build:llms` - `git diff --check` - `bun test test/openclaw-gbrain-plugin-contract.test.ts test/build-llms.test.ts` - result: 12 pass / 0 fail - `node --check plugins/openclaw-gbrain/index.js` - `bun run check:privacy` Related: #643, #544. --- Need help on this PR? title: OAuth verifyAccessToken returns 500 instead of 401 on invalid bearer token (v0.33.0)
body:
## Bug

`verifyAccessToken` in `src/core/oauth-provider.ts` throws plain `Error` instances when a bearer token is invalid or expired. The MCP SDK's `requireBearerAuth` middleware (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/auth/middleware/bearerAuth.js`) classifies thrown errors:
- `InvalidTokenError` → HTTP 401 + WWW-Authenticate (per RFC 6749 / RFC 6750)
- `InsufficientScopeError` → HTTP 403
- `ServerError` → HTTP 500
- **Anything else (plain `Error`) → HTTP 500 with `server_error`**

Because gbrain throws plain `Error`, bearer-token validation failures return HTTP 500 `server_error` instead of the canonical RFC 6750 401 `invalid_token`.

## Reproducer

```bash
# Server v0.33.0 running (postgres engine, OAuth clients registered)
curl -X POST https://your-gbrain/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer invalid_token" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'

# Actual:
# {"error":"server_error","error_description":"Internal Server Error"}
# HTTP/2 500

# Expected (per RFC 6750 §3.1):
# {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"Invalid token"}
# HTTP/2 401
# WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Invalid token"
```

Verified on both local (macOS) and remote (Railway) v0.33.0 deployments.

## Root cause

`src/core/oauth-provider.ts`:
- Line ~423: `throw new Error('Token expired');`
- Line ~458: `throw new Error('Invalid token');`

Both inside `verifyAccessToken`. SDK `bearerAuth.js:53-69` catch block routes plain `Error` to the `else` branch:

```js
else {
  const serverError = new ServerError('Internal Server Error');
  res.status(500).json(serverError.toResponseObject());
}
```

## Suggested fix

```diff
 import type { AuthInfo } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/auth/types.js';
+import { InvalidTokenError } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/auth/errors.js';
 import { hashToken, generateToken, isUndefinedColumnError } from './utils.ts';

   ...
   const expiresAt = coerceTimestamp(row.expires_at);
   if (expiresAt === undefined || expiresAt < now) {
-    throw new Error('Token expired');
+    throw new InvalidTokenError('Token expired');
   }
   ...
-  throw new Error('Invalid token');
+  throw new InvalidTokenError('Invalid token');
```

**Caveat:** I tried this patch locally. It typechecks (`bun run typecheck` passes) and works perfectly when running via `bun run src/cli.ts serve --http`. But `bun build --compile` then fails at runtime — the binary exits silently. My hypothesis is that the deep import path `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/auth/errors.js` doesn't bundle correctly with `bun build --compile` (the SDK's `exports` map uses a `./*` glob fallback for this path rather than an explicit entry). The interpreted path is fine.

Possible workarounds for the build issue:
1. Re-export `InvalidTokenError` from a path that IS explicit in the SDK's `exports` map.
2. Define a local class that extends the SDK's `OAuthError` with `errorCode = 'invalid_token'` so `instanceof InvalidTokenError` still matches via the prototype chain (or `instanceof OAuthError` in the SDK side).
3. Lazy `await import()` inside `verifyAccessToken`.

## Impact

- Security posture: clients receive misleading 500 `server_error` on invalid tokens (suggests server bug) instead of clean 401 `invalid_token` (which clients should auto-refresh on).
- Spec compliance: RFC 6750 §3.1 requires 401 + `WWW-Authenticate` for invalid bearer tokens.
- Client behavior: well-behaved OAuth clients (claude.ai web app's token-refresh logic) interpret 500 as transient and retry instead of refreshing the token.

## Doctrine references

- `SECURITY.md` — OAuth 2.1 compliance section
- `docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md` — DEPLOY troubleshooting cites "missing_auth" and "invalid_token" as canonical client-facing error codes

## Notes

- Same pattern may apply to refresh-token validation throws (lines ~367, ~374) but those go through `mcpAuthRouter` `/token` endpoint (RFC 6749 §5.2 → HTTP 400 `invalid_grant`), not bearerAuth. Out of scope for this fix.
- Found during a forensic audit of a Railway-deployed `gbrain serve --http` instance integrated with claude.ai web — happy to share the audit notes if useful.

title: feat(autopilot): allow GBRAIN_AUTOPILOT_MAX_RSS_MB env override for worker RSS watchdog
body: # feat(autopilot): allow GBRAIN_AUTOPILOT_MAX_RSS_MB env override for worker RSS watchdog Branch: `feat/autopilot-rss-env-overlay` Base: `master` Commit: `23869b2` ## Motivation The autopilot supervisor in `src/commands/autopilot.ts` hardcodes the Minions worker RSS watchdog at 2048 MB: ```ts const args = ['jobs', 'work', '--max-rss', '2048']; ``` On hosts that legitimately need a higher ceiling (large embed batches, mirror imports, multi-source ingest cycles), the worker exceeds 2 GB resident, gets killed by the watchdog, and restarts in a loop — even when the host has plenty of free RAM. The only escape today is to fork the file or stop using autopilot. Bare `gbrain jobs work` already has no default; the supervisor and autopilot path is the only consumer of the `--max-rss 2048` floor. So an env override there is a minimal, surgical fix. ## Summary of change Read `GBRAIN_AUTOPILOT_MAX_RSS_MB` from the environment and pass it as the `--max-rss` value to the spawned worker. Default remains `'2048'` when unset. The startup log line now reports the effective value so the operator can confirm the override is live. ```diff - const args = ['jobs', 'work', '--max-rss', '2048']; + const maxRssOverride = process.env.GBRAIN_AUTOPILOT_MAX_RSS_MB ?? '2048'; + const args = ['jobs', 'work', '--max-rss', maxRssOverride]; const { cmd: spawnCmd, args: spawnArgs } = buildSpawnInvocation(tiniPath, cliPath, args); const child = spawn(spawnCmd, spawnArgs, { stdio: 'inherit', env: process.env }); workerProc = child; lastWorkerStartTime = Date.now(); - console.log(`[autopilot] Minions worker spawned (pid: ${child.pid}, watchdog: 2048MB${tiniPath ? ', tini: active' : ''})`); + console.log(`[autopilot] Minions worker spawned (pid: ${child.pid}, watchdog: ${maxRssOverride}MB${tiniPath ? ', tini: active' : ''})`); ``` 3 insertions, 2 deletions in one file. No new flags, no new files, no schema/config changes. ## Backward compatibility - Default remains 2048 MB; existing deployments see no behavior change. - Only the autopilot-supervised path is touched — bare `gbrain jobs work` is untouched. - The env var is opt-in: unset = identical to current behavior. ## Test method - Unset `GBRAIN_AUTOPILOT_MAX_RSS_MB`, start autopilot → log shows `watchdog: 2048MB` (unchanged). - Set `GBRAIN_AUTOPILOT_MAX_RSS_MB=4096`, restart autopilot → log shows `watchdog: 4096MB` and the spawned worker process receives `--max-rss 4096`. - `bun run typecheck` passes on this branch (clean `tsc --noEmit`). - Field-tested on contributor's machine for ~2 weeks of continuous autopilot operation, no incidents. ## Status Ready for human review — NOT pushed. Owner will open the PR manually after review. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith with what you need. - [ ] Let Codesmith autofix CI failures and bot reviews

title: PGLite WASM runtime aborts on init (Windows 11 + Bun 1.3.13, gbrain 0.33.1.0)
body:
## Summary

`gbrain init --pglite --fresh` and every subsequent DB-touching command (`list`, `import`, `query`) abort during PGLite WASM runtime init on Windows 11. The error text mentions the macOS 26.3 WASM bug (#223) but the symptom reproduces on Windows under Bun 1.3.13, so this is either a separate root cause or a broader runtime issue.

## Environment

- gbrain: **0.33.1.0** (fresh `gbrain upgrade` + `bun install --ignore-scripts && bun link` from `~/Development/gbrain`)
- Bun: **1.3.13** (bf2e2cec)
- OS: **Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise**, Build 26200 (10.0.26200)
- Engine: pglite (default, no Supabase config)
- Install method detected by `gbrain upgrade`: `bun-link`

## Reproduction

```
$ gbrain init --pglite --fresh
Setting up local brain with PGLite (no server needed)...
PGLite failed to initialize its WASM runtime.
  This is most commonly the macOS 26.3 WASM bug: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/223
  Run `gbrain doctor` for a full diagnosis.
  Original error: Aborted(). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.
```

Same abort on `gbrain list`, `gbrain doctor` (DB layer), and any command that opens the engine. `gbrain doctor` filesystem checks pass; skill conformance 42/42; DB section reports:

```
[WARN] connection: Could not connect to configured DB (URL from config-file-path); filesystem checks only
Health score: 90/100. All checks OK (some warnings).
```

Pre-upgrade build (0.32.x) had identical behaviour, so this is not a regression introduced by 0.33.1.0 — just confirming it survived the upgrade.

## Notes

- The postinstall step in `gbrain upgrade` also fails on Windows with a bash redirect parse error (`expected a command or assignment but got: "Redirect"` on `1>&2`). Worked around with `bun install --ignore-scripts && bun link`. Likely a separate small issue worth its own report.
- Build with `-sASSERTIONS` in the PGLite WASM module would help pin the actual abort cause.
- Happy to provide more diagnostics if useful.

## Summary
`mcp__gbrain__query` returns an empty array (`[]`) for natural-language questions whose content is well-indexed and returns top-1 hits at 0.99+ relevance when reissued as keywords. The empty result carries no diagnostic, "did you mean", or threshold note — it looks indistinguishable from "the brain has no relevant content," which is the wrong inference.

This is the highest-impact agent UX failure: agents default to phrasing queries as sentences, see `[]`, and fall back to Grep / give up — never discovering content that's actually indexed at 0.99 relevance.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64)
- Engine: Postgres on Supabase
- Transport: stdio MCP via Claude Code

## Repro
```jsonc
// Natural-language form → []
{"name":"query","arguments":{"query":"How does the EHS GUARD permission system enforce LBAC for hazards and which middleware layer applies it?"}}
// → []

{"name":"query","arguments":{"query":"core-service integration API authentication, rate limiting and tenant scoping"}}
// → []

{"name":"query","arguments":{"query":"GUARD-672 system roles API interceptor rationale"}}
// → []
```

Same content, keyword form:
```jsonc
{"name":"query","arguments":{"query":"LBAC location based access control"}}
// → docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-08-permission-lbac-consistency-design  (score: 0.99968546628952)
//   docs/permissions-audit-2026-04-07                                       (score: 0.911878526210785)
```

In an evaluation of 9 query calls, **5 returned `[]`** when phrased as natural-language sentences. After reissuing the same intent in 2-5 keywords, hit rate jumped to 100%.

## Expected
Either:
1. Return the same top hits with their actual scores (let the caller threshold), OR
2. Return `[]` only when there genuinely are no chunks above some confidence floor — and surface that floor in the response

## Actual
Empty array, no metadata, no fallback to keyword tokenization.

## Hypotheses
Most likely the multi-query expansion / hybrid reranker is filtering all candidates below a hardcoded threshold when the natural-language form pushes vector scores down (longer queries → diluted embeddings, mismatched embedding space against short doc chunks). Worth testing whether disabling `expand` or lowering the threshold restores hits.

## Impact
- AI agents see `[]` → assume no data → fall back to Grep → never use the brain. This is the dominant interaction pattern and it fails closed.
- Documented "ask gbrain in natural language" UX doesn't work; users must learn to phrase as keywords (which is the opposite of what semantic search should provide).
- Compounds with #784/#891: even if scoping worked, the dominant query pattern silently returns nothing.

## Suggested fix
- Don't return `[]` without surfacing top-K scores (even if below threshold). A `top_score: 0.3, threshold: 0.4, hidden: 12` response is far more recoverable than `[]`.
- Or: fall back to keyword search when hybrid returns nothing, label results as `"mode": "keyword-fallback"`.

title: put_page over MCP skips auto_links + auto_timeline (reason: "remote") — agent writes cannot grow the graph
body:
## Summary
Every `mcp__gbrain__put_page` response shows `auto_links: {skipped: "remote"}` and `auto_timeline: {skipped: "remote"}`. Agents writing pages via MCP cannot participate in `[[wikilink]]` extraction or timeline reconciliation, so `brain_score`'s graph dimensions stay at 0 from agent activity. The 25-point graph contribution to brain_score only ever comes from human CLI usage.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5
- Engine: Postgres on Supabase
- Transport: stdio MCP

## Repro
```jsonc
{"name":"put_page","arguments":{"slug":"test-evaluation-2026-05-13","content":"# Test\n\nMentioning [[some-other-page]] and the date 2026-05-13."}}

// response includes:
{
  "auto_links":    {"skipped": "remote"},
  "auto_timeline": {"skipped": "remote"},
  "writer_lint":   {"skipped": "flag_disabled"}
}
```

CLI `gbrain put` (same content, same brain) DOES run the extractors. The skip is purely transport-gated.

## Impact
- Agent-authored pages are graph-disconnected. They contribute to embedding coverage but never to `link_count` or `timeline_entry_count`.
- `brain_score` is stuck at 45/100 (the embed+dead-links ceiling without graph) for agent-only workflows.
- The "agents are first-class brain citizens" promise breaks: agents see results from human-curated pages but cannot meaningfully add to the graph themselves.
- Compounds with the fact that `gbrain extract` doesn't recover this — extract walks `--source fs` which doesn't see DB-only agent writes anyway.

## Expected
Either:
1. Run extractors regardless of transport (parse `[[wikilinks]]` in the markdown body — there's nothing transport-specific about that operation), OR
2. Surface this as a feature flag the agent can opt into (`auto_links: true` argument), with clear docs that it's off by default for remote callers and why.

## Actual
Silently skipped with reason `"remote"`. No way to opt in. No documentation surfacing this asymmetry.

## Suggested
The skip predicate appears to be `ctx.transport === "remote"`. Remove that gate or make it overridable. Wikilink parsing is pure-function over markdown body — there's no security or trust reason to require local transport.

title: think over MCP returns 'no LLM available' — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not threaded through stdio transport
body:
## Summary
`mcp__gbrain__think` returns `{"answer": "(no LLM available — set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or pass client)", "warnings": ["NO_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]}` over the stdio MCP transport, even when the wrapping Claude Code session has full LLM capability. The "synthesis flagship" tool is non-functional for any MCP caller.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5
- Engine: Postgres on Supabase
- Transport: stdio MCP via Claude Code
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: not set in user's shell (intentionally — Claude Code provides the LLM context)

## Repro
```jsonc
{"name":"think","arguments":{"question":"Why did we choose granular permissions over a 5-row visual grouping for the custom-roles wizard?"}}

// response
{
  "answer": "(no LLM available — set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or pass client)",
  "warnings": ["NO_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"],
  "evidence": [ /* still returns relevant pages */ ]
}
```

The retrieval portion works (evidence is populated). The synthesis step is what breaks.

## Impact
- `think` is the documented multi-hop synthesis primitive ("cited answer with conflict + gap analysis"). It's the one tool that promises to do real reasoning over the corpus instead of just retrieval. Over MCP, it's a no-op.
- Agents fall back to manually pulling pages via `query` and synthesizing in their own context — which is what they'd do without gbrain at all.

## Hypotheses
This is the same `ctx`-not-threaded family as #713 (`whoami` unknown_transport). The MCP server doesn't get the calling Claude Code session's LLM credentials. Two design choices:
1. **Bring-your-own-key**: gbrain MCP server reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from its own env at startup (won't work for Claude Code MCP since the CC parent doesn't propagate it down)
2. **Per-call client**: accept a `client_id` / `model` arg from the MCP caller and route through it (cleaner but bigger contract)

## Expected
Either:
- Document that `think` requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to be set in gbrain server env (and the auto-launched stdio server picks it up from user's shell)
- Or accept a `model` arg + route synthesis through whatever LLM the MCP caller designates

## Actual
Silent degrade to "evidence-only" mode with a one-line warning that's easy to miss in a 50KB response.

title: MCP search/query responses exceed token cap on common-term queries (--limit 20 → 90KB persisted to disk)
body:
## Summary
`mcp__gbrain__search` and `mcp__gbrain__query` with `--limit 20` and a common term (e.g., "permission", "user") produce 60-90KB responses that exceed Claude Code's MCP tool output cap. The response gets persisted to disk and the agent has to read it back, doubling the round-trip cost. Effectively forces all agent MCP queries to `limit ≤ 5`.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5
- Engine: Postgres on Supabase
- Transport: stdio MCP

## Repro
```jsonc
{"name":"search","arguments":{"query":"user","limit":20}}
// → response is 58.8KB, exceeds MCP tool output cap, persists to disk for read-back

{"name":"query","arguments":{"query":"permission","limit":20}}
// → response is 90KB, same outcome
```

## Impact
- Agents must pre-emptively pass `limit ≤ 5` for any common-term search or pay the read-back cost.
- Useful queries that legitimately need more candidates (e.g., "find all docs about permissions, I'll re-rank in my context") become expensive.
- Discoverability suffers: an agent that wants to scan 20 candidates and pick the most relevant has to do 4× sequential queries with offset.

## Suggested
Server-side options:
1. **`detail` parameter respected**: `detail: "low"` should return slugs + scores + ≤1 line of preview each, sized for agent consumption. Currently `detail: medium` is the practical max but already too large at limit=20.
2. **Chunk-preview truncation**: cap each result's snippet to ≤200 chars when `limit > 5`.
3. **Pagination headers**: when result set is large, return first N + a continuation token instead of the full payload.

The MCP transport has a hard cap; the tool should fit inside it for reasonable parameter ranges, not force callers to discover the limit empirically.

## Workaround
Document `limit ≤ 5` as the recommended ceiling for MCP `search` / `query` calls in the README and the tool descriptions.

title: gbrain doctor --fast reports 'Health score: 90/100' while skipping DB connection check
body:
## Summary
`gbrain doctor --fast` prints `Health score: 90/100. All checks OK (some warnings).` while simultaneously emitting `[WARN] connection: Skipping DB checks (--fast mode...)`. The aggregate score is computed across checks that didn't run. Looks reassuring while hiding the fact that the most important check (DB reachability) was skipped.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5

## Repro
```
$ gbrain doctor --fast
[WARN] resolver_health: Could not find skills directory
[WARN] connection: Skipping DB checks (--fast mode; remove --fast for full)
[OK]   pgvector: Extension installed
[OK]   schema_version: Version 39 (latest: 39)
...
Health score: 90/100. All checks OK (some warnings).
```

The user sees 90/100 and assumes the brain is healthy. The brain might be unreachable.

## Impact
- Agents and humans use `gbrain doctor --fast` as a quick health probe (e.g., in shell-init checks). A misleading 90 invites false positives.
- Compounds with the broader pattern of silent-degrade in gbrain (`--source` ignored, `query` returns [], `auto_links` skipped) — every "looks OK on the surface" footgun erodes trust.

## Expected
Either:
1. Don't compute a score in `--fast` mode (just print check statuses)
2. Compute score from only the checks that actually ran, AND label it differently (e.g., `Health score (fast mode, no DB): 8/9 checks OK`)
3. Cap score at the count of checks that ran (5/10 ran, max possible is 50/100)

## Actual
Score includes skipped-check slots as if they passed.

## One-liner suggested fix
```diff
- const score = (ok / total) * 100;
+ const ran = ok + warn + err;
+ const score = ran === 0 ? 0 : Math.round((ok / ran) * 100);
+ const label = skipped > 0 ? `Health score (partial, ${skipped} skipped)` : 'Health score';
```

title: near_symbol / symbol_kind / lang parameters operate on transcript prose, not parsed code — no real code index in v0.28.12
body:
## Summary
The `mcp__gbrain__query` tool exposes `near_symbol`, `symbol_kind`, `lang`, and `walk_depth` parameters whose descriptions imply they operate over a parsed-code index ("Anchor retrieval at this qualified symbol name", "Filter to chunks where content_chunks.symbol_type matches"). In v0.28.12 they operate over transcript prose, not actual code. Symbol lookup returns Claude Code conversations that *mention* the symbol, not the file/line where it's defined.

The CLI subcommands referenced in the v0.19.0 / v0.20.0 release notes for "Cathedral II" code indexing — `gbrain code-def`, `gbrain code-refs`, `gbrain code-callers`, `gbrain code-callees` — also don't appear in `gbrain --help` output despite being listed in the help under "CODE INDEXING".

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5

## Repro
EHS has a function `seedEhsSystemRoles` defined at `server/db/seed/roles.ts:59`. Look it up via each path:

```bash
# Ground truth (works, ~0.14s)
$ grep -rn "function seedEhsSystemRoles\|export.*seedEhsSystemRoles" server/ shared/
server/db/seed/roles.ts:59:export async function seedEhsSystemRoles(...)
server/db/seed/index.ts:214:    seedEhsSystemRoles,

# gbrain query with near_symbol (3s wall, wrong answer)
$ gbrain call query '{"query":"seedEhsSystemRoles","near_symbol":"seedEhsSystemRoles"}'
# → top hit: transcripts/claude-code/upkeepapp-ehs/2026-04-28-...  (score: 0.304)
#   This is a conversation that mentions the symbol, not the definition.

# gbrain query with symbol_kind: function (returns [])
$ gbrain call query '{"query":"PERMISSION_META source of truth","symbol_kind":"function"}'
# → []
```

## Impact
- `code-def` / `code-refs` / `code-callers` / `code-callees` are advertised at the top of `gbrain --help` as headline v0.20.0 features. They appear to not exist as CLI subcommands in v0.28.12.
- The `near_symbol` / `symbol_kind` params on `query` give the false impression of code-aware retrieval. They silently fall back to text matching against the transcript corpus.
- For any "where is X defined / who calls X" question, Grep beats gbrain by 10-100× and is 100% accurate. There's no signal that gbrain should be tried first.

## Expected
Either:
1. Ship the documented code index — parse code files into `content_chunks` with `symbol_type` populated, build `code_edges`, expose `code-def` / `code-refs` / `code-callers` subcommands as the help text implies, and have `near_symbol` actually anchor retrieval at the symbol's chunk.
2. OR: remove the symbol-flavored params from `query` and remove "CODE INDEXING (v0.19.0 / v0.20.0 Cathedral II)" from the `--help` output. False advertising erodes trust more than the missing feature does.

## Actual
Symbol-related machinery exists as parameter surface only; underneath, it's keyword-search over the transcript corpus.

title: Every gbrain CLI invocation prints 3 [ai.gateway] warnings to stderr — promote to debug level
body:
## Summary
Every single `gbrain` CLI command (including `gbrain --version`, `gbrain doctor`, `gbrain search`, `gbrain --help`) prints these 3 lines to stderr:

```
[ai.gateway] recipe "google" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.
[ai.gateway] recipe "ollama" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.
[ai.gateway] recipe "litellm" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.
```

## Environment
- gbrain 0.28.12
- macOS 26.5

## Impact
- Breaks log scanning: scripts that diff stderr or grep for "real" errors have to filter these out every time.
- Breaks JSON-piped CLI output: `gbrain call list_pages '{}' | jq` fails because the stderr/stdout merging in some shells injects warnings into the JSON stream (yes, even with `2>/dev/null` they sometimes leak — see repro below).
- Pollutes the dev experience: in a 5-minute eval session, these accounted for ~30% of all visible terminal output.

## Repro
```bash
$ gbrain --version 2>&1 | head -10
[ai.gateway] recipe "google" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.
[ai.gateway] recipe "ollama" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.
[ai.gateway] recipe "litellm" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.
gbrain 0.28.12

# Even `--version` triggers them — they fire at CLI init, before the subcommand runs.
```

## Suggested fix
Two clean options:
1. **Fix the upstream recipe configs.** Add `max_batch_tokens` to the google/ollama/litellm AI gateway recipes (it sounds like a config-only fix — they already have batch caps via recursion as the safety net).
2. **Promote to debug level.** If `max_batch_tokens` is genuinely worth warning about, gate behind `GBRAIN_LOG=debug` or `gbrain --verbose`. Don't print warnings the user can't act on.

Either fix is a one-character change to a few config files. The current state is paper-cut spam on every CLI invocation.

title: Per-OAuth-client source scoping for multi-agent isolation
body:
## Context

Running gbrain 0.32.0 with a multi-source brain (PGLite) serving five OpenClaw agents.
Each agent has a dedicated OAuth client registered via DCR (`openclaw-main`,
`openclaw-lens`, `openclaw-dev`, `openclaw-learn`, `openclaw-jobsearch`). What I want:
each agent's queries scoped to a specific source by default — one source is federated
(shared research layer) and the rest are isolated per agent.

## What I noticed

The plumbing for this already exists, but the last mile isn't connected:

1. `src/commands/serve-http.ts:929` reads `(authInfo as AuthInfo & { sourceId?: string }).sourceId`
   and threads it through `ctx.sourceId` to every operation. The cast is forward-looking —
   the field is never populated anywhere in the codebase.

2. `OperationContext.sourceId` is plumbed through ~20 call sites in `operations.ts` (search
   the file for `// v0.31.8 (D7/D20): thread ctx.sourceId` comments). Reads, writes, deletes,
   links — all scope-aware.

3. `sources.config.federated` is a JSONB key that determines what `gbrain sources list`
   prints, but `buildVisibilityClause(p, s)` in `src/core/search/sql-ranking.ts:128` only
   emits `AND p.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT s.archived`. It doesn't reference
   `s.config->>'federated'`. So `searchKeyword` and `searchVector` return matches from
   every non-archived source regardless of the federated flag.

Net result: the `federated`/`isolated` distinction shown by the CLI is metadata-only.
For real per-agent isolation, callers have to rely on convention/prompting — there's no
enforcement.

## Proposed fix

### Part A — Populate `authInfo.sourceId` from a new `oauth_clients.source_id` column

```sql
-- Migration:
ALTER TABLE oauth_clients
  ADD COLUMN source_id TEXT REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
```

CLI:
```bash
gbrain auth register-client lens-client \
  --grant-types client_credentials \
  --scopes "read write" \
  --source lens          # NEW
```

`verifyAccessToken` JOINs `oauth_clients.source_id` and surfaces it on AuthInfo (~6 lines).

### Part B — Make `buildVisibilityClause` honor it

```ts
export function buildVisibilityClause(
  pageAlias: string,
  sourceAlias: string,
  scopeSourceId?: string,
): string {
  const base = `AND ${pageAlias}.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT ${sourceAlias}.archived`;
  if (!scopeSourceId) return base;
  // Sanitize scopeSourceId via parameterized binding at caller. See sql-ranking
  // injection notes (codex pass-1 #5).
  return `${base} AND (${sourceAlias}.id = $scopeSourceId
    OR (${sourceAlias}.config->>'federated')::boolean = true)`;
}
```

Threaded into `searchKeyword` / `searchVector` / `searchKeywordChunks` from the
existing `ctx.sourceId` carrier.

### Behavior

- OAuth client with `source_id = 'lens'`: sees `lens` (own) + every `federated: true` source
  (shared research layer). Cannot see other isolated sources.
- OAuth client with `source_id = NULL` (admin / unspecified): current behavior (everything
  non-archived).
- Stdio MCP callers: unchanged (no auth path, `ctx.sourceId` stays undefined).

## Why this matters

For multi-agent deployments where each agent has its own client identity:

- **Audit**: the admin dashboard's request log already shows `clientName`. With per-client
  scoping, you can see "lens-client read 47 pages in `lens` source today" instead of every
  call appearing as the same shared identity.
- **Data isolation**: agent A's queries can't accidentally surface agent B's private notes.
  Today's mitigation is convention via agent prompts; that breaks down at scale.
- **Federation stays useful**: marking one source as federated means it remains discoverable
  to every client, while everything else partitions cleanly.

## Open questions

1. Should the federation filter cascade across multiple federated sources, or do we keep
   it to "own source + first federated source"? My read: anything `federated: true` is
   fair game — matches the existing `gbrain sources list` semantics.
2. Should `sources_admin` scope override the source filter for ops like `sources_list`?
   I think yes — admins should see the full picture; data ops respect the filter.
3. Migration: should existing `access_tokens` legacy bearer rows (which grandfather to
   `read+write+admin`) also get a nullable `source_id`? My read: yes for parity, NULL
   default keeps backward compat.

title: v0.33.1.1 fix: Voyage output_dimension + flexible-dim guard + OOM-cap rethrow
body:
Re-opens [#866](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/866) by @100yenadmin from `electricsheephq/eva-brain` on upstream so the voyage-4-nano fixup and two Codex-caught follow-ups can land in the same PR (the GitHub `maintainerCanModify` flag doesn't grant push access across forks for upstream pushes — both HTTPS and SSH return 403).

## Summary

**Voyage core fix (Eva's commit `ee90709e`, preserved verbatim)**

Fixes Voyage 2048-dim embeddings. `src/core/ai/dims.ts` now returns `{ openaiCompatible: { dimensions: N } }` (SDK-supported) instead of `output_dimension` (Voyage wire key the AI SDK silently drops). Existing `voyageCompatFetch` at `src/core/ai/gateway.ts:541` translates `dimensions → output_dimension` before the HTTP body is sent. New wire-level test stubs `globalThis.fetch` and asserts the actual outbound body contains `output_dimension: 2048` + `encoding_format: base64`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["embedding_dimensions=2048"] --> B["dimsProviderOptions"]
  B --> C["AI SDK openai-compatible"]
  C --> D["voyageCompatFetch"]
  D --> E["Voyage /embeddings"]
  B -->|"SDK key"| C
  C -->|"dimensions"| D
  D -->|"output_dimension"| E
```

**voyage-4-nano fixup (commit `8b02e238`)**

Voyage's `voyage-4-nano` is an open-weight variant listed separately as fixed 1024-dim — it doesn't accept `output_dimension` on the hosted API. Caught by adversarial Codex review during PR evaluation, confirmed against Voyage's docs.

- Drops `voyage-4-nano` from `VOYAGE_OUTPUT_DIMENSION_MODELS`.
- Tightens the voyage recipe docstring so the "all v4 variants are flexible" claim doesn't lead a future contributor to re-add it.
- Flips the test case to a negative regression pin (`voyage-4-nano returns undefined`).

**Codex P3 follow-ups (commit `d5dc5fad`)**

1. **`gateway.ts:619` OOM-cap was theatrical.** The per-embedding Layer 2 base64 cap was throwing a generic `Error` that the surrounding `catch {}` silently swallowed, then returning the original (oversized) response into the AI SDK's JSON parser. Now wrapped in tagged `VoyageResponseTooLargeError` and rethrown via `instanceof` check. Parse-error fall-back preserved for non-OOM errors. Pinned by 2 behavioral tests + a structural assertion.

2. **Voyage flexible-dim runtime validation.** Brains misconfigured for Voyage flexible-dim models with `embedding_dimensions` outside `{256, 512, 1024, 2048}` (most common: leaving it unset → default 1536) now throw `AIConfigError` with a paste-ready fix at the embed boundary instead of waiting for Voyage's opaque HTTP 400.

3. **`gbrain models doctor` embedding_config probe.** New zero-token check runs first, before any chat/expansion probes, surfacing the misconfiguration via `gbrain doctor` at config-test time. New `config` status + `fix` hint rendered in both human and JSON output.

title: fix: pass no-recurse-submodules to git pull
body: ## Summary Fixes `pullRepo()` so `--no-recurse-submodules` is passed as a `git pull` subcommand option instead of a top-level `git` option. ## Problem `pullRepo()` previously built an argv shape equivalent to: ```bash git -C -c http.followRedirects=false -c protocol.file.allow=never -c protocol.ext.allow=never --no-recurse-submodules pull --ff-only ``` On Git versions that do not accept `--no-recurse-submodules` as a top-level option, this fails before `pull` runs: ```text unknown option: --no-recurse-submodules ``` That causes `gbrain sync` / dream-cycle maintenance to warn and continue from local state instead of pulling cleanly. ## Fix - Keep SSRF hardening config flags in `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS`. - Split the submodule recursion guard into `GIT_NO_RECURSE_SUBMODULES`. - Pass it after the relevant subcommand: - `git ... clone --no-recurse-submodules ...` - `git -C ... pull --ff-only --no-recurse-submodules` ## Verification - `bun test test/git-remote.test.ts` — 37 passed - `bun run typecheck` — passed --- Need help on this PR? title: feat(sync): sort files newest-first for faster salience on recent content
body: ## Problem Sync processes files in `git diff` order (alphabetical), so `meetings/2020-*` gets embedded before `meetings/2026-*`. After a burst of writes, new pages can be invisible to search for hours while older pages in the alphabet process first. Real-world impact: divorce attorney consultation pages written on May 11 were never found by gbrain search because the sync lock got stuck, and when sync finally ran, it would have processed them last (alphabetically after thousands of older pages). ## Fix Sort `addsAndMods` descending in both: - **Incremental sync** (`sync.ts` line 690) — the git-diff path - **Full import** (`import.ts`) — the `runImport` walker Brain paths are date-prefixed by convention (`meetings/2026-05-13-*`, `daily/2026-05-13.md`), so lexicographic descending naturally prioritizes recent content. ## Impact - Zero behavior change for completed syncs (same pages processed, just different order) - Massive salience improvement for interrupted/slow syncs — newest pages become searchable first - Two lines of actual logic (`.sort()` calls), rest is comments ## Testing - Verified sort order with sample brain paths - No existing tests assert processing order (order was undefined/alphabetical before) --- Need help on this PR? title: Refresh source last_sync_at on up-to-date sync
body:
## Summary

`gbrain sync --source <id>` can return `up_to_date` without refreshing `sources.last_sync_at`. That makes `gbrain doctor` continue warning that the source is stale even immediately after a successful no-op sync.

## Repro

1. Have a configured source whose repo HEAD matches `sync.last_commit`.
2. Set `sources.last_sync_at` to an old timestamp.
3. Run:
   ```bash
   gbrain sync --source default --no-embed --no-extract
   gbrain doctor --json
   ```

## Observed

`gbrain sync` reports up-to-date / no content changes, but `gbrain doctor` still reports:

```text
sync_freshness: Source 'default' last synced <N>h ago. Run `gbrain sync --source <id>` to refresh
```

## Expected

A successful source sync attempt should refresh `sources.last_sync_at` even if there are no content changes, so the doctor freshness check reflects that the source was checked.

## Local patch tested

I added a small helper in `src/commands/sync.ts` to update `sources.last_sync_at = now()` when `performSync` returns `status: 'up_to_date'` for a source-backed sync, plus a regression test in `test/sync.test.ts`.

Verification:

```bash
bun test test/sync.test.ts
# pass

gbrain sync --source default --no-embed --no-extract
gbrain doctor --json
# healthy / 100 locally
```

title: Feature: opt-in global-basename wikilink resolution for Obsidian-convention vaults
body:
## Problem

When `gbrain extract links` ingests `[[wikilinks]]` from markdown files, the resolver only matches by:

1. **Parallel directory + same basename** (e.g., a link from `originals/foo.md` resolves `[[bar]]` to `originals/bar.md`)
2. **Same directory + sibling basename** (e.g., a link from `concepts/foo.md` resolves `[[bar]]` to `concepts/bar.md`)

It does **not** do a global-basename lookup. So a wikilink like `[[struktura]]` written in `concepts/knowledge-graph.md` does **not** resolve to `projects/struktura.md`, even though that page exists, has a unique basename in the vault, and resolves correctly in Obsidian.

This silently drops cross-directory bare-basename wikilinks. They're not flagged as broken — they're just missing from gbrain's graph layer.

## Repro

```bash
# Set up a minimal vault with cross-directory link
mkdir -p /tmp/vault/{concepts,projects}
cat > /tmp/vault/projects/struktura.md <<EOF
---
title: Struktura
type: project
---
A project page.
EOF
cat > /tmp/vault/concepts/knowledge-graph.md <<EOF
---
title: Knowledge Graph
type: concept
---
This concept relates to [[struktura]].
EOF

gbrain init --force --dir /tmp/test-brain
GBRAIN_HOME=/tmp/test-brain gbrain import /tmp/vault
GBRAIN_HOME=/tmp/test-brain gbrain extract links
GBRAIN_HOME=/tmp/test-brain gbrain stats
# Links: 0 (expected: 1)
```

Obsidian's graph view correctly links the two nodes. Gbrain's graph layer does not.

## Why it matters

For users who follow Obsidian's standard convention (flat-namespace wikilinks, globally-unique basenames), this silently drops most of their interlinking from gbrain's graph layer. We hit this on a fresh wiki: 71 wikilinks total across 20 pages in Obsidian (avg 3.55/page, dense galaxy), but gbrain's `extract links` only produced 12 — all of which were same-directory. The remaining ~60 cross-directory bare-basename links were dropped silently.

Symptoms downstream:
- `gbrain graph <slug>` returns thin or missing edges that exist in the source files
- `gbrain backlinks <slug>` undercounts incoming references
- Graph-traversal queries (e.g., "what concepts touch this project") return incomplete neighbors
- Semantic search via `gbrain query` is unaffected (works on chunks/embeddings, not the graph layer) — but anyone relying on graph traversal gets a partial view

## Why it's probably intentional (and what to do anyway)

Gbrain's parent/ancestor resolution suggests it's designed for monorepo-style knowledge bases where basename collisions across folders are common, and path disambiguation is necessary. That's a defensible design choice for one user population. But Obsidian convention is the opposite — flat namespace, globally-unique basenames, bare wikilinks everywhere. The two assumptions clash.

## Proposed: add an opt-in "global basename" resolution mode

```yaml
# gbrain.yml or config
link_resolution:
  mode: ancestor          # current default — backward compatible
  # OR
  mode: global_basename   # treat bare wikilinks as referring to any uniquely-named page in the vault
```

In `global_basename` mode, `resolveSlug("struktura", from_page)` would:
1. Try parent/ancestor lookup first (current behavior)
2. Fall back to: search `allSlugs` for any slug whose basename matches
3. If exactly one match → resolve to it
4. If multiple matches → ambiguous, drop with a warning (so the user knows to disambiguate via path prefix)
5. If zero matches → drop silently (existing behavior)

Default stays `ancestor` for back-compat. Users with flat-namespace vaults flip to `global_basename` in their config.

### Alternative — auto-detect from `gbrain doctor`

`gbrain doctor` could count bare-basename wikilinks that fail to resolve under ancestor mode but WOULD resolve under global mode, and surface that as a hint:

```
ℹ️  Detected 60 wikilinks that would resolve under global_basename mode but currently drop.
   Your vault appears to use Obsidian-flat-namespace convention.
   Set `link_resolution.mode: global_basename` in gbrain.yml to enable.
```

## Severity

Medium. Doesn't break anything (semantic search works fine), but silently undercounts the graph for Obsidian-convention users, leading to thin/wrong graph traversal results. Easy upstream fix; current workarounds (path-prefixed wikilinks everywhere) are ugly enough that most users would rather accept the gap than adopt them.

## Affected file

`src/core/link-extraction.ts` — the `resolveSlug` function around line 160-192.

## Diagnosed by an agent

This was caught by an LLM agent (Hermes-driven Echo) doing read-after-write verification on a freshly-seeded wiki, then reading gbrain's source to confirm the resolver mechanism. Worth noting as evidence that the verify-before-done discipline catches real architectural gaps that wouldn't show up in CLI smoke tests.

title: Bootstrap gap: applyForwardReferenceBootstrap misses files.source_id + files.page_id (v0.18 forward-refs)
body:
## Problem

Migrating a pre-v0.18 brain (in my case, schema version 13 from gbrain v0.14.2) to v0.33.x fails during `init --migrate-only` with:

```
column "page_id" does not exist
```

The wedge fires inside `SCHEMA_SQL` apply, immediately after `idx_files_page` creation. `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` covers most v0.13–v0.27 forward-references but doesn't pre-add the two columns `files` gained in v0.18.0 Step 7.

## Reproduction

Any brain at schema version <= ~v17 (no `files.source_id` / `files.page_id`) running `init --migrate-only` against `src/core/schema-embedded.ts` from v0.33.x will hit this. Confirmed today on v0.33.1.1 and v0.33.2.0 (same code path).

## Root cause

`applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` docstring in `src/core/postgres-engine.ts` lines 273–296 enumerates what it covers:

> - `sources` table + default seed (FK target of pages.source_id) — v0.18
> - `pages.source_id` column (indexed by `idx_pages_source_id`) — v0.18
> - `links.link_source` column (indexed by `idx_links_source`) — v0.13
> - `links.origin_page_id` column (indexed by `idx_links_origin`) — v0.13
> - `content_chunks.symbol_name` column ... — v0.19
> - ... etc

The two `files` columns added in the same v0.18.0 step as `pages.source_id` are missing:

- `files.source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default' REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `files.page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`

Both are forward-referenced by unguarded `CREATE INDEX` statements in `src/core/schema-embedded.ts:493-494`:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_files_page_id ON files(page_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_files_source_id ON files(source_id);
```

`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` checks for the index name, not the column — so it tries to index a column that doesn't exist yet on old brains.

## Fix sketch

Three additions to `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` (mirror in `PGLiteEngine` per the existing pattern):

1. Probe existence:
   ```ts
   files_exists, files_source_id_exists, files_page_id_exists
   ```
2. Backfill conditionally:
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE files ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'
     REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
   ALTER TABLE files ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS page_id INTEGER
     REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
   ```
3. Update the docstring + add coverage to `test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts` (PGLite) and `test/e2e/postgres-bootstrap.test.ts`.

Happy to send a PR if you'd like.

## Workaround (for anyone hitting this)

Apply the two ALTER TABLE statements manually before `init --migrate-only`. Migration runs from v13 → v57 (38 migrations on v0.33.1.1, +3 more on v0.33.2.0) succeed cleanly afterward.

## Environment

- gbrain: v0.14.2 → v0.33.2.0 (this hit both v0.33.1.1 and v0.33.2.0 the same way)
- DB: Supabase Postgres 17.6, 1,334 rows in `files` (all backfilled to source_id='default' on ALTER)
- Network: also hit dual-pool IPv6 ECONNREFUSED on derived direct URL; workaround was `GBRAIN_DISABLE_DIRECT_POOL=1` — separate issue, mentioning for completeness in case others land here looking for "v33 migration won't run."

Related context:
- `src/core/schema-embedded.ts:473-494` — files CREATE TABLE + unguarded index statements
- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:235-237` — bootstrap call site immediately before SCHEMA_SQL apply
- Comment at `src/core/schema-embedded.ts:467` calls out "v0.18.0 Step 7: files gains source_id + page_id"

title: sync --source X attributes pages to source_id='default' instead of X
body:
## Summary

When using `gbrain sync --repo <path> --source <id>` to ingest content from a named source, the resulting `pages` table rows are written with `source_id = 'default'` rather than the source ID passed via `--source`. The sync command does correctly write the source-scoped tracking state (`sources.last_commit`, `sources.last_sync_at`), but the page rows themselves end up unattributed.

Net effect: `gbrain sources list` reports `0 pages` for every named source, even though the content has been ingested successfully and is fully searchable via the `default` bucket.

## Repro

Tested on a fresh multi-source setup with three federated sources (`bh-brain`, `bh-vault`, `bh-studio-general`):

```bash
# Register + federate a new source
gbrain sources add my-source --path /path/to/my-source
gbrain sources federate my-source

# Sync it
gbrain sync --repo /path/to/my-source --source my-source
# → imports N pages, last_sync_at updates, last_commit advances

# List sources
gbrain sources list
# → my-source shows "0 pages, last sync <timestamp>"
# → default shows aggregate count of everything

# Confirm content is actually in the DB
psql -c "SELECT source_id, COUNT(*) FROM pages GROUP BY source_id;"
# →  default | <N+existing>
# → no row for my-source

# Search works (so content is real, just mis-attributed)
gbrain search "<some unique phrase from my-source content>"
# → returns the new pages, ranked correctly
```

## Expected vs. actual

| | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `pages.source_id` for content ingested via `sync --source X` | `X` | `default` |
| `gbrain sources list` page_count for named source | accurate | always 0 |
| Search across federated sources | works | works (unaffected) |
| Source-scoped delete / re-sync | works | doesn't (everything's in `default`) |

## Diagnosis

The migration at `src/core/migrate.ts:519` adds `pages.source_id TEXT DEFAULT 'default'` (correct).

`performSync` in `src/commands/sync.ts` correctly reads/writes per-source state via `readSyncAnchor` / `writeSyncAnchor` when `opts.sourceId` is set.

But the actual page-insert path runs through `importFile` (in `src/core/import-file.ts`) — and that function doesn't appear to receive or propagate the `sourceId` from the sync caller. Pages are inserted without an explicit `source_id`, so the column DEFAULT (`'default'`) kicks in.

The fix is likely:
1. Thread `sourceId` from `performSync` → `importFile` → page INSERT statements
2. Have a one-time migration / `gbrain sources reconcile <id>` command to retro-attribute pages that have already landed under `default` for a given local_path

## Environment

- gbrain commit: `kyledeanjackson/gbrain` (fork of `garrytan/gbrain`) — fix branch from PR #775
- Backend: Postgres 17.9 with pgvector
- Multi-source schema migrations applied: yes (`v0.18.0 Step 5` source-scoped sync state ✓, `v0.18.0 Step 7` files.source_id ✓)

## Impact

Mild — content lands and is queryable, so the core functionality works. The visible symptom is the misleading `0 pages` count on every named source row, which makes it hard to:
- Verify a new source ingested what you expected
- Use source-scoped operations (delete-all-for-source, etc.)
- Filter searches to a specific source's content

## Workaround

For now: query the `pages` table directly with a `LIKE` filter on `slug` to confirm a source's content is present, and rely on semantic search returning the right hits regardless of attribution.

title: fix(operations): add items schema to extract_facts.entity_hints
body:
## Summary

`extract_facts.entity_hints` declared `type: 'array'` with no `items`, which JSON Schema requires. OpenAI/Codex's strict tool-schema validator rejects the entire tool list with HTTP 400 `invalid_function_parameters` when any tool has an array param missing `items`, so every agent wired to the Codex backend silently falls back to a more lenient provider on tool-bearing turns.

One-line fix + a structural regression test that walks every op and asserts no array param ever lacks `items`.

## Repro (before the fix)

Point any MCP client at `gbrain serve` while the upstream provider is OpenAI Codex (e.g. `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`), then trigger any tool-bearing chat. Logs show:

```
WARNING run_agent: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError
  provider=openai-codex base_url=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex model=gpt-5.5
  summary=HTTP 400: Invalid schema for function 'mcp_gbrain_extract_facts':
  In context=('properties', 'entity_hints'), array schema missing items.
⚠️ Non-retryable error (HTTP 400) — trying fallback...
🔄 Primary model failed — switching to fallback: deepseek-v4-pro via deepseek
```

The primary model never runs. Lenient providers (Deepseek, OpenRouter) accept the schema, so the bug is invisible there.

## Fix

- `src/core/operations.ts:2576` — add `items: { type: 'string' }` to `entity_hints`. Type already aligned: `operations.ts:2611` casts `p.entity_hints as string[]`.
- `test/mcp-tool-defs.test.ts` — new test walks every operation and pins the invariant "every array param declares items." Catches this bug class at test time instead of at provider-400 time.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/mcp-tool-defs.test.ts` — 6 pass / 0 fail
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] Verified the MCP `tools/list` response over JSON-RPC stdio now ships `items: { type: 'string' }` on `extract_facts.entity_hints`
- [x] Codex backend (gpt-5.5 via `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`) accepts the tool list post-patch — zero HTTP 400 since the change landed in my deployment

## Notes

- Only two array params exist in `operations.ts` today: `ingest_log.pages_updated` (already correct) and `extract_facts.entity_hints` (this fix). The regression test guards both.
- No version/CHANGELOG bump — leaving release-time discipline to the maintainer per the repo's PR convention.

title: Pluggable embedding provider (Gemini support)
body:
## Context

I'm running gbrain against Supabase across a few agents (Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes) and recently wired up a GitHub Actions workflow that ingests a repo of project artifacts into the shared brain on every push. The one thing missing for end-to-end vector search in CI is an embedding provider key.

We're already on Google AI Tier 2 for other agent work. Provisioning a separate OpenAI API key just for `text-embedding-3-large` would mean a second billing rail for one feature, when the same `1536`-dim vector space is available from `gemini-embedding-001` via `outputDimensionality=1536`.

Before opening a PR, I wanted to check fit with the project's direction.

## Proposal

Add a thin provider abstraction inside `src/core/embedding.ts` so `embed` / `embedBatch` route to either OpenAI or Gemini, with provider resolved once at first use from the environment.

**Selection precedence (proposed):**
1. `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai|gemini` (explicit override)
2. `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, route to openai (current default)
3. `GEMINI_API_KEY` set, route to gemini
4. Neither, `embed()` throws a clear error at call time, not at import (matches today's OpenAI only behavior of failing at API call, so importing the module never throws for users who never embed)

**Backward compatibility:** when both keys are set without an explicit override, OpenAI wins. Existing brains keep working with no env changes.

**Schema:** unchanged. Both providers emit `Float32Array(1536)`. The `vector(1536)` pgvector column and HNSW index are untouched. No migration.

**Cross provider hygiene:** documented limitation. Brains that switch providers mid life have mixed space embeddings until `gbrain embed --all` re-embeds under the new provider.

**Cost estimation:** still uses OpenAI tiktoken via `chunkers/code.ts`. For Gemini the per token cost preview is approximate (under 10% gap for English content). Could be tightened later with a Gemini specific `models.countTokens` call.

## Footprint

I have a working implementation locally that I'd open as a PR if the direction is welcome:

- `src/core/embedding.ts`: provider abstraction, both providers, lazy selection, backward compatible `EMBEDDING_MODEL` / `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` / `EMBEDDING_COST_PER_1K_TOKENS` exports.
- `test/embedding-provider.test.ts`: 8 unit tests covering selection precedence and the Gemini request shape (mocked, no live API).
- `test/sync-cost-preview.test.ts`: relax the OpenAI exact price pin to a supported provider band, since the cost constant now reflects whichever provider resolved.
- `docs/ENGINES.md`: new "Embedding providers" section.
- `README.md`: one line pipeline diagram update.

Net change: ~400 LOC added (most of it the new provider class plus tests), ~50 LOC modified.

Public API (`embed`, `embedBatch`) is unchanged. No call sites elsewhere in the codebase need updates.

## Questions for you

1. Is a Gemini provider in scope, or do you prefer to keep `embedding.ts` OpenAI only and let users solve this externally (e.g. wrapper at the CLI level)?
2. If yes: any preferences on selection precedence, env var names, or scope (e.g. would you want this gated behind a config flag in `~/.gbrain/config.json` rather than env driven)?
3. Naming: I went with `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` as the explicit override. Happy to change to whatever convention fits the project.

Happy to open the PR as is, iterate on the design before coding, or close this out if it's not the direction you want.

Thanks for gbrain. It's been quietly useful.

title: fix(sync): raise maxBuffer to 100 MiB to prevent silent ENOBUFS crash
body:
## What

`git()` helper in `sync.ts` uses `execFileSync` with Node's default 1 MiB `maxBuffer`. On repos with 60–100K files, `git diff --name-status -M` output exceeds this limit, killing the sync process silently — no error, no stack trace, just a dead PID.

## Root Cause

Observed on a 99K-file brain repo (62K tracked by git). Sync consistently died during the rename-detection phase at ~15% through `buildSyncManifest()`. The `ENOBUFS` error from `execFileSync` is not caught or logged — the process just vanishes.

## Fix

Raise `maxBuffer` to `100 * 1024 * 1024` (100 MiB). A 100K-file diff with long paths tops out around 10–20 MiB in practice, so 100 MiB is generous but bounded.

## Testing

- Survived 5+ full syncs on a 99K-file corpus (62K in git ls-files) without dying
- Previously failed at 15% on every attempt without the patch
- No behavioral change for repos under 1 MiB diff output (the vast majority)

fix(git-remote): move --no-recurse-submodules from global to per-command args
body:
## Problem

`GIT_SSRF_FLAGS` in `src/core/git-remote.ts` places `--no-recurse-submodules` in the global-options slot (before the subcommand). On git ≥2.43 this fails:

```
$ git -C /path -c http.followRedirects=false -c protocol.file.allow=never -c protocol.ext.allow=never --no-recurse-submodules pull --ff-only
unknown option: --no-recurse-submodules
```

`--no-recurse-submodules` is a per-command option for `clone` / `pull` / `fetch` only, not a top-level git flag. Older git versions were more lenient about flag position; modern git (2.43+, default on Ubuntu 24.04 and current macOS) enforces strict placement.

## Repro

Reproduces on git 2.43.0 / Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on every `gbrain sync` operation. The error surfaces as:

```
[gbrain phase] sync.git_pull error 5ms (git pull failed in /apps/kyle/lattice/bh-brain: Command failed: git -C /apps/kyl)
Warning: git pull failed: git pull failed in /apps/kyle/lattice/bh-brain: Command failed: git -C /apps/kyle/lattice/bh-brain -
```

Found while upgrading BH-DevServer (Ubuntu 24.04, git 2.43.0) to v0.33.2 — every autopilot cycle's sync phase reported failed git pull on all federated sources. Cycle completed (embed --stale still ran) but staleness detection from upstream commits was bypassed.

## Fix

- Drop `--no-recurse-submodules` from `GIT_SSRF_FLAGS`
- Append it explicitly to clone args (after `'clone'`)
- Append it explicitly to pull args (after `'--ff-only'`)

Net result: same submodule-recursion safety guarantee, with correct flag placement that works on git 2.43+.

## Testing

Verified locally: `sync.git_pull start` → `sync.git_pull done <N>ms` (success) across 3 federated sources on dev-server post-fix. Pre-fix all three failed in <10ms with the unknown-option error.
