title: fix: warn when env vars override ze-switch embedding config
body:
## Problem

`ze-switch` writes the new embedding model to DB config and `~/.gbrain/config.json`, but `loadConfig()` gives **highest precedence** to `process.env.GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL`. If the user has this env var set (common in `.env` files loaded at gateway/shell startup), the switch silently does nothing at runtime.

The user sees `Switch status: applied` and thinks it worked. But every gbrain command still uses the old OpenAI model because the env var overrides DB + file config.

**Real-world impact:** 716K chunks had to be re-embedded because the env override meant the switch to ZeroEntropy silently didn't take effect. Doctor reported `openai:text-embedding-3-large` dimension mismatch for hours before the root cause was traced to stale env vars.

## Fix

### 1. `ze-switch` env override warning

After applying the switch, checks if `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL` or `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` are set in the process environment and differ from the target. Prints a prominent warning box:

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  ⚠️  ENV OVERRIDE DETECTED — ACTION REQUIRED                ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL is set in your environment:         ║
║    Current env: openai:text-embedding-3-large               ║
║    Switch target: zeroentropyai:zembed-1                    ║
║                                                              ║
║  The env var takes HIGHEST PRECEDENCE and will override      ║
║  this switch. Update your .env file or shell environment.    ║
║                                                              ║
║  Without this change, the switch has NO EFFECT at runtime.   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### 2. `doctor` env/DB mismatch detector

New `embedding_env_override` check: if the env var disagrees with DB config, warns with the exact fix. Surfaces the mismatch on every doctor run instead of reporting a confusing dimension error.

## Testing

- Set `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL=openai:text-embedding-3-large` in env
- Run `gbrain ze-switch --non-interactive --force`
- Verify warning box appears after "Switch status: applied"
- Run `gbrain doctor --fast`
- Verify `embedding_env_override` warning appears

title: gbrain dream silently fails all DB phases on PostgreSQL — connectEngine() swallowed by try/catch in cli.ts
body:
Version: 0.41.2.0
Schema: v94
Database: PostgreSQL 18.4 (local, pgbouncer-style connection)
OS: CachyOS Linux
Install path: ~/skynet/hermes/gbrain-latest/

Summary
gbrain dream runs successfully against a PostgreSQL brain but silently fails every DB-dependent phase. Only local file-scanning phases (lint, backlinks, extract) execute. All other phases — sync, extract_facts, patterns, consolidate, propose_takes, grade_takes, calibration_profile, embed, orphans, purge, extract_atoms, synthesize_concepts — return "No database connection."
gbrain doctor works correctly and connects to the same PostgreSQL instance without issue.

Root cause identified
In src/cli.ts lines 1007–1024, connectEngine() is wrapped in a try/catch that silently swallows failures:
typescriptlet eng: BrainEngine | null = null;
try { eng = await connectEngine(); }
catch { /* DB unavailable — lint + backlinks still run */ }
When connectEngine() throws, eng stays null and the dream cycle proceeds with no database. All DB-dependent phases fail silently with "No database connection: connect() has not been called."
gbrain doctor uses a different initialization path that succeeds. The dream path's connectEngine() → loadConfig() → createEngine() → connectWithRetry() chain is throwing somewhere but the error is swallowed.

Evidence DB is healthy
bashgbrain doctor
 3,125 pages, schema v94, 100% embedded, health 70/100
 PostgreSQL connected, all checks pass

Direct Bun test also confirmed connection:
import createEngine, connectWithRetry → returned full stats cleanly

Steps to reproduce

Fresh install of v0.41.2.0 against PostgreSQL (not PGLite)
Confirm gbrain doctor returns healthy
Run gbrain dream --json
Observe: lint, backlinks, extract complete (0 results — local file ops only)
Observe: all DB phases return "No database connection"
Brain score unchanged, atoms 0, concepts 0, cost $0


Additional context

GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL exported in gbrain wrapper — no effect
gbrain init --postgres run to ensure ~/.gbrain/config.json has correct URL — no effect
Stale gbrain_cycle_locks rows cleared manually between attempts — no effect
4 separate dream cycle attempts, all same result
gbrain jobs stats connects to DB fine
gbrain schema active connects to DB fine
Only gbrain dream fails to establish engine connection


Expected behaviour
gbrain dream should use the same engine initialization path as gbrain doctor and connect to PostgreSQL successfully.
Suggested fix
Remove the silent swallow in the try/catch, or at minimum surface the actual error thrown by connectEngine() so operators can diagnose. The current behaviour makes debugging impossible without reading source.

title: fix(postgres): prevent transient module engines from disconnecting a shared singleton
body:
## Summary

This fixes a module-singleton ownership bug in `PostgresEngine.disconnect()`.

Today, a module-style `PostgresEngine` cannot tell whether it opened the shared `db.ts` singleton or merely attached to another holder had already opened. On disconnect, both cases call `db.disconnect()`. A transient probe can therefore close the shared module connection out from under a still-running cycle/worker.

Concrete path found while investigating #1413:

- `resolveLintContentSanity()` in `src/commands/lint.ts` creates a second Postgres engine to lift content-sanity config from the DB.
- With no `poolSize`, that second engine uses the module-singleton path.
- When the main cycle/worker already has the singleton open, the lint probe only attaches to it.
- The lint probe’s `finally { engine.disconnect() }` currently calls `db.disconnect()` anyway, nulling the shared singleton.
- Later consumers routed through `db.getConnection()` fail with `No database connection: connect() has not been called`.

This is a confirmed localization for #1413’s “something nulls the singleton mid-cycle” note. A second manifestation is `autopilot-cycle --follow`: the lint phase completes, then the inline worker fails while completing/failing the job because the shared singleton was disconnected mid-cycle.

## Fix

Make module-style `PostgresEngine` disconnect ownership-aware:

- Add `db.isConnected()` so a module-style `PostgresEngine` can capture ownership before `db.connect(config)`.
- On `PostgresEngine.connect()` in module mode, set `_ownsModuleConnection = !db.isConnected()` before connecting.
- On `PostgresEngine.disconnect()` in module mode, call `db.disconnect()` only when this engine opened the module singleton.
- Attaching engines only detach their own wrapper state; they do not close the shared singleton.

This keeps production defaults unchanged. It does not introduce a global ref-count, which would be easy to unbalance because module `db.connect()` is intentionally idempotent. The opener still closes the module singleton explicitly, so the fix avoids both premature close and stranded pool slots.

## Relationship to #1415

This PR is complementary to #1415, not a competing rewrite.

- #1415 moves autopilot’s main engine onto an instance-owned pool, removing that path’s dependence on the module singleton.
- This PR fixes the lower-level footgun: transient module-style engines should not be able to close a module singleton they only attached to.

Both can coexist. #1415 shields the autopilot daemon. This change protects any consumer that uses a long-lived module singleton while a transient module-style probe opens and disconnects during the same process.

## Test

Adds a real-Postgres regression to `test/e2e/postgres-engine-disconnect-idempotency.test.ts`:

1. Open the module-level connection as holder A.
2. Connect holder B as a module-style `PostgresEngine` so it attaches to the already-open singleton.
3. Disconnect holder B.
4. Assert `db.isConnected()` is still true and `db.getConnection().unsafe('SELECT 1 as ok')` succeeds.
5. Disconnect holder A and assert the module singleton is closed.

Pre-fix, step 4 fails with `connect() has not been called`. Post-fix, the attaching engine detaches without clobbering the holder’s connection.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- Real-Postgres fail-before/pass-after was validated during triage.
- On upstream `main` (`6a10bad8`), an equivalent holder/probe reproduction fails with `CLOBBERED No database connection: connect() has not been called`.
- On this fix branch, the same reproduction prints `ALIVE 1` and exits 0.
- The new e2e regression passes on the fix branch: `3 pass, 0 fail`.
- On current upstream `master` (`ca68633f`), `bun test test/audit/audit-writer.test.ts` passes without an extra audit-writer patch, so this PR only carries the Postgres ownership fix.

Closes #1413.

title: feat(synopsis): tail-truncate documentText for small-model chat handlers
body:
## Summary

Add `SYNOPSIS_DOC_MAX_CHARS` env-overridable cap (default 32768 chars,
~8K tokens) applied in `buildUserPrompt` for the per-chunk synopsis
prompt. Truncates the TAIL of `documentText` so the head (title,
frontmatter, intro) carries the document-level anchor the synopsis
needs.

## Motivation

Small local chat models (Gemma 4 E2B, Qwen3 4B on Ollama / LM Studio)
get dramatically slower on long contexts even when their declared
window is 131K tokens. A 73K-char page synopsis on Gemma 4 E2B takes
60-120s, exceeding the worker's default 30s `lockDuration` and tripping
`lock-lost` errors during the contextual-retrieval per_chunk_synopsis
backfill.

This is a companion lever to issue #1014 / PR #1177 (`--lock-duration`
on `gbrain jobs work`) — bumping the lock TTL alone helps but lets each
job consume more wall-clock per chunk; capping `documentText` makes each
call complete *faster*, which lets the existing 30s lock survive on
medium-length pages too. Both together get the synopsis backfill running
reliably on small local LLMs without burning Anthropic credit.

## Behavior

- Default `SYNOPSIS_DOC_MAX_CHARS = 32768` (~8K tokens at 4 chars/tok)
- Env override: `GBRAIN_SYNOPSIS_DOC_MAX_CHARS=<int>` with range
  `[512, 1048576]` (clamped via regex; falls back to default on invalid)

title: Postgres install hardcodes embedding dimension at 1536
`gbrain sync --skip-failed` drops bare-markdown log files from the index
body:
_Filed via brain-janitor from `Learning and Strategy/Wiki/reference/gbrain-known-bugs.md` (bug #6)._

- **Filed**: 2026-05-24 (pending upstream filing — not yet posted)
- **Symptom**: After running `gbrain sync --skip-failed`, a domain `log.md` that was previously indexed is silently removed from the gbrain page store. The sync output includes a single line `Deleted un-syncable page: <slug>` and proceeds. The on-disk file is untouched (all entries intact), but `mcp__gbrain__get_page` for that slug returns `page_not_found` and the page no longer surfaces in retrieval. Distinct from bug #7 (createVersion) — that fails on edit, this one *deletes* on `--skip-failed`.
- **Root cause** (suspected): the sync's `--skip-failed` parse-failure handler treats "no YAML frontmatter" as un-syncable rather than as bare-markdown-valid. Domain `log.md` files are valid per the vault schema (`Append-only chronological record. Format: ## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <subject>`) and intentionally have no frontmatter — they are operational logs, not typed pages. The sync collapses two different conditions (genuinely malformed vs. valid-but-untyped) into the same deletion path.
- **India's encounter**: Ran `gbrain sync --skip-failed` on 2026-05-24 after the [[phase-6-architecture-blind-spots-2026-05-23]] decision-log landed. Sync output: `Deleted un-syncable page: learning-and-strategy/log`. The file at `Learning and Strategy/log.md` (3755 bytes, 37 lines, two recent appends from the same session) was unchanged on disk but `mcp__gbrain__get_page` returned 404 for `learning-and-strategy/log` immediately after.
- **Workaround**: None applied yet. Two options India can pick from:
  1. Add a minimal `---\ntype: log\nid: <slug>\n---\n` frontmatter to every domain `log.md` so gbrain parses them as typed pages. Requires extending the schema with a `log` page type (or repurposing `reference-list`).
  2. Pin the affected log files in an `~/.gbrain/sync-exclude` (if such a mechanism exists in this version) so sync ignores them entirely, preserving the bare-markdown convention.
- **Scope of impact**: Only `learning-and-strategy/log.md` confirmed dropped (only modified log in this session — the file is what triggered the re-parse attempt). Other domain logs (`Ninjacat/log.md`, `Tall Pines/log.md`, `IGE/log.md`, etc.) are likely still indexed from earlier successful syncs, but will hit the same deletion path the next time they are edited and re-synced with `--skip-failed`. Vault root `log.md` is in the same risk class. Pattern is vault-wide; impact will surface incrementally as each log gets touched.
- **Status**: Pending upstream filing. Filing will request `--skip-failed` distinguish between "parse error in YAML" (drop) and "no frontmatter at all" (treat as bare markdown, index with synthesized minimal metadata or leave unchanged) — the second case is intentional per vault conventions like Karpathy's, not an error to acknowledge-away.

title: `gbrain sync` `modified` counter inflates on per-file failures (cosmetic)
body:
_Filed via brain-janitor from `Learning and Strategy/Wiki/reference/gbrain-known-bugs.md` (bug #8)._

- **Filed**: 2026-05-25 (pending upstream filing — not yet posted)
- **Severity**: Low. Cosmetic; doesn't cause data loss when other signals are read.
- **Symptom**: `gbrain sync --skip-failed` summary block can report `~N modified, 0 chunks created` even when all N files were skipped due to per-file failures. The `modified` count reflects iteration progress rather than commit success. The reliable signal that nothing landed is `0 chunks created` alongside per-file `Warning: skipped ...` lines — not the summary counter.
- **Root cause** (suspected): the progress counter advances on iteration completion regardless of whether the per-file write actually committed. Per-file failure aborts the write but the counter has already been bumped. Exit code reflects "ran to completion," not "all files committed."
- **India's encounter**: 2026-05-25 manual `gbrain sync --skip-failed` of [[phase-6-online-arbitrage-sourcing]] reported `~1 modified, 0 chunks created`. **Proximate cause was env-not-sourced**, not an absent embedding key in the abstract: `ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY` IS defined in `~/.gbrain/env`, but the manual sync invocation didn't `source ~/.gbrain/env` first, so the env var wasn't visible to the gbrain process. When the cron entry sources the env file (which it now does), embedding succeeds and the counter is accurate. **The earlier framing of this bug (that gbrain has no embedding-key fallback) was misdiagnosed** — gbrain correctly requires an embedding provider and the user's config provides one; the issue was invocation hygiene. The remaining real bug is just the misleading counter on whatever path causes per-file failure (source mismatch, missing env, dimension mismatch, etc.).
- **Workaround**: Treat `0 chunks created` and any `Warning: skipped` lines as the truth signal when sync accuracy matters — not the `~N modified` count. Always `source ~/.gbrain/env` before manual sync; the cron entry does this automatically.
- **Status**: Pending upstream filing as a polish bug. Filing will request the `modified` count only increment after successful commit. Embedding-fallback behavior is a separate (and probably unnecessary) request that the earlier draft of this entry incorrectly bundled in.

title: Read paths disagree based on `source_id` awareness
body:
_Filed via brain-janitor from `Learning and Strategy/Wiki/reference/gbrain-known-bugs.md` (bug #9)._

- **Filed**: 2026-05-25 (pending upstream filing — not yet posted)
- **Symptom**: `mcp__gbrain__get_page` with an exact slug returns `page_not_found` for a page that exists in the database. The same MCP call with `fuzzy: true` returns the same slug as an `ambiguous_slug` candidate. Direct SQL (`SELECT * FROM pages WHERE slug = '<slug>'`) confirms the page exists. Multiple read paths reach divergent conclusions about the same page in the same session.
- **Root cause** (verified 2026-05-25 via source inspection): `src/mcp/server.ts:42` initializes the MCP server's default source from `process.env.GBRAIN_SOURCE || 'default'`. Exact `get_page` calls scope queries to that source_id. The fuzzy resolver does NOT scope by source_id — it searches the entire `pages` table. When the MCP server is launched with `GBRAIN_SOURCE` unset (or set to a source that doesn't hold the page), exact lookups 404 while fuzzy resolves correctly. **Same root cause as bug #7**, surfaced as a read inconsistency rather than a write failure.
- **India's encounter**: 2026-05-25 verifying [[phase-6-online-arbitrage-sourcing]] landed in the brain after a sync attempt. Exact `get_page` returned 404; fuzzy returned the slug as a candidate. The MCP server was launched from `~/.claude.json` with `env: {}` — no `GBRAIN_SOURCE` set — so it queried `source_id='default'` which held 1 page (the orphan decision-log). Fixed on 2026-05-25 by adding `"GBRAIN_SOURCE": "studiovault"` to all three `mcpServers.gbrain.env` blocks in `~/.claude.json` (takes effect on next Claude Code restart) and migrating the orphan page to `studiovault`.
- **Workaround**:
  1. Set `GBRAIN_SOURCE=<source_id>` in the MCP launch env — for Claude Code, in `~/.claude.json` under each `mcpServers.gbrain.env` block.
  2. When `get_page` returns unexpected 404, try `fuzzy: true`; if it surfaces the slug as a candidate, the issue is source scope, not page existence.
- **Status**: Pending upstream filing. Filing will request: (a) `gbrain serve --help` document the `GBRAIN_SOURCE` env var (currently undocumented in help output even though it's the only documented lever); (b) exact `get_page` return a source-aware error (`"page not found in source 'X' — try 'fuzzy: true' or specify another source"`) instead of the generic 404; (c) consider whether `fuzzy` and exact resolvers should share filter semantics by default.

title: `gbrain query` CLI defaults to `source=default` when `--source` omitted
body:
_Filed via brain-janitor from `Learning and Strategy/Wiki/reference/gbrain-known-bugs.md` (bug #10)._

- **Filed**: 2026-05-25 (pending upstream filing — not yet posted)
- **Symptom**: `gbrain query "<phrase>" --top-k N` returns literal `No results.` even when matching content exists in the index. Adding `--source studiovault` to the same command returns expected results with high confidence (0.9996 in the test case below). The CLI does not appear to honor `GBRAIN_SOURCE` env var even when `~/.gbrain/env` is sourced into the shell beforehand — only the explicit `--source` flag works.
- **Root cause** (suspected, same family as #7 and #9): the `query` CLI scopes retrieval to `source_id` and defaults to `'default'` when `--source` is omitted. The `default` source holds 0 pages (all 515 live under `studiovault`), so retrieval returns the empty set. Same `source_id` misuse pattern as bug #7 (sync write path) and bug #9 (MCP exact `get_page` read path); this is the CLI read path equivalent. The asymmetry with MCP — MCP honors `GBRAIN_SOURCE` since the 2026-05-25 fix to `~/.claude.json`, CLI does not — is itself the most surprising finding here.
- **India's encounter**: 2026-05-25 during the end-to-end verification test sequence run after the `GBRAIN_SOURCE=studiovault` MCP fix landed and Claude Code was restarted. `gbrain query "Phase 6 sourcing intelligence four agents" --top-k 3` returned `No results.`; the same command with `--source studiovault` appended returned `[0.9996] learning-and-strategy/wiki/projects/phase-6-online-arbitrage-sourcing` as the top hit. First reflex was to suspect an embedding gap (the sync run earlier in the day had reported only `2 pages embedded` — a worrying signal), but applying the #7/#9 pattern (try `--source` first) resolved on first re-test. Embedding gap thesis discarded.
- **Workaround**: Always pass `--source studiovault` explicitly to `gbrain query`, `gbrain search`, `gbrain get`, and any other CLI command that reads pages. Setting `GBRAIN_SOURCE=studiovault` in the shell env is not sufficient — the CLI ignores it. (The cron entry already passes `--source studiovault` explicitly for sync, so scheduled runs are unaffected. Manual CLI invocations are the exposed surface.)
- **Status**: Pending upstream filing as a UX bug, third entry in the `source_id`-default-misbehavior family (#7 write, #9 MCP read, #10 CLI read). Filing will request: (a) CLI read commands default to the only non-empty source when exactly one exists in the `sources` table; (b) when the queried source is empty AND other sources hold pages, emit a warning (`"source 'default' has 0 pages — did you mean 'studiovault'?"`) instead of a bare `No results.` that is indistinguishable from a real retrieval miss; (c) CLI honor `GBRAIN_SOURCE` env var symmetric with the MCP server, so a single env-level config covers both surfaces. The bare `No results.` is the worst failure mode of the three because it looks identical to a genuine semantic-search miss — it doesn't even hint that source scope is involved.

title: `gbrain sync` reports `+1 added` but page never persists when ZeroEntropy embedding step errors
body:
_Filed via brain-janitor from `Learning and Strategy/Wiki/reference/gbrain-known-bugs.md` (bug #11)._

- **Filed**: 2026-05-25 (pending upstream filing — not yet posted)
- **Symptom**: `gbrain sync --source studiovault` runs against a working tree containing one new page. Output shows `[sync.imports] 1/1 (100%) done` and `Synced <a>..<b>: +1 added`. A warning line earlier in the output reads `Warning: skipped <path>: ZeroEntropy embedding requires ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY.` Subsequent `gbrain get <slug>` returns `page_not_found`; `gbrain list --type <T>` does not show the page. Re-running with `--skip-failed` does not recover — the failure is acknowledged in `~/.gbrain/sync-failures.jsonl` but the page is still absent from the index. The "+1 added" counter is a lie.
- **Root cause** (suspected, same family as #6 and #8): the embedding step is a non-optional gate in the sync pipeline even though ZeroEntropy is an external service. When the embedding fails (missing key, network error, quota), the per-page transaction rolls back but the sync orchestrator reports success against the commit hash. Next sync sees the same commit as "already synced" and refuses to retry. Functionally: a single transient embedding-service issue can cause permanent silent dropouts.
- **India's encounter**: 2026-05-25 during Step 7/8 of the agent-factory rollout. Synced the new `agent-factory.md`; sync output looked clean (`1/1 done`, `+1 added`). Five minutes later, `gbrain query` against the agent-factory page returned no results. Inspection: `gbrain get` returned `page_not_found`; `gbrain list --type project --source studiovault` showed phase-6 and phase-7 but not agent-factory. The `ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY` was present in `~/.gbrain/env` but the daemon-equivalent (here: the CLI shell context where the user ran `gbrain sync`) didn't have it loaded. After sourcing `~/.gbrain/env` and re-running, gbrain reported "Already up to date" — the previous commit was marked synced. Only `gbrain put <slug> < file.md` (direct write path, bypassing sync) successfully landed the page.
- **Workaround**: (a) Always `source ~/.gbrain/env` before invoking `gbrain sync` so the embedding key is in scope; (b) if a sync run shows a `ZeroEntropy embedding requires…` warning, do NOT trust the "+N added" counter — verify with `gbrain get <slug>` for each new page; (c) when sync has already marked a commit as synced but the page didn't land, use `gbrain put <slug> < <path-to-md>` to push directly. The `put` path appears to be embedding-tolerant (succeeds with or without ZeroEntropy).
- **Status**: Pending upstream filing. This is a third instance of the broader "sync orchestrator reports success on partial failure" pattern (compare #6, #8). The right fix is for the sync orchestrator to (a) defer marking the commit synced until ALL pages in the diff are queryable, and (b) downgrade ZeroEntropy embedding from a hard gate to a deferred optional step (insert the page without embedding; queue the embedding for retry). The CLI should also exit non-zero when any page in the diff fails — currently exit code is 0 even when the warning fires.

title: v0.41.9.0 — UX/reliability fix wave (5 defects from production report)
body:
## Summary

Five distinct UX/reliability defects from a single production bug report, shipped as one wave.

**D1 — Pre-flight embedding credential check.** `gbrain sync`, `gbrain embed`, and `gbrain import` now check `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, etc.) before touching the import phase. Bypass with `--no-embed`. New `gateway.diagnoseEmbedding()` tagged-union API drives a paste-ready error message; `isAvailable('embedding')` delegates so existing callers keep their boolean contract. Closes the "565 identical entries in sync-failures.jsonl" bug class.

**D2 — Classify embedding errors.** Four new patterns in `classifyErrorCode` (sync.ts): `EMBEDDING_NO_CREDS`, `EMBEDDING_NO_TOUCHPOINT`, `EMBEDDING_RATE_LIMIT`, `EMBEDDING_QUOTA`, `EMBEDDING_OVERSIZE`. Patterns derived from verbatim provider error strings (native-openai, native-google, anthropic-as-embed-provider misconfig, openai-compat via `defaultResolveAuth`). Doctor's `sync_failures` summary now bucketing useful instead of `UNKNOWN`.

**D3 — Default timeouts + lock-owner verification.** New `withTimeout<T>` helper. `cli.ts` wraps `connectEngine` AND dispatch for read-only commands at 30s (search) / 10s (sources list); user `--timeout=Ns` wins. New `inspectLock` / `listStaleLocks` / `deleteLockRow` in `db-lock.ts`. Rich "Another sync in progress" message names holder PID + hostname + age. New `gbrain sync --break-lock --source <id>` (safe; refuses when alive PID + recent lock; combines PID-dead with 60s age guard to defeat PID reuse) + `--force-break-lock` (escape hatch). Both flags refuse `--all` (per-source invocation required). New `stale_locks` doctor check uses `ttl_expires_at < NOW()` as the canonical signal.

**D4 — Schema-probe deadlock silenced on the common race.** New `tryRunPendingMigrations(engine, deadlineMs)` retries on SQLSTATE 40P01 once with 250ms backoff, then polls `hasPendingMigrations` every 250ms over 5s deadline. Silent success when the race resolved (the COMMON case the user complained about). Warns with revised wording (drops destructive-sounding `gbrain init --migrate-only` hint) when migrations are genuinely stuck.

**D5 — SIGPIPE + cleanup registry.** New `src/core/process-cleanup.ts`: `registerCleanup` + `installSignalHandlers` for SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGPIPE/uncaughtException/unhandledRejection (NOT SIGINT — the existing AbortController at `cli.ts:254` owns Ctrl-C). EPIPE-on-stdout routes through cleanup registry. Single ownership: `tryAcquireDbLock` auto-registers; `release()` deregisters. Idempotent on double-signal.

title: fix: ze-switch preserves embedding_image column dimensions
body:
## Problem

`runSchemaTransition` drops and recreates **both** `embedding` and `embedding_image` columns at the target dimension. But `embedding_image` uses a separate multimodal model (e.g. `voyage-multimodal-3` at 1024d) whose dimensions are independent of the text embedding model.

Switching from OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` (1536d) to ZeroEntropy `zembed-1` (1280d) also changes `embedding_image` from `vector(1024)` → `vector(1280)`, creating a silent dimension mismatch that prevents the multimodal provider from writing image embeddings.

## Fix

Only transition the primary `embedding` column. Leave `embedding_image` dimensions untouched — just rebuild its HNSW index for safety.

## Impact

Without this fix, every `ze-switch` run silently breaks multimodal search for brains using a separate image embedding model with different dimensions.

## Summary

**CI wallclock on every PR drops from ~23 min to ~9-10 min, with ≤2 min on cache-hit PRs.** Five orthogonal levers, one cathedral PR with atomic bisect-friendly commits.

### Performance levers

- **Restructured `test.yml` jobs** — `verify` + `serial-tests` extracted from shard 1 into their own runners. Shard 1 stops carrying ~3min of verify + serial overhead on top of its matrix work.
- **Matrix 4 → 6 shards** — stays under GitHub free-tier ~20-job concurrency budget on multi-PR days (6 shards × 2 PRs + verify + serial + gitleaks + cache jobs = ~24 jobs).
- **Weight-aware LPT bin-packer** — `scripts/sharding.ts` replaces FNV-1a path-hash partition. Real-weight 6-shard projection: every shard estimated at 534s = 8.9 min wallclock (compare to current p100 of 23-26 min on the unlucky shard).

## Summary

Three production reliability fixes in one wave, rebuilt from closed community PRs #1414, #1416, #1421 (originally proposed by @garrytan-agents) with structural improvements from `/plan-eng-review` + codex outside-voice review.

**The user-visible wins:**

1. **`dream.*` config you set via `gbrain config set` now actually reaches the cycle phase that reads it.** Pre-fix, `gbrain config set dream.synthesize.session_corpus_dir /path` wrote successfully to DB but `extract-atoms` skipped with "no transcripts to process" because it read via file-plane-only `loadConfig()`. The systemic fix lives in `loadConfigWithEngine()`'s sparse-merge block.

2. **Your background `extract` and `sync` cycles stop silently losing rows on PgBouncer connection drops.** Pre-fix, ~30% of batched inserts threw `No database connection: connect() has not been called` and silently dropped 100 rows each. Now a single 500ms retry catches the recycle. Snapshot-before-clear contract means the retry sends the same data even if the producer wrote more during the delay.

3. **`gbrain ze-switch` won't silently corrupt your brain when env vars override the switch.** Pre-fix, `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL=openai:text-embedding-3-large gbrain ze-switch` migrated schema to 2560d columns then embedded with OpenAI's 1536d model — the documented 716K-chunk damage incident. 4. **`extract_atoms` stops creating duplicate atoms on re-runs across days.** Pre-existing v0.41.2.0 bug: atom slugs were `atoms/${todayDate()}/${title-slug}`, so re-discovering the same content on day N+1 wrote a second atom. ## Summary

The recall miss on 60K+ message iMessage/Slack imports (a chunk reading only \`Locker 93 code 9494\` has no topical anchor because \"cabin\" was established 50K messages earlier) gets fixed by bulk-extracting facts from those pages with a topical/temporal header, so the facts table — which retrieval already blends in — fills with anchor-rich claims the chunk store can't represent.

- **Per Codex T6d: close #1406 AFTER this PR is green**, not before. Preserves the comparison artifact and social attribution.

## What changes for the user

```bash
# Preview cost before running.
gbrain sources audit default --json | jq '.facts_backfill_estimate'

# Run the backfill with a $5 cap on the first pass.
gbrain extract-conversation-facts --max-cost-usd 5

# Or background it.
gbrain extract-conversation-facts --background --max-cost-usd 5
gbrain jobs follow <printed-job-id>

# Doctor surfaces backlog.
gbrain doctor --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.name==\"conversation_facts_backlog\")'

# Optional: enable autopilot drain.
gbrain config set cycle.conversation_facts_backfill.enabled true
```

Two-layer cost AND walltime protection on the cycle phase: per-source caps (\$1, 20min) AND brain-wide caps (\$5, 30min). A 10-source brain can't quietly spend 10× its config.

## Architecture decisions (all locked through 2 Codex rounds + 2 eng review passes)

- **Strict per-source core** — \`runExtractConversationFactsCore({sourceId, ...})\` always takes one sourceId. CLI + cycle phase each do their own multi-source iteration because PHASE_SCOPE='source' is taxonomy-only per cycle.ts:131.
- **Two-phase enumeration** — paginated \`listPages({type, sourceId, limit:10})\` so worst case is 10×25MB=250MB resident vs PR's unbounded; per-page body cap MAX_PAGE_BODY_BYTES=25MB with skip+warn+doctor surfacing.
- **Page-global row_num accumulator** — facts unique index is \`(source_id, source_markdown_slug, row_num)\` per migration v51; per-segment row_num would collide on segment 2 (Codex C1).
- **Page-level TERMINAL audit row** — written after all segments commit (source=\`cli:extract-conversation-facts:terminal\`); doctor's NOT EXISTS query matches the terminal row, NOT any-fact-for-slug, so partial-extraction pages stay in backlog (Codex C7).
- **Optional opts.budgetTracker** — nested \`withBudgetTracker\` REPLACES per gateway.ts:2011; cycle phase passes brain-wide tracker through opts so core doesn't auto-wrap-and-replace it (Codex C5).
- **Body read covers compiled_truth + timeline** — iMessage importers put history in the timeline half; PR's \`compiled_truth ?? ''\` would silently drop it (F1).
- **Honors facts.extraction_enabled kill-switch** with --override-disabled escape (F2).
- **--types reads cycle config as single source of truth** so doctor backlog and CLI default agree (Eng-v2 A2).
- **Fingerprint on sourceId only** — widening cycle.types config doesn't invalidate completed-page state (Eng-v2 A3).

- Streaming/per-segment fetch for 50MB+ conversation pages (today's 25MB hard cap is the explicit boundary).
- Fact-blending in hybrid search (\`SearchResult\` is chunk-shaped today per Codex C4; making facts first-class search results is weeks of work outside this wave).
- Speaker provenance via \`fact.spoken_by\` column — dropped after Codex T4 caught the semantic error (entity_slug ≠ speaker). Filed as properly-scoped follow-up TODO.
- Bulk-purge via \`gbrain forget --where\` (today's \`gbrain forget\` takes one fact-id).
- Smart segment splitting on topic shift via embedding-cosine drift.

title: fix(doctor): guard getConfig() returns against non-string values
body:
## Problem

`gbrain doctor` crashes on v0.41.2 with:

```
undefined is not an object (evaluating 's.toLowerCase')
```

Reproduced on a production brain (~16K pages, Supabase Postgres) with a custom schema pack. The crash is intermittent — it depends on how config values were stored (JSON vs string).

## Error Log

```
$ gbrain doctor
undefined is not an object (evaluating 's.toLowerCase')
```

No stack trace printed. The entire doctor command aborts — no health checks are reported.

## Root Cause

`engine.getConfig()` is typed as `Promise<string | null>` but can return non-string values (boolean `true`, number `1`) when:
- Config was stored via `gbrain config set key value --force`
- Config was set programmatically with a JSON value
- The underlying config table stores JSONB and the value isn't a string

The crash site is `checkGraphSignalsCoverage()` at line 1083:

```typescript
const cfgVal = await engine.getConfig('search.graph_signals');
// cfgVal is boolean `true`, not string "true"
const v = cfgVal.trim().toLowerCase();  // 💥 boolean has no .trim()
```

The guard `if (cfgVal !== null && cfgVal !== undefined)` passes for boolean `true`, then `.trim()` is undefined on booleans.

## What We Tried

1. Checked all `getConfig()` call sites in doctor.ts — found 4 vulnerable patterns
2. Noted that line 1089 already had the correct pattern: `typeof modeRaw === 'string' ? ...`
3. Considered inline fixes vs a shared helper — chose the helper to prevent future regressions

## Solution

Added `cfgToString()` helper that safely coerces any `getConfig()` return value:

```typescript
function cfgToString(val: unknown): string {
  if (val === null || val === undefined) return '';
  return typeof val === 'string' ? val.trim().toLowerCase() : String(val).toLowerCase();
}
```

Applied to all 4 vulnerable doctor checks:

| Check | Config key | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `graph_signals_coverage` | `search.graph_signals` | `cfgVal.trim().toLowerCase()` 💥 | `cfgToString(cfgVal)` |
| `reranker_health` | `search.reranker.enabled` | `cfg === 'true'` (silent mismatch) | `cfgToString(cfg) === 'true'` |
| `brainstorm_health` | `search.track_retrieval` | `trackCfg === 'false'` (silent mismatch) | `cfgToString(trackCfg) === 'false'` |
| `unified_multimodal_coverage` | `search.unified_multimodal` | `flag === 'true'` (silent mismatch) | `cfgToString(flag) === 'true'` |

The `graph_signals_coverage` fix prevents the crash. The other 3 fixes prevent silent logic errors where boolean config values would never match string comparisons.

## Testing

- Verified `gbrain doctor` completes successfully after the fix on the same production brain that previously crashed
- Confirmed all 55+ health checks pass through to completion
- The helper handles: string → trim+lower, boolean/number → String()+lower, null/undefined → empty string

title: docs: v0.29 to v0.41.2 production upgrade audit — 3 bugs + 8 feature gaps
body:
## Problem

A production brain (~16K pages, Supabase Postgres, custom schema pack) was upgraded from v0.29-era to v0.41.2. Post-upgrade audit found **3 critical bugs** and **8 features with no discoverability path** — operators can't activate what they can't find.

## Critical Bugs

### 1. Dream cycle loses DB connection on Supabase pooler (P0)

`gbrain dream` on a 16K-page brain fails for 13/16 phases:

```
  ✗ sync        No database connection: connect() has not been called.
  ✗ synthesize  No database connection: connect() has not been called.
  ✗ extract_facts  No database connection: connect() has not been called.
  ... (10 more phases)
```

The extract phase partially completes (scans 15,752 files) but loses ~381 timeline rows in late batches when the pooler drops the idle connection. All subsequent DB-dependent phases fail.

**Root cause:** Supabase PgBouncer (port 6543) evicts idle backends. The filesystem-scanning phases create long gaps with no DB queries. No reconnect logic between phases or on batch error.

### 2. `gbrain doctor` crashes on v0.41.2

```
$ gbrain doctor
undefined is not an object (evaluating 's.toLowerCase')
```

Worked on v0.41.0, broke after v0.41.2 upgrade. Likely null-safety issue in the new domain-aggregator code path when `calibration_domains` is empty/undeclared in the active schema pack.

### 3. Minion worker has no supervision or discoverability

A job has been `waiting` for 5 days with no worker to process it. Doctor's `queue_health` check reports "no stalled jobs" (technically true — it's waiting, not stalled). There's no:
- Doctor check for "jobs waiting but no worker running"
- `gbrain autopilot --install` option that includes the worker
- Default healthcheck/restart mechanism

## Feature Discoverability Gaps

An operator upgrading across 12 minor versions (v0.29 → v0.41) gets automatic schema migrations but **zero guidance** on new features to configure:

| Feature | Version | Requires | Discoverable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibration domains | v0.41.2 | `calibration_domains` in pack YAML | ❌ No CLI, no docs, aggregator enum only in source |
| Dream cycle atom extraction | v0.41.2 | `phases:` field in custom pack | ❌ Not suggested by `schema review-candidates` |
| Nightly quality probe | v0.41.1 | Config flip | ❌ Doctor doesn't suggest |
| Eval gate / search baseline | v0.41.1 | `bench publish` + `eval gate` | ❌ No getting-started workflow |
| Code intelligence | v0.33-v0.34 | Code pages in brain | ❌ Commands exist but undocumented for operators |

Custom packs extending `gbrain-base` silently miss new pack-level features (`phases`, `calibration_domains`). No diff mechanism exists to show "gbrain-base now supports X that your pack doesn't declare."

## Proposed Solutions

### P0 — Fix broken things
1. **Connection resilience in cycle runner** — reconnect between phases; retry on batch insert error
2. **Null-safety in doctor's domain-aggregator path** — handle empty/missing `calibration_domains`

### P1 — Make doctor the upgrade advisor
3. Add `[SUGGEST]` tier to doctor output for feature activation hints:
   - "calibration_domains not declared — per-topic accuracy tracking available"
   - "nightly quality probe disabled — ~$10/mo for automatic regression detection"
   - "no eval baseline — `gbrain bench publish` protects search quality"
   - "jobs waiting but no worker detected"
   - "custom pack missing `phases` field — dream cycle won't run extract_atoms/synthesize_concepts"

### P2 — Upgrade experience
4. `gbrain upgrade --changelog` or `gbrain doctor --post-upgrade` — show what's new
5. `gbrain schema review-candidates` should suggest `phases` + `calibration_domains`
6. Document Supabase pooler idle timeout behavior and `GBRAIN_DISABLE_DIRECT_POOL`

## Full Audit

See [`docs/audits/v041-production-upgrade-audit.md`](docs/audits/v041-production-upgrade-audit.md) for the complete feature-by-feature analysis including environment details, error logs, and a prioritized action plan.

## Testing

- Audit performed on a live production brain
- Dream cycle failure reproduced on Supabase transaction pooler (port 6543)
- Doctor crash reproduced on fresh v0.41.2 install with custom pack (no calibration_domains)

title: fix: check-resolvable reports 227 issues on bundled skills (missing RESOLVER.md)
body:
## Problem

`gbrain check-resolvable` reports 227 issues (47 errors, 180 warnings) because the bundled `skills/` directory in the gbrain package has 47 skills but no `RESOLVER.md`. Every bundled skill shows as `unreachable`, and every `routing-eval.jsonl` entry shows as `routing_fixture_lint` because the expected skill isn't in a resolver.

```
Auto-detected skills directory from skills/ found by walking up from cwd (v0.33): /data/.bun/install/global/node_modules/gbrain/skills
resolver_health: FAIL — 227 issue(s): 47 error(s), 180 warning(s)
  • unreachable        ingest          Add a trigger row for 'skills/ingest/SKILL.md' in RESOLVER.md
  • unreachable        query           Add a trigger row for 'skills/query/SKILL.md' in RESOLVER.md
  ... (47 unreachable, 180 routing_fixture_lint)
```

This also affects agents running `gbrain doctor`, which reports `resolver_health: WARN` even when the brain is healthy — the warnings are about the gbrain package's own bundled skills, not the user's brain.

## Root Cause

The bundled `skills/` directory ships 47 skills with `routing-eval.jsonl` fixtures but no `RESOLVER.md` to register their triggers. `check-resolvable` auto-detects `skills/` by walking up from cwd, finds the bundled skills, and correctly reports they're unreachable.

## Proposed Fix

Ship a `skills/RESOLVER.md` in the gbrain package that registers all 47 bundled skills with their triggers. This can be auto-generated from the `triggers:` frontmatter in each skill's `SKILL.md`.

Alternatively, `check-resolvable` could skip bundled/package skills and only validate user-workspace skills, or auto-register skills from `triggers:` frontmatter without requiring a RESOLVER.md.

resolver_health: skillpack-harvest false-positive — 7 routing-miss warnings on vanilla install (v0.40.8.0)
body:
## Symptom
`gbrain doctor --json` reports 7 `routing_miss` warnings under `resolver_health`, all pointing at `skillpack-harvest` on a vanilla install.

## Diagnosis
- `/opt/gbrain/skills/skillpack-harvest/routing-eval.jsonl` has 7 intent phrasings ("lift this skill back into gbrain so others can use it", "publish my fork-only skill upstream", etc.)
- `/opt/gbrain/skills/skillpack-harvest/SKILL.md` `triggers:` block has 5 phrasings ("harvest this skill into gbrain", "publish this skill to gbrain", etc.)
- `/opt/gbrain/skills/RESOLVER.md` line 65 lists the same 5 triggers
- The resolver doesn't fuzzy-match well enough to route the 7 varied eval intents to the 5 canonical triggers → 7 `routing_miss` warnings

## Local fix attempts that didn't cleanly work

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Expand SKILL.md triggers (5 new variants close to eval phrasings) | Doctor still reports 7 routing-miss — resolver reads RESOLVER.md, not SKILL.md frontmatter |
| Replace eval intents with verbatim copies of the 5 canonical triggers | Doctor flips from `routing_miss` (7) → `routing_fixture_lint` (5) — "intent is verbatim-identical to trigger" anti-pattern |

## Suggested fix
- Re-align shipped triggers + eval to land in the "similar but not verbatim" sweet spot, OR
- Tune resolver to use embedding-based fuzzy matching, OR
- Remove the `verbatim-identical` lint check

## Repro
```bash
gbrain doctor --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.name=="resolver_health")'
```

title: sync_freshness false-positive for sources with no git remote (local-only sources warn forever)
body:
## Symptom
`gbrain doctor` reports `sync_freshness warn` for sources whose data lives in local-only paths (no git remote).

## Repro
```bash
# Source 'default' at /data/brain — no .git remote
gbrain sync --source default
# Output: "No origin remote on /data/brain; skipping git pull. Syncing from local working tree. Already up to date."

# But doctor still complains:
gbrain doctor --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.name=="sync_freshness")'
# Reports source as stale because last sync timestamp never advances
```

## Root cause
`sync_freshness` reads the `last_sync_at` timestamp from the source row. The timestamp only advances when `git pull` brings new commits. Sources with no git remote (or no new upstream commits) have stale timestamps forever, even though there's literally nothing to sync.

## Suggested fix
Distinguish "no remote, no work to do" from "stale because not synced" in `sync_freshness`. Sources without git remotes should be either:
- Exempt from the check, OR
- Flagged as "ok (local-only)" instead of warn, OR
- Have their `last_sync_at` advanced on any successful sync attempt (even no-op)

title: feat: support bracket-time format in conversation facts parser
body:
## Problem

`extract-conversation-facts` only recognizes one message format:

```
**Speaker** (2026-05-25 6:30 PM): message text
```

Conversation pages synced from Telegram use a different bracket-time format:

```
**[18:37] 👤 G T:** message text
**[18:38] 🤖 Bot:** response text
```

A production brain with 134 conversation pages typed correctly as `conversation` shows 0 eligible segments because every line fails the regex match. Doctor reports the pages as backlog, but the extractor silently skips them all.

## Solution

Add a second regex (`BRACKET_TIME_RX`) that matches the bracket-time format:

| Component | Format 1 (existing) | Format 2 (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Pattern | `**Name** (YYYY-MM-DD H:MM AM/PM): text` | `**[HH:MM] 👤 Name:** text` |
| Date source | Inline in each line | Page frontmatter `date` field |
| Time format | 12-hour with AM/PM | 24-hour |
| Speaker prefix | None | Optional emoji (stripped) |

### Changes

**`src/commands/extract-conversation-facts.ts`**
- New `BRACKET_TIME_RX` regex: `/^\*\*\[(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\]\s+(.+?):\*\*\s*(.*)$/`
- `cleanSpeaker()` helper strips leading emoji + whitespace from speaker names using Unicode property escapes
- `ParseConversationOpts.fallbackDate` parameter supplies the date for time-only lines
- `processPage()` derives `fallbackDate` from `page.frontmatter.date` (preferred) or `page.effective_date` (fallback)
- Parser tries Format 1 first, then Format 2, then treats the line as a continuation — preserving full backward compatibility

**`test/extract-conversation-facts.test.ts`**
- 6 new test cases:
  - Bracket-time with 👤 emoji speaker prefix
  - Bracket-time with 🤖 robot emoji
  - Multi-line continuation after bracket-time anchor
  - Fallback to 1970-01-01 when no `fallbackDate` provided
  - Mixed Format 1 + Format 2 in the same body
  - Bracket-time without emoji prefix

## Testing

33/33 tests pass (`bun test test/extract-conversation-facts.test.ts`). All 27 existing tests unchanged; 6 new tests added.

## Behavior Matrix

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `**Alice** (2024-03-15 9:00 AM): hi` | ✅ Parsed | ✅ Parsed (unchanged) |
| `**[18:37] 👤 G T:** hello` | ❌ Orphan line | ✅ Parsed, speaker=`G T` |
| `**[06:00] 🤖 Bot:** response` | ❌ Orphan line | ✅ Parsed, speaker=`Bot` |
| `**[22:15] Plain Name:** text` | ❌ Orphan line | ✅ Parsed, speaker=`Plain Name` |
| Continuation lines after any format | ✅ Appended | ✅ Appended (unchanged) |

title: facts:absorb logging can fail on disconnected engine handle
body:
## Bug Description

`facts:absorb` is intended to make best-effort facts/backstop failures observable via `ingest_log` reason-coded rows. In at least the page-write / CLI facts-backstop queue path, the observability path itself can fail because `writeFactsAbsorbLog()` calls `engine.logIngest()` on an engine handle that is not connected.

The user-facing page write succeeds, but instead of a durable `ingest_log` row, stderr prints a one-off warning:

```text
[facts:absorb] suppressed: 'No database connection' fires on a separate engine handle (known WARN-4 in v0.38; subsequent occurrences silent this process). First-occurrence trace for v0.38.4 diagnosis:
GBrainError: No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
    at getConnection (.../src/core/db.ts:153:15)
    at logIngest (.../src/core/postgres-engine.ts:4014:17)
    at writeFactsAbsorbLog (.../src/core/facts/absorb-log.ts:81:18)
    at <anonymous> (.../src/core/facts/backstop.ts:173:15)
    at async runEntry (.../src/core/facts/queue.ts:166:19)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed on `gbrain 0.41.11.1` during a normal page write where facts backstop was queued:

```bash
gbrain put personal/local-favorites < /tmp/gbrain-local-favorites.md \
  && gbrain get personal/local-favorites
```

The `put` response included successful durable write-through plus queued facts backstop:

```json
{
  "status": "created_or_updated",
  "facts_backstop": { "queued": true },
  "write_through": {
    "written": true,
    "path": "/home/.../brain/knowledge/personal/local-favorites.md"
  }
}
```

Then the warning above printed from the facts absorb logger.

## Expected Behavior

- The page write should continue to succeed. ✅
- If the optional facts backstop hits a failure / no-op / absorbed condition, the reason should be durably observable as an `ingest_log` row with:
  - `source_type='facts:absorb'`
  - stable reason-coded `summary` (`gateway_unavailable`, `parse_failure`, `embed_failure`, `no_candidates`, `pipeline_error`, etc.)
  - the relevant source/page/session ref
- Doctor/admin surfaces should be able to read those rows.
- No repeated noisy stderr spam.

## Actual Behavior

- The page write succeeds. ✅
- The facts backstop logger attempts to call `engine.logIngest(...)`.
- That call throws `GBrainError: No database connection: connect() has not been called` because the facts subsystem / queue path is holding a disconnected engine handle.
- The observability event is therefore not written to `ingest_log`; only the first occurrence is printed to stderr and subsequent occurrences are suppressed.

## Why this matters

This is not data loss for the canonical page write, but it defeats the purpose of facts absorb observability: failures become less inspectable by `doctor` / admin dashboards exactly when the system needs structured reason codes.

## Suspected Root Cause

`src/core/facts/backstop.ts` queue-mode error handling calls:

```ts
await writeFactsAbsorbLog(ctx.engine, parsedPage.slug, reason, msg, ctx.sourceId);
```

`src/core/facts/absorb-log.ts` then calls:

```ts
await engine.logIngest({ source_type: 'facts:absorb', ... });
```

But in this path, `ctx.engine` can be a separate/disconnected engine handle.

## Proposed Solution Shape

Preferred upstream-shaped fix:

1. Ensure the facts queue/backstop logger uses the same connected engine lifecycle as the page-write caller; or
2. Make `writeFactsAbsorbLog()` safely obtain/connect a valid engine before `logIngest`; or
3. If DB logging is impossible, write a structured fallback diagnostic that `doctor` can inspect, rather than only stderr.

Keep the existing behavior that observability failures must not break the page write.

## Regression Test Requirement

Add a test that simulates facts backstop queue logging with a disconnected engine handle and verifies:

- the page write / caller path is not failed by absorb logging;
- facts absorb observability is durably captured somehow (`ingest_log` preferred; structured fallback acceptable if DB unavailable);
- stderr does not repeatedly spam on subsequent occurrences.

## Environment

- GBrain version: `0.41.11.1`
- Engine path in trace: `postgres-engine.ts`
- CLI path: `gbrain put ...` with `facts_backstop.queued=true`

title: resolveLintContentSanity disconnects shared module-level db singleton, killing the cycle's main engine connection
RFC: Parallel Chunked Sync for Large Federated Brains
body:
## Problem

The sync pipeline becomes a reliability bottleneck at 370K+ pages with 4 federated sources. Three compounding failure modes cause sources to fall behind:

1. **Serial timeout cascade** — monolithic `sync --all` times out, killing ALL sources including ones not yet reached
2. **Lock contention** — stale locks from timed-out runs block the next cron wave
3. **Embed blocks sync** — inline embed eats into the timeout budget

**Production data (last 24h):** 8 of 12 sync cron runs timed out at 1803s. Sources going 50+ hours stale.

## Proposal (RFC only — no code changes)

Four additive flags:
- `--timeout <seconds>` — graceful self-termination, commits partial progress
- `--break-lock-if-stale <seconds>` — cron self-healing without manual `--break-lock`
- `--independent` mode — per-source process isolation (one source timing out doesn't affect others)
- Deprecate monolithic `sync --all` as the default cron path

Full RFC: [docs/rfcs/parallel-chunked-sync.md](https://github.com/garrytan-agents/gbrain/blob/feat/parallel-chunked-sync/docs/rfcs/parallel-chunked-sync.md)

## Impact

| Metric | Current | After |
|--------|---------|-------|
| Sync reliability | ~33% (4/12 runs) | ~95%+ |
| Max source staleness | 50+ hours | < 2 hours |
| Recovery from timeout | Manual intervention | Automatic |

All changes are additive — `sync --all` continues to work as-is.

title: rfc: --workers N for all bulk operations
body:
## Problem

`extract-conversation-facts` processes 6,594 conversation pages serially. At ~2 pages/min, the full backfill takes **~50 hours**. The LLM extraction is I/O-bound (waiting on API responses) — perfect for concurrency — but there's no `--workers` flag.

The workaround today is manually launching 5 separate OS processes and relying on terminal audit rows as a distributed lock. This works (confirmed 5x speedup to ~10 pages/min) but it's brittle:

- **No coordination**: all 5 enumerate the full page list independently. Two workers can claim the same page before either writes the checkpoint → duplicate LLM calls and duplicate fact rows.
- **No backpressure**: 5 processes × N segments × embedding calls can spike API rate limits with no shared rate limiter.
- **No progress reporting**: each process logs independently. No unified "X of Y pages done, $Z spent."
- **Manual lifecycle**: if one crashes, nobody notices.

## What this PR does

Adds `docs/rfc-bulk-concurrency.md` — an RFC proposing:

1. **Extract `embed`'s sliding worker pool into `src/core/worker-pool.ts`** — `embed` already solved this correctly with jittered backoff, shared budget tracking, and sliding queue. Make it reusable.

2. **Add `--workers N` to every bulk command** — default 1 (backward compatible). Priority list:
   - **P0**: `extract-conversation-facts` (50hr backfill)
   - **P1**: `dream`, `extract`
   - **P2**: `edges-backfill`, `reindex-multimodal`
   - **P3**: `reindex`, `reindex-code`, `reindex-frontmatter`

3. **Make `--background` jobs inherit `--workers`**

## Real-world numbers

From the first backfill on a 197K-page brain (6,594 conversation pages):

| Workers | Pages/min | Est. total time | Method |
|---------|-----------|----------------|--------|
| 1 | ~2 | ~50 hours | Current default |
| 5 | ~10 | ~11 hours | Manual multi-process hack |
| 10 (proj) | ~20 | ~5.5 hours | With proper worker pool |
| 20 (proj) | ~35 | ~3 hours | May need rate limit tuning |

The 5x improvement from naive multi-process confirms the bottleneck is pure I/O wait. A proper worker pool with rate-limit-aware backoff should do better than raw process spawning.

## Also noted: dimension mismatch

The facts table ships with `halfvec(1536)` but zembed-1 produces 1280-dim vectors. Had to manually `ALTER TABLE facts ALTER COLUMN embedding TYPE halfvec(1280)` before extraction could insert. The schema should read the configured `embedding_dimensions` instead of hardcoding 1536.

title: gbrain bench publish: CLI verb documented but dispatcher missing in v0.41.13.0 (Unknown command: bench)
body:
**Title:** `gbrain bench publish` CLI verb documented + implemented but dispatcher wiring missing — `Unknown command: bench` on v0.41.13.0

**Version:** v0.41.13.0 (master @ `f56cc619`)

**Symptom:**

```bash
$ gbrain --version
gbrain 0.41.13.0

$ gbrain bench publish --from /tmp/captured.ndjson --to ~/.gbrain/baselines/test.baseline.ndjson --label "test"
Unknown command: bench
Run gbrain --help for available commands.

$ gbrain bench --help
Unknown command: bench
```

**Root cause:**

1. `docs/eval-bench.md` documents the user-facing invocation as `gbrain bench publish --from ... --to ...`
2. `CHANGELOG.md` v0.41.1.0 advertises **New CLI verbs:** `gbrain bench publish --from <captured.ndjson> --to <X.baseline.ndjson> [...]`
3. `src/commands/bench-publish.ts` implements `export async function runBenchPublish(args: string[]): Promise<void>` (line 269) and is fully functional
4. But `src/cli.ts` has NO dispatcher case for `command === 'bench'`. Verified via `grep -nE "command === '(bench|bench-publish)'" src/cli.ts` → 0 hits
5. Direct `bun run src/commands/bench-publish.ts --from ... --to ...` also fails silently because the file has no `if (import.meta.main)` main entry — it only exports the function

**Impact:**

The v0.41.1 "eval-loop" is broken end-to-end. Users can `gbrain eval export` and `gbrain eval gate`, but cannot create a baseline file with the documented command — leaving the regression gate unusable without a hand-edited NDJSON.

**Reproduction:**

```bash
git checkout master  # v0.41.13.0
bun install
gbrain bench publish --help    # → Unknown command: bench
bun run src/commands/bench-publish.ts --help   # → silent exit (no main entry)
grep -nE "command === 'bench'" src/cli.ts      # → no matches
```

**Suggested fix (likely ~15 lines in cli.ts):**

Add a `case 'bench':` block to the main command switch in `cli.ts` (alongside the existing `case 'eval':` at ~line 1280-1290) that:
1. Reads the sub-subcommand from `args[0]`
2. If `args[0] === 'publish'`: dynamic-imports `./commands/bench-publish.ts` and calls `runBenchPublish(args.slice(1))`
3. Otherwise: prints `Usage: gbrain bench publish ...` help

Optionally also add `if (import.meta.main) { runBenchPublish(process.argv.slice(2)) }` to `bench-publish.ts` so direct `bun run` works as a fallback.

**Workaround:** I wrote a shim at `scripts/run-bench-publish.ts` that imports `runBenchPublish` and invokes it with argv. Happy to PR the cli.ts fix if useful — would be a near-mechanical mirror of the existing `case 'eval':` pattern.

(Filed via gbrain upgrade audit by Mr-B-1 — sibling issues #1452-1455 from the same audit.)

title: fix(dream): propagate --source flag to runCycle (closes #1452)
body:
## Problem

`gbrain doctor` reports per-source `cycle_freshness` warnings and recommends the fix:

```
[WARN] cycle_freshness: Source 'foo' has never completed a full cycle
       (no entry in source.config->>'last_full_cycle_at').

  ACTION: Run 'gbrain dream --source <id> --dir <brain>' for each stale source
```

But following the recommendation has no effect. The warning never clears even after a full successful dream completes (32 minutes, 2478 chunks embedded, status=partial, exit 0).

`SELECT id, config->>'last_full_cycle_at' FROM sources` still returns NULL for the source.

## Root cause

Verified by reading master @ v0.41.14.0 (`32f8be96`):

`src/commands/dream.ts:36-57` `DreamArgs` interface had no `source` field:

```typescript
interface DreamArgs {
  json: boolean;
  dryRun: boolean;
  pull: boolean;
  phase: CyclePhase | null;
  dir: string | null;
  // ... no 'source' field
}
```

`src/commands/dream.ts:281-291` `runCycle` call missing `sourceId` propagation:

```typescript
const report = await runCycle(engine, {
  brainDir,
  dryRun: opts.dryRun,
  pull: opts.pull,
  phases,
  synthInputFile: opts.inputFile ?? undefined,
  // <-- no sourceId here
  // ...
});
```

`src/core/cycle.ts:1738` gates the marker write on `opts.sourceId` being truthy:

```typescript
if (opts.sourceId && engine && !dryRun &&
    (status === 'ok' || status === 'clean' || status === 'partial')) {
  await engine.updateSourceConfig(opts.sourceId, {
    last_full_cycle_at: new Date().toISOString(),
  });
}
```

With `opts.sourceId === undefined`, the gate silently skips. No warning. No write. No marker. So the warning loops forever.

`gbrain sync` accepts `--source` correctly; `gbrain dream` is the odd one out. Likely missed during the v0.38+ per-source cycle-tracking refactor.

## Fix

Four surgical edits to `src/commands/dream.ts`, all mirroring existing patterns:

1. Add `source: string | null` to `DreamArgs` interface (mirrors `dir: string | null`)
2. Parse `--source <value>` in `parseArgs` (mirrors `--dir` parsing)
3. Include `source` in the returned `DreamArgs` object
4. Pass `sourceId: opts.source ?? undefined` to `runCycle()`

13 lines added.

## Verification

Applied locally + tested on v0.41.14.0:

```bash
$ bun src/cli.ts dream --source foo --dry-run
No brain directory found. Pass --dir <path> or configure one via 'gbrain init'.
```

Pre-fix the same command would silently accept --source as garbage argv (`args.includes('--source')` returns true, `args.indexOf('--source')` would return a positive index but `parseArgs` never read it).

Post-fix:
- `--source` is parsed into `opts.source`
- threads through the returned DreamArgs
- reaches `runCycle({sourceId: opts.source ?? undefined, ...})`
- which threads to `cycle.ts:1738`'s gate
- which writes `source.config->>'last_full_cycle_at'`
- which clears the doctor warning

Closes #1452.

(Filed by Mr-B-1 — same v0.40.8 → v0.41.14 upgrade audit that produced sibling PR #1476 and issues #1452-1455, #1474, #1475.)

title: design: type proliferation — 94 types should be ~14 (DRY/MECE unification proposal)
body:
## Problem

A production brain with 186K pages has organically accumulated **94 distinct page types**. Most are duplicates, near-duplicates, or one-off types that should be subtypes via frontmatter fields. This violates DRY (same concept under multiple types) and MECE (types overlap, creating ambiguity about where new content goes).

The type system is the foundation for schema packs, search filtering, extract behavior, enrichment routing, and `expert_routing`. When types are noisy, every downstream feature degrades.

## Production Data

### Cluster 1: Social posts — 7 types, 106K pages

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| tweet | 33,409 |
| tweet-bundle | 42,498 |
| media/x-tweet/bundle | 9,246 |
| tweet-stub | 1,625 |
| media/x-account/daily | 19,631 |
| media/x-account/monthly | 67 |
| media/x-account | 15 |

**Should be:** `tweet` with `subtype: single|bundle|stub` + `social-digest` with `period: daily|monthly`. 7 → 2.

### Cluster 2: Articles — 5 types, 3.6K pages

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| article | 1,418 |
| media/article | 1,518 |
| sources/article | 635 |
| source/article | 40 |
| source | 24 |

**Should be:** ONE type `article`. 5 → 1.

### Cluster 3: Companies — 4 types, 13.5K pages

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| company | 5,210 |
| yc-company | 5,721 |
| product | 2,629 |
| organization | 2 |

"Accelerator membership" should be a field (`batch: S23`), not a separate type. **Should be:** `company` with `kind: company|product|org`. 4 → 1.

### Cluster 4: Atoms — 6 types, 18K pages

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| atom | 13,634 |
| atom-extraction | 395 |
| content-atom | 8 |
| atom-partner-link | 8 |
| partner-atom-link | 6 |
| lore | 4,088 |

`atom-partner-link` and `partner-atom-link` should be LINKS, not page types. **Should be:** `atom` with `origin: extraction|manual|lore`. 6 → 1.

### Cluster 5: Media/Content — 8 types, 8.7K pages

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| media | 7,510 |
| video | 618 |
| youtube-video | 130 |
| writing | 251 |
| essay | 159 |
| blog-post | 27 |
| book | 8 |
| podcast | 1 |

Content format is a frontmatter field, not a type. **Should be:** `media` with `format: video|article|essay|book|podcast`. 8 → 1.

### Cluster 6: Analysis — 8 types, 40 pages(!)

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| analysis | 9 |
| media/analysis | 2 |
| media-analysis | 1 |
| media/x-account/analysis | 1 |
| research | 8 |
| organization-research | 1 |
| competitive-intel | 1 |
| yc/competitive-intel | 17 |

8 types for 40 pages is the clearest sign of ad-hoc proliferation. **Should be:** `analysis` with `domain` field. 8 → 1.

### Cluster 7: Concept redirects outnumber concepts

- concept: 4,304
- concept-redirect: 5,519

More redirect pages than real pages. Redirects should be an **alias table**, not 5.5K stub pages that inflate orphan counts and waste embedding tokens.

### Cluster 8: One-off types — 25+ types with 1-2 pages each

civic, framework, insight, anecdote, principle, memo, rfs-draft, pitch-deck, policy-criticism, production-doc, recording-snippet, registry, reference, schema, video-script, web_page, log, agent-log, content-mining, meta-prompt, queue, eval-test...

**Should be:** tags or subtypes of `note`.

### Cluster 9: Symlinks as pages — 54 pages

symlink, partner-symlink, symlink-manifest — filesystem operations stored as brain pages.

## Why This Matters

1. **Schema packs can't be MECE** — the pack declares types but the brain has 94, many undeclared. `schema_review_orphans` can't distinguish intentional from noise.
2. **Search filtering is ambiguous** — `--type article` misses 2.2K articles typed as `media/article`, `sources/article`, etc.
3. **Enrichment routing is incomplete** — `enrichable_types` can only list a few. 80+ types means most pages never get enriched.
4. **Agent confusion** — when ingesting a new article, should it be `article`, `media/article`, `sources/article`, or `source/article`?
5. **Orphan inflation** — concept-redirect pages (5.5K) inflate orphan count without adding knowledge value.

## Proposed Target Taxonomy

| Type | Covers | Current types merged |
|---|---|---|
| `person` | People | person, partner, partner-profile |
| `company` | Companies, orgs, products | company, yc-company, product, organization |
| `concept` | Ideas | concept (redirects → alias table) |
| `atom` | Knowledge units | atom, atom-extraction, content-atom, lore |
| `tweet` | Social posts | tweet, tweet-bundle, tweet-stub, media/x-tweet/bundle |
| `social-digest` | Social summaries | media/x-account/* |
| `article` | Web content | article, media/article, sources/article, source/* |
| `media` | Rich content | media, video, youtube-video, book, podcast |
| `writing` | Original writing | writing, essay, blog-post |
| `meeting` | Temporal discussions | meeting, call, interview |
| `analysis` | Research + intel | analysis, research, competitive-intel, all variants |
| `event` | Events | event, convention |
| `deal` | Deals | deal |
| `note` | Everything else | note, memo, insight, principle, framework, all one-offs |

**94 types → 14 types.** Distinctions move to frontmatter fields (`subtype`, `format`, `origin`, `period`, `domain`).

## Migration Path

1. Schema pack declares the 14 canonical types with `aliases` covering the old names
2. Migration script retypes pages (e.g., `media/article` → `article` with `source_collection: media`)
3. concept-redirect pages → alias table entries + soft-delete
4. symlink/atom-partner-link pages → proper link table entries + soft-delete
5. One-off types → retype to `note` with original type preserved as `legacy_type` tag

## Impact on Existing Features

- `inferType` path prefix mapping shrinks dramatically
- Schema pack `page_types` goes from 30+ to 14 entries
- `enrichable_types` covers more of the brain naturally
- `extract` type filters work correctly across the whole corpus
- `find_experts` expert_routing covers all entity types cleanly
- `schema_review_orphans` becomes meaningful (currently noisy)
- Agent ingestion becomes unambiguous (one type per domain)

## Related

- #1383 (gbrain onboard — migration prompts would drive this)
- #1409 (consolidated design doc)
