title: feat: gbrain skillopt — SkillOpt-style self-evolving agent skills
body:
## Summary

Proposal to add `gbrain skillopt` — a validation-gated, bounded text-space optimizer for agent skill documents. Based on [SkillOpt](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904) (Microsoft Research, May 2026), which treats the skill doc as trainable external state of a frozen agent with deep-learning-style controls.

SkillOpt is best or tied on all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells. It adds +23.5 points over no-skill on GPT-5.5, beats human-written skills, TextGrad, GEPA, EvoSkill, and Trace2Skill, and the learned skills transfer across models and harnesses.

gbrain already has: 47 bundled skills (SKILL.md), routing-eval fixtures, `gbrain eval --qrels`, `gbrain dream`, and `gbrain skillify`. What's missing is closing the loop — skills don't evolve from execution feedback.

---

## The Problem

### User needs
- Skills are hand-written and static. Once shipped, they only improve when a human rewrites them.
- Human-written skills plateau because humans can't process 40+ execution trajectories to find which rules help and which hurt.
- Agents using skills accumulate failure patterns that the skill never adapts to.
- Different target models (GPT-5.5, Claude, Gemini) need different skill formulations, but currently every model gets the same SKILL.md.

### Agent needs
- Skills should improve from production feedback without human intervention.
- The improvement loop must be safe — never ship a skill that's worse than what it replaced.
- Skills must remain inspectable (markdown, not opaque weights).
- Optimization cost must be bounded and amortizable (train once, deploy everywhere).
- The skill format shouldn't change — existing SKILL.md files should be valid inputs.

---

## Prior Art Landscape

| System | What it optimizes | Feedback | Controls | Skills transfer? |
|--------|------------------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| APE (2022) | Prompts | Generate + select | None | No |
| OPRO (2023) | Prompts | Meta-prompt with scores | None | No |
| DSPy (2023+) | Pipeline parameters | Module-level metrics | Compilation-time | No |
| TextGrad (Nature 2025) | Any text variable | Textual gradients | PyTorch-like API | No |
| GEPA (2025) | Prompts + code | Execution traces + Pareto | Genetic selection | Partial |
| EvoSkill (Apr 2026) | Agent skills | Co-evolutionary verification | Mutation + selection | Cross-model |
| Trace2Skill (Mar 2026) | Skills from trajectories | Parallel fleet analysis | Hierarchical patches | Cross-model |
| **SkillOpt (May 2026)** | **Agent skill docs** | **Scored rollouts** | **LR, validation gate, rejected-edit buffer, slow/meta update** | **Cross-model, cross-harness, cross-benchmark** |

SkillOpt's key insight: apply the same discipline that makes weight-space optimization reproducible — learning rate, validation gating, negative feedback memory — to text-space optimization.

### Implementations reviewed
- [microsoft/SkillOpt](https://github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt) — official, Python, full pipeline
- [zou-group/textgrad](https://github.com/zou-group/textgrad) — Nature-published text optimization
- [stanfordnlp/dspy](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy) — programmatic prompt compilation
- [google-deepmind/opro](https://github.com/google-deepmind/opro) — LLM-as-optimizer
- [gepa-ai/gepa](https://github.com/gepa-ai/gepa) — genetic-pareto with traces
- [sentient-agi/EvoSkill](https://github.com/sentient-agi/EvoSkill) — co-evolutionary skill discovery
- [AMAP-ML/SkillClaw](https://github.com/AMAP-ML/SkillClaw) — skill evolution from sessions
- [NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution) — DSPy + GEPA

---

## The SkillOpt Algorithm

```
Input: initial skill s₀, target model M, harness h,
       D_train, D_sel, D_test, num_epochs, batch_size,
       learning rate schedule L_t

s_best = s₀
best_score = eval(s₀, D_sel)
rejected_buffer = []

for epoch in 1..num_epochs:
    for step in 1..steps_per_epoch:
        # 1. FORWARD PASS: rollout batch
        trajectories = [h(M, x, s_current) for x in sample(D_train)]
        
        # 2. BACKWARD PASS: minibatch reflection
        fail_edits = reflect(failures, s_current, rejected_buffer)
        succ_edits = reflect(successes, s_current, rejected_buffer)
        
        # 3. BOUNDED UPDATE: apply under learning rate
        edits = rank_and_clip(merge(fail_edits, succ_edits), L_t)
        s_candidate = apply_edits(s_current, edits)
        
        # 4. VALIDATION GATE: accept only if improved
        if eval(s_candidate, D_sel) > best_score:
            s_current = s_candidate
            best_score = eval(s_candidate, D_sel)
        else:
            rejected_buffer.append(edits)
    
    # 5. EPOCH-WISE SLOW UPDATE
    s_current = apply_slow_update(s_current, compare_epochs(...))

export(s_best)  # 300-2000 token skill document
```

### The Deep Learning Analogy (Operational, Not Decorative)

| DL Concept | SkillOpt Analog |
|------------|-----------------|
| Parameters | Skill document (natural language) |
| Forward pass | Rollout batch (execute tasks with current skill) |
| Backward pass | Minibatch reflection (analyze trajectories) |
| Gradient | Proposed add/delete/replace edits |
| Learning rate | Edit budget L_t (max edits per step) |
| LR schedule | Cosine/linear/constant decay |
| Validation set | D_sel (held-out gate) |
| Momentum | Epoch-wise slow update |
| Negative examples | Rejected-edit buffer |
| Checkpointing | best_skill.md |

### Ablation Results (what matters)

| Component removed | Effect |
|-------------------|--------|
| Learning rate (bounded edits) | Unbounded rewriting erases useful rules |
| Validation gate | Harmful proposals accumulate |
| Rejected-edit buffer | Optimizer repeats failed edits |
| Slow/meta update | Long-horizon patterns lost |
| Cosine schedule | Slight degradation vs cosine |

---

## Proposed Architecture: `gbrain skillopt`

### CLI Interface

```bash
gbrain skillopt <skill-name> \
  --benchmark <path>          # Task set with expected outcomes
  --epochs 4                  # Training epochs (default: 4)
  --batch-size 40             # Rollout batch per step (default: 40)
  --lr 4                      # Max edits per step (default: 4)
  --lr-schedule cosine        # Edit budget schedule (default: cosine)
  --optimizer-model opus      # Optimizer model (default: models.think fallback)
  --target-model default      # Target model executing the skill
  --split 4:1:5               # train:validation:test ratio
  --patch                     # Patch mode (default) vs --rewrite
  --dry-run                   # Preview optimization plan without executing
  --json                      # Machine-readable output
```

### Benchmark Format

Extend the existing `routing-eval.jsonl` with execution expectations:

```jsonl
{"task": "Research company Acme Corp for an investor meeting", "skill": "meeting-prep", "expected_elements": ["company_profile", "key_people", "recent_news"], "judge": "llm"}
{"task": "Draft a tweet about network effects", "skill": "tweet-composition", "expected_elements": ["claim", "evidence", "under_280_chars"], "judge": "rule"}
{"task": "Check if claim X is supported by the brain", "skill": "fact-check", "expected_elements": ["verdict", "citations", "confidence"], "judge": "llm"}
```

### Scoring Functions

Three built-in scoring modes:

1. **Rule-based** (`judge: rule`): Check for expected structural elements (has citations? under length limit? includes required sections?)
2. **LLM-as-judge** (`judge: llm`): Optimizer model scores execution quality 0-1 against the expected outcome
3. **Qrels** (`judge: qrels`): Existing `gbrain eval` retrieval metrics for search/retrieval skills

### Edit Operations

```yaml
# Example edit proposal from optimizer
edits:
  - op: add
    location: "## Error Handling"
    content: "When gbrain think returns no citations, fall back to gbrain search with broader keywords before reporting 'not found'."
  - op: replace
    target: "Always use gbrain search for lookups"
    replacement: "Use gbrain think for multi-page synthesis. Fall back to gbrain search only for simple keyword lookups."
  - op: delete
    target: "Include a disclaimer about AI-generated content"
    reason: "This rule consistently causes output to include unnecessary boilerplate that lowers quality scores."
```

### Output Artifacts

```
skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md               ← updated best skill (or unchanged if no improvement)
├── skillopt/
│   ├── history.json        ← full optimization trace
│   ├── rejected.json       ← rejected-edit buffer (negative feedback)
│   ├── versions/
│   │   ├── v0000_initial.md
│   │   ├── v0001_step1.md
│   │   └── v0042_best.md
│   └── report.md           ← human-readable optimization report
```

### Integration with Existing Commands

| Command | Current | With SkillOpt |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| `gbrain skillify` | Creates new skills | Creates → then `skillopt` optimizes them |
| `gbrain eval` | Retrieval quality | Extended: skill execution quality |
| `gbrain dream` | Overnight maintenance | Optional `--phase skillopt` for skill optimization |
| `gbrain check-resolvable` | Routing health | Also reports skills with low eval scores |
| `gbrain doctor` | Brain health | Reports skill optimization status |

### Dream Cycle Integration

```
gbrain dream --phase skillopt
```

The dream cycle already runs overnight. Adding a `skillopt` phase:
1. For each skill with a benchmark file and an eval score below threshold
2. Run one epoch of SkillOpt (bounded by time/cost budget)
3. If improvement found, update SKILL.md and commit
4. Report in the CycleReport

This means skills improve every night, automatically, with the same validation discipline as the rest of the dream cycle.

---

## Failure Modes & Gotchas

### From the paper
1. **Optimizer model quality matters:** Needs frontier model for reflection. Weak optimizers produce worse skills.
2. **Training cost:** Each step = rollout batch + validation eval. At batch_size=40, this is significant. Budget controls are essential.
3. **Local optima:** Validation gating prevents regression but can't guarantee global optimum.
4. **Small training sets:** < 20% of data significantly degrades performance.
5. **Rewrite mode instability:** Full rewrites can erase useful rules. Patch mode is safer for incremental refinement.

### gbrain-specific
6. **Skills are router-triggered, not batch-executed.** SkillOpt assumes batch execution. gbrain needs an adapter that executes a skill on a task and captures the trajectory.
7. **No scalar scoring today.** `routing-eval.jsonl` tests routing accuracy, not execution quality. Need execution-level scoring (the benchmark format above).
8. **Multi-skill routing.** Optimizing one skill could affect routing for others. Need isolation: optimize one skill's execution quality while holding routing fixed.
9. **Skill size constraints.** SkillOpt outputs 300-2000 tokens. gbrain SKILL.md files are often 2000-5000 tokens. May need to separate the "trained" section from static reference material.
10. **Cold start for new skills.** `gbrain skillify` creates an initial skill. SkillOpt needs a benchmark to optimize against — who creates the benchmark?

### Mitigations
- **Cost control:** `--max-cost` flag, per-step cost tracking, dream phase has a time budget
- **Safety:** Validation gating is mandatory (not optional). Rejected-edit buffer prevents regression loops.
- **Routing isolation:** SkillOpt only modifies the skill's execution behavior, not its routing triggers.
- **Benchmark bootstrapping:** For skills with `routing-eval.jsonl`, auto-generate an execution benchmark from the routing fixtures. For new skills, require a benchmark file.

---

## Use Cases

### 1. Overnight skill improvement
A brain with 47 skills runs `gbrain dream --phase skillopt`. Each skill with a benchmark gets one epoch of optimization. Over a week, skills that had 60% execution quality reach 85%+.

### 2. New skill onboarding
User runs `gbrain skillify "meeting prep"` to create a skill. Then `gbrain skillopt meeting-prep --benchmark meeting-prep-tasks.jsonl` to optimize it against real tasks. The skill goes from generic to domain-adapted in 4 epochs.

### 3. Model migration
User switches from GPT-5.4 to Claude 4.5. Runs `gbrain skillopt --all --target-model claude-4.5` to re-optimize all skills for the new model. Skills transfer but may need fine-tuning for model-specific patterns.

### 4. Skill debugging
A skill is underperforming. `gbrain skillopt <skill> --dry-run` analyzes the benchmark and reports: "This skill fails on tasks involving multi-page synthesis because it uses `gbrain search` instead of `gbrain think`." The optimization trace shows exactly which rules cause failures.

---

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Foundation (MVP)
- `gbrain skillopt` command with benchmark input
- Patch-mode edits with validation gating
- LLM-as-judge scoring
- Rejected-edit buffer
- Cosine LR schedule
- Output: updated SKILL.md + history.json

### Phase 2: Dream Integration
- `gbrain dream --phase skillopt`
- Auto-discovery of skills with benchmarks
- Per-skill time/cost budgets
- Reporting in CycleReport

### Phase 3: Ecosystem
- Auto-generate benchmarks from routing-eval.jsonl
- Cross-model optimization (optimize once, deploy to multiple models)
- Skill quality dashboard in admin UI
- Meta-skill (optimizer-side bookkeeping for long-horizon patterns)

---

## References

- [SkillOpt paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904) — Yang et al., Microsoft Research, May 2026
- [microsoft/SkillOpt](https://github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt) — official implementation
- [TextGrad](https://github.com/zou-group/textgrad) — Nature 2025, textual gradient descent
- [DSPy](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy) — programmatic prompt optimization
- [OPRO](https://github.com/google-deepmind/opro) — LLM-as-optimizer
- [GEPA](https://github.com/gepa-ai/gepa) — genetic-pareto execution trace analysis
- [EvoSkill](https://github.com/sentient-agi/EvoSkill) — co-evolutionary skill discovery
- [SkillsBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06056) — benchmark for agent skills
- [SoK: Agentic Skills](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20867) — skill lifecycle taxonomy

title: feat(sync): .gbrainignore + multi-layer per-repo exclusion (v0.40.9.0)
body:
## Summary

Stop indexing files you didn't want indexed. Three additive layers gate every sync walker and incremental diff:

1. **`.gbrainignore`** at the repo root — committed, travels with the repo
2. **`sources.config.excludePatterns`** — persistent per-source (JSONB)
3. **`--exclude <glob>`** CLI flag — one-shot override

Full gitignore parity via the [`ignore`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ignore) npm lib (same parser ESLint, Prettier, and Husky use). Merge order: `dotfile → source.config → cli`, last wins per gitignore's last-match-wins semantics.

## Why

The user dropped this in plain English: "now when using /sync-gbrain in some project, it syncs every file in the project directory into the brain. Some data file directories shouldn't enter gbrain." Before this PR there was no `.gbrainignore`, no `--exclude` flag, no per-source ignore config in `sources.config`, and `.gitignore` was not consulted. A project with `data/`, `datasets/`, `*.parquet`, `fixtures/`, `models/` got all of it indexed. The only escape hatches were renaming the data dir to start with a dot, moving it under `*.raw/`, or `--no-code`.

## What's new at a glance

```bash
# Drop in any project root:
echo "data/
fixtures/large/
*.parquet" > .gbrainignore

# Next /sync-gbrain or `gbrain sync --source <id>` honors it.
# Existing orphan pages get reaped on next sync (safety-guarded).

# CLI escape hatch for one-offs:
gbrain sync --source <id> --exclude '!data/keep.md'

# Persistent per-source (survives autopilot cycles):
gbrain sources add my-repo --path /path --exclude 'data/' --exclude '*.parquet'
gbrain sources update my-repo --exclude 'fixtures/' --clear-excludes

# Surfaced in:
gbrain doctor                # new gbrainignore_health check
```

## Architecture decisions (locked in `/plan-eng-review`)

| Tag | Decision |
|-----|----------|
| Step 0 | Hold scope — all three layers ship in one wave |
| **A1** | Thread `cfg.excludePatterns` + `cfg.strategy` through `cycle.runPhaseSync` (closes daemon gap) |
| **A2** | Auto-reconcile pages on pattern-hash change; 50%/1000 safety guard refuses runaway deletions |
| **A3** | Negation-aware descent-prune fallback (walker walks dirs when any `!` pattern present) |
| **A4** | Merge order: cli > source.config > .gbrainignore (gitignore-style last-match-wins) |
| **C1** | Single `resolveExclusions()` helper consumed by 4 call sites (DRY) |
| **C2** | mtime-based cache invalidation (autopilot daemon picks up dotfile edits within one cycle) |
| **P1** | Reconciliation streams 1000 rows per query (memory-bounded on 200k-page brains) |

## Failure modes pinned by IRON-RULE tests

The /plan-eng-review IRON RULE captures regressions where silent bugs cost real data. All four are pinned in `test/sync-exclude.test.ts`:

1. **Negation-aware descent-prune fallback** — `data/* + !data/keep.md` correctly emits `keep.md`. Without the `safeForDescentPrune` flag, walker would short-circuit on the parent dir and silently lose the rescue.
2. **50%-deletion safety guard** — refuses to delete >50% of a source's pages without `--reconcile-excludes --yes`. The class of bug this catches: a user typos `**` in `.gbrainignore`, walker excludes everything, reconciliation would otherwise wipe the source.
3. **1000-row absolute guard** — same posture for huge brains where percentage looks small.
4. **1000-row batched reconciliation** — crosses BATCH_SIZE boundary cleanly on a 1100-row seeded fixture. Memory stays bounded.

## File-by-file change list

```
PRODUCTION (8 files)
  src/core/gbrainignore.ts          NEW   load + resolveExclusions + mtime cache (~280 LOC)
  src/core/cycle.ts                 MOD   A1 — thread cfg.excludePatterns + cfg.strategy
  src/commands/import.ts            MOD   walker descent-prune guarded by safeForDescentPrune (A3)
  src/commands/sync.ts              MOD   4 call sites + reconciliation + 1000-row batching
  src/commands/sources.ts           MOD   sources add --exclude, new sources update subcommand
  src/core/sources-ops.ts           MOD   AddSourceOpts.excludePatterns, updateSource()
  src/commands/doctor.ts            MOD   gbrainignore_health check
  (no src/core/sync.ts pruneDir extension — descent-prune is path-aware, lives in walker)

TESTS (4 files, 47 new cases — 150 total green after this PR)
  test/gbrainignore.test.ts         NEW   22 cases (module + cache + mtime)
  test/sync-exclude.test.ts         NEW   15 cases incl. 4 REGRESSION-CRITICAL
  test/sources-exclude.test.ts      NEW   10 cases (CLI + opsUpdate semantics)
  test/doctor-behavioral.test.ts    MOD   +3 cases (gbrainignore_health)

DOCS/META (3 files)
  docs/guides/sync-filtering.md     MOD   new "User-configurable exclusion" section
  CHANGELOG.md                      MOD   v0.40.9.0 wave entry
  package.json + VERSION            MOD   ignore@^7.0.5, bump to 0.40.9.0

DEP
  ignore@^7.0.5                     NEW   MIT, ~17KB packed, zero transitive
```

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- `bun test test/gbrainignore.test.ts test/sync-exclude.test.ts test/sources-exclude.test.ts test/doctor-behavioral.test.ts test/sync-strategy.test.ts test/sync.test.ts test/sync-walker-*.test.ts` — **150 pass / 0 fail / 503 expect()**
- `bun run verify` — clean (privacy, source-id, jsonb, ops-filter-bypass, all 13 guards)

## Honest notes

- Planned `pruneDir(name, parentDir?, dirExcludes?)` extension at `src/core/sync.ts` cancelled during implementation. `pruneDir` operates on single segment names; descent-prune is path-aware so the right home is the walker in `src/commands/import.ts`. Documented in commit message.
- `sources.config` JSONB reads use untyped casts matching the existing `cfg.strategy` pattern. A zod schema for the whole shape is a deferred follow-up — not load-bearing because writers (`sources add` / `sources update`) are typed at entry.
- Autopilot daemon's `runPhaseSync` doesn't accept its own `--exclude` flag for ad-hoc fan-out. The daemon reads `cfg.excludePatterns` per source from the DB. A user wanting a one-off daemon-side exclusion would `sources update --exclude` first. Daemon-side CLI plumbing is a follow-up if anyone hits the use case.

## Gitignore semantics gotcha (documented)

Once a directory is excluded via `data/`, children **cannot** be re-included with `!data/keep.md` — this is documented gitignore behavior, not a gbrain quirk. The rescue pattern requires excluding contents instead: `data/* + !data/keep.md`. Called out in `docs/guides/sync-filtering.md` so users hit it once and never again.

title: fix(salience): exclude soft-deleted pages from getRecentSalience
body:
## What

`getRecentSalience()` returns rows where `deleted_at IS NOT NULL` because the `WHERE` clause only filters by `updated_at + salience_touched_at + slug prefix`.

## Reproduce

```bash
gbrain capture "test page content" --slug reports/test-salience-bug
gbrain delete reports/test-salience-bug
gbrain salience --days 90 --limit 10
```

The deleted page still appears in the salience ranking even though it's been soft-deleted.

## Why this matters

The 72-hour recovery window means a deleted page can keep appearing in `salience` output for three days, where the user is actively trying to identify "what's been meaningful lately" (the documented purpose of the command). Soft-deleted pages should not weight an active-state ranking — that's effectively the contract every other read path is already enforcing.

## Fix

Add `p.deleted_at IS NULL` to the `WHERE` clause in both `PostgresEngine.getRecentSalience()` and `PGLiteEngine.getRecentSalience()`.

This matches the existing pattern in 19 other query call sites in `postgres-engine.ts` (e.g. `getPage`, `listPages`, `searchKeyword`, `findOrphans`, `traverseGraph` — all already gate on `deleted_at IS NULL`).

## Verification

After patch on a brain with one soft-deleted page in the window:

Before:
```
1   0.989   ...   技能库/hermes-gbrain-诊断与修复经验
2   0.987   ...   技能库/第二大脑设计原则与决策
3   0.964   ...   概念/gbrain-vault-index
4   0.928   ...   reports/2026-05-26-hermes-gbrain-maintenance-pm  ← soft-deleted
5   0.924   ...   技术文档/创业者手册构建-ai-原生创业公司
```

After:
```
1   0.975   ...   技能库/hermes-gbrain-诊断与修复经验
2   0.973   ...   技能库/第二大脑设计原则与决策
3   0.951   ...   概念/gbrain-vault-index
4   0.912   ...   技术文档/创业者手册构建-ai-原生创业公司    ← shifted up
```

## Notes

- No new option exposed; this is a defense-in-depth fix matching the rest of the codebase.
- If a future caller wants to surface deleted pages (parallel to `list_pages --include-deleted`), a separate `include_deleted` flag could be added — but that's out of scope here.
- I considered also touching `findAnomalies` (right below in the same file) but its query semantics differ (counting page activity per cohort rather than ranking pages), so leaving as a follow-up if anyone confirms the desired behavior there.

## Environment where caught

- gbrain `0.41.14.0`
- Postgres engine, vault size ~1400 pages.

title: Windows: bun install fails due to Unix shell redirect syntax in postinstall script
body:
**What happened?**

在 Windows 上执行 `bun install` 时，postinstall 脚本因使用了 Unix shell 重定向语法（`1>&2`、`>/dev/null`、`command -v`）导致 Bun 的内置脚本解析器解析失败，安装报错退出。

**What did you expect?**

`bun install` 应正常完成安装，postinstall 脚本在检测到环境不满足条件时应优雅跳过，而非报错退出。

**Steps to reproduce**
1. 在 Windows 11 环境下 `git clone` gbrain 仓库
2. 执行 `bun install`
3. 观察终端输出：postinstall 阶段报错，`exit code 1`

**Environment**
- gbrain version: 0.41.14.0
- OS: Windows 11 Home China 10.0.26200
- Bun version: 1.3.14
- Database: N/A（`bun install` 阶段，尚未配置数据库）

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**
```
N/A — 安装未完成，gbrain 二进制尚未可用
```

**Additional context**

失败行位于 `package.json` 的 postinstall 脚本：

```json
"postinstall": "command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 && gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive || echo '...' 1>&2"
```

三个不兼容 Windows 的语法点：

- `command -v` — POSIX shell 命令，Bun 在 Windows 上的内置解析器不支持
- `>/dev/null 2>&1` — `/dev/null` 在 Windows 上不存在，`2>&1` 被 Bun 解析器拒绝
- `1>&2` — 触发错误 `expected a command or assignment but got: "Redirect"`

临时修复：将 postinstall 替换为 `node -e "try{...}catch(e){...}"` 跨平台写法后，`bun install` 可正常完成。

title: gateway.chat(): incorrect tool schema format breaks non-Anthropic providers (agent.use_gateway_loop)
body:
## Bug description

When `agent.use_gateway_loop=true` and the subagent model is a non-Anthropic
provider (e.g. DeepSeek, OpenRouter, any OpenAI-compatible recipe), the gateway
tool loop fails with:

```
[chat(deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash)] schema is not a function. 
(In 'schema()', 'schema' is an instance of Object)
```

## Root cause

In `src/core/ai/gateway.ts`, the `chat()` function passes tool schemas as raw
JSON Schema objects under the `inputSchema` key to the AI SDK's `generateText()`:

```typescript
// gateway.ts ~line 2360
const tools = (opts.tools ?? []).reduce((acc, t) => {
    acc[t.name] = {
      description: t.description,
      inputSchema: { jsonSchema: t.inputSchema } as any,
    };
    return acc;
  }, {} as Record<string, any>);
```

The Vercel AI SDK expects tools to use the `parameters` key with a
`jsonSchema()`-wrapped value (the `jsonSchema` helper from the `ai` package).
The `inputSchema` key is silently ignored for openai-compatible providers.

When the SDK resolves tool definitions, it attempts to call `.schema()` on
whatever lands under `parameters` — which is `undefined` since that key is
never set. This falls through to the `inputSchema` value (a plain Object),
and the `.schema()` call fails.

## Scope of impact

This bug affects **all non-Anthropic providers** using the gateway tool loop
path (`agent.use_gateway_loop=true`). The default Anthropic-direct subagent
path is unaffected because it bypasses `gateway.chat()` entirely.

**Affected versions:** all releases that include `agent.use_gateway_loop`
support — introduced in the v0.38 series and present through current HEAD
(v0.41.14.0).

## Reproduction

Prerequisites: a configured non-Anthropic chat model with API key set.

```bash
gbrain config set agent.use_gateway_loop true
# Create a transcript file >2000 chars
gbrain dream --phase synthesize --input <transcript>
```

Result: the significance judge phase completes, but the subagent job dies
with `schema is not a function`.

## Fix

Import `jsonSchema` from the `ai` package and use the correct `parameters`
key with `jsonSchema()` wrapping:

```diff
-import { embed as aiEmbed, embedMany, generateObject, generateText } from 'ai';
+import { embed as aiEmbed, embedMany, generateObject, generateText, jsonSchema } from 'ai';

-      inputSchema: { jsonSchema: t.inputSchema } as any,
+      parameters: jsonSchema(t.inputSchema),
```

## Additional context

Discovered while running a Hermes multi-agent cluster with DeepSeek as the
primary LLM. A fix branch is available at
`justemu/gbrain:fix/gateway-tool-json-schema` for reference.

title: fix: use jsonSchema() wrapper and 'parameters' key for AI SDK tool definitions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1487 - the gateway chat() function passes tool schemas in a format incompatible with the Vercel AI SDK for non-Anthropic providers.

## Problem

When agent.use_gateway_loop=true, the subagent handler routes through gateway.toolLoop(), which calls gateway.chat(). The chat() function passes tool schemas as { inputSchema: { jsonSchema: rawObject } } to generateText(). The AI SDK expects { parameters: jsonSchema(rawObject) } where jsonSchema is imported from the ai package.

This causes all non-Anthropic subagent tool loops to fail with: [chat(deepseek:...)] schema is not a function

## Changes

2 lines changed in src/core/ai/gateway.ts. Import jsonSchema from ai, and use parameters: jsonSchema(t.inputSchema) instead of inputSchema: { jsonSchema: t.inputSchema }.

## Testing

Tested with DeepSeek v4 Flash as the subagent model. The Anthropic-direct path is unaffected.

## Affected versions

All releases with agent.use_gateway_loop support (v0.38+ through current HEAD).

title: fix(sync): refresh source freshness on no-op sync
body:
## Summary

- Refresh source `last_sync_at` when a sync exits via the `up_to_date` path.
- Preserve the existing global `sync.last_run` behavior for non-source syncs.
- Add a regression test that repeats a same-HEAD source sync and verifies freshness advances.

## Why

Autopilot or other periodic sync callers can successfully check an unchanged source and receive `status: 'up_to_date'`. Before this change, that early return skipped the freshness write, so source-health checks could report the source as stale even though polling was running successfully.

## Test Plan

- `bun run typecheck`

title: autopilot: minion worker crashes with "No database connection: connect() has not been called"
body:
## Description

The minion worker subprocess (`gbrain jobs work`) spawned by `gbrain autopilot` crashes repeatedly because `engine.connect()` has not been called before the worker's main loop attempts to access the database.

This prevents ALL autopilot cycles from completing, and causes data loss during the extract phase.

## Environment

- **gbrain version**: 0.41.14.0
- **Engine**: Postgres
- **Config**: `agent.use_gateway_loop=true`, `chat_model: deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash`
- **OS**: Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu)

## Symptoms

### 1. Worker crash loop (51 crashes recorded)

```
Promotion error: No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
[autopilot] worker exited code=1 signal=null after 1409ms, crashCount=4, cause=runtime_error
[autopilot] crash backoff 8111ms (crashCount=4)
```

Error counts:
- **51** worker crashes
- **265** "Promotion error" in `promoteDelayed()`
- **446** total "No database connection" errors
- **52** batch link row losses during extraction

### 2. Data loss during extract.links_fs

```
[extract.links_fs] 60/60 (100%)
[extract.links_fs] connection blip, retrying 26 rows in 500ms (No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>)
  batch error (26 link rows lost): No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
[extract.links_fs] 60/60 (100%) done
Links: created 0 from 60 pages
```

### 3. Unhandled rejection during conversation_facts_backfill

```
[cycle.conversation_facts_backfill] start
[unhandledRejection] GBrainError: No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
    at getConnection (/.../gbrain/src/core/db.ts:153:15)
    at transaction (/.../gbrain/src/core/postgres-engine.ts:764:34)
    at failJob (/.../gbrain/src/core/minions/queue.ts:855:24)
    at executeJob (/.../gbrain/src/core/minions/worker.ts:831:39)
    at processTicksAndRejections (native:7:39)
```

### 4. All sources never complete a full cycle

```
[FAIL] cycle_freshness: Source 'aevum' has never completed a full cycle;
Source 'agent-arch' has never completed a full cycle; ... (all 9 sources)
```

Brain score permanently stuck at 51/100 because link extraction (3/25), timeline extraction (2/15), and orphan resolution (1/15) cannot complete.

## Root Cause Analysis

The main `gbrain` CLI process correctly calls `createEngine()` → `connectWithRetry()` at startup (`src/cli.ts:1687-1691`). However, the minion worker is spawned as a **separate** `bun gbrain jobs work` subprocess by the supervisor (`src/core/minions/supervisor.ts`). This child process also goes through the full CLI initialization and should call `connectWithRetry()`, but something in the worker's startup path causes `connect()` to not be reliably established before `promoteDelayed()` or `executeJob()` attempts DB access.

The worker's `queue.promoteDelayed()` runs in the main loop before any job is claimed (`src/core/minions/worker.ts:434`), and if the engine's connection pool isn't ready at that point, the error is caught but the worker then crashes with an unhandled rejection when `executeJob()` later tries to call `getConnection()`.

## Contrast: Main process works fine

The parent autopilot process and direct `gbrain dream` invocations work correctly — DB access succeeds. Only the minion worker child process experiences this.

## Suggested Fix Direction

The worker's main loop should verify that `engine.connect()` has been called before entering the `promoteDelayed()` / claim / execute cycle. Alternatively, the connection should be lazily established on first use rather than requiring an explicit `connect()` call.

A workaround might be to pass `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` as an environment variable so the worker can self-initialize without depending on parent state.

## Related

- PR #1488 (gateway tool schema fix for non-Anthropic providers) — submitted separately
- The subagent functionality is also affected because subagent phases (consolidate, synthesize) run inside the worker process

title: dream: phases fail with "No database connection" on Postgres backend (lint+backlinks succeed in same run)
body:
### Summary

`gbrain dream` (and `gbrain dream --dry-run`) consistently fails with `No database connection: connect() has not been called` on every phase that needs the brain engine, even though the serve process at the same `DATABASE_URL` works fine. `lint` and `backlinks` (which presumably use a different connect path) complete successfully in the same invocation.

### Environment

- gbrain v0.41.10.1, commit `d036a97`
- Backend: Postgres (Supabase self-hosted; not PGLite)
- `gbrain init --url <postgres-url>` ran cleanly on container first-boot; `serve --http --port 3131` works, OAuth flow works, `query`/`search`/`extract links` all hit the DB normally
- `/var/lib/gbrain/.gbrain/config.json` contains `engine` + `database_url` fields (6 lines total)

### Repro

```bash
docker exec gbrain gbrain dream --dry-run
```

Output (abridged):

```
  ! lint        523 issue(s) found (dry-run, no writes)
  ✓ backlinks   no missing back-links found
  ✗ sync        sync phase failed
      [InternalError/UNKNOWN] No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
  ✗ synthesize  synthesize phase failed
      [InternalError/SYNTH_PHASE_FAIL] No database connection: connect() has not been called.
  ✗ extract_facts ...
  ✗ patterns ...
  ✗ recompute_emotional_weight ...
  ✗ consolidate ...
  ✗ propose_takes ...
  ✗ grade_takes ...
  ✗ calibration_profile ...
  ✗ embed ...
  ✗ orphans ...
  ✗ schema-suggest ...
```

The same failure occurs with `HOME=/var/lib/gbrain` explicitly passed via `docker exec -e HOME=...`. The cycle lock IS acquired (a row appears in `gbrain_cycle_locks`), so SOME DB connection is being established — just not the one each phase needs.

### Impact

Dream cycle (the documented backbone of "consolidate → propose_takes → grade_takes → calibration_profile") is unusable on Postgres backends. Brains running on the Postgres engine can't populate the `facts` table, `recall` returns empty, autopilot doesn't help (presumably hits the same path).

### Guess at root cause

The phase runner appears to construct its own brain-engine instance without inheriting the connection pool the parent `dream` process used to acquire the cycle lock. Looks like a DI gap — the lock-subsystem connect happens, the per-phase engine instances don't reuse it and don't reconnect from config.

### Workaround used

Switched to running individual extract-and-embed steps via host cron (`gbrain extract links --source db && gbrain embed --stale`) until this lands. Drops fact consolidation / take grading entirely.

### Related

- The lock row in `gbrain_cycle_locks` has a 30-min TTL but stays held on phase failure (acquired by failed dream-cycle, not released on the engine-side crash). Workaround: `DELETE FROM gbrain_cycle_locks WHERE id='gbrain-cycle';` as superuser. Possibly worth a separate `gbrain dream --abort` CLI.

title: extract links: hardcoded DIR_PATTERN whitelist drops all Obsidian/Notion-style wikilinks silently (created: 0 from N pages, no warning)
body:
### Summary

`gbrain extract links` silently creates 0 edges from an Obsidian-style vault export because the hardcoded `DIR_PATTERN` regex in `src/core/link-extraction.ts` only matches gbrain's own slug conventions. Operators ingesting any non-canonical directory layout (Obsidian vaults, Notion exports, custom topic taxonomies) get 0% graph coverage with no error and no warning.

### Where

```ts
// src/core/link-extraction.ts
const DIR_PATTERN = '(?:people|companies|meetings|concepts|deal|civic|project|projects|source|media|yc|tech|finance|personal|openclaw|entities)';
```

…and the three regex variants below it all bake `DIR_PATTERN/` into the link-target requirement.

### Impact

For an Obsidian export with directories like `books/`, `documentation/`, `guides/`, `ideas/`, `nutrition/`, `travel/`, `writing-dump/`, `archive/`, none of the wikilinks resolve. The extractor reports `created: 0 from N pages` with no clue what's wrong. Operators have to grep the source to discover the hardcoded whitelist; the docs don't mention it.

Even when the directory DOES match (e.g. `projects/` is in the whitelist), Obsidian's *title-form* wikilinks (`[[Yomumichi Documentation]]`) fail because the regex requires `[[directory/slug-path]]`. Obsidian users never write that form — Obsidian resolves by title via its own fuzzy index, and exports preserve title-form.

### Repro

```bash
# Pages exist:
gbrain sources list
# → some-source  321 pages
gbrain get projects/project-list/yomumichi/yomumichi
# → full content with [[Yomumichi Documentation]], [[Project List.base]], [[Notes on X]]

gbrain extract links --source db
# Links: created 0 from 321 pages
gbrain get-links projects/project-list/yomumichi/yomumichi
# → []
```

### Proposed fix

1. **Make `DIR_PATTERN` configurable** via `gbrain config set link_extraction_dirs "books,documentation,..."`. Hardcoded whitelists in extraction layers are an anti-pattern; per [search results from older versions](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/05/22/) some external write-ups already document this config key as if it exists, suggesting it was either planned or removed.
2. **Add a title-resolver fallback** so `[[Some Title]]` resolves to the slug of the page whose `title` (or `frontmatter.aliases[]`) matches. This is the Obsidian-compatibility move. Could be opt-in via a `link_extraction.resolve_by_title=true` config.
3. **Emit a warning** when extract finishes with `created: 0` despite the source having `count(*) > 0` pages — silent failure here is the worst part.

### Operator workaround (today, no upstream changes)

Pre-process the markdown during sync: rewrite all `[[Title]]` and `[[Path/Title]]` references to `[[canonical-slug/path]]` form before ingest. ~50-line Python pre-commit hook in the sync repo. Brittle and duplicates the title→slug logic, but it's the only path forward right now for Obsidian/Notion-export users.

### Environment

- gbrain v0.41.10.1, commit `d036a97`
- 321-page corpus (Notion export → Gitea → gbrain sources via path-based ingestion)
- Backend: Postgres

title: fix(embedding-dim-check): honor user_provided_models recipes (llama-server, litellm-proxy)
body:
## Summary

`gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model llama-server:<id> --embedding-dimensions <N>` currently fails with:

> Refusing to init: Provider "llama-server" model "..." does not support custom dimensions N (this model only emits its default vector size). Either drop --embedding-dimensions or pick a Matryoshka-aware model.

The same hard-refuse hits `litellm:<id>`. Every local llama.cpp / LiteLLM-proxy install is blocked from initializing.

## Root cause

`src/core/ai/recipes/llama-server.ts` and `litellm-proxy.ts` declare:

```ts
touchpoints: {
  embedding: {
    models: [],
    user_provided_models: true,   // "user owns model id"
    default_dims: 0,               // "user owns dim"
  },
}
```

But `src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts:isCustomDimValidForProvider` never reads `user_provided_models`. Its three-tier validation chain:

1. recipe-declared `dims_options` — `llama-server` declares none ➜ skip
2. provider-specific allow-lists (`openai` / `voyage` / `zeroentropyai`) — `recipe.id` doesn't match ➜ skip
3. fall through to "this model only emits its default vector size" reject

So any `requestedDims != 0` triggers Tier-3 reject. And dropping `--embedding-dimensions` doesn't help either — `default_dims=0` gets rejected one branch up by the `dim > 0` check at line 369.

The recipe author and the dim-check author had opposite intents:

- `llama-server.ts:43` setup_hint: *"Build llama.cpp, then `llama-server --model <gguf-path> --embeddings`. Set --embedding-model llama-server:<id> + --embedding-dimensions <N>."*
- `embedding-dim-check.ts:458` error: *"Either drop --embedding-dimensions or pick a Matryoshka-aware model."*

The setup hint tells you to pass `--embedding-dimensions`. The dim-check tells you not to. Both can't be right.

## Fix

Short-circuit Tier 3 when the recipe's embedding touchpoint declares `user_provided_models: true`. The recipe author already said "user owns the dim" — honor that. 4 lines:

```ts
const embTp = (recipe.touchpoints as { embedding?: { user_provided_models?: boolean } } | undefined)?.embedding;
if (embTp?.user_provided_models === true) {
  return { valid: true, error: '' };
}
```

Placed AFTER the existing Tier-2 provider-specific allow-lists so OpenAI / Voyage / ZE recipes (which DON'T set `user_provided_models`) still get their tight Matryoshka validation.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/embedding-dim-check.test.ts` — 29 pass / 0 fail (existing 26 + 3 new regression cases)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Smoke-test: `gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model llama-server:qwen3-embed --embedding-dimensions 1024` now succeeds against a real `llama-server` process on :8080

New cases in `test/embedding-dim-check.test.ts` cover the real-world scenarios this unblocks:

- `llama-server:qwen3-embed` @ 1024 dims (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B native, what motivated this PR)
- `llama-server:qwen3-embed-8b` @ 4096 dims (Qwen3-Embedding-8B native)
- `litellm:custom-model` @ 1024 dims (proves the fix isn't llama-server-specific)

## Motivation

Setting up a local-only gbrain with Qwen3-Embedding + Qwen3-Reranker via llama.cpp on a 16GB M4 — no API spend, no cloud calls. The `llama-server-reranker.ts` recipe note at L:32 explicitly mentions Qwen3-Reranker as a target use case, and `llama-server.ts` exists for exactly this kind of deployment. The Tier-3 reject just made the embedding side unreachable.

title: fix(gateway): preflight honors user-supplied modelId for user_provided_models recipes
body:
## Summary

Companion to #1496 — same bug class (`user_provided_models: true` not respected), different file, distinct surface.

After landing #1496, `gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model llama-server:qwen3-embed --embedding-dimensions 1024` succeeds. But the next step (`gbrain sync` / `gbrain embed --stale`) fails immediately at the gateway preflight:

> Provider "llama-server" requires a specific model name to be configured.
>
>   Set one: gbrain config set embedding_model llama-server:\<model-name\>

…even though `embedding_model` IS already set to `llama-server:qwen3-embed`. Same dead-end for `litellm:<id>`.

## Root cause

`src/core/ai/gateway.ts:670-674` in `isAvailable('embedding')`:

```ts
const isUserProvided = (tp as any).user_provided_models === true;
if (
  Array.isArray(tp.models) &&
  tp.models.length === 0 &&
  (recipe.id === 'litellm' || isUserProvided)
) {
  return { ok: false, reason: 'user_provided_model_unset', ... };
}
```

The condition reads recipe-level intent (`models: []` + `user_provided_models: true`) but never looks at whether the user has actually supplied a modelId. For `llama-server` and `litellm-proxy`, `models: []` means "the model is whatever the user launched the server with" — NOT "the user hasn't picked one yet." If `embedding_model` is `llama-server:qwen3-embed`, `parsed.modelId` is `qwen3-embed`, and the gate should pass.

The downstream user-facing fix instruction (`Set one: gbrain config set embedding_model llama-server:<model-name>`) is exactly what the user already did, so the error message becomes a riddle.

## Fix

Add `&& !parsed.modelId` to the guard:

```ts
if (
  Array.isArray(tp.models) &&
  tp.models.length === 0 &&
  (recipe.id === 'litellm' || isUserProvided) &&
  !parsed.modelId
) {
```

`parseModelId` already rejects empty modelIds (`provider:`) at an earlier stage via `unknown_provider`, so the strengthened guard is defense-in-depth at the touchpoint check rather than load-bearing. But the pre-fix unconditional refusal blocked every legitimate local-llama-server / litellm-proxy deployment.

The companion PR #1496 patches the same bug class in `embedding-dim-check.ts` (init-time dim validation). Together, the two fixes restore the full local-llama-server flow:

```bash
gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model llama-server:qwen3-embed --embedding-dimensions 1024   # fixed by #1496
gbrain sync --repo ~/coding/personal-brain                                                    # fixed by this PR
# → 7 pages imported, 11 chunks embedded via Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B on llama-server:8080
```

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/embed-preflight.test.ts` — 15 pass / 0 fail (existing 11 + 4 new)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Smoke test: `gbrain sync --repo ~/coding/personal-brain` + `gbrain embed --stale` now succeed end-to-end against Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B running on `llama-server :8080`

New cases in `test/embed-preflight.test.ts`:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `llama-server:qwen3-embed`, no env | `user_provided_model_unset` (wrong) | passes (correct) |
| `litellm:custom-model`, no env | `user_provided_model_unset` (wrong) | passes (correct) |
| `llama-server:` (empty modelId) | rejected | still rejected (`unknown_provider` via parseModelId) |
| `litellm:` (empty modelId) | rejected | still rejected (same) |

The fail-loud cases use `toThrow(EmbeddingCredentialError)` rather than locking the specific `reason` field — the strengthened guard is defense-in-depth, the actual rejection path is `parseModelId`'s `unknown_provider`. Test comments document this explicitly.

## Why a separate PR

#1496 fixes init-time dim validation; this fixes sync/embed-time preflight. Same root cause class but distinct surfaces and distinct call sites. Reviewers can land them independently; tests and patches don't overlap. If only one ships, the other still has standalone value (each unblocks a different stage of the local-llama-server flow).

title: Bug: lint phase engine.disconnect() kills worker shared DB pool, causing crash-loop
body:
## Summary

During autopilot cycle execution, the lint phase creates a second PostgresEngine and shares the module-level db.sql singleton via engine.connect({}) (no poolSize). When the phase completes, engine.disconnect() in the finally block destroys the shared pool, rendering the worker unable to operate. All subsequent phases fail, and the worker crashes with an unhandled rejection.

## Impact

- All 9 sources never completed a full cycle
- Brain score stuck at 51 (links 3/25, timeline 2/15, orphans 1/15)
- Worker crash-loops: 51 crash records, max 5 restarts before autopilot gives up

## Root Cause

src/commands/lint.ts:298-319, resolveLintContentSanity():

```typescript
const engine = await createEngine({...});
try {
    await engine.connect({});  // no poolSize -> module singleton path
    const lifted = await loadConfigWithEngine(engine, base);
} finally {
    await engine.disconnect(); // -> db.disconnect() -> sql.end(); sql = null
}
```

engine.connect({}) without poolSize routes through the module-level db.sql singleton. The subsequent engine.disconnect() in the finally block kills the shared pool for ALL callers in the process, including the MinionWorker.

## Diagnosis

Instrumented db.disconnect(), PostgresEngine.disconnect(), and getConnection() with stack traces. The stack trace confirms the disconnect originates from resolveLintContentSanity -> lint.ts:319 -> runLintCore -> runPhaseLint -> runCycle.

## Fix

Pass poolSize: 2 so the lint engine gets its own instance-level pool that does not share state with the module singleton:

```typescript
await engine.connect({ poolSize: 2 });
```

## Related

The /No database connection/i pattern in retry-matcher.ts (added v0.41.2.1) marks this terminal error as retryable, producing misleading connection blip log messages and wasting a 500ms retry. Since the error means the module-level singleton is null, retrying without explicit reconnect is guaranteed to fail.

title: PGLite WASM crash on Windows 11 ARM64 (same Aborted() as #223 on macOS arm64)
body:
﻿## Bug Description

Same `Aborted(). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.` PGLite WASM crash as #223, but on **Windows 11 ARM64** — not macOS. The user-facing wrapper in `gbrain` currently attributes this only to the macOS 26.3 bug; the underlying failure mode appears to be cross-OS on **arm64**.

## Environment

- OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, **ARM 64-bit Processor**
- Bun: 1.3.14
- gbrain: 0.40.8.1 (installed from `github:garrytan/gbrain#af5ee1e` via `bun install -g`)
- `@electric-sql/pglite`: 0.4.3 (note: #223 is on 0.4.4 — so the regression is not pinned to a single PGLite version)
- Engine: pglite (default), brain at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`

## Steps to reproduce

Any PGLite-touching command fails. Examples that hit it in my session:

```
gbrain config set autopilot.nightly_quality_probe.enabled true
gbrain query "test"
```

Both crash with:

```
PGLite failed to initialize its WASM runtime.
  This is most commonly the macOS 26.3 WASM bug: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/223
  Run `gbrain doctor` for a full diagnosis.
  Original error: Aborted(). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.
```

`gbrain doctor --fast` works because it deliberately skips DB checks; `gbrain doctor` (full) does not.

## What still works

- `gbrain --version`
- `gbrain doctor --fast`
- `gbrain routing-eval` (pure-file analysis, no DB)
- `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` reports "All migrations up to date" — though I am unsure whether that codepath actually opens PGLite or just inspects the migrations dir.

## Workaround

Editing `~/.gbrain/config.json` directly (e.g. to enable `autopilot.nightly_quality_probe.enabled`) avoids the crash since `loadConfig()` reads the JSON file before any PGLite boot. This is a workaround for `config set` only; data-plane commands (`query`, `serve`, `export`, anything that reads/writes pages) still cannot run.

## Analysis / suggestion

- #223 reports the same WASM `Aborted()` on **macOS 26.3 arm64**. This is **Windows 11 arm64**. Common thread: **arm64 + PGLite WASM**.
- PGLite versions differ (0.4.4 in #223, 0.4.3 here) — so pinning PGLite alone is unlikely to fix both.
- The error wrapper string ("This is most commonly the macOS 26.3 WASM bug") should probably broaden once this is confirmed, so Windows arm64 users do not get pointed at a macOS-only issue.

Happy to gather more diagnostics (e.g. a `-sASSERTIONS`-enabled PGLite build, full Node/Bun stack with `--inspect`) if useful.

title: Cycle extract phase still writes links/timeline to `default` source on federated brains (follow-up to #1204)
body:
# Cycle extract phase still writes links/timeline to `default` source on federated brains (follow-up to #1204)

## Summary

#1204 fixed the **CLI** `gbrain extract` source-awareness by adding `--source-id` (v0.37.7.0). But the **automated dream/autopilot cycle** still hits the same root cause on a federated brain: every cycle logs `Links: created 0 from N pages` / `Timeline: created 0 entries from N pages` and persists nothing, because the cycle's extract phase never threads a `sourceId` and falls back to the literal `'default'` source.

Two interacting defects, both still present on **v0.41.2.0**:

1. **`runPhaseExtract` doesn't thread `sourceId`.** It calls `runExtractCore({ mode, dir, slugs })` with no source. `ExtractOpts` has no `sourceId` field, so the full-walk extractors (`extractLinksFromDir`/`extractTimelineFromDir`) never set `from_source_id/to_source_id`, and `addLinksBatch` maps missing → literal `'default'`, then INNER-JOINs `pages ON (slug, source_id='default')`. On a brain whose content lives in a non-`default` source, every row is dropped by the JOIN → 0 inserted, no error. (Same mechanism as #1204 Bug 1, just reached via the cycle instead of the CLI.)

2. **`noExtract: willRunExtractPhase` disables the *working* path.** `runPhaseSync` resolves the correct `sourceId` (`resolveSourceForDir`) and `performSync` would run the source-aware inline hooks (`extractLinksForSlugs`/`extractTimelineForSlugs`, which #1204 confirmed are correct). But sync passes `noExtract: willRunExtractPhase` to avoid duplicate work — so when the cycle's extract phase is scheduled (the default, `ALL_PHASES`), sync **skips its source-correct inline extraction** and defers to the broken full-walk phase. Net: the cycle turns off the good path and keeps the broken one.

## Environment

- gbrain **v0.41.2.0**, Supabase Postgres engine
- Federated brain, 3 sources: `default` (0–10 pages, isolated), `sos` (~32.7k pages, repo-backed, the live vault), `msft` (~2.8k pages)
- Symptom in `~/.gbrain/autopilot.log`, every cycle:
  ```
  Links: created 0 from 13671 pages
  Timeline: created 0 entries from 13671 pages
  ```

## Repro

On a federated brain whose content is in a non-`default` source, run a full dream cycle (or let autopilot run). The extract phase reports `created 0`. Meanwhile the source-scoped CLI path works:

```
$ gbrain extract all --source db --source-id sos --dry-run
{ "links_created": 91, "timeline_entries_created": 376, "pages_processed": 32701 }
```

vs. the cycle's full-walk phase on the same content: `created 0`.

## Relevant code (v0.41.2.0)

- `src/core/cycle.ts:810` — `runPhaseExtract` calls `runExtractCore(engine, { mode: 'all', dir: brainDir, slugs: changedSlugs })`, no `sourceId`.
- `src/commands/extract.ts:302-318` — `ExtractOpts` has no `sourceId` field; the full-walk path (`extractLinksFromDir`/`extractTimelineFromDir`) can't scope.
- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:2064-2077` — `addLinksBatch` maps missing `from_source_id/to_source_id` → `'default'`, INNER-JOINs `pages ON (slug, source_id)`.
- `src/core/cycle.ts:745-752` — `runPhaseSync` resolves the correct `sourceId` but passes `noExtract: willRunExtractPhase`, disabling the source-aware inline hooks when the (broken) extract phase will run.
- `src/core/cycle.ts:1371` — `willRunExtractPhase = phases.includes('extract')`.
- Working, source-aware hooks already exist: `src/commands/extract.ts:719` (`extractLinksForSlugs`) / `:748` (`extractTimelineForSlugs`), used by `src/commands/sync.ts:1104-1109`.

## Suggested fix

Thread the source through the cycle extract path, mirroring what `runPhaseSync` already does:

1. Add `sourceId?: string` to `ExtractOpts`; have `runExtractCore` pass it to the full-walk extractors and on to `addLinksBatch` (the incremental `extractForSlugs`/`extractLinksForSlugs` path already accepts `{ sourceId }`).
2. In `runPhaseExtract`, resolve `sourceId = await resolveSourceForDir(engine, brainDir)` and pass it down.

Alternatively (or additionally): when the cycle can't resolve a single source for `brainDir`, fall back to the source-aware sync-inline extraction (i.e., don't set `noExtract` for the broken full-walk path) so federated brains aren't silently left at 0 coverage.

## Impact

On federated brains the nightly cycle contributes nothing to graph/timeline coverage; coverage is maintained only by the per-source sync hook on *changed* pages. Already-synced pages that were never individually extracted stay uncovered, and there's no automated path to close the gap (the manual workaround is `gbrain extract all --source db --source-id <id>`, the #1204 fix).

## Summary

Adds a native Mistral embedding recipe for `codestral-embed`. Mistral's `/v1/embeddings` is OpenAI-shaped on the response, so this ships as a pure openai-compatible provider (recipe file + register, no gateway shim) per the rule in `src/core/ai/recipes/index.ts`.

title: v0.41.15.0 feat(sync): --timeout + --max-age + partial status (closes #1472 RFC)
body:
## Summary

Two new CLI flags + a documented shell cron pattern that breaks the hourly sync cascade documented in the closed [PR #1472](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1472) RFC from @garrytan-agents (8/12 hourly cron runs timing out, sources going 50+ hours stale, manual `--break-lock` per source for recovery).

- **`gbrain sync --source X --timeout <s>`** — graceful self-termination. Per-source `AbortController` inside `runOne` so `--timeout --all` gives each source its own budget. Returns `SyncResult { status: 'partial', filesImported, reason: 'timeout' | 'pull_timeout' }` with `last_commit` UNCHANGED by construction (abort checks fire strictly before the bookmark write). CLI exits 0 so cron doesn't classify as failure.
- **`gbrain sync --break-lock --all --max-age <s>`** — drops the prior `--all` refusal + adds age-gated breaking via `last_refreshed_at` semantic (not `acquired_at`). Healthy refreshing holders survive by construction; wedged-but-alive holders get correctly identified.
- **Recommended cron pattern (README + CHANGELOG):** shell `timeout(1)` per-source loop for OS-level process isolation + gbrain `--timeout` for graceful self-termination half-a-minute earlier.

## Honest scope (per the gstack voice rules)

Three deliberate gaps documented in CHANGELOG + failure-modes table:

1. `--timeout` covers pull + delete + rename + import only. Extract + embed run to completion (D-V3-1 — bookmark write is the boundary).
2. First 30 min after migration v98, `--max-age` cannot identify wedged pre-upgrade holders (D-V4-1 rollout-safety — backfill sets `last_refreshed_at = NOW()` to protect healthy old-binary holders).
3. Full-sync triggers (first sync, `--full`, chunker-version rewalk) don't respect `--timeout` yet. Filed for v0.42+.

## Architecture provenance

Plan went through 1 eng review (10 decisions) + 3 codex passes (24 findings, all absorbed via 17 architectural + 7 mechanical fixes). Plan file at `~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-parallel-valley.md`. Codex's load-bearing catches in the rollout:
- **CMT1**: rejected the v1 "add age-based steal to routine `tryAcquireDbLock`" path because `withRefreshingLock` keeps `ttl_expires_at` fresh but not `acquired_at` — would have stolen healthy long-running locks. Moved to the explicit `runBreakLock` SQL only.
- **CMT2**: rejected `--independent` Minion fan-out — `MinionWorker` is in-process worker pool, not OS-process-per-source; `waitForCompletion` throws on timeout but doesn't cancel the underlying job. Shell `timeout(1)` per-source is the right shape.
- **D-V4-1**: rejected backfilling `last_refreshed_at = acquired_at` in migration v98 — would let `--max-age 1800` immediately delete healthy pre-upgrade holders during the rollout window. Backfilling `= NOW()` trades 30 min of degraded recovery for zero-risk rollout.

## Commit chain (bisect-friendly)

1. `3eee3817` feat(sync): migration v98 last_refreshed_at + deleteLockRowIfStale helper
2. `cd1c0e8a` feat(sync): --timeout + --max-age + partial status + per-source AbortController
3. `8b342120` test(heavy): sync_timeout_rescue.sh reproducer for the cron-cascade
4. `a9da5067` docs(v0.41.15.0): CHANGELOG + README + TODOS + version bump
5. `7b9bda96` Merge origin/master (catch-up from v0.41.12 → v0.41.14)

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] `bun run test` → **11,087 pass / 0 fail** across 4 shards (553-1039s per shard, 18 minutes total)
- [x] `bun run test:serial` → **508 pass / 0 fail** across 46 files
- [x] PGLite hermetic suite (13 cases in `test/sync-break-lock-all.test.ts`): tryAcquireDbLock writes `last_refreshed_at` on INSERT, refresh bumps both columns, inspectLock surfaces the new field, deleteLockRowIfStale refuses fresh / breaks stale / safe on holder_pid mismatch / refuses NULL (pre-v98)
- [x] Unit cases (15 cases in `test/sync-timeout.test.ts`): parseDurationSeconds full grammar (`60s`/`10m`/`1h`/bare int; reject 0/neg/decimals/garbage), partial JSON envelope additivity
- [x] E2E case extension (`test/e2e/sync-parallel.test.ts`): real Postgres, abort-mid-import returns partial, `last_commit` unchanged, `filesImported` bounded
- [x] Heavy reproducer (`tests/heavy/sync_timeout_rescue.sh`): smoke-tested at PAGES=50 × 4 sources × WAVES=2 × TIMEOUT=2s → every source converges within 2 waves; cascade is broken
- [x] `gbrain --version` reports `0.41.15.0` from compiled binary
- [x] CI version-gate trio: VERSION + package.json + CHANGELOG header all read `0.41.15.0`
- [ ] Local smoke against the CEO-class brain (run after merge — operator step, not CI)

title: fix(entities): make tryPrefixExpansion symmetric with findPrefixCandidates
body:
`tryPrefixExpansion` matches `<dir>/<token>-%` only; the sibling
function `findPrefixCandidates` 40 lines above (resolve.ts:211-214)
matches both `<dir>/<token>` AND `<dir>/<token>-%`. Both target the
same resolution problem from opposite sides (hot-path top-1 vs
ambiguity-detector top-10) and should agree on which pages qualify
as candidates.

The bare form was added to `findPrefixCandidates` in v0.35.5 (codex
finding #11, phantom-redirect ambiguity detection) but this hot-path
query was never updated to match. This aligns them.

## Impact

In the common case, fuzzy match catches a bare `<dir>/<token>` slug
before prefix expansion runs â^@^T `similarity('people/alice', 'alice')`
clears the 0.4 threshold (â^I^H 0.417), so headline 'invisible to
resolver' behavior does NOT reproduce on a clean test fixture. The
fix is therefore primarily defensive consistency, biting in:

- Thin-band cases where multiple similar-name pages compete for
  fuzzy's LIMIT cutoff and the bare slug falls below it.
- Future fuzzy-threshold tuning that pushes bare slugs below the gate.
- Any explicit caller of `tryPrefixExpansion` (e.g. via the
  phantom-redirect path) that bypasses fuzzy entirely.

## Changes

- `src/core/entities/resolve.ts`: extend `tryPrefixExpansion` patterns
  to include the bare form; swap `LIKE $2` for `LIKE ANY($2::text[])`
  (already canonical elsewhere in this file).
- Updated function JSDoc to reflect both pattern forms.
- `test/entity-resolve-perf.slow.test.ts`: corrected stale comment
  noting that the perf benchmark's single-pattern `LIKE $2` form is
  intentional (it benchmarks the correlated-subquery vs derived-table
  shape, not the multi-pattern matching).

## Test plan

- `bun run typecheck` â^@^T clean.
- `bun test test/entity-resolve.test.ts` â^@^T 24/24 pass (no behavior
  regression on the 11 prefix-expansion cases that do bite the
  function, including Bob/Charlie/Dave fuzzy-fallthrough paths).
- `bun test test/phantom-redirect.test.ts` â^@^T 38/38 pass (covers
  `findPrefixCandidates`, the sibling function this aligns with).
- No new test cases added in this PR: the bare-form behavior is
  difficult to isolate from the fuzzy short-circuit on a realistic
  fixture without refactoring to export `tryPrefixExpansion` for
  direct testing, which is outside this PR's scope.

title: fix(auth): create command works when --takes-holders is omitted
body:
## Summary

`gbrain auth create <name>` exits 1 with the usage line when `--takes-holders` is not provided. The positional-name parser at `src/commands/auth.ts:472` uses `rest[takesIdx + 1]` as an exclusion value, but when the flag is absent `takesIdx` is `-1` and that expression evaluates to `rest[0]` — the actual name. The `find` filter then excludes the legitimate name and `positional` ends up `undefined`.

## Repro

```bash
$ gbrain auth create my-client
Usage: auth create <name> [--takes-holders world,garry]
$ echo $?
1
```

With `--takes-holders` present, the bug is masked:

```bash
$ gbrain auth create my-client --takes-holders world
Token created for "my-client" (takes_holders=["world"]):
gbrain_...
```

## Fix

Guard the lookup so the filter only excludes the takes-holders VALUE when the flag is actually present.

```diff
-      const positional = rest.find(a => !a.startsWith('--') && a !== rest[takesIdx + 1]);
+      const takesValue = takesIdx >= 0 ? rest[takesIdx + 1] : undefined;
+      const positional = rest.find(a => !a.startsWith('--') && a !== takesValue);
```

After:

```bash
$ gbrain auth create my-client
Token created for "my-client" (takes_holders=["world"]):
gbrain_...
```

## Test plan

- [x] `gbrain auth create my-client` succeeds and creates a token with default `["world"]` takes-holders
- [x] `gbrain auth create my-client --takes-holders world,garry` still works
- [x] `gbrain auth create my-client --takes-holders world,garry,brain` still parses the list correctly
- [x] `gbrain auth create` (no name) still surfaces the usage error

Caught while wiring gbrain HTTP MCP into a 4-agent OpenClaw deployment — the create call is hit on every per-agent token registration.

title: v0.41.16.0 feat: conversation parser cathedral + progressive-batch primitive (closes #1461)
body:
## Summary

Replaces PR #1461's single-format Telegram regex with a **12-pattern built-in registry** covering every common chat-export format, plus an **opt-in LLM polish + fallback** layer for the long tail. Same wave extracts a new **`progressive-batch` primitive** (Wintermute-inspired ramp-up: trial 10 → 100 → 500 → full with verification at each stage) after rule-of-three was satisfied across 12+ ad-hoc cost-prompt sites.

**The user impact:** a real production brain has 134 Telegram-shaped pages typed `conversation` that the existing parser silently drops. After this upgrade, the dream cycle's `conversation_facts_backfill` phase extracts facts from them automatically. Same for any Discord, WhatsApp, Signal, IRC, Matrix, Teams, or email-thread page.

PR #1461 contributor's `BRACKET_TIME_RX` + `cleanSpeaker` survive verbatim as the `telegram-bracket` built-in pattern + `DEFAULT_SPEAKER_CLEAN` export. All 33 of their test cases pass against the new orchestrator. Co-Authored-By preserved.

### The 12 built-in patterns

| id | sample |
|---|---|
| `imessage-slack` | `**Alice** (2024-03-15 9:00 AM): hi` |
| `telegram-bracket` | `**[18:37] 👤 Alice:** hi` (PR #1461 verbatim) |
| `telegram-text-export` | `Alice, [Mar 15, 2024 at 6:37:00 PM]` |

**Total: 350/350 across touched suites. `bun run verify`: 24/24 green.**

Real bug caught + fixed during gap audit: `IdempotentMutationVerifier` was comparing absolute mutated-count vs per-stage expected (failed silently on stage 2+); now uses per-stage delta semantics matching `OutputCountVerifier`.

## Pre-Landing Review

Codex outside-voice review during planning absorbed 8 substantive technical findings (all adopted):

- **Privacy posture** — LLM polish/fallback flipped to opt-IN (chat content goes to Anthropic only when user explicitly enables)
- **ReDoS theater** — dropped arbitrary user regex; user patterns wait for v0.42+ with worker-isolated regex (safe-regex / RE2)
- **LLM-inferred-regex persistence** as silent-corruption machine — dropped entirely; LLM fallback parses for THIS page only, cached by content_hash
- **Pattern priority scoring** across first 10 lines (not first-wins) — defeats overlap mis-routing
- **Timezone policy per PatternEntry** — `inline_utc | frontmatter_tz | utc_assumed_with_warn`; time-only formats warn when no frontmatter timezone
- **Verifier shape** discriminated union (output_count | idempotent_mutation | noop) — fits reindex / embed / eval-contradictions / parser cleanly
- **Behavior parity for retrofits** — sites that previously jumped to full keep doing so; ramp is opt-in per-site via `interactiveAbortMs > 0`

title: doctor: pgvector and jsonb_integrity checks throw false warnings on PGLite
Fix/user provided model validation
body:
## Problem

Three independent bugs made `llama-server:` and `litellm:` recipes completely
unusable for the `--embedding-model` flag with a custom model name and explicit
`--embedding-dimensions`. Hitting all three in sequence was required to successfully
run `gbrain init --embedding-model llama-server:<id> --embedding-dimensions N`.

## Root causes

**Bug 1 — `embedding-dim-check.ts`: Matryoshka allow-list rejects all user-supplied dims**

`validateDimAgainstTouchpoint` has a guard for custom dimensions that walks the
recipe's `dims_options` list. `user_provided_models` recipes set `default_dims=0` as
a sentinel meaning "no default — user must supply any positive integer." The guard
didn't check for the sentinel, so every user-supplied dimension was rejected as
"does not appear in declared dims_options."

Fix: skip the allow-list check when `defaultDims === 0`.

**Bug 2 — `gateway.ts` `diagnoseEmbedding`: fires "model unset" error even when model IS set**

`diagnoseEmbedding` has a check intended to catch the case where the user forgot to
pass a model name to a `user_provided_models` recipe. The check fired whenever
`models: []` and `isUserProvided` were both true — it didn't verify that `parsed.modelId`
was actually absent. Users who passed a fully-specified model (e.g.
`llama-server:mlx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-8B-4bit-DWQ`) got the "model unset" error.

Fix: add `&& !parsed.modelId` to the guard condition.

**Bug 3 — `gateway.ts` embed: `dimensions` param not sent to the endpoint**

`dimsProviderOptions` returns `undefined` for model IDs it doesn't recognize (i.e.,
any user-supplied model name for a `user_provided_models` recipe). When it returns
`undefined`, the `dimensions` field is not injected into the embedding request body.
For models where native output size differs from the configured schema width — for
example, a 4096-dim model being used at 2048 dims via MRL truncation — the endpoint
returns full-size vectors and the insert fails with a dimension mismatch.

Fix: when `dimsProviderOptions` returns `undefined` and the recipe has
`user_provided_models: true`, inject `{ openaiCompatible: { dimensions: effectiveDims } }`.

## Tests

Adds four regression tests to `test/embedding-dim-check.test.ts` covering Bug 1:
the llama-server recipe's `default_dims=0` sentinel path (any positive dim accepted,
zero/missing dims still rejected correctly). All 30 tests in that file pass.

Existing gateway tests (`test/ai/gateway.test.ts`, `test/gateway-embed-model-override.test.ts`)
pass unchanged. TypeScript typecheck clean. Privacy, jsonb, and test-isolation checks pass.

## Scope

These bugs are not specific to any particular embedding model. They affect any user
of `llama-server:` or `litellm:` recipes who specifies a model name and explicit
embedding dimensions. The fixes are confined to the validation and gateway code paths
for `user_provided_models` recipes and have no effect on standard provider recipes.

---

## Commits

1. `9d8526d` — fix: user_provided_models recipes (llama-server/litellm) unusable end-to-end
2. `6f35a91` — test: regression coverage for user_provided_models dim validation (Bug 1)

## Files changed

- `src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts` — Bug 1 fix
- `src/core/ai/gateway.ts` — Bug 2 + Bug 3 fixes
- `test/embedding-dim-check.test.ts` — 4 new regression tests

title: fix(gateway): handle embed preflight with user-provided models and reasoning model output
body:
## Description

Two fixes in `src/core/ai/gateway.ts` addressing bugs found during autopilot diagnosis:

### Fix 1: Embed preflight rejects user-provided models (closes #1516)

When a brain is configured with `embedding_model: llama-server:text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b`, `diagnoseEmbedding()` returns `user_provided_model_unset` even though the model string is fully specified. The guard checks `tp.models.length === 0` without verifying whether the resolved `parsed.modelId` is populated.

**Fix:** Add `!parsed.modelId` to the condition. A non-empty model id after the colon satisfies the "user provided a model" requirement.

### Fix 2: Reasoning model output falls through response normalization (closes #1517)

The `chat()` response normalization skips `type: "reasoning"` parts in `result.content` and does not check `result.reasoningText` in the flat fallback. When a reasoning model (DeepSeek, etc.) returns content through reasoning channels, the blocks array remains empty.

**Fix:**
- In the `result.content` branch: treat `type: "reasoning"` parts as text blocks
- In the flat fallback: when `result.text` is empty, check `result.reasoningText`

## Related

- Issue #1516
- Issue #1517

title: query: since/until filters on updated_at instead of effective_date
body:
## Bug

The `since` / `until` parameters on the `query` operation are documented as filtering on `effective_date`:

> `since`: v0.29.1 — filter to pages whose effective_date is >= this.
> `until`: v0.29.1 — filter to effective_date <= this.

But the actual SQL in `postgres-engine.ts` (lines 1401, 1406, 1554, 1559, 1676, 1681) filters on `COALESCE(p.updated_at, p.created_at)`:

```sql
AND COALESCE(p.updated_at, p.created_at) > $N::timestamptz
AND COALESCE(p.updated_at, p.created_at) < $N::timestamptz
```

## Impact

For pages ingested via `sync` or `import`, `updated_at` reflects **import time**, not the content's actual date. Email pages with filenames like `2026-05-22_$

In practice, `query --since 2026-05-18 --until 2026-05-25` returns **zero results** even though dozens of pages have `effective_date` within that range. The $

## Reproduction

1. Import a markdown directory with date-prefixed filenames
2. Verify `effective_date` is populated: `SELECT effective_date, slug FROM pages WHERE effective_date IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5;`
3. Run `gbrain query "anything" --since 2026-05-01 --until 2026-05-31` — returns empty
4. Run `gbrain query "anything"` (no date filter) — returns pages with `effective_date` in that range

## Fix

Change all 6 occurrences in `postgres-engine.ts` from:
```sql
COALESCE(p.updated_at, p.created_at)
```
to:
```sql
COALESCE(p.effective_date, p.updated_at, p.created_at)
```

This respects `effective_date` when set (filename-derived, frontmatter, etc.) and falls back to `updated_at` / `created_at` for pages without one.

The same bug likely exists in `pglite-engine.ts` (same pattern at lines ~1398–1728).

## Environment
- gbrain v0.41.14.0
- Postgres engine with pgvector
- 1,416 pages (1,227 emails with filename-derived effective_date, 189 concepts)
