title: schema fork/show/diff/lint/validate `gbrain-base-v2` fails with "Unknown pack" — `packPathByName` only resolves `gbrain-base`
PC3 timeline backfill (C1, one-shot)
body:
One-shot backfill of structured timeline_entries — component C1 of tasks/gbrain-weekly-meta-cognitive-cron, under goals/standing/gbrain-compile-itself (PC3).

## What
Mines dated events from correspondence/* + meetings/* page bodies (regex-only) and writes them onto the person/company entities those pages link to (post-call-processor idiom — timeline entries live on entity pages).

## Key correction vs spec
timeline_coverage is ENTITY-SCOPED in gbrain v0.40.x (person|company pages with >=1 timeline_entry / person|company pages) per the Goodhart-correction (project_gbrain_brain_score_entity_scoped). Writing entries onto correspondence/meeting pages themselves moves the metric ZERO. So entries land on the linked entities instead. The spec assumption predated this change.

## Results (verified live)
- timeline_coverage 0.3957 -> 0.4321
- brain_score 67 -> 68
- entities with timeline 5842 -> 6383 (+541 newly covered)
- 2958 rows written, 1250 entities touched
- Idempotency proven: 3046 backfill rows = 3046 distinct keys (zero dups); re-run only adds rows for entities that gained new links (88, then 1)
- 7 ambiguous month-day-without-year cases deferred

## Honest shortfall
Per-page median >=2.5 is not met corpus-wide: the real corpus (3072 correspondence pages) is dominated by single-date Gmail threads (median 1), unlike the specs ~490-page estimate. Inflating single messages into fake dates would be Goodhart; declined.

## Guardrails
Junk-hub/self denylist per link-mine 2026-05-25 lesson. Pool-throttled. No Haiku/Ollama. Rows stamped source=timeline-backfill<date> (auditable + reversible).

title: fix(heavy-tests): unbreak frontmatter_scan_wallclock (Heavy Tests red since 2026-05-23)
body:
## Summary

The Heavy Tests scheduled workflow has been failing every night since **2026-05-23** because `tests/heavy/frontmatter_scan_wallclock.sh` calls `gbrain init --pglite --yes`, and v0.37.10.0 (#1278, a55de712) made init require an embedding provider. The CI runner has no `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `VOYAGE_API_KEY` / `ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY` configured, so init exits non-zero and the heavy runner aborts on the first script.

The same PR that introduced the gate also shipped the `--no-embedding` D9 opt-in for exactly this case ("deferred setup, no embedding tier"). The test never embeds anything — it seeds raw `.md` files and measures doctor's frontmatter scan wallclock. `--no-embedding` is the canonical fix.

## Failing log excerpt (most recent run, 2026-05-27 11:50 UTC)

```
[fm_wallclock] init brain...
[fm_wallclock] FAIL: gbrain init exited non-zero

No embedding provider configured. Set one of:
  export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-…
  export ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY=ze-…
  export VOYAGE_API_KEY=pa-…
Or defer setup: gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding
```

The error message literally suggests the fix this PR applies.

## Scope check

`grep "gbrain init" tests/heavy/*.sh` → only `frontmatter_scan_wallclock.sh` calls init. This PR is the full surface fix; no other heavy script needs touching.

## Why not configure an embedding key in CI

- Costs API spend on every nightly run for a test that doesn't embed.
- Adds a secret-management dependency for a test that doesn't need one.
- Hides intent — the test legitimately measures `doctor`, not embedding pipeline.

Using `--no-embedding` makes the test's actual scope explicit and keeps CI free.

## Test plan

Verified locally with a small fixture (full 60K fixture takes ~3min to seed):

```
$ REAL_PAGES=100 NODE_MODULES_PAGES=500 WALLCLOCK_BUDGET_S=60 \
    bash tests/heavy/frontmatter_scan_wallclock.sh

[fm_wallclock] running gbrain doctor (budget 60s)...
[fm_wallclock] doctor exit=0 wallclock=627ms
[fm_wallclock] frontmatter_integrity: status=ok msg=No registered sources to scan
[fm_wallclock] PASS (doctor=627ms < 60s budget, frontmatter_integrity=ok)
```

title: PGLite + google provider: query with expand=true returns empty while expand=false hits (score 0.9998)
body:
## Summary

With the **google (native) provider**, `query` with expansion enabled (the default, `expand: true`) returns an **empty result set**, while the exact same query with `expand: false` returns the correct hit at a near-perfect score. So expansion is not merely disabled (cf. #1156) — it actively evicts the true hit and yields `[]`.

## Environment

- gbrain **v0.41.26.0** (master HEAD `42d99b6f`)
- macOS, Apple Silicon
- Engine: **PGLite local**
- `embedding_model: google:gemini-embedding-001` (768d)
- `expansion_model: google:gemini-2.0-flash`
- Accessed via the stdio MCP server (`gbrain serve`), `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` injected.

## Repro

1. `gbrain init --force --pglite --embedding-model google:gemini-embedding-001` (with `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` set).
2. Put one page:
   > The deployment failed because the SSL certificate had expired and the load balancer rejected all inbound HTTPS traffic.
3. Query the same topic.

| Call | Result |
|------|--------|
| `query("SSL certificate expired load balancer rejected HTTPS", expand=false)` | ✅ hit, score **0.9998** |
| `query("SSL certificate expired", expand=true)` (default) | ❌ `[]` |
| `query("deployment outage caused by certificate problem", expand=true)` | ❌ `[]` |
| `search("SSL certificate expired")` (BM25) | ✅ hit, score 0.777 |

Vector path is healthy (proven by `expand=false`). Only the expansion-enabled path is empty.

## Notes

- `expandQuery()` in `src/core/search/expansion.ts` has a `catch { return [query] }` fallback and prepends the original query, so an LLM failure alone should *not* produce empty results. The eviction appears to happen in the downstream multi-query RRF fusion (`src/core/search/hybrid.ts`) when google-native expansion output is present.
- Possibly related: #1156 (expansion silently disabled on openai-compat endpoints — different symptom), #1469 (hybrid query identical results on vector path).

## Workaround

Pass `expand: false` / `--no-expand`.

title: v0.13.1 grandfather sweep hangs indefinitely on attachment page (PGLite, 82K-page brain)
body:
**Version**: gbrain v0.35.0.0 (commit `baf1a47798cb145d00bfce4fa94f85a94c8d7e07`)
**Engine**: PGLite
**Brain size**: 82,829 pages (72.5K message + 7K attachment + 3.3K person), 195,158 chunks, 100% embed coverage

## Summary

`gbrain apply-migrations --yes` ran the v0.11.0 → v0.13.1 cascade after a `--force-retry 0.11.0` to clear a wedged minions-migration marker. Migrations v0.11.0, v0.12.0, v0.12.2, and v0.13.0 completed cleanly (v0.12.0 created 8,610 new links + 72,518 timeline entries in ~30s; v0.13.0 added 0 new links). v0.13.1 hung indefinitely after writing 4,223/82,829 pages.

The hang is a CPU-bound spin in `bun`, not a slow operation: process held 95% CPU at 252MB RAM with zero disk I/O for 70+ minutes after the rollback log stopped advancing. Killing bun and restoring from a pre-migration PGLite snapshot recovered the brain to a clean state.

## Repro

1. Install gbrain v0.35.0.0 against a PGLite brain large enough that v0.12.0's auto-extract has measurable cost (this repro has 82K pages, 195K chunks, 100% embedded).
2. Get a `minions_migration` wedge for v0.11.0 (3+ consecutive `status: "partial"` ledger entries).
3. `gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry 0.11.0`
4. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`
5. Observe: cascade runs through v0.11.0 / v0.12.0 / v0.12.2 / v0.13.0 cleanly, then v0.13.1's `phaseCGrandfather` loop stops emitting work after ~4,223 pages while bun keeps burning CPU.

## Expected

Per the header comment at `src/commands/migrations/v0_13_1.ts:24` — "Scale: on a 30K-page brain, ~15s on Postgres, ~30s on PGLite. Batched in chunks of 100 with a commit per batch." Extrapolated linearly to 82K pages: ~80s on PGLite. Should complete in under two minutes.

## Actual

- Wall time at kill: **75 min** since v0.13.1 start
- Bun CPU time at kill: **4,290s** (95% utilization throughout)
- Rollback log size at kill: **4,223 entries** (last entry timestamped 3 minutes after v0.13.1 start; no writes since)
- Disk I/O on rollback log path at kill: **zero** (verified via `LastWriteTime`)
- Last 3 slugs in `~/.gbrain/migrations/v0_13_1-rollback.jsonl`:
  - `attachments/90/9072ae050a...`
  - `attachments/90/90748f9bea...`
  - `attachments/90/908b703e10...`
- Next slug alphabetically (DB-stored): `attachments/90/90990fbdcd7125cbb7378e49dc752f4345611dfe5b562e6a4a5b6ad90896c625` — a 1.1KB page with `type: attachment, file_type: ppt, parse_status: unsupported`. Body is the literal string `*(no extractable text — see parse status above)*`. Frontmatter is unremarkable YAML.

The page itself is not the problem. The hang is somewhere in the gbrain putPage path that this page triggers.

## Hypothesis

v0.13.1's `phaseCGrandfather` (`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_1.ts:117-159`) calls `engine.putPage(slug, { type, title, compiled_truth, timeline, frontmatter })` per page with no `noEmbed` semantics. On the markdown import path this routes through `importFromContent` (`src/core/import-file.ts`), which chunks the page and writes chunk rows. Per the chunk-upsert CASE expression at `pglite-engine.ts:1275-1296`, embeddings on changed bytes get set NULL — there's no embed call here directly, so this is probably not the embed gateway recursing.

The persistent `[ai.gateway] recipe "google" declares an embedding touchpoint without max_batch_tokens; recursion is the only safety net for batch caps.` warning emitted multiple times per migration is suspicious — if the `getPage` or `putPage` path eagerly resolves an AI-gateway recipe and the resolver itself has a recursion bug on a specific config shape, that would be a CPU-bound spin without disk I/O.

Alternatively: a regex in title/heading extraction has catastrophic backtracking on a specific character sequence in this attachment page. The body string contains an em-dash (`—`, U+2014) — worth ruling out as a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence that breaks a single-byte-assuming regex.

## Mitigation options for upstream

Listed in increasing order of invasiveness:

1. **Add `noEmbed: true` to v0.13.1's `putPage` call** (`src/commands/migrations/v0_13_1.ts:144-151`). Grandfather is just adding one frontmatter key; it shouldn't trigger any chunk-level work. Whether or not embed is the actual hang source, decoupling migration writes from the embed/chunk pipeline is the right fix for migrations that only mutate frontmatter.
2. **Per-page timeout in phaseCGrandfather**. The orchestrator currently has no per-page time bound — one stuck page wedges the whole migration. A 5s budget per page with a `failures.push` on timeout would let the cascade complete and surface the bad slug for manual triage.
3. **Investigate ai.gateway "google" recipe recursion**. The warning is emitted from a code path with comment text "recursion is the only safety net for batch caps". If a specific page can blow the recursion stack, that's an unrelated bug worth fixing regardless of the migration interaction.

## Workaround for affected users (no upstream change required)

1. Snapshot `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` before attempting the cascade.
2. Pre-build a skip list of `attachments/<sha-prefix>/<sha>` slugs that might trigger the hang. Lacking a clean way to identify them in advance, the practical move is to run a dry-run of v0.13.1 first to identify the slug-set, then quarantine known-large or known-pathological attachments via a SQL `UPDATE pages SET frontmatter = jsonb_set(frontmatter, '{validate}', 'false') WHERE slug = ...` BEFORE the migration, so phaseCGrandfather's idempotency check skips them.
3. Or: patch v0.13.1 locally to add the `noEmbed: true` hint (option 1 above) and rebuild gbrain.

**Important caveat about `scripts/gbrain-snapshot.ps1`**: this snapshot script does NOT capture `~/.gbrain/migrations/`. After restoring from a snapshot taken before a partial migration, manually:
- Truncate `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl` to remove the post-snapshot "complete" lines (otherwise the runner skips already-claimed-complete migrations whose DB effects no longer exist).
- Delete `~/.gbrain/migrations/v0_13_1-rollback.jsonl` if present.

Extending the snapshot script to include `~/.gbrain/migrations/` is a separate workspace-side TODO.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.35.0.0 (commit `baf1a47798cb145d00bfce4fa94f85a94c8d7e07`)
- Bun (whatever ships in the v0.35.0.0 binary)
- PGLite (single-user local; no Postgres backend)
- Windows 11 Enterprise 26200, 64GB RAM
- Brain: 82,829 pages / 195,158 chunks / 100% embed coverage / 135,980 links pre-cascade
- Page-type distribution: 72,526 message / 6,998 attachment / 3,296 person / 11 misc

## Evidence artifacts (kept locally; can be uploaded on request)

- Full stdout of the failed `apply-migrations --yes` run (~370 lines)
- `~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl.bak-pre-cleanup-20260526` (pre-truncate ledger)
- `~/.gbrain/migrations/v0_13_1-rollback.jsonl.deleted-20260526` (4,223-entry rollback log)
- PGLite snapshot taken before the attempt (9.4GB), retained for forensics
- The suspect attachment page on disk: `C:\Users\rwo3\.gbrain-brain\attachments\90\90990fbdcd7125cbb7378e49dc752f4345611dfe5b562e6a4a5b6ad90896c625.md` (1.1KB)

title: fix(lint): preserve shared Postgres connection during config lift
body:
## Summary

Use an instance-owned Postgres pool for lint's temporary DB-backed config lift.

## Problem

`runLintCore()` can open a short-lived engine to read DB-backed content-sanity
config. On Postgres, that temporary engine was using the module-level singleton
connection and disconnecting it on cleanup.

In long-running workflows that share a `PostgresEngine` instance, this could
tear down the caller's connection mid-run.

Observed downstream symptom:
- `gbrain dream` reached later phases and then failed with
  `No database connection: connect() has not been called`

## Fix

- connect the temporary lint probe engine with `poolSize: 1`
- keep the connection instance-owned so cleanup cannot clobber the shared
  module-level singleton

## Tests

- add E2E regression coverage proving `runLintCore()` does not disconnect a
  shared `PostgresEngine`

title: fix(gateway): accept explicit litellm embedding model ids
body:
## Summary

Do not reject `litellm:<model>` embedding configs when the model id is already
explicitly present.

## Problem

Embedding preflight treated LiteLLM's empty allowlist as equivalent to
"no model specified", even when the configured embedding model already had a
concrete suffix like `litellm:bge-m3-emb`.

That caused embedding preflight to fail with the user-provided-model-unset
diagnosis even though the configuration was valid.

## Fix

- keep the user-provided-model guard
- only fire it when the parsed model id is actually empty
- allow explicit `provider:model` strings through

## Tests

- add regression coverage for `litellm:bge-m3-emb`

title: fix: harden source-scoped dream cycle
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens source-scoped `gbrain dream` runs and cleans up several doctor/integrity false positives found while exercising multi-source cycle dry-runs.

Changes:

- default `gbrain dream --source <id>` to the selected source's `local_path` when `--dir` is not provided
- isolate lint's DB-backed content-sanity probe so lint-as-a-library does not connect/disconnect a caller-owned engine
- treat `conversation_facts_backfill` as optional/non-fatal while preserving abort/cancel propagation
- release cycle locks reliably on error paths
- scope the v0.32.2 legacy-facts migration dirty-source check to sources that actually need fence writes
- register dynamically imported onboard doctor checks in doctor categories
- avoid integrity/frontmatter false positives for `X-*` API headers and Docusaurus `index.md(x)` `slug: /` routing metadata

## Why

Source-scoped cycle runs can otherwise fail late with `No database connection: connect() has not been called` after lint probes DB config, and some healthy repos can report doctor warnings from framework routing metadata or API/header prose rather than actual GBrain data issues.

## Testing

- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`
- `bun test test/dream-cli-flags.test.ts test/integrity.test.ts test/migrations-v0_32_2.test.ts test/extract-conversation-facts.test.ts`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run verify`

## Notes

This keeps `conversation_facts_backfill` optional, but does not swallow abort/cancel signals. Abort still propagates so a canceled cycle is not marked fresh.

title: dream synthesize writes synthesized pages to 'default' source, ignoring the resolved brain source
body:
## Summary

`gbrain dream --phase synthesize --dir <brain-dir>` writes the synthesized
reflection/idea pages to the `default` source, even when `<brain-dir>` is a
registered source (its `.gbrain-source` dotfile names the source id). Result:
persistent `multi_source_drift` warnings in `doctor`, and the named source's
`last_sync` never advances ("stale" forever).

## Root cause

In `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts`, `collectChildPutPageSlugs()` (~L870)
hardcodes `source_id: 'default'` for all subagent-written pages. The comment at
L849-854 acknowledges this is a known gap:

> Subagent put_page tool schema doesn't expose source_id (subagents are scoped
> to a single source); default to 'default' for the current dream-cycle product
> behavior. Threading the source_id through reverseWriteRefs guarantees getPage
> targets the correct (source, slug) row...

So the `brain_put_page` write path never honors the resolved source from the
6-tier `resolveSourceId` chain (`--source` / `GBRAIN_SOURCE` / `.gbrain-source`
/ path-match / brain-default / 'default').

## Impact

- `doctor` → `multi_source_drift`: pages live at `default` but their intended
  source is the named brain source.
- `doctor` → `sync_freshness`: the named source is flagged stale forever,
  because dream writes land in `default` and never advance the source's sync.
- Workaround forces operators to `git commit && gbrain sync --source <id>` to
  re-home the pages, which leaves duplicate copies (one in `default`, one in the
  named source). Search dedupes by slug so retrieval is unaffected, but
  `page_count` / `chunk_count` inflate.

## Repro

1. `gbrain sources add mybrain --path ~/mybrain` (so `~/mybrain/.gbrain-source`
   = `mybrain`)
2. `gbrain dream --phase synthesize --dir ~/mybrain`
3. `gbrain doctor` → `multi_source_drift` lists the new reflection/idea pages as
   intended=`mybrain` but present at `default`.

## Suggested fix

Thread the resolved sourceId into the subagent put_page write path and through
`collectChildPutPageSlugs` / `reverseWriteRefs`, so synthesized pages are
attributed to the correct source at write time instead of the hardcoded
`'default'`.

## Env

gbrain 0.35.8.0, postgres engine, multi-source setup (multiple federated
sources).

title: v0.18.2: `sync --source <id>` doesn't tag imported pages — they fall back to schema default `source_id='default'`
body:
## Summary

In gbrain v0.18.2, running `gbrain sync --repo <path> --source <id>` correctly resolves and stores the `--source` value as a sync anchor, but the imported page rows themselves end up with `source_id = 'default'` instead of the requested source id. The multi-source registration (`gbrain sources add/list/attach`) and the schema (`pages.source_id`) are wired up correctly — only the sync → import call drops the source id.

## Affected version

- gbrain `0.18.2` (`gbrain check-update --json` reports no newer release as of 2026-05-28)
- macOS 26.3 (Darwin 25.3.0), PGLite engine

## Root cause (in this repo's source)

1. `src/core/pglite-schema.ts:46` — `pages.source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'`. The column exists, the default is `'default'`. ✓
2. `src/commands/sync.ts:545-555` — `runSync` resolves the flag correctly:
   ```ts
   const explicitSource = args.find((a, i) => args[i - 1] === '--source') || null;
   let sourceId: string | undefined = undefined;
   if (explicitSource || process.env.GBRAIN_SOURCE) {
     const { resolveSourceId } = await import('../core/source-resolver.ts');
     sourceId = await resolveSourceId(engine, explicitSource);
   }
   ...
   const opts: SyncOpts = { repoPath, dryRun, full, noPull, noEmbed, skipFailed, retryFailed, sourceId };
   ```
   `opts.sourceId` is populated. ✓
3. `src/core/import-file.ts` — `importFromFile()` and `importFromContent()` only accept `{ noEmbed?: boolean }`:
   ```ts
   export async function importFromContent(engine, slug, content, opts: { noEmbed?: boolean } = {}): Promise<ImportResult>
   export async function importFromFile(engine, filePath, relativePath, opts: { noEmbed?: boolean } = {}): Promise<ImportResult>
   ```
   They never receive `sourceId`, so the page INSERT statement omits the column, and the schema default `'default'` kicks in. ✗

`opts.sourceId` from `SyncOpts` ends up reaching `readSyncAnchor` / `writeSyncAnchor` (so per-source `last_commit` works), but never the page-insert path.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Fresh PGLite brain, no pages
gbrain sources add personal-brain --path ~/dev/personal-brain --federated
gbrain sources add tesseract     --path ~/dev/tesseract     --no-federated
gbrain sync --repo ~/dev/personal-brain --source personal-brain
gbrain sources list
```

### Observed

```
SOURCES
───────
  default            federated   6 pages  never synced
  personal-brain     federated   0 pages  last sync 2026-05-28T07:41:14Z
                     ~/dev/personal-brain
  tesseract          isolated    0 pages  never synced
                     ~/dev/tesseract
```

The 6 imported pages live under `source_id = 'default'`. The `personal-brain` source's `last_commit` anchor updates correctly, but page count remains 0.

### Expected

```
SOURCES
───────
  default            federated   0 pages  never synced
  personal-brain     federated   6 pages  last sync 2026-05-28T07:41:14Z
                     ~/dev/personal-brain
  ...
```

All 6 imported pages should have `source_id = 'personal-brain'`.

## Why this matters

The v0.18.0 sources work is a major capability: federated vs isolated sources, kebab-context-style `attach`, per-source default search. With this gap, sources only function as labels for sync state, not for the pages themselves — so federation/isolation semantics silently don't apply to actual page data. Multi-source brains end up with all pages in `'default'` regardless of which `--source` was passed.

Two concrete downstream consequences observed:

1. **Federation/isolation broken in practice.** `gbrain query "..."` returns hits regardless of source attribution because all hits live in `'default'` (which is federated). An `--no-federated` source can't actually hide its pages from default search because no pages are actually attributed to it.
2. **Slug collision risk.** With `pages_source_slug_key UNIQUE (source_id, slug)`, syncing a second repo (e.g. one that also has a top-level `readme`) collides on `('default', 'readme')` instead of creating two distinct `(personal-brain, readme)` and `(tesseract, readme)` rows.

## Suggested fix

Thread `sourceId` from `SyncOpts` through to the import path:

1. Widen the `importFromFile` / `importFromContent` options:
   ```ts
   opts: { noEmbed?: boolean; sourceId?: string } = {}
   ```
2. Default `sourceId` to `'default'` inside the import functions, then include it in the page INSERT (both `pglite-engine.ts` and `postgres-engine.ts` paths).
3. In `runSync`, pass `sourceId: opts.sourceId` into the import call.
4. Add a test asserting `pages.source_id === '<requested source>'` after `sync --source <requested>`.
5. Backfill helper: a one-shot command (or migration) to move existing pages from `'default'` to a target `sourceId` for users who already ran a v0.18.x sync against the wrong source. Otherwise upgraders will silently keep their pages mis-attributed until they re-sync.

Happy to send a PR for items 1-4 if useful.

## Workaround for users until fixed

- Don't rely on the sources subsystem for actual page isolation in v0.18.x.
- Use a single `'default'` source and namespace pages by directory prefix (`personal/...`, `deals/...`) until the fix lands.

Filed from a setup where personal-brain (federated) and tesseract-ventures (isolated) were configured and only personal-brain was synced; the report above is from the live state.

title: v0.41.28.0 feat(auth): grant-read / revoke-read / set-federated-read / list-clients (atomic SQL race-safe)
body:
## Summary

Four new CLI subcommands close the visibility + manageability gap on
OAuth client `federated_read` scope. Before this PR, the only way to
inspect or change "who can read which source" on a multi-source brain
was raw SQL against `oauth_clients.federated_read`.

**New surface:**

```bash
gbrain auth list-clients [--json] [--include-deleted]
gbrain auth grant-read <client> <source> [--dry-run]
gbrain auth revoke-read <client> <source> [--dry-run]
gbrain auth set-federated-read <client> "s1,s2" [--dry-run]
```

All four resolve by friendly name (the one you passed to `register-client`)
OR full `client_id`, default-hide soft-deleted clients, and validate
source ids at the boundary (so a typo can't silently land a malformed
entry in the array).

**Commits:**
1. `feat(auth): federated_read CLI commands + atomic SQL race-safety` — substantive change (CLI surface + helpers + tests).
2. `chore: bump version and changelog (v0.41.28.0)` — release metadata.

## Pre-Landing Review

Codex pre-merge review caught 1 HIGH + 4 MEDIUM findings on the first draft; all in-scope ones fixed in this PR before push.

1. **HIGH — concurrent grant/revoke race could silently restore revoked access.** Read-modify-write let racing `revoke-read X` + `grant-read Y` clobber the revoke. Fixed via atomic SQL (`array_append` / `array_remove` + NOT/ANY guard + `deleted_at IS NULL` guard + `RETURNING`). Postgres serializes both UPDATEs at the row lock.
2. **MEDIUM — soft-deleted clients still mutable.** `resolveClient` + `listClients` default-filter `deleted_at IS NULL`; mutating commands have no escape hatch.
3. **MEDIUM — source-id shape not validated.** `assertSourceExists` now calls `assertValidSourceId` before the DB existence query.
4. **MEDIUM — `register-client` seeds malformed entries.** `parseRegisterClientArgs` now validates `--source` + `--federated-read` element shape at the CLI boundary.
5. **LOW — terminal control-char injection.** New `sanitizeForTerminal` escapes ALL C0/C1/DEL bytes (including `\n` and `\t`) in human output. Applied to `printOutcome`, `listClients`, and `revokeClient` success message.

**Deferred (filed in `TODOS.md` as v0.41.28.0 follow-ups):**
- `TODO-FR-A (P2)`: no FK on `oauth_clients.federated_read` array — needs schema migration (join table).
- `TODO-FR-B (P3)`: admin `POST /admin/api/update-client-ttl` skips `deleted_at` filter — small follow-up patch.

## Test Coverage

72 cases across two test files (67 new + 3 extending an existing file):

- pure helpers: `parseSourceCsv`, `extractDryRun`, `sanitizeForTerminal`
- DB-coupled: `resolveClient` + soft-delete filter, `assertSourceExists` + shape validation
- Core fns: `grantReadCore`, `revokeReadCore`, `setFederatedReadCore` — idempotency, race-safety (the `grant+revoke serialize at row-lock` regression test), dry-run semantics, error paths
- `parseRegisterClientArgs` — `--source` + `--federated-read` shape validation + canonical case regression

All tests use the canonical PGLite block from CLAUDE.md test-isolation rules.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: **CLEAN.** Stated intent: "add CLI for federation management". Delivered exactly that + in-scope hardening from the adversarial review. No expansion into unrelated areas.

## Documentation

No external docs reference `federated_read` management (the commands didn't exist before). Help text in `gbrain auth` lists all four new subcommands. CHANGELOG entry carries the user-facing story (ELI10 lead + numbers table + caveats + "what we caught" section per CLAUDE.md voice rules).

## Test plan

- [x] All 72 unit tests pass (`bun test test/auth-federated-read.test.ts test/auth-register-client-args.test.ts`)
- [x] 98 adjacent oauth tests still pass (`bun test test/oauth.test.ts test/oauth-confidential-client.test.ts`)
- [x] Typecheck clean (`bun run typecheck`)
- [x] Full verify gate passes (`bun run verify` — 28/28 checks green)
- [x] Live-fire against a multi-user gbrain deployment:
  - `gbrain auth list-clients` — prints registered clients with scope details
  - `gbrain auth grant-read <client> <source>` → "Did grant"; verified in DB
  - Re-running the same grant → "No change: already reads"
  - `--dry-run` variant → "[dry-run] Would grant"; DB unchanged
  - Malformed source id → exit 1, "Invalid source_id" with paste-ready hint

## Note for the maintainer

Submitting from a fork since I only have read access on the upstream repo. Branch was developed while resolving a real "I need to add a new source and share it with multiple teammates" question on a self-hosted gbrain; the CLI commands were exactly the missing surface that turned a multi-line SQL task into a one-second operator command. Built + tested + reviewed in one session.

title: fix: refresh sync freshness on no-op sync
body:
## Problem
Kayako GBrain maintainer refreshes could finish successfully and still leave `doctor` reporting `sync_freshness=fail` for the `kayako` source.

## Root Cause
`checkSyncFreshness()` reads only `sources.last_sync_at`, but `performSyncInner()` returned early with `status: 'up_to_date'` whenever `last_commit === HEAD`. That fast path skipped the metadata updates that happen on other successful sync paths, so a no-op refresh never advanced `last_sync_at`.

## Change Summary
- refresh `last_sync_at`, `sync.last_run`, `repo_path`, and `chunker_version` on the no-op `up_to_date` sync path
- add a regression that forces `last_sync_at` stale, verifies `doctor` fails, runs a no-op source sync, and verifies freshness returns to `ok`

## Verification
- `/paperclip/gbrain/bun/bin/bun test test/sync.test.ts -t "source-scoped no-op sync refreshes last_sync_at so doctor stops reporting stale freshness"`

## Risk
Low. The change only touches the already-successful no-op sync fast path and makes its bookkeeping match the existing successful sync branches.

## Paperclip
- Issue: KAY-790

title: fix(retry): reconnect engine pool in batchRetry onRetry — singleton-null repair
body:
## Problem

[#1416](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1416) added `"No database connection"` to `retry-matcher.ts`'s retryable patterns, but the retry path never re-establishes the connection pool. When `engine.disconnect()` runs mid-cycle (for example between dream phases, or via `connection-manager` lifecycle), the module-level singleton in `db.ts` goes null; the in-flight batch flunks with `"No database connection: connect() has not been called."`, `withRetry` faithfully fires 3/3 retries against the same null singleton, and the batch is **silently lost**.

### Live repro

`gbrain dream` on v0.41.26.0 against direct Postgres (not Supavisor):

```
[extract.timeline_fs] 706/706 (100%)
[extract.timeline_fs] connection blip, retrying (attempt 1/3): No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
[extract.timeline_fs] connection blip, retrying (attempt 2/3): No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
[extract.timeline_fs] connection blip, retrying (attempt 3/3): No database connection: connect() has not been called. Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url <connection_string>
  batch error (13 timeline rows lost): No database connection: connect() has not been called.
[extract.timeline_fs] 706/706 (100%) done
Timeline: created 0 entries from 706 pages
```

Downstream doctor symptoms:

```
[FAIL] batch_retry_health: 192 exhausted batch retries in last 24h
       (worst: extract.links_fs = 174). Sustained circuit-breaker incident.
[FAIL] cycle_freshness: Source 'default' has never completed a full cycle.
```

The `cycle_freshness` FAIL is a downstream effect: a later phase (`conversation_facts_backfill`) hits the dead singleton via `engine.getConfig()` and aborts the cycle.

### Root cause

Three load-bearing facts confirmed in source:

- `retry-matcher.ts:23-27` matches `/No database connection/i` and adds the typed `problem === 'No database connection'` branch — explicitly cited as the [#1416](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1416) follow-up.
- `postgres-engine.ts:batchRetry` `onRetry` only logs + audits — no reconnect path.
- `postgres-engine.ts:reconnect()` already exists and is exactly what's needed; it's invoked from `minions/supervisor.ts:600` but not from the retry path. `_savedConfig` is preserved at `postgres-engine.ts:95` for this purpose.
- Bonus: `retry.ts:withRetry` calls `opts.onRetry?.(...)` **without `await`**, so an async repair callback would race the next attempt regardless.

## Fix

Two-file change. ~92 lines including tests.

### `src/core/retry.ts`

Widen `WithRetryOpts.onRetry` to allow `Promise<void>` and `await` the call in `withRetry`. The old fire-and-forget call meant async pre-retry repair work (e.g. `engine.reconnect()`) could not run atomically with the retry. Sync callers are unaffected — `await undefined` resolves immediately.

### `src/core/postgres-engine.ts`

In `batchRetry`'s `onRetry`, call `this.reconnect()` before the next attempt sleeps. Mirrors the supervisor pool-restart pattern. `engine.reconnect()` no-ops when `_savedConfig` is null (module-singleton mode without a saved engine config), so the call is defensively safe. `withRetry` only invokes `onRetry` after `isRetryableConnError` matches, so every `onRetry` call is for a connection-class error where reconnect is the right repair.

```diff
   onRetry: async (attempt, err) => {
     // ... existing audit + log ...
+    try {
+      await this.reconnect();
+    } catch (reconnectErr) {
+      process.stderr.write(
+        `[${auditSite}] reconnect failed (will retry against existing pool): ${(reconnectErr as Error).message}\n`,
+      );
+    }
   },
```

## Tests

In `test/core/retry.test.ts`:

- **`async onRetry is awaited before the next attempt`** — pins the contract `batchRetry` now depends on. Asserts event ordering across an async `onRetry` with a microtask boundary; without the `await` patch the assertion would break.
- **`async onRetry that throws does not crash withRetry`** — pins the best-effort repair contract: a throwing reconnect surfaces visibly rather than being swallowed.

```
$ bun test test/core/retry.test.ts
 39 pass, 0 fail, 194 expect() calls

$ bun test test/core/retry.test.ts test/core/retry-stress.slow.test.ts test/retry-matcher.test.ts test/connection-resilience.test.ts test/doctor-batch-retry.test.ts
 94 pass, 0 fail

$ bun run typecheck
$ tsc --noEmit   # clean
```

Full `bun test` run also clean against this branch (the two `pglite-engine.test.ts > Stats & Health` failures repro on `origin/master` without these changes — pre-existing, unrelated).

## Scope of this PR

Intentionally narrow — only the batch path. The non-batch path (`conversation_facts_backfill`'s direct `engine.getConfig()` call) has the same root cause but a different fix shape (likely `engine.ensureConnected()` at phase start, or wrapping `getConfig` itself in withRetry). Happy to follow up in a second PR if this direction is approved.

## Risk

- `await opts.onRetry?.(...)` adds at most one event-loop tick per retry. No throughput impact on the common case.
- `this.reconnect()` is already exercised in production by the supervisor path. Calling it on every connection-class retry adds pool churn on a real connection blip but eliminates the pathological case of N retries against a dead pool. Net win.
- `reconnect()` is `_reconnecting`-guarded so concurrent retries collapse into a single re-init.

## Why not just block the `disconnect()` call?

Considered. `engine.disconnect()` mid-cycle is intentional in some lifecycle paths (Astra autopilot between phases, test teardown reuse, etc.) and the existing `_connectionStyle === 'module'` guard already prevents accidental clobbering between engines. Removing legitimate disconnects to paper over the retry-path gap moves the bug, doesn't fix it. The retry path is the right place to be resilient — that's what `retry-matcher`'s `"No database connection"` entry already implies the design intends.

title: Dream synthesize: hardcoded 30-min subagent timeout silently drops transcripts
body:
# Dream synthesize: hardcoded 30-min subagent timeout fails on dense session transcripts

## Summary

`gbrain dream --phase synthesize` consistently fails with `wall-clock timeout exceeded` on transcripts that exceed ~20k tokens, even when the subagent is making valid progress. The 30-minute per-chunk timeout is **hardcoded as a literal** in `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts` (line 481) rather than being exposed as a config knob, so users cannot raise it without forking.

## Environment

- gbrain: v0.41.14.0 (Bun global install)
- Engine: Supabase (PostgreSQL 17.6, pgvector, transaction pooler @ port 6543)
- macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.14
- Embedding: `openai:text-embedding-3-small` (1536d)
- Subagent model: `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`

## Reproduction

1. Configure `dream.synthesize.session_corpus_dir` to a directory of `.txt` transcripts, where each transcript is a dense Telegram/chat-style log (~20k–50k tokens).
2. Run `gbrain dream --dir <brain> --phase synthesize --json`.
3. Watch jobs queue as `subagent` rows; each gets the hardcoded `timeout_ms: 30 * 60 * 1000`.
4. Every job runs to wall-clock timeout, retries 3x, ends `dead`. Zero `wiki/personal/reflections/*` pages get written.

In my run, 6/6 worthwhile transcripts (per the verdict pass) hit `wall-clock timeout exceeded` on all 3 attempts.

## Relevant code

`src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts:481`
```ts
const submitOpts: Partial<MinionJobInput> = {
  max_stalled: 3,
  on_child_fail: 'continue',
  idempotency_key,
  timeout_ms: 30 * 60 * 1000, // 30 min per chunk    <-- hardcoded literal
};
```

`src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts:502`
```ts
const job = await waitForCompletion(queue, jobId, {
  timeoutMs: 35 * 60 * 1000,                          <-- also hardcoded
  pollMs: 5 * 1000,
});
```

Attempting `gbrain config set subagent.timeout_ms 600000` returns `[config] No similar known key`, confirming there is no published override path.

## Why 30 min is not enough for some users

The subagent is allowed `max_turns: 30`. With ~25k–50k input tokens per transcript:
- Sonnet spends most turns on `search` + `get_page` exploring existing brain content before calling `put_page` (the prompt mandates wikilink discovery first).
- Each tool round-trip can be 30–90 sec on Anthropic.
- A 25–30 turn read-heavy session can legitimately blow past 30 min wall-clock even when the subagent is making real progress.

The result is **silent data loss**: the verdict pass identifies worthwhile transcripts, but the brain never receives the synthesized pages.

## Proposed fix

Promote both literals to config keys with sane defaults:

```ts
const submitTimeoutMs =
  Number(await engine.getConfig('dream.synthesize.subagent_timeout_ms')) ||
  30 * 60 * 1000;

const waitTimeoutMs =
  Number(await engine.getConfig('dream.synthesize.subagent_wait_timeout_ms')) ||
  35 * 60 * 1000;
```

Register both keys in the config schema validator so `gbrain config set …` accepts them without `--force`.

Optional follow-ups (lower priority):
- Surface `dream.synthesize.max_turns` (currently fixed at 30 inline in the synthesize prompt builder).
- Emit a structured event when a synthesize subagent is **terminated by timeout while still making tool calls** so operators can distinguish "timed out but progressing" from "stuck/looping".

## Workaround

Disable the phase entirely:
```bash
gbrain config set dream.synthesize.enabled false
```
…which loses the whole feature.

## Will to contribute

Happy to PR this if you want — straightforward 10-line patch + a unit test that asserts the override is honored. Tag me if you'd prefer it shipped under a different config namespace.

title: (fix) typo with alphaclaw.com url (should be alphaclaw.md)
fix(engine): module-singleton shared-ownership — joiner must not tear down shared pool
body:
## Problem

Companion to [#1593](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1593) — that PR repairs the batch-retry path so existing data loss stops. This PR fixes the **root cause**: a temp engine that joins the shared module-level singleton silently kills it for the whole cycle on `disconnect()`.

### Repro (full dream cycle on direct Postgres)

1. Cycle's main engine connects without `poolSize` → module path. `db.ts` singleton initialized; `_connectionStyle='module'`.
2. Lint phase's `resolveLintContentSanity` ([src/commands/lint.ts:298](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/src/commands/lint.ts)) creates a temp `PostgresEngine` to read 4 config keys, calls `engine.connect({})`.
3. `db.connect()` no-ops because singleton is already alive. Temp engine sets `_connectionStyle='module'` regardless — even though it did nothing.
4. Lint's `try/finally` calls `await engine.disconnect()` on the temp engine. **Pre-fix**: falls through to `db.disconnect()` because `_connectionStyle === 'module'` — and silently nulls the shared singleton for the rest of the cycle.
5. `sync`, `synthesize`, and `embed` phases that run AFTER lint flunk with `"No database connection: connect() has not been called."`

`extract` survives because [#1593](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1593)'s `batchRetry` `onRetry` calls `this.reconnect()` — but the non-batch phases have no such cushion.

### Live evidence

Traced `db.disconnect()` on a v0.41.26.0 install with a temporary stack-trace probe:

```
[DBG] db.disconnect called, sql=alive
Error
    at disconnect (db.ts:228)
    at disconnect (postgres-engine.ts:211)
    at resolveLintContentSanity (lint.ts:319)
    at async runLintCore (lint.ts:395)
    at async runPhaseLint (cycle.ts:676)
    at async runCycle (cycle.ts:1421)
```

The first `db.disconnect()` of the cycle comes from **lint**, not from anything the cycle author would expect.

## Fix

Track per-engine whether THIS instance actually initialized the singleton (`_ownsModuleSingleton`) by snapshotting `db.isConnected()` BEFORE calling `db.connect()`. Only the initializer is allowed to call `db.disconnect()` on cleanup. Joiners no-op — the CLI's main engine retains exclusive teardown rights.

### Two-file change

**`src/core/db.ts`** — export new helper `isConnected()`:

```typescript
export function isConnected(): boolean {
  return sql !== null;
}
```

**`src/core/postgres-engine.ts`** — track ownership in `connect()`, gate teardown in `disconnect()`:

```diff
+ private _ownsModuleSingleton = false;

  async connect(...) {
    ...
    } else {
+     const singletonWasLive = db.isConnected();
      await db.connect(config);
      this._connectionStyle = 'module';
+     this._ownsModuleSingleton = !singletonWasLive;
    }
  }

  async disconnect() {
    ...
    if (this._connectionStyle === 'module') {
+     if (this._ownsModuleSingleton) {
        await db.disconnect();
+     }
      this._connectionStyle = null;
+     this._ownsModuleSingleton = false;
    }
  }
```

## Tests

`test/postgres-engine-module-ownership.test.ts` pins the contract hermetically via `mock.module` on `db.ts`. Four cases:

- first engine initializes; joiner does NOT disconnect on cleanup
- `joiner.disconnect()` BEFORE `primary.disconnect()` leaves singleton alive (the exact lint-phase repro)
- `joiner.disconnect()` is idempotent
- solo engine round-trips correctly

```
$ bun test test/postgres-engine-module-ownership.test.ts
 4 pass, 0 fail, 16 expect() calls

$ bun test test/postgres-engine-module-ownership.test.ts test/engine-factory.test.ts \
          test/connection-resilience.test.ts test/connection-manager.serial.test.ts \
          test/core/retry.test.ts
 99 pass, 0 fail

$ bun run typecheck  # clean
```

## End-to-end verification

Deployed both PRs to the same install + ran `gbrain dream`:

**Before (master + nothing):**
```
✗ sync         sync phase failed
   [InternalError/UNKNOWN] No database connection: connect() has not been called.
✗ synthesize   synthesize phase failed
   [InternalError/SYNTH_PHASE_FAIL] No database connection: connect() has not been called.
✓ extract     285 link(s), 0 timeline entries  ← 13 rows lost in batch
```

**After (PR #1593 + this PR):**
```
✓ sync         +0 added, ~0 modified, -0 deleted
✓ synthesize   73 transcript(s) synthesized in 0.4s     ← drained the backlog
✓ extract      285 link(s), 37 timeline entries         ← full recovery
```

Zero `"No database connection"` in the log. The remaining `✗ embed` is an unrelated `OPENAI_API_KEY` config issue, not the singleton bug.

## Why ship both PRs

[#1593](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1593) and this PR are independently load-bearing:

- This PR alone — `batchRetry`'s pre-existing retry loop has no reconnect, so even though the singleton no longer dies mid-cycle, any **real** (non-leak) connection blip still loses batches. [#1593](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1593) is the defense-in-depth.
- [#1593](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/1593) alone — `extract` recovers, but `sync` and `synthesize` keep flunking on every cycle. This PR is the root-cause fix.

Either can land first; merging both gives a fully clean cycle.

## Risk

Minimal — the only behavior change is that **passive sharers** stop tearing down the shared pool. The CLI's main engine, autopilot's long-lived engine, and any first-connecting engine still teardown exactly as before. Second/third-connecting engines (lint's content-sanity, frontmatter audit, any future similar pattern) now correctly no-op on cleanup.

title: getConfig lacks retry protection on transient connection loss
Migration subprocess fails with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` on Windows + bun + Supabase pooler (reproducible across 3 weeks)
body:
# Migration subprocess fails with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` on Windows + bun + Supabase pooler (reproducible across 3 weeks)

## Summary

On Windows, `gbrain apply-migrations` consistently fails on migrations that spawn a child `gbrain init --migrate-only` subprocess. The **parent process** connects to Supabase fine (`gbrain doctor` runs the full 25-check pack with DB roundtrips), but the **spawned subprocess** dies with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` (or `spawnSync ETIMEDOUT` historically) before it can connect.

Result: schema gets stuck on the first migration that uses the spawn pattern (v0.12.0 / v0.13.0) and never advances. I'm stuck on `schema_version 44` while the binary is at v107.

Reproduced twice with different gbrain versions, 19 days apart — not a transient.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 (English locale, cp950 codepage)
- **Shell**: git-bash (MSYS) + occasionally cmd.exe
- **Bun**: 1.3.10 (30e609e0)
- **gbrain**: 0.41.26.0 (also reproduced on 0.13.0 in May)
- **DB engine**: Postgres (Supabase pooler, `aws-1-ap-southeast-2.pooler.supabase.com:6543`, `prepare=false`)
- **Install method**: `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain`

## Reproduce

```bash
# Parent process can connect fine
gbrain doctor --json | head     # ✅ runs 25 checks against Supabase
gbrain stats                    # ✅ reports page/chunk/embed counts

# But the orchestrator's subprocess can't
gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive
# → fails on the first migration that spawns `gbrain init --migrate-only`
```

## Observed (3 separate attempts across 3 weeks)

`~/.gbrain/migrations/completed.jsonl`:

```jsonl
{"ts":"2026-05-09T19:48:26.664Z","version":"0.12.0","status":"partial","phases":[
  {"name":"schema","status":"complete"},
  {"name":"backfill_links","status":"failed","detail":"spawnSync C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\cmd.exe ETIMEDOUT"},
  {"name":"backfill_timeline","status":"failed","detail":"spawnSync C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\cmd.exe ETIMEDOUT"}
]}
{"ts":"2026-05-09T19:51:20.251Z","version":"0.13.0","status":"partial","phases":[
  {"name":"schema","status":"failed","detail":"Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only"}
]}
{"ts":"2026-05-28T14:58:37.377Z","version":"0.12.0","status":"partial","phases":[
  {"name":"schema","status":"failed","detail":"Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only"}
]}
{"ts":"2026-05-28T15:05:27.621Z","version":"0.13.0","status":"partial","phases":[
  {"name":"schema","status":"failed","detail":"Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only"}
]}
```

CLI output during latest fail (5/28):

```
=== Applying migration v0.12.0: Knowledge Graph wires itself ===
[gbrain] Prepared statements disabled (PgBouncer transaction-mode convention on port 6543)
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND
Migration v0.12.0 reported status=failed.
```

Both failure modes (`ETIMEDOUT` and `ENOTFOUND`) are subprocess-spawned DNS / socket-level failures, not Postgres-level errors. That's the diagnostic tell: the connection string never resolves in the child.

## Diagnosis hypothesis

**The parent gbrain process resolves Supabase DNS fine** (doctor talks to Postgres mid-run). **The spawned subprocess (`spawnSync cmd.exe → gbrain init --migrate-only`) doesn't**.

Possible causes:

1. **Env not propagated to child**: `DATABASE_URL` / proxy / DNS-relevant env vars (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, custom resolver) read at module-load time in the parent but missing from the child's `process.env` snapshot under `spawnSync`. The bun+Windows spawn path might be using `env: {}` instead of `env: process.env` somewhere.
2. **Windows + bun + IPv6 fallback**: parent uses Node.js DNS resolver via long-lived connection; child does fresh `getaddrinfo` and hits a Windows IPv6/IPv4 fallback bug.
3. **cmd.exe wrapping**: the spawn goes through `cmd.exe /c gbrain ...` — if PATH gets reset by cmd, the child might find a different `gbrain` or fail to find network DLLs.

The fact that `spawnSync C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe ETIMEDOUT` literally names cmd.exe suggests the orchestrator is shelling out via cmd, not invoking bun/node directly.

## Suggested fixes (in order of leverage)

1. **Pass `env: process.env`** explicitly on every migration spawn site so child inherits the active connection string + proxy config.
2. **Invoke gbrain directly** via `bun.cmd <gbrain-cli.ts>` or call the migration phase function in-process instead of shelling out. The current shape (parent process → cmd.exe → gbrain init → bun runtime → reconnect to Postgres) is fragile on Windows; everything in-process would skip the bug class entirely.
3. **Surface the actual child stderr** — current error log says `Command failed: gbrain init --migrate-only` with no stack. The `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` line above came from a separate stderr line, not the orchestrator's captured error. Capturing + propagating the child's full stderr would have saved 3 weeks of debugging.

## Impact

I'm stuck on `schema_version 44`. Can't use anything from v0.31+ (hot memory, recall, who-knows-X, lens packs, voice agent, etc.). The CLI binary is at v0.41.26.0 — fully installed — but every new feature that touches a new column / table no-ops or errors.

Rolled back to v0.30.2 binary tonight to match `schema 44` so `gbrain sync` keeps working. Will retry the upgrade when the spawn issue is fixed.

Happy to test any patch on this machine.

— Charles (https://github.com/bockybocky)

title: v0.41.27.0 fix: withRetry self-heals on null singleton + facts:absorb drain + disconnect audit (closes #1570)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1570 — production loss of ~150 link rows per `gbrain dream` cycle on Supabase, plus silent `'No database connection'` errors after `gbrain capture`. Three small surgical commits + diagnostic instrumentation.

This is the **instrument-then-fix pivot** the codex outside-voice review recommended. The original plan proposed an architectural refactor (remove singleton nullability, rename `disconnect → shutdown`, ~30-50 file diff) — but it designed a refactor for a root cause never actually identified. v0.41.27.0 ships:

1. **Symptom fix (retry self-heals on null singleton)** — `withRetry` gains an opt-in `reconnect?: () => Promise<void>` callback awaited between the `isRetryableConnError` classification and the inter-attempt sleep. `PostgresEngine.batchRetry` injects `() => this.reconnect()` — race-safe via the existing `_reconnecting` guard, handles both module and instance pools. Closes the headline production loss: next attempt sees a live pool instead of the same null singleton.

2. **Facts queue drain (well-understood bug class)** — `FactsQueue.drainPending({timeout: 1000})` — new method distinct from `shutdown()`. Stops accepting new enqueues, awaits in-flight settle, bounded by timeout. `cli.ts` op-dispatch finally awaits the drain BEFORE `engine.disconnect()`. Mirrors the v0.41.8.0 `awaitPendingLastRetrievedWrites` pattern. Closes the silent `'No database connection'` tail-end errors when the fire-and-forget facts:absorb queue outlives the CLI process's connection lifetime.

3. **Diagnostic instrumentation (find the offender for v0.41.28+)** — `src/core/audit/db-disconnect-audit.ts` (NEW): every `db.disconnect()` and `PostgresEngine.disconnect()` call writes a JSONL audit record with engine_kind + connection_style + 6-frame caller stack + command + pid. `gbrain doctor`'s `batch_retry_health` check surfaces 24h disconnect count + most-recent caller. File: `~/.gbrain/audit/db-disconnect-YYYY-Www.jsonl` (ISO-week rotated, honors `GBRAIN_AUDIT_DIR`). v0.41.28+ will use this production data to identify the actual mid-process disconnect caller and apply a targeted ownership-boundary fix. The singleton-removal architectural plan is deferred per the same review — see TODOS.md.

## Version

`v0.41.27.0` — rebumped past two queue collisions: v0.41.25.0 (#1538 batched sync deletes) and v0.41.26.1 (#1572 lock-renewal cathedral) landed during this branch's review cycle.

## Test Coverage

| Surface | Tests | Status |
|---|---|---|
| retry-reconnect callback contract | 8 hermetic unit cases | NEW `test/core/retry-reconnect.test.ts` |

title: Docs/setup and ingest guide
fix(gateway): avoid Response.clone() in ZeroEntropy/Voyage embed shims (bun <1.1.27 truncation)
body:
Fixes #1610.

## Problem
`gbrain embed` fails with `[embed(zeroentropyai:zembed-1)] Invalid JSON response` for any page that produces **2 or more chunks**; single-chunk pages succeed. Same failure mode for the Voyage compat path. The ZeroEntropy API itself is fine — a direct `fetch` of the exact multi-input request returns HTTP 200 valid JSON (~124 KB for 5 chunks).

## Root cause
On **bun < 1.1.27**, `Response.clone()` truncates large in-progress streaming bodies (oven-sh/bun#6348, oven-sh/bun#4765; fixed in bun v1.1.27). Both `zeroEntropyCompatFetch` and `voyageCompatFetch` read the upstream response via `await resp.clone().json()`, so for responses with ≥2 embeddings the clone is truncated → `JSON.parse` throws `Unexpected end of JSON input` → the shim's `catch` silently `return resp` → the AI SDK reports `Invalid JSON response`. Single-result responses (~25 KB) stay under the truncation threshold, which is why it looks intermittent / size-dependent.

Confirmed by logging the shim's catch:
```
[ZEDBG] catch: Unexpected end of JSON input | name: SyntaxError
```

## Fix
Read the body directly (`await resp.json()`) instead of cloning, in both compat shims (3 call sites). Also drop the now-stale `content-length` / `content-encoding` / `transfer-encoding` headers when returning the rewritten body, since its length differs from the original.

Minimal, surgical change (verified: after this, all previously-failing multi-chunk pages embed successfully and a full brain reaches 100% coverage).

## Note
This change leaves the existing `if (!modified) return resp;` / `catch { return resp; }` fallback paths as-is. For ZeroEntropy/Voyage these are unreachable (a `results[]` array is always present, and `JSON.parse` no longer fails once the body isn't truncated), so they don't return a consumed body in practice. If you'd prefer fully-defensive fallbacks, I'm happy to read the body once into a local and reuse it across all return paths — just say the word.

## Test environment
gbrain 0.41.27.0 (also repros on 0.41.26.x), bun 1.0.36, macOS (Apple M1 / arm64). The bug is architecture-independent.

title: Docs: DEPLOY.md contradicts localOnly remote availability
body:
Thank you for maintaining gbrain. I noticed a small docs mismatch around the MCP trust boundary.

In `docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md`, the `Scopes and localOnly` section says these operations are rejected over HTTP regardless of scope:

- `sync_brain`
- `file_upload`
- `file_list`
- `file_url`

That matches `src/commands/serve-http.ts`, where HTTP MCP tools are built from `operations.filter(op => !op.localOnly)`. It also matches `docs/mcp/CHATGPT.md`, which says the same four operations are rejected over HTTP.

Later in `docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md`, the `Operations` section says all operations are available remotely, including `sync_brain` and `file_upload`, and describes remote `file_upload` confinement. That looks stale relative to the current HTTP behavior.

Suggested fix: update or remove the later `Operations` paragraph so it says HTTP remote clients do not see `localOnly` operations, and point local users to stdio or CLI for those local filesystem surfaces.

I did not open a PR because I wanted to confirm the intended docs wording first, but this looks like a documentation-only correction.

title: fix(conversation-parser): add bold-name-no-timestamp builtin (Circleback/Granola/Zoom)
body:
## Problem

gbrain's conversation parser ships 13 builtin patterns in `src/core/conversation-parser/builtins.ts` — **every one requires a per-line timestamp** (an inline date or a time anchor like `(HH:MM)` / `[HH:MM]`).

Modern meeting-transcription tools — **Circleback, Granola, Zoom** — emit transcripts as `**Speaker Name:** message text` with **no per-line timestamp**:

```
**Garry Tan:** Okay, start on. And then weirdly like zoom doesn't...
**Participant 2:** he tried to reset it remotely the other night. Let me ask him.
**Garry Tan:** I mean it's really just like we need to get zoom to fix this.
**Participant 2:** Okay, let me.
```

With no time anchor, this shape matches no builtin. A single accidental anchor on a long page scores ~`0.002`, well below the `SCORING_MIN_ACCEPTANCE` gate of `0.05` in `parse.ts`, so the page parses to **0 messages** and extracts **zero conversation-facts**.

### Real-world impact

In a production brain, the coverage scan reported `conversation_format_coverage: 100% _no_match` — **104/104 conversation pages** plus **3,423 eligible pages** matched no builtin pattern and silently yielded nothing.

## The fix

New **additive** builtin `bold-name-no-time`:

- regex `/^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.*)$/` — captures the speaker **inside** the bold markers (`**Name:**`), message text in group 2.
- No time capture. `date_source: 'frontmatter'` with `hour_group` undefined routes through `parse.ts`'s existing no-time branch (the same convention as `irc-classic`), anchoring every message at `00:00:00` of the page's frontmatter date. **No wall-clock time is fabricated**; intra-day ordering is preserved by line order.
- Declared **after** the timestamped bold patterns (`imessage-slack`, `telegram-bracket`, `bold-paren-time`) so it can never shadow them. The scorer tie-breaks on declaration index, and the regex requires the colon **inside** the bold markers, so the `**Name** (time):` paren-time shape (colon outside) still matches `bold-paren-time`, not this pattern.

No existing pattern is modified.

## Tests

Added a dedicated `bold-name-no-time` test block in `test/conversation-parser/parse.test.ts`:
- parses the real 4-line `**Speaker:** text` sample → 4 messages with correct speaker/text, anchored at `00:00:00` of the frontmatter date;
- scores above the `0.05` acceptance floor on a pure bold-name transcript (epoch-default date when none supplied);
- **regression**: `**Garry** (HH:MM): text` still matches `bold-paren-time` (not the new pattern);
- **regression**: a pure `telegram-bracket` transcript still matches `telegram-bracket` (wins the score tie via lower declaration index).

Updated the existing `disabledBuiltinIds` test: disabling `telegram-bracket` now correctly falls through to `bold-name-no-time` (the bracket line's colon is inside the bold markers); disabling both yields the genuine `no_match`.

Full suite result:

```
bun test test/conversation-parser/ test/conversation-parser-cli.test.ts test/extract-conversation-facts.test.ts
131 pass / 134
```

The 3 failures are **pre-existing on master** and env-driven (`probeLlmAvailability returns null when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset` and two sibling "provider unavailable" fail-open tests) — they fail identically on clean `master` in this sandbox because an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is present in the environment. They are unrelated to this change. `eval-conversation-parser-cli` and `extract-conversation-facts-workers` are fully green (32/32). All 14 builtins (13 existing + new) pass their module-load `validatePatternEntry` checks and their `test_positive` parse loop.

---

### Separately noticed (not in this PR)

`doctor --source <id>` does **not** scope the `orphan_ratio` check. In `src/commands/doctor.ts` (~line 4559), `getOrphansData(engine, { includePseudo: false })` takes no source filter, so `--source default` still reports a brain-wide orphan ratio across all federated sources. Suggested follow-up: thread `sourceId` into `getOrphansData`. (Note only — intentionally not fixed here.)

title: fix(postgres): coerce timeline batch dates to text before unnest cast
body:
## Problem

`gbrain extract --from-meetings` silently writes **0 timeline entries** on the Postgres engine, even with hundreds of meetings and entity pages. `gbrain doctor` shows timeline coverage stuck at 0% with no error reported.

## Root cause

`PostgresEngine._addTimelineEntriesBatchOnce` builds the date array and binds it into an `unnest(...::text[])`:

```ts
const dates = entries.map(e => e.date);
// ...
unnest(${slugs}::text[], ${dates}::text[], ...)
```

On the Postgres engine, `effective_date` (the source of these dates in `extract-timeline-from-meetings.ts`) comes back as a **JS `Date`**. `postgres.js` then infers the array parameter as `timestamptz[]`, and the `::text[]` cast throws:

```
PostgresError: cannot cast type timestamp with time zone to text[]  (SQLSTATE 42846)
```

The whole batch fails. Because `extractTimelineFromMeetings`'s `flush()` swallows the batch error in a bare `catch {}`, the CLI cheerfully reports `timeline_entries_created: 0` and exits 0. Nothing surfaces.

This only bites the Postgres/Supabase engine (PGLite returns date strings, so the array binds as `text[]` and the cast is a no-op).

## Fix

Coerce non-string date values to `'YYYY-MM-DD'` before binding, so the array binds as `text[]`. String callers are unaffected, and the SQL already does `v.date::date`.

## Verification

On a Supabase brain with 307 meetings and 316 entity pages:

- **Before:** `timeline_entries_created: 0`, `timeline_entries` table empty, doctor timeline coverage 0%.
- **After:** `timeline_entries_created: 2561` across 260 entity pages; re-run is idempotent (0 new); doctor timeline coverage populated.

A 1-row batch and synthetic 50/200-row batches with **string** dates always succeeded — the only differing variable was the date *type* (Date vs string), which this patch normalizes.

## Suggested follow-up (not in this PR)

The bare `catch {}` in `extractTimelineFromMeetings`'s `flush()` masked this for a long time. Consider logging the swallowed batch error (or surfacing a non-fatal warning) so future write failures aren't invisible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix: auto-reconnect connection pool before batch retry
body:
## Problem

The `batchRetry` helper retries transient connection errors but never re-establishes the database connection between attempts. When the postgres.js pool drops (network blip, Supavisor circuit-breaker) or the module-level `db.sql` is nulled mid-cycle (`"No database connection: connect() has not been called"`), every retry fails with the same error and all rows in the batch are silently lost.

Observed in the wild: `extract.links_fs` reports `connection blip, retrying (1/3)... (2/3)... (3/3)` followed by `batch error (66 link rows lost): No database connection: connect() has not been called.`

## Fix

Two minimal changes:

1. **`PostgresEngine.batchRetry()`**: call `this.reconnect()` before each retry attempt. `reconnect()` already handles both instance-level and module-level connection styles, has its own `_reconnecting` mutex to prevent races, and no-ops if the pool is healthy.

2. **`withRetry` (`retry.ts`)**: `await` the `onRetry` callback so async reconnect operations complete before the inter-attempt delay starts. Non-async callbacks resolve immediately (backward-compatible interface change: `void | Promise<void>`).

## Testing

- ✅ `bun run build` — compiles cleanly
- ✅ `bun test test/core/retry.test.ts test/retry-matcher.test.ts` — all 52 tests pass
- ✅ `gbrain dream --phase extract --json` — cycle completes cleanly on 365-page brain

Closes #1603

title: docs: retrieval incident — vector search returns pages by their weakest chunk (RFC + fix menu + eval design)
body:
**Docs-only PR (no code).** Full incident writeup + boil-the-ocean fix menu + eval design for a brain-wide retrieval defect.

## TL;DR
Querying **"Greek amphitheater"** failed to confidently surface the page titled *"The Mingtang (明堂) — Indoor **Greek amphitheater**…"*, returning it at cosine **0.64** via a weak body chunk. The same page's **title chunk scores 0.9866** on a richer query — the embedding is fine, the retrieval aggregation is broken.

**Root cause:** `searchVector` (both postgres + pglite engines) returns top-k *chunks* with **no per-page max-pool**. A page is represented by whichever chunk survives the candidate cut, not its best chunk. The keyword path (`searchKeyword`) already does the correct `DISTINCT ON (slug) ORDER BY score DESC`. The vector path does not.

**Secondary:** `reranker_enabled` / `expansion` are a **no-op** on this query across all modes — suggesting the CLI default does not exercise the documented hybrid stack (RETRIEVAL.md claims 49.1 P@5 / 97.9 R@5). Doc/reality gap flagged.

## In the doc
- Incident narrative + reproduction with exact CLI output
- Code-level root cause with line refs (searchVector vs searchKeyword asymmetry, innerLimit, pglite parity)
- Boil-the-ocean fix menu: Tier 1 (per-page max-pool — the actual bug, ~1 day) → Tier 6 (graph-assisted named-entity recall)
- Eval design ("NamedThingBench") on the existing eval/code-retrieval harness + baseline→compare→gate: title-substring, generic-label→named-entity, alias/synonym, multi-chunk dilution, short-vs-rich pairs, hard negatives; Hit@1/3, MRR, nDCG@5, score calibration vs the 0.85 dedup threshold; CI gate + engine parity

## Recommendation
Ship Tier 1, **measure**, then decide Tiers 2–6 by data. No code in this PR by request — review the plan before implementation.

title: gbrain dream: extract phase silently drops all link/timeline batches when the module-singleton DB connection is null mid-cycle (retry-on-null can't recover)
body:
## Summary

On a Postgres (Supabase) brain-host running the nightly `gbrain dream` cycle, the `extract` phase reliably writes **zero** links and timeline entries:

```
[extract.links_fs] connection blip, retrying (attempt 1/3): No database connection: connect() has not been called.
[extract.links_fs] connection blip, retrying (attempt 2/3): No database connection: connect() has not been called.
[extract.links_fs] connection blip, retrying (attempt 3/3): No database connection: connect() has not been called.
  batch error (N link rows lost): No database connection: connect() has not been called.
Links: created 0 from 346 pages
Timeline: created 0 entries from 346 pages
```

The cycle's `sync` phase (earlier in the same process) works fine, and a separate `gbrain extract all` invocation (fresh process) writes the links correctly. So the brain repo + content are fine — the problem is the cycle's shared DB connection going null before the `extract` phase.

## What's certain

`PostgresEngine.sql` getter returns `this._sql ?? db.getConnection()`. For the module-style engine `gbrain dream` uses, `_sql` is null by design, so it falls through to `db.getConnection()` (`src/core/db.ts:151`), which throws `connect() has not been called` when the module singleton `sql` (`src/core/db.ts:7`) is null.

`addLinksBatch` → `batchRetry` → `withRetry` re-invokes `_addLinksBatchOnce`, which re-reads `const sql = this.sql` on **every** attempt. Since both `_sql` and the singleton are null, all 3 retries hit the identical error and the batch is dropped. The v0.41.19.0 / v0.41.2.1 retry work only recovers a *transient* pool drop where postgres.js reconnects the existing `sql` object — it structurally cannot recover a permanently-nulled singleton (retry-on-null re-reads the same null).

The extract phase also swallows the per-batch error and reports `created 0` rather than failing loudly (`src/commands/extract.ts`), so the cycle exits 0 and the data loss is silent.

## Likely trigger (hypothesis)

Within a single `gbrain dream` process there is no explicit `db.disconnect()` in the cycle subtree. The most plausible cause is the `synthesize` phase: it submits subagent jobs and `waitForCompletion`s on a separate `gbrain jobs work` process, leaving this process's DB connection idle for a long time; the pooler / postgres.js drops the idle connection and the singleton ends up null. The comment at `src/core/retry-matcher.ts:23-27` already names this exact shape ("engine.disconnect mid-cycle, or postgres.js's auto-recovery between queries").

## Proposed fix

**Reconnect-on-null**, not just retry-on-null: when the module singleton is null, `getConnection()` (or the batch writers) should call `db.connect(savedConfig)` to re-establish it before failing. `db.ts` would need to retain the last-used config; `postgres-engine.ts` already keeps `_savedConfig` for the instance path via `reconnect()`. Secondary: make extract batch failures fatal (or surface them in the cycle exit code) so total data loss isn't reported as `created 0` with exit 0.

## Workaround

Running each maintenance phase as its own short-lived process (the pattern in `docs/guides/cron-schedule.md`) sidesteps it — a fresh `gbrain extract all` gets a fresh module singleton that nothing disconnects for that process's lifetime.

## Environment

- gbrain 0.41.26.0
- Postgres engine (Supabase), session-mode pooler (`:5432`)
- Headless brain-host on Railway, nightly `gbrain dream --dir $REPO --pull`

Key files: `src/core/db.ts` (7, 151-160, 227-233), `src/core/postgres-engine.ts` (sql getter, `_addLinksBatchOnce`), `src/core/retry-matcher.ts` (14-28), `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts`, `src/commands/extract.ts`.

title: v0.41.29.0 feat(conversation-parser): bold-name-no-time builtin + fix(orphans): source-scoped orphan_ratio (supersedes #1613)
body:
Supersedes #1613 (re-homed from the fork so CI can run with secrets; real names scrubbed for the privacy rule; orphan_ratio `--source` scoping bundled in).

## What ships (two fixes, 3 bisect-friendly commits)

### 1. `bold-name-no-time` conversation parser builtin (the 14th)
Parses `**Speaker:** text` transcripts with **no per-line timestamp** — the shape Circleback / Granola / Zoom emit. Every prior builtin required a time anchor, so this shape matched nothing: a production brain had **104 conversation pages + 3,423 eligible pages** silently extracting zero conversation-facts. This is the unlock for whole-brain conversation-facts extraction.

- Messages anchor at `T00:00:00Z` of the frontmatter date (no fabricated wall-clock; line order preserves sequence), same convention as `irc-classic`.
- regex `/^\*\*(?!\[)(.+?):\*\*\s*(.*)$/`: the **colon-inside-bold** (not declaration order) prevents shadowing `bold-paren-time`; the `(?!\[)` lookahead rejects telegram-bracket `**[18:37] Name:**` so disabling telegram-bracket yields an honest `no_match` instead of `speaker="[18:37] Name"`.
- new optional `PatternEntry.score_full_body`: `**Label:** text` is a common prose idiom, so a notes page with bold labels **clustered in its first 10 lines** scored 0.3 on the head pass (NOT `< SCORING_HEAD_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD`, so the full-body fallback never fired) and cleared the 0.05 floor. `parse.ts` now recomputes the winner over the full body before the floor, so such a page stays `no_match`.
- scrubbed pre-existing real names from `bold-paren-time` test samples (privacy rule).

### 2. orphan_ratio / `find_orphans` source scoping
`gbrain doctor --source <id>` and `gbrain orphans --source <id>` now scope to that source instead of reporting brain-wide.

- `findOrphanPages(opts?: { sourceId?, sourceIds? })` on both engines scopes the candidate set (scalar `= $1` / federated `= ANY($1::text[])`). Cross-source inbound links still count, so a page in X linked from Y is reachable (not an orphan of X).
- **Corrected the `total_linkable` denominator**: excluded pages (templates/, scratch/) that have inbound links no longer inflate it and suppress warnings. Changes orphan_ratio output for every brain, in the accurate direction.
- The `find_orphans` MCP op threads `sourceScopeOpts(ctx)`, closing a cross-source read leak for source-bound OAuth clients (v0.34.1 source-isolation class).
- Under explicit `--source` below 100 entity pages, `orphan_ratio` reports the ratio with a low-scale caveat instead of a vacuous "ok". Thin-client `doctor --source` deferred (TODOS.md).

## Review
- `/plan-eng-review` (cleared) + `/codex` outside-voice (8 findings, 7 actioned + 1 confirmed-good). Codex caught the `score_full_body` floor gap, the bracket-timestamp mis-capture, the pre-existing denominator bug, and the find_orphans MCP leak.

title: reindex --markdown wipes DB-side tags that aren't in frontmatter (resets tags table to frontmatter-only)
body:
## Summary

Running `gbrain reindex --markdown` on a Postgres brain silently wiped the `tags` for many pages. After the reindex, pages that previously had tags return empty from `get_tags`:

- `people/xavi` → `[]`
- `projects/preparapp` → `[]`
- `concepts/yc-ai-native-principles` → `[]`

`SELECT count(DISTINCT tag) FROM tags` dropped from ~848 to ~100 over the reindex.

## Root cause (high confidence)

The wiped pages' **frontmatter does not contain those tags**. For example `projects/preparapp`'s frontmatter is `{home, github, status, former_name, canonical_name}` — no `tags:` field. Those tags came from DB-side enrichment (auto-tagging / dream synthesize / signal-detector writing to the `tags` table), not from the source `.md` frontmatter.

`reindex --markdown` re-imports each page (`importFromFile` / `importFromContent` with `forceRechunk: true`). The import path DELETEs the page's tag rows (`DELETE FROM tags ...` in `postgres-engine.ts`) and re-INSERTs only the tags parsed from the frontmatter. For a page whose frontmatter has no `tags:`, that nets to **zero tags** — the DB-side enrichment tags are silently dropped.

Pages whose tags ARE in frontmatter (or that weren't reindexed because their `chunker_version` was already current) kept their tags — consistent with "re-import resets tags to frontmatter-only".

## Expected

`reindex --markdown` is a re-chunk/re-embed operation, not a content-authoring one. It should NOT destroy tags that aren't in the frontmatter. Either preserve existing `tags` rows across a re-chunk, or merge frontmatter tags with existing DB tags instead of replacing.

## Impact

Silent loss of all enrichment/auto-generated tags on reindexed pages, with no warning. Not catastrophic (source content + frontmatter survive; vector search + reranker are unaffected), but tag-based filtering degrades. Notably the tags are **not** recoverable via `gbrain sync --force` — it re-imports from frontmatter through the same path with the same result. They only come back by re-running the enrichment that originally created them.

## Possibly related (lower confidence)

Across several `reindex --markdown` runs in one session the `chunk_count` changed each time (1558 → 1449 → 1462 → 2160) rather than no-op'ing once the chunker version was current — suggesting reindex may not be idempotent / re-chunks every run. Concurrent dream-cycle + `sync --force` were also running, so they may contribute to that number.

## Environment

- gbrain 0.41.26.0, Postgres (Supabase), `reindex --markdown` run via a Railway cron with the brain repo cloned.

Companion to #1619 (same brain; separate dream-cycle extract connection bug).

title: fix(postgres): don't close a module singleton an engine only joined (deeper #1570 root cause)
body:
## What

The deeper root cause behind #1570 / #1608. A module-style `PostgresEngine` that **joined** an already-open `db.ts` singleton calls `db.disconnect()` (→ `sql.end()`) on its own `disconnect()`, ending the **shared** connection for the whole process.

#1608 added a `withRetry` self-heal (reconnect between attempts) + a disconnect audit, and its message notes: *"The deeper bug (who's calling disconnect mid-cycle) is left [as follow-up]."* This PR fixes that deeper bug and names the culprit.

## The culprit

`gbrain dream` on Postgres: the **lint** phase's content-sanity probe `resolveLintContentSanity` (`src/commands/lint.ts:315`/`319`) opens a module-style engine to lift `content_sanity` config from the DB, then `disconnect()`s it. That engine merely joined the cycle's already-open singleton (its `db.connect()` was a no-op), so the disconnect ends the shared connection. Every later DB phase (extract write, embed, conversation_facts_backfill) then throws `connect() has not been called` → the cycle exits 1 and silently loses link/timeline writes. `--phase lint` alone "works" because nothing runs after it.

## The fix

Ownership tracking — same pattern as the v0.28.1 jobs-path idempotency fix:
- `db.ts`: new `isConnected()`.
- `postgres-engine.ts`: new `_ownsModuleSingleton`, set to `!db.isConnected()` **before** `db.connect()`. Module-style `disconnect()` only calls `db.disconnect()` when it owns the singleton; a joiner leaves it for its opener to close.

Complements #1608 (prevents the clobber instead of recovering from it).

## Verification

- Full `gbrain dream --source default` exits 0 (was exit 1); extract/embed writes land.
- `test/e2e/postgres-engine-disconnect-idempotency.test.ts`: 3/3 pass incl. a new regression case (`module engine that JOINED an open singleton does NOT clobber it`).
- Typecheck clean.
