title: fix(oauth): default omitted authorize scope to client's full registered grant
body:
## What

`authorize()` computes the granted scope as `(params.scopes || []).filter(s => hasScope(allowedScopes, s))`. When a client omits `scope` on `/authorize`, `params.scopes` is empty, so the **granted set is empty** — even for a client registered with `read write`.

That empty grant is written to `oauth_codes`, then flows into the access **and refresh** tokens. Since refresh inherits the stored grant (`exchangeRefreshToken`), it **never self-heals**: reconnecting just mints another empty-scoped token, and every op fails `insufficient_scope`.

## Why it matters

Some MCP connectors (observed with **Claude Desktop**) omit `scope` on `/authorize`. Those clients authenticate successfully but then get `insufficient_scope` on every call, with no obvious cause — the `oauth_clients.scope` column looks correct (`read write`); only the *token's* scopes are empty.

## Fix

When no scope is requested, default to the client's full registered scope (RFC 6749 §3.3 permits a server-chosen default). This mirrors `exchangeClientCredentials` in the same file, which already does `requestedScope ? parseScopeString(requestedScope) : allowedScopes`. The result is **still clamped** to the allowed set, so an explicit over-broad request cannot escalate.

```ts
const allowedScopes = parseScopeString(client.scope);
const requestedScopes = (params.scopes && params.scopes.length) ? params.scopes : allowedScopes;
const grantedScopes = requestedScopes.filter(s => hasScope(allowedScopes, s));
```

## Tests

Adds `test/oauth-authorize-scope-default.test.ts` (PGLite, no real DB), 5 cases:

- omitted scope → inherits full registered scope
- empty scope array → inherits full registered scope
- explicit subset honored (not overridden to full)
- clamp preserved: over-broad request cannot escalate (`read` client requesting `read admin` → `read`)
- clamp preserved: disallowed-only request grants nothing, no inheritance (`read write` client requesting `admin` → `[]`)

`bun test test/oauth-authorize-scope-default.test.ts` → 5 pass. Existing `test/oauth-confidential-client.test.ts` + `test/oauth-scope-probe.test.ts` → 15 pass. `bun run typecheck` clean.

## Compatibility / security

Not a privilege escalation: the clamp against the client's allowed scope is unchanged. The only behavioral change is that clients which previously received an empty (broken) grant now receive their **registered** scope. Clients that explicitly request a subset are unaffected.

title: bug: extract --stale aborts on 'invalid input syntax for type json' — excerpt() slices surrogate pairs
body:
## Problem

`gbrain extract all --source db --stale` aborts hard with `invalid input syntax for type json` and commits zero links/timeline entries. On a 192K-page brain it died at ~1,550/61,300 pages every run; the stale watermark re-hits the same point so extraction stays wedged.

## Root cause

`excerpt()` in `src/core/link-extraction.ts` slices the link-context window by raw UTF-16 char index:

```ts
function excerpt(s, idx, width) {
  const half = Math.floor(width / 2);
  const start = Math.max(0, idx - half);
  const end = Math.min(s.length, idx + half);
  return s.slice(start, end).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
}
```

When a window boundary lands inside a surrogate pair (any non-BMP char — emoji 🏆/🌌, math alphanumerics, etc.), the slice keeps a lone surrogate (e.g. `U+D83C` with no `U+DC00`–`U+DFFF` partner). That flows into the link `context` field; the batch is serialized to JSONB for `jsonb_to_recordset(($1::jsonb)->'rows')` (the #1861 path) and Postgres rejects the whole batch on `::jsonb` — killing the entire run, not just the row.

Confirmed by instrumenting `executeRawJsonb`: the failing batch had `row[18].context` with a lone `U+D83C` sliced out of an emoji in a person page's profile text.

## Fix

Strip unpaired surrogate halves from the excerpt before returning:

```ts
return s.slice(start, end)
  .replace(/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/g, '')
  .replace(/(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/g, '')
  .replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
```

Verified: after patching, `extract --stale` ran cleanly through all 59,902 stale pages -> 13,735 timeline entries + 76 links committed (was dying at 1,550).

## Defense in depth (optional)

The batch-insert primitives already strip NUL (`buildTakeRows`); they should also strip lone surrogates centrally via a `sanitizeForJsonb()` over batch row string fields, so any future slicer can't re-trigger this jsonb class.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.42.37.0, Postgres (Supabase) engine, 192K-page brain. Reproduced every run until the excerpt() fix.

title: v0.42.37.0 fix(jobs): reap stale locks, bound disconnect, complete cooperative-abort (#1972)
body:
Closes #1972. Three independent job-layer bugs, each traced to source, fixed in one PR with atomic per-bug commits. Hardened by `/plan-eng-review` + a Codex outside-voice round (11 findings folded in).

## The three bugs

**1. Stale locks never reaped.** A crashed sync (OOM/recycle/SIGKILL) stranded its `gbrain_cycle_locks` row — reclaim was on-contention only, no background sweep, so a low-traffic source looked "syncing" indefinitely. Added `reapDeadHolderLocks`: a host-scoped sweep at cycle start that deletes locks whose holder PID is provably dead, **scoped to the `gbrain-sync:*` / `gbrain-cycle*` namespaces only** (never elections/supervisor/reindex — that was a Codex blast-radius catch), with a **snapshot-matched delete** (`date_trunc` on `acquired_at`) that's TOCTOU-safe against PID reuse, plus the existing 60s grace. `gbrain doctor --fix` runs the same reaper for no-autopilot brains. DRY: `selectLockRows` + a shared mapper now back `inspectLock`/`listStaleLocks`.

**2. `disconnect()` hung ~10s and ate CLI output (#1959).** `pool.end()` never drained against PgBouncer transaction-mode, so teardown blocked until the CLI's 10s force-exit fired and `process.exit()`'d mid-write — truncating stdout (why a relational query returned empty though the query worked). Added a gbrain-owned `endPoolBounded` (`Promise.race` of `pool.end({timeout})` against a hard timer), applied across `db.ts`/`postgres-engine.ts`/`connection-manager.ts` (the two conn-manager pools close concurrently so bounds don't stack).

**3. Cooperative-abort was incomplete (#1737 follow-up).** v0.42.29 covered only embed. Threaded the signal into every cycle-reachable long loop: `extract` (incremental `extractForSlugs` + full-walk `extractLinksFromDir`/`extractTimelineFromDir` — a Codex correction; my first scope named the wrong functions), `extract_facts` (per-page loop + `embed` signal + the phantom-redirect 30s lock-retry), and `consolidate`'s bucket loop. `lint` yields + checks abort every 200 pages (it's synchronous; the yield is what lets the signal land). Added a **terminal abort check** so a cancelled cycle never stamps `last_full_cycle_at` as a completed run, and a per-phase duration warning that names any phase overrunning the 30s force-evict.

## Scope decisions

title: put_page write-through mirrors unrouted pages into an arbitrary federated source's repo
body:
**Version:** gbrain 0.40.6.0 (engine: postgres/Supabase, MCP stdio via `gbrain serve`)

**Summary:** When `put_page` (called over MCP) creates a page that has no project/source context, its markdown write-through mirror is written into the on-disk `local_path` of an unrelated federated source, rather than the source the page is actually assigned to.

**Observed behavior:**
- `gbrain serve` runs with cwd = `$HOME` (no `.gbrain-source` pin there).
- Creating cross-cutting pages (tagged `internal`, no project) via `put_page` returns `write_through: { written: true, path: "/Users/me/Projects/housefax/<slug>.md" }`.
- `housefax` is an unrelated registered federated source. Its `page_count` stays at 4 (the new pages are **not** assigned to it) — yet ~20 unrelated pages' `.md` mirrors accumulated in its repo dir, including auto-created subfolders (`office-hours/`, `internal/pitfalls/`).
- The pages themselves correctly live in the `default` source (`local_path: null`).

**Expected behavior:** write-through should either (a) mirror to the assigned source's `local_path`, or (b) skip the on-disk mirror entirely when the assigned source has `local_path: null` (as `default` does). It should **not** fall back to writing into some other federated source's working tree — that silently pollutes an unrelated git repo.

**Impact:** unrelated project repos accumulate stray untracked markdown files from every cross-cutting page write. Confusing, and easy to accidentally commit another topic's notes into the wrong repo.

**Workaround:** periodically sweep untracked `.md` files out of the affected source dir. There is no config knob (`gbrain config`, `put`, `export`, `sources`) to control the write-through target.

title: v0.42.39.0 feat(context): Retrieval Reflex — teach the agent when/what to retrieve (#1981)
body:
## Retrieval Reflex — teach the agent *when* and *what* to retrieve (#1981)

Closes #1981.

gbrain stored knowledge and injected deterministic per-turn context, but never taught the host agent the **policy** of retrieval: when to look something up, and what to pull. That lived in each user's hand-rolled instructions and failed silently — the agent could discuss a contact with a rich brain page for several messages without ever opening it. This makes the reflex a property of having a brain.

### Two layers, on by default
- **Deterministic pointer layer** (`src/core/context/`): a zero-LLM, precision-biased scan of each turn resolves salient entities (capitalized names, `@handles`) to existing pages and injects a compact pointer (name → slug → safe synopsis → "open before relying on details"). Detect + point, never auto-dump. Fail-open, capped at 3, suppression scans **prior** context only (not the triggering turn).
- **Policy skill + recipe** (`recipes/retrieval-reflex/`): encodes the trigger policy and the pointer → full-page → graph-neighbors escalation ladder. Installs into the host resolver via `gbrain integrations install retrieval-reflex`.

### Engine-aware, no second DB connection
PGLite is single-connection (your `gbrain serve` owns it), so the context engine resolves **through** the live holder over a local unix socket — never opens its own (a subprocess would force-steal the lock past the 5-min staleness window and corrupt the brain). Resolver ladder: host `ctx.brainQuery` → PGLite serve resolve IPC → Postgres cached direct → disabled (honestly reported by doctor, never a silent no-op).

### Safety
- Synopsis runs through the **same privacy boundary** `get_page` applies to untrusted readers (takes/private-fact fences stripped) — private content never reaches the prompt.
- Source-scoped via the canonical `source-resolver.ts` (honors `.gbrain-source` / `GBRAIN_SOURCE`).
- Whole path wrapped in fail-open + a hard timeout; a zero-candidate turn touches no brain at all.

### Also
- **Fix:** the install resolver-row fence is now keyed by recipe id (was hardcoded to the first recipe's name, so a second `copy-into-host-repo` recipe wrote a mislabeled block).
- **Doctor:** `retrieval_reflex_health` reports real runtime status from a heartbeat.

### Review
Hardened by `/plan-eng-review` (architecture/code/test/perf) + a Codex outside-voice pass before implementation. The load-bearing call (PGLite single-connection → engine-aware A+C hybrid) and Codex's findings (privacy bypass, namespaced-slug recall miss, suppress-always bug, imaginary doctor status, init host-mutation) are all folded in. Plan + GSTACK REVIEW REPORT at `~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-wild-yeti.md`.

### Test plan
- `test/context/entity-salience.test.ts` — extractor units (stopwords, sentence-start, dedup, cap, documented lowercase-miss).
- `test/retrieval-reflex.test.ts` — resolver + `assemble()` regression (the encoded motivating failure) on PGLite: namespaced-slug recall, alias arm, privacy non-leak, prior-context-only suppression, fail-open, cap, pre-v110 alias-table absence.
- `test/context/resolve-ipc.test.ts` — socket round-trip, absent-socket fallthrough, stale-socket cleanup.
- `test/doctor-retrieval-reflex.test.ts` — health check states.
- `test/integrations-install.test.ts` — fence-by-recipe-id regression.

All targeted tests + typecheck green against merged master. (Full-suite run during ship was contaminated by concurrent `bun test` from other workspaces — 83 `(fail) (unnamed)` ~7s timeouts; every sampled suspect passes in isolation.)

title: fix(sync): skip Python venv/ in the code walker
body:
## Problem

Running `gbrain sync --strategy code` against a Python repo crashes on the
first full sync. The first-sync walker `collectSyncableFiles`
(`src/commands/import.ts`) skips `node_modules` but **not** Python `venv/`,
so it descends into the virtualenv and tries to index thousands of vendored
files. The resulting slug collisions blow up `putPage`'s
`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING` (PGLite returns no row), surfacing as:

```
undefined is not an object (evaluating 'row.deleted_at')
```

On a real-world repo this was **1418 of 1467 "files" failing**, with the
1418 coming almost entirely from `venv/` (3258 files on disk). Excluding
`venv/` drops the walk to the 16 real tracked files and sync completes
cleanly (0 errors).

## Fix

Add `venv` alongside `node_modules` in both walk paths:

- `src/commands/import.ts` — the inline skip in the first-sync `collectSyncableFiles` walker.
- `src/core/sync.ts` — `PRUNE_DIR_NAMES`, so the incremental walker stays consistent.

`venv` is the Python equivalent of `node_modules`: a vendored dependency
tree that should never be indexed. (`.venv` is already covered by the
existing leading-dot exclusion; this closes the dotless `venv` gap.)

## Test

Existing walker/syncable suites pass unchanged:

```
bun test test/disk-walk.test.ts test/import-file.test.ts \
  test/brain-writer-walk-prune.test.ts test/check-resolvable-cli.test.ts
# 115 pass, 0 fail
```

title: serve --http (OAuth transport) ignores legacy token permissions.source_id grant — remote __all__ pinned to 'default'
body:
## Summary

The #1336 legacy-token source grant (`access_tokens.permissions.source_id`) is honored by `src/mcp/http-transport.ts` (`parseLegacyTokenScope`), but **not** by the OAuth transport that `gbrain serve --http` actually uses. `GBrainOAuthProvider`'s legacy `access_tokens` fallback branch (src/core/oauth-provider.ts, ~line 635) only `SELECT name`, never reads `permissions`, and hardcodes `sourceId: 'default'` with no `allowedSources`.

## Effect

On a multi-source brain, every remote caller authenticating with a legacy bearer token through `serve --http` is silently pinned to the `default` source:

- `query`/`get_page` with `source_id: "__all__"` collapses to `default` only (resolveRequestedScope → sourceScopeOpts → scalar ctx.sourceId), regardless of any array grant stored in `permissions.source_id`.
- Combined with v0.42.37.0's grant enforcement (#1999) this is a hard regression for multi-source MCP setups: cross-source retrieval returns `[]` with no error.

This contradicts the CLAUDE.md invariant: *"Source isolation. Every read-side op routes through sourceScopeOpts(ctx); precedence is federated array (ctx.auth.allowedSources) > scalar (ctx.sourceId) > nothing."* — the OAuth transport never populates the federated array for legacy tokens, while http-transport.ts does.

## Repro

1. Multi-source brain (Postgres engine), `gbrain serve --http`.
2. `UPDATE access_tokens SET permissions = jsonb_set(permissions, '{source_id}', '["default","src-a","src-b"]') WHERE name='<token>';`
3. Remote MCP `query` with `source_id: "__all__"` → results only from `default`; `tools/call whoami` shows transport "legacy".
4. Same grant via the bearer-only http-transport honors the array.

## Suggested fix

In the legacy fallback of `GBrainOAuthProvider`, select `permissions` and reuse `parseLegacyTokenScope` (array → `allowedSources` + first element as scalar write floor; string → scalar; absent → 'default'), mirroring http-transport.ts. The serve's tool dispatch already threads `auth: authInfo` into the op context, so populating `allowedSources` on the AuthInfo is sufficient. Happy to PR if useful.

title: v0.42.40.0 fix(extract,ingest): well-form lone UTF-16 surrogates before jsonb (#2011)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2011 — `gbrain extract --stale` aborting on brains that contain emoji or other non-BMP characters.

**Root cause.** `excerpt()` in `link-extraction.ts` sliced the link-context window by raw UTF-16 index, so a window boundary landing inside a non-BMP char's surrogate pair left an unpaired surrogate half in `context`. Serialized to JSONB for the `jsonb_to_recordset` batch insert, Postgres rejects it at the `::jsonb` cast and aborts the **whole batch** — and since the staleness bookmark only advances on a clean finish, every retry re-hit the same point and extraction stayed wedged.

**Fix (two layers + one consolidation):**
- **`ensureWellFormed()`** (`src/core/text-safe.ts`) — one shared primitive on Bun's `isWellFormed`/`toWellFormed`; replaces unpaired surrogates with U+FFFD, leaves valid pairs untouched.
- **Slicer fix** — `excerpt()` well-forms the sliced window (root cause).
- **`sanitizeForJsonb()`** (`src/core/batch-rows.ts`) = `ensureWellFormed(stripNul(s))`, applied centrally to every free-text body field (link `context`; timeline `summary`/`detail`/`source`; take `claim`/`source`) across both the batch builders and the scalar `addLink`/`addTimelineEntry` paths on **both engines**. Defense in depth: no future slicer can re-trigger this crash class.
- **Identity/security fields stay un-sanitized** (slugs, source ids, holders, link_type) — a malformed identifier still fail-closes/rejects rather than being silently rewritten. Locked by explicit fail-closed tests.
- **DRY** — brainstorm's hand-rolled `sanitizeUnicode` consolidated onto `ensureWellFormed` (also fixes a consecutive-lone-surrogate case the old regex left half-cleaned).

Commits (excluding the version/changelog bookkeeping commit):
- `fix(extract,ingest): well-form lone UTF-16 surrogates before jsonb (#2011)`
- `docs: update project documentation for v0.42.40.0 (commit subject says 0.42.39.0 — superseded by the re-slot commit)`

## Test Coverage

AI-assessed: **95%**, 1 low-severity gap (brainstorm `buildCrossPrompt` wiring — a private function covered transitively by the exhaustive `ensureWellFormed` unit tests). Coverage gate: PASS (target 80%).

```

  valid pairs preserved, clean/empty, mixed, JSON round-trip ......... ★★★ (unit)
excerpt() window splits non-BMP char (asserts malformed precondition) . ★★★ (unit)
sanitizeForJsonb: link context; timeline summary/detail/source;

fail-closed: lone surrogate in identity field rejects the batch ..... ★★★ (PGLite + PG-e2e)
```

Local run (always-on lanes): **271 pass / 0 fail**. The Postgres e2e lane is `DATABASE_URL`-gated (CI); this build's PGLite also reproduces the `::jsonb` rejection (`22P02`), so the PGLite lane locks the crash too.

Checklist + 4 specialists (testing, maintainability, security, performance). 2 informational findings, both auto-fixed:
- `stripNul` export clarified (steer jsonb callers to `sanitizeForJsonb`).
- **Takes `source` was an unsanitized same-class crash vector** (free-text provenance through `::jsonb`) — now sanitized + tested. PR Quality Score: 10/10.

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent was #2011; delivered that plus the eng/codex-surfaced same-class hardening (timeline `source`, takes `source`, scalar paths) and the DRY consolidation.

6/6 plan tasks DONE (helper, excerpt, batch+scalar sanitize incl. timeline source, PG e2e, fail-closed tests, brainstorm consolidation).

Plan verification is test-command based (`bun test` / `bun run typecheck`) — executed, all green. No dev server involved.

Claude adversarial + Codex structured review — both clean, cross-model agreement. Claude empirically verified the dedup-collision concern is non-exploitable (PGLite already stored U+FFFD pre-change; Postgres rejected raw surrogates, so re-extraction dedup behavior is unchanged). Codex: no `[P1]`.

title: fix(cli): arm the disconnect hard-deadline at teardown, not before the op handler (#1775)
body:
Fixes #1775.

## The bug

The 10s "disconnect hang guard" in `src/cli.ts` is armed at the top of the op-dispatch path, **before the op handler runs**, and only cleared in the `finally` after `engine.disconnect()` returns. That makes it accidentally a **whole-run deadline, not a disconnect guard**: any shared op whose total wall time exceeds 10s gets `process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0)` mid-handler. The user sees empty stdout, exit 0, and a misleading `engine.disconnect() did not return within 10000ms` warning for a disconnect that never ran.

This is why #1775 reproduces only on `search`/`query`: they're the shared ops that routinely exceed 10s (remote Postgres over WAN, reranker passes, LLM query expansion), while `list`/`get`/`status` finish fast, and bulk commands (`embed`, `sync`) dispatch through the CLI-only path that never hits this timer. Root cause was diagnosed exactly by @danashburn in the issue thread — this PR is that one-move fix, plus a regression test.

Note: #2015 (`endPoolBounded`) fixes a *different* bug in the same blast radius — a genuinely hung `pool.end()` against PgBouncer. It doesn't touch this timer; with #2015 merged, an op handler slower than 10s still gets killed mid-run. The two compose.

## The fix

Arm the timer in the `finally`, immediately before `drainAllBackgroundWorkForCliExit()` + `engine.disconnect()` — the teardown it exists to bound (its warning message already says so). The C13 defense-in-depth contract ("a hung disconnect cannot defeat the force-exit") is fully preserved: the timer is armed synchronously at teardown start, before the drain/disconnect awaits. This also brings the op-dispatch path to the same shape `handleCliOnly`'s teardown has used since v0.42.20.0 (#1762) — the pre-handler placement was the outlier, not the design.

**Trade-off, stated honestly:** a hung op *handler* is no longer killed at 10s. There is deliberately no uniform whole-run wallclock after this change — handlers are bounded piecemeal by the layers underneath (6s query-embed deadline in hybrid.ts, 60s/300s AI gateway deadlines via `withDefaultTimeout`, Postgres `statement_timeout` default 5min), so the worst-case wedge for a pathological case (e.g. client-side TCP blackhole mid-query) moves from 10s to ~minutes. The old behavior was strictly worse for that case too: it reported the failure as an exit-0 success with empty output. If a uniform backstop is wanted for unattended callers, a generous (minutes-scale) pre-handler deadline with a distinct warning and nonzero exit would be a separate, additive change — happy to file it.

## Tests

`test/cli-disconnect-deadline-placement.test.ts` — source-shape regression test pinning that the arming sits after `op.handler(...)` and before the drain, with exactly one arming site in `main()`. Placement is the load-bearing property, so this follows the pattern the repo endorses in `test/fix-wave-structural.test.ts` (a behavioral repro would need a >10s op against a live engine just to observe the timer fire).

Also updates the one `KEY_FILES.md` phrase that described the old whole-run behavior ("hanging past the 10s force-exit") to the current truth.

## Verification

- New test + `test/cli-should-force-exit.test.ts`, `test/cli.test.ts`, `test/cli-options.test.ts`, `test/cli-dispatch-thin-client.test.ts`, `test/fix-wave-structural.test.ts`, `test/build-llms.test.ts`: all pass. The placement test fails on current master, passes with the fix.
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.
- Manually verified on a Postgres brain with a local reranker where `gbrain query` takes 13–28s: before the fix, empty stdout + exit 0 + the misleading warning at exactly 10s; after, full ranked results print and the process exits cleanly.

title: fix(gateway): carry asymmetric input_type across the AI SDK to the wire body (supersedes #1400)
body:
Supersedes #1400 (closed unmerged) — same AsyncLocalStorage mechanism @billy-armstrong proposed, extended to cover Voyage and every openai-compatible recipe (llama-server, litellm, ollama, …). Full credit to him for the original diagnosis.

## The bug

```
embedQuery(text)
  → embed([text], {inputType: 'query'})
  → dimsProviderOptions(..., 'query')
  → {openaiCompatible: {dimensions: N, input_type: 'query'}}   ✓ threaded
  → AI SDK embedMany / openai-compatible adapter                ✗ input_type DROPPED
  → per-recipe fetch shim sees a body with no input_type
  → wire: input_type: 'document' (ZE default) / absent (everyone else)
```

The AI SDK's openai-compatible adapter validates `providerOptions.openaiCompatible` against a fixed schema (`dimensions`, `user`) and silently drops every other field before building the request body. So for asymmetric embedding models — where queries and documents are encoded with different prompts — **every query was encoded document-side**, and asymmetric retrieval silently collapsed toward surface-token overlap. The failure is invisible at the providerOptions layer: `test/asymmetric-encoding-contract.test.ts` pins that `input_type: 'query'` reaches the transport's providerOptions, and it stays green while the wire carries the wrong value. Embeddings remain valid vectors, hybrid search still returns results — they're just systematically worse, with the BM25 arm masking the vector-arm failure on keyword-y queries.

Affected consumers on master:
- **ZeroEntropy hosted** (`zeroentropyai:zembed-1`): the shim's `input_type = 'document'` default fires for queries too.
- **Voyage v3+** (`input_type` is part of Voyage's retrieval API): the field never reaches the wire at all.
- **llama-server / litellm / ollama** (local/proxy asymmetric models): no shim existed, so those deployments had no way to receive the signal.

## The fix

One mechanism, all consumers. A module-level `AsyncLocalStorage` (`__embedInputTypeStore`, mirroring the existing `__budgetStore` pattern in the same file) is populated in `embedSubBatch()` **only when `providerOptions.openaiCompatible.input_type` is actually present**, and read at body-rewrite time by the fetch shims:

- `zeroEntropyCompatFetch`: recovers the threaded value; the `'document'` default is preserved byte-for-byte for paths that didn't thread one (ingest).
- `voyageCompatFetch`: opt-in, mirroring the dims.ts Voyage branch — injects only when a caller threaded one; otherwise the field stays off the wire (pre-v0.35.0.0 behavior preserved).
- `openAICompatAsymmetricFetch` (new): the fallthrough default for every openai-compatible recipe without its own compat fetch (llama-server, litellm, ollama, …) — the canonical local/proxy paths for asymmetric models (a zembed-1 behind llama.cpp, vLLM, or an OpenAI-compatible proxy). Strictly opt-in: when nothing was threaded the request passes through untouched, so symmetric deployments see **zero wire change** (dims.ts threads input_type by model id, never for Azure/DashScope/Zhipu-style fixed models); when threaded, the field is injected (OpenAI-compatible servers ignore unknown body keys; asymmetric-aware servers/proxies read it). Recipes with their own compat fetch (azure) keep it via the `compat.fetch ??` precedence.

**`KNOBS_HASH_VERSION` bumped 10→11**: the semantic query cache keys rows by query-embedding similarity, and every pre-fix row was written with document-side query vectors. Without the bump, pre-fix rows could be served to post-fix lookups for up to `cache.ttl_seconds`. Same convention as the v=3 embedding-provider bump; one-time global cold-miss on upgrade, refills within TTL. The four test pins on the version were updated accordingly.

## Tests

`test/embed-input-type-wire.test.ts` — runs the **real SDK transport** with a mocked global `fetch` and asserts on the outbound body, the only layer where this regression is observable (one layer below the existing contract test):

- ZE hosted: query → `input_type: 'query'`; index path → `'document'`.
- llama-server + zembed-1: query → `'query'`; index → `'document'`; non-asymmetric model → **no** `input_type` (strict pass-through pinned).
- litellm + ollama serving zembed-1: query → `'query'` (the fallthrough shim covers them).
- Voyage: query → `'query'` (alongside the existing `output_dimension`/`encoding_format` translations); index path → field stays off the wire (opt-in pinned).

**4 of the original 7 assertions fail on current master**, proving the test pins the actual bug. One structural pin in `test/ai/zeroentropy-compat-fetch.test.ts` updated to the new line shape (same semantic: document default preserved). `KEY_FILES.md`'s gateway.ts entry updated to describe the new mechanism.

## Verification

- New file + `test/asymmetric-encoding-contract.test.ts`, `test/ai/*`, `test/search-mode.test.ts`, `test/cross-modal-phase1.test.ts`, `test/search-alias-resolved-boost.test.ts`, `test/search/knobs-hash-reranker.test.ts`, `test/query-cache-knobs-hash.serial.test.ts`, `test/embedding-dim-check.test.ts`, `test/embed-multimodal-batching.test.ts`, `test/openai-compat-multimodal.test.ts`, `test/doctor-ze-checks.test.ts`, `test/build-llms.test.ts`: **543 pass / 0 fail**.
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.
- Verified end-to-end on a real brain running zembed-1 locally behind llama-server: before the fix, semantically-phrased queries (no keyword overlap with the target page) ranked near-empty stub pages above the exact page; after, the query-side encoding reaches the serving layer and the exact page ranks top-1 consistently.

title: autopilot: reconnect path calls connect() with no args → FATAL restart-loop on every DB blip
body:
## Bug

After any transient DB error (network blip, Supabase pooler restart, idle-connection drop), the autopilot daemon FATALs with:

```
[autopilot] FATAL: unrecoverable DB error (undefined is not an object (evaluating 'config.database_url')). Exiting so launchd ThrottleInterval can apply backoff.
```

The launchd ThrottleInterval safety net (v0.37.7.0) catches this and restarts the daemon, but the underlying reconnect path never succeeds — it exits on every attempt, making "reconnect" effectively a process-restart loop.

Found on v0.37.11.0 (2026-05-22); **confirmed still present at v0.42.1.0 (`eefe8b57`)** — same bare call at `src/commands/autopilot.ts:337`.

## Repro

Run autopilot against any Postgres brain. Wait for a network blip or for the Supabase pooler to recycle the connection (typically <24h). Check `~/.gbrain/autopilot.err`:

```
[reconnect] ERROR: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'config.database_url')
[autopilot] FATAL: unrecoverable DB error ...
```

## Root cause

`src/commands/autopilot.ts:337` (at `eefe8b57`):

```ts
await (engine as any).connect?.();
```

The bare `connect?.()` call passes NO arguments. `PostgresEngine.connect(config)` immediately dereferences `config.database_url`, which throws when `config` is undefined.

The engine already has a proper `reconnect()` method (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts:4653` at `eefe8b57`) that reuses `this._savedConfig` and needs no argument.

## Fix

```diff
@@ src/commands/autopilot.ts:336-337
-        await engine.disconnect();
-        await (engine as any).connect?.();
+        await (engine as any).reconnect?.();
```

`reconnect()` handles disconnect + connect with the saved config internally.

## Impact

The `classifyReconnectError` defense from #1162 bails cleanly so launchd backs off — correct safety net, but the underlying reconnect never works. Autopilot reboots on every DB blip instead of recovering in-process.

We run this one-line patch locally; verified across multiple pooler recycles — daemon survives blips in-process.

title: cli: calibration missing from CLI_ONLY set → "Unknown command" despite dispatch case existing
body:
## Bug

`gbrain calibration` reports `Unknown command: calibration` even though the dispatch case exists:

```
$ gbrain calibration
Unknown command: calibration
Run gbrain --help for available commands.
```

Found on v0.37.11.0 (2026-05-22); **confirmed still present at v0.42.1.0 (`eefe8b57`)**: the dispatch case is at `src/cli.ts:1567` but `calibration` is missing from the `CLI_ONLY` set at `src/cli.ts:38`.

## Root cause

`src/cli.ts` has two parallel dispatch paths: commands in the `CLI_ONLY` set go to `handleCliOnly`; anything else falls through to the cliOps map and then the "Unknown command" error. `calibration` is in the `handleCliOnly` switch but not in `CLI_ONLY`, so it can never reach its own case.

## Fix

One word added to the `CLI_ONLY` set literal:

```diff
@@ src/cli.ts:38
-... 'status', 'skillopt']);
+... 'status', 'skillopt', 'calibration']);
```

## Impact

The entire `gbrain calibration` CLI family (print/regenerate the active profile) is inaccessible. The MCP `get_calibration_profile` op works, but the documented CLI command doesn't — blocks the v0.36.1.0 hindsight-calibration wave from CLI use.

## Suggested audit

A sweep of `case '...':` labels inside `handleCliOnly` against the `CLI_ONLY` set would catch any other top-level commands with the same dispatch gap.

title: migrate: renumbered migration recorded without executing (v102 timeline_entries_source_in_dedup) → all timeline writes fail
body:
## Bug

Our brain reads `schema_version` 111, but `idx_timeline_dedup` was still the 3-column `(page_id, date, summary)` shape. Migration **v102 `timeline_entries_source_in_dedup`** — whose own comment says "originally v99, bumped to v102 after master merge" — never executed: the version counter passed it via the pre-renumber chain, so it was recorded as applied without its SQL ever running.

An artifact audit of v101–v109 against the live schema showed **only v102 missing** (link_kind column, migration_impact_log, atom-hash idx, slug_aliases, extract_rollup_7d, generation clock, embedding_signature, newest_content_at all present).

## Consequence at v0.42.x

Every `addTimelineEntry` / `addTimelineEntriesBatch` call fails:

```
there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification
```

because both code paths infer on the 4-column index `(page_id, date, summary, source)` (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts`, both insert sites at `eefe8b57`). On our mesh this silently broke timeline writes on every node, including the hub.

## Recovery (what we did)

Ran the migration's own SQL by hand:

```sql
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_timeline_dedup;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_timeline_dedup ON timeline_entries(page_id, date, summary, source);
```

## Suggested fixes

1. Key applied-migration tracking by stable **name**, not only the version integer — renumbering during merges then can't strand a migration as recorded-but-not-executed.
2. A doctor check that verifies migration **artifacts** (expected index/column/table per migration) rather than trusting the version counter — would have caught this immediately.
3. Defensively, `addTimelineEntry` could fall back to a plain insert-where-not-exists when the ON CONFLICT inference fails.

## Related observation

The `brain_score` SQL counts soft-deleted pages in every denominator (`SELECT count(*) FROM pages` with no `deleted_at IS NULL` filter), so a brain mid-purge-window is double-penalized on timeline/orphan/link-density components. Possibly intentional, but worth a look while in this code.

title: gateway toolLoop: no resume reconciliation — crash mid-tool-round leaves a dangling tool-call tail that dead-letters every retry (ModelMessage[] schema / missing tool results)
body:
## Summary

Two gaps in the gateway-native tool loop (`agent.use_gateway_loop=true`) make subagent retries fail **deterministically** after a mid-tool-round crash. Closely related to #1886 (which covers persisting the tool-results message in-loop); this is the **resume** half plus a history-poisoning class that persistence alone doesn't fix. We carry a local patch (described below, with unit tests) and are happy to PR.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.42.37.0, Postgres engine (Supabase session pooler)
- `agent.use_gateway_loop=true`, model `openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`
- Carrying the #1886-style persistence fix locally (`onToolResultsTurn` → `persistMessage`) — these failures occur **with** that fix in place

## Production evidence

Dream `synthesize` fan-out, 14 subagent children: **8 dead after 3 attempts each**. `error_text` on the dead jobs:

- 7×: `[chat(openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro)] Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema.`
- 1×: `[chat(openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro)] Tool results are missing for tool calls call_<id>, call_<id>, call_<id>.`

Telling detail: **5 of the 6 jobs that eventually completed show the same errors on early attempts** — when the crash point left a *consistent* persisted history, the retry succeeded; when it left a dangling tail, every retry failed identically until `max_attempts`. The failure is a deterministic property of the persisted history, so raising `max_attempts` cannot help.

## Root cause 1 — no resume reconciliation in `toolLoop`

`toolLoop` seeds the conversation straight from `replayState.priorMessages` and immediately calls `chat()`:

```ts
const messages: ChatMessage[] = opts.replayState
  ? [...opts.replayState.priorMessages]
  : [...opts.initialMessages];
```

Per D11 write-ordering, the assistant turn is persisted **before** tool dispatch, but the tool-results user message is only persisted **after the entire tool round completes**. A tool round can run for minutes (`put_page`, `search`, …), so a stall-kill / timeout / worker crash in that window leaves the persisted history ending in an assistant message with dangling `tool-call` blocks. On resume, the very first `chat()` sends that prompt; AI SDK v6 rejects it (`MissingToolResultError` / ModelMessage zod validation); the attempt fails before reaching any code that could repair the tail — and every subsequent retry replays the identical poisoned history.

The legacy Anthropic-direct path in `src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts` has had exactly this protection for a long time ("Replay reconciliation": settle dangling `tool_use` blocks from `subagent_tool_executions` outcomes, synthesize the tool-results user turn, then resume). The gateway path never got the equivalent, and all infrastructure it needs (`replayState.priorTools`, `onToolCallStart`'s ON-CONFLICT re-claim, idempotency flags) is already there.

A second, smaller miss in the same family: when the prior history ends in a **terminal** assistant turn with *no* tool calls (crash after persisting the answer but before job bookkeeping), the gateway resume calls `chat()` with a trailing assistant message — assistant-prefill, which several providers reject. The legacy path returns the persisted text instead.

## Root cause 2 — persisted-history poisoning passes through `toModelMessages`

`toModelMessages` (added for v6 in #1759/#1809) fixed the tool-result/`role:'tool'` conversion but still lets two shapes through:

1. **`tool-call` blocks with `input: undefined`.** `chat()` normalizes provider parts with `input: part.input ?? part.args` — DeepSeek emits zero-arg tool calls where both are absent, so `undefined` is persisted (JSONB drops the key) and replayed forever.
2. **Unknown block types fall through `return b` as-is** into the v6 messages array.

Either one, once persisted, fails zod validation on every later turn and every retry of that job → `Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema`.

## Fix we run locally

1. **Resume reconciliation in `toolLoop`** (mirrors the legacy path): if `replayState.priorMessages` ends in an assistant message with `tool-call` blocks, settle each call before the first `chat()` — prior `complete` → replay output; prior `failed` → error result; `pending` + idempotent → re-execute; `pending` + non-idempotent → unrecoverable (same contract as the in-loop path); unregistered tool → error result. Persist the synthesized tool-results turn via `onToolResultsTurn` so the *next* resume is also consistent. If the tail is a terminal assistant turn (no tool calls), return its text instead of assistant-prefilling.
2. **Defensive `toModelMessages`**: coerce missing `tool-call` input to `{}`, map `reasoning` text parts through, drop unknown block types, and drop messages whose content sanitizes to nothing.
3. **`?? {}` at both `chat()` normalization sites** so undefined input is never persisted in the first place.
4. **Diagnosability**: on prompt-validation failures, the `llm_call_failed` heartbeat now includes a `message_shapes` summary (roles + block types only, never content), so a poisoned history can be diagnosed from logs instead of needing a live repro.

Unit tests added (all green, plus the existing 15 pinned cases unchanged):

- `toolLoop` resume: settles dangling calls from prior outcomes before first `chat()` (no re-execution for `complete`)
- `toolLoop` resume: re-executes idempotent `pending`, maps `failed` to an error tool-result
- `toolLoop` resume: terminal assistant tail returns persisted text without calling `chat()`
- `toModelMessages`: undefined input → `{}`; unknown blocks dropped; `reasoning` preserved; empty messages dropped

Happy to open a PR with the full diff if maintainers want it.

title: search --json emits empty stdout when engine.disconnect() hangs and CLI force-exits
body:
## Symptom
`gbrain search "<query>" --json` exits 0 with completely empty stdout, while the same query works in plain mode and via `gbrain query`.
stderr shows: `[cli] engine.disconnect() did not return within 10000ms — force-exiting`

## Environment
gbrain 0.42.37.0, Postgres engine via Supabase transaction pooler (6543), search.mode=balanced. Observed immediately after a bulk `extract links --by-mention --source db` write (~4.3K mention edges on a ~1.5K-page brain) — possibly the denser links table slows whatever disconnect waits on, widening the race.

## Suspected cause
When the disconnect watchdog force-exits, the process dies before the --json payload flushes to stdout. Plain-mode output (written incrementally) survives; the JSON payload (written late, one chunk) is lost. Exit 0 makes it silent — an agent consuming --json sees "no results" and trusts it.

## Suggested fix
Flush/drain stdout before the force-exit path (or write payload before initiating disconnect). Related lineage: v0.41.27.0 disconnect work (#1570) + the facts-queue drain-before-disconnect fix — same class, output side.

title: fix(links): collapse hyphen runs in normalizeBasename
body:
## Bug

Under global-basename resolution, a wikilink whose target title contains `" - "` (space-hyphen-space) never resolves, so the edge is silently dropped. `[[Note - Quarterly Review]]` pointing at the page slugged `notes/note-quarterly-review` produces no link.

## Cause

`normalizeBasename` (src/core/link-extraction.ts) does `.replace(/\s+/g, '-')`, which collapses whitespace runs but not hyphen runs. `" - "` has a literal hyphen between two spaces, so it normalizes to a triple hyphen:

```
"Note - Quarterly Review"            ->  "note---quarterly-review"
slug tail keyed by buildBasenameIndex ->  "note-quarterly-review"
```

They never match. The slug generator already collapses separators, so the lookup side is asymmetric. This hits every page using the common `Type - Name` title convention.

## Fix

Collapse `[\s-]+` to one hyphen and trim stray edge hyphens, matching how slugs are built. Single-space titles are unaffected. Also bumps `LINK_EXTRACTOR_VERSION_TS` per the in-file convention so existing brains re-extract links on update.

## Testing

Added cases to `test/link-extraction.test.ts` for the hyphen-run collapse plus a no-regression check. `bun test test/link-extraction.test.ts` passes, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: fix(serve): enable parent-death watchdog on Windows via signal-0 liveness probe
body:
## Problem

On Windows, the stdio parent-death watchdog never runs. `readLiveParentPid` and `probeWatchdogAvailable` are hard-wired to `spawnSync('ps', ...)`, and `ps` doesn't exist on Windows — so the startup probe fails on **every** Windows host and serve logs:

```
[gbrain serve] watchdog disabled: ps unavailable, parent-death detection unavailable — child will rely on stdin EOF / signals only
```

The fallback channels are weaker on Windows than the comment suggests, because MCP hosts there typically launch serve through a `cmd.exe` wrapper (`.bat`/`.cmd`), and killing the wrapper does not kill the bun child. Observed failure on a real install (Windows 11, Claude Code, PGLite engine):

1. MCP host spawns `serve.bat` → `cmd.exe` → `bun src/cli.ts serve`; serve takes the PGLite write lock.
2. Host dies / kills the wrapper without closing stdin. No signal reaches bun, no stdin EOF fires, the watchdog is disabled → orphan.
3. The orphan holds the PGLite write lock indefinitely (until reboot). Every subsequent gbrain invocation — CLI and fresh MCP spawns alike — fails with `GBrain: Timed out waiting for PGLite lock`. The brain is bricked until someone hand-kills the orphan.

## Fix

Windows never re-parents orphans, so the cached `process.ppid` stays correct for the process's lifetime — the watchdog question inverts from *"did the live PPID change?"* to *"is the original parent still alive?"*. That's answerable in-process with a signal-0 existence probe (`process.kill(ppid, 0)`, OpenProcess under the hood). No external binary needed at all.

- `readLiveParentPid` / `probeWatchdogAvailable`: platform split — `ps` on POSIX (unchanged), signal-0 on win32. Parent dead → report PID 0 (kernel PID 0 is the System Idle Process, never our parent), which differs from `initialParentPid` and fires the existing shutdown path. EPERM counts as alive.
- `isPidAlive`: shared exported helper; rejects non-PIDs before probing.
- Install guard tightened from `initialParentPid !== 1` to `> 1`, so a PID-0 "parent already gone at install time" report can't install a phantom interval comparing 0 to 0 forever (stdin `close` already covers a parent that died before boot).
- Disabled-mode log generalized — it no longer claims `ps` is the only mechanism.
- Both defaults are now exported with a `platform` test seam, so CI on any OS exercises both branches (signal-0 works everywhere).

Known degraded mode, documented inline: Windows recycles PIDs aggressively, so a reused parent PID can mask a death. Stdin EOF / signals remain the primary shutdown channels and the watchdog stays the backstop — the same posture as POSIX.

## Impact on non-Windows hosts

None intended, and the surface is small:

- The POSIX `ps` reader and probe bodies are untouched.
- The `> 1` guard change only alters POSIX behavior when serve's initial ppid is 0 (serve running as a container's PID 1): previously that installed a watchdog that could never fire; now it's skipped, matching the documented PID-1 skip.
- The disabled-mode stderr line changed wording (the probe-fail test was updated to match).

## Testing

- New `watchdog platform defaults` suite (6 tests) covering `isPidAlive` (own PID alive, non-PIDs rejected, exited child dead), `readLiveParentPid('win32')` healthy-tick behavior, `probeWatchdogAvailable('win32')`, and the default-platform reader. Runs on POSIX CI via the platform seam.
- All 11 watchdog-related lifecycle tests pass (5 pre-existing + 6 new); `bun run typecheck` and `bun run verify` clean.
- **Live verification on Windows 11** (the original failure reproduced, then fixed): spawned serve via a `.bat` wrapper, killed the wrapper `cmd.exe` without closing stdin → bun child exited within ~10s (one 5s watchdog tick + shutdown) and the PGLite lock dir was released. Before this change the child survived indefinitely and bricked the brain.

Note for reviewers: `test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts` has a pre-existing hang on Windows under `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0` (the `idle timer is reset on every stdin data chunk` test, reproducible on unmodified master) — unrelated to this change; the affected test relies on real timers and passes on POSIX.

title: fix(sync): honor .gitignore in code walk; prune vendor/dist/build
body:
## Problem

`gbrain sync --strategy code` indexes git-ignored trees. On a Laravel/PHP repo this means it descends into `vendor/` (~50k Composer files), `storage/`, and `public/build/`, trying to import **52,164 files** where only ~1,000 are real source. The result: the full sync never finishes (watchdog SIGTERM at ~3%), and whatever it does import floods the index with library internals (`vendor/symfony/...`, `vendor/psy/psysh/...`), so semantic code search returns dependency files instead of project code.

Root cause: `collectSyncableFiles` (the full-sync / dry-run enumerator in `src/commands/import.ts`) reimplemented its own descent skip list inline — `if (entry === 'node_modules' || entry === 'ops') continue;` — bypassing the canonical `pruneDir` gate in `src/core/sync.ts` and ignoring `.gitignore` entirely. The two skip lists drifted, and neither covered `vendor`.

This is the concrete bug behind the open `--respect-gitignore` (#1159) / `.gbrainignore` (#1483) requests and overlaps the maintainer's #1942 vendor/dist/build prune.

## Fix

1. **Git-aware enumeration.** When `dir` is a git work tree, `collectSyncableFiles` now lists files via `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -z` (tracked + untracked-not-ignored), so the walk honors `.gitignore`. Non-git dirs fall through to the existing recursive FS walk unchanged. EroLab (a Laravel repo): **52,164 → 1,028 files**.
2. **Dedupe the FS fallback to the canonical gate.** The fallback walk now prunes through `pruneDir()` instead of the drifted inline `node_modules || ops` list, so the two can't diverge again.
3. **`PRUNE_DIR_NAMES` gains `vendor`, `dist`, `build`** — dependency/build-output trees that are git-ignored on virtually every repo. This covers the FS-fallback + incremental (`classifySync`) paths.

## Testing

- `git ls-files` path verified end-to-end via `--dry-run` on a real Laravel repo: 52,164 → 1,028.
- Walker regression suites green (90 pass, 0 fail): `test/sync-walker-symlink.test.ts`, `test/brain-writer-walk-prune.test.ts`, `test/sync.test.ts`, `test/sync-walker-submodule.test.ts`.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Symlink policy and submodule-gitlink skipping are preserved (each `ls-files` entry is `lstat`-checked).

title: v0.18.3 feat(extract): find bare wikilinks validated against the page table
body:
## Summary

**Headline:** `gbrain extract` now finds the wikilinks you actually wrote — flat slugs (`[[my-runbook]]`) and domain-specific dir prefixes (`[[tools/X]]`, `[[reference/X]]`) outside the canonical `people|companies|concepts|...` whitelist that have been silently dropped since v0.12.0.

Adds a second pass in `extractPageLinks` that captures any `[[X]]` not matched by the strict `DIR_PATTERN` regexes, validates X against the actual page table via a new `SlugResolver.exists()` method, and emits an edge if the page exists. The existing strict regexes still handle their happy path; the new pass picks up everything else.

Verified on a real 118-page knowledge brain: **0 → 117 edges discovered**, orphans dropped 118 → 82, idempotent on re-run.

## Test Coverage

11 new unit tests under `extractPageLinks bare-wikilink pass`:
- Flat slug to existing page emits a candidate
- Flat slug to missing page is silently dropped (no dead links)
- Non-canonical dir prefix (`tools/X`) to existing page emits a candidate
- Mixed whitelisted + bare wikilinks both emit
- Whitelisted slug not double-emitted by both passes (dedup)
- Bare wikilink inside code fence ignored
- Display-text syntax `[[slug|Display]]` resolves the slug
- Qualified `[[src:slug]]` not picked up by bare pass (already handled by `QUALIFIED_WIKILINK_RE`)
- Duplicate bare wikilinks dedup within page
- Trailing `.md` normalized
- Section anchor stripped

**Test results:** 2175 pass / 0 fail (unit), 186 pass / 0 fail (E2E).

## Itemized changes

### Link extraction
- `src/core/link-extraction.ts` — `DIR_PATTERN_SET`, `BARE_WIKILINK_RE`, new pass in `extractPageLinks`.
- `src/commands/extract.ts` — hybrid resolver when `--include-frontmatter` is off (null `resolve()`, real `exists()`). Without this the new pass would silently emit nothing on every flag-off run — the failure mode this PR was originally written without and discovered during production verification.

### SlugResolver interface
- Added `exists(slug: string): Promise<boolean>` — exact-slug existence check, no fuzzy, cached separately from `resolve()`.
- Updated all three fixture resolvers in tests (`allowAllResolver`, `nullResolver`, `makeFixtureResolver`).

### Tests
- `test/link-extraction.test.ts` — 11 new test cases covering the bare-wikilink pass.

### VERSION + CHANGELOG
- VERSION 0.18.2 → 0.18.3 (PATCH, additive non-breaking)
- `package.json` synced
- CHANGELOG entry with numbers-that-matter table, "What this means", "To take advantage of v0.18.3" block

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test` passes (2175 pass / 0 fail, 11 new tests for bare-wikilink pass)
- [x] `bun run test:e2e` passes (186 pass / 0 fail across 18 files, fresh test DB)
- [x] Real-world verification on a 118-page production brain: 0 → 117 edges, orphans 118 → 82, re-run idempotent (0 new edges on second pass)
- [x] Unlink + re-extract recreates removed edge (proves the new pass actually fires)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Documentation

- **CLAUDE.md** — refreshed `src/core/link-extraction.ts` description to cover the new v0.18.3 bare-wikilink pass (`BARE_WIKILINK_RE`, `DIR_PATTERN_SET`, `SlugResolver.exists()`); refreshed `test/link-extraction.test.ts` surface to enumerate the 11 new bare-wikilink test cases.

No other docs needed updating. The new behavior is internal to the extract pipeline — `gbrain extract links --source db` and `gbrain orphans` work the same way from the user's perspective, they just find the wikilinks they're supposed to find now. README, AGENTS, CONTRIBUTING, and docs/ are all current. CHANGELOG already has the full v0.18.3 entry.

title: addTimelineEntriesBatch binds Date objects into unnest(...)::text[] — timeline_entries silently stays empty forever
body:
Found during a deep audit of gbrain v0.42.26.0 (Postgres engine, but the same call shape exists in pglite-engine and the symptom was identical there: `Timeline: 0` despite daily extraction runs).

## Symptom
`gbrain extract timeline --from-meetings --source db` reports candidate generation (e.g. "on 1014 entity pages from 103 meetings") but `timeline_entries` stays at 0 rows, with no error anywhere.

## Root cause (two bugs compounding)

1. **`src/core/postgres-engine.ts` `_addTimelineEntriesBatchOnce`**: `const dates = entries.map(e => e.date);` — when `TimelineBatchInput.date` is a JS `Date` (which it is whenever the caller sources dates from SQL rows, e.g. `meeting.effective_date` in `extract-timeline-from-meetings.ts`), the driver types the bound array as `timestamptz`, and the statement's `${dates}::text[]` cast fails with:
   ```
   cannot cast type timestamp with time zone to text[]
   ```
   Every batch insert fails.

2. **`src/core/extract-timeline-from-meetings.ts` `flush()`**: the bare `catch {}` swallows that error, so the run completes "successfully" with 0 entries. The feature has plausibly never written a row for any user whose dates arrive as Date objects.

## Fix (verified locally)
```ts
const dates = entries.map(e => e.date instanceof Date ? e.date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : String(e.date));
```
plus logging the error in the `flush()` catch. After this one-liner, the same vault produced **3,212 timeline entries** on the first run.

Also worth checking `pglite-engine.ts`'s equivalent batch method for the same Date-binding hazard.

title: pglite-lock force-removes locks of LIVE processes after 5 minutes (no heartbeat) — concurrent serve processes share the single-writer data dir; WAL corruption observed
body:
Found during a deep audit of gbrain v0.42.26.0 after a real PGLite WAL corruption event.

## Mechanics (src/core/pglite-lock.ts)
- `STALE_THRESHOLD_MS = 5 min` (line ~22); the acquire loop force-removes a lock whose holder PID is **alive** once the lock is older than 5 minutes ("Still alive but probably stuck — force remove", lines ~82-85).
- `acquired_at` is written once at acquisition (lines ~102-106) and never refreshed — there is no heartbeat, so **every** healthy long-lived holder is classified stale after 5 minutes.
- `releaseLock` (lines ~140-148) `rmSync`s the shared lock dir without checking ownership, so a finishing short-lived CLI process deletes whichever holder's marker is present.

## Consequence
`gbrain serve` connects the engine at startup and holds it for the process lifetime (cli.ts "serve doesn't disconnect"). With per-client stdio MCP registration (Claude Desktop + every Claude Code/Codex session spawns its own serve), serve #2 starting >5 min after serve #1 steals the lock, and so on. Observed live: **4 concurrent `gbrain serve` processes each holding 40+ read-write FDs inside the same `brain.pglite` data dir (two sharing the same WAL segment), with no `.gbrain-lock` dir present at all** — exactly the concurrent access the module's own header says PGLite cannot survive (`Aborted()`). We experienced a WAL/checkpoint corruption that required a full rename-aside + reimport, plus recurring "PGLite lock contention persisted after 3 attempts" failures in scheduled sync runs.

## Suggested fix
Mirror the design already present in `src/core/db-lock.ts` (`last_refreshed_at`, lines ~154-160):
1. Heartbeat: refresh a timestamp in the lock file every ~60s (unref'd interval) while the engine is connected.
2. Steal only when the holder PID is dead OR the heartbeat (not `acquired_at`) is stale.
3. `releaseLock` should verify the lock file's pid === process.pid before `rmSync`.

Note the behavior change: a second stdio serve then fails fast with the actionable 30s timeout instead of silently sharing the data dir — correct for a single-writer database, and it makes the documented `serve --http` single-daemon mode the explicit multi-client answer.

title: fix(gateway): reconcile dangling tool-call replay
body:

title: fix(config): ignore DATABASE_URL auto-loaded from cwd .env (#427)
body:
Closes #427.

## Problem

Bun merges `.env` files from the process cwd into `process.env` before any user code runs, and `loadConfig()` prefers env `DATABASE_URL` over `~/.gbrain/config.json`. So any gbrain invocation from inside a checkout whose `.env` defines `DATABASE_URL` — Next.js, Hono, Supabase, most web apps — silently retargets the brain at that app's database:

- Reads hit the wrong DB (`relation "pages" does not exist`, misleading "check your config.json" errors — the original #427 report).
- Writes are worse: `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` run from such a directory attempts gbrain's schema DDL against the app's database. One #427 commenter had gbrain's schema **written into their production Supabase**, including the DDL event trigger. I hit the same failure mode against a production Railway Postgres — saved only because that instance lacks the `pgvector` extension.

The operator never opted into any of this: the `.env` belongs to the project in cwd, not to gbrain.

## Fix

Bun gives no way to ask which env vars came from a `.env` file (the merge happens before module load), so `effectiveEnvDatabaseUrl()` re-parses the `.env` files Bun auto-loads from cwd and treats a `DATABASE_URL` whose value matches one of them as file-origin: ignored, with a one-time stderr notice telling the operator what happened and how to override deliberately.

Resulting precedence:

| Source | Honored? |
|---|---|
| `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` (any origin) | always — namespaced to gbrain, never auto-ignored |
| `DATABASE_URL` exported in the shell / CI | yes — its value won't match a cwd `.env` assignment (and if it's identical, the same database was meant by the file anyway, so honoring config.json is the safe reading) |
| `DATABASE_URL` auto-loaded by Bun from cwd `.env` | **ignored + warned** |
| `~/.gbrain/config.json` | as before |

Applied at all four read sites so behavior stays consistent: `loadConfig()`, `getDbUrlSource()` (doctor must not report `env:DATABASE_URL` while loadConfig ignores it), `init --non-interactive` (prevents seeding a brain config with the app's DB), and `migrate --to` (prevents the app DB becoming a migration target).

## Why not `--no-env-file` in the shebang?

`#!/usr/bin/env -S bun --no-env-file` fixes this on my machine, but it's wrong as the upstream fix: Windows bin shims never read shebangs (the #427 reporter is on Windows), `env -S` is unavailable on busybox/Alpine, and it would also stop `.env` from supplying other keys (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`) that some workflows rely on — #464 explicitly wants cwd-`.env` auto-loading for autopilot. The in-code guard is cross-platform and narrowly scoped to the one variable that causes cross-database damage.

## Testing

- `test/config-env-hijack.test.ts` — 8 cases pinning the guard: parser (quotes/`export`/comments/multi-file), hijack ignored, differing exported URL honored, `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` never ignored, no-`.env` and unset-env passthrough. Uses `withEnv` + injectable dir (no `process.chdir`, parallel-shard safe).
- Existing `config-env`, `loadConfig-merge`, `config` suites: 56 pass, 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- End-to-end: from a repo whose `.env` carries a production `DATABASE_URL`, `bun src/cli.ts doctor --json --fast` now reports `URL present from config-file-path` (previously `env:DATABASE_URL`) and prints the notice once.

title: fix(sync): stamp last_sync_at on no-op up_to_date sync
body:
When `performSync` finds git HEAD unchanged, it returns early with status `up_to_date` but never calls `writeSyncAnchor`, so `sources.last_sync_at` is never refreshed.

doctor's `sync_freshness` check reads `sources.last_sync_at` directly (`doctor.ts`), so a quiet, fully-caught-up source shows as **stale indefinitely** — a successful no-op sync is *proof* of freshness but left the timestamp untouched. In practice this surfaces as a `sync_freshness` warning that never clears no matter how many times you run `gbrain sync`.

### Fix
Stamp the freshness anchor before the `up_to_date` return (`src/commands/sync.ts`) by reusing the existing `writeSyncAnchor(engine, sourceId, 'last_commit', headCommit, commitTimeMs(repoPath, headCommit))` path. Re-writing the same `last_commit` value is value-neutral; the point is the `now()` timestamp + `newest_content_at` refresh in the same atomic UPDATE that branch already performs.

### Test
Adds a regression test in `test/sync.test.ts` (`no-op up_to_date sync stamps last_sync_at`) asserting `last_sync_at` strictly advances across a no-op `up_to_date` sync. Fails against current `master`, passes with the fix. Full `test/sync.test.ts`: **67 pass, 0 fail**. `tsc --noEmit`: clean.

### Scope
Single short-circuit branch; no behavior change to `synced` / `first_sync` / `dry_run` / `partial` paths (those already stamp via their own `writeSyncAnchor` calls).

Two silent-failure bugs found and traced live on a production brain behind a Supabase transaction pooler (6-10s per fresh connection), plus a recipe-order defect found three times in the same codebase.

- `fix(cli)`: the op-dispatch disconnect hard-deadline timer was armed BEFORE the try block, so any op whose handler ran past 10s wall-clock was force-exited mid-flight with code 0 and zero stdout. On a slow pooler every `gbrain search` hit this — an empty "success" indistinguishable from no results. The timer now arms at teardown entry (same placement as the fall-through owner-disconnect site). Verified: a search that died at 10s now returns correct results at ~21s.
- `fix(cli)`: read-scope handlers and context build (DB I/O for every op) get a real wallclock bound — 180s default, `--timeout=Ns`, exit 124 — and the timeout path hard-exits after teardown so the abandoned handler (withTimeout races, never cancels) can't hold sockets that zombify the process. This also completes the TODOS.md item "(v0.42.20.0 follow-up) Decouple the op-dispatch force-exit timer".

**Code graph: scoped `code-callers`/`code-callees` returned 0 rows**
- `fix(import)`: `importCodeFile` never stamped `source_id` on extracted edges → every edge NULL → the scoped filter `AND source_id = ...` never matched. title: fix(postgres-engine): atomic JSONB merge in updateSourceConfig — eliminate lost-update race
body:
## Problem

`updateSourceConfig` in `postgres-engine.ts` used a read-then-write pattern:
read the current `config` row, normalize it in JavaScript, then write the merged
result back with `SET config = <normalized> || <patch>`.

Under concurrent callers (two background autopilot or cycle paths patching
different keys simultaneously), both callers can read the same stale row. The
later `SET config = ...` then clobbers the earlier patch, silently dropping
whatever keys the first caller wrote. Running `gbrain dream` + `gbrain autopilot`
in parallel reproduced 21/25 lost-update events on real Postgres.

Note that `pglite-engine.updateSourceConfig` already used an atomic `||` merge; this
PR closes the parity gap in the Postgres engine.

## Fix

Fold the normalization and merge into a single atomic `UPDATE … SET config = CASE … END || patch` statement. Because the `SET` expression evaluates against the row-locked latest version of `config`, there is no snapshot window between read and write. Concurrent callers converge correctly.

The `CASE` normalizes historical bad JSONB shapes inline:

- `object` — used as-is
- `string` — double-encoded config; inner text is parsed using the SQL `IS JSON` predicate (Postgres 16+) to distinguish valid JSON (parsed and merged) from unparseable text (reset to `{}`, avoiding an `invalid input syntax for type json` error that would abort the whole `UPDATE`)
- `array` — flattened via `jsonb_object_agg`
- anything else — reset to `{}`

## Tests

Added two test cases to `test/list-all-sources.test.ts`:

1. JSONB string holding non-JSON text normalizes to `{}` without throwing
2. JSONB string holding double-encoded valid JSON is parsed then merged with the patch

```
12 pass, 0 fail
```

These run against PGLite (in-memory Postgres 17), which supports the `IS JSON` predicate at parity with Postgres 16+.

title: fix(doctor): five correctness fixes — stale locks, content sanity, graph coverage, exit code, gateway guard
body:
Five independent correctness fixes for `gbrain doctor`, all found while running it
in production. Each is a small, isolated change; grouped here because they all touch
`src/commands/doctor.ts`.

---

### 1. Stale lock break hints cover `gbrain-cycle:` keys

The stale-lock report only recognized `gbrain-sync:` prefixes; everything else fell
back to `gbrain sync --break-lock`, which is wrong for cycle/dream locks. A
`gbrain-cycle:<source>` lock now suggests `gbrain dream --break-lock --source <name>`,
bare `gbrain-cycle` suggests `gbrain dream --break-lock`, and truly unknown lock shapes
fall back to `gbrain doctor` instead of a misleading sync command.

### 2. `content_sanity_audit_recent` counts `reject` and `quarantine` as hard failures

v0.42 renamed the hard-disposition path: rejected pages emit a `reject` event and
quarantined junk pages emit `quarantine`; `hard_block` is now only the pre-v0.42 legacy
alias. The status check only counted `hard_block`, so fresh `reject`/`quarantine` events
cleared as `ok` whenever fewer than 10 events existed. The check now sums
`hard_block + reject + quarantine` for the hard count and `soft_block + flag` for soft.

### 3. `graph_coverage` excludes test-fixture entity pages from the denominator

Brains seeded with code sources can accumulate test-fixture pages typed as `entity` or
`person` (e.g. fixtures under `tools/gbrain/test/`). Including these in the entity-count
denominator diluted coverage and produced spurious warnings. The check now computes
coverage against an eligible-entity CTE that excludes `tools/gbrain/test/*` slugs and
the `templates/new-person` stub, with an additional short-circuit for the all-fixture
case (`eligibleEntityCount = 0 → ok`).

### 4. `process.exitCode` instead of `process.exit` at doctor's main exit point

`process.exit(hasFail ? 1 : 0)` was a hard kill that prevented cleanup handlers (Bun
unload events, open DB connections) from running. `process.exitCode = hasFail ? 1 : 0`
defers termination until the end of the event loop so cleanup completes normally.

### 5. `checkSubagentCapability` exported + gateway-loop guard

The function was private, making it untestable as a standalone unit. It is now exported.

Additionally, when `agent.use_gateway_loop=true` is configured, subagents route via
the gateway and do not need `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` directly. The previous check fired a
spurious warning for users who had a non-Anthropic `chat_model` and had the gateway
loop enabled.

---

## Tests

`bun test test/doctor.test.ts` → 77 pass, 0 fail (no regressions from any of these changes).

title: extract links: globalBasename resolution exists but no CLI flag exposes it — cross-folder bare wikilinks underivable
body:
## Summary

`extract links` has working machinery for resolving bare wikilinks by basename across folders — `opts.globalBasename` (extract.ts ~307–313: "Ancestor walk misses + globalBasename on + basename hits → all matches") — but no CLI flag wires it, so it's unreachable in practice.

## Why it matters

Obsidian's default link style is bare `[[Page Title]]` regardless of folder. In a foldered vault (`10-people/`, `11-companies/`, `12-meetings/`, ...), most wikilinks point across folders, and the ancestor-walk-only default derives **zero** edges for them. Measured on a real vault: hundreds of dangling cross-folder refs that `extract links` couldn't resolve, all of which had unambiguous basename targets — the only path was scripting manual `add_link` calls.

## Ask

A `--global-basename` flag on `extract links` (opt-in, default off to preserve current behavior). Ambiguity policy can stay exactly as the existing code documents (return all matches / skip ambiguous).

title: markdown walker ignores .gitignore on full reimport (incremental sync skips those files) — sync.respect_gitignore referenced in doctor but unimplemented
body:
## Summary

For markdown (default-source) syncs, gitignored files are invisible to **incremental** sync (it enumerates via `git diff lastCommit..HEAD`) but ARE imported — and embedded — by **full reimports**: `collectSyncableFiles` (import.ts:532) prunes only dot-prefixed dirs, `node_modules`, `ops`, and `.raw`, never consulting `.gitignore`. Meanwhile `sync.respect_gitignore` already appears in doctor.ts (~line 2117) as a config nudge, but nothing implements it.

## Why the divergence is the problem

A gitignored `.md` under the synced tree behaves as "not indexed" for months of routine syncs — then a full reimport fires (first sync, a `CHUNKER_VERSION` bump on upgrade, or the sync anchor commit going missing after a history rewrite) and the file is silently imported and embedded. For users who use `.gitignore` as their "private/local-only" boundary, that's surprise egress of exactly the content they meant to exclude, triggered by an event they didn't initiate (an upgrade or a git history operation).

The two sync modes disagreeing about what's in the corpus also means a full reimport doesn't reproduce the incremental state — page counts jump and search results change after what should be a no-op rebuild.

## Ask

Implement `sync.respect_gitignore` for the markdown walker (filter `collectSyncableFiles` through `git check-ignore` / parsed gitignore rules when the flag is set). Default off is fine — the doctor nudge already implies the flag's existence, so the fix is mostly making the documented surface real.

Related: #1073 asks for the same gitignore awareness on the `--strategy code` walker. This issue is specifically about the markdown/default source path and the already-referenced-but-unimplemented config key.

title: fix(gateway): thread asymmetric input_type to ZeroEntropy via request header — AI-SDK adapter drops providerOptions.openaiCompatible.input_type
body:
## Problem

`embedQuery()` exists and threads `inputType: 'query'` into `providerOptions.openaiCompatible` — but the AI-SDK's openai-compatible adapter **silently drops unrecognized providerOptions fields**. `dimensions` survives (known param); `input_type` doesn't. Every embed request therefore reached the ZeroEntropy compat shim without an `input_type`, and the shim's correct-for-ingest default (`'document'`) applied to **queries too**.

Net effect: the entire vector arm performs asymmetric retrieval with symmetric (document-typed) query vectors. Nothing errors — rankings are just quietly wrong, especially for natural-question phrasings against note-style passages (exactly what asymmetric encoding exists to fix).

## How this was found (evidence chain)

On a real ~2.3k-page / ~9.7k-chunk corpus (zembed-1 @ 1280, Postgres engine):

1. Hybrid search consistently missed targets for natural-question queries that **pure-vector SQL with a properly query-typed vector ranked #1**.
2. A manually **document-typed** query embedding reproduced production's broken rankings **byte-identically** (cosine sims equal to 16 decimal places) — production was provably searching with document-typed query vectors.
3. `gbrain`'s own `embedQuery()` output matched that document-typed vector, not the query-typed one.
4. Post-fix: 8/8 previously-missing natural-question probes rank their target #1 on the same corpus. (An unrelated dims experiment — 1280 vs native 2560 — measured a flat wash, which was the tell: dims should have moved something. The model was never the problem.)

Worth noting: `test/asymmetric-encoding-contract.test.ts` stayed **green** through all of this — it captures `providerOptions` at the `__setEmbedTransportForTests` seam, *upstream* of the adapter that drops the field. The contract it pins is real but doesn't reach the wire.

## Fix

- `embedSubBatch()` threads the input type as an **`x-gbrain-input-type` request header** — headers survive the adapter, travel with the request (race-free), and need no module state.
- `zeroEntropyCompatFetch` consumes + strips the header during its existing body rewrite and writes `input_type` into the request body.
- No API change. The Voyage path is unaffected (it builds its request body directly rather than going through the openai-compatible adapter — `input_type` already reaches the wire there).

## Test

New `test/ze-input-type-wire.test.ts` drives `embed()`/`embedQuery()` through the **real** adapter via a new `__setZeFetchForTests` terminal-fetch seam (mirrors the existing `__set*ForTests` conventions) and asserts the final wire body:

- `embedQuery(...)` → body `input_type: 'query'`, threading header stripped, URL rewrite ran
- `embed([...])` → body `input_type: 'document'`

**Verified to fail without the fix** (the query-side assertion sees `'document'`). `bun run verify`: 30/30 green. Full unit suite: **no new failures vs master** — a set of provider-env-sensitive serial tests (reranker/cross-modal/think-gateway) fails identically on a clean master checkout in my environment (host injects `ANTHROPIC_*` env vars), so I'm expecting CI's clean env to be green.

## Operational note for existing installs

Any cached query-embedding artifacts produced while the bug was live are document-typed — after upgrading, clear the query cache and restart long-running `gbrain serve` processes so they pick up the fixed code.

Possibly related: #1469 reports the hybrid vector path returning identical results regardless of input (ollama). Different symptom — a fixed/ignored query vector vs. a wrong-typed one — so this PR does not claim to fix it, but it's the same subsystem and worth re-testing against this change.

title: query path still hits 10s disconnect force-exit on PgBouncer txn-mode — search-arm teardown bypasses endPoolBounded (residual of #1972)
body:
## Residual from #1972 (Bug 2): `gbrain query` still hits the 10s disconnect force-exit on PgBouncer txn-mode — a teardown path bypasses `endPoolBounded`

**Version:** 0.42.39.0 @ `8f45624e`. Same deployment as #1972 (386K pages, Supabase split-pool: direct `:5432` + read `:6543` PgBouncer transaction-mode, federation `default` + `straylight-brain`).

The 0.42.37 fix (#2015) landed `endPoolBounded` (db.ts: 2s per-pool cap) and wired it through `ConnectionManager.disconnect()` (concurrent, non-stacking) and the db.ts module-singleton `disconnect()`. **It works** — the worst symptom from #1972 Bug 2 (force-exit racing/swallowing CLI stdout) is gone, and simple commands now exit clean:

```
gbrain status            → 6s wall, no force-exit ✅
gbrain query "x" --limit 1 → 15s wall, force-exit banner EVERY time ❌
   [cli] engine.disconnect() did not return within 10000ms — force-exiting
```

100% reproducible on the query path; 0% on status. Output is intact (results print fully before teardown — the damage half is fixed), but every query pays a flat **10s teardown tax** and exits via the hard-deadline backstop instead of cleanly.

### Where the bound is being bypassed

The teardown sequence (cli.ts `finally`, ~line 408) is:
1. `drainAllBackgroundWorkForCliExit({ timeoutMs: 1000 })` — bounded ✅
2. `await engine.disconnect()` — this is what exceeds 10s on the query path ❌

Since `ConnectionManager.disconnect()` and db.ts module `disconnect()` are both bounded (2s each, concurrent → worst case ~2.5s), whatever hangs must be a connection/handle the query path opens that doesn't drain through either:

Candidates, in likely order:
- **Federation / brain-registry path:** `BrainRegistry.disconnectAll()` (brain-registry.ts:387) does `Promise.allSettled(handles.map(h => h.engine.disconnect()))` — bounded *per engine*, but a multi-source query (`default` + `straylight-brain` here) initializes multiple engines; if any engine's disconnect resolves the bound but leaves a socket open, Bun's event loop stays alive and only the unref'd force-exit timer ends the process.
- **`bumpLastRetrievedAt` fire-and-forget** (last-retrieved.ts:173, called from operations.ts:1396 on every search): if its write-back is in flight on a connection that outlives the 1s drain window, the open socket keeps the loop alive even after pools "ended."
- **Embeddings call socket** (provider HTTPS keep-alive): query embeds the search string; a keep-alive agent socket would also hold the loop open and is invisible to pool teardown.

The distinguishing fact — `status` (touches DB, no search arm, no embedding, no multi-source fan-out) exits clean; `query` (embedding + federated search + last-retrieved write-back) never does — points at the search-arm-only resources.

### Suggested fix direction
Either route every engine/socket the search path opens through the bounded teardown registry, or — simpler and arguably more correct for one-shot CLI (per the existing note in timeout.ts:13 that the kernel reclaims sockets on exit) — after the bounded drains complete, `process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0)` immediately instead of waiting for the event loop to empty. The 10s backstop should be the never-hit safety net, not the routine exit path for the most-used command in the CLI.

Happy to run a patched build against this deployment to verify — same offer as #1972, which went filed-Sunday → merged-Wednesday. 🙏
