title: Long-running jobs worker never refreshes AI gateway config — propose_takes hard-fails per page on hardcoded anthropic default when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent
body:
**Version:** 0.42.37.0 (1eb430a), Postgres engine, Linux VPS, autopilot installed as a systemd user service.

## Symptom

Every `autopilot-cycle` job logged one warning **per page** in the `propose_takes` phase:

```
extractor failed on <slug>: Anthropic chat requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
```

~70–100 warnings per cycle, for ~36 hours. No Anthropic key exists on this brain — `chat_model` is `deepseek:deepseek-chat`, set both in DB config (`gbrain config set chat_model …`) and as `GBRAIN_CHAT_MODEL` in the env file sourced by the autopilot unit. `gbrain config get chat_model` returned the correct value the whole time, which made the failure very confusing to diagnose.

## What happened

1. The autopilot service (which spawns the `gbrain jobs work` child that executes cycles) had been **started before** `chat_model` was configured.
2. The AI gateway config is resolved once at process startup (`connectEngine` → file/env merge + DB merge + `reconfigureGatewayWithEngine`). A long-running worker never re-reads it.
3. With no `chat_model` resolved at boot, the gateway falls back to the hardcoded `DEFAULT_CHAT_MODEL = 'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6'` (`src/core/ai/gateway.ts`). `instantiateChat` then throws `AIConfigError` for every page because `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is absent.
4. Net effect: `gbrain config set chat_model …` (or fixing the env file) has **no effect on already-running workers** — the per-page failures persist silently in job warnings until the operator thinks of restarting the service.

Restarting the autopilot service fixed it instantly: the same job (`autopilot-cycle` with `phases:["propose_takes"]`) went from ~70 per-page failures to `100 pages scanned, 0 warnings, proposals inserted` on deepseek.

## Why this is worth fixing

- The failure mode is a per-page hard-fail buried in job warnings — easy to miss for days (takes/atoms silently stop accruing while everything else looks healthy).
- The fallback targets a provider the operator may never have configured. Other phases gate cleanly when prerequisites are missing (e.g. `extract_atoms: not_in_active_pack — skipped`); chat-bearing phases could do the same.

## Suggestions (any subset helps)

1. Re-resolve gateway config at job start (or on a TTL) in the jobs worker, so `gbrain config set chat_model` applies without a service restart.
2. When the effective chat model resolves to a provider with no credentials, skip the phase once with an explicit status (like pack-gating) instead of emitting N per-page `AIConfigError`s.
3. `src/core/extract-takes-from-pages.ts` defaults to a hardcoded `'anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5'` (`opts.model ?? …`) — the same dormant failure for brains without an Anthropic key; defaulting to the configured `chat_model` would be consistent.

Happy to provide logs or more repro details.

## What

Adds a `chat` touchpoint to the MiniMax recipe (currently embeddings-only).

## Why

The capabilities hint in `src/core/ai/capabilities.ts` already lists minimax among "Known providers with chat", but the recipe never declared the touchpoint — so `minimax:<model>` fails at `getProviderCapabilities()` with *does not offer a chat touchpoint*, and the model can't be used for `models.tier.subagent` / dream synthesis via the gateway tool loop. Verified against `api.minimax.io` with `MiniMax-M3`: tool calling and plain text both return correctly (we run dream synthesis on it in production on our install).

title: fix(pglite): heartbeat file lock without stealing live holders (#2058)
body:
## What & why

Closes #2058.

The current PGLite lock can remove a lock from a still-live holder once `acquired_at` crosses the stale threshold. That is unsafe for embedded PGLite: a paused or starved process can still hold open database files even if its JS timers are not making progress, so a second process deleting the lock can recreate concurrent access/WAL corruption risk.

Before this PR, a second process could delete a live holder's lock after five minutes. After this PR, stale heartbeat metadata is diagnostic only; the lock is not recovered unless the same-host PID is provably dead and past a short PID-reuse grace window, or the lock directory is an old orphan with missing/corrupt metadata.


## Why this shape

This intentionally does not use a stale heartbeat as a takeover signal. For PGLite, a starved or paused JS process can still hold database files open, so heartbeat age is useful diagnostic data but not proof that it is safe for another process to enter.

The safety choices here are meant to close the race windows around that:

- `owner_id` prevents an old handle from releasing a newer lock created by the same PID.
- `last_refreshed_at` gives waiters better diagnostics without becoming an unsafe steal condition.
- Same-host dead-PID recovery keeps normal crash recovery working, but the short grace window reduces PID-reuse risk.
- Cross-host, `EPERM`, and unknown PID-probe results fail closed because they cannot prove the holder is gone.
- Quarantine rename avoids deleting the active lock directory after reading stale metadata.

## The fix

- Add per-acquisition ownership metadata: `owner_id`, `pid`, `host`, `acquired_at`, `last_refreshed_at`, and `command`.
- Add an owner-checked heartbeat that refreshes `last_refreshed_at` via temp-file write plus atomic rename.
- Fail closed for live PIDs, stale heartbeats, cross-host metadata, `EPERM`, and unknown PID probe results.
- Recover only dead same-host PIDs after a grace window, or old missing/corrupt orphan metadata after initialization grace.
- Replace direct lock-directory deletion during recovery with an atomic quarantine rename followed by best-effort removal.
- Make release owner-checked so a stale handle cannot remove a replacement lock from the same PID.

## Scope decisions

- No release metadata (`VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`).
- No public exports, CLI flags, docs, or generated `llms` files.
- No changes to `db-lock.ts` or `pglite-engine.ts`.
- Test seams are internal to `acquireLock` options only.

## Tests

Added deterministic coverage for:

- live PID with old `acquired_at` and fresh `last_refreshed_at` is not stolen
- live PID with stale `last_refreshed_at` is not stolen
- old-format live lock without heartbeat metadata is not force-stolen
- dead same-host PID past grace is cleaned up
- dead same-host PID inside grace is not cleaned up
- unknown and EPERM-equivalent PID probe results are treated as unsafe/alive
- cross-host locks are not auto-stolen
- fresh missing metadata inside initialization grace is not removed
- old corrupt metadata is recovered as orphaned
- acquired locks write `owner_id`, `host`, and `last_refreshed_at`
- heartbeat refreshes `last_refreshed_at` and stops after release
- release removes own lock
- release does not remove same-PID different-owner lock
- release no-ops for corrupt, missing-file, and missing-directory lock state

## Verification

- `bun test test/pglite-lock.test.ts` — 19 pass, 0 fail
- Docker: `docker compose -f docker-compose.ci.yml run --rm --no-deps runner bash -lc 'bun test test/pglite-lock.test.ts'` — 19 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- `bun run verify` — 30 pass, 0 fail
- `gitleaks detect --source . --redact --no-banner` — no leaks found

I also ran `bun run ci:local -- --no-pull` against both this branch and a clean upstream checkout under local Docker/Colima. Both runs reproduced the same current local-Docker baseline failures, including the same `validateUploadPath` fuzz counterexample (`./../../../tmp`) and shard 3 exit 137, so I did not treat that as branch-specific evidence.

title: (withdrawn — superseded)
body:
## Problem

Retrieval is pull-based. The agent has to *know to ask* (`gbrain query "X"`) before the brain contributes anything. In practice this means:

- **Deep sessions can use zero gbrain calls.** A multi-hour session ran entirely on warm context + direct file reads — not because the brain had nothing relevant, but because nothing prompted the agent to ask.
- **Entity misses are silent.** When a conversation mentions people or projects with real history in the brain, nothing surfaces unless the agent notices the entity AND decides to look it up AND picks the right query string.
- **Literal-string retrieval misses named concepts.** Canonical failure mode: a page stored under a coined proper name is missed because the query used the generic/descriptive phrase for the same concept. Storage is by meaning, retrieval is by string, and the gap eats exactly the highest-value pages — named projects, aliased people, coined concepts.

## Proposal: push-based context surfacing

A `gbrain watch` / serve-mode capability that takes a rolling conversation window and **volunteers** relevant pages:

1. **Entity/alias extraction** over the live window (people, projects, named concepts), resolved through an alias table — not raw vector similarity. Alias index pages and people-page `aka:` frontmatter are seed alias sources.
2. **Push surface:** return top-k pages with one-line relevance rationales, cheap enough to run per-turn (local embeddings + alias index; LLM only for tie-breaking).
3. **Confidence gating:** only volunteer when signal is strong (named entity match, alias hit, high-sim concept) — push noise is worse than pull silence.
4. **Feedback loop:** log which volunteered pages the agent actually used (opened/cited) to tune precision.

## Relationship to existing work

- Builds on / supersedes the alias-aware-retrieval direction — alias resolution is the shared core; this issue adds the push transport.
- Complements agent-side entity-detection gates: today those fire inside the agent and cost a CLI roundtrip per entity; serve-mode amortizes it.

## Success criteria

- Mention of an aliased entity surfaces the right page with zero agent-initiated queries.
- Deep sessions show >0 brain contributions without the agent having to remember to ask.
- False-positive rate low enough that pushed context is read, not ignored.

title: fix(facts): durable facts-absorb jobs for one-shot CLI processes + source-scoped fence paths
body:
### Problem 1: facts:absorb never completes from one-shot CLI processes

Since the v0.42.20.0 drain-then-abort teardown, every `gbrain capture`/`put` from a short-lived CLI process loses its facts extraction:

1. `put_page` enqueues the extraction chat into the in-process `FactsQueue` (queue mode).
2. `cli.ts`'s exit teardown drains background work for 1–2s, then `abort()` → `FactsQueue.shutdown()` aborts the in-flight chat (extraction takes 5–30s; the 10s `DISCONNECT_HARD_DEADLINE_MS` force-exit prevents waiting longer).
3. Result: `pipeline_error: [chat(anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6)] The operation was aborted.` in ingest_log on every eligible CLI page write, zero facts extracted.

Observed in production: 100% of CLI-written eligible pages over 4 days. Timing evidence: page `created_at` → absorb error row ~4s later, i.e. drain+abort, not the 300s gateway timeout.

**Fix:** `cli.ts` marks one-shot processes (every command except `serve`/`jobs`/`autopilot`) via a new leaf module `src/core/facts/cli-process-mode.ts`. `runFactsBackstop`'s queue mode then submits a durable `facts-absorb` minion job (new handler in `registerBuiltinHandlers`) for the long-lived `gbrain jobs work` worker instead of the doomed in-process enqueue. Content-hash idempotency key dedups rapid identical writes while allowing re-extraction after edits; falls back to the in-process queue if job submission fails (old schema, no minions infra). Daemons keep the in-process queue — their event loop outlives the work. A marker (not argv heuristics) so tests and embedded/server callers are never affected.

### Problem 2: fence writes land at the repo root for non-default sources

`writeFactsToFence` built its path as `join(local_path, slug + '.md')`, while the put_page write-through and dream-cycle reverse-render both use `resolvePageFilePath()` (non-default sources → `.sources/<id>/<slug>.md`). Facts resolving to a non-default-source page therefore wrote stray fence files into the repo ROOT — the default source's tree — polluting the brain repo and risking duplicate stub pages on a later default-source directory import.

**Fix:** route fence paths through `resolvePageFilePath()`.

### Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean on master + this branch.
- `bun test` on facts-backstop-gating, facts-backstop-integration, fence-write, facts-fence, facts-absorb-log, facts-anti-loop, handlers, autopilot-cycle-handler: all pass.
- Production validation on a live brain: capture → `facts-absorb` job completed in 5.8s with 2 facts inserted; an 18-page backfill of previously-aborted pages recovered 132 facts with 0 failures.

title: cli.ts arms the 10s force-exit timer before the shared-op handler — local ops >10s are killed with exit 0
body:
## Summary

`runLocalOp` in `src/cli.ts` installs the 10s `DISCONNECT_HARD_DEADLINE_MS` force-exit timer **before** `op.handler` runs (around line 366). The timer is unref'd but still fires 10 seconds after arming, calling `process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0)`.

Consequence: any local-engine **shared op** that takes longer than ~10s total (op + drain + disconnect) is killed mid-work — and because `process.exitCode` is unset when the op hasn't errored, the process exits **0**, so the truncation looks like success to callers and scripts.

## Why it mostly goes unnoticed

- Ops routed to a remote MCP server (thin-client mode) don't take this path.
- The CLI_ONLY command path arms the same timer correctly — *after* the command completes, scoped around drain + disconnect (`cli.ts` ~line 1930).
- Most local shared ops (get_page, list, put of small pages) finish well under 10s.

But e.g. a local-engine `think`/`query` with an LLM call, or a `put_page` of a large multi-chunk page on a slow embed provider, can exceed 10s and gets silently killed with exit 0. The warning it prints ("engine.disconnect() did not return within 10000ms") is also misleading in that case — disconnect never ran.

## Suggested fix

Arm the timer in the `finally` block (immediately before the drain/disconnect sequence), matching the CLI_ONLY path's placement, so it bounds teardown rather than the whole op.

## Context

Found while debugging the facts:absorb abort class fixed in #2104 (the 10s cap is one of the reasons a longer exit-drain cannot rescue in-flight extraction work in one-shot CLI processes).

title: Gateway-native tool loop loses tool results on deepseek parallel tool calls; subagent model config keys inconsistent (models.subagent vs models.tier.subagent)
body:
## Summary
With `agent.use_gateway_loop=true`, subagent jobs running on `openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` die with:

```
[chat(openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash)] Tool results are missing for tool calls call_xxx, call_yyy.
```

The error message users hit first (`subagent job: resolved model ... is non-Anthropic but agent.use_gateway_loop is not enabled`) explicitly recommends enabling the gateway loop for non-Anthropic providers — but on deepseek the gateway loop then fails mid-conversation when the model emits parallel tool calls and the loop doesn't return results for all of them. Observed 6/8 dream-pipeline subagent jobs dead with this signature (v0.42.26.0).

## Repro
1. `gbrain config set models.subagent openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` (or models.default resolving there)
2. `gbrain config set agent.use_gateway_loop true`
3. Let the dream cycle enqueue a subagent job (multi-turn, tool-using synthesis prompt)
4. Job dead-letters after retries with "Tool results are missing for tool calls …"

## Expected
gateway.toolLoop() should return a tool_result for every tool_call id in the assistant turn (including parallel tool calls), or the gateway loop docs/error text should not recommend providers it can't drive.

## Side note — config key inconsistency
While remediating: the subagent handler reads `models.subagent` (`src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts:211` → `resolveModel(..., configKey: 'models.subagent')`) but the `subagent_capability` doctor hint tells users to set `models.tier.subagent`. One of the two should be canonical. Also `gbrain config set agent.use_gateway_loop true` warns `Nothing in gbrain reads this` (unregistered key) even though the subagent handler reads exactly that key via `engine.getConfig('agent.use_gateway_loop')`.

## Workaround used
Reverted the gateway loop and moved subagent jobs to `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` (set on BOTH `models.subagent` and `models.tier.subagent`).

title: facts extraction: finish_reason=length never checked — mandatory-reasoning models silently extract zero facts (maxTokens: 1500)
body:
## Version
gbrain 0.42.37.0

## Summary
`src/core/facts/extract.ts:182` hardcodes `maxTokens: 1500` for the extraction chat call, and the result path never inspects `finish_reason`. Models whose reasoning cannot be disabled and whose reasoning tokens count against the completion cap (e.g. `openrouter:google/gemini-3.5-flash` — the Gemini 3.x API rejects attempts to disable thinking with 400 "Reasoning is mandatory") burn ~1,400–1,500 tokens thinking, hit the cap, and return `finish_reason=length` with **empty content**. The 4-strategy JSON parser then finds nothing and the pipeline treats it as "no facts in this turn" — **silently**. No error, no log line distinguishing "model produced nothing" from "turn genuinely had no facts".

## Observed
- `facts.extraction_model = openrouter:google/gemini-3.5-flash`: 3/3 test calls died with `finish_reason=length`, reasoning tokens 1,437–1,496 of the 1,500 budget, zero visible output → 0 facts inserted, no error surfaced.
- Same prompt against the same model **without** a cap: completes fine, valid JSON.
- Result in production: ~30 pages ingested over 2 days extracted zero facts before we noticed (combined with the queue-abort issue #2108).

## Expected
Either of:
1. Check `finish_reason`. On `length` + empty/truncated content: log loudly (ingest_log), and ideally retry once with a raised cap.
2. Document that `facts.extraction_model` must be a non-reasoning (or reasoning-optional) model, and/or have `gbrain doctor` flag mandatory-reasoning models configured for capped call sites.

Related failure class: #1302 (judge phase truncated at a 4000-token cap).

title: subagent toolLoop: reasoning-model output breaks next-turn history — "Invalid prompt: messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema" (deterministic on DeepSeek V4, intermittent on Gemini 3.5 Flash)
body:
## Version
gbrain 0.42.37.0

## Summary
When `models.dream.synthesize` / `models.subagent` is a model that emits reasoning content, the multi-turn subagent loop (`src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts` → gateway toolLoop) intermittently or deterministically fails on the *next* call with the AI SDK validation error:

```
Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema.
```

Evidence points to reasoning/thinking parts of the assistant message being persisted into `subagent_messages` and rebuilt into the conversation history in a shape the AI SDK rejects on the subsequent turn/attempt.

## Observed (dream synthesize jobs, via OpenRouter)
- `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (thinking on by default): **deterministic** — 3/3 attempts fail with the schema error; job dead-letters after burning the full transcript input 3×.
- `google/gemini-3.5-flash` (thinking mandatory): **intermittent** — same job: attempts 1–2 fail with the schema error, attempt 3 succeeds cleanly (5 turns, end_turn). Retry roulette, ~2/3 of attempt budget wasted.
- `anthropic:` models (no reasoning emitted by default): never reproduced.

## Why this is distinct from (but related to) #1886 / #2039
#1886 covers dropped tool-result messages and #2039 covers crash-mid-round dangling tool-call tails. This report adds the **reasoning-content dimension**: with reasoning models the corruption occurs *without* any crash — a clean turn that includes reasoning parts is enough to poison the rebuilt history. Fix likely overlaps: strip/normalize reasoning parts when persisting and rebuilding history (most providers require either omitting reasoning or echoing it in a provider-specific field — e.g. DeepSeek's thinking mode returns 400 unless `reasoning_content` is handled per their spec).

## Repro sketch
1. `gbrain config set models.dream.synthesize openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`
2. Queue a synthesize job on any ≥2000-char transcript that triggers tool use (search + put_page).
3. Watch attempts 2..n fail with the ModelMessage[] schema error.

title: `gbrain search` post-print [last-retrieved] write-back fails with `UNDEFINED_VALUE: Undefined values are not allowed` on Postgres (0.42.40)
body:
### Version

gbrain 0.42.40.0 (clone @ `ecd6ae87`), Postgres engine (postgres.js client), macOS.

### Summary

On some `gbrain search` invocations, the post-print best-effort `[last-retrieved]` write-back fails with the postgres.js `UNDEFINED_VALUE` error: somewhere in the write-back path an `undefined` lands in a query parameter. Results print correctly; the failure is only the write-back. This is the same post-print seam as #1887, but a different failure: #1887 is the connection being torn down before the write (CONNECTION_ENDED / hang), while here the connection is alive and the write itself passes an undefined value.

### Repro

Reproduced twice on the same brain (before and after a pack migration, so not migration-related), with the same query both times:

```
$ gbrain search "acme freight" --limit 3
[0.9752] companies/acme-freight -- # Acme Freight

> Logistics company based in ...
[0.8636] people/jane-exampleton -- # Jane Exampleton

> Cloud architect at ...
[0.8236] people/sam-samplewood -- # Sam Samplewood

> Partner-program contact at ...
[last-retrieved] write-back failed (best-effort): UNDEFINED_VALUE: Undefined values are not allowed
```

(Page names above are synthetic; the real pages are ordinary company/person pages. The error line is verbatim.)

Not every query triggers it: on our brain, 5 other fixed queries run in the same sessions completed without the line, and this query produced it deterministically both times (identical result set both runs). That points at a property of the returned rows rather than timing: presumably one of the rows lacks a field the write-back binds without a null-coalesce.

### Observed

`[last-retrieved] write-back failed (best-effort): UNDEFINED_VALUE: Undefined values are not allowed` after correct results, exit 0.

### Expected

The write-back either binds defined values for every result row (coalescing optional fields to null) or skips rows it cannot bind, silently. A best-effort write should not surface a parameter-shape bug as a per-query error line.

### Local mitigation

None needed for correctness (results are unaffected); the line is noise in captured smoke-test output. Filing because UNDEFINED_VALUE indicates the write-back binds a field that can legitimately be absent, so some result sets never get their `last_retrieved` updated.

### Related

- #1887: same post-print write-back seam on Postgres, different failure (teardown race / hang). A fix that hardens the write-back path could address both.

title: `config get` reads only the DB plane -- a runtime-effective key in `~/.gbrain/config.json` reports not-found (`loadConfigWithEngine` exists but `get` does not use it)
body:
### Version

gbrain 0.42.40.0 (clone @ `ecd6ae87`), Postgres engine.

### Summary

`gbrain config get <key>` reads only the DB plane: `src/commands/config.ts:101` calls `engine.getConfig(key)` and reports not-found when that returns null. There is no file-plane fallback, even though the merged-read helper already exists (`loadConfigWithEngine` at `src/core/config.ts:501`). The result is the mirror image of the `config set anthropic_api_key` issue (filed separately): for keys that the runtime resolves from `~/.gbrain/config.json`, `set` writes a plane the runtime ignores, and `get` ignores the plane the runtime reads. The one CLI surface an operator uses to answer "what key is in effect?" can contradict actual runtime behavior in both directions.

### Repro

1. Postgres engine. Put `"anthropic_api_key": "<your-key>"` in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (the runtime-effective location; verify with `cd /tmp && gbrain think "Reply with the single word: pong"` succeeding with no env key).
2. Ensure no DB-plane row for the key (`gbrain config unset anthropic_api_key` if one exists).
3. `gbrain config get anthropic_api_key`

### Observed

Not-found / unset -- while the runtime happily resolves and uses the file-plane key (step 1's `think` probe succeeds from a keyless cwd).

### Expected

`config get` reports the effective value with its provenance, e.g. resolve env > file plane > DB plane and print which plane supplied it (`anthropic_api_key = <redacted> (file: ~/.gbrain/config.json)`, ideally redacted for `*_api_key` keys). The plumbing for a merged read exists (`loadConfigWithEngine`); `get` just does not call it.

### Local mitigation

Operator runbook: never trust `config get` for key state; verify rotation with a real runtime call from a keyless cwd (`cd /tmp && gbrain think ...`). That works but is tribal knowledge -- the CLI answer should not contradict the runtime.

### Related

- Companion issue: `config set anthropic_api_key` writes the DB plane the runtime never reads for keys -- #2119.
- #1025 (closed) is the earlier generic report of set/show plane confusion.

title: fix(cycle): recompute emotional weight after consolidate — take-receiving pages were stuck at emotional_weight=0
body:
## Problem

In incremental mode, the cycle's `recompute_emotional_weight` phase only recomputes `union(syncPagesAffected, synthesizeWrittenSlugs)`. But active takes — a direct input to `computeEmotionalWeight` (take density / avg weight / holder ratio) — are also created by the `consolidate` phase (facts→takes promotion), which:

1. runs **after** `recompute_emotional_weight` in the phase order, and
2. reports only counts in its `PhaseResult`, not which pages were affected.

So a page that gains an active take via consolidate — without being synced or synthesized that cycle — never gets its emotional weight recomputed: not this cycle (the phase already ran), and not in any later cycle (the page is never in the union). The weight stays at the column default of `0` indefinitely.

**Real-world impact:** after enabling `cycle.conversation_facts_backfill`, an operator brain accumulated **70 pages with active takes and `emotional_weight=0`** (surfaced by `doctor` as a `salience_health` WARN) — backfilled facts were promoted to takes by consolidate on pages the sync path never touched. Only a manual full walk (`gbrain dream --phase recompute_emotional_weight`) cleared it, and the pages would drift back to stale as consolidate kept writing takes.

## Investigation notes

- `propose_takes` does **not** need to feed the union: it only writes to the `take_proposals` queue; acceptance is manual and outside the cycle (D17).
- `grade_takes` auto-resolutions don't change weight inputs today: `resolveTake` stamps `resolved_*` columns but never flips `active`, and `batchLoadEmotionalInputs` aggregates only `active = TRUE` takes.
- That leaves **consolidate** as the only in-cycle mutator of emotional-weight inputs not covered by the union.

## Fix

- Move `recompute_emotional_weight` after `consolidate` in `ALL_PHASES` and in the `runCycle` dispatch order (it sat between `synthesize_concepts` and `consolidate`; the v0.29 ordering predates v0.31's consolidate). No intra-cycle phase consumes `emotional_weight`, so the move has no other ordering effects.
- `consolidate` now reports `details.pages_affected` — slugs of pages whose takes were created or refreshed this run (re-promotions included, so pre-fix brains self-heal as their clusters re-promote).
- `runCycle` captures those slugs (mirroring the `synthesize` `written_slugs` capture) and the incremental union becomes `sync ∪ synthesize ∪ consolidate`.

Behavioral note: `gbrain dream --phase consolidate,recompute_emotional_weight` previously did a *full* walk (no anchors); it now runs incrementally over consolidate's affected pages. `--phase recompute_emotional_weight` alone still does the full walk.

This PR also completes the embedding mock in `test/e2e/dream-cycle-phase-order-pglite.test.ts` (spread the real module, stub only the network-touching surface) — on master that test currently fails at import with `Export named 'willEmbedSynchronously' not found`, so the phase-order assertion this PR updates couldn't run at all.

## Tests

- New `test/cycle-consolidate-recompute-weight.test.ts`: seeds a page + 3 clustered unconsolidated facts (no sync/synthesize, no high-emotion tags), runs `--phase consolidate,recompute_emotional_weight`, and pins: phase ordering, `pages_affected` plumbing, `mode: 'incremental'`, same-cycle `emotional_weight > 0`, and that an untouched control page keeps its sentinel weight (no accidental full walk).
- Updated `test/e2e/dream-cycle-phase-order-pglite.test.ts` (`EXPECTED_PHASES` reorder) and `test/e2e/cycle-recompute-emotional-weight-pglite.test.ts` (position assertion now also pins `idx > consolidateIdx`).
- `bun test` over the six cycle/consolidate/recompute suites: 26 pass, 0 fail against this branch; `bun run typecheck` clean.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Takes created **outside** the cycle (`gbrain takes propose --accept N`, direct `add_take`) on never-synced pages still wait for the next full walk. A doctor auto-fix for `salience_health` (recompute the flagged slugs) would close that residual gap; happy to file it as an issue.

title: extract_atoms never stamps frontmatter.concepts — synthesize_concepts permanently skips ("no atoms with concept refs")
body:
## Summary

`extract_atoms` never writes the `concepts` frontmatter field that `synthesize_concepts` consumes, so the atoms → concepts pipeline is broken end-to-end: every cycle reports `synthesize_concepts: skipped — no atoms with concept refs`, no matter how many atoms accumulate.

## Evidence (v0.42.37.0 / current master)

**The consumer documents that the producer should stamp the field** — `src/core/cycle/synthesize-concepts.ts` header:

> 2. Group by `concepts:` frontmatter field on each atom (when the Haiku 3-check from extract_atoms decides "this atom is about concept X", it stamps the field).

and consumes ONLY that field (`synthesize-concepts.ts:92`):

```ts
concept_refs: r.frontmatter!.concepts!,
```

with atoms filtered by `Array.isArray(r.frontmatter?.concepts)`.

**The producer never stamps it** — `src/core/cycle/extract-atoms.ts` writes `type` / `atom_type` / `source_hash` / `source_slug` / `source_quote` / `lesson` / `virality_score` / `emotional_register` / `extracted_at` / `extracted_by`, but `grep -n "concepts" src/core/cycle/extract-atoms.ts` has zero hits in the frontmatter write path (page path and transcript path both).

## Reproduction (production brain, postgres engine, pack `gbrain-everything`)

1. Run cycles until atoms accumulate — we have **696 page-derived atoms** (`extracted_by: extract_atoms-v0.41.2.1`).
2. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages WHERE type='atom' AND frontmatter ? 'concepts'` → **0**.
3. Every `gbrain dream` reports `synthesize_concepts: skipped — no atoms with concept refs`.

## The consumer side works once fed

We validated the consumer by stamping `concepts` externally (1-3 kebab-case shared-vocabulary topic labels per atom, batch-labeled with one LLM call per 40 atoms): the very next `gbrain dream --phase synthesize_concepts` wrote **33 concept pages (T2=7, T3=26) from 60 stamped atoms**, $0.044, zero failures. So the fix is purely on the extractor side.

## Proposed fix (PR to follow)

Add `concepts` to the extractor's per-atom JSON contract — `"concepts": 1-3 kebab-case topic labels, reuse labels already seen in this run"` — validate kebab shape, and stamp the field in the same frontmatter write. One extra field in the existing extraction call; no new LLM round-trip. The shared-vocabulary instruction matters: labels must cluster (synthesize_concepts only materializes groups of ≥2), so the prompt should bias reuse-over-coinage.

Happy to send the PR — we're running this shape in production via an external backfill script and the tiering/synthesis downstream behaves exactly as the v0.41 design comment describes.

title: fix(jobs): refresh gateway config for queued AI work
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2088.

Long-lived Minion workers can outlive DB-backed AI gateway/model config changes. This refreshes the gateway immediately before queued gateway-backed jobs run, so worker-owned cycle/propose_takes work uses the operator's configured provider instead of a stale process-level Anthropic default.

Also fixes the `propose_takes` model metadata path:

- `propose_takes` now records `opts.model ?? getChatModel()` instead of hardcoding `claude-sonnet-4-6` in budget checks and `take_proposals.model`.
- Provider-qualified IDs like `openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` stay intact for budget/proposal metadata.
- `skipFence` is explicitly passed to the extractor so the default `skipPagesWithFence=true` behavior still truncates existing fence content before dedupe extraction.

## Why this is narrower than existing related PRs

Related open PR #1979 makes `propose_takes` fail softer when no Anthropic key exists. This PR fixes the root routing problem from #2088: queued worker jobs refresh and honor DB-backed gateway config before running, so a configured non-Anthropic provider is actually used by long-lived worker processes.

## Tests

- `bun test test/cycle-abort.test.ts test/handlers.test.ts test/propose-takes.test.ts --timeout 60000`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run verify`
- Codex autoreview on exact diff: `CLEAN`

## Notes

This keeps refresh scoped to gateway-backed built-in job names instead of every worker job, so non-AI maintenance jobs do not start failing because of unrelated provider config problems.

title: v0.42.41.0 fix: triage wave — 6 data-loss/availability fixes + 9 community PRs
body:
## Summary

A triage of open reports surfaced six bugs with no fix yet plus a batch of community PRs. This ships them together as one wave (v0.42.41.0), each authored fix with a regression test, each community PR reviewed against the cross-cutting invariants (fail-closed trust, source isolation, JSONB-no-stringify, engine parity, migration discipline).

**Authored critical fixes (no prior PR):**
- **#1928 — conversation facts survived a cycle.** The `extract_facts` reconcile delete-then-reinserts from a page's `## Facts` fence; conversation facts (`cli:`-origin) live on fenceless pages, so a cycle could delete them and reinsert nothing — a failed sync escalated it to a full-brain walk. Fix: exclude `cli:` facts from the wipe, don't inherit the failed-sync full-walk for the destructive phase, `warn` on net-negative reconcile.
- **#2018 — `put_page` write-through leaked into an unrelated source's repo.** It resolved the disk target from the global `sync.repo_path`; a default-source page (no `local_path`) got mirrored into a sibling federated source's working tree. Fix: mirror to the assigned source's own `local_path`; null `local_path` skips (sole-source falls back).
- **#2034 — autopilot crash-looped on transient DB errors.** Health-probe recovery called `connect()` with no args (config lost → throws every retry → FATAL). Fix: use `engine.reconnect()` (restores captured config); added `reconnect()` to both engines for parity; the supervisor reconnect path uses it too.
- **#2058 — concurrent PGLite processes corrupted the WAL.** A live holder's data-dir lock was stolen after 5min age alone. Fix: heartbeat while held + steal-grace; reaped only when the PID is dead or the heartbeat stalled past grace; a pid+acquired_at ownership token stops a resumed-stale holder from refreshing/removing the new owner's lock.
- **#2038 — timeline writes silently stopped.** A migration renumbered during a merge could be recorded-as-applied without its index DDL running, so every timeline insert failed its `ON CONFLICT`. Fix: an always-run, version-counter-blind drift probe in `runMigrations` (dedupe-then-rebuild keyed on index shape) + a `timeline_dedup_index` doctor check.
- **#2057 — the meetings timeline extractor swallowed batch errors.** Fix: surface `batch_errors` (stderr + non-zero exit); a Date-typed batch date round-trips (the `#1861` jsonb refactor already fixed the original `::text[]` cast — pinned by test).

**Community PRs merged (each reviewed):** #2064 (ignore cwd `.env` DATABASE_URL, closes #427), #2052 + #2020 (sync walker honors .gitignore, prunes vendor/dist/build/venv), #2033 (asymmetric embedding `input_type` across the AI SDK, supersedes #1400), #2074 (atomic `updateSourceConfig` JSONB merge), #2075 (doctor correctness pass), #2009 + #2072 (OAuth scope-default + legacy token source grants, shared scope parser), #2073 (search 10s force-exit + scoped call-graph + migration v116).

## Test Coverage

Each authored fix ships a regression test on both engines where engine-affecting:
- #1928 — `test/facts-reconcile-protect-cli.test.ts` (cli: facts survive; fence/empty-source deleted)
- #2018 — `test/write-through.test.ts` (+2: multi-source leak skipped; per-source local_path)
- #2034 — `test/pglite-reconnect.test.ts` (reconnect reuses saved config; no-op when unconnected)
- #2058 — `test/pglite-lock.test.ts` (+5: live heartbeating holder not stolen; dead PID reaped; stolen-lock not clobbered on release)
- #2038 — `test/timeline-dedup-repair.test.ts` (3-col drift healed; dupes deduped MIN(id) first; idempotent)
- #2057 — `test/timeline-date-batch.test.ts` (Date batch round-trips both engines)

Integrated targeted gate across all 6 fixes + the 9 PRs' test files: **327 pass / 0 fail**. `bun run typecheck` clean on the full merged tree. The full sharded unit suite runs in CI as the authoritative gate (the single-process `bun test` OOMs locally; the repo shards for this reason).

## Pre-Landing Review

Plan hardened by `/plan-eng-review` + a codex outside-voice pass (caught that 4 of 6 authored fixes were wrong/incomplete as first drafted — corrected before any code). A second codex adversarial pass on the **as-built** diff surfaced 4 more real issues, all fixed in this PR:
- #2058 lock ownership token (stolen-then-resumed holder must not clobber the new owner)
- #1928 destructive-full-walk guard misfired on a *skipped* (not failed) sync
- #2038 dedupe keeps `MIN(id)` not `MIN(ctid)` (deterministic, matches the existing migration rule)
- #2057 CLI caller now surfaces `batch_errors` instead of printing success over failed inserts

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Plan Completion

All 8 plan tasks complete (T1–T6 authored fixes, T7 PR wave, T8 ship). Plan + GSTACK REVIEW REPORT at `~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-zany-thacker.md`.

Filed 4 deferred follow-ups (eng-reviewed as separate scope): #1994 (supervisor backoff), #1963 (PGLite statement_timeout), #2050 (drain-worker self-deadlock), and a name-keyed migration ledger (#2038 structural follow-up).

Updated `docs/architecture/KEY_FILES.md` to current-state truth (no release-history clauses, per reference-doc discipline): write-through per-source `local_path` (#2018), `reconnect()` as a required lifecycle method (#2034), migration v116 + the always-run dedup self-heal (#2073/#2038), new entries for `timeline-dedup-repair.ts` + `timeline_dedup_index` doctor check (#2038) and `pglite-lock.ts` heartbeat + `GBRAIN_PGLITE_LOCK_STEAL_GRACE_SECONDS` (#2058), and `extract-facts.ts` cli:-protection + net-deletion warn (#1928). `bun run build:llms` + freshness/current-state guards green.

title: fix(code-graph): tag code_edges_symbol rows with source_id on extraction
body:
## Problem

`code_callers` / `code_callees` (and the `resolve_symbol_edges` pass) return `count: 0` / `status: "not_built"` even on brains whose `code_edges_symbol` table is fully populated, while `code_def` / `code_refs` work fine.

## Root cause

`importCodeFile` builds each `CodeEdgeInput` **without** `source_id`, so every extracted call-graph edge is persisted with `source_id = NULL` (`addCodeEdges` maps `e.source_id ?? null`). The reader paths are source-scoped:

- `getCallersOf` / `getCalleesOf` add `AND source_id = <scoped>` → the NULL rows are excluded → `count: 0`.
- `resolveSymbolEdgesIncremental` loads edges with `AND source_id = $2` → 0 rows → it resolves nothing yet still stamps `content_chunks.edges_backfilled_at`, so the chunks are marked done and not retried.

`source_id` is already in scope at the edge-building site (it's used a few lines above in `engine.getChunks(slug, { sourceId })`); it simply wasn't propagated onto the edge input.

`code_def` / `code_refs` are unaffected because they read `content_chunks` brain-wide, without the source filter — which is why the call graph looks "half-broken".

## Fix

Set `source_id: sourceId ?? 'default'` on the `CodeEdgeInput`, mirroring exactly how pages and chunks are persisted everywhere else in the same file (e.g. the `source_id: sourceId ?? 'default'` used around lines 333 and 1070). One line.

## Verify

On a brain with code under a named source: before, `code_callers <symbol>` returns `count: 0` / `not_built`; after a re-`sync` / `reindex-code` with the fix, edges are born tagged and `code_callers` / `code_callees` return `ready` with the correct callers. Verified end-to-end on a small repo (8 edges, all source-tagged) and at scale (~56k edges across 5 sources, 0 NULL).

title: feat: cost gates should respect tokenmax posture — blocking ConfirmationRequired wedges non-interactive syncs
body:
## Problem

The sync inline-embed cost gate (`sync.cost_gate_min_usd`, default $0.50) fires on every serial recovery sync of a large active brain, and there is no first-class way to say "this operator has decided cost is not the constraint — never gate."

On a 193K-page production brain in **tokenmax** posture (operator explicitly optimizing for maximum knowledge quality, not spend):

- `--skip-failed` is incompatible with `--parallel` (v0.42.x: failures log is brain-global, parallel acks race), so any sync that needs failure acknowledgment must drop to `--serial`
- `--serial` embeds **inline**, which arms the blocking `ConfirmationRequired` gate
- Routine daily syncs estimate ~$8 (155-160M new tokens), far above the $0.50 floor → **every cron sync blocks on a human confirmation**, and the brain silently stops embedding new content until someone notices

The operator's instruction was literally: "disable cost gates when token maxing mode." Today that takes archaeology: discovering `sync.cost_gate_min_usd` + `embed.backfill_max_usd_per_source_24h` (both `--force`-gated, undocumented in `config show`), and setting both to absurd sentinel values (100000) because `0`/`off` is rejected.

## Proposal

1. **Mode-aware gating (the right fix).** The brain already has a tokenmax search/quality mode concept. When the operator has expressed tokenmax intent — e.g. `gbrain config set spend_posture tokenmax` — *all* cost gates (sync inline gate, embed backfill 24h cap, enrich/onboard `--max-usd` prompts) should default to **informational FYI, never blocking**. Print the estimate, proceed, log to the spend ledger.

2. **First-class off switch.** Accept `0` / `off` / `unlimited` on `sync.cost_gate_min_usd` and `embed.backfill_max_usd_per_source_24h` instead of silently falling back to defaults — sentinel-large-number configuration is a smell.

3. **Non-interactive contexts should defer, not block.** When stdin is not a TTY (cron/agent), a blocking ConfirmationRequired gate guarantees a wedged pipeline. The deferred-backfill path (federated_v2) already has the right shape — make non-TTY serial syncs auto-defer embeds to the capped backfill job instead of exiting 2.

4. **Document the spend-control surface** in one place: every gate, its key, default, and how to widen/disable.

## Related
- The `--skip-failed` x `--parallel` incompatibility is what forces serial (and thus inline-embed gating) in the first place — fixing that (per-source failure acks?) would also defuse this.

## Environment
- gbrain 0.42.39.0, Postgres engine, 193K pages, 4 sources
- Daily `sync --all` cron; gate fired 4 consecutive days; embeds silently stalled each time until manually approved

title: v0.42.42.0 fix(cli): bounded teardown + explicit exit — kill the 10s force-exit tax on txn-mode poolers (#2084)
body:
Closes #2084

## Summary

**The fix (#2084 — residual of #1972):** `gbrain query` on transaction-mode poolers paid a flat 10s teardown tax and exited via the force-exit banner on every invocation. Two stacked defects: the hard-deadline timer armed *before* the op handler (so handler time burned the teardown budget, and any >10s op was silently killed mid-run with exit 0 and truncated output), and the clean path never exited explicitly — it waited for Bun's event loop to drain, which a stuck pooler socket holds open forever.

**Teardown contract** (`feat(core)` + `fix(cli)`): `finishCliTeardown` (src/core/cli-force-exit.ts) owns bounded drain → bounded disconnect under a backstop whose deadline is **computed from the bounds it guards** (fires only when a component violated its own bound; `GBRAIN_TEARDOWN_DEADLINE_MS` override). All nine cli.ts disconnect sites route through it (op-dispatch, fall-through, search dashboard, sources, dream, doctor ×3 — fixing a pre-existing pool leak — and ze-switch; closes the #1972-era drain-before-owner-disconnect TODO). The ONE process exit lives in `main().then/catch`: `flushThenExit` fences stdio, holds a ref'd aliveness grace (`GBRAIN_FLUSH_GRACE_MS`, default 250ms on pipes / 0 on TTY), then exits — Bun delivers queued pipe writes only while the process is alive (no flush API reaches the native queue; verified by probes), so the grace *is* the flush (#1959 class).

**Exit-code integrity** (`fix(pglite)`): PGLite's Emscripten runtime writes its own status into `process.exitCode` at arbitrary points mid-run (99 at create; in-memory initdb status on a later tick; 0 at close) — every error exit on PGLite has been reporting success. The verdict now lives in a gbrain-owned channel (`setCliExitVerdict`/`currentExitCode`; 12 writer sites converted); `PGlite.create` is wrapped in `preservingProcessExitCode` (close deliberately unwrapped — its 0-write is baseline behavior test runners depend on).

**Adversarial hardening** (cross-model, both reviewers P1'd it): `shouldForceExitAfterMain` now resolves the command through `parseGlobalFlags` — the old first-non-dash heuristic read `gbrain --timeout 30s serve` as command `30s` and the new seam would have killed the daemon ~250ms after boot. Plus: ref'd backstop (a hung teardown on an empty loop previously exited naturally, skipping the flush), per-process exit latch, drain defense-in-depth.

**Tests & infra**: 3 new test files (teardown units, spawned-Bun flush harness proving 4MB byte-complete to a late reader), extended e2e (error-path exit 1, all nine swept commands spawned with brain-copy isolation, slow-handler regression via the deadline knob, piped-JSON parse-complete, banner absence everywhere, daemon survival untouched), structural pins (no bare awaited disconnects in cli.ts; `DISCONNECT_HARD_DEADLINE_MS` gone). Also fixed two pre-existing R1 env-isolation violations that failed `bun run verify` on master (superseded by master's own equivalent fixes in the merge).

## Test Coverage

title: Add artifact attestations for release binaries
body:
## Improvement opportunity

Add GitHub artifact attestations for the compiled release binaries produced by `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

## Evidence inspected

Repo-local evidence:

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:27-33` runs `bun build --compile` for `gbrain-darwin-arm64` and `gbrain-linux-x64`, then uploads those binaries as workflow artifacts.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:39-47` downloads those artifacts and publishes the same binaries into the GitHub Release.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:7-8` only grants `contents: write`. There is no `id-token: write` or `attestations: write` permission, and no `actions/attest` / `actions/attest-build-provenance` step.
- Repository workflow scan found pinned action usage and least-privilege read permissions in the test workflows, so this is a focused release-provenance gap rather than a broad Actions-hardening request.

Current baseline:

- GitHub artifact attestations establish where and how build artifacts were produced.
- GitHub's documented binary flow requires `id-token: write`, `contents: read`, `attestations: write`, and an `actions/attest@v4` step with `subject-path` pointed at the built binary.
- Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/using-artifact-attestations/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds

## Expected impact

Users downloading `gbrain-darwin-arm64` or `gbrain-linux-x64` from a release should be able to verify the binary's provenance with `gh attestation verify ... -R garrytan/gbrain`. That gives release consumers a machine-checkable link from the downloaded binary back to the repository's release workflow run, improving supply-chain integrity without changing the CLI runtime.

## Suggested fix

Keep this scoped to the release workflow:

1. Move the release workflow permissions to job-level least privilege:
   - `build`: `contents: read`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`
   - `release`: `contents: write`
2. After each `bun build --compile ... --outfile bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}` step, add an attestation step for `bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}`.
3. Pin the attestation action consistently with the rest of this repo's workflows. The existing workflows pin `actions/checkout`, `setup-bun`, `upload-artifact`, `download-artifact`, and `softprops/action-gh-release` by commit SHA.
4. Optionally add a short release note or README snippet showing:

```bash
gh attestation verify ./gbrain-linux-x64 -R garrytan/gbrain
gh attestation verify ./gbrain-darwin-arm64 -R garrytan/gbrain
```

## Duplicate check

I inspected the required open items with `gh` before filing:

- `gh issue list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,url,labels,updatedAt`
  - 200 open issues inspected, covering #2140 through #1520 in the returned set.
- `gh pr list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,url,headRefName,isDraft,updatedAt`
  - 200 open PRs inspected, covering #2135 through #1276 in the returned set.

Title/body keyword scans for the specific release-provenance terms found no covering open issue or PR:

- `artifact attestation`
- `artifact attestations`
- `attest-build-provenance`
- `actions/attest`
- `build provenance`
- `release provenance`

I also searched all open GitHub issues/PRs through `gh api -X GET /search/issues` for the same terms, including `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "artifact attestation"`, `"attest-build-provenance"`, `"actions/attest"`, `"build provenance"`, `"release provenance"`, `SLSA`, and `"binary provenance"`; those searches returned no covering items.

## Commands/files inspected

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`

title: doctor validates only models.tier.subagent — an unresolvable chat_model/models.default silently kills the chat touchpoint (green)
body:
## Summary

`doctor`'s model check only validates `models.tier.subagent`. If `chat_model` / `models.default` is set to a string that `resolveRecipe()` cannot parse — e.g. a **bare, prefix-less id** (`grok-4.3`) or an unknown provider — the **chat touchpoint silently dies and `doctor` stays green**: `isAvailable('chat')` catches the `parseModelId` throw and returns `false`, so the chat-gated consumers no-op.

Reproduced live on **0.42.40.0** (master HEAD).

## Repro

1. `gbrain config set chat_model grok-4.3` (a bare id; gbrain has no xAI/grok recipe and the id has no provider prefix).
2. `resolveRecipe("grok-4.3")` → **throws** `Model id "grok-4.3" is missing a provider prefix`.
3. `gbrain providers test --touchpoint chat` → `Chat provider not configured or not ready.`
4. `gbrain doctor` → **green** for chat; it WARNs only on `models.tier.subagent`.

## What silently breaks

`isAvailable('chat')` swallows the resolve throw into `false` (`src/core/ai/gateway.ts:797`), which disables every chat-gated consumer:
- LLM fact extraction → returns `[]` (`src/core/facts/extract.ts:159`)
- classify dedup → falls back to cosine (`src/core/facts/classify.ts:98`)
- query-intent expansion → falls back (`src/core/search/llm-intent.ts:48`)
- `enrich_thin` → skipped every cycle (`src/core/cycle/enrich-thin.ts:158`)

The **subagent** tier is handled gracefully (`enforceSubagentCapable` falls back + warns — the only thing `doctor` surfaces). The chat/reasoning tiers get no such treatment, so an operator who points the main model at an unresolvable id ends up with a quietly degraded brain and a green health check.

## Suggested fix

- `doctor` should validate `chat_model` and `models.default` (not just `models.tier.subagent`) via a `resolveRecipe` dry-run, and WARN/FAIL loudly when they don't resolve.
- `isAvailable('chat')` should distinguish an **unresolvable-config throw** (loud config error) from a **missing-key `false`** (legitimately unavailable).
- Apply the subagent tier's `enforceSubagentCapable` graceful-degrade to the chat/reasoning tiers.

Same silent-degradation class as the propose_takes / facts-pipeline issues (see #2106).

title: Optional LLM cycle phases grade_takes + calibration_profile lack the cycle.<phase>.enabled gate other optional phases have
body:
## Summary

The optional LLM-using cycle phases **`grade_takes`** and **`calibration_profile`** are dispatched unconditionally from `ALL_PHASES` with **no `cycle.<phase>.enabled` gate** — unlike the other optional phases (`skillopt`, `conversation_facts_backfill`, `enrich_thin`), each of which reads such a key and skips when false. So an operator cannot turn these LLM phases off without patching the source.

This is the same gap `propose_takes` had (see #2106 / #1467) — an expensive optional phase, default-ON, in `ALL_PHASES`, with no off-switch.

Observed on **0.42.40.0** (master HEAD).

## Evidence

- `grade_takes`: in `ALL_PHASES` (`src/core/cycle.ts:152`), dispatched unconditionally at `src/core/cycle.ts:1995-2004` — no `cycle.grade_takes.enabled` check. It also ships a **stub evidence retriever** that its own docstring calls near-worthless: `defaultEvidenceRetriever` returns the literal `[evidence retrieval not yet wired — v0.36.1.0 ship-state]` plus the take's own claim as "evidence" (`src/core/cycle/grade-takes.ts:294-305`); the file docstring (`:24-37`) states "Most verdicts produced by the stub-judge against the stub-evidence will be unresolvable."
- `calibration_profile`: in `ALL_PHASES` (`src/core/cycle.ts:153`), dispatched unconditionally at `src/core/cycle.ts:2006-2014` — no `cycle.calibration_profile.enabled` check.

The only per-phase control today is `cycle.<phase>.budget_usd`, which is **not** a reliable off-switch (`budget_usd <= 0` *disables* the cap and runs uncapped — separate issue).

## Suggested fix

Give each optional cycle phase a `cycle.<phase>.enabled` gate (default-ON for back-compat) that, when false, pushes a `skipped` PhaseResult — mirroring the existing `skillopt` / `conversation_facts_backfill` wrappers. This lets operators disable phases that are dormant or undesirable on their deployment without a fork patch.

title: grade_takes: a thrown judge error writes no take_grade_cache row → a persistently-failing take is re-judged (LLM) every cycle
body:
## Summary

`grade_takes` re-LLMs a **persistently-failing** take on every cycle, because a thrown judge error writes no `take_grade_cache` row. Same negative-result-cache gap as `propose_takes` (#2106), in a different phase.

Observed on **0.42.40.0** (master HEAD).

## Mechanism

- Dedup SELECT keyed on `(take_id, prompt_version, judge_model_id, evidence_signature)` — `src/core/cycle/grade-takes.ts:443-452`.
- Cache row is INSERTed **only on success** — `src/core/cycle/grade-takes.ts:544-551`.
- `defaultJudge` (`:310-340`) caches **parse** failures as a synthetic `unresolvable@0.0` row. But a **thrown** `gatewayChat` error (model-resolution `AIConfigError`, revoked key, network, rate-limit) propagates up to `:472-476`, which does `warnings.push(...); continue;` and **writes no row**.
- → next cycle the dedup SELECT never matches that take → it is re-judged (LLM) again, forever, as long as it keeps erroring.

(Bounded today by `takeLimit` ~50/cycle, and currently dormant because no takes are old enough to grade — but the pattern is the same forever-reprocess shape as #2106.)

## Suggested fix

On a **persistent** judge throw (config / model-resolution / auth error class), write a negative-cache row (verdict `unresolvable`, confidence 0, applied false, plus an error marker e.g. `reasoning='judge_error:<code>'`) keyed on the same composite, so the next dedup SELECT hits and the take isn't re-judged.

Gate on error class: do **not** cache transient failures (rate-limit / 5xx / network) so genuine transients still retry. Optionally add max-retry/backoff.

title: BudgetMeter cap is unenforceable for unpriced/non-Anthropic models and disabled at budget_usd<=0; synthesize/patterns bypass it
body:
## Summary

The per-cycle `BudgetMeter` cost cap is **unenforceable for unpriced / non-Anthropic models** and is **disabled when `budget_usd <= 0`** — so on an OpenRouter (or any non-native-Anthropic) deployment the cap never trips. Separately, `synthesize` / `patterns` subagent spend bypasses the meter entirely, leaving the `dream-budget` ledger blind.

Observed on **0.42.40.0** (master HEAD).

## Cap unenforceable for unpriced models

`src/core/cycle/budget-meter.ts:92-119`: when `estimateMaxCostUsd` returns `null` (the model isn't in `ANTHROPIC_PRICING`), the meter writes a `submit_unpriced` ledger line and returns `{allowed: true}`. Because `splitProviderModelId` splits on the **leading** colon (OpenRouter markup ≠ native Anthropic pricing), any `openrouter:*` id (e.g. `openrouter:anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`, `openrouter:auto`) yields a tail that isn't a pricing key → `null` cost → **bypass**. So the per-cycle `budget_usd` cap **never fires** on an OpenRouter deployment.

Runtime-proven: a week of `dream-budget` telemetry shows thousands of `submit_unpriced` events on `openrouter:auto` with the cap never tripping.

`BudgetTracker` has the stricter contract this should mirror: it hard-throws `BudgetExhausted(no_pricing)` when a cap is set and pricing is unavailable.

## `budget_usd <= 0` disables the cap

`src/core/cycle/budget-meter.ts:121-135`: `budgetUsd <= 0` is treated as "budget disabled" → every submit allowed (uncapped). This is a footgun — an operator who sets a phase's `budget_usd` to `0` to *stop* it actually makes it run **uncapped**.

## Telemetry blind spot

`synthesize` (`src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts:483`) and `patterns` (`src/core/cycle/patterns.ts:88`) spend LLM via subagents that **bypass BudgetMeter** (wired at only `drift.ts:137`, `auto-think.ts:111`, `base-phase.ts:167`; the base-phase header explicitly notes synthesize/patterns are not retrofitted). Their spend never lands in `dream-budget-*.jsonl`, so an operator reading that ledger is blind to it.

## Suggested fix

- When `budget_usd > 0` and `estimateMaxCostUsd` returns `null`, do **not** return `{allowed: true}` — price off the inner provider tail (with optional markup), or fail-closed / surface a loud "cap-unenforceable" status. Add an OpenRouter/non-Anthropic pricing path so live model strings price non-null.
- Reconsider the `budget_usd <= 0` = "disabled" semantics (it's an easy way to accidentally run uncapped).
- Wrap the `synthesize` / `patterns` subagent fan-outs in the budget meter/tracker (or retrofit them onto `BaseCyclePhase`) so their spend is metered and ledgered.

title: parseMarkdown flags MISSING_CLOSE on valid YAML # comment lines inside the frontmatter fence
body:
**What happened?**

`parseMarkdown` (in `src/core/markdown.ts`) raises a `MISSING_CLOSE` validation error on a file whose YAML frontmatter
starts with one or more `#` comment lines, even when the closing `---` is present. The cause is the scanner at lines
~219-248: it walks the lines after the opening `---` and records the first `^#{1,6}\s`-shaped line as
`headingBeforeClose`. When the closing fence is later found, the scanner still flags the recorded "heading" as a
MISSING_CLOSE finding with the message `Heading at line N found inside frontmatter zone (closing --- comes after)`. The
line is a perfectly valid YAML comment, not a markdown heading.

YAML permits `#` comments anywhere outside string scalars, so a leading-`#` line inside the fence is a comment by
definition. The heading-shape heuristic was meant to catch unclosed frontmatter; using it inside a fence that DOES close
is the false-positive.

**What did you expect?**

The parser should accept the file (no `MISSING_CLOSE` finding) when the closing `---` is present, regardless of `#`
comment lines that appear between the fences.

**Steps to reproduce**

Create a markdown file with YAML comment lines at the top of its frontmatter:

```markdown
---
# Research Template
# This file serves as a template for all research findings

research_id: "R19"
title: "iOS App Clip security limitations"
---

body
```

Run `bun test --bail test/markdown-validation.test.ts` against a test that calls `parseMarkdown(md, undefined, {
validate: true })` on the content above and asserts the errors list does not contain `MISSING_CLOSE`. With current
master at `4ee530f3` (v0.42.42.0), the assertion fails. The errors list contains a `MISSING_CLOSE` with the message
`Heading at line 2 found inside frontmatter zone (closing --- comes after)`.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: master at `4ee530f3` (v0.42.42.0)
- OS: Linux
- Bun: 1.3.14
- Database: not relevant (the bug is in pure string parsing; no engine state involved)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**

Not material, because the bug is in `src/core/markdown.ts:collectValidationErrors` and reproduces against unit tests
without any engine state. The bug-report template's doctor-output paste block is included for completeness:

```text
(omitted — reproducible without a connected engine)
```

**Adjacent context**

- v0.37.5.0 (#1229) fixed the same parser's `NESTED_QUOTES` validator to stop flagging valid YAML: direct precedent for
  this fix's shape. The proposed fix in the paired PR follows the same "stop the false positive without weakening the
  genuine-error path" pattern.
- #1074 (`frontmatter audit: false-positive MISSING_OPEN on convention plain-markdown files`) is the closest open
  neighbor: same parser, different error code, same class of false-positive. The two fixes are independent and
  non-conflicting.

**Proposed fix**

When walking lines between the opening `---` and the closing `---`, do NOT track a `headingBeforeClose`. Once the
closing `---` is found, content between the fences is YAML by definition; `#` lines are comments. The heading hint
remains valuable in the genuine-missing-close branch (still surface the first heading-shaped line so the error message
points the user at the right line). Paired PR: #2153.

title: fix(markdown): treat `#` lines inside closed frontmatter as YAML comments, not headings
body:
Closes #2152

## Summary

**The bug.** `parseMarkdown` walked the lines after the opening `---` and recorded the first `^#{1,6}\s`-shaped line as
`headingBeforeClose`. When the closing `---` was later found, the scanner still flagged the recorded line as
`MISSING_CLOSE` with `Heading at line N found inside frontmatter zone (closing --- comes after)`. But `#` lines inside a
closed YAML fence are comments by spec, not markdown headings. Templates that lead their frontmatter with annotation
comments (e.g. `# Research Template` above the keys) tripped the false positive on every parse.

**The fix.** Only walk for the closing `---`. When it is found, content between the fences is YAML; `#` lines are
comments, not headings. When the close is genuinely missing, surface the first heading-shaped line as the
where-it-went-off-the-rails hint (this branch was already correct and preserved verbatim).

**Precedent.** v0.37.5.0 (#1229) `fix(markdown): YAML-aware NESTED_QUOTES validator (stops flagging valid YAML)` is the
twin pattern: same parser, same "stop the false positive without weakening the genuine-error path."

## Tests

- `bun test test/markdown-validation.test.ts` → 27 pass / 0 fail (25 prior + 2 new regression tests covering YAML `#`
  comments at the top of a closed frontmatter and `#` comments interleaved with keys). 33 expect() calls.
- `bun test test/markdown.test.ts test/lint-frontmatter.test.ts test/doctor-frontmatter-partial.test.ts
  test/frontmatter-cli.test.ts` → 68 pass / 0 fail across the four adjacent test files. 146 expect() calls.
- `bun run verify` → 30/30 checks green in 10s, exit 0.
- `bun run typecheck` → exit 0, no diagnostics.

title: feat(ai/ollama): accept passthrough dims + register qwen3-embed-8b / snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2
body:
Closes #2271

Companion to #1072 (the openai-compat `dimensions` dispatch-side fix). The two patches are orthogonal and independently useful but together enable running gbrain on Qwen3 / non-nomic Ollama models end-to-end. Either order of landing works.

## Summary

The Ollama recipe accepts the modern embedding models at their native dims with no operator-side workaround after this PR. Two coupled changes:

- **Validator passthrough tier** in `src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts` so Ollama (by id) and any recipe with `touchpoints.embedding.user_provided_models === true` (llama-server, litellm-proxy) accept any positive integer dim up to `PGVECTOR_COLUMN_MAX_DIMS`.
- **Model registrations** in `src/core/ai/recipes/ollama.ts` so `qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` join the recognized-models list, making them discoverable via `gbrain models` and resolvable via the standard resolver path.

## Before this PR

| Surface                                                                                        | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:mxbai-embed-large --embedding-dimensions 1024`           | Preflight rejects: `Provider "ollama" model "mxbai-embed-large" does not support custom dimensions 1024 (this model only emits its default vector size).` The recipe declares `default_dims: 768` and gates every model against it. |
| `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:qwen3-embed-8b --embedding-dimensions 4096`              | Same rejection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2 --embedding-dimensions 1024` | Same rejection. The model isn't in the recipe's known list, so even after the validator relaxation it would still need explicit `ollama:<exotic>` syntax.                                                                           |
| `gbrain models` output                                                                         | `qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` not in the recognized-models list.                                                                                                                                               |
| `llama-server` / `litellm-proxy` embeddings                                                    | Same gate fires because Tier 3 rejects whatever dim the user picks even though those recipes declare `user_provided_models: true`.                                                                                                  |

## After this PR

| Surface                                              | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any modern Ollama embedding model at its native dim  | Accepts cleanly. `mxbai-embed-large @ 1024`, `qwen3-embed-8b @ 4096`, `snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2 @ 1024`, `qwen3-embedding:4b @ 1536` (Matryoshka), `qwen3-embedding:8b @ 4096` (native). |
| `gbrain models`                                      | Lists `qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` as recognized Ollama models.                                                                                                       |
| `llama-server` / `litellm-proxy` embeddings          | Accept user-chosen dims (the recipes already declare `user_provided_models: true`; the validator now respects the flag).                                                                    |
| `gbrain init --embedding-model voyage:voyage-3-lite` | Behavior unchanged because voyage has a real Matryoshka allow-list which still applies. The passthrough tier only fires for passthrough-shaped recipes.                                     |
| `PGVECTOR_COLUMN_MAX_DIMS` cap                       | Still enforced. `validateDimAgainstTouchpoint` runs before this function and rejects dims above the column cap or non-positive integers.                                                    |

## Why the validation tier (not extending `dims_options`)

Two viable shapes were considered:

1. Extend `dims_options` on each passthrough recipe to enumerate the common dims (384 / 768 / 1024 / 4096 / …). Cheap, but lossy and unmaintainable: Ollama is a passthrough. Any model the user can `ollama pull` is fair game, and any native dim is a candidate. Today's list misses tomorrow's model.
2. Recognize the passthrough class at validation time. Local-backend recipes have no business gating dims when the local model decides for itself; the only sensible upper bound is the `PGVECTOR_COLUMN_MAX_DIMS` cap pgvector itself enforces.

This PR is shape #2. The new tier sits between the provider-specific Matryoshka allow-lists and the final fallback, so existing recipes that DO declare `dims_options` (or fall under a known allow-list like voyage/zeroentropy/openai) keep their current behavior unchanged.

Detection of passthrough recipes:

- `recipe.id === 'ollama'`. The recipe ships an illustrative `models` list, so the existing `user_provided_models` flag (which assumes `models: []`) doesn't apply. Recognize Ollama by id.
- `recipe.touchpoints.embedding?.user_provided_models === true` (covers llama-server, litellm-proxy, and any future bring-your-own-backend recipe without a per-id update).

## Model registrations

The 2nd commit adds `qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` to the recipe's `models` list. These are the two modern Ollama embedding models that surface immediately after the validator relaxation as "registered but not in the list" gaps. Future passthrough-recognized models can be added in the same way as they become widely deployed; the validator change covers anyone running an arbitrary `ollama pull`-able model.

## Tests

- `bun test test/embedding-dim-check.test.ts` → 36/36 pass (existing 27 untouched, 9 new in the `passthrough recipes accept arbitrary positive dims` describe block). New cases cover: ollama/mxbai @ 1024, ollama/qwen3-embedding:4b @ 1536 (Matryoshka), ollama/qwen3-embedding:8b @ 4096 (native), ollama/snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2 @ 1024, llama-server @ explicit dim, litellm @ explicit dim. Negative cases: ollama rejected above pgvector cap, ollama rejected on negative, llama-server still demands explicit `--embedding-dimensions`.
- `bun test test/ai/` → 335/335 pass on master + this change.
- `bun test test/brain-score-recommendations.test.ts test/embed-input-type-wire.serial.test.ts test/e2e/v0_28_5-fix-wave.test.ts` → 44/44 pass (every other test file that touches ollama / llama-server / litellm strings).
- `bun run typecheck` clean.
- Manual: `gbrain init` against a fresh PGLite with each of the four target model + dim pairings; all four accept; pages embed and round-trip.

## Notes

- The Ollama recipe's `models` list is illustrative rather than authoritative for an arbitrary `ollama pull`. This PR registers the two specific modern embedding models that have material recognition value (`qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2`) but a future cleanup could either drop the list entirely (documenting that any `ollama pull`-able embedding model works) or expand it as a discovery hint. Neither is required to land this fix.

title: gbrain onboard --apply --auto returns "Nothing to do" while --check --explain shows auto-eligible recommendations
body:
**What happened?**

`gbrain onboard --apply --auto --max-usd N --target-score N` returns `Brain at score X/100, target Y/100. Nothing to do.` even when `gbrain onboard --check --explain` lists several auto-eligible onboard-check recommendations (e.g. `extract-ner`, `extract-timeline-from-meetings`). The check path threads `extraRemediations` into the planner correctly; the apply path never receives them.

Diagnosis:

- `commands/onboard.ts:105-106` gathers `extraRemediations` via `runAllOnboardChecks(engine).flatMap(r => r.remediations)`.
- `commands/onboard.ts:109` (the `--check` branch) passes `{ targetScore, extraRemediations }` to `computeRemediationPlan`.
- `commands/onboard.ts:129` (the `--apply --auto` branch) calls `runRemediation(engine, { targetScore, maxUsd }, hooks)` with no `extraRemediations` field.
- Downstream, `core/remediation/run.ts:71` builds the pre-flight plan via `computeRemediationPlan(engine, { targetScore })` with no extras, and `core/remediation/run.ts:90` calls `computeRecommendations(initialHealth, ctx)` with the default empty `extraRemediations = []`. Only generic brain_score remediations (sync, embed, etc.) reach the runner. For a brain that's clean on those (0 stale pages, 0 missing embeddings), `recs.length === 0` and the runner fires `onNothingToDo`.

`RemediationOpts` (`core/remediation/types.ts`) has no `extraRemediations` field, so the gap is structural — even if the caller wanted to pass extras through `runRemediation`, the type signature does not accept them.

**What did you expect?**

`onboard --apply --auto` should submit jobs for every auto-eligible recommendation that `onboard --check --explain` would surface, scoped by `--max-usd` and `--target-score`. The two paths should agree on which remediations are in scope.

**Steps to reproduce (deterministic)**

1. `gbrain init` against a fresh PGLite (or Postgres) engine.
2. `gbrain sources add <id> --path <dir-with-markdown> --federated` against a corpus where `entity_link_coverage` and `timeline_coverage` will report below target after sync (e.g. markdown with meeting notes but no extracted entities or timeline).
3. `gbrain sync --source <id>`: drives `embed_coverage` to 100% but leaves entity/timeline coverage below target.
4. `gbrain onboard --check --explain`: lists `extract-ner` / `extract-timeline-from-meetings` (or similar) as auto-eligible.
5. `gbrain onboard --apply --auto --max-usd 5 --target-score 70`: prints `Brain at score X/100, target Y/100. Nothing to do.` instantly. No jobs queued in `minion_jobs`.

Observed on master at `4ee530f3` (v0.42.42.0), reproduced against both PGLite and Postgres 16 + pgvector 0.8.2.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: master at `4ee530f3` (v0.42.42.0)
- OS: Linux
- Bun: 1.3.14
- Database: PGLite + Postgres 16 / pgvector 0.8.2 (both reproduce)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**

Not material to the bug. The plan envelope returned by `computeRemediationPlan` is the same shape; the bug is that `runRemediation` calls the planner without the extras and stops before any work is dispatched. `doctor` itself is unaffected.

**Proposed fix**

Add `extraRemediations?: RemediationStep[]` to `RemediationOpts`, read it in `runRemediation` (`core/remediation/run.ts`), and thread it into both `computeRemediationPlan` (line 71) and `computeRecommendations` (line 90). Then update `commands/onboard.ts:129` to pass the already-gathered `extraRemediations` the same way line 109 (the `--check` branch) already does. Three-file, ~15-line patch.

A regression test would feed `runRemediation` an extra step that the brain_score generator never emits (e.g. `extract-ner`) and assert it appears in `result.submitted`.

**Adjacent observation (separate issue if confirmed worth)**

`onboard --apply --auto` has an undocumented prereq: a worker (`gbrain jobs work` or `gbrain autopilot`) must be running to claim queued jobs. With the patch above landed, the apply path correctly queues jobs; with no worker `attempts_started` stays 0 and onboard times out at 540s (`error: timeout after 540007ms waiting for job 1`). The failure mode reads as a broken handler. A heartbeat check on `minion_jobs` emitting a one-line hint when no row has `attempts_started > 0` within K seconds, or a docs touch in `gbrain onboard --help`, would close the gap. Happy to file a follow-up.
