title: synthesize_concepts writes concept pages that are never chunked/embedded → unreachable by retrieval despite source-boost 1.3×
body:
## Summary

`synthesize_concepts` writes `concepts/` pages via `putPage`, but those pages end up with **0 `content_chunks` and a NULL embedding** — so they are invisible to `query` (vector retrieval) and effectively unreachable. This is despite `src/core/search/source-boost.ts` assigning `'concepts/': 1.3`, i.e. the retrieval layer is explicitly designed to rank concept pages *above* bulk content. In practice that boost is dead — there are no concept chunks to boost.

The CHANGELOG's own worked example shows the intended behavior (`concepts/widget-pattern` → "returned (rank 1)"), but a deployment whose concept pages are never embedded can never reproduce it.

## Environment

Observed on a v0.42.x deployment. Verified the gap still exists on `main` at **v0.42.42**: `src/core/cycle/synthesize-concepts.ts` still only calls `engine.putPage('concepts/${title}', …)` with no chunk/embed step, and the header comment still reads `// … dedup-by-embedding-similarity ship in v0.42+.`

## Evidence (deployment with ~1,700 concept pages)

- `SELECT count(*) FROM content_chunks c JOIN pages p ON p.id = c.page_id WHERE p.slug LIKE 'concepts/%'` → **0**
- Every `concepts/` page has `embedding_signature IS NULL`.
- A 20-question retrieval probe (questions chosen to match concept topics) returned a concept page in top-5 in **0/20** cases.
- FTS `search` also fails to surface them even on near-verbatim title queries: the pages *do* have `search_vector` populated, but being short they are out-ranked by longer pages and fall below the result limit.
- **Control:** `distilled/` and `dream-cycle-summaries/` pages (also dream-generated) *do* have chunks. So the `dream_generated` anti-loop guard is not the cause — it is specific to the `synthesize_concepts` (and `extract_atoms`) write path.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** concept pages — the curated "distilled framework" output the schema treats as first-class and `source-boost.ts` prioritizes at 1.3× — should be in the retrieval surface (chunked + embedded) so `query`/`search` can return them.
- **Actual:** `synthesize_concepts` writes them but they are never chunked/embedded, so they are unreachable via the primary retrieval paths.

## Possible directions (maintainers to weigh)

1. Have `synthesize_concepts` enqueue chunking/embedding for the concept pages it writes. This is the natural home and it composes with the planned v0.42+ embedding-similarity dedup, which will need concept embeddings anyway.
2. Alternatively, document that concepts need a separate `reindex`/`embed` pass, and add a `doctor` check that flags "concept pages present but unchunked" so operators know to run it.

## Note

`atoms/` are intentionally substrate (no `source-boost` entry) and presumably should *not* be embedded — this report is specifically about `concepts/`.

title: v0.42.42.0 fix(config): render nested config values as JSON in `config show`
body:
## Problem

`gbrain config show` renders nested config values as `[object Object]`:

```
GBrain config:
  engine: postgres
  schema_pack: gbrain-base-v2
  mcp: [object Object]
  self_upgrade: [object Object]
  search: [object Object]
  database_url: postgresql://...:***@...
```

The show loop interpolated each value straight into a template literal:

```ts
const display = typeof v === 'string' ? redactConfigValue(k, v) : v;
console.log(`  ${k}: ${display}`);
```

When `v` is a non-string (`mcp`, `self_upgrade`, `search`), template-literal
coercion calls `.toString()` → `[object Object]`, hiding the actual config.

## Fix

Extract a `formatConfigValue(key, value)` helper (single source of truth,
matching the existing `redactConfigValue` pattern in this file):

- **strings** → `redactConfigValue` (secrets still masked)
- **objects/arrays** → `JSON.stringify`
- **primitives** → `String(value)`

After:

```
  mcp: {"publish_skills":true}
  self_upgrade: {"mode":"notify","mode_prompted":true}
  search: {"mode":"balanced"}
```

## Tests

Adds a `formatConfigValue` describe block to `test/config.test.ts`:
- nested objects/arrays JSON-stringify (no `[object Object]`)
- secret string values stay redacted (`api_key` → `***`, db password masked)
- plain strings + primitives pass through

`bun test test/config.test.ts` → 27 pass / 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: Feature: semantic clustering + dedup-by-merge command
body:
## Problem

gbrain has embeddings and pgvector similarity query (`<=>`), but no first-class command to **cluster** near-duplicate pages or **merge** them. Large corpora accumulate many pages that restate the same idea from different sources/angles. Today the only options are manual review or deleting duplicates — both lose information.

## Proposed capability

A `cluster` + `merge` workflow that turns redundancy into a salience signal instead of throwing it away.

### 1. `gbrain cluster`
- Group pages by cosine similarity above a threshold (default ~0.86) using existing pgvector embeddings.
- Scope by slug prefix / type filter.
- Connected-components or greedy agglomeration above threshold.
- Optional LLM **distinctness guard**: confirm cluster members are true duplicates of one mechanism vs. genuinely distinct ideas; split clusters that aren't. Similarity proposes, judgment disposes.
- Output clusters as JSON (member slugs, pairwise similarity, suggested canonical).

### 2. `gbrain merge`
Fold a cluster into a single canonical page (highest-quality member), preserving every framing:
- `merge_count` (int) in frontmatter — number of absorbed pages. **This is a salience metric**: a high count means the idea was independently re-derived many times, i.e. it matters.
- `backlinks` (list) — each absorbed page's source + the specific angle it contributed (`{source, angle, date}`).
- A `## Facets` body section — canonical statement up top, then short per-source variations beneath.
- Absorbed pages **moved** to a `_merged/` tree (reversible) rather than deleted, so the operation is fully undoable.

### 3. Emergent promotion
- When `merge_count` crosses a threshold, auto-promote the page from atom tier to concept tier. This makes the atom/concept boundary **emergent from usage** rather than hand-drawn — a recurring, heavily-referenced idea earns concepthood.

## Why
- Deletion is irreversible and discards the frequency signal.
- Merge-with-backlinks keeps every framing, captures "this idea keeps recurring" as a first-class metric, makes concept promotion data-driven, and is reversible.

## Notes
- Reuse existing embeddings; no re-embed needed beyond `embed --stale`.
- Thresholds should be knobs, calibrated on the actual similarity/merge_count distribution, not hardcoded.
- pgvector cosine: `SELECT slug, embedding <=> $1 AS dist FROM pages WHERE slug LIKE $2 ORDER BY dist LIMIT k;` (similarity = 1 - dist).

title: feat(dream): add --break-lock for gbrain-cycle (closes #1591)
body:
## Summary

The cycle lock (held by `gbrain dream` / autopilot) had no CLI escape hatch, so a wedged cycle stranded it indefinitely and `gbrain doctor`'s hint routed operators to `gbrain sync --break-lock` which couldn't actually break it.

This PR adds `gbrain dream --break-lock` with the same safety semantics as the existing `gbrain sync --break-lock`:

- **safe path** (no flag): refuses if holder alive, refuses cross-host (process.kill(pid, 0) is invalid across hosts)
- **`--max-age <seconds>`**: atomic TOCTOU-safe age-gated DELETE keyed on `(id, holder_pid, last_refreshed_at < NOW() - N * INTERVAL)`
- **`--force-break-lock`**: skip guards, atomic DELETE, loud warning that the holder may still be writing
- **`--source <id>`** / **`--json`**: per-source scoping (resolves to `gbrain-cycle:<id>` lock key) and machine-readable output

Doctor at `src/commands/doctor.ts:2417+` already routes cycle locks to `gbrain dream --break-lock` (the if-else chain is in place), so the moment this lands, the existing hint becomes actionable for the first time.

## Test plan

- `gbrain dream --break-lock` (no cycle lock held) → `Lock gbrain-cycle is not held (nothing to break).` exit 0
- `gbrain dream --break-lock` while a healthy cycle holds it → `holder is alive, use --max-age or --force-break-lock` exit 1
- `gbrain dream --break-lock --max-age 60` while a long-dead cycle holds it → `Broke cycle lock gbrain-cycle ...` exit 0
- `gbrain dream --break-lock --force-break-lock` → atomic DELETE, warning emitted
- `gbrain doctor` after merge → `stale_locks` WARN should clear

## Files

- `src/commands/dream.ts`: +129 lines (`runCycleLockBreak` + `formatAgeHuman` + `--break-lock` short-circuit + 3 imports)
- `CHANGELOG.md`: +4 lines ([Unreleased] section)

Closes #1591

title: v0.42.43.0 feat(context): push-based context (#2095) + teardown-exit hardening (#2084)
body:
# v0.42.43.0 — push-based context (#2095) + teardown-exit hardening (#2084)

Closes #2095. Closes #2084 (the residual of #1972 beyond what #2141 landed).

## What this ships

**The brain now volunteers relevant pages instead of waiting to be asked (#2095).** Retrieval used to be pull-only: a deep session could run for hours with zero brain contributions — not because the brain had nothing, but because nothing prompted the agent to ask, and pages stored under coined names were missed by literal-string queries. Push-based context inverts that on **three channels sharing one zero-LLM, confidence-gated core**:

| Channel | Surface | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| ambient reflex | context engine `assemble()` | every turn, now over a rolling 4-turn window |
| `volunteer_context` op | CLI stdin + MCP tool | agent calls it per turn (window in, pointers out) |
| `gbrain watch` | streaming CLI | transcript piped in, volunteered pages stream out |

Every volunteered page carries an honest confidence (`alias` 0.9 / `title` 0.8 / `slug-suffix` 0.6, +0.05 repeated/newest-turn boost; default gate 0.7) and a deterministic one-line rationale. A feedback loop closes the tuning circle: volunteers are logged (migration v117, RLS'd, 90-day retention via the dream cycle), "used" is derived from subsequent retrieval, and `gbrain volunteer-context --stats` reports per-arm precision (labeled approximate — the retrieval signal is throttled).

```
window text ─ parseWindow() ─→ turns[] ─ extractCandidatesFromWindow() ─→ candidates
        │                                  (recency + frequency + user-role weights)
        ▼
resolveEntitiesToPointers(sourceIds[])
  arm 1: page_aliases unambiguous hit ──────────── confidence 0.9
  arm 2: exact title ───(JS provenance map)─────── confidence 0.8
         slug / slug-suffix ──────────────────────  confidence 0.6
        │
        ▼
excludeSlugs (pre-cap) → min_confidence gate → suppression → cap (3 / 5 max)
        │
        ├──→ caller: [{slug, source_id, display, confidence, arm, rationale, synopsis}]
        └──→ fire-and-forget batched INSERT → context_volunteer_events (drained at exit)
```

**#2084 (teardown):** master's #2141 landed the exit core at v0.42.42.0; this branch reconciles onto it as a **strict superset**:

- **PgBouncer transaction-mode pooler in the local CI gate** — a real pooler service + `test/e2e/pgbouncer-teardown.test.ts` reproduce the topology behind three consecutive teardown waves (#1972 → #2015 → #2084), verified live in this branch. The bug class is now CI-visible before it ships.
- **Exit-verdict sweep completed across every command surface** — nine in-handler `process.exit` sites converted to the owned verdict channel; notably `gbrain doctor`, whose FAIL verdict could still report exit 0 (its raw `process.exitCode =` write was zeroed by the owned exit).
- **Structural pins** — `test/cli-exit-verdict-pin.test.ts` fails CI on the next raw exit-code write anywhere in the CLI; `test/cli-pipe-truncation.test.ts` pins the piped-stdout integrity class (incident #1959) against the real compiled CLI.

## Review + hardening trail

- **Plan** eng-reviewed (24 findings folded) + codex outside voice (26 raw → 11 absorbed: slug-only suppression under windowing, arm provenance, RLS+retention, session attribution, reflex-channel measurement, watch lifecycle/wiring). All 13 decisions resolved in-session; plan audit: 36 DONE / 5 CHANGED-for-the-better.
- **Pre-landing specialists**: federated alias resolution parallelized per source, untrusted-caller knob clamps (`min_confidence`, `max_pages`, `days`, `session_id` length, `turn` int4 range), shared `TURN_PREFIX_RE`/`formatVolunteeredPage`/`volunteerEventRowsFrom` so the three channels can't desynchronize.
- **Red team** (post-specialist): pre-cap `excludeSlugs` so a recurring already-pushed entity can't starve fresh pages behind the cap; reflex-channel logging moved to the **delivery point** (IPC `onDelivered` post-write; `buildReflexAddition` post-timeout) so abandoned blocks never pollute the precision stats; `--window-turns` clamped to [1, 64]; PGLite watch connection monopoly documented + filed.

## Tests

Full suite green (units + `bun run verify` + `bun run check:all` + e2e incl. engine parity, the new pooler teardown e2e, and Postgres-side volunteer op parity). New/extended: `volunteer-context.test.ts`, `watch-command.test.ts`, `watch-sigint.serial.test.ts`, `retrieval-reflex.test.ts` (window, suppression modes, delivery-side logging, IPC wiring), `cli-exit-verdict-pin.test.ts`, `cli-pipe-truncation.test.ts`, `e2e/pgbouncer-teardown.test.ts`, migrate v117 + RLS + pruner coverage.

## Documentation

`docs/guides/push-context.md` (new guide), KEY_FILES.md entries for the five new/changed context files, CLAUDE.md op count + push-context row, CHANGELOG, TODOS (6 follow-ups filed: SSE push, policy skill/doctor check, structured `messages[]`, resolver index shapes, batched first-prune, watch-via-IPC + host capability gate), `bun run build:llms` regenerated.

## Note for dev brains only

The feedback-log migration shipped as **v117** after master claimed v116 mid-flight. A dev brain that ran this branch *before* the renumber (stamped at branch-116) will skip master's v116 on upgrade; fix is the idempotent re-run: `gbrain apply-migrations --from 116`. Brains that never ran the pre-renumber branch are unaffected — `gbrain upgrade` just works.

title: `litellm:` (and `llama-server:`) embedding setup is a catch-22: `--embedding-dimensions` is required yet rejected
body:
## Summary

Configuring an embedding model through the **`litellm`** proxy recipe is impossible: gbrain requires `--embedding-dimensions` for it, but then rejects any value you pass. The two errors are mutually exclusive, so there is no valid invocation. The **`llama-server`** recipe has the identical defect (both declare `default_dims: 0`).

Verified by source inspection of **v0.42.42.0** (installed via `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain`), macOS, PGLite engine.

## The catch-22

**Omit `--embedding-dimensions`:**
```
Embedding dimensions must be a positive integer; got 0.
```

**Pass `--embedding-dimensions 768` (or any N > 0):**
```
Provider "litellm" model "<model>" does not support custom dimensions 768
(this model only emits its default vector size).
Either drop --embedding-dimensions or pick a Matryoshka-aware model.
```

So: the first error says *add* `--embedding-dimensions`; the second says *drop* it. No setting satisfies both. Reproduced against every backend tried through the proxy (openai `text-embedding-3-small`/`-3-large`, `cohere/embed-v4.0`, fireworks `nomic`).

## Root cause (source-pinpointed)

1. `src/core/ai/recipes/litellm-proxy.ts:27` sets `default_dims: 0` with the comment *"user must declare --embedding-dimensions explicitly"*, and `setup_hint` (line 44) instructs the user to `pass --embedding-model litellm:<model> and --embedding-dimensions <N>`.

2. In `src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts`, `validateDimAgainstTouchpoint()`:
   - Line 369: `const dim = requestedDims ?? defaultDims;` → with no `--embedding-dimensions`, `dim = 0`.
   - Lines 371-374: `dim <= 0` → **"Embedding dimensions must be a positive integer; got 0."** (the *omit* half).
   - Line 386: `if (requestedDims !== undefined && requestedDims !== defaultDims)` → since `defaultDims = 0`, **any** passed `N > 0` enters custom-dim validation.

3. `isCustomDimValidForProvider()` (lines 408-461) only trusts user-declared dims for a hardcoded set of `recipe.id` values — `voyage` (426), `zeroentropyai` (435), `openai` (444). `litellm` matches none, so it falls through to **Tier 3 (lines 454-461)**: *"...does not support custom dimensions ... Either drop --embedding-dimensions."* (the *pass* half).

The `litellm` recipe is a **passthrough proxy** with `user_provided_models: true` (litellm-proxy.ts:26) — gbrain cannot introspect the arbitrary backend behind LiteLLM, which is exactly why `default_dims` is 0 and the user is told to declare dims. The recipe's own comment (litellm-proxy.ts:39-40) states the design intent: *"we trust the model id and surface the provider's rejection (D12 dim-validation catches mismatched-dim responses pre-storage)"* — i.e. trust the user's declared dims and validate the **actual returned vector size** after the first embedding call, not pre-reject via the Matryoshka allow-list.

The pre-flight allow-list in `isCustomDimValidForProvider` contradicts that intent for any `user_provided_models` / `default_dims: 0` recipe.

## Affected recipes

- `litellm` (`src/core/ai/recipes/litellm-proxy.ts`, `default_dims: 0`)
- `llama-server` (`src/core/ai/recipes/llama-server.ts:34`, `default_dims: 0`, *"forces explicit --embedding-dimensions"*)

Native `openai:` and `ollama:` recipes are unaffected (the former is in the allow-list; the latter declares a non-zero `default_dims`).

## Reproduction

```bash
# either form fails:
gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model litellm:openai/text-embedding-3-small --embedding-dimensions 1536
gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model litellm:openai/text-embedding-3-small
```
(Requires `LITELLM_BASE_URL` set per the recipe's setup_hint; the failure is in client-side dim validation, before any call to the proxy.)

## Proposed fix

In `isCustomDimValidForProvider` (or its caller at `embedding-dim-check.ts:386`), short-circuit for passthrough recipes: when the touchpoint has `user_provided_models === true` **and** `default_dims === 0`, accept the user-declared `requestedDims` as authoritative and defer to the post-call D12 dim-validation (which already catches a mismatch between declared and actually-returned dims before storage). This restores the documented "trust the user, validate the response" behavior for `litellm` and `llama-server` without weakening the Matryoshka checks for `voyage`/`zeroentropyai`/`openai`.

## Workaround

Use the native `ollama:` recipe (e.g. `ollama:nomic-embed-text`, 768d) — fully local, no proxy, unaffected by this validation path.

---
*Reported from a local install used to back a personal knowledge wiki. Happy to test a patch.*

title: fix(sync): first-sync indexes only git-tracked files (skip build output, temp, worktrees)
body:
## Problem

The first-sync filesystem walker (`collectSyncableFiles`) honored only a hardcoded prune set (`node_modules`, `ops`, dot-dirs), so beyond gitignored build output it also indexed untracked temp files and **nested linked worktrees**. On a real iOS repo a `worktrees/ux-simplification` checkout duplicated the whole codebase: 4,284 source files → **8,649 indexed pages**. The incremental git-diff path already skips all of this, so first-sync and incremental-sync disagreed on scope and polluted the brain with generated/duplicate files.

## Fix

For a git repo, enumerate via `git ls-files` (tracked = the user's committed work), applying the same name-based prune set. This excludes vendored deps, build output (iOS `build/`/`DerivedData/`/`Pods/`, Rust `target/`, web `dist/`), temp files, submodules (separate repos, not in the index), and nested worktrees. Non-git directories fall back to the legacy filesystem walk unchanged (returns `null` → fallback), so non-git imports are unaffected.

## Verification

- MirrorBuddy (nested worktree): 8,659 → 4,284 pages, 0 worktree dupes, 0 build artifacts.
- MirrorHR (iOS): 2,983 → 401 pages, 0 build artifacts, real Swift sources only.
- Non-git dir: unchanged (1 file in, 1 file out).
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.

title: Feature: brain-resident skillpacks + a proactive gbrain setup/upgrade advisor
body:
# Feature: brain-resident skillpacks + a proactive "make the most of gbrain" advisor

## Summary

Today a skillpack is something **gbrain ships** (bundled in `openclaw.plugin.json`) or
something **a third party publishes** to the registry. There is no first-class concept of
a **brain repo carrying its own publishable skillpack** — skills authored *for* and *with*
a specific brain, versioned in the brain repo, and offered to any harness that connects to
that brain.

This proposes two tightly-related pieces:

1. **Brain-resident skillpacks** — a brain repo can declare a publishable skillpack at a
   well-known path, using the *existing* `skillpack.json` v1 manifest + scaffold/trust
   pipeline. When gbrain connects to a brain (either connection topology), it discovers the
   pack, tells the harness what's in it, and **prompts the user to install — and nags a
   little** if they don't.

2. **A proactive gbrain advisor skill** — a standing capability where gbrain periodically
   pings the user with concrete things to do to get more out of their brain, upgrade gbrain,
   and improve their setup. The current `post-install-advisory.ts` is a hardcoded one-shot;
   this generalizes it into a real, recurring, brain-state-aware coaching loop.

Both reuse the skillpack machinery that already exists. Nothing here forks the manifest,
the installer, or the trust model.

---

## Motivation

A brain is not just data — it accrues *capabilities*. A research brain wants a citation-graph
skill; a deal brain wants a diligence-ingestion skill; a media brain wants a clip-extraction
skill. Those skills are co-evolved with the brain's schema and conventions. Right now they
live in the host agent's workspace, invisible to the next harness that connects to the same
brain. Connect a fresh Claude Code or a thin-client to a mature brain and it has **no idea**
the brain expects a particular meeting-ingestion or enrichment protocol — even though those
skills are exactly what make the brain compound.

Brain-resident skillpacks make the brain self-describing at the *capability* layer the same
way `get_brain_identity` makes it self-describing at the identity layer. The brain travels
with its own operating manual, and any connecting harness is offered it.

Second problem: gbrain is mostly **passive**. It answers when asked. It does not tell the
user "you're on 0.40, 0.42 shipped a taxonomy migration you'd benefit from," or "you've
ingested 400 meetings but never installed the meeting-ingestion skill," or "your embeddings
backfill has been stalled for 6 days." A brain that builds itself should also *advise* its
owner on how to run it better. We have the data to do this; we just don't surface it.

---

## Part 1 — Brain-resident skillpacks

### 1.1 Where it lives

A brain repo MAY declare a skillpack at its root:

```
<brain-repo>/
  skillpack.json            # existing gbrain-skillpack-v1 manifest
  README.md                 # human + harness entry point (see 1.3)
  skills/
    <skill-a>/SKILL.md
    <skill-b>/SKILL.md
  runbooks/
    bootstrap.md            # optional, displayed post-scaffold
  CHANGELOG.md
```

This is **identical** to the third-party pack layout `manifest-v1.ts` already validates.
The only new idea is *location*: the pack lives inside the brain's own git repo, and gbrain
knows to look for it when connecting. No new manifest schema. A brain pack is just a
third-party pack whose "source repo" happens to be the brain repo itself.

### 1.2 Spec (reuse, don't reinvent)

- **Manifest:** existing `skillpack.json` / `gbrain-skillpack-v1` (`src/core/skillpack/manifest-v1.ts`).
  Add ONE optional field:
  ```jsonc
  {
    "api_version": "gbrain-skillpack-v1",
    "name": "<brain>-pack",
    // ... all existing required fields ...
    "brain_resident": true,        // NEW (optional): flags this pack as authored
                                    // for the brain in this repo. Drives discovery +
                                    // the connect-time prompt. Absent = legacy/third-party.
    "schema_pack": "gbrain-base-v2" // NEW (optional): the schema pack these skills
                                    // assume, so a mismatch can warn at install time.
  }
  ```
  Both are additive and forward-compatible (the validator already refuses unknown
  `api_version` but tolerates extra fields).

- **Install path:** existing `scaffold-third-party.ts` →
  `resolveSource → loadSkillpackManifest → askTrust → enumerateScaffoldEntries → copyArtifacts → saveState → buildBootstrapDisplay`.
  A brain-resident pack resolves its source as the **already-connected brain repo** (local
  federated path) or as the **registry/git source** behind a thin-client. The trust prompt
  (`trust-prompt.ts`) still fires on first install of a given `(name, author, pinned_commit)`
  triple — TOFU is unchanged.

- **No auto-execution.** Same contract as `bootstrap-display.ts`: scaffold drops files
  additively, refuses to overwrite, then *displays* the runbook for the harness to walk at
  its discretion. We do not auto-run skills on connect. The user/harness decides.

### 1.3 README.md contract

The pack README is the entry point for both humans and harnesses. It must contain, in a
machine-parseable order (headers gbrain can scan):

1. **What this brain is** — one paragraph, mirrors `get_brain_identity`.
2. **Skills in this pack** — a list, each with: slug, one-line description, when to use it,
   and any schema/version assumptions.
3. **Install** — the exact `gbrain skillpack scaffold <source>` command.
4. **Conventions this brain expects** — the operating rules a connecting harness should
   honor (e.g. "always search before writing", "meetings propagate to all entity pages").
5. **Version compatibility** — `gbrain_min_version`, `schema_pack`.

gbrain should ship a `gbrain skillpack init-brain-pack` scaffolder that writes a starter
`skillpack.json` + README.md skeleton into a brain repo (analogous to the existing
`init-scaffold.ts` / `scaffold.ts`), so authors don't hand-roll the manifest.

### 1.4 Discovery + the connect-time prompt (the nag)

This is the heart of the request. **Two connection topologies, two hook points:**

#### Topology A — federated git repo loaded into a local gbrain instance
Hook: `gbrain sources add <id> --path <brain-repo> --federated` (`src/commands/sources.ts`).
After a source is added/federated, gbrain checks for `skillpack.json` at the source root.
If found and `brain_resident: true`:
- Emit an **agent-readable advisory** (same channel as `post-install-advisory.ts` — printed
  to terminal output the host agent reads) that:
  1. Names the pack + version.
  2. Lists each skill with its one-line description.
  3. Tells the harness EXPLICITLY: *ask the user whether to install these skills, and which.*
  4. Prints the exact `gbrain skillpack scaffold <source>` command.

#### Topology B — MCP thin-client to a remote `gbrain serve --http`
Hook: `gbrain connect` (`src/commands/connect.ts`) + the `list_skills` MCP path.
The remote brain exposes its resident pack over MCP. Two sub-pieces:
- Extend the MCP surface with a **`list_brain_skillpack`** tool (sibling to `list_skills` /
  `get_skill`) that returns the resident pack manifest + per-skill descriptions, gated by
  `mcp.publish_skills` exactly like the existing skill-catalog tools.
- The `connect` `LEARN_INSTRUCTION` string (already teaches the agent to call
  `get_brain_identity` + `list_skills`) gains a line: *after orienting, call
  `list_brain_skillpack`; if the brain ships a pack, ask the user whether to install it.*

#### The nag (shared by both topologies)
A connection that surfaces an uninstalled brain pack records a small bit of state
(`~/.gbrain/skillpack-state.json` already exists — add a `prompted_at` / `declined_count`
per `(brain, pack, version)`). Nag policy:
- **Connect #1:** full advisory + install offer.
- **Subsequent connects / `gbrain sync` / `gbrain upgrade` while uninstalled:** a shorter
  one-line reminder ("brain ships N skills you haven't installed — `gbrain skillpack scaffold ...`"),
  escalating mildly, with a hard ceiling (e.g. stop after 3 declines or `--no-skill-nag`).
- **Pack version bump while installed:** advise the `reference --apply-clean-hunks` update lens
  (already exists) rather than re-scaffold.
- Respect non-TTY / `--yes` / CI: advisory still prints (agent-readable) but never blocks.

This reuses `post-install-advisory.ts`'s "print, don't execute; tell the agent to ask the
user" model — the difference is the recommended set is **read from the brain's `skillpack.json`**
instead of a hardcoded constant.

### 1.5 Security / trust

- Brain packs go through the **same trust gate** as any third-party pack (`trust-prompt.ts`
  TOFU on first install; identity block shows name/author/source/pinned-commit/tier).
- Installer's data-loss protections are unchanged: per-file diff, refuse-overwrite,
  `shared_deps` closure, lockfile.
- Thin-client `list_brain_skillpack` is gated behind `mcp.publish_skills` (off by default —
  reuse the existing `skillPublishStatus` banner/nudge in `serve-http.ts`).
- SSRF allowlist for git sources is reused as-is (`remote-source.ts`).

---

## Part 2 — The gbrain advisor skill (proactive setup/upgrade coaching)

### 2.1 Problem
`post-install-advisory.ts` only fires on `init` / `upgrade`, recommends a **hardcoded** v0.25.1
skill set, and never speaks again. gbrain has no recurring, state-aware voice telling the user
how to run their brain better.

### 2.2 Proposal
Ship a first-class **`gbrain advisor`** capability (CLI op + a published skill in gbrain's own
bundle, so harnesses know how to run it):

- **`gbrain advisor`** — compute and print a ranked, agent-readable list of high-leverage
  actions for *this* brain right now. Pure read; no mutation. Harness decides what to surface.
- A bundled **`gbrain-advisor` skill** that teaches a harness to run `gbrain advisor` on a
  cadence (cron) and ping the user with the top items in their own voice/channel.

### 2.3 Signals the advisor computes (all from data gbrain already has)
- **Version drift:** installed gbrain version vs latest (and whether a migration is pending).
- **Uninstalled brain-pack skills** (ties directly into Part 1).
- **Uninstalled / outdated bundled skills** (generalizes today's hardcoded advisory — read the
  newest migration's recommended set, not a constant).
- **Schema-pack staleness:** brain on `gbrain-base` while `gbrain-base-v2` is available.
- **Stalled jobs:** embed-backfill / federated sync that hasn't advanced (the sync code already
  tracks `last_sync_at` / backfill visibility).
- **Underused capability vs usage shape:** e.g. heavy meeting volume but the meeting-ingestion
  skill isn't installed; many person pages but `find_experts` never called; no cron jobs.
- **Setup smells:** thin-client misconfig, `publish_skills` off when agents are connecting and
  hitting empty `list_skills`, embeddings provider unset.

### 2.4 Output contract
Ranked list, each item: severity, one-line *why it matters*, and the **exact command** to fix
it. Same "print, agent asks user" discipline — never auto-applies. Nag policy mirrors Part 1
(escalating-but-bounded, `--no-advisor-nag` / `advisor.cadence` config).

### 2.5 Cadence
- On `init` / `upgrade` (replaces the current one-shot).
- On `gbrain sync` (cheap; only prints when something material changed).
- Via a bundled cron recipe the `gbrain-advisor` skill installs, so even idle brains get a
  weekly "here's how to get more out of this" ping.

---

## Implementation sketch (files)

**Part 1**
- `src/core/skillpack/manifest-v1.ts` — add optional `brain_resident`, `schema_pack` fields.
- `src/core/skillpack/init-scaffold.ts` (or new `init-brain-pack.ts`) — `skillpack init-brain-pack`.
- `src/commands/sources.ts` — post-`add`/`federate` brain-pack discovery + advisory emit.
- `src/commands/connect.ts` — extend `LEARN_INSTRUCTION`; document `list_brain_skillpack`.
- `src/mcp/tool-defs.ts` + `src/mcp/dispatch.ts` — `list_brain_skillpack` tool, `publish_skills`-gated.
- `src/core/skillpack/state.ts` — `prompted_at` / `declined_count` per brain-pack; nag ceiling.
- `src/core/skillpack/post-install-advisory.ts` — read recommended set from a manifest, not a const.

**Part 2**
- `src/commands/advisor.ts` — new `gbrain advisor` op (pure read; ranked actions).
- `src/core/advisor/*` — signal collectors (version, jobs, schema, usage-shape, setup smells).
- `skills/gbrain-advisor/SKILL.md` + cron recipe — bundled in `openclaw.plugin.json`.
- Generalize `post-install-advisory.ts` to delegate to the advisor.

**Tests**
- Manifest: `brain_resident`/`schema_pack` round-trip + forward-compat.
- Discovery: federated-add and thin-client-connect both surface an uninstalled pack.
- Nag: escalation + ceiling + `--no-skill-nag`.
- Advisor: each signal collector fires on a fixture brain; ranking + command strings correct.
- E2E: connect to a brain shipping a resident pack, accept install, verify scaffold + state.

---

## Open questions
1. **Pack name collisions** between a brain-resident pack and a registry pack of the same name —
   namespace by brain identity? Prefix? Require the registry name to differ?
2. **Multi-source brains:** if three federated sources each ship a pack, do we merge advisories
   or prompt per-source? (Lean: per-source, deduped by skill slug.)
3. **Thin-client install target:** a thin-client has no local engine — scaffolding skills into
   *its* workspace is fine, but should the pack's `schema_pack` assumption be checked against
   the *remote* brain's schema? (Lean: yes, warn on mismatch via `get_brain_identity`.)
4. **Advisor signal extensibility:** hardcode the v1 collectors vs. a pluggable collector
   registry. (Lean: hardcode v1, refactor to registry once the set stabilizes.)
5. **Cadence vs. annoyance:** what's the right default advisor cadence, and should the nag
   ceiling reset on a version bump?

## Acceptance criteria
- A brain repo can carry a `skillpack.json` + README.md + `skills/` and publish it via the
  existing scaffold pipeline with zero manifest forks.
- Connecting to that brain via **both** topologies (federated git source + MCP thin-client)
  surfaces the pack, lists its skills, and prompts the user to install — with bounded,
  escalating nagging while uninstalled.
- `gbrain advisor` returns a ranked, command-bearing action list from real brain state, and a
  bundled skill + cron lets a harness ping the user on a cadence.
- Trust/data-loss/SSRF/`publish_skills` gates are all reused, not weakened.

title: Add scheduled OSV-Scanner dependency vulnerability scan
body:
## Improvement opportunity

Add an OSV-Scanner GitHub Actions workflow for dependency vulnerability scanning.

## Evidence inspected

Repo-local evidence:

- `package.json:98-137` declares a non-trivial runtime/dev dependency surface (`@ai-sdk/*`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `express`, `cookie-parser`, `js-yaml`, `openai`, `postgres`, `typescript`, etc.).
- Existing workflows are strong on secret scanning and Actions hardening, but not dependency vulnerability drift:
  - `.github/workflows/test.yml:71-82` runs Gitleaks in PR CI.
  - `.github/workflows/test.yml:14-15`, `.github/workflows/e2e.yml:12-13`, and `.github/workflows/heavy-tests.yml:22-23` use least-privilege `contents: read`.
  - `.github/workflows/release.yml:9-12` now has provenance permissions for release attestations.
- Repo/workflow grep found no `osv-scanner`, `OSV-Scanner`, `dependency-review`, `Semgrep`, `CodeQL`, or `OpenSSF Scorecard` workflow in `.github/workflows/`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:148-161` documents the local CI gate as `gitleaks + unit + E2E`, with no dependency vulnerability scan step.

Current external baseline:

- OSV-Scanner's GitHub Action docs describe two reusable workflows: PR scanning for newly introduced vulnerabilities and scheduled/full scans for dependency trees. The scheduled workflow fails on known vulnerabilities by default and can upload SARIF to GitHub code scanning.
- Reference inspected: https://google.github.io/osv-scanner/github-action/

## Expected impact

Maintainers get an automated signal when an existing dependency becomes vulnerable after merge, not just when a secret is introduced. This is especially useful for a CLI/agent project with direct runtime dependencies and frequent release tags: the project can catch dependency risk before cutting binaries or before a contributor bumps a package in a PR.

## Suggested fix

Keep this scoped and low-noise:

1. Add `.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml` using the official reusable workflow.
2. Trigger it on a staggered weekly schedule plus `workflow_dispatch` first. Optionally add `pull_request` later if maintainers want dependency changes blocked in PRs.
3. Use least-privilege permissions required by OSV SARIF upload:
   - `contents: read`
   - `actions: read`
   - `security-events: write`
4. Use `scan-args` scoped to the repository root / lockfiles, and start with the scheduled full scan so false positives can be triaged before making it a required PR check.
5. If the repo wants PR blocking instead, use the OSV PR reusable workflow on `pull_request` to fail only on newly introduced vulnerabilities.

## Duplicate check

I inspected the required open items with `gh` before filing:

- `gh issue list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,url,labels,updatedAt`
  - 200 open issues inspected.
- `gh pr list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,url,labels,updatedAt,headRefName,author`
  - 200 open PRs inspected.

Keyword scans over those 400 open titles/bodies found no covering OSV/dependency-vulnerability issue or PR. The only broad supply-chain hit was #2142 (`Add artifact attestations for release binaries`), which is release provenance, not dependency vulnerability scanning.

Exact GitHub search results:

- `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "OSV-Scanner"` → 0
- `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "osv-scanner"` → 0
- `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "vulnerability scan"` → 0
- `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "vulnerability scanning"` → 0
- `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "dependency vulnerability"` → 0
- `repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open "dependency review"` → only #2142 via its duplicate-search command list, not as its requested fix

## Commands/files inspected

- `README.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `docs/guides/skill-development.md`
- `examples/skillpack-reference/README.md`
- `SECURITY.md`
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/tier5-queries.md`
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md`
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`
- `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`
- `.github/workflows/heavy-tests.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `package.json`
- `gh pr list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state merged --limit 30 --json number,title,body,url,mergedAt,files`
- `git grep -n -i -E 'dependency-review|osv|semgrep|codeql|scorecard|openssf|gitleaks|attest|permissions:|uses:' -- .github package.json SECURITY.md CONTRIBUTING.md README.md`
- `gh api -X GET search/issues -f q='repo:garrytan/gbrain state:open ...'`

title: Add source-aware authority weighting / authority profiles for cross-source search
body:
## Problem

GBrain preserves source boundaries with `source_id`, but cross-source ranking does not currently understand user-defined source authority.

In practice, some sources are canonical while others are staging, provisional research, archives, or working synthesis. A staging/research source can outrank a canonical source in a cross-source query when it has stronger lexical/vector relevance.

That is useful for recall, but not enough for authority-sensitive answering.

## Requested Feature

Add optional source-aware authority weighting for search/ranking.

Example config shape:

```yaml
authority_profiles:
  operating_context:
    canonical-ops: 1.5
    orchestration-docs: 1.2
    research-staging: 0.6
    archives: 0.3
```

Then search could support something like:

```bash
gbrain search "AI operating systems" --authority-profile operating_context
```

or the equivalent API/MCP parameter.

## Desired Behavior

- Keep retrieving across sources.
- Do not hide lower-authority sources.
- Re-rank or boost/demote based on the active authority profile.
- Preserve `source_id` on every result.
- Expose the applied authority profile/weight in result metadata.
- Allow query-time override, not only global config.
- Keep existing relevance-only search available.

## Use Case

For a user with multiple source wikis/repos:

- a canonical ops/wiki source may contain approved doctrine or durable operating context;
- a research/staging source may contain provisional synthesis;
- archives may be useful for recall but lower-authority for current answers.

For authority-sensitive questions, the canonical source should generally outrank staging/research material when both are relevant, while lower-authority sources should remain discoverable.

## Non-goal

This is not asking GBrain to determine truth automatically.

It is asking GBrain to support explicit, user-defined source authority policy as one ranking signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can define per-source authority weights.
- Search can invoke a named authority profile.
- Results show which profile/weight affected ranking.
- Existing relevance-only search remains available.
- Lower-authority sources remain discoverable but are not treated as equally canonical when an authority profile is active.

title: LiteLLM user-defined embedding models are not recognized as embedding-capable
body:
When configuring GBrain with a LiteLLM Proxy embedding model using a user-defined model name, GBrain does not recognize the litellm provider as embedding-capable.

The LiteLLM provider is documented/hinted as supporting usage like:

gbrain init \
  --url "$GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL" \
  --embedding-model litellm:gbrain-embedding \
  --embedding-dimensions 4096

However, after initialization, gbrain providers list shows litellm with EMBED —, and embedding commands fail with:

Provider "litellm" requires a specific model name to be configured.
  Set one: gbrain config set embedding_model litellm:<model-name>
  Or run with --no-embed to import-only and embed later.

This happens even though embedding_model is already configured as litellm:gbrain-embedding.

Environment

* GBrain version: 0.42.42.0
* Engine: PostgreSQL
* pgvector: enabled
* LiteLLM Proxy: running locally on http://localhost:4000/v1
* Embedding backend: vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint
* Embedding model: qwen3-embedding-8b-nvfp4
* Embedding dimensions: 4096
* Chat model: Qwen model behind LiteLLM, exposed as gpt-4o-mini

LiteLLM model list:

model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-4o-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/qwen3.6-35b
      api_base: http://192.168.1.12:30000/v1
      api_key: EMPTY
  - model_name: gbrain-embedding
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/qwen3-embedding-8b-nvfp4
      api_base: http://192.168.1.12:30001/v1
      api_key: EMPTY
      mode: embedding
      extra_body:
        encoding_format: float

The LiteLLM endpoint works correctly:

curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer EMPTY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gbrain-embedding",
    "input": "test"
  }' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'

Returns:

4096

Steps to reproduce

1. Run LiteLLM Proxy with a user-defined embedding model, for example:

model_list:
  - model_name: gbrain-embedding
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/qwen3-embedding-8b-nvfp4
      api_base: http://192.168.1.12:30001/v1
      api_key: EMPTY
      mode: embedding
      extra_body:
        encoding_format: float

2. Export environment variables:

export GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://gbrain:password@localhost:5432/gbrain
export LITELLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/v1
export LITELLM_API_KEY=EMPTY
export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/v1
export OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY

3. Initialize GBrain:

gbrain init \
  --url "$GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL" \
  --embedding-model litellm:gbrain-embedding \
  --embedding-dimensions 4096

4. Check providers:

gbrain providers list

Actual behavior

litellm appears as ready, but not embedding-capable:

PROVIDER              TIER              EMBED   EXPAND  CHAT    STATUS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
litellm               openai-compat     —       —       —       ✓ ready

Then embedding fails:

gbrain embed --all

Output:

Provider "litellm" requires a specific model name to be configured.
  Set one: gbrain config set embedding_model litellm:<model-name>
  Or run with --no-embed to import-only and embed later.

But config already contains:

{
  "embedding_model": "litellm:gbrain-embedding",
  "embedding_dimensions": 4096
}

Expected behavior

If embedding_model is configured as:

litellm:gbrain-embedding

and embedding_dimensions is explicitly provided, GBrain should treat the LiteLLM provider as embedding-capable and allow:

gbrain providers test --model litellm:gbrain-embedding
gbrain embed --all

Expected providers list:

litellm               openai-compat     yes     —       —       ✓ ready

Expected provider test:

Probing embedding provider...
  ✓ 99ms, 4096 dims
All probes green.

Temporary local workaround

I patched src/core/ai/recipes/litellm-proxy.ts to expose an embedding touchpoint:

touchpoints: {
  embedding: {
    models: ['gbrain-embedding'],
    user_provided_models: true,
    default_dims: 4096,
    cost_per_1m_tokens_usd: 0,
    price_last_verified: '2026-06-14',
    no_batch_cap: true,
    supports_multimodal: true,
  },
}

After this change:

gbrain providers list

correctly shows:

litellm               openai-compat     yes     —       —       ✓ ready

and:

gbrain providers test --model litellm:gbrain-embedding

returns:

Probing embedding provider...
  ✓ 99ms, 4096 dims
All probes green.

Suggested fix

The LiteLLM recipe should advertise embedding support when user-provided models are allowed.

Instead of requiring hardcoded models, the provider could support:

embedding: {
  models: [],
  user_provided_models: true,
  default_dims: 0,
  no_batch_cap: true,
  supports_multimodal: true,
}

and the embedding pipeline should treat litellm:<model-name> as a valid embedding model when --embedding-dimensions is provided.

Why this matters

LiteLLM is commonly used as a proxy in front of OpenAI-compatible providers, including vLLM. Modern local/self-hosted embedding models are often exposed this way, and may use custom model names.

In this case, the backend was:

* vLLM
* Qwen3-Embedding-8B-NVFP4
* 4096-dimensional embeddings
* LiteLLM Proxy as the routing layer

This setup works at the API level, but GBrain does not currently recognize the LiteLLM provider as embedding-capable without patching the recipe.

title: Codex/skillopt review route
autopilot: multi-source Postgres fan-out produces continuous dead autopilot-cycle jobs + recurrent queue wedge
body:
## Summary

On a multi-source Postgres brain, autopilot's per-source fan-out generates a continuous stream of **dead `autopilot-cycle` jobs** (200+/24h in our deployment) and periodically **wedges the queue** (worker alive, 0 active, no completions). Root cause is a three-way interaction between `fanoutMax`, worker concurrency, and the fact that per-source cycle *locks* are isolated but the heavy cycle *phases* are still brain-wide.

## Environment

- `gbrain` autopilot + Minions supervisor, Postgres engine (PgBouncer txn-mode, port 6543).
- 5 federated sources, all local-path, `fanoutMax` resolves to **4** (Postgres default, `autopilot-fanout.ts:83`).
- Supervisor run with `--concurrency 3`.
- `--interval 300` (5-min tick).

## Observed

`jobs list` shows a steady cadence: every ~5-min tick dispatches 3–4 `autopilot-cycle` jobs (one per stale source). Per tick, typically **1–2 complete and 2–3 go DEAD after ~250–470s** with `max_attempts` exhausted, e.g.:

```
15305 autopilot-cycle dead       397.9s
15304 autopilot-cycle dead       399.9s
15303 autopilot-cycle completed  254.1s
15302 autopilot-cycle completed  169.0s
15301 autopilot-cycle dead       249.7s
```

`jobs stats` over 24h: `autopilot-cycle 309 total / ~91 done / 213 dead`. Doctor intermittently reports `wedged_queue: worker alive but not claiming work (1 waiting, 0 active, 19m since last completion)`; the documented remediation (`supervisor stop && start`) clears it, but it returns within the hour.

## Root cause (verified by reading source)

1. **Fan-out exceeds worker capacity.** `resolveFanoutMax()` returns 4 for Postgres (`autopilot-fanout.ts:83`), independent of the worker's `--concurrency`. With concurrency 3 and 4 fanned-out cycles, at least one cycle is queued behind the others every tick. `dispatchPerSource` deliberately omits `maxWaiting:1` (correct, to preserve per-source fan-out), so nothing back-pressures the surplus.

2. **Per-source locks are isolated, but the expensive phases are not.** `cycleLockIdFor(sourceId)` correctly hands each source its own `gbrain-cycle:<source_id>` DB lock, so cycles for different sources *do* run concurrently on Postgres. But several phases (`embed`, `orphans`, `purge`, `resolve_symbol_edges`, `grade_takes`, `calibration_profile`) operate **brain-wide regardless of `sourceId`** — this is acknowledged in the `CycleOpts.sourceId` doc comment in `cycle.ts` ("this only scopes the LOCK ... global-scoped phases inside each will still touch the same rows"). So N concurrent cycles thrash the same rows and each runs far slower than it would alone.

3. **Cycle duration outruns the lock TTL / stalled threshold.** `LOCK_TTL_MS` was dropped to **5 min** (`cycle.ts`). Under contention, real cycles run 250–470s — right at or past 5 min. The in-phase `yieldDuringPhase`/lock-refresh keeps a *healthy* solo cycle alive, but contended cycles spend long stretches CPU-bound in brain-wide phases, miss refreshes, get marked stalled, and (`max_attempts: 2`) dead-letter.

4. **Self-perpetuating storm.** A dead/timed-out cycle never writes `last_full_cycle_at` for its source. The freshness gate (`isSourceStale`) therefore keeps that source "stale," so it is **re-fanned-out on the very next tick**. The pile of dead jobs is not transient backlog — it is the same handful of sources failing and re-dispatching every 5 minutes, forever.

5. **Wedge.** When enough contended cycles hold/abandon DB connections against the txn-mode pooler, the worker ends up alive but unable to claim (pool exhausted / stale leases), producing the `wedged_queue` 0/100 doctor state until a supervisor restart rebuilds the pool.

## Why this shouldn't ever happen

Autopilot is supposed to be a self-healing maintenance loop. As designed on a multi-source Postgres brain it instead manufactures a permanent dead-letter stream and recurrent queue wedges — the opposite of "keeps the brain healthy unattended." The dead jobs also mask real failures and trip health checks on every poll.

## Suggested fixes (in priority order)

1. **Clamp `fanoutMax` to the worker's effective concurrency** (reserve ≥1 slot for targeted sync/embed jobs that share the `default` queue). Fanning out more cycles than there are slots guarantees waiters that then race the stalled-sweeper.
2. **Don't re-fan-out a source whose last cycle failed/timed-out within the current interval** — add a short failure-cooldown so a chronically-slow source can't re-dispatch every tick. Today only *success* (`last_full_cycle_at`) gates dispatch; failure is invisible to the gate, which is what makes the storm self-perpetuating.
3. **Serialize (or globally single-flight) the brain-wide phases** so concurrent per-source cycles stop thrashing the same rows — or split the cycle so the genuinely per-source phases fan out while the brain-wide phases run once. The current state ("locks are per-source but the work isn't") gives concurrency's costs without its isolation.
4. **Make cycle timeout/lock-TTL adaptive to observed cycle p95** instead of a fixed 5 min, so a legitimately long cycle under load isn't reaped mid-flight.
5. **Surface fan-out vs concurrency mismatch in `gbrain doctor`** as a config warning (`fanoutMax(4) > concurrency(3)`), since the failure is silent today.

## Workaround we're using

Run the supervisor with concurrency ≥ `fanoutMax`, or set the `fanoutMax` override ≤ concurrency−1, plus the periodic supervisor restart the doctor already recommends. Neither addresses the self-perpetuating re-dispatch (fix #2).

title: PGLite WASM runtime fails on Windows 11 x64 (AMD64) — same Aborted() as #223 / #939
body:
# PGLite WASM runtime fails on Windows 11 x64 (AMD64) — same `Aborted()` as #223 / #939

## Summary

`gbrain init --pglite` and all subsequent DB-touching commands fail with `PGLite failed to initialize its WASM runtime` on Windows 11 **x64 (AMD64)** — not ARM64. The error message points to the macOS 26.3 bug (#223), but this is a separate platform.

## Environment

- **OS:** Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, Build 26200 (10.0.26200), **x64 (AMD64)**
- **Bun:** 1.3.14 (installed via `powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex"`)
- **gbrain:** 0.42.40.0 (installed via `git clone + bun install + bun link`)
- **@electric-sql/pglite:** version bundled with gbrain 0.42.40.0
- **Node.js:** v24.11.1 (available on same machine)

## Steps to Reproduce

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git E:\OpenClaw-GBrain\app\gbrain
cd E:\OpenClaw-GBrain\app\gbrain
bun install
bun link
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding --brain-path "E:\OpenClaw-GBrain\data\brain.pglite"
```

## Actual Result

```
Setting up local brain with PGLite (no server needed)...
  --no-embedding: deferred setup — configure with `gbrain config set embedding_model <id>` before import
PGLite failed to initialize its WASM runtime.
  Most common cause: the macOS 26.3 WASM bug
  (https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/223).
  Run `gbrain doctor` for a full diagnosis.
  Original error: [object Object]
```

`gbrain doctor` reports:
- `connection: Could not connect to configured DB (URL from config-file-path); filesystem checks only`
- Overall health score: **65/100**

## Additional Diagnostics

- **Bun `WebAssembly` object is complete** — Bun has WASM support
- **PGLite loads fine under Node.js** — `node -e "const { PGlite } = require('@electric-sql/pglite'); console.log('ok')"` outputs `ok` from the gbrain directory
- The issue is specific to **Bun + PGLite WASM on Windows x64**, not a general PGLite failure

## Related Issues

- **#939** — Same `Aborted()` on Windows 11 + Bun 1.3.13 (no comments, no fix)
- **#1502** — Same on Windows 11 ARM64 (confirms arm64 is not the only affected arch)
- **#1549** — Windows 10 x64: init succeeds but pgvector extension missing from WASM binary (different symptom, same root cause: PGLite WASM on Windows is broken)
- **#223** — macOS 26.3 ARM64 (the error message currently points here, misleading Windows users)
- **#2024** — Draft PR to fix diagnostic routing (not yet merged)

## Notes

- All related Windows issues (#939, #1502, #1549) have **zero comments** from maintainers
- The error message currently tells Windows users to look at a **macOS-specific** bug (#223), which is misleading
- There is **no documented workaround** for Windows users other than installing a full PostgreSQL server

## Request

1. Acknowledge Windows x64 as a known-affected platform (not just ARM64)
2. Provide a documented workaround or fix for PGLite WASM on Windows
3. Update the error message to not point Windows users to a macOS-specific issue

title: gbrain dream: migration v0.32.2 silently fails / wedges (even with 0 facts), blocking extract_facts
body:
## Summary
On a Postgres-engine brain, migration **v0.32.2** ("Facts join the system-of-record — your hot memory now lives in markdown, indexed by the DB") **fails silently** and becomes WEDGED, which permanently blocks the `extract_facts` cycle phase — so `recall` / hot-facts never populate and `cycle_freshness` stays FAIL.

Critically, it **still fails with 0 rows in the `facts` table**, so it is not data-dependent — the migration itself appears broken.

## Environment
- gbrain **0.42.44.0** (commit `090bb53`), installed via `git clone master` + `bun install` + `bun link` (the `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain` path aborts with a self-dependency loop — separate minor issue).
- Engine: **Postgres 16.14** + pgvector; upgraded from 0.41.14.0.
- Schema auto-migrated 97 → 117 cleanly on first `gbrain doctor`; only **v0.32.2** fails.

## What happens
```
$ gbrain apply-migrations --yes
=== Applying migration v0.32.2: Facts join the system-of-record — your hot memory now lives in markdown, indexed by the DB ===
=== v0.32.2 — facts join the system-of-record invariant ===
Migration v0.32.2 reported status=failed.
```
- **No error detail is printed.**
- `~/.gbrain/upgrade-errors.jsonl` **does not exist** (the wedged-migration message points there, but nothing is ever written).
- `gbrain doctor` → `[FAIL] minions_migration: WEDGED MIGRATION(s): 0.32.2 (>=3 consecutive partials). Run: gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry 0.32.2`
- `gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry 0.32.2` writes a retry marker, but the next `apply-migrations --yes` fails the same silent way.
- Deleting the only 2 legacy v0.31 facts (so `facts` table = **0 rows**) does **not** help — v0.32.2 still fails.

## Impact
- `extract_facts` cycle phase is skipped → `recall` / hot-facts never populate.
- `cycle_freshness` permanently FAIL (the cycle never "fully completes").
- All other cycle phases (sync, embed, purge, synthesize, propose_takes, grade_takes, consolidate) run fine on 0.42.44.

## Repro
1. Brain on Postgres; upgrade an older (0.41.x) brain to 0.42.44.
2. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`.
3. Observe v0.32.2 `status=failed` with zero diagnostics.

## Asks
1. **Surface the real error** for v0.32.2 — it currently fails with no diagnostics and `upgrade-errors.jsonl` stays empty.
2. Make v0.32.2 succeed (or no-op) on Postgres when `facts` is empty.

title: fix(kos-jarvis): rewrite kos-patrol gap detector — drop NER-truncated entities
body:
## Summary

Fork-local fix to the `kos-patrol` daily brain-health patrol. The `## Gaps`
section ("frequently-mentioned entities without pages") was ~85% NER garbage
from a coarse proper-noun regex. Rewrites `phase4` in
`skills/kos-jarvis/kos-patrol/run.ts` so the list surfaces real entity gaps.

No `VERSION` bump — this is a fork-local `skills/kos-jarvis/` change; `VERSION`
tracks the upstream gbrain release and only moves on sync.

### What was broken (2026-06-14 dashboard)
| Garbage gap | Root cause |
|---|---|
| `Link Systems Inc` (3710) | truncated `TP-Link Systems Inc` — regex dropped `TP-` hyphen prefix |
| `Peters Canyon` / `Peters Canyon Road` / `Fulton Way` / `Richmond Hill` | office addresses |
| `GTM Manager` / `Product Line Manager` / `Technical Support Engineer` / `Product Department` | job titles |
| `Lianzhou International` / `Link Canada` | already have company pages, but exact-match existence check missed them |
| `Omada\nController` | newline-split span glued by the `\s` connector |

### Fix (three changes in `phase4`)
1. **Regex** captures hyphenated brand tokens (`TP-Link`, `Cloud-Based`) and
   joins words on horizontal whitespace only (`[ \t]+`) so spans don't cross
   line breaks.
2. **Existence check** normalizes both sides — strips legal suffixes
   (`Inc/Ltd/GmbH/Sdn/Bhd/...`) and punctuation — so a mention resolves to an
   existing entity page despite suffix/punct drift.
3. **Filters**: address-tail + job-title-tail regexes + doc/boilerplate
   stoplist additions.

### Result (2026-06-15 dashboard, post-fix)
Every flagged garbage entry gone. The 20-slot list is now dominated by real
entities: `Niko Wang`, `MCMC JENDELA`, `DHCP Option`, `Access Point`,
`Vendor-Specific Attributes`, `Gary Gui`, `Fusion Pro AIO`. A thin tail of
generic terms remains (stoplist incrementally per the code comment).

title: Federated read scope not honored by get_page or the semantic query cache (by-slug reads fail in federated sources; cross-client cache leak)
body:
Hi @garrytan, two related bugs on current `master` (`543f9a71`, v0.41.21.0). They share one root cause: a client's `federated_read` source set reaches `search` and `query`, but not the final downstream boundary. One affects `get_page`, the other affects the semantic query cache. I found these while running a multi-source OAuth client and confirmed them by static inspection. Happy to send a PR if the proposed fixes look right to you.

## Bug A: `get_page` ignores `federated_read`

A client whose primary `source_id` is `A` and whose `federated_read` set is `['A', 'B']` can find a page that lives only in `B` through `search` and `query`, but `get_page` for that same slug returns not-found. The federated scope is applied to search and query, but not to the actual page fetch.

Evidence (master `543f9a71`):
- `sourceScopeOpts(ctx)` gives `ctx.auth.allowedSources` precedence as `{ sourceIds }` at `src/core/operations.ts:413-421`.
- `search` uses it at `src/core/operations.ts:1224-1228`. `query` builds `querySourceScope` and spreads it into the search call at `src/core/operations.ts:1353-1361` and `1401-1412`.
- `get_page` builds a scalar-only `sourceOpts` at `src/core/operations.ts:464-469`, then calls `ctx.engine.getPage(...sourceOpts)` at `:478` and `:484`. It only uses `sourceScopeOpts(ctx)` for fuzzy slug candidates at `:470-482`, never for the exact fetch.

Repro:
1. Register a client with `source_id='A'` and `federated_read=['A','B']`.
2. Create a page only in source `B`.
3. `search` or `query` returns the `B` page.
4. `get_page` for that slug returns not-found.

Impact: any agent that relies on `get_page` for deterministic by-slug reads cannot read its federated sources, even though it is authorized and can see those pages in search.

Proposed fix: extend `GetPageOpts` with `sourceIds?: string[]`, implement array precedence in `PostgresEngine.getPage` and `PGLiteEngine.getPage`, then have `get_page` use `sourceScopeOpts(ctx)` for both the exact and the fuzzy fetch. Resolve tags via the concrete page's source (`{ sourceId: page.source_id }`).

## Bug B: semantic query cache key under-specifies the federated source scope

A federated `query` is scoped correctly on a cache miss (the fresh path honors the full source set), but the cached row is stored and looked up under only the scalar source key, which defaults to `default` when the scalar is absent. A later caller with a different federated set, or a `default`-scope caller, can hit that row and receive results from outside its own source set.

Evidence (master `543f9a71`):
- Federated `query` passes `{ sourceIds: [...] }` via `querySourceScope` at `src/core/operations.ts:1353-1361` and `1401-1412`, and `hybridSearch` forwards both `sourceId` and `sourceIds` into `searchOpts` at `src/core/search/hybrid.ts:461-486`, so the fresh path is correct.
- The cache path uses only `opts?.sourceId`: lookup at `src/core/search/hybrid.ts:1111`, writeback at `:1194`.
- `SemanticQueryCache` defaults a missing `sourceId` to `'default'` and filters on `qc.source_id = $2`: lookup at `src/core/search/query-cache.ts:127-135` and `:161-163`, store at `:203-214`.

Repro:
1. Enable the query cache and an embedding provider.
2. Client 1 (`federated_read=['default','B']`) runs a query that returns a page from `B`. The row is cached under `default`.
3. Client 2 (`federated_read=['default']` or `['default','C']`) runs the same or a semantically close query.
4. Client 2's cache lookup can return Client 1's cached `B` result without reapplying Client 2's source set.

Impact: a correctness issue and a cross-client isolation gap. A federated cache row can leak across clients that have different read scopes.

Proposed fix:
- Minimal and safe: skip the semantic cache whenever `opts.sourceIds?.length` is nonzero, so federated reads always take the correctly scoped fresh path.
- Performance-preserving: derive a canonical cache scope key from the sorted, deduped `sourceIds` (hashed with a prefix), and use it consistently across lookup, store, clear, and invalidation.

Both are the same theme: federated read scope not reaching the final operation and cache boundary, so I have kept them in one issue. Glad to PR either or both.

title: OpenAI-compatible providers with default thinking (e.g. DeepSeek) waste ~50% tokens on non-reasoning calls
body:
## Problem

Several OpenAI-compatible providers, notably **DeepSeek v4-flash**, default to thinking/reasoning mode. When gbrain uses these models for non-reasoning calls (embeddings, search expansion, linting, etc.), every response carries unnecessary thinking tokens, inflating token costs by roughly 50%.

DeepSeek v4-flash is a popular provider for gbrain because of its competitive pricing and good performance, but the default thinking mode silently increases billable tokens for every chat call that gbrain makes — including short, fact-based queries that gain nothing from reasoning.

## Reproduction

1. Configure gbrain with a DeepSeek provider (or any openai-compatible provider that supports thinking)
2. Run any gbrain command that triggers a chat call: `gbrain query`, `gbrain search`, `gbrain embed`, etc.
3. Observe that the response includes reasoning/thinking tokens for every call

## Root Cause

The `chat()` function in `src/core/ai/gateway.ts` does not explicitly disable thinking for openai-compatible providers. Unlike Anthropic Claude (which uses a different parameter `thinking` under `providerOptions.anthropic`) and OpenAI o-series (which uses `reasoning_effort`), openai-compatible providers pass their thinking parameter through `providerOptions[recipe.id]`, which gets spread into the request body. If the provider defaults to thinking enabled, gbrain has no way to opt out.

## Proposed Fix

Explicitly set `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` for all openai-compatible providers (`recipe.implementation === "openai-compatible"`) in the `chat()` function. The `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider spreads `providerOptions[recipe.id]` into the request body; providers that do not support thinking silently ignore the parameter — so the fix is safe for ALL openai-compatible providers, not just DeepSeek.

This does not affect native providers (OpenAI o-series, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini), which use different parameter names for reasoning control.

## Impact

- Token waste: ~50% reduction in unnecessary output tokens for DeepSeek users
- Backward compatible: no change in behavior for providers that don't support thinking
- Future-proof: covers providers (Ollama, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, llama-server) that may add thinking support later

title: fix(gateway): disable thinking for all openai-compatible providers (#2202)
body:
Closes #2202

## Summary

Explicitly disables thinking/reasoning mode for all openai-compatible providers. DeepSeek v4-flash defaults to thinking mode, producing ~50% unnecessary output tokens for gbrains non-reasoning use cases (search, embed, lint, etc.).

## Change

In `src/core/ai/gateway.ts`, `chat()` function sets `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` via `providerOptions.openaiCompatible` when `recipe.implementation === "openai-compatible"`.

## Safety

- The `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider spreads `providerOptions[recipe.id]` into the request body
- Providers that do not support thinking silently ignore the parameter - 100% safe
- Does not affect native providers (OpenAI o-series, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini)

title: diagnoseEmbedding() falsely returns user_provided_model_unset when modelId is parsed from config string
body:
## Problem

When using a non-default embedding provider with `user_provided_models: true` (such as a local LM Studio / llama-server embedding endpoint), `diagnoseEmbedding()` in `src/core/ai/gateway.ts` unconditionally returns `user_provided_model_unset` if the recipe has an empty `models: []` array, even when a valid model name is supplied via the config string.

For example, a config like:
```
embedding_model: "llama-server:text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b"
```
correctly parses `modelId = "text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b"`, but the preflight guard ignores it and rejects the call.

This makes custom embedding providers (LM Studio, Ollama, llama-server, vLLM) entirely non-functional when configured through `user_provided_models`.

## Reproduction

1. Set up gbrain with a custom embedding provider (e.g. LM Studio running on localhost):
   ```
   embedding_model: "llama-server:text-embedding-model-name"
   ```
   with provider config:
   ```json
   {
     "providers": {
       "llama-server": {
         "base_url": "http://localhost:1234/v1",
         "user_provided_models": true,
         "models": []
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Run any command that triggers embedding: `gbrain search`, `gbrain embed`
3. Observe: embedding fails with `user_provided_model_unset`

## Root Cause

In `src/core/ai/gateway.ts`, the `diagnoseEmbedding()` function checks:
```typescript
if (
  Array.isArray(tp.models) &&
  tp.models.length === 0 &&
  (recipe.id === "litellm" || isUserProvided)
) {
  return { ok: false, reason: "user_provided_model_unset", ... };
}
```

The guard rejects based solely on `models` array being empty and `isUserProvided` being true, without checking whether `parsed.modelId` was successfully extracted from the config string. If the user has specified a model name in the embedding_model config, the guard should accept it.

## Proposed Fix

Add `!parsed.modelId` to the condition:
```typescript
if (
  Array.isArray(tp.models) &&
  tp.models.length === 0 &&
  (recipe.id === "litellm" || isUserProvided) &&
  !parsed.modelId
) {
  return { ok: false, reason: "user_provided_model_unset", ... };
}
```

When a valid modelId has been parsed from the config string, the guard no longer rejects.

## Impact

- Fixes local LM Studio / llama-server / Ollama / vLLM embedding for all gbrain users
- Minimal change: one extra conjunct in an existing condition
- No behavioral change for other embedding configurations

title: litellm: subagent loop falls back to anthropic and dies without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (chat/expansion touchpoints missing)
body:
**What happened?**

The `litellm` recipe ships only an `embedding` touchpoint. When `models.tier.subagent` (or `models.default`, or `GBRAIN_MODEL`) resolves to a `litellm:*` model, the resolver and capability gate disagree silently:

1. `gbrain models` warns `[models] tier.subagent resolved to "litellm:gpt-5.4" via "models.tier.subagent", which is an unrecognized provider` and falls back to `TIER_DEFAULTS.subagent` (`anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`).
2. On a brain that routes paid traffic through a LiteLLM-shaped proxy and has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env, every subagent loop dispatch then throws `AIConfigError: Anthropic ... requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

The warn text says "unrecognized provider," but the recipe IS registered. The gate is gating on missing touchpoint, not on missing recipe. Specifically: `getProviderCapabilities()` in `src/core/ai/capabilities.ts:74-104` throws when `recipe.touchpoints.chat` is missing; `classifyCapabilities()` catches and returns `'unknown'`; `enforceSubagentCapable()` in `src/core/model-config.ts:231-281` treats `'unknown'` as fail-closed and replaces the user's choice. Net effect: explicit `models.tier.subagent = litellm:*` is overridden without the user's knowledge, and the loop dies on missing Anthropic auth.

**What did you expect?**

`models.tier.subagent = litellm:gpt-5.4` should dispatch through the litellm route (which forwards to whatever the proxy is configured to back). The subagent capability gate should classify a litellm chat as capable, not unknown.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Fresh brain with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env.
2. `gbrain config set models.tier.subagent litellm:gpt-5.4` (or any `litellm:*` string).
3. `gbrain models` → warns "unrecognized provider" and falls back to `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`.
4. Submit any subagent job → `AIConfigError: Anthropic ... requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.42.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 + PGLite both reproduce.

**Proposed fix**

Declare `chat` and `expansion` touchpoints on the litellm recipe, mirroring the openai recipe's shape:

- `models: []` (litellm proxies arbitrary backends; `assertTouchpoint` already skips allowlist checks for `tier: 'openai-compat'`)
- `supports_tools: true`
- `supports_subagent_loop: true`
- `supports_prompt_cache: false` (OpenAI-compat backends don't honor Anthropic-style `cache_control`; loop emits a one-time `degraded:no_caching` warn; accepted trade for the proxy path)
- `max_context_tokens: 200_000` (conservative GPT-5-family default; per-deployment override needed for smaller-context backends — see "Open design questions" below)
- costs `undefined` (varies by proxied provider)

After this change, `classifyCapabilities('litellm:gpt-5.4', recipe)` returns `degraded:no_caching` (chat-capable, no Anthropic-style prompt cache). `enforceSubagentCapable` no longer steals the model choice.

**Open design questions** (worth settling in review):

1. Should `ChatTouchpoint` grow a `user_provided_models?: true` field (parallel to the existing `EmbeddingTouchpoint.user_provided_models`) so the design intent is explicit, rather than relying on `tier === 'openai-compat'` to skip the allowlist check in `assertTouchpoint`? Cleaner long-term shape.
2. Should `max_context_tokens` be `200_000` (correct for GPT-5 family but wrong for many openai-compat backends; Llama 3 = 8K–128K depending on quant, DeepSeek = 128K, Mistral = 32K–128K) or `undefined` (let `getProviderCapabilities` fall through to its own 128K default at line 102)? Probably `undefined` so per-deployment reality wins, with a doctor warn when a route's actual context exceeds the recipe's declared cap.
3. Should the same patch land on the `llama-server` recipe (currently embedding-only too)? And is `ollama`'s `supports_subagent_loop: false` too conservative for modern tool-capable local models (Qwen2.5, Llama 3.1+, Mistral Small 3.1+ all support function calling natively via Ollama)?

**Adjacent observation worth surfacing in the same PR:** the warn message "unrecognized provider" is misleading. The recipe IS in the registry; the classifier reports `'unknown'` because the `chat` touchpoint is missing. A clearer message would be `provider does not declare a chat touchpoint` (or similar): same severity, less misdirection. Drop-in change at `src/core/model-config.ts:258`.

title: litellm: setup_hint silent on /v1 path convention; OpenAI-shaped proxies 401 with no signal
body:
**What happened?**

The litellm recipe's `setup_hint` says only "set LITELLM_BASE_URL" with no guidance on whether to include a path prefix. Vanilla LiteLLM serves `/chat/completions` at the host root, so `LITELLM_BASE_URL=http://host:port` works. But OpenAI-shaped proxies (codex-proxy, some Azure-OpenAI mirrors, third-party translators) serve only `/v1/chat/completions` and reject the bare path with **401 Unauthorized** (not 404, which would be the diagnostic-correct answer).

The AI SDK's `createOpenAICompatible` appends `/chat/completions` to the base URL. When the proxy expects `/v1/chat/completions` and gets `/chat/completions`, it returns a generic 401. The AI SDK surfaces this as `AIConfigError: Unauthorized — Check your API key`, so the user's natural diagnostic move is to rotate or re-check the bearer token. That dead-ends. The actual fix is appending `/v1` to `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.

**What did you expect?**

The setup_hint should call out the path convention difference so users hitting 401s with codex-proxy-class endpoints know to check the URL shape, not the bearer.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run codex-proxy (or any openai-shaped endpoint that serves `/v1/...` only) on `:8080`.
2. `export LITELLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080` (no `/v1`).
3. `gbrain config set models.tier.reasoning litellm:gpt-5.4`.
4. Any chat dispatch → `AIConfigError: Unauthorized`. `curl $LITELLM_BASE_URL/models` returns 200 with the same bearer.
5. `export LITELLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1` → success.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.42.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- Reproduces with any openai-shaped reverse proxy (codex-proxy and similar translators); vanilla LiteLLM is unaffected.

**Proposed fix (doc-only)**

Append path-convention guidance to `src/core/ai/recipes/litellm-proxy.ts`'s `setup_hint`. Suggested shape (matches the existing one-paragraph string concatenation pattern from `llama-server-reranker.ts`):

```text
Run LiteLLM (https://docs.litellm.ai) in front of any provider; set
LITELLM_BASE_URL + pass --embedding-model litellm:<model> and
--embedding-dimensions <N>. Path convention: vanilla LiteLLM serves
/chat/completions at the host root (LITELLM_BASE_URL=http://host:port).
OpenAI-shaped proxies (codex-proxy, some Azure-OpenAI mirrors,
third-party translators) serve /v1/chat/completions and require the
/v1 suffix (LITELLM_BASE_URL=http://host:port/v1). If chat dispatch
returns 401 Unauthorized but `curl $LITELLM_BASE_URL/models` returns
200 with a valid bearer, the /v1 suffix is the missing piece.
```

**Adjacent surface (worth flagging or splitting off):** `gbrain models doctor` could probe `${LITELLM_BASE_URL}/chat/completions` and `${LITELLM_BASE_URL}/v1/chat/completions` with the configured bearer and surface the path-shape mismatch explicitly. Two-line diff to the doctor probe logic; saves the next user 20 minutes of confusion. Out of scope for the doc-only PR; happy to file as a follow-up.
