title: gbrain orphans / orphan_ratio overcount on PARA / Obsidian / agent-organized brains — no user-extensible deny list
body:
## Symptom

`gbrain orphans` reports thousands of "orphan" pages on brains organized by anything other than gbrain's own internal conventions. The same overcount drives `orphan_ratio` in `gbrain doctor`'s brain-score, so the user's brain-score is dominated by reference material that is orphan-by-design.

Two distinct overcount sources contribute, each living at a different filter layer:

1. **Slug-prefix layer**: PARA brains have `resources/`, `archives/`, `inbox/`; Obsidian brains have `clips/`, `attachments/`; code corpora have `transcripts/` (gstack-memory-ingest landing dir); agent runtimes have `agents/<name>/state`. The shipped `DENY_PREFIXES` doesn't cover any of these.
2. **Page-type layer**: code-symbol extractions (`pages.type = 'code'`), system artifacts (`extract_receipt`), gstack-memory-ingest commit-summary pages (`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`). These have no inbound-link semantics regardless of slug.

## Concrete numbers

A 2K-page Obsidian vault organized PARA-style plus 11 federated code-stage source repos (gstack-memory-ingest) plus a `transcripts/` corpus:

```text
$ gbrain orphans --count
2906       # raw (shipped DENY_PREFIXES only)

# Adding PARA convention dirs to the prefix knob:
$ gbrain config set orphans.exclude_prefixes 'resources/,transcripts/,agents/,clips/'
$ gbrain orphans --count
1418       # dropped 1488 PARA convention pages

# Adding default page-type filter (post-fix):
$ gbrain orphans --count
928        # dropped 490 code + system + commit-summary pages
```

928 actual signal vs 2906 raw. The 928 remaining are dominated by `concept` (414), `project` (291), and `note` (204) types: pages the user actually wrote and might want to graph.

## Diagnosis

`src/commands/orphans.ts:47-56` carries the shipped exclusion lists:

```ts
const DENY_PREFIXES = ['output/', 'dashboards/', 'scripts/', 'templates/', 'openclaw/config/'];
const FIRST_SEGMENT_EXCLUSIONS = new Set(['scratch', 'thoughts', 'catalog', 'entities']);
```

These cover gbrain-internal convention dirs but miss the convention layer AND the page-type layer entirely. There's no mechanism for a user to extend the deny list or filter by page type short of patching source and rebuilding.

## Proposed fix

Two complementary per-brain config knobs, layered at the surface where the noise actually lives:

```text
# Slug-prefix layer (opt-in; additive to shipped DENY_PREFIXES):
gbrain config set orphans.exclude_prefixes 'resources/,transcripts/,agents/'

# Page-type layer (shipped defaults apply automatically; additive via config):
gbrain config set orphans.exclude_types 'guide,reference'
```

Shipped `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_TYPES` covers types whose pages are orphan-by-construction on every brain shape:

- `code`: code-symbol extractions. Code files don't wikilink to code files.
- `extract_receipt`: system artifact from extract phases.
- `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`: gstack-memory-ingest commit-summary types.

Same one-directional contract as `DENY_PREFIXES`: shipped entries always apply; user config extends but cannot remove.

The fix touches `src/commands/orphans.ts` (helpers + filter wiring), `src/core/engine.ts` + both engines (`findOrphanPages` gains optional `excludeTypes`), `src/core/config.ts` (registry), plus tests.

## Why this fixes more than just `gbrain orphans --count`

`getOrphansData` is the canonical "what counts as an orphan in this brain" pure-data function shared between `gbrain orphans` and doctor's `orphan_ratio` check (per the v0.42.0.0 D1 unification). Both knobs therefore correct the brain-score input. A brain federating code-stage sources stops being penalized for code-symbol extractions, and a PARA-organized brain stops being penalized for web clips, the moment the config lands.

## Behavior change to call out

The `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_TYPES` list shifts orphan counts downward for every brain that has any of those six types. The orphan-ratio doctor check stops counting code-symbol and commit-summary pages. This is a one-time correction, not a regression. A code-symbol page never had inbound-link semantics; the count was just lying about it.

## Future surface (out of scope here, worth noting)

- **Frontmatter-level `orphan_expected: true` per-page opt-out.** Complementary to dir-level prefixes + type-level filters; useful for one-off pages where neither rule fits. Worth a follow-up.
- **Glob support** for `orphans.exclude_prefixes`. The existing semantics are `startsWith`; adding globs would need a wider rework. Prefix-only is sufficient for the patterns this PR targets.

Adjacent issue from the same operational-health theme: `orphan_ratio` recommends `extract links --by-mention` as the remediation, but backlink counting excludes mention-only links so the recommendation is structurally unactionable. Out of scope here; flagging for theme awareness.

title: release.yml: run verify before bun build
body:
## Issue

The Release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) runs `bun test` before `bun build` but skips the `verify` job (which includes `typecheck`, `check:privacy`, `check:admin-build`, and 24 other static checks). A TypeScript compile error, privacy leak, or broken admin build step can ship to users as a published binary.

## Evidence

**release.yml build step — no verify step:**
```yaml
- run: bun install
- run: bun test
- run: bun build --compile --target=${{ matrix.target }} --outfile bin/${{ matrix.artifact }} src/cli.ts
```

**test.yml has a separate "verify" job that gates merges but NOT releases:**
```yaml
# test.yml
verify:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - run: bun run verify   # runs scripts/run-verify-parallel.sh (27 checks)
```

**What verify covers that release is missing:**
- `typecheck` — TS errors caught before publish
- `check:privacy` — no real names / PII in agent voice
- `check:admin-build` — admin bundle must compile
- `check:jsonb` — no jsonb injection patterns
- `check:source-config-leak` — no API keys in source config
- `check:cli-exec` — CLI is executable after build
- `check:worker-pool-atomicity` — concurrent worker correctness
- `check:gateway-routed` — no direct Anthropic SDK calls
- 20 more checks in `scripts/run-verify-parallel.sh`

## Expected Impact

A TS error introduced between releases would block the release immediately instead of producing a broken binary that gets published. The same applies to any privacy or build-break regressions introduced in release-branch commits that never touched master.

## Suggested Fix

In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, add `bun run verify` between `bun test` and `bun build`:

```yaml
- run: bun install
- run: bun test
- run: bun run verify   # add this line
- run: bun build --compile --target=${{ matrix.target }} --outfile bin/${{ matrix.artifact }} src/cli.ts
```

## Commands Inspected

```bash
# Confirmed: release.yml has no verify step
grep -n "verify" .github/workflows/release.yml

# Confirmed: test.yml has a verify job
grep -n "verify:" .github/workflows/test.yml

# Confirmed: verify runs 27 checks via run-verify-parallel.sh
head -60 scripts/run-verify-parallel.sh
```

## Duplicate Check

- Searched 200 open issues for "verify in release", "typecheck in release", "release verify", "verify before build" — no matches.
- Related but distinct: #2142 (artifact attestations) and #2182 (OSV scanner), both already open.

title: v0.42.45.0 feat(sync): delta-aware cost estimator — stop wedging the daily cron (#2139)
body:
Closes #2139.

## What this does

The `gbrain sync` inline-embed cost gate priced the **entire corpus** whenever the working tree was dirty — which is always on an active brain — so a routine daily sync estimated ~158M tokens / ~$8 when the real delta was a few hundred files / ~$0.04, then blocked the cron with a confirmation it could never answer. Embeds silently stalled until someone noticed.

The estimate now **mirrors execution**: it fetches first and prices only the files this run will pull and import, through the same diff machinery (`computeSyncDelta`) the sync itself uses. A brain whose commits are caught up but whose tree is dirty estimates **$0**, because an attached-HEAD sync imports only the committed diff.

When the gate does fire in a non-interactive session it no longer exits 2 — it imports now and **auto-defers** embedding to capped background jobs, so a cron is never wedged. Operators who've decided cost isn't the constraint get one switch — `gbrain config set spend.posture tokenmax` — that makes every cost gate informational across sync, reindex, enrich, and onboard (spend is still ledgered; the switch removes the ceiling, not the accounting). The USD knobs accept `off` / `unlimited`, and every gate message carries paste-ready commands.

This also lifts the rule that blocked `--skip-failed` / `--retry-failed` under parallel sync — failure recovery no longer has to drop to `--serial` (which is what armed the inline gate in the first place).

## How it's built

- **`src/core/sync-delta.ts`** — one `computeSyncDelta` consumed by both the executor (`performSyncInner`) and the estimator, so the gate's dollar figure can't drift from what the sync imports. Fail-open ladder (anchor-missing / diff-failed → labeled full-tree ceiling).
- **`src/core/spend-posture.ts`** — `spend.posture` + `parseUsdLimit`/`formatUsdLimit` (off/unlimited → no limit; `undefined` at the budget boundary so ledger rows never serialize `null`).
- Delta-aware estimator + posture-aware `shouldBlockSync` + shared `runInlineCostGate` on both `--all` and single-source paths; `--full` prices delta + stale backlog.
- Per-source failure acks (the #1939 ledger is per-source + lock-serialized) lift the D15 parallel refusal.
- `spend.posture` + the five spend knobs registered in `KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS` (no more `--force` archaeology).

## Reviews

- `/plan-eng-review` (4 findings folded) + codex outside-voice (12 points absorbed) at plan stage.
- Ship-stage codex pre-landing review caught 4 P1s, all fixed in this PR: the estimator's fetch-first bypassed the SSRF-hardened remote path (now routes through a new hardened `fetchRemote`), and the `--max-cost/--max-usd off` + tokenmax-uncapped behavior was incomplete on reindex/enrich/onboard (now delivered, spend still ledgered).

## Tests

`bun run verify` 30/30; new `test/sync-delta.test.ts` + `test/sync-cost-estimate.test.ts` + `test/spend-off-switch.test.ts`; rewritten cost-gate serial tests (auto-defer, posture, off-switch, format split, single-source); extended preview/backfill/config suites. Full sharded suite green except 8 pre-existing failures in the `conversation-parser` LLM suite (unrelated; they fail identically on `origin/master` due to a local `~/.gbrain` config key, CI-clean).

Docs: `docs/operations/spend-controls.md` (every gate, key, default, off switch, posture interaction).

Recurring queue wedge: dueling supervisors under split $HOME + per-cycle RSS blowout trip crash-budget breaker on the healthy supervisor
body:
# Recurring queue wedge: dueling supervisors under split `$HOME` + worker RSS blowout → crash-budget breaker trips on the *healthy* supervisor

## Summary
On a multi-source Postgres deployment, the minion queue wedges every ~1h. Doctor reports `Score 0/100 wedged_queue` and "auto-fixes" by restarting the supervisor, but the wedge returns. Root cause is **three interacting bugs**, none individually fatal:

1. **Split `$HOME` makes the single-supervisor guard blind.** The supervisor's default pid-file is `${HOME}/.gbrain/supervisor-${brainId}.pid` (supervisor.ts:143). Different launchers run under different `$HOME`: the long-lived keeper runs with `HOME=/root`, while doctor / ops / interactive runs use `HOME=/data`. Two supervisors therefore resolve **different pid-file paths**, so the pidfile collision check (supervisor.ts:758) never sees the other instance. They both start; the second one trips the DB-level fence ("Supervisor already running for queue 'default' on this database", supervisor.ts:531) and fast-exits — **but that fence-collision exit is recorded as a crash** on the shared 24h ledger.

2. **Doctor's wedged_queue auto-fix spawns a duplicate that's guaranteed to fence-crash.** When doctor (HOME=/data) sees a stall, it runs `jobs supervisor start` against the same DB where the keeper's supervisor (HOME=/root) is already healthy. Because of bug #1 it can't see the existing pid-file, so it spawns, hits the DB fence, and dies — adding one "crash" per doctor run. ~10 doctor/keeper cycles later, `max_crashes_exceeded` trips (supervisor.ts:831) and the supervisor **permanently gives up**, even though a healthy supervisor was running the whole time. Doctor then reports 0/100 while the queue is actually fine — and eventually really kills it.

3. **A per-source `autopilot-cycle` blows the worker RSS from ~4GB → ~10GB in <60s, then gets RSS-killed mid-job.** Observed live: a single cycle's brain-wide phase loads a huge working set; worker RSS climbed 4459MB → 7069MB → 9695MB in three 20s samples, then the RSS watchdog SIGKILL'd the worker at the cap, orphaning 3 in-flight `autopilot-cycle` jobs as `active (stalled?)`. The supervisor respawns the worker (another crash-budget tick), and the stalled jobs feed the "wedged_queue" signal that triggers bug #2.

The net loop: fat cycle → RSS kill → stalled jobs → doctor "wedged" → duplicate supervisor spawn → fence crash → crash budget burns → breaker trips → real wedge → doctor reports 0/100.

## Evidence
- `jobs supervisor status` showed `Crashes (24h): 20 (runtime=0 oom=0 unknown=20 legacy=0)`, `Clean exits: 0`, `Max crashes exceeded`. All 20 "unknown" — i.e. not OOM, not runtime: they're the fence-collision fast-exits + RSS-kill respawns, which the audit can't classify.
- Supervisor log: repeated `started supervisor_pid=… → shutting_down reason=SIGTERM exit_code=0 → stopped` every ~30s. Clean SIGTERMs, not crashes — consistent with duplicate-spawn fence exits, not code faults.
- Two pid-file names observed in the same deployment: `supervisor.pid` (keeper) and `supervisor-<brainId>.pid` (doctor's spawn / default path). `supervisor status` read the randomized one and reported "not running" while a healthy supervisor existed under the canonical name.
- Worker process env confirmed `HOME=/root` for the keeper-spawned supervisor; doctor/ops use `HOME=/data`.

## Suggested fixes
1. **Make the single-supervisor guard `$HOME`-independent.** Key the pid-file / liveness check on `(database, queue, brainId)` resolved from the DB or a fixed state dir (e.g. always `/data/.gbrain` or a configured `state_dir`), not `${HOME}`. Two launchers with different `$HOME` against the same DB must resolve the **same** guard. At minimum, document that `GBRAIN_SUPERVISOR_PID_FILE` must be pinned identically across every launcher (cron, doctor, service manager) and have doctor refuse to spawn if it can't write/read the canonical path.
2. **Don't count a DB-fence fast-exit as a crash.** supervisor.ts:531's "already running" exit is the guard working correctly — it should exit with a distinct non-crash code that the crash-budget ledger ignores. Otherwise the guard *causes* the breaker trip it's meant to prevent.
3. **Doctor should detect an existing healthy supervisor (by DB fence / canonical pid-file) and NOT spawn a duplicate.** If a supervisor is already claiming+completing on the DB, the wedged_queue "auto-fix" should retry stalled jobs only, never `supervisor start`.
4. **Cap per-cycle memory / shrink the brain-wide working set.** A single `autopilot-cycle` should not be able to take the worker from 4→10GB in 60s. Either stream the brain-wide phases (embed/orphans/purge/resolve_symbol_edges/grade_takes/calibration_profile) in bounded batches, or set the worker `--max-rss` low enough that a graceful recycle happens *before* the spike forces a hard SIGKILL mid-job (graceful drain vs. orphaned stalls).
5. **Stalled-on-RSS-kill jobs should be auto-retried, not left `active (stalled?)`** feeding a false wedge signal — or the stalled-sweeper TTL should be shorter than the doctor's wedge threshold so the queue self-heals before doctor escalates.

## Environment
- Postgres via PgBouncer txn-mode (port 6543, prepared statements disabled).
- 5 federated sources; per-source fan-out submitter on a 5-min cron (submitter-only; a separately-managed standalone worker processes the queue).
- Worker: tini-wrapped, `--concurrency 3 --max-rss 16384 --nice 15`. ~182K-page primary source.
- Supervisor crash budget: `max_crashes=10` / 24h.

title: Route the subagent loop through gateway.chat() so models.tier.subagent can target non-Anthropic providers (Gemini)
body:
## Summary

`models.tier.subagent` is hard-gated to Anthropic providers (the three-layer `enforceSubagentAnthropic` guard in `src/core/model-config.ts`, the queue rejection in `src/core/minions/queue.ts`, and the `subagent_provider` check in `src/commands/doctor.ts`). On a Gemini-only deployment this means the entire agentic layer — `brainstorm` / `lsd`, `autopilot-cycle`, and the dream cycle's `synthesize` / `patterns` / `consolidate` phases — either no-ops/fails or silently bills Anthropic via the `claude-sonnet-4-6` fallback.

Requesting that the subagent loop be routed through the provider-neutral `gateway.chat()` seam so `models.tier.subagent` can target Gemini (or any gateway-supported provider).

## Why it's currently gated

The gate is explicit about the cause — from `src/core/model-config.ts`:

> "The subagent loop in `src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts` makes Anthropic Messages API calls with prompt caching on system + tools; routing it elsewhere silently breaks."

The coupling, concretely:

- `subagent.ts` calls the raw Anthropic Messages API (`MessagesClient`) directly instead of going through `gateway.chat()`.
- Anthropic prompt caching (`cache_control`) on the system prompt + tool defs.
- Anthropic-shaped persistence: `subagent_messages.content_blocks` and `subagent_tool_executions` store Anthropic `tool_use` / `tool_result` block shapes; replay/reconciliation keys on `tool_use_id`.
- Rate-leases keyed on `anthropic:messages`.

So it's a provider-coupling problem, not a model-capability gap — Gemini supports multi-turn function-calling agentic loops.

## Precedent

`src/core/think/index.ts` was migrated off `new Anthropic()` to wrap `gateway.chat()` in v0.35.5.0, with a stated *"v0.36.x TODO: drop the `ThinkLLMClient` indirection entirely."* The subagent loop is the remaining holdout. The gateway already supports Gemini (used today for chat / expansion / fact-extraction, and as a slot in cross-modal eval).

## Proposed approach

- Route the subagent loop through `gateway.chat()`, translating the Anthropic content-block message/tool format to/from the gateway's provider-agnostic shape (Gemini `functionCall` / `functionResponse`).
- Replace Anthropic prompt-caching with the gateway's caching abstraction (or make it a no-op for providers without it).
- Generalize the `subagent_messages` / `subagent_tool_executions` persistence (or add a translation layer) so non-Anthropic block shapes round-trip.
- Once the loop is provider-neutral, drop `enforceSubagentAnthropic` (or downgrade it from a hard fallback to a capability check).

## Environment

Observed on gbrain **0.37.5.0** (gate present since v0.31.12, unchanged through v0.37).

## Motivation

Gemini-only deployments (a brain host with unlimited Gemini credits and no Anthropic billing) currently can't use any of the agentic / takes / brainstorm features. The dream cycle's consolidate phase silently produces zero takes and no calibration profile, because the subagent loop it relies on can't run on Gemini.

title: Feature/gbrain memory voice stack
Sync is single-core-bound at the DB layer: global page_generation_clock trigger serializes all writers (+4 related sync bugs)
body:
## Summary

Sync is **single-core-bound at the database layer**, not the queue layer. A global per-statement trigger on the `pages` table serializes every concurrent writer on one counter row, so process- or worker-level parallelism just moves the bottleneck from CPU to commit-lock wait. This is the real reason large-delta syncs are slow regardless of `--workers`.

Found during an investigation where one source went ~76h behind HEAD while every other source stayed fresh. Five distinct, independent defects across three layers (database schema, sync logic, queue handler). Ranked by depth below.

---

## BUG 1 — Global generation-clock trigger serializes all page writes (root cause)

**Severity: HIGH.** This is why "sync is single-core."

`pages` carries a statement-level trigger:

```sql
-- src/core/migrate.ts (page_generation_clock_and_statement_trigger)
CREATE TRIGGER bump_page_generation_clock_trg
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON pages
  FOR EACH STATEMENT
  EXECUTE FUNCTION bump_page_generation_clock_fn();

-- bump_page_generation_clock_fn():
UPDATE page_generation_clock SET value = value + 1 WHERE id = 1;
```

`page_generation_clock` is a **single-row table** (`id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1)`). Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statement against `pages` takes a `RowExclusiveLock` on that one tuple and must wait for the prior writer's transaction to **commit** before proceeding. Because the importer commits **once per file** (`engine.transaction(...)` in `src/core/import-file.ts`), each file import is one clock bump = one serialization point. Concurrent importers serialize on it.

**Live evidence (8 parallel `import` processes against a large delta):**

- `pg_stat_activity`: 18 connections `state=active wait_event_type=Lock wait_event=transactionid`, 1 on `Lock/tuple`.
- `pg_locks`: `page_generation_clock` held `RowExclusiveLock granted=true` by ~19 connections (all queued on it).
- Blocked query: `INSERT INTO pages (...)`.
- Throughput: 8 processes → **0.8–0.9 cores total**, ~0.64 pages/sec. Not CPU-bound. Commit-serialized.

**Why it exists (legitimate):** the clock backs the query-cache Layer-1 bookmark. The prior version read `MAX(generation) FROM pages`, which had two correctness bugs (UPDATE-to-non-max didn't advance MAX; DELETE didn't fire at all). The single-row counter fixed cache correctness, and it was deliberately made `FOR EACH STATEMENT` (not row-level) to avoid turning a large batch DELETE into N counter UPDATEs. That solved the batch-DELETE case, but the **per-file-INSERT path during sync still hits it once per file**, and concurrent importers serialize on commit.

**Fix directions:**
1. **Batch the page writes** — write N pages per transaction so the clock bumps once per N files instead of once per file. Highest leverage for sync throughput.
2. **Make the clock contention-free** — replace the locked-row `UPDATE ... value+1` with a sequence (`nextval`), or a debounced/coarse clock bumped at most once per K ms by a background task, removing the hot row from the write path entirely. Cache invalidation tolerates ms-scale coarseness.
3. **Bump once per import batch** rather than per statement on the sync path.

> Note: **#2236 (core-aware sync concurrency) is effectively blocked on this.** Adding worker concurrency cannot help until this global serialization point is removed — the writers will still queue on one row.

---

## BUG 2 — Queue/worker sync path ignores the concurrency parameter

**Severity: MEDIUM.**

The explicit CLI path `import <dir> --workers N` genuinely parallelizes (N engine connections, concurrent file processing). But the **queue/worker-driven sync** runs the delta-apply with `importFile` **in-process, single-threaded**, ignoring the concurrency param (`job.data.concurrency` is read in `src/core/jobs.ts` but the import phase doesn't fan out). So the production path never engages parallelism even for the per-file parse/hash/embed CPU that could overlap between clock bumps.

**Fix:** route the queue sync's import phase through the same worker pool the CLI `import` command uses, honoring a concurrency param. Combined with BUG 1's batching, this is what unlocks real multi-core sync.

---

## BUG 3 — Recurring `op_checkpoints.completed_keys` scalar corruption

**Severity: MEDIUM.** Crashes every sync of a large-delta source until repaired.

`op_checkpoints` rows for `op='sync-target'` intermittently get `completed_keys` stored as a **scalar string** instead of a JSONB array. The checkpoint loader then throws `cannot extract elements from a scalar` on **every** sync attempt for that source, wedging it. Observed: repaired the rows to `'[]'::jsonb`, ran a sync, and the corruption **reappeared** (new fingerprint) — so a write path in the sync logic itself re-stores the scalar on the large-delta case. The known-good writer (`recordCompleted` in `src/core/op-checkpoint.ts`) does a correct `JSON.stringify` of a sorted array, and `APPEND_PATHS_SQL` inserts a valid `'[]'::jsonb` parent + writes children to `op_checkpoint_paths` — so the scalar source is a **different, unlocated write path** that fires on large deltas.

**Repro signal:** large-delta sync of a source many commits behind HEAD.

**Repair (idempotent, safe — child `op_checkpoint_paths` rows are the append-only source of truth):**
```sql
UPDATE op_checkpoints
   SET completed_keys = '[]'::jsonb, updated_at = now()
 WHERE jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) <> 'array';
```

**Fix:** locate the write path that stores a non-array `completed_keys` for `op='sync-target'`, force array serialization, and add `CHECK (jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) = 'array')` so it can't re-corrupt.

---

## BUG 4 — `last_sync_at` only advances on full completion, so partial syncs never bookmark

**Severity: MEDIUM.** Makes a slow/interrupted source look permanently stale.

`last_sync_at`/`last_commit` are only stamped when a sync fully completes and writes the commit anchor at the END (`writeSyncAnchor(...)` in `src/commands/sync.ts`). If a sync makes partial progress (imports some files) but is killed before the anchor write, the bookmark never moves — so the next run re-computes the full delta from the same old commit and the source reads as "N hours stale" forever, even though it imports every cycle. The affected source was ~1,043 commits behind HEAD (a clean ancestor, normal delta) and had been making partial progress for days, losing the bookmark each time.

This interacts viciously with BUG 1: BUG 1 makes a large-delta sync slow → slow sync gets killed before completion → BUG 4 means it gets zero credit → infinite staleness.

**Fix:** checkpoint the anchor incrementally (advance `last_commit` to the last fully-applied commit boundary as the sync progresses), so partial progress is durable and a killed sync resumes instead of restarting from scratch.

---

## BUG 5 — `--force-break-lock` fast-exits doing nothing

**Severity: LOW.** Misleading no-op.

The `--force-break-lock` path exits in ~4s reporting `Lock ... not held (nothing to break)` with `rc=0`, even when a sync is genuinely wedged. It doesn't do the work the flag promises, sending operators down a dead end.

**Fix:** either make the flag actually break a held lock, or report honestly (non-zero exit when there's nothing to break) so callers don't treat it as a successful unwedge.

---

## Source references

- Clock trigger + rationale: `src/core/migrate.ts` (migration `page_generation_clock_and_statement_trigger`), mirrored in `src/core/pglite-schema.ts`, `src/core/schema-embedded.ts`, `src/schema.sql`.
- Per-file commit: `src/core/import-file.ts` (`engine.transaction`).
- Page insert SQL: `src/core/postgres-engine.ts`, `src/core/pglite-engine.ts`.
- Queue concurrency param: `src/core/jobs.ts`.
- Anchor write: `src/commands/sync.ts` (`writeSyncAnchor`).
- Checkpoint writers: `src/core/op-checkpoint.ts` (`APPEND_PATHS_SQL`, `recordCompleted`).
- Delta primitive: `src/core/sync-delta.ts` (`computeSyncDelta`).
- Walker symlink skip: `src/commands/import.ts` (`collectSyncableFiles` — `lstat` + `isSymbolicLink()` continue).

## Suggested fix order

1. **BUG 1 + BUG 2 together** (batch writes + worker-pool the queue sync) — unlocks real multi-core throughput.
2. **BUG 4** (incremental anchor) — makes slow syncs durable so they stop looking stale.
3. **BUG 3** (find scalar-writer + CHECK constraint) — stops large-delta sources from wedging.
4. **BUG 5** (honest `--force-break-lock`).

title: v0.42.46.0 fix(engine): federated read scope reaches by-slug reads (#2200)
body:
## Summary
Closes the read-path half of gbrain#2200: a `federated_read` grant now reaches every by-slug read, not just search and query. Reported (with a proposed fix) by @mlobo2012.

**Engine (`425c7626`)** — `getTags` / `getLinks` / `getBacklinks` / `getTimeline` (both engines) and `TimelineOpts` accept a federated `sourceIds[]` scope, precedence over scalar `sourceId`, filtering `source_id = ANY($::text[])` — mirroring `getPage` from v0.42.37.0.
- `getTags`: `page_id = (subquery)` → `IN (subquery)` + `DISTINCT`, so a slug present in more than one granted source unions tags instead of throwing on a multi-row subquery.
- `getLinks` / `getBacklinks`: the federated branch scopes **all three** page endpoints — source, target, AND the authoring origin — so a link crossing out of grant can't surface a foreign slug. Scalar/unscoped branches are unchanged (trusted internal callers keep the cross-source view).
- `getTimeline`: the Postgres 8-branch query collapses into one fragment-composed query; PGLite gains the `sourceIds` branch.

**Ops (`332d760d`)** — `get_page` resolves tags against the concrete page's source; `get_tags` / `get_links` / `get_backlinks` / `get_timeline` route through `sourceScopeOpts(ctx)`. New `linkReadScopeOpts` promotes an untrusted-remote scalar scope (legacy / pre-`federated_read` tokens) to `sourceIds[]` so they also get all-endpoint link scoping; trusted local CLI keeps cross-source.

**Tests (`30adae1f`)** + **Docs (`231db3cd`)**.

Bug B from the issue (semantic query cache) was already fixed in v0.42.34.0 via `cacheScopeKey()`; verified, no change needed.

## Test Coverage
All new code paths covered (AI-assessed 100% after closing 2 symmetry gaps).
```
op handlers       get_page tags · get_tags · get_links · get_backlinks · get_timeline
  federated grant   ✓ reads across granted sources (union)
  isolation         ✓ out-of-grant slug → empty, never the default decoy
  far-endpoint leak ✓ cross-source link target NOT returned (D4A)
  origin leak       ✓ out-of-grant origin_slug nulled (F1)
  scalar-remote     ✓ untrusted remote scalar promoted to all-endpoint (D1)
  trusted local     ✓ keeps cross-source view
engine methods    getTags/getLinks/getBacklinks/getTimeline (PGLite + parity arms)
  sourceIds[]       ✓ match / exclude / precedence-over-scalar / empty-array contract
  union (D3A)       ✓ same slug across two sources
  timeline window   ✓ date filters after the Postgres fragment refactor (D5A)
```
Tests: `test/get-page-federated-scope.test.ts` 28 pass (+18); `test/e2e/engine-parity.test.ts` federated arms (CI / DATABASE_URL).

## Pre-Landing Review
10 findings, 0 critical, all informational — all auto-fixed (stale "two-branch" comments → three-branch, federated/idiom doc notes, empty-array contract test, Postgres timeline date-window parity coverage). Quality score 9.5/10. Performance: no findings (all queries hit existing indexes).

## Adversarial Review
Claude + Codex, both independently confirmed two real cross-source leaks — both fixed before commit:
- **F1 (multi-model):** the federated link branch scoped from+to but left the third endpoint (the authoring origin, surfaced as `origin_slug`) unscoped. Fixed: origin LEFT JOIN carries the same grant filter; regression-tested both engines.
- **D1 (Codex HIGH):** untrusted remote callers with a legacy scalar token hit the scalar branch (near-endpoint only). Fixed: `linkReadScopeOpts` promotes them to all-endpoint scoping; internal/CLI callers untouched.

## Design Review

## Eval Results
No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Scope Drift

## Plan Completion
17 DONE, 1 CHANGED (D4A both-endpoint scoping applied in the federated branch only — remote clients always route there; the scalar branch is left for trusted internal callers, documented in engine comments). 0 NOT DONE.

## Verification Results
Backend-only change, no dev server — automated plan verification skipped. Verified via tests + typecheck.

## TODOS
Filed `gbrain#2200 federated-read follow-ups` (P1): the sibling by-slug read ops (`get_chunks`, `get_raw_data`, `get_versions`, `resolve_slugs`) still use scalar-only scope and don't yet thread a federated grant — same class, next wave.

## Documentation

CHANGELOG / TODOS / VERSION shipped with the fix; CLAUDE.md's source-isolation invariant already accurate (no edit, no llms-bundle change).

title: v0.42.49.0 feat(pace): native DB-contention pacing for embed/sync backfills
body:
## What

Native, opt-in DB-contention pacing for embed/sync backfills — gbrain now throttles itself when the database gets busy, so clearing a large backlog can't starve the minion supervisor's lock renewals (the `lock-renewal-failed` → dead-jobs cascade). This replaces external SIGSTOP/SIGCONT wrapper scripts, which were blind (a side-pool latency probe read low while the pool that mattered starved), unsafe (SIGSTOP can freeze a process mid-transaction holding locks), and couldn't touch peak pressure.

Default `off` — nothing changes until you opt in.

## How it works

One composable primitive (`src/core/db-pacer.ts`):
- **Concurrency cap is the lever** — bounds simultaneous in-flight DB writes (= pooler slots held). Embed lowers its worker count to the cap; `sync` uses a shared permit across its parallel worker engines (the multi-pool case).
- **In-band signal** — measures the work's *own* query latency (EWMA), so it can never be blind the way an out-of-band probe was.
- **Cooperative sleep** — jittered `setTimeout` between safe points (never mid-transaction, so the lock heartbeat keeps firing). Abort-throwing; fail-open (a pacer bug never kills a backfill).

Named bundles (`src/core/pace-mode.ts`): `off`/`gentle`/`balanced`/`aggressive`, resolved **per-call → `GBRAIN_PACE_*` env → config → bundle** (env above config = incident escape hatch).

## Surfaces

- `gbrain embed --stale --pace[=mode]` (bare `--pace` = balanced), `--pace-max-concurrency=N`
- `pace.mode` config paces every `runEmbedCore` caller (cycle embed, catch-up, sync-auto-embed) **and** the prod `embed-backfill` job automatically
- `--background` carries the explicit override into the queued job; the handler re-resolves env>config>bundle at execution
- `EmbedResult.pacing` telemetry (`--json`) + one-line stderr summary

## Correctness fixes pacing would otherwise worsen

- `embed --stale` single-flights per source via the same lock the `embed-backfill` job holds (all-source runs lock every source in sorted order) — closes the concurrent-backfill upsert-race window
- Bounded end-of-run keyset re-entry (paced runs only) catches rows that land behind the cursor during a longer run
- Embed wall-clock budget excludes paced-sleep time so a contended DB converges instead of exiting early

## Review

- CEO review (SELECTIVE_EXPANSION) + Eng review — both CLEARED
- Codex outside-voice: 2 plan passes (18 + 5 findings, all absorbed) + 1 pre-landing pass on the implementation diff (2 P1 + 3 P2, all fixed)
- Unit tests: `test/db-pacer.test.ts`, `test/pace-mode.test.ts`; full sharded suite green on the merged tree

## Deferred (TODOS.md)

`doctor` pace-check (E2), `--pace=auto` autotune (E3), first-class pacing in more job handlers (E5), supervisor concurrency 3→2 + job-kind slot fairness (E7, the daemon root cause), `gbrain sync --pace` flag, real-PG e2e.

title: v0.42.48.0 feat(durability): auto-harden brain repos for git durability on PAT+URL
body:
## v0.42.48.0 — Brain-repo git durability Fresh agents kept drifting out of sync with their knowledge-wiki git repos: writes sat local-only and never pushed, long-lived sessions edited a stale tree, scratch output landed outside the repo and vanished. The moment gbrain is given a PAT + a GitHub URL for a brain repo, it now auto-hardens that working tree for durability, idempotently. ### What ships - `gbrain sources harden [--pat-file

] [--branch ] [--no-cron] [--no-verify] [--dry-run] [--json]` — the idempotent 6-step audit/fix. - `gbrain sources pull | --path

[--branch ]` — divergence-safe rebase-pull; `--path` runs **DB-free** (the cron's entry; never opens the local engine lock). - `gbrain sources unharden ` — removes cron/hook/credential wiring; runs automatically before `sources remove`. - `--pat-file` / `--no-harden` on `sources add`; managed clones auto-harden on add. - `git-remote.ts`: `divergenceSafePull` (skip-on-dirty, conflict-abort-clean, never-mid-rebase), `detectDefaultBranch`, `pushProbe`, `GIT_ENV_AUTH`, and an env-gated `GBRAIN_GIT_ALLOW_FILE_TRANSPORT` escape hatch. ### The six durability guarantees 1. Pull current state (divergence-safe rebase). 2. Local, **untracked** post-commit auto-push hook (best-effort fallback). 3. Committed `scripts/brain-commit-push.sh` that **refuses to report success without a confirmed push** (the guarantee). 4. Always-on durability rules in the active resolver file (deterministic filing from the canonical taxonomy; commit-and-push-never-deferred; pull-before-each-write-batch). 5. A 30-minute DB-free background pull so an idle session can't go stale. 6. Push-access verification up front (a read-only token or protected branch surfaces immediately). ### Security posture (gbrain's first push path + first credential storage) - Push automation installed **locally per machine**, not committed into the repo (a pulled commit can't rewrite executed code next to the token). - Credential is **repo-scoped** (least-privilege); an existing credential helper is reused when present rather than writing a new one. - Token never enters the repo, the tracked remote URL, logs, or the run report (redacted via the existing exact-value scrubber). ### Review Cleared through `/plan-eng-review` (13 findings folded, 0 unresolved) plus a Codex outside-voice pass that reversed two early calls: committed hooks → local untracked (RCE/exfil + inert-on-clone), and a scheduler extraction → minimal-now. Decisions D1–D13 implemented as cleared. ### Tests - 41 new durability tests across 4 files (git helpers, core harden/unharden, hook+helper E2E with real background push, cron generators). - Typecheck clean; `verify` gate 30/30; existing `git-remote.test.ts` 37/37; impacted sources/cli 145/145; 134/134 on the merged tree. Binary builds + smokes (DB-free `sources pull --path` runs with no brain configured). ### Not in scope (filed in TODOS.md) - gbrain write-path calling commit-push synchronously when hardened (covers writes never committed by an agent). - Unifying the durability cron with autopilot's OS-scheduler. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

v0.42.50.0 fix(autopilot): kill the dead-job storm + supervisor queue wedge (#2194 #2227 #1994)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring failure mode on multi-source Postgres brains where autopilot manufactured a continuous stream of dead `autopilot-cycle` jobs and the minion supervisor periodically wedged the queue it is meant to keep alive. Root cause was one disease with several interacting parts; this wave addresses all of them. Closes gbrain#2194, gbrain#2227, gbrain#1994.

## What changed (8 atomic commits)

1. **`test`** — pin that the duplicate-supervisor LOCK_HELD fence-exit is never counted as a crash (#2227).
2. **`fix` (prerequisite)** — per-source cycles bind filesystem phases to `source.local_path`, not the global repo path, so FS/DB phases and the freshness stamp agree on the source (#2194/#2227, TODOS:634).
3. **`fix`** — `gbrain jobs supervisor status` / `gbrain doctor` detect a live supervisor via the queue-scoped DB lock when the `$HOME`-derived pidfile is absent. Keyed on lock freshness, never a bare PID probe (PID-reuse-safe) (#2227).
4. **`fix`** — supervisor degrades to capped-backoff retry instead of permanently giving up at the soft crash budget; self-heals on a transient DB blip; hard ceiling via `GBRAIN_SUPERVISOR_HARD_STOP_CRASHES` (#1994/#2227, TODOS:92).
5. **`feat`** — clamp per-tick fan-out to `max(1, concurrency−1)` (gated on a live supervisor) + a `gbrain doctor` warning on mismatch (#2194).
6. **`feat`** — per-source failure cooldown (bounded exponential 10→120min), checked at dispatch AND claim time; a success clears it (#2194).
7. **`feat`** — **split the cycle**: per-source jobs run only source-scoped phases; a single `autopilot-global-maintenance` job runs the brain-wide phases once per window (structural single-flight). This kills the 4→10GB RSS blowout that was the shared root cause of #2194 and #2227 (#2194/#2227).
8. **`fix`** — categorize the new doctor check + a nullable-engine guard.

## Why the split (the load-bearing decision)

The plan first proposed single-flight-skip (concurrent cycles skip the global phases if another holds a lock). A codex outside-voice review during `/plan-eng-review` caught that skip-then-stamp-fresh poisons the only freshness gate — a source gets marked done while its new rows go unembedded. The split design (per-source phases + one global-maintenance job) is the codebase's documented Phase-2 design: no skip semantics, no freshness poisoning, single-flight by construction.

## New config / surface
- Jobs: `autopilot-global-maintenance`
- Config: `autopilot.failure_cooldown_min` (0=off), `autopilot.failure_cooldown_cap_min`, `autopilot.fanout_clamp_to_concurrency`, `autopilot.global_floor_min`
- Env: `GBRAIN_SUPERVISOR_HARD_STOP_CRASHES`
- Doctor check: `autopilot_fanout_concurrency`
- Source config field: `last_source_cycle_at`; brain config: `autopilot.last_global_at`

All on by default; existing brains pick them up on the next tick with no migration (one catch-up global pass on first tick).

## Test plan
- `bun run typecheck` — clean.
- New/changed unit tests across the blast radius all pass (supervisor, child-worker-supervisor, db-lock, fanout, cooldown, global-maintenance, doctor, doctor-categories) — 438 tests green post-merge.
- Engine-parity: new `test/e2e/autopilot-cooldown-parity.test.ts` (PGLite half local; Postgres half runs in CI).
- Reviewed via `/plan-eng-review` + codex outside-voice (logged CLEAR).

v0.42.50.0 ci: reliability hardening — cancel-superseded + per-job timeouts + actionlint + hermetic E2E env
body:
## Summary

Brings the CI-reliability hygiene from the sibling GStack project over to gbrain's two hot-path workflows. gbrain already had the deep machinery (content-hash run-skip cache, weight-aware shard balancing, test-isolation guards, hermetic E2E) — this closes the cheap-but-missing GitHub-Actions gaps that were already wired into `heavy-tests.yml` but never into `test.yml`/`e2e.yml`.

## What changed (3 atomic commits + version)

1. **`ci:` concurrency cancel-superseded + per-job timeouts** (`test.yml`, `e2e.yml`)
   - `concurrency` cancels a superseded run when a newer commit lands on the same PR. Keyed on **PR number** for `pull_request` events (fork-safe — two PRs from forks sharing a branch name won't cancel each other) with a `github.ref` fallback so push/scheduled runs always complete.
   - `timeout-minutes` on **every** job (test matrix 15, verify 12, serial 15, slow 12, e2e tier1 20 / tier2 30, trivial jobs 5-10). Converts a wedged job from a 6-hour zombie (GitHub's default) into a fast, legible fail. `fail-fast: false` was already set on the matrix.
2. **`ci:` add `actionlint` workflow** (`rhysd/actionlint@v1.7.11`, SHA-pinned to gbrain's convention) — lints workflow YAML on `.github/workflows/**` changes so a malformed workflow / bad action ref / missing-permission bug is caught before it ships a broken pipeline.
3. **`ci(e2e):` hermetic env scrub** in `scripts/run-e2e.sh` — drops `CONDUCTOR_*` / `MCP_* `/ `OPENCLAW_*` / `GBRAIN_*` (except the isolation-critical `GBRAIN_HOME`) before bun starts, so a dev or Conductor shell's config overrides can't bleed into E2E child processes and make "hermetic" E2E non-hermetic. Denylist scrub — `PATH`/`HOME`/`TMPDIR`/`DATABASE_URL` survive.

## What was deliberately NOT ported

GStack CI that is product-specific: windows-free-tests / windows-setup-e2e (gbrain has no Windows surface), the evals matrix + prebuilt ghcr CI image (GStack needs Playwright Chromium; gbrain has no browser), make-pdf-gate (no PDFs), pr-title-sync + its `pull_request_target` hardening (gbrain enforces PR-title via `/ship` + version-gate). Also explicitly NOT adding blanket `bun test --retry` — gbrain's flake philosophy is root-cause via isolation guards, not retry-masking; adding retries would hide the isolation bugs those guards exist to surface.

## Verification
- `actionlint` clean on all workflows (the new gate lints itself + the edits).
- `shellcheck -S warning scripts/run-e2e.sh` clean; `bash -n` syntax OK.
- Hermetic scrub validated end-to-end: a 78-test E2E file passes against a local Postgres with `DATABASE_URL` surviving the scrub and a planted `GBRAIN_BRAIN_ID` dropped.
- No source code (`.ts`/`src/`) changed — unit suite and typecheck are unaffected.
- Adversarial pass (codex) caught and fixed the original `head_ref` concurrency key (fork-collision); now PR-number-keyed.

title: v0.42.51.0 fix(sync): contention-free clock + checkpoint integrity + honest sync freshness
body:
## Summary
Sync concurrency + reliability wave (4 fixes + a test-isolation fix).

**Performance / concurrency**
- **Contention-free page-generation clock** (`migrate.ts` v118, `query-cache-gate.ts`, `schema.sql` + `pglite-schema.ts` + `schema-embedded.ts`). The clock backing the search cache moved from a single locked counter row (`UPDATE … WHERE id=1`, a transaction-length `RowExclusiveLock` every page write serialized on) to a `nextval()` sequence. Concurrent sync workers no longer wait in line on one tuple's commit, so a large `gbrain sync` actually uses the workers it's given. The Layer-1 cache contract is unchanged (it over-invalidates, never serves stale); `last_value` is non-transactional, which is the safe direction.

**Reliability**
- **`op_checkpoints` array-shape guard** (`migrate.ts` v119 + 3 fresh schemas, `op-checkpoint.ts`). `completed_keys` now carries a DB-enforced `CHECK (jsonb_typeof = 'array')` (named so the fresh-install blob and the migration don't double-add), the migration repairs any pre-existing scalar under `LOCK TABLE`, and the loader skips a bad parent row instead of throwing and discarding all banked progress for that source.
- **Doctor distinguishes in-progress from stale** (`doctor.ts`). A source holding a live per-source sync lock is reported as actively syncing (naming the holder pid+host) rather than flagged stale; a genuinely stuck/blocked/never-completed sync still reports stale. The signal is the live lock — checkpoint banking is not used, because a blocked sync banks too.
- **Honest `--force-break-lock`** (`sync.ts`). When no lock is held it now says so plainly and points at how to inspect a genuinely wedged sync, instead of a terse no-op that read like a successful unwedge.

**Tests**
- **Hermetic no-key tests** (`with-env.ts` + 5 test files). `hasAnthropicKey()` / `checkZeEmbeddingHealth()` read the key from env OR `~/.gbrain/config.json`; several "no key" tests cleared only the env var, so they passed in key-less CI but failed on a dev machine with a real config key. Added a shared `emptyHome()` and isolated `GBRAIN_HOME` in every no-key path.

BUG 2 from the source postmortem (queue sync ignoring concurrency) was verified already-correct in current code — no change. Push/webhook sync paths pass no concurrency field and rely on `autoConcurrency` auto-scaling.

## Test Coverage
Coverage audit: 88% (23/26 changed code paths), 0 regressions uncovered. Three minor gaps, all non-regression: two fail-safe defensive `catch→false` paths in doctor (untested but fail toward staleness by design), the op-checkpoint corruption-warning string (the branch that emits it is exercised), and the v118-reworded mid-upgrade `catch` (behavior unchanged). Gate: PASS (≥80% target).

New/updated tests: PGLite sequence round-trip + `is_called` trap, monotonic re-seed regression, rollback-over-invalidation-is-safe, trigger-uses-nextval mechanism, scalar CHECK rejection + exactly-one-constraint + loader-survives-scalar + v119 repair, doctor live-lock × 6 (incl. blocked-with-banked-rows stays FAIL), force-break-lock diagnostic × 3.

## Pre-Landing Review
Codex adversarial review of the implementation diff found and fixed three:
- **[P1]** fresh-schema `setval` was not monotonic — `initSchema` replay could move the sequence backward below a stored cache bookmark (stale-serve risk). Fixed: seed via `GREATEST` over the sequence's own `last_value` in all 3 schemas + v118; pinned by a regression test.
- **[P2]** v119 CHECK-exists guard keyed on `conname` only (not globally unique) — scoped to `conrelid = 'op_checkpoints'::regclass`.
- **[P3]** in-progress note punctuation in fail/warn doctor messages.
Also pre-vetted at plan stage by `/plan-eng-review` (eng + codex outside-voice, 7 findings all folded).

## Plan Completion
Plan: sync concurrency & reliability fix wave. 18 DONE, 3 CHANGED (goals met by different means), all goals addressed. Follow-ups deferred (non-blocking): doctor aliveness uses `!ttl_expired` only (not the steal-grace-window refinement; safe direction); no dedicated v117→v118 migration-replay test (covered transitively by the seed/round-trip tests + the migration running in every initSchema).

## TODOS
No TODO items mapped to these fixes; none marked complete.

## Documentation
Reference docs synced to current-state truth (history-free, passes `check-key-files-current-state.sh`):
- `docs/architecture/KEY_FILES.md` — `doctor.ts` `checkSyncFreshness` now documents live-lock in-progress detection; `op-checkpoint.ts` now documents the `jsonb_typeof='array'` union gate + v119 CHECK/repair/fresh-install mirrors.
CHANGELOG 0.42.51.0 entry intact; llms bundles unchanged (KEY_FILES is link-only).

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] Full unit suite GREEN — 0 failures (~13,964 pass across 4 shards + serial)
- [x] Migrations v118 + v119 apply cleanly on PGLite in every suite's `initSchema`
- [ ] Postgres multi-connection concurrency proof — optional; needs the e2e Postgres harness (not run locally)
