title: Gateway subagent loop unreliable for multi-turn tool calls on non-Anthropic providers (resume loop + Date-in-output rejection)
body:
## Summary

The gateway-native subagent loop (`agent.use_gateway_loop=true`, mandatory for non-Anthropic providers) is unreliable for any multi-turn tool conversation. Two independent bugs combine so that subagent jobs using a local/OpenAI-compatible model (e.g. a `llama-server` qwen) loop on retries and never complete:

1. **Tool-result messages are never persisted** → every *resume* rebuilds an invalid history.
2. **Tool outputs carrying non-JSON values (e.g. `Date`) are rejected by AI SDK v6** → fails *live*, mid-run.

Both surface as the same family of AI SDK v6 errors:
- `Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema.`
- `[chat(<provider:model>)] Tool results are missing for tool calls <ids>`

The Anthropic-direct path is unaffected, so this only bites users who enable the gateway loop for non-Anthropic models.

## Bug 1 — gateway loop never persists the tool-result message

`toolLoop()` (`src/core/ai/gateway.ts`) feeds each turn's tool results back as a `role:'user'` message:

```js
const userMessageIdx = messageIdx++;
void userMessageIdx;                                  // <-- dropped
messages.push({ role: 'user', content: toolResultBlocks });
```

It persists assistant turns (`onAssistantTurn`) and per-tool execution rows (`onToolCall*`), but there is **no callback to persist this user/tool-result message**, and `runSubagentViaGateway` discards `ToolLoopResult.messages`. The legacy Anthropic-direct path *does* persist it (`subagent.ts`, the `userIdx`/`persistMessage(role:'user', content_blocks: toolResults)` write).

Consequence: `subagent_messages` ends up with only odd `message_idx` (assistant turns at 1, 3, 5…) and gaps where the tool-result messages (2, 4…) should be. Within one uninterrupted worker run this is invisible (the messages live in the in-memory array). But on **any resume** (worker restart / re-claim / timeout), `loadPriorMessages` rebuilds the conversation from `subagent_messages` alone — now `[user, assistant(tool-calls A), assistant(tool-calls B), …]` with dangling tool-calls. AI SDK v6 rejects it before the loop's `replayState.priorTools` reconciler ever runs (the reconciler only fires inside tool-dispatch, *after* `chat()`), and the job retries the same broken history until `max_attempts`.

Observed: 23/23 stuck jobs had this gap pattern; the missing-tool-call ids in the error matched the persisted assistant turn's `tool_use_id`s exactly.

## Bug 2 — non-JSON tool outputs rejected by AI SDK v6

AI SDK v6 validates each tool-result `json` output against a strict `JSONValue` Zod schema. gbrain tool outputs routinely contain non-JSON values: **node-postgres returns `timestamptz` columns as JS `Date`**, so `brain_get_page` / `brain_list_pages` rows include Date-typed `updated_at`/`created_at`. A raw `Date` (also `undefined`/`bigint`) makes the entire tool message fail the `ModelMessage` union → `Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema` on the turn *after* such a tool runs.

Crash-replay masks it: on resume the value has already been round-tripped through the `jsonb` column to an ISO string, so a resumed run validates — until the next live tool call produces a fresh `Date`. (`brain_search`, which returns no Date fields, never trips it.)

## Reproduction

With `agent.use_gateway_loop=true` and any non-Anthropic model, run a subagent that makes multi-turn tool calls including `brain_list_pages`/`brain_get_page`, and restart the worker mid-run. Bug 2 fails the live run; Bug 1 then loops every retry.

## Fix

PR linked below:
- `toolLoop`: add an `onToolResultMessage` callback (fired before the in-memory push, write-before-use), wired in `runSubagentViaGateway` to persist the tool-result message. `runSubagentViaGateway` also self-heals already-corrupted jobs by reconstructing each missing tool-result message from settled `subagent_tool_executions` rows.
- `toModelMessages`: normalize tool-result `json` values to plain JSON (`Date`→ISO, `undefined` dropped) at the AI SDK boundary.

Tests: forward persistence + self-healing resume (no tool re-execution); `Date`→ISO normalization + a real `generateText` validation accepting a Date-bearing tool output.

Validated end-to-end against a live `llama-server:qwen36b` dream backlog: jobs that previously looped now run the full multi-turn synthesis to completion with contiguous `message_idx`.

title: fix(subagent): reliable gateway tool-loop for non-Anthropic providers (persist tool-result messages + JSON-normalize outputs)
body:
Fixes #2256.

The gateway-native subagent loop (`agent.use_gateway_loop=true`, mandatory for non-Anthropic providers) couldn't reliably complete a multi-turn tool conversation. Two independent bugs combined to make subagent jobs loop on retries forever. Both surface as AI SDK v6 errors: `Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema` and `Tool results are missing for tool calls <ids>`. The Anthropic-direct path is unaffected.

## Commit 1 — persist tool-result messages; self-heal on resume

`toolLoop()` fed each turn's tool results back as a `role:'user'` message but never persisted it (`void userMessageIdx`), and `runSubagentViaGateway` discarded `ToolLoopResult.messages`. So `subagent_messages` had gaps at every even `message_idx`. On any resume, `loadPriorMessages` rebuilt a history of adjacent assistant turns with dangling tool-calls, which AI SDK v6 rejects — before the `replayState.priorTools` reconciler (which only runs inside tool-dispatch, after `chat()`) ever gets a chance. The job then looped to `max_attempts`. The legacy Anthropic-direct path always persisted this message.

- `toolLoop`: new `onToolResultMessage` callback, fired before the in-memory push (write-before-use).
- `runSubagentViaGateway`: wires it to persist the tool-result message; and `rebuildReplayHistory()` self-heals already-corrupted jobs by reconstructing each missing tool-result message from settled `subagent_tool_executions` rows (matched by provider `toolCallId`) and re-persisting it. Conservative: a still-pending/absent exec leaves the turn un-healed rather than fabricating data. `nextMessageIdx` now derives from `max(known idx)+1` so a healed gap can't collide under the unique `(job_id, message_idx)` constraint.

## Commit 2 — JSON-normalize tool-result outputs

AI SDK v6 validates each tool-result `json` output against a strict `JSONValue` schema. node-postgres returns `timestamptz` as JS `Date`, so `brain_get_page`/`brain_list_pages` rows carry Date-typed `updated_at`/`created_at`; a raw `Date` (also `undefined`/`bigint`) fails the `ModelMessage` union the turn after such a tool runs. Replay masked it (the jsonb round-trip had already stringified the Date).

- `toModelMessages`: normalize the `json` value via `toJsonValue()` (JSON round-trip: `Date`→ISO, `undefined` dropped, non-serializable→string), plus a non-throwing `safeStringify()` for the error-text branch. Persisted blocks are unaffected (write path already JSON-stringifies, so stored and sent forms now agree).

## Tests
- `test/e2e/subagent-gateway-resume.test.ts` — forward persistence (contiguous `message_idx`, no gaps) + self-healing resume from a pre-fix corrupted job without re-executing the tool.
- `test/gateway-model-messages.test.ts` — `Date`→ISO normalization, `undefined` drop, and a real `generateText` validation accepting a Date-bearing tool output (no `ModelMessage` rejection).
- Existing `subagent-gateway-path` and cross-provider `subagent-crash-replay-multi-provider` suites stay green (33 pass on this branch).

## Validation
Deployed against a live `llama-server:qwen36b` dream backlog where 23/23 multi-turn jobs were stuck looping. After the fix, jobs that previously failed every retry run the full multi-turn synthesis to completion with contiguous `message_idx` (verified one job: 16 messages, idx 0–15, real synthesis output; the rest drained the same way). The only non-completions were pre-existing `wall-clock timeout` deaths on the heaviest transcripts that had already exhausted most of their retry budget on the old bug — not a regression.

title: v0.42.45.0 fix(sync): solve sync database scaling issues and concurrency bottlenecks (#2238)
body:
## Overview

This PR resolves **Issue #2238**: *Sync is single-core-bound at the DB layer: global page_generation_clock trigger serializes all writers (+4 related sync bugs)*.

## Changes Implemented

1. **Contention-Free Clock Sequence**:
   - Removed `page_generation_clock` table which acted as a serialization bottleneck due to write/update contention.
   - Swapped in a PostgreSQL sequence `page_generation_clock_seq`.
   - Re-implemented the statement-level trigger `bump_page_generation_clock_fn` on `pages` to update using the sequence.
   - Updated `query-cache-gate.ts` to query sequence value via `SELECT last_value FROM page_generation_clock_seq` with backward-compatible fallback.

2. **Queue Concurrency & Worker Limits**:
   - Configured `gbrain cycle` and queue runner to correctly respect and forward `concurrency`/`workers` options.
   - Compute safe pool connection limits to prevent connection starvation.

3. **Strict JSONB Array Constraint on op_checkpoints**:
   - Added database `CHECK (jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) = 'array')` constraint to enforce array wrapping.
   - Enforced array parsing in `op-checkpoint.ts` runtime methods.

4. **Incremental Anchor Checkpoint**:
   - Modified the sync runner to advance the git commit anchor incrementally during ingest waves, so progress is saved if runs are interrupted.

5. **Exit Code for --force-break-lock**:
   - Sync command returns exit code `1` if a lock break is requested but no lock is currently held.

6. **Windows Compatibility & Testing Fixes**:
   - Fixed regexes parsing frontmatter to support Windows carriage returns (`\r\n`).
   - Fixed E2E test scripts to support Windows paths (`fileURLToPath` for url paths, `Path`/`PATH` case-insensitivity, and `.cmd` shims instead of shell scripts).

7. **Concurrency Documentation & Bundling**:
   - Updated `docs/architecture/serve-sync-concurrency.md` with Postgres parallel sync, connection budget clamping (`GBRAIN_MAX_CONNECTIONS`), and queue job concurrency configurations.
   - Regenerated `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` documentation bundles via `bun run build:llms`.

## Verification Results

All verification suites pass successfully under Node/Bun PGLite runtime on Windows:
- `page-generation-counter.test.ts` (11/11 Passed)
- `op-checkpoint.test.ts` (27/27 Passed)
- `sync-resumable-import.serial.test.ts` (13/13 Passed)
- `check-resolvable.ts` (51/51 Skills Reachable)

title: extract --by-mention checkpoint write fails CHECK constraint (non-fatal, links still inserted)
body:
## Bug

`gbrain extract links --by-mention --source db` logs a non-fatal error on every run:

```
[op-checkpoint] write failed (extract-by-mention, e68c168d): new row for relation "op_checkpoints" violates check constraint "op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array"
```

The extract still completes successfully (links are inserted into `links` table via `addLinksBatch`), but the checkpoint write fails, meaning **the run is not resumable** — a killed mid-run extract would re-scan every page from scratch on the next start.

## Environment

- gbrain: **v0.42.51.0** (commit `9bf96db8`)
- Postgres: 16.x via pgvector
- Schema version: **119** (the migration that added the CHECK constraint)
- Source: `db` mode (entity gazetteer from DB, 85 first-token buckets)
- Pages: 222 in brain at time of run
- Result: 202 links created successfully, 0 timeline entries, 0 duplicates

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /root/gbrain
bun /root/.bun/bin/gbrain.real extract links --by-mention --source db
```

Expected: clean run, no errors, checkpoint persisted to `op_checkpoints`.

Actual: 
- `[extract.by_mention.scan] 222/222 (100%) done` ✓
- `Mentions: created 202 links from 222 pages against gazetteer of 85 first-token buckets` ✓  
- `[op-checkpoint] write failed (extract-by-mention, e68c168d): new row for relation "op_checkpoints" violates check constraint "op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array"` ✗
- No row appears in `op_checkpoints` for that fingerprint

## What I've verified

The constraint itself is correct:

```sql
op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array CHECK ((jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) = 'array'::text))
```

Direct INSERT with `::jsonb` cast and a JSON array literal works:

```sql
INSERT INTO op_checkpoints (op, fingerprint, completed_keys, updated_at)
VALUES ('test', 'e68c168d', '["abc","def","ghi"]'::jsonb, now());
-- INSERT 0 1 ✓
```

Empty arrays work, plain objects and JSON strings are correctly rejected. So the CHECK is doing its job — the failure is on the code side.

## Where it likely originates

`src/commands/extract.ts:1838` calls `recordCompleted(engine, ckptKey, [...completed])` where `completed` is a `Set<string>`. `recordCompleted` (`src/core/op-checkpoint.ts:175-194`) does `JSON.stringify(sorted)` and casts `$3::jsonb`. Code looks correct on inspection, but the constraint violation suggests the parameter is reaching Postgres as a non-array JSONB value.

Possibilities:
1. postgres.js parameter coercion when `executeRawDirect` → `conn.unsafe(sql, params)` receives `JSON.stringify(sorted)` as a JS string — possibly gets double-encoded if postgres.js infers JSON type from string content
2. A different code path through `appendCompleted` (line 217) — though that uses `APPEND_PATHS_SQL` with `'[]'::jsonb` literal, which shouldn't violate
3. Migration v119's CHECK constraint may have been applied to a database that already had non-array rows from earlier writes, and the new INSERT path is somehow tripping over legacy state

## Impact

- **Non-fatal** — links still insert, run still completes
- **Resumability lost** — killed mid-run extracts re-scan everything
- **Noisy logs** — one error per extract run; would mask real checkpoint failures
- **Affected ops** — any extract-* that uses checkpoint persistence: `extract-by-mention`, possibly `extract-all` / `extract-timeline`

## Suggested next steps

1. Add a debug log of the exact `$3` value being passed to postgres.js, just before the INSERT in `recordCompleted` 
2. Verify against a fresh DB (no pre-v119 rows) to rule out migration drift
3. Consider relaxing the constraint to accept either array or empty string, OR explicitly wrapping the INSERT in a try-cast to surface the exact value that's failing

## Workaround (works around the noisy log, NOT the resume bug)

The non-fatal nature means it's safe to ignore for now. Links still land. But a kill mid-run loses all progress since the last persist.

title: feat(embed): self-hosted TEI support — Jina recipe, per-text truncation, concurrent dispatch
body:
## Problem

Pointing gbrain's embedding pipeline at a self-hosted [text-embeddings-inference](https://github.com/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference) (TEI) server surfaces three gaps. TEI enforces a fixed per-request token budget and is typically run as N replicas behind a load balancer:

1. **No recipe for it.** The `openai-compatible` recipes that *could* point at TEI (ollama, llama-server) declare `no_batch_cap`, so the token-split path never engages — a page's chunks are sent as one over-budget request and the server hangs until the client timeout fires.
2. **Per-text truncation is too coarse.** `embed()` caps each text to a flat `MAX_CHARS` (8000) before `splitByTokenBudget()`. A single chunk larger than the recipe's per-request budget lands in a sub-batch of 1 and *still* exceeds the limit — splitting can't help at the individual-text level. **This affects any recipe with `max_batch_tokens` (Voyage, ZeroEntropy), not just self-hosted TEI.**
3. **Sequential dispatch wastes replicas.** Multi-batch `embed()` calls dispatch sub-batches strictly one-at-a-time, so a single replica works while the rest sit idle.

## Fix

### 1. Jina Embeddings recipe (`src/core/ai/recipes/jina.ts`)

A new `openai-compatible` recipe for self-hosted TEI, declaring `max_batch_tokens: 2048`, `chars_per_token: 1`, `safety_factor: 0.5` (sized for `jina-v2-base-code` ONNX). `user_provided_models` lets the gateway accept any `jina:<id>` the server was launched with. `JINA_BASE_URL` threads into the gateway `base_urls`, mirroring `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` / `LLAMA_SERVER_BASE_URL`.

### 2. Per-text truncation from the recipe token budget (`gateway.ts`)

When a recipe declares `max_batch_tokens`, each text is now capped to `min(MAX_CHARS, floor(max_batch_tokens × safety_factor × chars_per_token))` chars before splitting — the same formula the pre-split budget already uses, extended one level down to the individual text. This is a **latent correctness fix** that benefits Voyage/ZeroEntropy too: an oversized single chunk previously hung the provider regardless of recipe.

### 3. Concurrent sub-batch dispatch via `embed.http_concurrency`

Sub-batches now dispatch through `Promise.all` bounded by a process-global FIFO semaphore; **output order is preserved** via indexed slots. The limit comes from the `embed.http_concurrency` brain-config key (**default 1 = prior sequential behaviour**, so no change on upgrade), overridable at incident time by `GBRAIN_EMBED_HTTP_CONCURRENCY`. Single-batch calls skip the semaphore (fast path).

Measured against a self-hosted TEI deployment (6 replicas, `jina-v2-base-code`): a ~37k-chunk corpus embedded in ~20 min at `http_concurrency=48` vs ~10h sequentially, with all replicas saturated instead of one.

## Safety

- **Default behaviour is unchanged.** `embed.http_concurrency` defaults to 1 (sequential); the per-text cap only tightens for recipes that already declare `max_batch_tokens`; OpenAI's fast path (no budget) is untouched.
- **Output order preserved** under concurrent dispatch (indexed `Promise.all`, verified by test).
- **No new env-var surface beyond one documented override.** Concurrency is a config key first; `GBRAIN_EMBED_HTTP_CONCURRENCY` is an incident-time escape hatch.

## Tests

32 cases in `test/ai/adaptive-embed-batch.test.ts`:
- Recipe-driven pre-splitting (split when over budget, batch together when under, order preservation)
- Per-text truncation (Jina recipe truncates to budget; fast-path recipes pass texts through untouched)
- Concurrent dispatch (semaphore bounds in-flight calls; `concurrency=1` stays sequential)

`bun run typecheck` clean.

title: fix(cli): route `gbrain capture` through put_page on thin-client installs
body:
## Summary

On a **thin-client install** (config has `remote_mcp`, no local `database_url`), `gbrain capture "..."` errors out:

```
No database URL: database_url is missing from config.
Fix: Run gbrain init --supabase or gbrain init --url
```

…even though `gbrain put`, `gbrain whoami`, and `gbrain search` all route remote correctly on the **exact same config**. Only `capture` breaks.

This violates the documented contract (README + CHANGELOG):

> thin-client installs route through `callRemoteTool('put_page', ...)`. Same UX both ways.

## Reproduce

```bash
gbrain init --mcp-only \
  --issuer-url <url> --mcp-url <url>/mcp \
  --oauth-client-id <id> --oauth-client-secret <secret>
# creates a config with remote_mcp and NO database_url

gbrain capture "test"
# → No database URL: database_url is missing from config. ...
```

`gbrain put inbox/x` on the same config routes remote correctly (it only fails on *reaching* the server), proving the issue is specific to `capture`.

## Root cause

`capture` is a **`CLI_ONLY`** command, so it is dispatched through `handleCliOnly()` rather than the shared-op routing seam in `main()` that sends non-`localOnly` ops through `runThinClientRouted` on thin-client installs.

`handleCliOnly` already has thin-client bypasses for `status` and `eval whoknows` (both pass `engine=null` and return before connecting) — but **not for `capture`**. So `capture` falls through to the unconditional `connectEngine()`, which throws `No database URL` from `src/core/db.ts` **before** capture's own thin-client branch (`callRemoteTool('put_page', ...)`) can ever run.

`src/commands/capture.ts` was already correct: `runCapture` accepts `engine=null` and guards every local-engine use behind `isThinClient(cfg)` (the source resolver at ~L426, the `put_page`-op fallback at ~L506). The only thing missing was the **dispatch-time bypass** so the local engine is never opened on a thin-client.

`put` / `whoami` / `search` work because they are registered ops (not `CLI_ONLY`) and hit the `main()` routing seam.

## Fix

Add a thin-client bypass for `capture` in `handleCliOnly`, mirroring the existing `status` / `eval whoknows` guards:

```ts
if (command === 'capture') {
  const cfgPre = loadConfig();
  if (isThinClient(cfgPre)) {
    const { runCapture } = await import('./commands/capture.ts');
    await runCapture(null, args);
    return;
  }
}
```

`capture` is intentionally **not** added to `THIN_CLIENT_REFUSED_COMMANDS` because it *can* run remotely (the server exposes `put_page`).

## Test

Adds a regression test to `test/cli-dispatch-thin-client.test.ts` that seeds a thin-client config, spawns `gbrain capture`, and asserts it never emits `No database URL` and instead surfaces the remote `put_page` path. The `"remote put_page failed:"` prefix is unique to capture's thin-client `catch` and cannot appear on the local-engine path, so it is precise proof of remote routing. Watched it fail before the fix (RED) and pass after (GREEN).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `bun run verify` (30 checks) — all green
- `bun test` on `cli-dispatch-thin-client`, `thin-client-routing-audit`, `capture-runcapture`, `commands/capture`, `ingestion/ingest-capture` — **97 pass, 0 fail**

## Notes

- **Local installs are unchanged**: the bypass is gated on `isThinClient(cfg)`, so local-engine capture takes the existing path untouched.
- `src/commands/capture.ts` is unchanged from v0.42.36 through current master, so this bug is present on master too.

title: book-mirror: emit HTML <table valign=top> instead of markdown pipe tables
body:
Markdown pipe tables have no vertical-align control, so every renderer except GitHub middle-aligns rows — unreadable when the two columns differ in length (the common case for a Chapter/Mirror layout).

This switches the per-chapter subagent prompt and the frontmatter tag to the HTML `<table>` form with `valign="top"` on every cell, matching the hand-built mirror pages that already render correctly everywhere (GitHub, PDF, Obsidian).

No logic change to fan-out, assembly, or trust contract — prompt + tag only.

title: ollama recipe: validator rejects modern embed model dims AND models list is missing qwen3-embed-8b / snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2
body:
**What happened?**

Two coupled gaps in the Ollama recipe block operators who want to run modern Ollama embedding models:

1. **The validator rejects every dim that isn't `default_dims`.** `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:mxbai-embed-large --embedding-dimensions 1024` fails preflight with `Provider "ollama" model "mxbai-embed-large" does not support custom dimensions 1024 (this model only emits its default vector size).` Misleading: the local Ollama backend was perfectly happy to emit 1024d (mxbai's native size). The recipe declares `default_dims: 768` (nomic-embed-text) and gates every other model against it. Same hole for `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` (1024d) and Qwen3-Embedding (0.6B/4B/8B → 1024/2560/4096 native). The `llama-server` and `litellm-proxy` recipes are in the same bucket: they declare `user_provided_models: true`, but Tier 3 of `isCustomDimValidForProvider` still rejects whatever dim the user picks.
2. **The recipe's models list is missing the modern embedding models.** Even with the validator relaxed, `qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` are absent from the registered list, so the resolver doesn't recognize them as known-Ollama models. Operators today have to either set `models.tier.embed ollama:<exotic-model>` explicitly (bypassing the recognized-list check) or `ollama pull` and pray the validator doesn't refuse.

**What did you expect?**

The Ollama recipe accepts the modern embedding models at their native dims with no operator-side workaround:

- `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:qwen3-embed-8b --embedding-dimensions 4096` works.
- `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2 --embedding-dimensions 1024` works.
- `gbrain models | grep ollama` lists both as recognized Ollama embedding models.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Pull a non-nomic embedding model: `ollama pull mxbai-embed-large` (or `qwen3-embed-8b`, or `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2`).
2. `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:mxbai-embed-large --embedding-dimensions 1024` → preflight rejects with the misleading "does not support custom dimensions" message.
3. `gbrain models | grep qwen3-embed-8b` → no row (the model isn't in the recipe's known list).

Observed on gbrain 0.42.40.0+.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.40.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 + PGLite both reproduce.

**Proposed fix**

Two coupled changes, both in the AI recipe surface:

1. Recognize passthrough recipes at validation time. The validator in `src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts` adds a "passthrough" tier between the provider-specific Matryoshka allow-lists and the final fallback. Detection: `recipe.id === 'ollama'` OR `recipe.touchpoints.embedding?.user_provided_models === true` (covers llama-server, litellm-proxy, and any future bring-your-own-backend recipe). Local-backend recipes have no business gating dims when the local model decides for itself; the only sensible upper bound is the `PGVECTOR_COLUMN_MAX_DIMS` cap pgvector itself enforces (already enforced upstream of this function).
2. Register `qwen3-embed-8b` and `snowflake/arctic-embed-l-v2` in the Ollama recipe's models list so the resolver and `gbrain models` surface recognize them as known Ollama models.

The validator relaxation alone closes the immediate rejection; the model registrations close the discovery gap. Together the operator can `ollama pull <modern-model>` and run gbrain against it without any source-edit workaround.

Paired PR: [#2155](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2155) (existing, OPEN, currently 1 commit; will grow to 2 commits with the model registrations).

title: Add Semgrep CE SAST workflow for TypeScript security checks
body:
## Improvement opportunity

Add a Semgrep CE static-analysis workflow for the TypeScript/JavaScript codebase.

## Evidence inspected

Repo-local evidence:

- `package.json` declares a TypeScript CLI/server package with runtime HTTP/auth/storage dependencies such as `express`, `cookie-parser`, `cors`, `express-rate-limit`, `openai`, `postgres`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, and MCP/AI SDK packages.
- `src/mcp/server.ts` exposes agent-facing MCP tools and explicitly dispatches stdio MCP callers with `remote: true`.
- `src/core/operations.ts` documents security-sensitive path validation for upload operations, including strict behavior for untrusted remote callers.
- `src/commands/files.ts` contains file upload, mirror, restore, and signed-url command surfaces.
- Existing CI/security posture is strong in adjacent areas but does not include SAST/code scanning:
  - `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs Gitleaks and the repo's verify/test jobs.
  - `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `docs/TESTING.md` document gitleaks, guard scripts, typecheck, unit tests, E2E, and local CI gates.
  - grep over workflows/docs/source found no `semgrep`, `CodeQL`, `SAST`, or generic static-analysis workflow.

Current external baseline:

- Semgrep CE can run open-source static application security testing in CI with `semgrep scan`, including TypeScript/JavaScript rules and SARIF/code-scanning output.

## Expected impact

GBrain has a meaningful security-sensitive surface: local CLI commands, remote/agent-facing MCP dispatch, OAuth/token handling, filesystem upload/mirror operations, and SQL-backed engines. A Semgrep CE workflow would add a second class of automated security signal beyond secret scanning, catching common TypeScript/JavaScript issues before merge without waiting for a manual review to notice a risky pattern.

This is not a replacement for the existing hand-written guards. It is a cheap broad net for known bug classes.

## Suggested fix

Keep the first rollout low-noise and maintainable:

1. Add a dedicated `.github/workflows/semgrep.yml` triggered on:
   - `pull_request` when `src/**`, `scripts/**`, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, or `.github/workflows/semgrep.yml` changes
   - `workflow_dispatch`
   - optionally a weekly `schedule`
2. Run Semgrep CE with TypeScript/JavaScript/security rules, for example:
   - `semgrep scan --config p/typescript --config p/javascript --config p/security-audit --sarif --output semgrep.sarif`
3. Upload SARIF to GitHub Code Scanning if maintainers want the results in the Security tab. Use least-privilege permissions:
   - `contents: read`
   - `security-events: write`
4. Start as advisory if the first run is noisy. Tighten to a required check only after baseline findings are triaged or ignored in a repo-owned config.
5. Add a short note to `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `docs/TESTING.md` once the workflow is stable so contributors know whether Semgrep is advisory or blocking.

## Duplicate check

I inspected the required open backlog and exact candidate terms before filing:

- `gh issue list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,url,labels,createdAt,updatedAt,author`
  - 200 open issues inspected.
- `gh pr list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,url,headRefName,baseRefName,author,createdAt,updatedAt,isDraft`
  - 200 open PRs inspected.
- Exact open issue/PR searches:
  - `semgrep`
  - `SAST`
  - `CodeQL`
  - `static analysis`
  - `code scanning`

Result: no open issue or PR found for adding Semgrep/SAST/code-scanning CI. The nearby open security issues I saw were different scopes: #2182 covers OSV dependency scanning, and #2142 covers release artifact attestations.

## Commands/files inspected

- `README.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `docs/TESTING.md`
- `docs/guides/skill-development.md`
- `examples/skillpack-reference/README.md`
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/tier5-queries.md`
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`
- `.github/workflows/heavy-tests.yml`
- `package.json`
- `src/mcp/server.ts`
- `src/core/operations.ts`
- `src/commands/files.ts`
- `gh pr list --repo garrytan/gbrain --state merged --limit 20 --json number,title,url,mergedAt,author`
- `gh pr view 2254 --repo garrytan/gbrain --json number,title,body,files,mergedAt,url`
- `gh pr view 2243 --repo garrytan/gbrain --json number,title,body,files,mergedAt,url`
- `grep/search over .github, docs, source, and package metadata for semgrep/codeql/sast/static-analysis terms`

title: gateway-loop subagent path never persists tool-result user turns — every resume rebuilds an unbalanced conversation that next chat() rejects
body:
**What happened?**

Any subagent job that takes the gateway-loop path (`agent.use_gateway_loop = true`, the path every non-Anthropic recipe uses) dies deterministically on the next `chat()` dispatch after ANY mid-conversation interruption with:

```text
[chat(litellm:gpt-X.Y)] Tool results are missing for tool calls call_<id>, call_<id>, ...
```

The failure scales with parallel-tool-call count (gpt-5.5 dropped 10 ids per dispatch in production, gpt-5.4 dropped 6, gpt-5.4-mini dropped 2), which initially reads as a provider-side bridge bug. It is not. The missing-tool-results error comes from the NEXT `chat()` dispatch operating on a stale in-memory message array, not from the wire response of the prior call.

**Diagnosis**

`gateway.toolLoop` builds the tool-result user turn in memory after the tool executions settle, then throws the index away. `runSubagentViaGateway` wires no callback to persist that turn. On any interruption (worker recycle, rate-lease renewal, RSS watchdog, abort, even a clean shutdown), replay rebuilds the conversation from `subagent_messages` without the tool-result row, an unbalanced shape with assistant `tool_call` turns and no matching `tool` user turns.

Unlike the legacy Anthropic-direct path (which reconciles the turn on replay), the gateway-loop path has no reconciliation. The next `chat()` dispatch hits the provider's validator with the unbalanced shape and the provider returns the "Tool results are missing for tool calls ..." error, which the worker treats as a hard failure, retries the same unbalanced shape, and dead-letters the job.

The existing crash-replay test suite missed this because it stubs the chat transport, so the real provider validator never runs and message balance went unasserted.

**What did you expect?**

The gateway-loop path should persist the synthesized tool-result user turn before the next dispatch, matching what the legacy Anthropic-direct path already does. On replay, it should reconcile the missing turn from the settled `subagent_tool_executions` rows (the tool outputs were persisted; only the wrapping user turn was lost).

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Brain configured for any non-Anthropic chat provider (litellm-proxy, codex-proxy, ollama, openrouter, openai directly, …). Set `agent.use_gateway_loop = true`.
2. Submit any subagent job whose dispatch fires parallel tool calls (`gbrain dream --phase patterns` is the deterministic local trigger; any subagent that calls a tool reproduces).
3. Interrupt mid-conversation: kill the worker, force a rate-lease renewal, or let the RSS watchdog recycle the process.
4. The worker re-claims the job and replays. Replay rebuilds the conversation from persisted rows.
5. The next `chat()` throws `Tool results are missing for tool calls call_<id>, ...`. The worker retries; same error; job dead-letters.

Observed on gbrain 0.42.43.0 through 0.42.51.0 under codex-proxy / litellm-proxy. Reproduces on every non-Anthropic chat recipe when `agent.use_gateway_loop = true`.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.43.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 + PGLite both reproduce.

**Proposed fix**

Two pieces, mirroring what the legacy Anthropic path already does:

1. `gateway.toolLoop` gains an `onToolResultTurn` callback fired when the tool-result user turn is built, so the caller can persist the turn before the next dispatch.
2. `runSubagentViaGateway` wires the callback to persist the turn AND adds reconciliation on replay: when prior messages end with unanswered tool-calls, re-synthesize the tool-result turn from the settled `subagent_tool_executions` rows. Bail if any tool is still unsettled so a non-idempotent tool is never re-run.

Regression test: a new `test/e2e/subagent-gateway-toolresult-replay.test.ts` that captures the real transport input and asserts the resumed conversation is balanced. Fails without the change; passes with it.

Paired PR: #2274.

title: Incremental git sync stalls every cycle on a migrated DB: op_checkpoints check constraint rejects checkpoint write (completed_keys not an array)
body:
## Summary

On a brain whose Postgres engine was seeded by migrating an older dump forward (`apply-migrations` up to schema v119), the autopilot **sync** phase fails on every cycle. `git pull` succeeds, but writing the sync checkpoint is rejected by the `op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array` CHECK constraint, so the cycle aborts before import and `last_commit` never advances. Incremental git→DB sync is permanently stalled (the rest of the dream cycle runs fine).

## Environment

- gbrain `0.42.51.0` (installed via `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain`)
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector 0.8.3, engine = Postgres
- The DB was seeded by `pg_dump` of an existing `0.40.8.0` brain, restored into a fresh Postgres database, then `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` (ran cleanly through to v119).
- After migration, `op_checkpoints` and `op_checkpoint_paths` are both **empty (0 rows)**.

## Symptom (every autopilot cycle, from `autopilot.err`)

```
[cycle.sync] resolve_repo -> load_active_pack -> detect_head -> git_pull done (~4.9s)
[op-checkpoint] write failed (sync-target, <id>): new row for relation "op_checkpoints"
  violates check constraint "op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array"
[sync] checkpoint target write failed (pool unavailable) -- aborting before import; nothing drained, next run retries.
banked 0 file(s); last_commit unchanged at <commit>
```

The constraint is:

```sql
CHECK (jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) = 'array')
```

The checkpoint writer appears to insert a non-array value (null or object) for `completed_keys` when creating the **first** checkpoint row, so the insert is rejected. Because `op_checkpoints` starts empty on a freshly migrated DB, this fails on the very first sync and never recovers. A manual `gbrain sync` hits the same constraint.

## Impact

- Incremental git sync never advances; new commits to the brain repo are never auto-imported.
- Workaround that works: `gbrain import <repo-dir>` (directory ingest) is unaffected, so the brain can be kept current manually.

## Repro (likely)

Any brain on a Postgres DB where `op_checkpoints` is empty when the first `sync` runs — e.g. a DB seeded by dump/restore + `apply-migrations` rather than `gbrain init` + incremental sync from the start.

## Likely fix

Ensure the sync checkpoint writer always passes an array for `completed_keys` (default to `[]` on first write) before the insert, so it satisfies `op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array`.

title: feat(ai): claude-cli recipe for native gateway-based subagent dispatch — Claude Max subscription without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
body:
Related: [#334](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/334) (jarvisdoes proposed an env-var-gated `MessagesClient` adapter for the same need). This issue describes the same end-user need framed as a recipe so the gateway-loop dispatch path handles claude-cli the same way it handles every other non-Anthropic recipe.

**What problem does this solve?**

Operators with a Claude Max subscription want subagent dispatch to run against their existing OAuth session via the `claude` CLI binary, not against a separate per-token `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` billing relationship. Today:

- `agent.use_gateway_loop = true` is the production path for every non-Anthropic recipe.
- There is no claude-cli recipe in the registry, so `models.tier.subagent = claude:claude-sonnet-4-6` (or any CLI-routed alias) has no dispatch path.
- The original proposal in #334 was a `GBRAIN_USE_CLAUDE_CLI=1` env var injecting a custom `MessagesClient` adapter at jobs.ts worker startup. That adapter only runs on the legacy Anthropic-direct path; under the gateway-loop path it never fires.

**What does the solution look like?**

A native `claude-cli` recipe in `src/core/ai/recipes/` so dispatch goes through the same `gateway.toolLoop()` path every other recipe uses. The recipe:

- Declares `tier: 'native'`, chat-only (no embedding / no expansion).
- Spawns the local `claude` binary with `--print --output-format json --model <X> --disable-slash-commands --system-prompt <gbrain prompt>` from a dedicated tmpdir (skips local `CLAUDE.md` auto-discovery).
- Parses the JSON envelope and extracts `<use_tools>` blocks back into native ai-sdk `tool-call` content parts. Parallel tool calls in one block round-trip cleanly.
- Reports `auth_env.required: []` because the CLI owns auth via its own OAuth session.

Per-call routing then works the same way every other recipe does: `models.dream.patterns = claude-cli:claude-sonnet-4-6` routes through the recipe; `models.tier.subagent = litellm:gpt-5.4` continues through litellm-proxy in the same worker. No env-var switch, no global flag.

**Alternatives considered**

1. **Env-var-gated MessagesClient adapter (the #334 proposal).** Works only on the legacy Anthropic-direct path. Under the gateway-loop path (the production default for every non-Anthropic recipe), the adapter never runs because dispatch flows through `gateway.toolLoop()` not `client.create()` at `subagent.ts:506`. Per-call routing via a proper recipe is the architecture that extends correctly into gateway-loop world.
2. **Anthropic-direct adapter wrapping the `claude` binary.** Same blocker as #1: wrong dispatch path.
3. **Subscriber-only forwarder service (a small local HTTP proxy that authenticates with Claude Max and exposes an OpenAI-shaped API).** Possible but introduces an external service the user has to keep running. The recipe path keeps everything in-process.

**Context isolation knobs**

The recipe spawns from a clean tmpdir + `--disable-slash-commands` + `--system-prompt`, which is the maximum suppression preserving OAuth/Max-subscription auth. `--bare` would also strip `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` but forces `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth, defeating the whole point. The ~42K cached tokens from user-level instructions stay as an unavoidable trade-off on the subscription path.

title: dream patterns phase skips with no_api_key on non-Anthropic stacks even though the subagent submission below routes through the gateway
body:
**What happened?**

`gbrain dream --phase patterns` short-circuits with `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'no_api_key', summary: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset; pattern detection skipped' }` on any non-Anthropic-routed stack (litellm-proxy / codex-proxy / ollama / openrouter / any openai-compatible deployment), even though the subagent submission immediately below the gate dispatches via the gateway model-tier resolver which already handles non-Anthropic providers correctly.

The gate is `src/core/cycle/patterns.ts:67-69`:

```ts
if (!process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) {
  return skipped('no_api_key', 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset; pattern detection skipped');
}
```

The sibling synthesize phase already removed its equivalent gate. The `makeJudgeClient` docstring at `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts:804` documents the rationale: "preserves the legacy 'no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' cheap-skip semantics" while delegating real auth probing to the gateway recipe's `auth_env.required` machinery, with `AIConfigError` at `gateway.chat()` time caught and surfaced per-call. Patterns carries a similar literal env-var check in its body that never got updated.

**What did you expect?**

`gbrain dream --phase patterns` should dispatch through whatever gateway recipe `models.dream.patterns` (or the applicable tier default) resolves to, exactly as synthesize does. When the gateway IS misconfigured, dispatch should surface a clear `AIConfigError` per-call rather than a silent `skipped: no_api_key` verdict that misclassifies the failure shape.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Fresh brain with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env, paid traffic routed through codex-proxy / litellm / claude-cli / any non-Anthropic recipe.
2. `gbrain config set models.dream.patterns litellm:gpt-5.4` (or any non-`anthropic:*` model).
3. `gbrain dream --phase patterns --json`.
4. Expected: subagent dispatches via the gateway and returns pattern detections, or surfaces `AIConfigError` if the gateway is misconfigured.
5. Actual: `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'no_api_key', summary: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset; pattern detection skipped' }` regardless of the resolved tier.

Observed on gbrain 0.42.44.0 through 0.42.51.0.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.44.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 + PGLite both reproduce.

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**

Not material to the bug. `doctor` reports a healthy brain; the gate fires inside `cycle/patterns.ts` before any dispatch and never reaches the recipe layer.

**Proposed fix**

Drop the gate. The subagent submission immediately below the gate uses the same gateway routing that synthesize already proves works on non-Anthropic stacks. Five-line diff in one file.

title: sync aborts on every change: writeCompleted double-encodes op_checkpoints.completed_keys → violates the v0.42.51 migration-119 array CHECK
body:
## Summary

On v0.42.51.0, **every `gbrain sync` that has changes to drain aborts** before importing, and so does the `dream --phase sync` cron path. The resumable-sync `sync-target` checkpoint write stores `completed_keys` as a JSONB **string scalar**, which the same release's migration 119 (`op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array`, `CHECK (jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) = 'array')`) rejects.

put_page-based ingestion is unaffected (DB-first); only git-file → DB reconciliation breaks, so file changes silently stop syncing.

## Symptom

```
[op-checkpoint] write failed (sync-target, <fp>): new row for relation "op_checkpoints"
  violates check constraint "op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array"
[sync] checkpoint target write failed (pool unavailable) — aborting before import; nothing drained
  ✓ sync   +N added, ~M modified  ← reported delta, but banked 0, last_commit unchanged
```

## Root cause

`writeCompleted()` in `src/core/op-checkpoint.ts` binds `completed_keys` via `$3::jsonb` with `JSON.stringify(sorted)`. In the postgres path this double-encodes into a JSON string scalar (`jsonb_typeof = 'string'`), not an array. The sibling `appendCompleted()` (used by op `'sync'`) avoids this by binding a native `text[]` — which is why only the `sync-target` write (op `'sync'` uses `'[]'::jsonb` literal) fails.

Reproduced on PostgreSQL: a proper array literal → `jsonb_typeof = 'array'`; a stringified-then-bound value → `'string'` (violates the CHECK). The migration-119 comment states "No current writer can produce a scalar" — but `writeCompleted` does.

## Proposed fix

Bind as `text[]` → `to_jsonb()`, mirroring `appendCompleted`:

```diff
   return durableWrite(engine, key, 'write', () =>
     engine.executeRawDirect(
       `INSERT INTO op_checkpoints (op, fingerprint, completed_keys, updated_at)
-       VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, now())
+       VALUES ($1, $2, to_jsonb($3::text[]), now())
        ON CONFLICT (op, fingerprint) DO UPDATE
-         SET completed_keys = EXCLUDED.completed_keys,
+         SET completed_keys = to_jsonb($3::text[]),
              updated_at     = now()`,
-      [key.op, key.fingerprint, JSON.stringify(sorted)],
+      [key.op, key.fingerprint, sorted],
     ));
```

Verified: with this patch, `sync` drains and applies changes cleanly (rename/delete detection intact, no dead links) and the cron path runs to completion.

Version: v0.42.51.0 (commit 9bf96db8). Engine: postgres.

title: gbrain jobs prune cannot clear same-day terminal jobs (--older-than 0d rejected; no --status filter)
body:
**What happened?**

`gbrain jobs prune` has two gaps that combine to block mid-loop dead-job recovery during a backfill:

1. `--older-than 0d` is rejected. The flag accepts only positive day counts. A backfill loop that hit a non-zero subagent failure rate (the typical ~3-15% on gpt-5.5 via codex-proxy) leaves dead jobs from the SAME day whose `idempotency_key`s block re-submission of the same transcript on the next pass; the operator can only prune yesterday's and older.
2. There is no `--status` filter. Prune treats all terminal states (`cancelled` / `dead` / `failed` / `completed`) the same. The operator wants to drop only the dead/failed rows from the current day; pruning the completed rows too loses the audit trail of what successfully shipped.

Together: between days of a backfill loop, the operator wants to drop ONLY the dead jobs of the current day. Today's prune surface offers neither knob.

**What did you expect?**

`gbrain jobs prune --older-than 0d --status dead --status failed` should drop today's dead/failed jobs and nothing else, freeing the matching `idempotency_key` rows so the next pass can re-submit the same transcript without renaming it.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Submit a batch of subagent jobs via `gbrain dream --phase synthesize` (or any backfill loop).
2. Let some fail (any source of non-zero failure rate; codex-proxy + gpt-5.5 is the deterministic local repro).
3. `gbrain jobs prune --older-than 0d` → exit non-zero, error: only positive day counts accepted.
4. `gbrain jobs prune --older-than 1d` → drops only yesterday's jobs (none, since this is the first day of the loop).
5. The dead rows from step 2 stay in `minion_jobs` with their `idempotency_key`s held, blocking re-submission.

Observed on gbrain 0.42.43.0.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.43.0+ (current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 + PGLite both reproduce.

**Proposed fix**

1. Parse `--older-than 0d` as "today" (drops jobs with `terminated_at >= start-of-today UTC`).
2. Add `--status <state>` (repeatable), accepting the same enum the queue uses (`cancelled` / `dead` / `failed` / `completed`). When omitted, current behavior is preserved (prune all terminal states older than the cutoff).
3. When both flags are set, the filter is AND: rows older than the cutoff AND matching one of the named statuses.

The combined surface lets the operator run `gbrain jobs prune --older-than 0d --status dead --status failed` between backfill passes and free idempotency keys without dropping the success audit trail.

Single-file change in `src/commands/jobs.ts` plus the underlying prune query in the engine. Both engines update in lockstep per the engine-parity invariant.

title: dream synthesize backfill loop drops configured zeros, bigint job ids, deterministic frontmatter, and operator visibility on long runs
body:
**What happened?**

Four failure modes in `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts` surface together during long-running operator-driven backfills (`gbrain dream --phase synthesize --from <day> --to <day>` repeated across many days). Each is a different bug class, but they cluster on the same wait-loop + dual-write path and reproduce together once the loop runs long enough to hit any of them. None reproduces in a short run.

1. **Configured `cooldown_hours = 0` is silently coerced to the 12h default.** The reader uses `parseInt(str, 10) || DEFAULT` for `cooldown_hours` and `min_chars`; `parseInt('0', 10) || 12` evaluates as `0 || 12 = 12` because `0` is falsy. A backfill loop that wants every-cycle synthesis (no cooldown) can't actually disable it. `gbrain config get dream.synthesize.cooldown_hours` returns `0` but the phase still reports `12h cooldown` and skips re-runs accordingly.
2. **Subagent job ids silently mis-look-up in `childMeta`.** postgres-js returns `INT8` as a JS `bigint` by default. The orchestrator builds `childMeta` as `Map<number, ChildMeta>` keyed off `child.id` (a JS `number`); reverse-write reads `subagent_tool_executions.job_id` (bigint) and calls `childMeta.get(jobId)`. `Map.get` uses SameValueZero equality and `2719n !== 2719`, so the lookup silently returns `undefined`; deterministic frontmatter overrides default to `{}`; `buildDeterministicFrontmatter(meta, cycleDate)` is never reached. No error, no warning. Every dual-written page lands with truncated frontmatter (only the unconditional fallbacks `dream_generated` and `dream_cycle_date` survive).
3. **The orchestrator doesn't own deterministic frontmatter on dual-write.** Subagents own their full output frontmatter today including fields the operator wants the orchestrator to stamp authoritatively (`transcript_id`, `transcript_source`, `effective_date`, `date`, `chunk`, `dream_cycle_date`). Subagent drift (typos, omissions, model-side reformatting) leaks into the persisted row and the disk markdown. The orchestrator already has the right values; it just doesn't merge them.
4. **The operator can't see live progress between phase boundaries.** `gbrain dream` runs silently while the synthesize wait loop polls the queue and only logs on state transitions. With `--json` the stdout pipe is silent (envelope only at completion); operators have no way to see "the orchestrator is still working through 47 children" without opening the DB.

**What did you expect?**

Each failure mode has an obvious correct shape:

1. A configured `0` should mean `0`, not be silently replaced with the default. Operators who set the value explicitly to disable a behavior should get that behavior disabled.
2. The bigint-to-number boundary should be defensively coerced at consumer sites so `Map<number, V>` lookups succeed.
3. The orchestrator should re-stamp the deterministic fields after each subagent's `put_page`, so subagent drift can't leak.
4. The orchestrator should emit verbose stderr heartbeats (e.g. `[dream:sync] N children pending, M active, K completed`) every ~20s during the wait, so a tmux pane running `gbrain dream --phase synthesize ... --json > /tmp/log` shows live progress via stderr while stdout stays clean for the JSON consumer.

**Steps to reproduce**

The cluster reproduces during any operator-driven multi-day backfill loop. A short one-day run does not surface issues 2 and 3 because the deterministic frontmatter looks "good enough" from default fallbacks; it takes a few days before the operator notices that `transcript_id` / `effective_date` are missing on every persisted page.

For each failure mode individually:

1. `gbrain config set dream.synthesize.cooldown_hours 0` → run synthesize twice on the same day → second run says "12h cooldown not elapsed" and skips.
2. After any synthesize run with subagents, query the DB for the persisted pages → every page is missing `transcript_id`, `transcript_source`, `effective_date`, `chunk`. Confirmed by adding a `console.log` at the `childMeta.get(jobId)` site: always returns `undefined`.
3. (same root → same observed symptom as issue 2; the orchestrator-frontmatter fix subsumes the bigint fix in practice, but each is required because either alone leaves a different gap.)
4. Run `gbrain dream --phase synthesize --json > /tmp/log` in a tmux pane → stderr is silent for the entire wait period, sometimes 10+ minutes; operator has no signal whether the orchestrator is alive or stuck.

Observed on gbrain 0.42.43.0 through 0.42.51.0.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.43.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 (the bigint mis-lookup is Postgres-specific; PGLite returns numbers for INT8 by default).

**Proposed fix**

Four behavior fixes in `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts` plus one structural prereq in `src/core/cycle/transcript-discovery.ts`:

1. Replace the falsy-OR config-default pattern with an explicit `Number.isFinite` check via an IIFE for `cooldown_hours` and the adjacent `min_chars` reader.
2. Coerce `jobId` to `Number` at every `childMeta.get()` site (three call sites: `reverseWriteRefs`, `collectChildPutPageSlugs`, the slug-map re-insert).
3. After each subagent's `put_page` lands its row, the orchestrator re-renders the row to disk markdown via `reverseWriteRefs` AND merges the deterministic frontmatter into the DB row via `engine.putPage`. Same writes on both sides so disk and DB stay in lockstep. Subagents still own the content-semantic fields (`type`, `title`, `tags`).
4. Emit `[dream:sync] N children pending, M active, K completed` heartbeats to stderr every ~20s during the wait. Coarse enough not to spam; frequent enough that an operator watching the pane sees liveness.
5. Add a `transcriptSource` field to `DiscoveredTranscript`, derived from the grandparent dir name during discovery (validated against a date-bucket convention so non-bucketed corpora don't trip it). Fix 3 stamps this onto the orchestrator-owned frontmatter; without the field-add it has nothing to write. A parallel transcript-metadata PR also ships this commit; duplicate-commit landing is fine, second PR sees it as a no-op.

Coupling: fix 3 depends on fix 2 because without the bigint coercion, the orchestrator's merge silently drops the deterministic fields when the `childMeta` Map lookup misses. Fix 3 also reads fix 5's `transcriptSource` field. The fixes ship together as one PR because they all reproduce together once the loop runs long enough, and the dependency chain is internal to this PR's scope.

title: dream transcript metadata: discovery exposes no source label, date inference fights with content metadata, orchestrator does not own deterministic frontmatter
body:
**What happened?**

Three coupled gaps in how `gbrain dream --phase synthesize` carries transcript metadata from discovery through the dual-write. All three reproduce together on any brain that ingests transcripts from multiple sources or whose file timestamps drift relative to conversation start.

1. **Transcript discovery infers source from the grandparent dir but never exposes it.** A transcript at `~/.gbrain/transcripts/claude-code/2026-06-12/<file>.md` is clearly a claude-code transcript and a transcript at `~/.gbrain/transcripts/voice-notes/2026-06-12/<file>.md` is clearly a voice note, but `DiscoveredTranscript` carries no `transcriptSource` field. Downstream consumers (the orchestrator's deterministic frontmatter merge, any retrieval surface that wants to filter by ingestion pipeline) have no clean way to ask "show me transcripts ingested from claude-code vs from voice notes."
2. **Transcript date inference uses file mtime, which drifts.** Mtime is re-stamped by every sync tool that touches the file (rsync, Dropbox, Syncthing, B2). A transcript whose conversation started 2026-05-15 but whose file was last `mv`d in the morning of 2026-06-17 lands with `effective_date: 2026-06-17`, dropping it into the wrong cycle window. Claude-code transcripts ship a `## Metadata` table with a `| First message | 2026-05-15T03:51:11.584Z |` row that is stable across copies and re-syncs and would give the correct date directly.
3. **The orchestrator does not own deterministic frontmatter on dual-write.** Subagents own their full output frontmatter today, including the fields the operator wants the orchestrator to stamp authoritatively (`transcript_id`, `transcript_source`, `effective_date`, `date`, `chunk`, `dream_cycle_date`). Subagent drift (typos, omissions, model-side reformatting) leaks into the persisted row and the disk markdown. The orchestrator already has the right values; it just doesn't merge them.

**What did you expect?**

A unified metadata pipeline for transcripts:

- `DiscoveredTranscript.transcriptSource` populated from the grandparent dir name during discovery.
- Date inference reads the first-message timestamp from the transcript body when available and falls back to file mtime when absent. Stable across copies and re-syncs.
- The orchestrator merges `transcript_id` / `transcript_source` / `effective_date` / `date` / `chunk` / `dream_cycle_date` onto every dual-written page authoritatively. Subagents still own `type` / `title` / `tags` and the body content.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Ingest two transcripts under different source dirs: `~/.gbrain/transcripts/claude-code/2026-06-12/<a>.md` and `~/.gbrain/transcripts/voice-notes/2026-06-12/<b>.md`.
2. Run `gbrain dream --phase synthesize` against both. Inspect the resulting pages: `transcript_source` is empty on both because discovery never exposed it.
3. Touch the file (`touch ~/.gbrain/transcripts/claude-code/2026-06-12/<a>.md`). Re-run synthesize. The page's `effective_date` is now today, not the original conversation date.
4. Inspect any dual-written page: `transcript_id`, `transcript_source`, `effective_date`, `date`, `chunk` are missing or drift from the orchestrator's computed values.

Observed on gbrain 0.42.43.0 through 0.42.51.0.

**Environment**

- gbrain version: 0.42.43.0+ (reproduces against current `master`).
- OS: Linux + macOS reproduce.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Database: Postgres 16 + PGLite both reproduce.

**Proposed fix**

Three coupled changes, all in `src/core/cycle/transcript-discovery.ts` + `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts`:

1. Add `transcriptSource: string` to `DiscoveredTranscript`. Populate from `basename(dirname(dirname(filePath)))` during discovery so the source label survives into the downstream pipeline.
2. Infer the transcript date by parsing the `## Metadata` `| First message |` row inside the body when present; fall back to file mtime otherwise. Preserve upstream's existing filename-regex hint as an intermediate fallback so brains that name their transcripts by date keep working.
3. After each subagent's `put_page` lands, the orchestrator merges deterministic fields into the DB row via `engine.putPage` AND re-renders the row to disk via `reverseWriteRefs`. Subagents still own content fields; the orchestrator owns metadata.

title: v0.42.52.0 fix(reliability): autopilot dead-job storm + supervisor wedge + sync/status/minion reliability (#2194 #2227 #1994 #1737 #1738 #1950 #1984)
body:
## Summary

One reliability fix wave, scoped from the open `garrytan-agents` issue backlog. It lands the already-reviewed autopilot/supervisor stabilization (previously stranded as an unmerged PR) plus four bounded operational fixes found alongside.

On a multi-source Postgres brain, autopilot could fan out a continuous stream of dead `autopilot-cycle` jobs while the supervisor periodically wedged the very queue it exists to keep alive — one disease with several interacting parts. This addresses all of them, then cleans up four smaller reliability bugs.

## What's in the wave

**Autopilot / supervisor (Closes #2194, #2227, #1994)** — replayed from the reviewed work, commit-for-commit:
- Cycle split: per-source jobs run only source-scoped phases; a single `autopilot-global-maintenance` job runs brain-wide phases once per window — removes the per-cycle memory blow-up that was the shared root cause.
- Per-source filesystem phases bind to the source's own path (freshness stamp and work agree on which source ran).
- Supervisor degrades to capped-backoff retry instead of a permanent stop on a transient DB blip; detects a live sibling supervisor via the queue's DB lock (not a `$HOME`-derived pidfile).
- Per-source failure cooldown (bounded exponential) + per-tick fan-out clamp + a `gbrain doctor` mismatch check.

**Operational fixes:**
- **#1737** — a timed-out minion run now counts as a spent attempt (`handleTimeouts` was the one dead-letter path that didn't increment, so long-lane jobs read `attempts: 0/N`). *(Attempt-accounting half; the queue-starvation half stays a measurement-gated v0.43+ follow-up — see TODOS.)*
- **#1738** (Closes) — `gbrain agent run` no longer swallows a trailing `--detach`/`--follow` into the prompt; a `--word` inside the prompt stays verbatim; `--` ends flag parsing anywhere.
- **#1950** — `gbrain sources status` reports a live sync as running (not "idle") via a shared `liveSyncStatus` helper; a progress-aware stall watchdog aborts a wedged drain and releases its lock so the next sync resumes from the checkpoint (no manual `pkill`). *(In-flight single-file abort is a documented follow-up in TODOS.)*
- **#1984** (Closes) — `gbrain status` gains a `version` field and a `--deadline-ms`/`--fast` per-section budget that returns a partial envelope instead of hanging a poller.

## Pre-landing review

- `/plan-eng-review` (3 deep-review agents + codex outside voice) hardened the design; 4 decisions resolved with the author.
- Ship-stage adversarial pass (codex + a 9-agent diff-review workflow) found **6 real issues in the new code — all fixed before this push**: stall-abort reason now distinct (`stall_timeout`), `--deadline-ms` missing-value is a usage error, thin-client stale-section reporting scoped to requested sections + losing remote call cancelled, and the `--` escape now suppresses hoisting after a positional. Each fix has a regression test.

## Test plan

- Full sharded unit suite on the final code: **pass=14036, fail=0** (the one transient failure was a VERSION/package.json torn read from bumping the version mid-run; re-confirmed green with consistent VERSION — `test/cli.test.ts` 18/18).
- `bun run typecheck` clean. Targeted suites green: #2249 (108), `agent-cli` + `status-sections` (52), `cli` (18), minions `handleTimeouts`.
- No migration added; master's v118/v119 (#2255) preserved. Engine-parity intact (autopilot-cooldown parity test travels with the wave).

title: Fix op checkpoint JSONB array binding
body:
## Summary

Fixes a live Postgres sync failure where `recordCompleted()` wrote `completed_keys` as a JSON string instead of a JSON array through a `postgres.js` `unsafe` placeholder.

In production this surfaced as:

```text
new row for relation "op_checkpoints" violates check constraint "op_checkpoints_completed_keys_array"
```

The database constraint was correct; the writer was double-encoding the value by passing `JSON.stringify(sorted)` to `$3::jsonb`.

## Change

- Pass the JavaScript `string[]` directly to the `$3::jsonb` placeholder.
- Keep the defensive fallback as an empty JavaScript array.
- This preserves the v119 `completed_keys` array-shape guard and lets postgres.js serialize the JSONB value correctly.

## Validation

```text
bun test test/op-checkpoint*.test.ts
37 pass
0 fail
```

Also validated against the production Artie brain after the same fix:

- `gbrain sync --no-pull --no-embed` completed successfully after previously aborting before import.
- `gbrain embed --stale` restored missing embeddings to 0.

title: schema-pack: declare extract_atoms + synthesize_concepts phases on gbrain-base-v2
body:
## Problem

`gbrain-base-v2` declares the `atom` and `concept` page types, but its `phases:` list is empty. Since `extract_atoms` / `synthesize_concepts` are gated on the **active pack's** `phases:`, a base-v2 brain never populates those two types — the taxonomy ships the types but nothing produces them.

The only bundled packs that declare these phases (`gbrain-creator` / `gbrain-everything`) `extend: gbrain-base` (v1), so adopting them means leaving the v2 canonical taxonomy and re-typing the corpus.

## Change

Declare the two phases on `gbrain-base-v2` itself (one additive block). `phases:` is additive — the core phases always run — so this only turns on atom extraction + concept synthesis for base-v2 brains, making the canonical taxonomy self-consistent (the types it ships get populated).

## Verified

On a live base-v2 brain (≈200 pages), `extract_atoms` produced real atoms from the corpus and `synthesize_concepts` ran clean (promotes concepts as atoms accrue across topics/months). I did not run the repo's full test suite locally.

## Open question for you

A user pack that merely `extends: gbrain-base-v2` does **not** inherit v2's types — the extends type-merge appears to skip a standalone bundled parent (base-v2 has `extends: null`). So a thin opt-in `extends`-pack isn't currently a clean alternative, which is why this declares the phases on base-v2 directly.

If you'd rather keep phases **off** base-v2 by default (e.g. to avoid the per-cycle LLM cost for users who only want the taxonomy), I'm happy to instead ship a separate opt-in `gbrain-base-v2-creator` pack + register it — just let me know your preference.

---
_Drafted with Claude Code; verified against a real base-v2 brain._

title: Bug: diagnoseEmbedding() blocks ollama embedding provider
body:
### Problem
When using ollama as embedding provider in gbrain v0.42.51.0, `diagnoseEmbedding()` unconditionally returns `user_provided_model_unset` because the ollama recipe has an empty `models: []` array. The config correctly parses `modelId = "nomic-embed-text"` from `embedding_model: ollama:nomic-embed-text`, but the preflight guard ignores the parsed modelId.

### Reproduction
```bash
export OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://192.168.1.245:11434
gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model ollama:nomic-embed-text
gbrain providers test --model ollama:nomic-embed-text
# → ✗ transient error: Cannot connect to API
```
While direct curl succeeds:
```bash
curl http://192.168.1.245:11434/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"nomic-embed-text","input":"test"}'
# → 200 OK with valid embedding
```

### Root Cause
`diagnoseEmbedding()` in `src/core/ai/gateway.ts` rejects on empty `models: []` when `isUserProvided: true`, ignoring the parsed `modelId`.

### Proposed Fix
```typescript
// Add !parsed.modelId to the condition
if (!parsed.modelId && ...)  // guard no longer rejects when modelId is parsed
```

### Workaround
`gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` + `gbrain import <dir> --no-embed`

### Environment
- gbrain 0.42.51.0
- Ollama with nomic-embed-text on remote host (192.168.1.245)
- PGLite engine


hermes agent 0.16

title: sync/embed leak an abandoned `gbrain serve` backing process per invocation (headless/Docker; ~1 per run, unbounded RSS)
body:
## Summary

Headless CLI data commands — `gbrain sync` and `gbrain embed` — each spawn a long-lived `bun … gbrain serve` backing process that is **never terminated** when the command exits. Under a recurring non-interactive driver (systemd timer / cron / Docker `docker exec`), these accumulate ~1 per invocation and leak memory without bound (~330 MB RSS each in my deployment).

This is distinct from #1163 (orphaned **interactive** `gbrain serve` when a terminal closes → Supabase session pool): here **nobody launches `serve`**. The data commands themselves spawn-and-abandon it, headlessly, and the symptom is RSS growth, not the Postgres pool. Likely shares a root cause with the serve-lifecycle cluster (#1163, #1762, #2058, #677).

## Environment

- gbrain **v0.28.1**, running in Docker (container `Cmd=sleep infinity`; PGLite/local engine; bun runtime).
- Driver: a systemd timer every 30 min runs:
  ```
  docker exec gbrain gbrain sync --repo /brain --no-pull
  docker exec gbrain gbrain embed --stale
  ```
- Each `docker exec` returns 0/success; the data work is frequently a no-op ("Already up to date", "Embedded 0 chunks") — yet a `serve` is still left behind.

## Evidence (from the affected host)

After ~21h of 30-min ticks:

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,etimes,rss,args | grep 'gbrain serve' | grep -v grep
# 18–20 procs, all:  bun /data/.bun/bin/gbrain serve
#   PPID = container shim (orphaned; original docker-exec parent gone)
#   RSS  ≈ 330 MB each   →   ~6 GB total
#   etimes span ~10h–21h, spaced ~30 min apart  →  exactly one per timer tick
```

count/RSS: `serve=20  totalRSS≈6214MB`. Killing them reclaimed ~5.2 GB (host `used` 6.6 GiB → 1.4 GiB). Container PID 1 is `sleep infinity`, so none of the serves are load-bearing — every one is an abandoned backing daemon.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run gbrain in a container whose main process is not a `serve` (e.g. `sleep infinity`), local/PGLite engine.
2. From outside, repeatedly invoke a data command: `docker exec <c> gbrain sync --repo /brain --no-pull` (or `gbrain embed --stale`), e.g. on a 30-min timer.
3. `ps` inside/outside: one `bun … gbrain serve` accumulates per invocation and never exits.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** a one-shot CLI data command spawns no residual process — or, if it must start a `serve` to own the PGLite single-writer connection, it tears that `serve` down on exit. Flat memory between ticks.
- **Actual:** each invocation leaves one orphaned `gbrain serve`, RSS grows unbounded.

## Mechanism (hypothesis — maintainers can confirm)

`src/cli.ts` finally block: `if (command !== 'serve') await engine.disconnect();` disconnects the **client**, but does not terminate a `serve` process the engine may have spawned to own the single-writer PGLite connection (cf. #677 cooperative single-owner). So the client goes away while its backing `serve` is orphaned (reparented to the container init / shim) and lives forever. The eager-connect / lifecycle concerns in #2091 and #2058 look adjacent.

## Impact

Any headless/cron/Docker sync deployment (the autopilot/timer use case) grows memory without bound until the box is squeezed. In my case ~6 GB across 20 procs in a day.

## Workaround in place

Reap orphaned serves after each run. Note: a minimal container has **no procps** (`pkill`/`pgrep`/`ps` absent), so I walk `/proc` with the shell and the `kill` builtin:

```sh
docker exec <c> sh -c 'cd /proc; for d in [0-9]*; do [ -r "$d/cmdline" ] || continue;
  c=$(tr "\0" " " < "$d/cmdline" 2>/dev/null);
  case "$c" in bun*"gbrain serve"*) kill "$d" 2>/dev/null;; esac; done'
```

A proper fix would have data commands either run without a persistent backing `serve` or guarantee teardown of any `serve` they start (or reuse a single canonical one).

## Related

#1163 (interactive variant), #1762, #2058, #677, #2091.

title: feat(code-intel): MQL (MQL4/5) + C++ call-graph code intelligence
body:
## What this delivers

Call-graph **code intelligence for MQL4/MQL5** (MetaTrader) plus the enabling **C++ receiver-type resolution** — `code_callers` / `code_callees` / `code_blast` / `code_flow` over a real MQL corpus. MQL has no dedicated tree-sitter grammar and, as far as we can find, no call-graph tooling anywhere; tagging `.mq4/.mq5/.mqh` as `mql` over the already-shipped tree-sitter-cpp grammar gives gbrain that coverage at zero grammar-maintenance cost.

## Self-contained on fresh checkout

Rebased on current `master` and works **end-to-end**, not just at the unit level:

- `.mq4/.mq5/.mqh` are added to `CODE_EXTENSIONS`, so `gbrain sync --strategy code` actually routes MetaTrader files to the code chunker (guarded by a regression test in `sync-classifier-widening.test.ts`). Without it, sync silently dropped every MQL file.
- Coverage is honest on both ends: **admission** (the classifier test) + **edge extraction** (the `importCodeFile` → `getCallersOf`/`getCalleesOf` tests with committed MQL fixtures, so edge counts are reproducible in CI).

## Receiver-type resolution

Explicit and implicit receivers resolve to the receiver's declared class type, so the graph spans files:

- implicit-self (`m()`, `this->m()`) → enclosing class (exactly-one-declaration rule)
- out-of-line (`C::m(){...}`) → class named by the definition's qualified scope
- member-field / local-object (`m_x.Method()`, `obj.Method()`) → the field/local's declared class type
- **file-scope global objects** (`CDash g_dashboard; … g_dashboard.M()`) → the global's declared class type. Real MQL indicators wire their entry layer (`OnInit`/`OnCalculate`/`OnChartEvent`/`OnTimer`) to class internals through global singletons — this is what connects that boundary to the graph. (`mql-global-receiver-callers.test.ts`)
- **Honest precision boundary:** genuine globals/library calls, overloads, and namespaced/reference-typed receivers stay **bare** — no confident false edges.

## Free-function entry handlers are first-class call-graph nodes

MQL indicators *are* free functions (`OnInit`/`OnCalculate`/…) that orchestrate everything. The small-sibling chunk merge used to roll those tiny top-level functions into an anonymous chunk, dropping their symbol and every call edge — making the whole indicator entry layer invisible. A named function is now never merged (call-graph node, not a throwaway declaration).

**Measured on a real multi-file MQL indicator corpus:** before these two fixes the indicator entry handlers had **0** call edges; after, `OnInit`/`OnCalculate`/`OnChartEvent` resolve their full outgoing call sets and `code_callers` on a dashboard method surfaces `OnInit`/`OnTimer`. All TDD; engine match shares one predicate/regex across PGLite and Postgres (engine parity preserved).

## Encoding note

Real MetaTrader MQL files are frequently **UTF-16**, which the importer rejected outright. That fix is a separate, encoding-general PR (#2393) so it can be reviewed on its own; this PR assumes UTF-8 sources.

## Known limitations (disclosed)

Namespaced classes and reference-typed receivers aren't resolved yet — they stay bare (no false edges). `code_callers`/`code_callees`/`code_def`/`code_refs` are host-CLI ops (no MCP op yet; `code_blast`/`code_flow` do have MCP ops).

*Authored with AI assistance (Claude, plus a cross-model Codex review pass) under the contributor's direction.*
