title: Support DashScope text-embedding-v4 and file-plane DashScope config
body:
## Summary

`gbrain 0.42.53.0` has a few DashScope gaps that show up when setting up a China-region Alibaba Model Studio workspace:

1. The DashScope recipe only lists `text-embedding-v3` and `text-embedding-v2`.
2. `text-embedding-v4` works through the DashScope OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint, but `gbrain` rejects it as an unknown/unsupported recipe model.
3. `provider_base_urls.dashscope` works when it is present in the file-plane config, but `gbrain providers test --model ...` does not use the same config path as normal runtime.
4. There is no file-plane `dashscope_api_key` mapping, so stdio MCP launches such as `claude mcp add gbrain -- gbrain serve` cannot use DashScope unless the host process exports `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`.

## Environment

- gbrain: `0.42.53.0`
- Engine: Supabase/Postgres via session pooler
- Region: China mainland Alibaba Model Studio workspace
- Base URL shape:

```text
https://<workspace-id>.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
```

No API keys or private workspace ids are included here.

## What I tried

Direct OpenAI-compatible request to DashScope v4 succeeds:

```bash
curl -s "$DASHSCOPE_BASE_URL/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DASHSCOPE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "text-embedding-v4",
    "input": ["gbrain setup smoke test"],
    "dimensions": 1024
  }'
```

Result shape:

```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-v4",
  "embedding_dim": 1024,
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 6,
    "total_tokens": 6
  }
}
```

After applying a local patch, these commands also pass without `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` exported in the shell:

```bash
gbrain providers test --json
echo "DashScope v4 smoke test" | gbrain put setup-gbrain-filekey-smoke-test
gbrain search "DashScope v4 smoke test"
```

## Local patch that made it work

The local changes were:

- Add `text-embedding-v4` to `src/core/ai/recipes/dashscope.ts`.
- Add `1536` and `2048` to the DashScope `dims_options`.
- Add `dashscope_api_key?: string` to `GBrainConfig` and `KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS`.
- Map `dashscope_api_key` to `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` in `buildGatewayConfig`.
- Make `src/commands/providers.ts` use `buildGatewayConfig(config ?? {})` instead of building a smaller gateway config by hand.

With those changes and this local config shape, stdio MCP works:

```json
{
  "embedding_model": "dashscope:text-embedding-v4",
  "embedding_dimensions": 1024,
  "provider_base_urls": {
    "dashscope": "https://<workspace-id>.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"
  },
  "dashscope_api_key": "<stored in ~/.gbrain/config.json mode 0600>"
}
```

## Expected behavior

- DashScope recipe accepts `text-embedding-v4`.
- China-region workspace base URLs can be used for DashScope.
- `gbrain providers test` tests the same gateway path that `put`, `search`, and `serve` use.
- DashScope API key can be stored in file-plane config for MCP/server processes that do not inherit shell env vars.

## Actual behavior

- `gbrain providers test --model dashscope:text-embedding-v4` fails against the default international endpoint unless the runtime path is manually patched.
- `gbrain providers test` can disagree with normal `gbrain put/search` because it does not use the same gateway config builder.
- Claude Code MCP can start `gbrain serve`, but DashScope embeddings fail unless `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` is available to that process.

title: CLI local-op output normalization crashes on BigInt (cli.ts JSON.stringify has no replacer)
body:
## Summary

The local-engine CLI path normalizes every op return value with a bare
`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(rawResult))` (`src/cli.ts:445`). When `rawResult`
contains a JS `bigint` — e.g. a `BIGSERIAL` primary key read back by the
Postgres engine — `JSON.stringify` throws `TypeError: Do not know how to
serialize a BigInt`, so the command crashes before any renderer runs.

The ENG-2 comment directly above that line documents the intended behavior:

> Date → ISO string; bigint → string (postgres.js shape); Buffer → object.

…but a plain `JSON.stringify` **cannot** turn a `bigint` into a string — it
throws. So the promised `bigint → string` parity is never actually achieved;
the op errors out instead.

## Repro

Any local op whose return shape includes a `bigint` column. The one we hit is
`get_calibration_profile` once a `calibration_profiles` row exists
(`id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY`, `src/schema.sql:1227`):

```
gbrain call get_calibration_profile --holder <h>   # local-engine op path → cli.ts:445
```

With **no** profile row it returns `null` and serializes fine — the crash only
appears once data exists, which makes it read as intermittent.

(`CalibrationProfileRow.id` is typed `number` in `src/commands/calibration.ts`,
but `getLatestProfile`'s `SELECT id …` returns the `BIGSERIAL` as a JS bigint,
so the type annotation is also masking the hazard.)

## Root cause

`src/cli.ts:445`

```ts
const result = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(rawResult));
```

No replacer → a bigint anywhere in the tree is unserializable → throw.

## Suggested fix

Add a replacer that mirrors the postgres.js wire shape the comment already
promises (postgres.js returns `int8` as a string):

```ts
const result = JSON.parse(
  JSON.stringify(rawResult, (_k, v) => (typeof v === 'bigint' ? v.toString() : v)),
);
```

This makes the local path match the routed path and removes the whole bigint
crash-class for every local op, not just calibration.

Note: the CLI-only `gbrain calibration --json` path has its own bare
`JSON.stringify(profile, …)` (`src/commands/calibration.ts`) with the same
hazard; it's currently unreachable due to #2035, but will surface the same
crash once that command is wired up, so it deserves the same treatment.

## Related (not duplicates)

- #2433 and #2256 are the same *family* (Date/timestamp serialization on the
  gateway tool-result path) but a different layer and root cause. This one is
  the CLI local-op output normalizer.

title: calibration_profile + voice-gate use bare model ids → parseModelId throws "missing a provider prefix"
body:
## Summary

The `calibration_profile` cycle phase and its voice gate hardcode **bare** model
ids with no provider prefix. `gateway.chat()` runs the model string through
`parseModelId` (`src/core/ai/model-resolver.ts:41`), which throws
`Model id "<id>" is missing a provider prefix.` for any string lacking a
`provider:` / `provider/` prefix. So the moment the phase actually invokes the
LLM (holder has ≥5 resolved bets, budget allows, no test judge injected), it
crashes.

## Bare ids

- `src/core/cycle/calibration-profile.ts:231`
  ```ts
  const modelId = opts.model ?? 'claude-sonnet-4-6';
  ```
  This `modelId` feeds the budget estimate (`checkBudget`, :273), the
  pattern/bias generation via `gatewayChat`, and the stored `model_id` row
  (:378) — all off a bare id.

- `src/core/calibration/voice-gate.ts:162` (`defaultJudge`, the production judge
  per `voice-gate.ts:203` → `judge = opts.judge ?? defaultJudge`)
  ```ts
  model: 'claude-haiku-4-5',
  ```

## Repro

Run the `calibration_profile` phase for a holder with ≥5 resolved bets and a
non-zero budget, without injecting a test `voiceGateJudge` / `patternsGenerator`.
The first `gateway.chat()` call throws `missing a provider prefix`.

## Suggested fix

Resolve through the existing `TIER_DEFAULTS` (`src/core/model-config.ts:74`),
which already carry the provider prefix and are the single source of truth for
tier defaults:

- calibration-profile default → `TIER_DEFAULTS.reasoning`
  (`anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`)
- voice-gate judge default → `TIER_DEFAULTS.utility`
  (`anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`)

That keeps the budget estimate, the gateway call, the voice gate, and the
stored `model_id` consistent on a single resolved `provider:model`.

## Related (not duplicates)

- #1857 is the same class (hardcoded judge model in `takes extract --from-pages`)
  but a different code path — and it at least carries the `anthropic:` prefix.
  These two are bare (no prefix) and crash on `parseModelId` instead of silently
  returning 0 claims.
- #1270 is hardcoded-model-rot in cross-modal-eval — adjacent, different site.

title: fix(calibration,takes,cli): model resolution, source-scoped takes reads, BigInt-safe output, calibration CLI reachability
body:
## Summary

Four fixes around the `calibration_profile` phase, takes read scoping, and the
local CLI — each verified against `upstream/master` (v0.42.53.0). Issues were
filed first; this PR closes them.

**2026-07-12 update** — folded in the two gaps flagged in the #2450 comment
thread ([takes_search MCP path](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/2450#issuecomment-4921442283),
[`gbrain call` exit](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/2450#issuecomment-4954688069));
see the new section below.

## Fixes

### BigInt-safe local-op output normalization — Fixes #2450
`cli.ts` normalized every local-engine op result with a bare
`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(rawResult))`. A bigint column (e.g.
`calibration_profiles.id BIGSERIAL`) threw `TypeError: Do not know how to
serialize a BigInt` and crashed the command — the ENG-2 comment promised
`bigint → string` but a plain `JSON.stringify` can't do that. Added a replacer;
covers every local op, `get_calibration_profile` included.

### #2450 comment thread: takes_search MCP path + `gbrain call` exit
Two sibling crash sites reported in the issue comments, same BigInt class:

- **`searchTakes` / `searchTakesVector`** returned raw driver rows cast
  straight to `TakeHit[]`; int8 columns (`take_id`, `page_id`) arrive as
  native BigInt from the pg driver, so MCP `takes_search` crashed the
  serializer the moment a query actually matched (no match → `[]` → reads as
  intermittent). `takes_list` was immune because it maps through
  `takeRowToTake`. Added `takeHitRowToHit` (mirrors `takeRowToTake`,
  `Number()` per the `TakeHit` numeric contract) and routed all four sites —
  Postgres + PGLite, keyword + vector — through it for engine parity.
- **`gbrain call`** bypasses cli.ts's op-output normalizer entirely — its own
  bare `JSON.stringify` at the command exit crashed on any op returning an
  int8 column (the calibration repro only survived because `getLatestProfile`
  now coerces at the source). Reused `bigintToStringReplacer` at that exit
  (static import is cycle-safe: cli.ts only dynamic-imports call.ts, and its
  main() sits behind `import.meta.main`).

Both fixes are pinned by mutation-verified regression tests: reverting either
one fails a test (e2e postgres searchTakes/searchTakesVector type +
serializability assertions; a `runCall` stub-engine wiring test). Without the
pins the whole suite stayed green under revert — PGLite returns int8 as plain
`number`, so only the real-driver e2e suite can produce the BigInt input, and
`searchTakesVector` previously had zero invocations repo-wide.

### calibration_profile + voice-gate model resolution — Fixes #2451
Both hardcoded bare model ids (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4-5`).
`gateway.chat()` → `parseModelId` throws "missing a provider prefix" for a bare
id, crashing the phase on its first LLM call. Routed both through
`TIER_DEFAULTS` (reasoning / utility) so the budget estimate, gateway call,
voice gate, and stored `model_id` share one resolved `provider:model`.

### `gbrain calibration` reachability — Fixes #2035
`calibration` was missing from `CLI_ONLY`, so dispatch fell through to
"Unknown command" despite the `case 'calibration'` handler. Added it to the set.

### takes reads honor source / federated_read scope — Addresses #2200
`takes_list` / `takes_search` / `takes_scorecard` / `takes_calibration` applied
no source scope, while page reads and `get_calibration_profile` route through
`sourceScopeOpts` — so a `federated_read` client saw takes outside its granted
sources. `takes` has no `source_id` column, so it's scoped through the take's
`page.source_id` (JOIN for list/search, EXISTS for scorecard/curve). Threaded
`sourceScopeOpts(ctx)` into the four handlers and filtered in **both** the
Postgres and PGLite engines. The holder allow-list stays an orthogonal,
unchanged filter. (Partial fix for the broader #2200 sweep — the takes slice;
see the issue comment.)

## Tests

New / extended (all green under `bun test`):
- `test/cli-bigint-normalize.test.ts` — bigint replacer + `CLI_ONLY`
  reachability + `takeHitRowToHit` BigInt coercion + `runCall` output-exit
  wiring (stub engine, bigint-carrying op result)
- `test/e2e/takes-postgres.test.ts` — searchTakes hits assert numeric
  take_id/page_id + JSON-serializability on the real pg driver; new
  searchTakesVector test with the same pins (the file header already claimed
  vector coverage; now it exists)
- `test/calibration-profile.test.ts` — default model resolves to a
  provider-prefixed `model_id`; tier defaults parse via `parseModelId`
- `test/takes-source-scope.test.ts` — PGLite: list/search (JOIN) +
  scorecard/curve (EXISTS) source filtering, and source × holder-allow-list
  composition

Run locally:
- `bun test` (cli-bigint-normalize, takes-source-scope, calibration-profile,
  calibration-cli, voice-gate, takes-engine) → **105 pass, 0 fail**; after the
  2026-07-12 update, all 29 takes-related files → **357 pass, 0 fail**
- `test/e2e/takes-postgres.test.ts` against a real Postgres 17 + pgvector
  scratch DB → **23 pass, 0 fail** (2026-07-12 update)
- `bun run typecheck` → clean
- `bun run verify` (30-check pre-push gate, incl. `check:source-id-projection`,
  `check:operations-filter-bypass`, privacy, typecheck) → **30/30 green**
  (re-run after the update)

Skipped (with reasons):
- Full `bun run test` (3700+ unit shards) and the rest of `test/e2e/*` were
  not run locally. The targeted suite + the 30-check verify gate cover the
  changed code; the takes source-scope behavior is exercised on **real
  PGLite**, and the BigInt coercion on **real Postgres** (takes e2e file).

title: fix(serve): lazy-connect stdio MCP engine
body:
Fixes #2091. Rebases/replaces the currently-conflicting #2092 against current `master`.

## Problem

`gbrain serve` on stdio received an eagerly-connected engine. For PGLite, that means the MCP `initialize` handshake waits on full WASM boot plus single-writer lock acquisition. Under contention the lock wait alone can reach the host's 30s connect timeout, so clients see an opaque MCP timeout instead of an actionable lock error.

There is also a shutdown race: if the host disconnects while the engine connect is still in flight, the old cleanup path could call `engine.disconnect()` before the lock was acquired, then the in-flight connect could complete and leave the lock behind.

## Fix

- Add `src/core/engine-provider.ts`, a lazy engine provider for stdio serve.
- Dispatch `gbrain serve` before `connectEngine()` in `cli.ts` and pass a lazy connector.
- Keep `--http` eager, because HTTP has no stdio initialize-handshake deadline.
- Have stdio `runServe` start connection in the background and pass the provider to the MCP server.
- Have `tools/call` await `provider.ensure()` and return a structured `engine_unavailable` tool error on connect failure; failed connects are retried on the next call.
- Have shutdown call `provider.disconnect()`, which awaits any in-flight connect before disconnecting the engine, closing the lock-leak race.
- Preserve Retrieval Reflex IPC by binding it only after the lazy engine becomes ready; includes current suppression + delivery logging behavior from master.

## Tests

- `bun test test/serve-lazy-engine-connect.test.ts test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts`
- `bun test test/e2e/serve-stdio-roundtrip.test.ts`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build:llms`

Note: `bun run verify` was attempted, but this checkout's parallel verify wrapper killed all 30 subchecks with rc=143 after ~13s even though the visible checks were clean up to termination. The targeted tests and typecheck above passed.

title: v0.42.54.0 fix(security): views enforce caller RLS via security_invoker
body:
## What

Migration **v120 `page_links_view_security_invoker`** defines GBrain's schema view `WITH (security_invoker = on)`, so it enforces the **querying role's** row-level security instead of the view owner's.

GBrain enables RLS on its core tables, but Postgres creates views SECURITY DEFINER by default — so a view over an RLS-protected table reads it as the view's owner and skips the caller's policy. This flips it to `security_invoker`, closing that gap. A managed-Postgres database linter flagged it (`0010_security_definer_view`).

## Why it's safe / scoped

- **No effect on gbrain itself** — it connects as the table-owning role, which bypasses RLS regardless. This only constrains untrusted roles on managed Postgres brains.
- **Embedded (PGLite) brains unaffected** — a single trusted connection with no separate roles; the option is a harmless no-op there.
- **Born-secure on fresh installs, auto-applied on upgrade.** Both `schema.sql` and `pglite-schema.ts` seed `version='1'`, so every fresh brain runs the full migration array including v120; existing brains pick it up on the next `initSchema()`. One migration covers all four cases (fresh/existing × Postgres/PGLite).
- View projection is unchanged (`id, from_page_id, to_page_id`).

## Test plan

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- PGLite (PG18.3) accepts the option and stores the reloption (verified directly)
- Full migration chain applies `[120] ✓` on both engines (`test/migrate.test.ts`)
- **New** `test/migrations-v120.test.ts` — 5 pass / 0 fail: asserts the view ends up `security_invoker=on` after `initSchema()` with its column shape intact

## Version

`0.42.53.0 → 0.42.54.0` (VERSION, package.json, CHANGELOG all in sync). No CLAUDE.md/docs edits, so no `build:llms` change.

title: fix: allow sync on repos with no commits (Dream Cycle sync phase)
body:
## Problem

When a gbrain repo was initialized but no commit was ever made
(e.g. after `gbrain init`, before the first `git commit`),
`git rev-parse HEAD` fails. The code throws an error and blocks
the entire Dream Cycle sync phase **every cycle**, indefinitely.

The repo has a `.git` directory (passes the "is it a git repo?"
check) but zero commits (fails the "get HEAD" check). Users who
ran `gbrain init` without manually committing are stuck with
`sync: fail` forever.

## Root Cause

`performFullSync` already handles the zero-commit case -- it walks
the filesystem directly. But the `throw` above prevents the code
from ever reaching it.

## Fix

When `git rev-parse HEAD` fails, set `headCommit` to `""` instead
of throwing. This lets the flow fall through to
`performFullSync(engine, repoPath, headCommit, opts)`, which
imports all syncable files from disk.

**5 lines changed** (including comment):

```diff
-    throw new Error(`No commits in repo ${repoPath}. Make at least one commit before syncing.`);
+    headCommit = '';
```

## Verification

- `!lastCommit` will be true (no prior sync anchor)
  → hits the "First sync" path at ~line 1722 → calls `performFullSync`
- Subsequent syncs with actual commits work normally via the
  incremental diff path
- Tested: `gbrain sync --dry-run` on a repo with zero commits now
  reports files to import instead of throwing

## Test impact

One test comment in `test/e2e/multi-source.test.ts:373` mentions
the old error message as a possible outcome. No assertions are
affected.

title: [codex] fix frontmatter scans to respect git excludes
body:
## Summary

`gbrain doctor` / `frontmatter audit` and `gbrain frontmatter validate <dir>` currently walk source directories independently from sync/import. That means they can report malformed frontmatter for files that sync never indexes, including files ignored by `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, or global git excludes.

This PR adds a shared git-visible file helper and uses it in both frontmatter scan paths:

- `frontmatter validate <dir>` via `collectFiles`
- `doctor` / `frontmatter audit` via `scanBrainSources`

When the target is inside a git worktree, the scanner enumerates files with:

```bash
git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -z
```

It falls back to the existing filesystem walker when git is unavailable or the target is not a git worktree.

## Root Cause

The sync/import path already has git-aware enumeration, but frontmatter integrity checks use separate walkers. `pruneDir()` fixed hardcoded directories like `node_modules`, but it does not honor project-local ignore rules such as `.git/info/exclude`.

So a local tooling directory can be correctly absent from the index while still making `frontmatter_integrity` warn.

## Related

- #799 fixed the same class of doctor/frontmatter false positive for hardcoded pruned directories like `node_modules`.
- #449 and #1148 cover broader `.gbrainignore` / source exclusion requests.
- #1074 covers frontmatter audit false positives on conventional plain Markdown files.

This PR is intentionally narrower: make the frontmatter scanners honor the same git-visible file boundary that sync/import already use.

## Tests

Added regression coverage in `test/brain-writer-walk-prune.test.ts`:

- `collectFiles` skips a malformed Markdown file under a `.git/info/exclude`d directory
- `scanBrainSources` ignores that same malformed ignored file and scans only the visible Markdown page

Validated locally:

```bash
bun test test/brain-writer-walk-prune.test.ts
bun run typecheck
```

Both pass.

title: fix(ai): honor base_urls override for native-anthropic chat/expansion
body:
## Problem

The `native-anthropic` branches in `instantiateChat` and `instantiateExpansion` (`src/core/ai/gateway.ts`) construct the Anthropic client with `createAnthropic({ apiKey })`, **ignoring `cfg.base_urls`**.

This is inconsistent with the rest of the gateway:
- The `openai-compatible` branches resolve `cfg.base_urls?.[recipe.id] ?? recipe.base_url_default`.
- The expansion/chat **cache keys** (lines ~2112 and ~2484) already fold `cfg.base_urls?.[recipe.id]` into the key.

So a `base_urls` override for an Anthropic recipe is threaded through config *and* the cache key, but then **dropped at client construction** — `provider_base_urls.anthropic` has no effect and chat/expansion always hit `api.anthropic.com`.

## Fix

Honor `cfg.base_urls?.[recipe.id]` in both `native-anthropic` branches, mirroring the `openai-compatible` convention. When no override is present, behavior is unchanged (default Anthropic endpoint).

This lets the Anthropic client target an Anthropic-compatible proxy (e.g. a LiteLLM `/v1/messages` endpoint serving an Anthropic-format model) for `think`/synthesis and chat, which are pinned to the Anthropic provider.

## Notes
- No version/CHANGELOG bump — leaving the release mechanics to the maintainer's ship flow.
- Minimal, additive, and a no-op when `base_urls` is unset.

title: Fix native local embedding setup blockers

title: fix(extract): deterministic atom slug — stop cross-day + trailing-dash duplicate atoms
body:
## Problem

`extract_atoms` mints duplicate atom pages two distinct ways. Together they account for the bulk of duplicate atoms in a long-running brain.

**Bug A — trailing-dash twins.** The local slugger does `.slice(0, 60)` with no re-strip. When the 60-char cut lands on a hyphen, the slug keeps a trailing dash (`…would-`). A second normalization path — the FS-import slugifier `slugifySegment` in `src/core/sync.ts` — *does* strip trailing dashes (`…would`). The two disagree, so the same atom persists under two slugs and the dedup-by-slug check never collapses them. (Verified in the field: twin pairs with identical title, identical `source_hash`, same-millisecond `extracted_at` — one extraction, two writes.)

**Bug B — cross-day re-mint.** The slug uses `todayDate()` (the run date), while the idempotency guard `atomsExistingForHashes` keys on `frontmatter.source_hash` = the hash of the **entire source file**. Append-only sources (chat/transcript exports) grow every day, so the whole-file hash changes, the guard never matches on later runs, the source is fully re-extracted, and each re-mint lands under a new date prefix → a new slug → no upsert → a duplicate per run. (Verified: the same atom minted on three consecutive days from one growing transcript, with different file hashes.)

## Fix

Make the atom slug a deterministic function of stable inputs:

```
atoms/<source-date>/<stem>-<title-hash>
```

- **`<source-date>`** is parsed from the source ref (the transcript filename, e.g. `…/2026-06-11-telegram.md`, or the page slug), **not** the run date. Re-extracting an append-only source on a later day now resolves to the **same** slug, so `putPage` upserts instead of minting a cross-day duplicate (fixes B).
- **`<stem>`** routes through the canonical `slugifySegment` (the same normalizer the FS-import path uses) and **re-strips a trailing dash after truncation**, so the two write paths can no longer disagree on `…would` vs `…would-` (fixes A).
- **`<title-hash>`** (6-char sha256 of the title) keeps two *distinct* atoms whose titles share the first 60 chars on separate slugs, so a deterministic slug never silently clobbers a different atom. Hash is over the title only (not body), so an LLM rewording the body on re-extraction still upserts rather than duplicates.

The whole-file `source_hash` batch check is **retained only as a cost fast-path** (skip re-running the model on an unchanged source). On append-only sources it won't skip, but the deterministic slug makes the re-run upsert rather than duplicate — correctness no longer depends on it.

## Relationship to existing work

- Implements the per-atom-idempotency item in `TODOS.md` (and the `extract-atoms.ts` header note flagging it as a follow-up).
- Complements #2169 (semantic clustering + dedup-by-merge) by stopping new duplicates **at the source**, rather than only cleaning them up after.
- **Diverges from the TODO's proposed `atoms/<source_hash16>/…` prefix on purpose:** `source_hash16` is the whole-file hash that mutates on every append, so it would *not* fix Bug B. The parsed source date is stable across appends.

## Tests

Adds a hermetic PGLite regression test in `test/extract-atoms-page-discovery.test.ts` (no `DATABASE_URL` required) asserting:
- the slug carries the **source date** (not the run date),
- a **6-char title-hash** suffix,
- **no trailing dash** before the hash (Bug A),
- **upsert** (one row, not a duplicate) when a grown append-only transcript is re-extracted with a changed file hash (Bug B).

It fails on the pre-fix code (old slug uses the run date and has no hash suffix), so it genuinely guards the behavior.

```
bun test test/extract-atoms*.test.ts test/cycle/extract-atoms*.test.ts test/doctor-extract-atoms-backlog.test.ts
# 62 pass / 0 fail
```
`bun run typecheck` is clean.

## Migration note

This stops *new* duplicates; it does **not** retract atoms already minted under the old scheme (existing atoms keep their old slugs until re-extracted). Cleaning up the existing duplicates is a separate one-time data pass (see #2169 / `TODOS.md`). Left out of this PR to keep it to the root-cause fix. Happy to add a `CHANGELOG`/version entry in whatever form you prefer.

title: fix(subagent): gateway tool-loop drops tool-results on resume → openai-compat dead-letter
body:
The gateway-native subagent loop (`runSubagentViaGateway` → `toolLoop`), used for non-Anthropic models, lacks the crash-recovery parity the legacy inline loop has:

1. It never persists the synthesized tool-result message (only the seed + assistant turns).
2. It has no resume reconciliation for a dangling assistant tool-call turn.

When a subagent job stalls (timeout / `max_stalled`) and is re-claimed, it reloads `[user, assistant(tool_calls), assistant(tool_calls), …]` with no tool-result messages between them. The first `chat()` then sends an assistant message whose `tool_calls` have no following tool results. Anthropic tolerates this; OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g. DeepSeek) reject it with `Tool results are missing for tool call X` → the job permanently dead-letters. Intermittent, since only stalled-then-resumed jobs hit it.

**Fix** (parity with the legacy loop):
- Add `ToolLoopOpts.onUserTurn`, fired before the in-memory push (write-before-side-effect). `runSubagentViaGateway` persists the tool-result user turn.
- Add replay reconciliation in `runSubagentViaGateway` mirroring the legacy reconciler: if the last persisted message is an assistant turn with dangling tool-call blocks, synthesize the tool-result user turn from `subagent_tool_executions` (complete → stored output, failed → stored error, pending/missing → re-dispatch idempotent tools, else throw), persist it, and feed it into `replayState`. Keyed by provider `tool_use_id`; `loadPriorToolsV2` now exposes it.

**Test**: `subagent-gateway-resume-reconciliation.test.ts` seeds the crash condition (assistant turn with parallel `tool_calls` + complete exec rows, no tool-result message). A validating stub transport throws the exact provider rejection on a dangling tool-call. Fails on baseline, passes with the fix, asserts reconciled results carry the real stored outputs.

Verified e2e against the DeepSeek API: without the fix a multi-turn synthesize subagent dead-letters 7/8 jobs; with it, 10/10 complete.

title: fix(gateway): drop non-string text parts in toModelMessages (AI SDK v6 schema reject)
body:
A reasoning model (e.g. DeepSeek v4) can return a text content part whose `text` is `undefined`/`null`. The block type is `{type:'text', text:string}`, but the value arrives from the provider at runtime. On the next turn, `toModelMessages` emits it verbatim and AI SDK v6 rejects the request locally with `Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema` — failing the whole turn. (Confirmed: v6 rejects a text part with `undefined`/`null` text; empty-string text is fine.)

Intermittent, and in the subagent loop it *recovers on resume* because the replay path (`adaptContentBlocksToChatBlocks`) already drops non-string-text parts — so the rebuilt conversation is clean while the in-memory one was not.

**Fix**: `toModelMessages` (the documented `ChatMessage[]` → v6 `ModelMessage[]` converter) drops text parts whose `text` is not a string, mirroring the replay path. Covers every message source (live loop, replay, future). Empty content is valid for v6, so a turn left empty by the drop still passes.

**Tests** pin: non-string text dropped, valid siblings kept, empty-string kept.

title: gateway.chat() prompt-cache marker is a silent no-op — cacheSystem never lands a breakpoint on @ai-sdk/anthropic 3.x
body:
# Bug: gateway prompt-cache marker is a silent no-op — `gateway.chat()` caches nothing on Anthropic

**Component:** `src/core/ai/gateway.ts` (`chat()` / `toolLoop()`)
**Severity:** Correctness + cost (no data loss). Every `gateway.chat()`-routed Anthropic call that requests `cacheSystem: true` pays full input price on its stable prefix on every call.
**Env:** gbrain `0.42.53.0`; `@ai-sdk/anthropic` `3.0.79`; `ai` `6.0.191`.
**Verified:** read-only source audit (line numbers below confirmed against the installed package).

## TL;DR

`chat()` sets the Anthropic ephemeral cache marker at the **top level** of the `generateText()` call and passes `system` as a **bare string**. In `@ai-sdk/anthropic` 3.0.79, `cacheControl` breakpoints are read **only** from each block's *own* `providerOptions` (system message, message part, tool). A top-level marker is emitted as a stray top-level `cache_control` request-body field that the Messages API does not honor as a prefix breakpoint, and a bare-string system carries no per-block `providerOptions`. Net: **no `cache_control` breakpoint ever lands**, so every gateway-routed caller gets zero cache writes and zero cache reads — regardless of how stable its prefix is.

The native-Anthropic subagent path (`minions/handlers/subagent.ts`) is unaffected — it uses the raw SDK with native `cache_control` blocks correctly. It is the current default (`agent.use_gateway_loop` unset).

## Root cause (verified line numbers)

`src/core/ai/gateway.ts`, `chat()`:
- `2714-2715`: `supportsCache = recipe.touchpoints.chat?.supports_prompt_cache === true; useCache = !!opts.cacheSystem && supportsCache;`
- `2733-2735`: `const providerOptions = {}; if (useCache) { providerOptions.anthropic = { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } }; }`  ← marker built at **call** level
- `2757`: `system: opts.system,`  ← passed as a **bare string**
- `2764`: `providerOptions: Object.keys(providerOptions).length > 0 ? providerOptions : undefined,`  ← attached to the **top level** of `generateText`

`@ai-sdk/anthropic` 3.0.79 (`dist/index.js`):
- `2218-2225`: the **system block** gets `cache_control` from each system message's *own* `providerOptions` — `validator.getCacheControl(providerOptions, { type: 'system message' })`.
- `2237`: per **user message part** `providerOptions`.
- `1440`: per **tool** `providerOptions`.
- `~3455`: a **call-level** `cacheControl` is written as a top-level `cache_control` body field — not a content-block breakpoint, so the API ignores it for prefix caching.
- `ai` core turns a bare-string `system` into a system message with **no** `providerOptions`, so `getCacheControl(undefined)` returns nothing.

Result: the marker at gateway.ts:2735/2764 is never read. The in-code comment near gateway.ts:2717-2719 ("cache markers go through `providerOptions.anthropic`") reflects the pre-3.x SDK shape and is no longer correct.

## Affected call paths

Every caller that routes through `gateway.chat()` with `cacheSystem: true` caches nothing today:
`page-summary.ts`, `enrich.ts`, `skillopt/{reflect,rollout,score,bootstrap-benchmark}.ts`, and the gateway tool-loop (`gateway.ts` `toolLoop()` → `chat()` at ~2978/2983).
Callers that pass a system prompt but never set `cacheSystem` (so they don't even request it): `cycle/synthesize.ts`, `think/index.ts`.
`cycle/propose-takes.ts` sets neither a system nor `cacheSystem` (single user message).

**Not affected (works correctly):** `minions/handlers/subagent.ts` legacy direct path — raw `@anthropic-ai/sdk` `client.create()` with `cache_control` on the system text block (`:485`) and the last tool def (`:498`).

## How to confirm

Make one `cacheSystem: true` chat call through the gateway and inspect the Anthropic usage in the response (`providerMetadata.anthropic` / the values read at gateway.ts:2813-2814): `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` will both be `0`. The same prompt sent twice within the 5-min TTL still shows `cache_read_input_tokens: 0`. The subagent raw-SDK path on the same system prompt shows non-zero `cache_read_input_tokens` on calls 2..n.

## Fix

**Primary — put the marker on the system block.** In `chat()`, stop passing `system` as a bare string + top-level `providerOptions`. Emit the system as a system-role message in the `messages` array carrying its *own* `providerOptions` (the only place the SDK reads it):

```ts
messages: [
  { role: 'system',
    content: opts.system,
    providerOptions: useCache ? { anthropic: { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } } } : undefined },
  ...toModelMessages(opts.messages),
],
// remove the top-level `system:` param and the top-level `providerOptions:` cache marker
```
Behavior-preserving when `useCache` is false. (Confirm `ai` 6.0.191 copies `message.providerOptions` for the array form — it does at `dist/index.js` core prompt builder.)

**Secondary — cache the last tool def.** When `useCache`, set `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl` on the last entry of the `tools` map (SDK reads `tool.providerOptions` at dist:1440). Mirrors the working raw-SDK pattern (`subagent.ts:498`).

**Accounting — price cache tokens (do this regardless).** `model-pricing.ts` `CANONICAL_PRICING` has only `input`/`output`; the cache_read/creation tokens already collected at gateway.ts:2813-2814 are priced at full input rate, so the budget tracker over-counts and cache benefit is never surfaced in dollars. Add cache-write (1.25× input) and cache-read (0.10× input) handling (single canonical table per CLAUDE.md; let derived views follow; guarded by `test/model-pricing.test.ts`).

## Guardrail (until the primary fix lands)

Do **not** enable `agent.use_gateway_loop`. It routes the subagent loop — currently the only path that caches correctly — through the broken `gateway.chat()`, regressing the one working cached path to zero.

## Notes on impact

The shared-prefix paths below Anthropic's class-minimum cacheable prefix (~1024 tok Sonnet / ~2048 tok Haiku) won't benefit even after the fix: `propose_takes` (~310 tok), `page-summary` (~177 tok), `think` base (~380 tok). The fix matters for large-stable-system callers reused within the 5-min TTL — e.g. `skillopt` rollouts (skill text is the system, multi-KB, identical across a batch). Estimated saving when caching works: ~$2.70 per 1,000 Sonnet calls per 1,000 prefix tokens (cache-read at 0.10× input vs full input).

title: fix(ai): serialize Date in tool-result json output so Postgres timestamps don't crash multi-tool loops (#2433)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2433. Any multi-tool rollout or subagent loop that called a brain tool returning Postgres timestamp columns (e.g. `brain_list_pages`, `brain_query`) crashed AI SDK v6 validation with `AI_InvalidPromptError: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema`.

## Root cause

`node-postgres` deserializes timestamp columns into JS `Date` instances. `toModelMessages()` (`src/core/ai/gateway.ts`) emitted the tool result in its `json` branch as `{ type: 'json', value: b.output }`, passing those `Date`s through raw. AI SDK v6's `jsonValueSchema` accepts only `null | string | number | boolean | record | array` — not `Date` — so the entire message tree was rejected.

## Fix

JSON-roundtrip the value in the `json` branch so `Date`s (including nested ones) serialize to ISO strings the validator accepts:

```ts
value: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(b.output ?? null)) as never
```

Scope kept tight: the `error-text` branch already stringifies and is untouched; no `BigInt` handling added (that's a separate concern, #2450).

## Test

`test/gateway-model-messages.test.ts` gains a case feeding a tool-result whose `output` nests a `Date`, asserting it serializes to the ISO string. Confirmed it **fails on the pre-fix code** (receives a raw `Date`) and **passes after**. The issue author independently verified the fix on a real workload (subagent rollout success 1/5 → 5/5).

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` → clean (`EXIT=0`)
- `bun test test/gateway-model-messages.test.ts` → all pass

Closes #2433.

title: fix(import): skip marked.lexer on fence-less pages to avoid transient-memory OOM on bulk import (#2437)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2437. `extractFencedChunks()` (`src/core/import-file.ts`) ran `marked.lexer()` on **every** page body to pull fenced code blocks. `marked.lexer` transiently allocates roughly 60× the input size, so a large (~2 MB) fence-less page spikes to ~110 MB and can OOM-kill bulk `sync`/`import`. Since ~99% of importable pages contain no code fence, ~99% of those lexer runs were pure waste.

## Fix

Add a cheap guard at the top of `extractFencedChunks()` that returns early when the body contains no fenced-code opener at all (a backtick or tilde fence at line start, per CommonMark), so `marked.lexer()` never runs on fence-less pages. About 3 lines; the happy path (pages that do contain fences) is unchanged.

## Test

`test/fence-extraction.test.ts` gains two cases, both exercised through the public `importFromContent` path:
- a large (~96 KB) fence-less prose body yields no fenced chunks — with a sanity guard asserting the body truly contains no fence, so the test can't pass on a body that happens to include one; and
- a body with a fenced code block still extracts its chunk, proving the guard doesn't break the happy path.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` → clean (`EXIT=0`)
- `bun test test/fence-extraction.test.ts` → all pass

Closes #2437.

title: fix(cli): BigInt-safe JSON serialization so local-op output normalization doesn't crash (#2450)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2450. The CLI local-op output normalizer crashed on `BigInt`: `JSON.stringify` throws on a bigint (e.g. a `BIGSERIAL` primary key from the Postgres engine), aborting the command before any renderer ran.

## Root cause

`src/cli.ts` round-trips every local read/write op result through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(rawResult))` for normalization, with no replacer. A `BigInt` anywhere in the result makes `JSON.stringify` throw.

## Fix

Add a small local `bigintReplacer` (serializes `BigInt` via `.toString()`) and route the normalization round-trip and the `formatResult` default renderer through it.

`.toString()` (not `Number()`) is deliberate: the normalization path exists to match the renderer output of the routed path, and postgres.js returns `int8` as a **string** on the wire — so `.toString()` preserves that parity and avoids the precision loss `Number()` would introduce past 2^53. (Matches the existing `gateway.ts` convention for serializing bigint.)

**Scope kept tight:** the two sites that share the live crash risk are fixed (the normalization round-trip + `formatResult`'s default case). The `reindex --multimodal --json` site was left alone because its input is typed entirely as `number` (TS guarantees no bigint reaches it), and `gbrain calibration --json` is unreachable per #2035 — the issue itself flags it as later treatment.

## Test

6 new cases in `test/cli.test.ts` covering the normalization path with a `BigInt` (no throw + correct string serialization, including a past-`MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` precision case) plus the `formatResult` default. Verified to throw on the pre-fix code and pass after.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` → clean (`EXIT=0`)
- `bun test test/cli.test.ts` → all pass

Closes #2450.

title: v0.42.54.0 fix(ai): embedding preflight accepts user-named models on litellm/llama-server (#1716)
body:
## What

The embedding preflight (`diagnoseEmbedding` in `src/core/ai/gateway.ts`) rejected **every** embedding model on the two bring-your-own-model recipes — **LiteLLM** and **llama.cpp's llama-server** — as `user_provided_model_unset`, even when the user named a concrete model like `litellm:my-model`. Those users could not embed at all.

Because `isAvailable('embedding')` delegates to `diagnoseEmbedding(...).ok`, the same false rejection **silently degraded hybrid search to keyword-only** on those brains — no error surfaced.

## Fix

One predicate. Only emit `user_provided_model_unset` when the model is **genuinely unset** (`parsed.modelId` empty). A named model now passes preflight and falls through to the (empty) auth-env check → `ok: true`. A bare provider with no model still errors as `unknown_provider` (the parser rejects it upstream, before the guard), which points the user at the `provider:model` form.

**Scope correction vs the original plan:** Ollama was **not** affected — it ships a non-empty built-in model list, so its models always resolved (`ollama:nomic-embed-text` was already `isAvailable === true`). The fix targets LiteLLM and llama-server, the only two recipes with `models: []` + `user_provided_models: true`.

## Tests

First-ever direct `diagnoseEmbedding` tests in `test/embed-preflight.test.ts`:
- `litellm:my-model`, `llama-server:bge-m3` → `ok: true` — **fail on the old code** (verified by reverting the predicate)
- bare `litellm` → `ok: false`, `reason: 'unknown_provider'`
- `ollama:nomic-embed-text` → `ok: true` (regression pin)
- `isAvailable('embedding')` → `true` for the named litellm/llama-server models (pins the keyword-only cascade)

Verification run locally:
- `bun run typecheck` → clean
- 82 pass / 0 fail across `embed-preflight`, `ai/gateway`, `gateway-embed-model-override`, `openai-compat-multimodal`, `recipe-llama-server`, `no-batch-cap-suppression`
- Reverting the one-line predicate flips exactly the 3 fix-pinning tests to fail — confirming they pin the bug, not just rubber-stamp the current code

## Issue references

Addresses #1716 and the #1812 / #2028 keyword-only-search cascade. The original wave also listed #2295, #2204, #1740, #1672, #1674, #2187 — I verified the **code path**, not each issue's text. Any issue specifically about **Ollama** is NOT addressed here (Ollama already worked), so I've deliberately avoided auto-close keywords; please confirm per-issue before closing.

title: v0.42.54.0 feat(ai): local-provider custom embedding dims + broaden Ollama catalog (#2170 #2271 #2051)
body:
## What & why

Local embedding via Ollama couldn't be initialized with 1024-dim models (`bge-m3`, `mxbai-embed-large`) — the most common modern local-embedder setup. `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:bge-m3 --embedding-dimensions 1024` exited 1 at preflight.

While verifying the root cause I found **the bug is bigger than the tickets**: it's not Ollama-specific. Running the pure resolver (`resolveSchemaEmbeddingDim`) confirms **all three local providers** are broken at init for any explicit dimension:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama:bge-m3 @ 1024` | ❌ rejected | ✅ |
| `ollama:mxbai-embed-large @ 1024` (already in the recipe!) | ❌ rejected | ✅ |
| `ollama:nomic-embed-text @ 768` (default) | ✅ | ✅ |
| `llama-server:my-model @ 1024` | ❌ rejected | ✅ |
| `litellm:some-model @ 1024` | ❌ rejected | ✅ |

## Root cause (verified)

`src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts:isCustomDimValidForProvider` validates a non-default requested dim through tiers: recipe `dims_options` → provider branches for **only** voyage/zeroentropy/openai → a blanket "does not support custom dimensions" reject. Every local provider falls through to that final reject.

A second correctness fact: for `openai-compatible` providers like Ollama, gbrain sends **no** `dimensions` param (`dims.ts:dimsProviderOptions`), so Ollama returns each model's **native** dim and cannot truncate. The schema's `vector(N)` column must therefore equal the model's true native dim exactly — which is why a per-model native-dim map is a *correctness* requirement, not a nicety.

## Changes (4 files, no migration)

- **`src/core/ai/dims.ts`** — `OLLAMA_NATIVE_DIMS` (verified against ollama.com/library: nomic 768, mxbai 1024, all-minilm 384, bge-m3 1024, snowflake-arctic-embed2 1024), `ollamaNativeDim()`, and `isLocalUserProvidedDims(recipe)` (ollama by id + llama-server/litellm via the existing `user_provided_models` flag).
- **`src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts`** — new local-provider branch before the final reject: trusts the explicit dim (the running backend is authoritative), but for *known* Ollama models rejects a contradicting dim with a paste-ready fix (since Ollama can't truncate).

- **`src/commands/init.ts`** — a verbose Ollama model picked **without** `--embedding-dimensions` now infers its native dim instead of the nomic-anchored 768 default. Closes a silent wrong-width footgun the preflight alone can't catch (when the derived dim equals `default_dims`, the custom-dim check is bypassed).
- Docs: `docs/integrations/embedding-providers.md` Ollama section updated for the new models + dim behavior.

## Scope decision

The `isLocalUserProvidedDims` helper is the honest predicate, so it fixes llama-server + litellm at init in the same stroke. This is **partial progress on #2176 / #2337** (their dim-init portion) — not full closure (those may also cover probe/model-list/multimodal work).

## Testing

Levenshtein`) hit a `beforeEach/afterEach` **hook timeout** (5002ms, "killed 1 dangling process"). title: fix(gateway): reliable tool-loop resume + Date-safe tool output on non-Anthropic providers (#2256 #2273 #2110 #2433)
body:
## Why

On non-Anthropic providers (Gemini / DeepSeek / openai-compat) the agentic subagent loop (`agent.use_gateway_loop=true`) is unusable across multi-turn tool conversations: after a crash+resume it rebuilds an unbalanced history ("Tool results are missing" / "messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema"), and any tool whose output contains a Postgres `Date` crashes the loop. These are the core reasons non-Anthropic agent loops don't work today.

## Root causes & fixes

**A — tool-result turn never persisted.** `toolLoop` built the tool-result user message but did `void userMessageIdx` — pushing it in-memory only. Only assistant turns were persisted, so resume rebuilt assistant `tool_use` blocks with no following `tool_result` turn → unbalanced → next `chat()` rejects.
→ Added `onToolResultMessage` to `ToolLoopOpts`, awaited **before** the in-memory push (mirroring `onAssistantTurn`'s persist-before-proceed ordering), and wired it in `runSubagentViaGateway` to persist the `role:'user'` tool-result turn to `subagent_messages`.

**B — mid-execution crash leaves a dangling tool_use.** A worker killed mid-tool-round persists the assistant `tool_use` turn (it fires before dispatch) but not the tool-result wrapper — the outputs live only in `subagent_tool_executions`. The existing crash-replay tests **stub `chat()`** and so never validated that the rebuilt history is balanced; against a real provider it still rejected the dangling `tool_use`.
→ On resume, synthesize the tool-result user turn from the **settled** executions so the rebuilt history is balanced before the first `chat()`. Done **subagent-side** (reads `output`/`error` directly) so it is **v1- and v2-safe**: a loop-side re-dispatch would mis-key v1 legacy rows (`ordinal=NULL` misses the `ON CONFLICT` key) and re-execute a completed tool. A still-`pending` tool (crashed mid-`execute`) is surfaced as unrecoverable rather than re-run or fabricated.

**C — `Date` in tool output.** `toModelMessages` emitted a tool output object straight into a `{ type:'json', value }` AI-SDK part; a `Date` survived as a `Date` instance and failed AI-SDK v6 `JSONValue` validation.
→ Round-trip the `json` arm through `toJsonSafe` (`Date` → ISO string). Serialization fix at the SDK boundary — **not** a `::jsonb` DB cast.

## Tests

The transport-stubbed suite missed all three bugs, so the new tests are written to actually catch them (each was confirmed to fail without its fix):

- `test/ai/gateway-tool-loop.test.ts` — multi-turn run asserting `onToolResultMessage` fires once per tool round with contiguous interleaved `message_idx`, then rebuilds the conversation and asserts it is **balanced** (every assistant tool-call turn is followed by its matching tool-result turn).
- `test/e2e/subagent-crash-replay-multi-provider.test.ts` — captures the **actual messages** handed to `chat()` on resume and asserts they're balanced (`toModelMessages` projects cleanly, no dangling `tool_use`), the synthesized turn is persisted durably, and a still-pending non-idempotent trailing tool surfaces as unrecoverable.
- `test/gateway-model-messages.test.ts` — a `Date` (and nested `{ts: Date}`) tool output yields a JSON-safe value (no `Date` instance survives; ISO string present).

## Scope

No schema change — reuses `subagent_messages` + `persistMessage` (binds via `$N::text::jsonb`, CLAUDE.md-compliant). Engine parity unaffected. No version/CHANGELOG bump (left to the maintainer's release wave).

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- subagent-direct tests (7 files incl. crash-replay e2e): 89 pass / 0 fail
- gateway-direct tests (4 files): 43 pass / 0 fail
- negative check: both new e2e tests fail with the fix disabled (genuine guards)
- guards pass: `check:jsonb`, `check:gateway-routed`, `check:test-names`, `check:privacy`, `check:test-isolation`, `check:proposal-pii`

Fixes #2256, #2273, #2110, #2433. Refs #2115, #2202.

fix(postgres): persist checkpoint completed_keys as jsonb array
body:
Summary:
- Fixes native Postgres checkpoint writes in `recordCompleted()`.
- Binds checkpoint keys as `text[]` and converts server-side with `to_jsonb($3::text[])`.
- Avoids JSON-stringified arrays being persisted as JSONB strings through the postgres.js unsafe/direct path.

- Replace `$3::jsonb` + `JSON.stringify(sorted)` with `to_jsonb($3::text[])` + sorted string array.
- Keeps deterministic sorting and replace/upsert semantics.

title: feat(extract): recognize inline [Source: ..., YYYY-MM-DD] citations as timeline entries
body:
## Why

gbrain's own quality conventions (`skills/conventions/quality.md`) require a dated `[Source: ..., YYYY-MM-DD]` citation on every brain write — so curated pages are full of dated evidence. But `extractTimelineFromContent` only recognizes two formats (timeline bullets and date headers), neither of which is the citation format the product itself mandates.

The result on a real brain: pages that follow the citation convention rigorously still score **zero timeline coverage** in `brain_score`, and `gbrain doctor` penalizes exactly the users who followed the rules. On my brain: 448 of 622 curated pages have dated citations but no recognized timeline format — timeline component stuck at 1/15.

## What

**Format 3** in `extractTimelineFromContent`: one timeline entry per inline citation.

- `date` + `source` come from the citation marker; commas inside the source are preserved (lazy match anchored on `, YYYY-MM-DD]`).
- `summary` is the line the citation annotates, with citation markers and list prefixes stripped, whitespace collapsed, capped at 300 chars.
- Lines already captured by Format 1 are skipped — a timeline bullet usually carries its own citation, and re-extracting it would file a duplicate under a different (source, summary) shape that DB-level uniqueness can't collapse.
- Bare citations with no surrounding text are ignored (a citation without context is not an event).
- Citations without a date are ignored (unchanged behavior for legacy `[Source: X]` markers).

Idempotency unchanged: persistence already dedupes at the DB layer (ON CONFLICT), same as Formats 1/2.

## Tests

7 new cases in `test/extract.test.ts` (simple citation, commas in source, multiple citations per line, no double-extraction from Format 1 bullets, bare citation, undated citation, list-marker stripping). `bun test test/extract.test.ts` 28 pass / 0 fail; `tsc --noEmit` clean; `test/extract-db.test.ts` 12 pass.

title: feat(embedding): Qwen3-Embedding Matryoshka dims on local openai-compat providers (ollama)
body:
## Problem

Local Matryoshka embedding is currently impossible. Every provider on the custom-dims allow-list (`voyage`, `zeroentropyai`, `openai` text-embedding-3, DashScope, Zhipu) is cloud-hosted, so:

1. `gbrain init --embedding-model ollama:qwen3-embedding:8b --embedding-dimensions 1536` is rejected at preflight with *"does not support custom dimensions"* (Tier 3 of `isCustomDimValidForProvider`), and
2. even past init, `dimsProviderOptions()` never emits the `dimensions` param for unlisted openai-compat models, so the server returns the model's native width (4096 for Qwen3-8B) and the first write explodes against the `vector(1536)` column.

For local-only / data-sovereignty setups that need to stay under pgvector's 2000-dim HNSW cap, there is no stock path — even though Qwen3-Embedding is MRL-capable and tops the MTEB multilingual leaderboard.

## Change (2 seams, mirrors the existing dashscope/zhipu pattern)

- **`src/core/ai/recipes/ollama.ts`** — list the `qwen3-embedding` models and declare `dims_options` so preflight accepts MRL steps (Tier 1).
- **`src/core/ai/dims.ts`** — emit `{ openaiCompatible: { dimensions } }` for `qwen3-embedding*` model ids. Qwen3 embeddings are symmetric, so no `input_type` is emitted.

## Verification

Ollama honors the OpenAI `dimensions` param for MRL models — measured on Ollama 0.31.1: `POST /v1/embeddings` and `POST /api/embed` with `qwen3-embedding:8b` + `dimensions: 1536` both return 1536-wide vectors.

End-to-end on a fresh PGLite brain (`init --embedding-model ollama:qwen3-embedding:8b-fp16 --embedding-dimensions 1536`): doctor reports `1536 dims, DB aligned`, 100% embed coverage, and semantic `query` retrieves a page sharing zero keywords with the query text.

## Tests

`test/ai/dims-qwen3-ollama.test.ts` pins both seams: dimensions emission (incl. quant-suffix tags), no `input_type` leakage, preflight acceptance at 1536, rejection outside `dims_options`, and the `nomic-embed-text` no-param regression. Existing dims/recipe/regression suites pass (`dims-openai`, `dims-zeroentropy`, `recipes-existing-regression`, `embedding-dim-check`: 80 tests, 0 fail).

title: gbrain files list crashes when Postgres returns size_bytes as bigint
body:
## Summary

`gbrain files list` can crash on Postgres-backed brains because `files.size_bytes` is returned as a JavaScript `bigint`, but the CLI divides it by the numeric literal `1024`.

This throws:

```text
Invalid mix of BigInt and other type in division
```

## Repro

On a Postgres-backed GBrain with rows in the `files` table:

```bash
gbrain files list
```

or:

```bash
gbrain files list <page-slug>
```

## Root cause

In `src/commands/files.ts`, `listFiles()` assumes `row.size_bytes` is a `number | null`:

```ts
const sizeBytes = row.size_bytes as number | null;
const size = sizeBytes ? `${Math.round(sizeBytes / 1024)}KB` : '?';
```

With Postgres, `size_bytes` may arrive as `bigint`. Dividing a `bigint` by the number literal `1024` throws at runtime.

## Suggested fix

Normalize the DB value before formatting:

```ts
const rawSizeBytes = row.size_bytes as number | bigint | string | null;
const sizeBytes = rawSizeBytes == null ? null : Number(rawSizeBytes);
const size = sizeBytes == null || !Number.isFinite(sizeBytes) ? '?' : `${Math.round(sizeBytes / 1024)}KB`;
```

This also handles `0` correctly as `0KB` instead of treating it as falsy and printing `?`.

## Local verification

After applying the above fix on a Postgres-backed host:

```bash
gbrain files list
```

returned:

```text
37 file(s):
...
```

and:

```bash
gbrain files list products/gbrain
```

returned cleanly:

```text
No files for page: products/gbrain
```

## Related

This is related in theme to #2450, but it is a separate crash site: this one is arithmetic in `files list`, not JSON serialization.

title: v0.42.56.0 feat(chronicle): Life Chronicle — temporal timeline + thought diary + bi-temporal per-entity ontology (#2390)
body:
## Life Chronicle (#2390, closes duplicate #2388)

gbrain gains a **temporal spine**. Meetings/transcripts project into a queryable timeline, entities carry a **bi-temporal ontology** (sourced, confidence-weighted properties that supersede over time), and a low-friction diary captures interiority — so an agent can reconstruct "what happened the week of X", answer "when did I last interact with Y", and see how an entity's role/stance changed, instead of re-deriving chronology from scratch every session.

Built entirely on existing primitives (pages, the `facts` table, `timeline_entries`) — **no new datastore**. Auto-emission is OFF by default.

### What shipped (16 commits, bisect-friendly)
- **Timeline object:** `type:event`/`type:diary` page types; an `event_page_id` projection (migration v121) with intra-day ordering, read-time hiding of deleted events, source isolation; reads `gbrain day [--week] [--narrative]` / `since [--kind]` / `last-seen` / `on-this-day`.
- **Auto-emit extractor:** put_page backstop (gated on `status=imported` + trust + `auto_chronicle`) → `chronicle_extract` minion job with an all-or-nothing LLM-JSON parse barrier + idempotent writes.
- **Bi-temporal ontology on `facts`** (migration v122: `dimension`/`value`/`value_hash`/`dim_status`): `mergeOntologyFact` (deterministic dedup, forward-supersession via `valid_until`/`superseded_by`, `--asof` valid-time travel, novel-dimension quarantine); ops `ontology` / `ontology-add` / `ontology-dimensions` / `ontology-contradictions`.
- **Capture, orient, backfill, delight, advisor:** `gbrain capture --type event/diary`, `gbrain orient` (zero-LLM agent context loader), `gbrain chronicle-backfill`, on-this-day/narrative, and a proactive advisor collector (conflicts + coverage gaps).
- **E1 ambient recall:** a bounded, intent-gated chronicle-type boost in `hybridSearch` — no-op on non-temporal queries (proven by the search suite).

### Security
Diary content + diary-sourced ontology are redacted from untrusted (remote/MCP) readers across reads, search, advisor, and orientation. Auto-emission runs only for trusted local writes.

### Proof
`gbrain eval chronicle` — a deterministic, CI-safe feature eval (synthetic month corpus + planted supersession/conflict) scoring day-order, last-seen, supersession, `--asof` time-travel, contradiction surfacing, and source isolation: **6/6**.

### Review provenance
- **CEO review** (Scope Expansion): approach C (bi-temporal), 4 expansions accepted.
- **Eng review** (CLEAR): reversed two same-session decisions after cross-model consensus — ontology **extends `facts`** (not a parallel table), stored **relationally** (not JSONB).
- **Codex outside voice** ran 3 rounds; the final pre-landing pass caught 3 real bugs (conflict `valid_until` filter, parse-barrier date validation, remote conflict redaction) — all fixed with regression tests in `d1bd5f9d`.

### Tests
Typecheck clean; ~50 new chronicle tests; 265 diff-touched tests green post-merge/post-fix; migrations v120–v122 apply on both engines. The full unit suite is completing as corroboration.

### Upgrade
`gbrain upgrade` → `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`. Enable auto-emit with `gbrain config set auto_chronicle true`, then `gbrain chronicle-backfill`. Manual capture + all reads work immediately.

title: Forward-reference bootstrap missing `timeline_entries.event_page_id` — pre-v121 Postgres/PGLite brains wedge on upgrade to v0.42.x
body:
## Symptoms

Upgrading a pre-v121 brain (schema `config.version < 121`) to v0.42.x wedges with `column "event_page_id" does not exist` before any migration runs. Same class as #695, #755, #682, #741, #1115 — `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` is missing a probe for v121's `timeline_entries.event_page_id`, so `SCHEMA_SQL` / `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` replay aborts on the index that forward-references the column.

Actual failure output from `gbrain upgrade` (0.32.0 → 0.42.56.0, bun-link install, Supabase Postgres backend):

```
⚠️  Schema version 50 is behind latest 122.
   Schema migrations run automatically on next connectEngine() / initSchema().
   To run them now: gbrain init --migrate-only

=== Applying migration v0.11.0: GBrain Minions — durable background agents ===
  Pre-v0.21 brain detected, applying forward-reference bootstrap
Phase A (schema) failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist. Aborting; re-run after fixing.
Migration v0.11.0 reported status=failed.
```

Once aborted, `runMigrations()` never gets to v121 (which adds `event_page_id` via `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`), so every subsequent `gbrain` invocation hits the same failure. `gbrain doctor` post-upgrade drops to `0/100` and exits 1 with the same `column "event_page_id" does not exist` error.

## Affected versions

Any brain with `schema_version < 121` upgrading to a binary at v0.42.x+ (v121 shipped in the Life Chronicle feature, #2390, v0.42.56.0). Both engines are affected — the same forward-referencing index appears in both `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` and `SCHEMA_SQL`.

In my case: 2026-05-11-vintage Supabase brain, 326 pages, `config.version=50`, upgraded from gbrain 0.32.0 → 0.42.56.0 via `git pull --ff-only && bun install` (bun-link source clone install).

## Root cause

At `origin/master` @ 6461790:

1. **Migration v121** (`src/core/migrate.ts:5443`, `timeline_entries_event_page_id`) is idempotent and guarded — it correctly adds the column via `ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER`, plus the FK and two indexes. That part is fine.

2. **`SCHEMA_SQL`** (`src/core/schema-embedded.ts:561-562`) and **`PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL`** (`src/core/pglite-schema.ts:387-388`) also declare the two forward-referencing indexes on `timeline_entries(event_page_id)`. On brains where the `timeline_entries` table already exists (which is every brain with `schema_version >= 12` or so), the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timeline_entries (…)` is a no-op — the new `event_page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` column is NOT minted — and then `CREATE INDEX … ON timeline_entries(event_page_id)` aborts.

3. **`applyForwardReferenceBootstrap`** in `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:389` and `src/core/pglite-engine.ts:418` runs before schema replay for exactly this scenario. But its probe list (`postgres-engine.ts:~580-607`) does not include `timeline_entries.event_page_id`, so on a pre-v121 brain, all its `needs*` flags are false, the short-circuit at line 607 returns, and the schema replay crashes.

Verified against my Supabase brain:

```sql
SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='timeline_entries';
-- id, page_id, date, source, summary, detail, created_at   (7 rows, no event_page_id)

SELECT key, value FROM config WHERE key='version';
-- version=50
```

## Repro

```bash
# On any brain with config.version < 121 (Postgres or PGLite):
gbrain init --migrate-only
# → column "event_page_id" does not exist
gbrain apply-migrations --yes
# → same failure looped through v0.11.0 orchestrator's Phase A
```

## Suggested fix

Mirror the pattern established by #695, #755, #682, #741. Three edits per engine (Postgres and PGLite), following the existing bootstrap conventions:

1. **Probe.** Extend the round-trip EXISTS check with `timeline_entries_event_page_id_exists` in `probeCr`.

2. **Bootstrap injection.** Add a `needsTimelineEventPageId` branch to the `if (…)` chain and to the short-circuit guard, injecting:
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER
     REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
   ```
   Only the column itself is strictly required by the SCHEMA_SQL indexes on lines 561-562. Migration v121 remains idempotent and completes the FK constraint + indexes properly in its own phase.

3. **Pin in CI.** Extend `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_COVERAGE` in `test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts`:
   ```ts
   // v0.42.x (v121) — forward-referenced by
   //   CREATE INDEX idx_timeline_event_page ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) …
   //   CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_timeline_event_dedup ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) …
   { kind: 'column', table: 'timeline_entries', column: 'event_page_id' },
   ```
   Strip-block extended accordingly so the test exercises the new branch.

## Downstream note (separate issue, mentioning for context)

Immediately after the bootstrap gap surfaces, `gbrain doctor` also flags a `facts.embedding` dimension mismatch — the column is `halfvec(1536)` on a pre-v0.37 brain but the v0.42.x default embedding model is `zeroentropyai:zembed-1` (1280 dims). Doctor's remediation SQL is helpful but requires a maintenance window (nulls all fact embeddings + rebuilds the HNSW index). Flagging in case the two problems co-occur enough to warrant a combined upgrade note in `docs/embedding-migrations.md`.

## Workaround for affected operators

Back up the brain (Supabase: pg_dump; PGLite: `cp -r ~/.gbrain/brain.pglite ~/.gbrain/brain.pglite.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)`), then pre-create the column manually:

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER
  REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
```

Then re-run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`. Migration v121's `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op, its FK add and index create idempotently succeed, and the chain proceeds.

Note that this workaround only unblocks this specific column; anything else v121-v122 adds that's forward-referenced will need the same treatment until the bootstrap gets extended.

title: recordCompleted() double-encodes completed_keys as jsonb string on Postgres, breaking checkpoint resume (sync-target, extract-conversation-facts)
body:
## Summary

`recordCompleted()` in `src/core/op-checkpoint.ts` writes `completed_keys` as a **JSONB scalar string** instead of a JSONB array, on Postgres (not PGLite). This breaks checkpoint resume for every op that uses `recordCompleted` (observed: `sync-target` pin write in `sync.ts`, and `extract-conversation-facts`), forcing full-corpus replays on every run instead of incremental resume — which in turn re-overwrites hand-edited/curated pages with stale synthesized content on every sync cycle.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/core/op-checkpoint.ts, recordCompleted()
const sorted = [...keys].sort();
return durableWrite(engine, key, 'write', () =>
  engine.executeRawDirect(
    `INSERT INTO op_checkpoints (op, fingerprint, completed_keys, updated_at)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, now())
     ON CONFLICT (op, fingerprint) DO UPDATE
       SET completed_keys = EXCLUDED.completed_keys,
           updated_at     = now()`,
    [key.op, key.fingerprint, JSON.stringify(sorted)],  // <-- bug
  ));
```

Binding `JSON.stringify(sorted)` (a JS **string**) to a `$N::jsonb` parameter through `postgres.js`'s `.unsafe(sql, params)` double-encodes: the driver serializes the already-JSON-text string again before Postgres applies the `::jsonb` cast, so the column ends up holding a jsonb **scalar string** containing the JSON text, not a jsonb array.

This is exactly the double-encode class the project already guards against in `sqlQueryForEngine`/`executeRawJsonb` and `scripts/check-jsonb-pattern.sh` — but the CI guard only pattern-matches the tagged-template-literal form (`` `${JSON.stringify(...)}::jsonb` ``), so it doesn't catch this parameterized-bind form, and this call site slipped through.

Downstream, `loadOpCheckpoint()`'s `jsonb_array_elements_text(completed_keys)` then throws on the scalar value:

```
[op-checkpoint] load failed (sync-target, <fingerprint>): cannot extract elements from a scalar
```

`loadOpCheckpoint` swallows this (returns `[]`, logs to stderr), so the op silently believes nothing is done yet and re-walks everything. For `sync`'s ~15-18k file repos, that means every single run does a full replay instead of an incremental resume — and since sync re-imports/re-synthesizes pages from source material, it clobbers any manually-curated edits to those pages made between runs.

## Reproduction (isolated, against real Postgres — not PGLite)

```js
import postgres from 'postgres';
const sql = postgres(DATABASE_URL, { max: 1 });

// Pattern A — current gbrain code
await sql.unsafe(
  `INSERT INTO op_checkpoints (op, fingerprint, completed_keys, updated_at)
   VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, now())
   ON CONFLICT (op, fingerprint) DO UPDATE SET completed_keys = EXCLUDED.completed_keys, updated_at = now()`,
  ['repro-op', 'a', JSON.stringify(['hash1', 'hash2'])]
);

// Pattern B — fix: bind the raw array, no JSON.stringify
await sql.unsafe(
  `INSERT INTO op_checkpoints (op, fingerprint, completed_keys, updated_at)
   VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, now())
   ON CONFLICT (op, fingerprint) DO UPDATE SET completed_keys = EXCLUDED.completed_keys, updated_at = now()`,
  ['repro-op', 'b', ['hash1', 'hash2']]
);

const rows = await sql.unsafe(
  `SELECT fingerprint, jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) AS typ, completed_keys::text AS val
   FROM op_checkpoints WHERE op = 'repro-op' ORDER BY fingerprint`
);
console.log(rows);
```

Output:

```json
[
  { "fingerprint": "a", "typ": "string", "val": "\"[\\\"hash1\\\",\\\"hash2\\\"]\"" },
  { "fingerprint": "b", "typ": "array",  "val": "[\"hash1\", \"hash2\"]" }
]
```

`postgres@3.4.x`, confirmed on gbrain v0.42.37.0 (latest at time of filing).

## Fix

One-line change — bind the raw array, don't pre-stringify:

```diff
- [key.op, key.fingerprint, JSON.stringify(sorted)],
+ [key.op, key.fingerprint, sorted],
```

Verified this produces `jsonb_typeof = 'array'` and that `gbrain sync` correctly resumes from checkpoint afterward (`resuming checkpoint: N file(s) already done; draining ...` instead of a full replay).

## Suggested follow-ups

1. Apply the same one-line fix to `recordCompleted` (affects every caller: `extract.ts`, `sync.ts`'s target-pin write, `enrich.ts`, `extract-conversation-facts.ts`).
2. Extend `scripts/check-jsonb-pattern.sh` to also catch the parameterized form (`JSON.stringify(...)` appearing as a bound parameter value where the corresponding `$N` position in the SQL string is cast `::jsonb`), not just the tagged-template interpolation form. The current regex (`\$\{JSON\.stringify\([^)]*\)\}::jsonb`) can't see this shape at all since there's no `${...}` interpolation in the query string itself.
3. Consider a schema-level backstop (e.g. a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger or a `CHECK (jsonb_typeof(completed_keys) = 'array')` constraint on `op_checkpoints`) so a future regression of this class fails loudly at write time instead of silently degrading resume behavior.

Happy to open a PR with the one-line fix + a regression test if useful.

title: fix(schema): bootstrap timeline_entries.event_page_id (v121) forward-reference
body:
## Problem

`applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` (both engines) pre-creates columns that the embedded schema blob (`SCHEMA_SQL` / `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL`) forward-references but that older brains lack — it covers ~20 such columns. **It's missing the v121 entry.**

`SCHEMA_SQL` has:
```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
```
but `timeline_entries.event_page_id` is only added by **migration v121** (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`).

On a brain whose `timeline_entries` predates v121, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op (the column is never added), so the schema-blob's `CREATE INDEX` throws **`column "event_page_id" does not exist`** during `initSchema()` — *before* `runMigrations()` can apply v121. Result: both `gbrain init --migrate-only` and `gbrain apply-migrations` wedge, the schema version stays behind (e.g. stuck at 120), and every query prints `Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist`.

This is the exact wedge class the `schema-bootstrap-coverage` guard was built to prevent (incidents #239/#243/#266/#357/#366/#374/#375/#378/#395/#396). It slipped through because the static A2 check treats a column present in the current `CREATE TABLE` body as covered — which is true for *fresh* installs but not for *upgrade* brains where the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` no-ops — and `event_page_id` was never added to `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_COVERAGE` nor stripped by the runtime tests.

### Observed live
A Postgres brain upgraded across the v121 boundary (image rebuild pulled a newer gbrain). `gbrain query` degraded to keyword-only with the schema-probe warning; `init --migrate-only` and `apply-migrations` both failed identically on `event_page_id`. Manually `ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER` then `init --migrate-only` recovered it (v121+v122 applied cleanly) — i.e. exactly what the missing bootstrap should have done.

## Fix

- **`postgres-engine.ts` + `pglite-engine.ts`**: probe `timeline_entries.event_page_id` and, when the table exists without it, `ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER` before the schema-blob replay. The guarded FK + partial indexes still land via the blob (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`) and the idempotent v121 migration — bootstrap only unblocks the replay, mirroring every other entry (e.g. v112 `links_extracted_at`).
- **`schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts`**: add the `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_COVERAGE` entry and strip `event_page_id` + its indexes/FK in both runtime tests so the wedge is reproduced and guarded going forward.

## Verification (local, bun 1.3.10)

- `bun test test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts` → **9 pass / 0 fail** (migration chain applies v121→v122; bootstrap runs).
- **Negative check** — disabling the new bootstrap block reproduces the failure: the coverage assertion fails **and** `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL` replay throws `column "event_page_id" does not exist`. Restoring the block makes it green again. So the test genuinely guards this regression.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for the edited files.

Additive + idempotent; no-op on fresh installs and on brains already at/after v121.

title: fix(cli): route shared ops to a live local serve daemon instead of dying on the PGLite lock
body:
## Problem

On a local PGLite install with `gbrain serve --http` running as a daemon (launchd/systemd), every shared CLI op (`search`, `query`, ...) goes `connectEngine()` → `acquireLock()` and times out after 30s with **"GBrain: Timed out waiting for PGLite lock"** — while the daemon is serving the same brain over loopback HTTP the whole time. MCP clients work; the CLI is dead on the host.

## Fix

New `src/core/local-daemon.ts` + a routing seam in `cli.ts` right before the local-engine connect:

- **Detection** reads the existing lock file (`<dataDir>/.gbrain-lock/lock`): live pid + `serve --http` argv + `--port N` (default 3131). Dead/corrupt/non-HTTP holders fall through to the unchanged local path.
- **Health** is confirmed with a loopback `GET /health` (1.5s cap) before routing.
- **Auth** is a raw bearer token — `GBRAIN_REMOTE_TOKEN` env, else `<gbrain home>/agents.token` — using the raw-bearer StreamableHTTP pattern from `connect-probe.ts` (`callRemoteTool` is OAuth-only). No token → immediate actionable error instead of the doomed 30s lock wait.
- **Rendering** goes through the same `unpackToolResult` + `formatResult` pair as the thin-client path — renderer parity by data shape. Timeout policy matches ENG-4 (180s `think`, 30s otherwise, `--timeout` wins). SIGINT aborts in-flight HTTP with exit 130.
- `localOnly` ops fall through unchanged: the server hides them, and the existing lock-timeout message already names the daemon pid to stop.

## Testing

- `test/local-daemon.test.ts` — 16 tests pinning holder classification (dead pid, stdio serve, embed, corrupt lock → all null), port parsing, and token precedence.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `cli-args` / `connect` / `thin-client-routing-audit` suites pass (139 tests).
- Live: with a launchd daemon holding the lock, `gbrain search` / `gbrain query` return results in ~1s (previously 30s timeout), TTY banner `[local-daemon → 127.0.0.1:3131 · pid N]` shows the route.
