title: fix(graph,autopilot): exclude connector-metadata frontmatter from link extraction; skip freshness sync for absent local_path
body:
## Summary
Two production incidents, one PR (PR-B2 of the 2026-07 gbrain remediation plan).

### FIX 3 — kill the junk `source:` edges
`FRONTMATTER_LINK_MAP` in `src/core/link-extraction.ts` had a generic
`{ fields: ['source'], type: 'source', dirHint: '' }` mapping. Connectors
(Salesforce/Paligo/Responsive) stamp `source: company` provenance frontmatter on
every ingested page, so this mapping turned each one into a fuzzy pg_trgm
title-resolved `source` edge — collapsing **40,310 pages onto a single page
titled "Company name"** in production.

Fix:
- Remove the generic `source` mapping from `FRONTMATTER_LINK_MAP`.
- Add an exported `CONNECTOR_METADATA_KEYS` set (`source`, `scope`, `origin`,
  `origin_source`) checked inside `extractFrontmatterLinks` **before** the field
  map, so no future pack-authored mapping for those keys can reintroduce the
  storm.

Not affected: the editorial plural `sources:` field (→ `discussed_in`),
`related`/`see_also` (→ `related_to`), and all page-typed pack mappings. The
active packs (`gbrain-bravura`, `gbrain-personal`) declare **no** `source` field
mapping, so no pack user regresses. Slug-shaped provenance still lives in the
pages table's `source` column — it does not need to be a graph edge.

### FIX 2 — autopilot freshness dead-job storm
The per-source freshness loop in `src/commands/autopilot.ts` guarded only
`!src.local_path`. A source whose clone lives on another pod (source
`bart-allan`) named a `local_path` that doesn't exist on this pod, so the loop
submitted a `sync` job every tick that could only fail — **~288 dead jobs/day**
in prod.

Fix: skip the source when `!existsSync(src.local_path)` **or** the source is
flagged `config.externally_synced === true` (a JSONB config key on the existing
`sources.config` — no new registry schema). The skip logs **once per source**
via a module-level `Set` (`freshnessSkipLogged`) rather than spamming per tick.

## Tests
- `test/link-extraction.test.ts` — updated 3 tests that asserted the old
  `source`-edge behavior to assert suppression; added coverage that all
  `CONNECTOR_METADATA_KEYS` produce zero edges and that editorial `sources:`
  still emits `discussed_in`. **128 pass.**
- `test/autopilot-freshness-wiring.test.ts` (new) — source-shape wiring guards
  matching the `autopilot-*-wiring.test.ts` pattern: existsSync guard +
  short-circuit, `externally_synced` opt-out, once-per-source dedup Set, skip
  ordered before `queue.add`. **5 pass.**
- Related suites (frontmatter-inference, pack link-inference, extract-fs,
  autopilot cycle/fanout/nightly-probe/auto-drain) green. `tsc --noEmit` clean
  for changed files.

title: import: seeding a brain from AI chat exports (ChatGPT/Claude) via memvelope envelopes
body:
every new gbrain starts empty - and the densest personal corpus most people have is years of AI chat history locked in per-vendor export formats. we run gbrain in production and hit this on day one: the cold-start problem isn't building the brain, it's filling it.

we built an open MIT standard for the export side (memvelope - one portable JSON envelope any chat export converts into; gbrain was the biggest influence on how we think about portable memory, credited in the spec) and a reference importer that maps an envelope into gbrain's markdown-brain-repo model: one page per conversation, provenance frontmatter, message-id citations, `type: conversation`.

live-verified against upstream v0.42.56.0: a real 662MB Claude export -> 353 conversations -> 353 distinct pages, keyword-searchable, provenance and citations intact. deterministic, zero deps, no network.

PR follows with the importer adapted to this repo's conventions plus a self-contained test. no behavior change to any existing path. happy to maintain it.

title: dream/synthesize: dream_generated provenance is render-time only — generated pages are unqueryable in DB, can leak during runs, and put_page writes erase it
body:
## What problem does this solve?

`dream_generated: true` is the identity surface for dream/synthesis output. It is used by the self-consumption guard (`isDreamOutput`, `src/core/cycle/transcript-discovery.ts`) and by generated-output demotion conventions in search/source handling. But on current `master` (`646179047a8e4ad9c462d83ce9a67a50ba076de8`), the stamp is not durable for generated child pages:

1. **DB/file split.** `renderPageToMarkdown()` in `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts` stamps generated child pages via `frontmatterOverrides` only (`dream_generated: true`, `dream_cycle_date`). `serializePageToMarkdown()` then merges `{...page.frontmatter, ...frontmatterOverrides}` at render time (`src/core/markdown.ts`). That gets the marker into the rendered markdown file, but it does not persist the marker into the `pages.frontmatter` JSONB row for those pages. DB-level consumers therefore cannot reliably enumerate generated child pages via `frontmatter->>'dream_generated'`.

2. **Stamp decay on later write-through.** `put_page` write-through in `src/core/operations.ts` re-renders from the saved DB row with only ingestion/source overrides. If the DB row never had `dream_generated`, a later `put_page` write can silently erase the marker from the file.

3. **Reverse-write failures/skips are hard to observe as provenance loss.** The summary page persists its own generated marker into DB, but generated children rely on reverse-write rendering. If a child page is listed in a dream-cycle summary but the reverse-write marker is missing or later erased, downstream systems have no durable membership predicate.

4. **Agent/MCP-driven synthesis has no generated-page identity.** Pages produced by synthesis-driving agents through `put_page` can look like ordinary curated writes (`ingested_via: mcp:put_page`) rather than generated output, even when operationally they are part of a synthesis run.

Measured on one production brain corpus that motivated this report, under `wiki/originals/ideas/`:

- 156 generated/synthesis idea pages inspected
- 68 stamped / **88 unstamped** (`56%` unstamped)
- 67 pages are listed from dream-cycle summaries; **8 of those are unstamped**
- 80 unstamped pages were not listed from the summaries and look like ordinary `put_page` writes

That means generated pages can be impossible to enumerate reliably, and can be treated by retrieval/agents with the same authority as human-authored/curated pages.

## Code references checked against current master

Current `origin/master`: `646179047a8e4ad9c462d83ce9a67a50ba076de8`.

- `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts:1113-1125` — `renderPageToMarkdown()` stamps `dream_generated` / `dream_cycle_date` as `frontmatterOverrides`.
- `src/core/markdown.ts:667-670` — `serializePageToMarkdown()` merges `page.frontmatter` with render-time overrides; this is a render funnel, not a DB write.
- `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts:1157-1165` — the dream summary is different: its marker is passed into `serializeMarkdown()` before parsing/persisting, so the summary marker survives in DB.
- `src/core/operations.ts:909-917` — `put_page` write-through only passes ingestion/source overrides when re-rendering.
- `src/core/cycle/transcript-discovery.ts:57-73, 114-120, 238-240` — the self-consumption guard depends on the frontmatter marker.
- `src/core/search/source-boost.ts:48-53` — generated receipts/search conventions rely on `dream_generated`-style demotion semantics.

## Expected behavior

Generated pages should have durable provenance. A page generated by dream/synthesis should remain identifiable as generated across:

- DB queries
- file render/write-through
- later `put_page` updates
- doctor/MCP/agent consumers
- backfills and summary-link reconciliation

## Possible fix shape

- Persist `dream_generated: true` / `dream_cycle_date` into the DB row frontmatter at generated-page write time, not only during markdown rendering.
- Preserve the stamp on later `put_page` write-throughs.
- Surface reverse-write provenance mismatches in cycle result details and/or a doctor check.
- Add an idempotent backfill path for pages already linked from `dream-cycle-summaries/*` and pages whose markdown files already carry the stamp.

## Alternatives considered

- **Query markdown files instead of DB.** This leaves MCP/doctor/engine consumers blind and does not solve stamp decay on rewrite.
- **Use dream summary links as the only provenance.** Summary links are useful evidence, but they are not a durable identity contract and miss out-of-band/agent-driven synthesis.
- **Do nothing.** The generated-page guard/demotion/review story silently degrades as generated corpora age and pages are rewritten.

Happy to contribute a focused fix and regression tests if this approach sounds right.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generated child pages persist `dream_generated: true` in DB frontmatter as well as rendered markdown.
- `put_page` update of a stamped generated page preserves the stamp in DB and file.
- DB-level generated-page count for a fresh run approximately matches summary-listed generated children, modulo explicit write failures/skips surfaced in the result.
- Backfill is idempotent on both PGLite and Postgres.
- Tests cover the render/write-through decay path.

title: buildGatewayConfig does not map openrouter_api_key into gateway env — chat-based operations fail for file-plane key users
body:
## Summary

`buildGatewayConfig()` in `src/core/ai/build-gateway-config.ts` maps `openai_api_key`, `anthropic_api_key`, and `zeroentropy_api_key` into the gateway environment dict, but **does not map `openrouter_api_key`**. Users who configure their OpenRouter API key in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (file-plane) find it silently dropped.

## Root Cause

Three missing seams:

1. **`GBrainConfig` interface** (`src/core/config.ts`) — no `openrouter_api_key` field to accept the key from file-plane parse
2. **`loadConfig` env overlay** (`src/core/config.ts`) — no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to `openrouter_api_key` merge path
3. **`buildGatewayConfig` mapping** (`src/core/ai/build-gateway-config.ts`) — missing the `c.openrouter_api_key` to `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` line

The OpenRouter recipe declares `auth_env.required: ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']`. When the gateway's `defaultResolveAuth` reads `cfg.env[required[0]]`, it finds `undefined` even though the key exists in `config.json`. The gateway then reports `missing_env` and skips the OpenRouter recipe entirely.

## Symptoms

| Operation | Outcome |
|-----------|---------|
| `gbrain takes extract --from-pages --yes` | Fails with "chat gateway unavailable (no API key configured)" |
| `gbrain dream` propose_takes phase | Runs but produces 0 proposals via chat gateway |
| Embedding via OpenAI recipe | Works (uses OPENAI_API_KEY, which IS mapped) |
| MCP server sessions | Work (inherits real OS env vars) |

## Workaround

Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` as a real OS environment variable (in `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, or the process launcher). This bypasses the file-plane gap because `process.env` is spread into the gateway env dict last.

## Fix

PR: https://github.com/psam-717/gbrain/pull/new/fix/openrouter-api-key-gateway

Adds `openrouter_api_key` to all three seams following the same pattern as `zeroentropy_api_key` (v0.37 fix wave).

2. **`loadConfig` env overlay** (`src/core/config.ts`) — no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to `openrouter_api_key` merge path
3. **`buildGatewayConfig` mapping** (`src/core/ai/build-gateway-config.ts`) — missing the `c.openrouter_api_key` to `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` line

The OpenRouter recipe declares `auth_env.required: ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']`. When the gateway's `defaultResolveAuth` reads `cfg.env[required[0]]`, it finds `undefined` even though the key exists in `config.json`. The gateway then reports `missing_env` and skips the OpenRouter recipe entirely.

## Symptoms

| Operation | Outcome |
|-----------|---------|
| `gbrain takes extract --from-pages --yes` | Fails with "chat gateway unavailable (no API key configured)" |
| `gbrain dream` propose_takes phase | Runs but produces 0 proposals via chat gateway |
| Embedding via OpenAI recipe | Works (uses OPENAI_API_KEY, which IS mapped) |
| MCP server sessions | Work (inherits real OS env vars) |

## Workaround

Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` as a real OS environment variable (in `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, or the process launcher). This bypasses the file-plane gap because `process.env` is spread into the gateway env dict last.

## Fix

PR: https://github.com/psam-717/gbrain/pull/new/fix/openrouter-api-key-gateway

Adds `openrouter_api_key` to all three seams following the same pattern as `zeroentropy_api_key` (v0.37 fix wave).

title: chat: no providerOptions passthrough for openai-compatible providers — hybrid-reasoning models (DeepSeek V4) silently break strict-output ops
body:
## Summary

`ChatOpts` has no way to pass provider-specific request-body params (e.g. DeepSeek's `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`), even though the underlying `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` layer already forwards unknown `providerOptions[<providerName>]` keys into the request body verbatim. For hybrid-reasoning models (DeepSeek V4 family) this makes strict-output ops silently unusable: thinking mode is the API default, the reasoning channel starves `content`, and e.g. `extract-conversation-facts` returns 0 facts across every segment with no error surfaced.

## Repro / evidence

Setup: Postgres brain, `chat_model = deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash` (openai-compatible recipe, `provider_base_urls.deepseek` pointing at an aggregator that serves DeepSeek V4).

1. DeepSeek V4 (`deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro`) defaults to **thinking mode ON** (verified against both api.deepseek.com and a Tencent-MaaS aggregator). `POST /chat/completions` with `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` cleanly disables it on both.
2. In thinking mode, strict-JSON extraction prompts return their tokens in `reasoning_content`; `content` is empty/truncated → `extractFactsFromTurn` parses nothing → `0 facts inserted across N segments` for every page. Same prompt with thinking disabled: 9 good facts on our test window.
3. gbrain cannot send that field today:
   - `ChatOpts` (src/core/ai/gateway.ts ~L2394) only carries `model / system / messages / tools / maxTokens / abortSignal / cacheSystem`.
   - Inside `chat()` the `providerOptions` object passed to `generateText` is local and only ever populated with `providerOptions.anthropic` for `cacheSystem`.
   - No config key feeds per-provider chat params.
4. The plumbing below is already done: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`'s `getArgs` spreads unknown keys from `providerOptions[this.providerOptionsName]` into the request body (only schema-known keys are filtered). So a passthrough would reach the wire with no SDK work.

## Suggested fix (small)

Either:
- add `providerOptions?: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>` to `ChatOpts` and merge it into the local `providerOptions` in `chat()`, or
- a config surface like `models.chat_provider_options.<recipeId> = {...}` merged at the same spot (lets `facts.extraction_model = deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash` run non-thinking without any caller changes).

Workaround we run today: a tiny local proxy in front of the provider that injects `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` for `deepseek-v4*` chat calls. Works, but it's a daemon nobody should need.

## Two sibling blind spots we hit on the same non-Anthropic path (can split into separate issues if preferred)

1. **BudgetTracker TX2 prices only via `ANTHROPIC_PRICING`** (src/core/budget/budget-tracker.ts `lookupPricing`): with `maxCostUsd` set (CLI default, minion jobs, cycle phases), any non-Claude chat model → `no_pricing` hard-throw → absorbed by callers like extract.ts → silent 0-output runs. DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi users can't run budget-capped ops at all. Suggestion: price chat via recipe `cost_per_1m_*` touchpoints (like embeddings already do) before falling back to hard-fail.
2. **`createAnthropic({ apiKey })` ignores `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`** (src/core/ai/gateway.ts native-anthropic branches): users on Anthropic-compatible proxies (common where api.anthropic.com is unreachable) get opaque `Invalid JSON response` on every native-anthropic call. One-liner: pass `baseURL` from env/config when present.

Happy to provide more repro detail or test a branch. Thanks for gbrain — the rest of the stack has been remarkably solid to align with.

title: PGLite upgrade to 0.42.56 fails: baseline schema references event_page_id before migration 121 adds it (bootstrap drift)
body:
## Summary

Upgrading an existing PGLite brain from 0.42.44.0 to 0.42.56.0 (`64617904`) fails during `apply-migrations`: the baseline schema blob now references `timeline_entries(event_page_id)` (partial indexes added by the Life Chronicle release, #2390), but `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` in `src/core/pglite-engine.ts` was not extended to pre-add the column. Fresh installs are unaffected (the embedded schema includes the column), which is likely why it shipped.

## Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon), install via `git clone + bun link`
- Engine: PGLite, existing brain at schema version 117 (created on 0.42.44.0)
- Upgrade: `git pull` 090bb532 → 64617904, `bun install`

## Repro

1. Have a PGLite brain created on ≤0.42.44.0 (schema version 117).
2. Upgrade the checkout to 0.42.56.0 and run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`.

```
=== Applying migration v0.11.0: GBrain Minions — durable background agents ===
Phase A (schema) failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist. Aborting; re-run after fixing.
Migration v0.11.0 reported status=failed.
```

`gbrain doctor` shows the same and its suggested fix (`gbrain apply-migrations --yes`) loops on the identical failure.

## Root cause

`PGLiteEngine.initSchema()` runs in this order:

1. `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` — pre-adds columns the schema blob forward-references on older brains
2. `this.db.exec(getPGLiteSchema(...))` — the baseline blob, which now contains (`src/core/pglite-schema.ts:387-388`):
   ```sql
   CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
   CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
   ```
3. `runMigrations()` — where migration **121** (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`) adds the column

On an existing brain, step 2 executes before step 3 and fails: `IF NOT EXISTS` guards the index name, not the referenced column. The bootstrap's own doc comment states the maintenance contract ("when a future migration adds a column-with-index … referenced by PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL, extend this method AND `test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts`") — migration 121's column was not added to it, and the coverage test evidently didn't catch the drift.

## Workaround (verified)

Pre-add the column using migration 121's own SQL via the engine, then re-run migrations:

```ts
await engine.db.exec(`ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;`);
```

After that, `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` completes cleanly (migration 121 lays down the FK + indexes idempotently) and a second run is a clean no-op.

## Suggested fix

Extend `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` (and `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_COVERAGE`) with `timeline_entries.event_page_id`; possibly also investigate why the coverage test missed it.

🤖 Filed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) from a live debugging session.

title: enrich: 'Chat gateway unavailable' despite valid chat model + key — availability gate runs before gateway configuration (--background path unaffected)
body:
**Version:** 0.42.56.0, Postgres engine. `chat_model = openai:gpt-4o-mini` (confirmed via `gbrain config get chat_model`), `OPENAI_API_KEY` exported in the shell.

**Observed:**
- `gbrain enrich --thin --types person --limit 3 --max-usd 0.25` → exits with `Chat gateway unavailable. Configure a chat model…`
- `gbrain enrich … --dry-run` → works (14 candidates enumerated).
- `gbrain enrich … --background` + `gbrain jobs work` → **all jobs complete successfully** with the same env/config.
- Passing `--model openai:gpt-4o-mini` explicitly does not change the direct-path failure.

**Cause (from reading the source):** the gate at src/commands/enrich.ts (`if (!parsed.dryRun && !isAvailable('chat'))`) runs before the engine/gateway is configured. `isAvailable` (src/core/ai/gateway.ts) returns `false` whenever `_config` is null — `configureGateway()` hasn't been called yet at that point in the direct CLI path — so the check reports "unavailable" regardless of actual config/keys. The jobs worker configures the engine before executing the handler, which is why `--background` succeeds.

**Suggestion:** move the availability gate after engine/gateway initialization (or call `configureGateway` from resolved config + process.env before the gate). The current error message sends users chasing model/key config that is actually fine.

title: v0.42.56.0: embedded schema forward-references timeline_entries.event_page_id (added by migration 121) — initSchema deadlocks on legacy brains, Chronicle unusable
body:
## Summary

Upgrading a **legacy brain** (existing `timeline_entries` table) to **v0.42.56.0** (`6461790`, Life Chronicle #2390) wedges schema migrations in a chicken-and-egg deadlock: the embedded schema forward-references `timeline_entries.event_page_id`, but that column is only added by **schema migration 121** — which runs *after* the schema replay that crashes on the missing column. All Chronicle ops then fail with:

```
column te.event_page_id does not exist
```

Fresh installs are unaffected (they get the full `CREATE TABLE` with the column), which is likely why CI didn't catch it.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.42.56.0 (`6461790`), upgraded from v0.42.53.0 (`814258d`)
- Postgres 17 engine (`GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL`), macOS, bun
- Brain schema_version was 119 before upgrade; `timeline_entries` existed (pre-Chronicle shape)

## Symptom

- `chronicle_since` / `chronicle_day` (MCP + CLI) → `internal_error: column te.event_page_id does not exist`
- serve startup log:
  ```
  Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist
  Re-run: `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`
  ```
- Re-running `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` does **not** help — it reports `All migrations up to date.` (that command tracks the orchestrator/file migrations, not the `migrate.ts` schema migrations), so the suggested remediation is a no-op for this failure.
- `config.version` stays pinned at 119; migrations 120/121/122 never apply, no matter how many restarts.

## Root cause (as of `6461790`)

`PostgresEngine.initSchema()` (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts`) executes in this order:

1. `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap(conn)` — adds columns that the embedded schema forward-references but older brains lack. **Its probe list does not include `timeline_entries.event_page_id`** (it covers `pages.source_id`, `links.link_source`, `content_chunks.*`, `oauth_clients.*`, `sources.*`, etc.).
2. `conn.unsafe(sqlText)` — replays the embedded schema. On a legacy brain, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timeline_entries` is a no-op (table exists without the new column), then:
   ```sql
   CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
   ```
   throws `column "event_page_id" does not exist`, aborting `initSchema`.
3. `runMigrations(this)` — **never reached**, so migration 121 (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`, the one that adds the column) can never run. Deadlock.

Note the post-migration `verifySchema()` self-heal (which exists precisely to fix missing columns) also sits after the failure point, so it can't save the situation either.

The PGLite engine appears to have the same gap by inspection: `src/core/pglite-schema.ts` ships the same two `CREATE INDEX ... (event_page_id)` statements, and `PGLiteEngine#applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` doesn't cover the column. (Only verified live on Postgres.)

Migration 122 (`facts_ontology_dimension`) is *not* affected — `facts` is migration-created and absent from the static schema, exactly the pattern that avoids this class of bug.

## Repro

1. Take any brain at schema_version ≤ 120 (i.e. `timeline_entries` exists without `event_page_id`) on Postgres.
2. Upgrade the repo to `6461790`, restart serve (or run any CLI command that triggers `connectEngine`).
3. Observe `Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist` on every start; `chronicle day/since` ops fail; schema migrations 120–122 never apply.

## Suggested fix

Add `timeline_entries.event_page_id` to `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` in both engines (same guarded `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` pattern as the existing entries, mirroring the doc-comment list), so the schema replay finds the column and `runMigrations` can then record 121 normally (it's already idempotent).

Longer-term, a CI guard that diffs "columns referenced by embedded-schema indexes" against "columns guaranteed by CREATE TABLE ∪ bootstrap list" would catch this whole class — this is at least the second time a new feature's index forward-referenced a migration-added column.

## Workaround (for anyone else hitting this)

Manually apply migration 121's own SQL (additive + idempotent), then restart serve:

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conname = 'timeline_entries_event_page_id_fkey'
       AND conrelid = 'timeline_entries'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE timeline_entries
      ADD CONSTRAINT timeline_entries_event_page_id_fkey
      FOREIGN KEY (event_page_id) REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
  END IF;
END $$;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
```

After restart, `initSchema` completes, migrations 120/121/122 apply and are recorded (121 no-ops cleanly), `config.version` reaches 122, and Chronicle ops work. Verified on the affected brain.

title: Nick/dashboard
get_timeline: engine implements after/before date filtering but the op exposes only slug — window args silently ignored
body:
**Version:** 0.42.56.0 (also current master `6461790`) · **Engine:** Postgres 16 + pgvector · **Runtime:** Bun

## What happens

The `get_timeline` operation exposes only a `slug` parameter. Any date-window arguments a caller passes (`since`/`until` — the names agents naturally reach for, since the sibling `query` op uses them) are silently accepted and dropped: there is no unknown-param rejection, so the caller gets the full unfiltered timeline back with no hint that the window was ignored.

Meanwhile the engine underneath already implements date filtering: `TimelineOpts` declares `after`/`before` (`src/core/types.ts:1271`) and `PostgresEngine.getTimeline` applies them (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts:3439-3440`, `afterCond`/`beforeCond`). The op handler just never passes them:

```ts
// src/core/operations.ts:2165-2178
const get_timeline: Operation = {
  name: 'get_timeline',
  description: 'Get timeline entries for a page',
  params: {
    slug: { type: 'string', required: true },
  },
  handler: async (ctx, p) => {
    return ctx.engine.getTimeline(p.slug as string, sourceScopeOpts(ctx));
  },
  ...
```

So date-window timeline reads are unreachable over MCP and the CLI even though the SQL support exists.

## What should happen

Either of:

- Expose `after`/`before` (and ideally `limit`, which the engine also supports) as op params and thread them through to `TimelineOpts`; or
- at minimum, reject or warn on unrecognized params so an agent that passes `since`/`until` learns the filter did not apply, instead of silently receiving unfiltered results.

## Where

- `src/core/operations.ts:2165-2178` (`get_timeline` op — slug only)
- `src/core/types.ts:1271-1288` (`TimelineOpts.after/before/limit` — implemented but unexposed)
- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:3422-3445` (working `afterCond`/`beforeCond` SQL)

## Evidence

Hit while building date-scoped recall for a personal markdown vault synced as a source: MCP callers passing `since`/`until` to `get_timeline` always got the complete timeline, indistinguishable from a correctly filtered empty/partial window. Related: #1520 covers the sibling bug where `query`'s `since`/`until` bind to `updated_at` instead of `effective_date` — together these left no working date-window read surface pre-Chronicle.

## Workaround

Fetch the full timeline per page and filter client-side; or use the 0.42.56 Life Chronicle commands (`gbrain day` / `since`), which read `timeline_entries.date` correctly.

title: Chronicle judge: output truncated at maxTokens=1500 is silently recorded as no_events (parse failure indistinguishable from empty page)
body:
**Version:** 0.42.56.0 (also current master `6461790`) · **Engine:** Postgres 16 + pgvector · **Runtime:** Bun · **Chat:** OpenAI-compatible endpoint

## What happens

The chronicle judge caps its completion at `maxTokens: 1500` (`src/core/chronicle/extract-events.ts:186`) and then treats any unparseable output as "no events":

- `parseJudgeJson` returns `[]` on any parse failure — missing `]`, truncated JSON, anything (`extract-events.ts:200-214`);
- `runChronicleExtract` maps an empty proposals array to `status: 'no_events'` (`extract-events.ts:129-130`);
- the only `stopReason` values handled are `refusal` / `content_filter` (`extract-events.ts:188`) — a `max_tokens` / length stop is not detected.

So when a page is event-dense enough that the JSON array exceeds ~1500 output tokens, the response is cut off mid-array, `lastIndexOf(']')`/`JSON.parse` fails, and the page is recorded as legitimately having no events. Nothing in logs, job output, or the result distinguishes this from a genuinely empty page.

## Evidence

Running chronicle extraction across ~61 daily/meeting-shaped pages: 49 extracted fine, but 11 pages persistently returned `no_events` across retries — and they were consistently the larger ones (3-4K chars of dense bullet lists, i.e. many events), while smaller pages extracted normally. That pattern matches the JSON array being truncated at the token cap and silently swallowed, rather than the model finding nothing.

## What should happen

Any of (ideally all):

1. Detect truncation: when `stopReason` indicates the token cap was hit, do not feed the text to `parseJudgeJson` as if complete — retry with a higher cap, or fail the page explicitly.
2. Distinguish `parse_failed` from `no_events` in `ChronicleExtractResult` (there is already a `reason` field and a `malformed_proposal` skip path — a parse failure after non-empty model text deserves the same visibility).
3. Make the judge `maxTokens` configurable (or scale it with input size), so event-dense pages have headroom.

## Where

- `src/core/chronicle/extract-events.ts:186` (`maxTokens: 1500`)
- `src/core/chronicle/extract-events.ts:188` (only refusal/content_filter checked)
- `src/core/chronicle/extract-events.ts:200-214` (`parseJudgeJson` → `[]` on failure)
- `src/core/chronicle/extract-events.ts:129-130` (`[]` → `no_events`)

## Workaround

None clean. Splitting large pages or hand-summarizing them before extraction works but defeats the point; the affected days were covered by deterministic timeline rows instead.

title: sync --full git fast path bypasses pruneDir/isSyncable — re-imports ops/ and metafile pages that incremental sync excludes
body:
**Version:** 0.42.56.0 (also current master `6461790`) · **Engine:** Postgres 16 + pgvector · **Runtime:** Bun

## What happens

Incremental sync and full sync disagree about what belongs in the corpus, because the full-sync file enumerator bypasses the canonical exclusion gate.

**Incremental** sync filters every manifest entry through `isSyncable` (`src/commands/sync.ts:445-447` and `1849-1855`), whose `classifySync` (`src/core/sync.ts:341-360`) excludes:

- any path with a segment blocked by `pruneDir` — dot-dirs, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `venv`, `.raw`, and `ops/` at any depth (`PRUNE_DIR_NAMES`, `src/core/sync.ts:242-259`);
- metafile basenames `schema.md` / `index.md` / `log.md` / `README.md` (`SYNC_SKIP_FILES`, `src/core/sync.ts:330`).

**Full sync** (`performFullSync` → `runImport` → `collectSyncableFiles`, `src/commands/sync.ts:2952`) never applies `isSyncable`. When the source is a git work tree it takes the `git ls-files` fast path, `gitListSyncableFiles` (`src/commands/import.ts:530-560`), which filters **only** by strategy/extension (`isCollectibleForWalker`) plus `.gitignore` — no `pruneDir`, no metafile exclusion. The non-git FS-walk fallback does call `pruneDir` at descent time (`import.ts:614`) but still imports the metafile basenames. And `runImport` itself applies no `isSyncable` check downstream.

Net effect on a git-backed source (the common case): `sync --full` imports — and *re-imports/resurrects previously soft-deleted* — everything incremental sync is designed to exclude: `ops/**`, `index.md`, `README.md`, `log.md`, `schema.md`, etc. A brain that was clean under months of incremental syncs silently regains excluded pages after any event that forces a full pass (first sync, `--full`, chunker-version bump, lost sync anchor).

## Observed

On a personal markdown vault synced as a source: pages under `ops/` that incremental sync had correctly excluded (and that had been soft-deleted) came back after a full re-import, with the incremental path then treating them as deletable again — the two modes cycle content in and out depending on which one ran last.

## What should happen

The full path should route candidate files through the same single source of truth: filter `gitListSyncableFiles` output (and `runImport`'s inputs generally) through `isSyncable(relPath, { strategy })`, exactly like the incremental manifest path. `classifySync` already exists precisely so the two "cannot drift" — the git fast path just doesn't call it.

## Where (master `6461790`)

- `src/commands/import.ts:530-560` (`gitListSyncableFiles` — extension filter only)
- `src/commands/import.ts:578-599` (`collectSyncableFiles` — git fast path returns early, before any prune logic)
- `src/core/sync.ts:242-259, 330, 341-360` (`PRUNE_DIR_NAMES`, `SYNC_SKIP_FILES`, `classifySync` — the gate the full path skips)
- `src/commands/sync.ts:445-447, 1849-1855` (incremental path applying `isSyncable`)

## Related

- #2082 — the mirror-image divergence (gitignored files: invisible to incremental, imported by full FS-walk). Same root disease: the two enumeration paths don't share a filter.
- #2404 — questions `ops/` being in `PRUNE_DIR_NAMES` at all; this issue is orthogonal (whatever the exclusion set is, full and incremental should agree on it).
- #2426 — `sync --full` delete-reconcile; another case of `--full` behaving differently from steady state.

## Workaround

Avoid `--full` on sources that rely on the built-in exclusions; after an unavoidable full pass, re-delete the resurrected pages by slug prefix.

title: gateway-native loop: tool results executed but never threaded back for OpenAI-compatible providers — subagent dies with 'Tool results are missing'
body:
## Symptom

Dream-cycle synthesize subagents (`agent.use_gateway_loop=true`, provider `deepseek` via `provider_base_urls.deepseek` custom base URL) die on any transcript where the model uses tools:

```
[chat(deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro)] Tool results are missing for tool calls call_3f2f11a684ea42a692eab6b4, call_2307aad6f31f465cbe7e0bcc.
```

## Key evidence: the tools DID run

`subagent_tool_executions` shows both calls completed, with tool_use_ids exactly matching the ones the error claims are missing:

```
 job_id |          tool_use_id          |   tool_name    |  status
--------+-------------------------------+----------------+----------
  12512 | call_3f2f11a684ea42a692eab6b4 | brain_search   | complete
  12512 | call_2307aad6f31f465cbe7e0bcc | brain_get_page | complete
```

So execution + logging succeed, but the loop's history builder never appends the tool-result messages before the next model turn, and its own validator then rejects the history. Reproduced with both `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, with 6 parallel calls and with 2. Injecting `parallel_tool_calls: false` at a proxy doesn't help (and a tool-less synthesize run on the same setup completes fine — job 12507).

## Summary
The Google recipe's chat touchpoint allowlist (`src/core/ai/recipes/google.ts`) only accepts `gemini-2.0-flash-exp`, `gemini-2.0-flash`, and `gemini-1.5-pro`. As of July 2026, Google's live API no longer serves `gemini-1.5-pro`, and none of the current-generation chat models (`gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, the `gemini-3.x` line) nor the auto-tracking aliases (`gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-pro-latest`) pass `probeChatModel`.

(gemini-1.5-pro in that list 404s on the live API.)

- Longer term: a doctor check probing the allowlist against ListModels would catch both directions of drift (the embedding path already went through this exact churn).

title: fix(ai): raise gateway default max output tokens 4096 -> 32000
body:
The three toolLoop-path defaults in gateway.ts still cap output at 4096 tokens. On current always-thinking models (Claude Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.7+ / Fable 5), thinking consumes the output budget before a text block is reached, so a caller that does not pass opts.maxTokens gets an empty final text: every turn stops at max_tokens with only thinking content, and downstream consumers see a silent zero-byte result.

We hit this in production: a nightly research-brief subagent on openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 returned 0 bytes on every run until these three defaults were raised (audit trail in our deployment notes, 2026-07-04). Bumping the default to 32000 removed the cap (observed per-turn output 147-776 tokens once no longer starved).

4096 predates always-thinking models (last touched ~v0.42.41.0); 32000 is a safe modern default - providers bill actual tokens, not the cap, so the only effect is headroom.

title: fix(ai): promote DeepSeek reasoning_content when content is empty
body:
## Bug

DeepSeek-style reasoning models served through the openai-compatible `deepseek:` recipe (deepseek-reasoner, GLM reasoning variants, etc.) can return the substantive answer in `choices[].message.reasoning_content` while `content` is empty. The AI SDK adapter reads only `content`, so `gateway.chat()` yields `text: ''` and callers classify the response as empty.

Real-world impact: on one such model, **~54% of per-chunk synopsis calls** returned reasoning-only responses → `sanitizeSynopsis` → `kind:'empty'` → 1,030 pages collapsed to the title-only contextual-retrieval fallback, silently defeating the synopsis tier.

## Fix

A recipe-scoped inbound response rewriter, following the exact `voyageCompatFetch` / `zeroEntropyCompatFetch` precedent: when `content` is empty/whitespace and `reasoning_content` is a non-empty string, promote it into `content` before the SDK parses the body. Non-streaming JSON chat completions only; non-empty `content` always passes through untouched.

Plumbing: a new optional recipe-level `compat.fetch` hook (types.ts) wired in `applyOpenAICompatConfig`, so a recipe can install a static transport shim while preserving the normal `base_urls[recipe.id]` override chain and any `resolveOpenAICompatConfig` fetch taking precedence.

## Tests

New `test/deepseek-reasoning-content.test.ts` (fetch-stub style, drives the full `chat()` path):
- empty `content` + `reasoning_content` → text promoted
- non-empty `content` + `reasoning_content` → content unchanged, no duplication
- both empty → stays empty, no crash

title: fix(fences): stop pipe characters from dropping facts and takes
body:
## What & why

Facts and takes fences escaped literal pipe characters on write (`|` -> `\|`), but the shared row parser still split on every `|`. A row like `Founded Acme\|Co in 2017` was parsed as extra cells, then rejected as malformed. On later fence rewrites, only successfully parsed rows were rendered back, so a pipe-bearing fact or take could disappear from the markdown source of truth.

For users, this meant normal text such as `A|B testing`, `Acme|Co`, or `source: CRM | LinkedIn` could corrupt a facts/takes row. The visible effects were confusing: a newly added fact might not make it into the derived DB, search/trajectory/scorecard results could miss it, and a later unrelated append/update could silently remove the original row from the fence.

This fixes the shared fence parser so escaped pipes are treated as cell text, then unescaped back to literal `|` after splitting. Because facts and takes both use `parseRowCells`, the fix applies to both fences.

## Changes

- `parseRowCells` now splits only on unescaped pipe delimiters.
- Added `unescapeFenceCell` as the inverse of `escapeFenceCell`.
- Added facts regression coverage for:
  - `renderFactsTable -> parseFactsFence` preserving pipes in text cells.
  - `upsertFactRow` preserving an existing pipe-bearing row during an unrelated append.
- Added takes regression coverage for:
  - `renderTakesFence -> parseTakesFence` preserving pipes in text cells.
  - `upsertTakeRow` preserving an existing pipe-bearing row during an unrelated append.

## Verification

- [x] `bun test test/facts-fence.test.ts test/takes-fence.test.ts`
- [x] `bun test test/facts-fence-typed.test.ts test/takes-holder-validation.test.ts test/takes-holder-semantics.test.ts`
- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] `bun run verify` - 31/31 checks green

## Documentation

No README or architecture-doc updates needed for this narrow parser fix. `CONTRIBUTING.md` says changelog/version entries are handled during the ship flow, so this PR leaves `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`, and `package.json` unchanged.

title: fix(gateway): stop misdiagnosing explicit litellm/user-provided embedding models as unset
body:
## Summary

`diagnoseEmbedding`'s `user_provided_model_unset` guard fires on recipe-**static** properties (`models: []` + `user_provided_models: true`) without ever inspecting the user's model string. A fully explicit `litellm:zembed-1` is diagnosed as "model unset", `isAvailable('embedding')` returns `false`, and `hybridSearch` silently drops its vector arm on every litellm-proxied (or llama-server, or any user-provided-models recipe) deployment.

The failure mode is nasty to debug because it is **read-side only**: `embed-backfill` does not run this preflight, so vectors keep getting written — the corpus looks fully embedded, `gbrain doctor` embedding checks pass, but no query can ever retrieve through the vector arm. `gbrain search diagnose` shows:

```
"vector": { "note": "skipped — no embedding provider configured" }
```

despite `GBRAIN_EMBEDDING_MODEL=litellm:zembed-1` and a reachable proxy.

## Why removal (not a condition) is correct

A genuinely missing model part can never reach this guard:

- bare `litellm` → `parseModelId()` throws "missing a provider prefix"
- `litellm:` (empty model) → `parseModelId()` throws "empty provider or model"

Both surface earlier in `diagnoseEmbedding` as `unknown_provider` with the paste-ready `provider:model` format hint. Every string that reaches the guard therefore has a non-empty parsed model id — the guard could only ever misfire. Removed, with an explanatory comment at the site.

The `user_provided_model_unset` variant stays in `EmbeddingDiagnosis` so consumer switch arms (`init-embed-check.ts`, `embed-preflight.ts`) keep compiling; `diagnoseEmbedding` just no longer emits it.

## Production verification

Found and verified in a production deployment (OpenBrain Cloud) that fronts gbrain with an OpenAI-compatible internal gateway via `LITELLM_BASE_URL`:

- Before: `gbrain search diagnose "personel knowlege memori engin" --target projects/opagent` → vector `skipped — no embedding provider configured`, target absent from hybrid top-50.
- After (same env, recipe gate bypassed): vector arm runs, target present; a CJK long-question probe whose keyword tokens cannot match jumped to **vector rank 2**.

Related: this is the same litellm-recipe blind-spot family as #2600 (litellm chat touchpoint).

## Test plan

- [x] New `test/diagnose-embedding-user-provided.test.ts` (7 cases): explicit `litellm:<model>` ok with and without optional env; `llama-server:<model>` ok; `modelOverride` probe ok against a foreign global default; bare `litellm` and `litellm:` → `unknown_provider`; `missing_env` ordering preserved for recipes with required auth.
- [x] Existing adjacent suites green: `gateway-embed-model-override`, `embed-preflight`, `init-embed-check`, `embed.serial`, `sync-cost-gate.serial`, `cross-modal-hybrid-integration.serial`, `hybrid-meta.serial`, `hybrid-search-lite.serial`, `gateway-model-messages`, `think-gateway-adapter`.

title: fix(schema): bootstrap timeline_entries.event_page_id before schema-blob replay
body:
## Summary

`initSchema` replays the embedded schema blob **before** running numbered migrations. The blob contains

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) ...
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) ...
```

but `event_page_id` is only added by migration **v121** (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`). On any pre-v121 brain the blob replay fails with `column "event_page_id" does not exist` — *before* v121 ever gets a chance to run. Both `gbrain init --migrate-only` and the automatic on-connect migration path wedge permanently, and every CLI command warns:

```
Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist
Re-run: `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`
```

(`apply-migrations` also fails, for the same reason — its Phase A schema step hits the identical replay.)

This is the same bootstrap-or-deadlock forward-reference class as #239 / #266 / #357 / #375 (links / chunks / pages columns), which `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` exists to prevent — v121's column just never got a bootstrap entry.

## Fix

Follows the established pattern exactly:

- `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` (both engines) probes `timeline_entries.event_page_id` and adds the bare column before the blob replay. The FK constraint and both partial indexes still land through v121's guarded DO block / the blob's `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`; v121 stays idempotent.
- New `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_COVERAGE` entry in `schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts` (the CI gate this column slipped past).
- New rewind scenario in `bootstrap.test.ts`: drop the column/indexes/FK, run bootstrap, assert the column returns, then run **full `initSchema`** end-to-end to prove the wedge is gone.

## Production verification

Hit in a production Postgres brain at schema v119 running a v0.42.56 binary: migration to v122 was impossible until the column was added manually (`ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER`), after which v120–v122 applied cleanly. With this patch the same upgrade completes without manual intervention.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/bootstrap.test.ts test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts` — 16 pass (incl. new pre-v121 rewind + full initSchema replay)

title: serve --http prints admin token to stdout (leaks into container log storage)
body:
## Summary

`gbrain serve --http` prints the auto-generated **admin token** in plaintext to stdout in the startup banner:

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Admin Token (paste into /admin login):              ║
║  ab1ab1…c5e36cf8d8239f                                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

In any containerized deploy, stdout is shipped to centralized log storage (Splunk, CloudWatch, Loki, etc.). That turns a privileged admin credential into a **standing secret in log storage** — anyone with log read access can recover a valid `/admin` token and reach the admin API (`/admin/api/*`) if the port is reachable.

## Impact

- The token grants admin scope (the admin console + `/admin/api/*`).
- It is generated once per process and lives for the pod's lifetime (not the `--token-ttl`, which governs issued access tokens), so the logged value stays valid until restart.
- Deployments that expose the HTTP port (e.g. behind an ingress routing `/`) expose `/admin` alongside `/mcp`.

## Request

Provide a way to avoid emitting the secret to stdout. Any of:

1. **Redact by default** — print `Admin Token: <hidden — set GBRAIN_ADMIN_TOKEN or see …>` instead of the value; only print the raw value when an explicit `--print-admin-token` / interactive TTY is set.
2. **Accept an operator-supplied token** — read `GBRAIN_ADMIN_TOKEN` from env so operators can inject a known secret from their secret manager and never have it generated+printed.
3. **`--no-banner` / `--quiet`** flag to suppress the banner entirely for headless/server deploys.

Option 2 is the most operator-friendly (lets us source the token from a k8s Secret / Whisper and rotate it), but any of the three closes the log-leak.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.42.56.0, `serve --http`, containerized (Bun on debian), OAuth 2.1 enabled.
- Workaround in place on our side: a higher-precedence ingress rule edge-redirects `/admin` off the external VIP so the logged token can't be replayed externally. That's defense-in-depth; the token is still in our logs, which is why the root fix belongs here.

title: fix(security): prevent leaking admin bootstrap token to non-TTY stdout
body:
Fixes #2624.

## Problem

`gbrain serve --http` printed the admin bootstrap token to stdout in the startup banner. On non-TTY stdout (piped, redirected, or a container runtime), that raw token lands in log storage — a credential leak.

## Fix

The startup banner no longer prints the raw token when stdout is not a TTY. Three paths, resolved in this order:

1. **`$GBRAIN_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` set** → banner shows `from $GBRAIN_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` (never the raw value, TTY or not).
2. **non-TTY, no env token** → token hidden behind a log-leak guard; banner tells the operator to set the env var or pass `--print-admin-token` on a trusted terminal.
3. **TTY (or `--print-admin-token`)** → raw token printed as before.

The token-visibility decision is a pure function (unit-tested); the banner is just its presentation.

## Verification

Exercised all four cases against a compiled binary (backgrounded serve, captured banner, killed):

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| non-TTY default | token hidden + guidance, raw value absent |
| non-TTY `--print-admin-token` | raw token printed (forced) |
| non-TTY + env token | `from env`, raw value absent (leak-check grep = 0) |
| TTY | covered by the pure-function unit test |

- `bun test test/serve-http-bootstrap-token.test.ts` → 14 tests pass
- `bun run typecheck` → clean
- `scripts/check-privacy.sh` → clean

title: Upgrade deadlock at schema v121: schema.sql eager-indexes timeline_entries.event_page_id before migration 121 adds the column
body:
## Summary

On an **existing** Postgres brain upgrading across schema version **121** (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`, the Life Chronicle feature #2390), `initSchema()` deadlocks and every command that connects fails.

`schema.sql` unconditionally runs, on **every** `initSchema`:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
```

But on a pre-121 DB the `event_page_id` **column** doesn't exist yet — it's added by migration 121. Because `initSchema` runs `schema.sql` (the baseline) **before** `runMigrations`, the index DDL throws `column "event_page_id" does not exist`, the connection aborts, and migrations 116–122 never get to run. The column that would fix it is gated behind the very step that keeps crashing. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` still evaluates the column reference, so `IF NOT EXISTS` doesn't save it.

## Environment

- gbrain **v0.42.56.0** (master `64617904`)
- engine: `postgres` (remote)
- DB was at schema version **115**, target **122** (i.e. an upgrade that crosses the 121 boundary)

## Symptoms

- `gbrain init --migrate-only` → `column "event_page_id" does not exist`
- `gbrain health` / `gbrain embed --stale` / `gbrain dream` → `Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist` (embed-stale even prints `Re-run: gbrain apply-migrations --yes`, which does not help — see below)
- `gbrain dream` **synthesize** and **propose_takes** phases fail with `write CONNECTION_CLOSED …:5432` (the pooled connection drops when `initSchema` aborts mid-phase). This silently half-breaks the nightly `dream` job — orphan/synthesis work stops while embed/sync still appear to run.

## Root cause (file references on master `64617904`)

- `src/schema.sql` **L557–558** — the two `event_page_id` indexes, created on every `initSchema`.
- `src/core/pglite-schema.ts` **L387–388** — same, for the pglite path.
- `src/schema.sql` **L545** — `event_page_id` is declared inside `CREATE TABLE timeline_entries (…)`, which is a **no-op on an existing table** (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), so the column is *not* backfilled onto existing DBs by the baseline.
- `src/core/migrate.ts` **L5443+** (migration `version: 121`, `timeline_entries_event_page_id`) — the only place the column is actually added to existing DBs (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;` at L5457, FK at L5467, indexes at L5473–5475).

Ordering: `initSchema` → `schema.sql` (eager index, **crashes here**) → `runMigrations` (never reached).

## Why fresh installs are unaffected (and CI stays green)

A fresh install's `CREATE TABLE timeline_entries (… event_page_id …)` creates the column up front, so the subsequent eager index DDL succeeds. Only DBs that already have a `timeline_entries` table and cross the 121 boundary hit the deadlock — a path a fresh-install test matrix won't exercise.

## `apply-migrations` is a red herring

The embed-stale hint suggests `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`, but that path runs named backfills (`v0.13.1`, `v0.29.1`, …) and does **not** fix the connect-time `schema.sql` index; it also surfaces a misleading `Applying migration v0.29.1 … status=failed` which is really the same missing column hit via `initSchema`.

## Workaround (what unblocked us — non-destructive)

Run once against the DB, then let the normal migrator finish:

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
```
```
gbrain init --migrate-only
```

With the column present, `schema.sql`'s index DDL becomes a no-op, `initSchema` stops aborting, and migrations 116–122 apply normally — migration 121 idempotently adds the FK + indexes and stamps the ledger. Schema reached 122; `health`/`dream` are clean.

## Suggested fix (approach is yours to choose)

The `event_page_id` index creation shouldn't live in the always-on `schema.sql` baseline **ahead of** the column that a later migration adds. Options:

1. **Move** the two `event_page_id` index statements out of `schema.sql` / `pglite-schema.ts` and rely solely on migration 121 (it already creates them `IF NOT EXISTS`) — assuming fresh installs run migrations after the baseline.
2. **Guard** them in `schema.sql` with a `DO $$ … IF column_exists … END $$;` block.
3. **Reorder** `initSchema` so `runMigrations` executes before the eager index DDL.

This class of bug will recur on any future migration that adds a column *and* eagerly indexes it in `schema.sql`, so a guard/convention (or a CI job that runs `init` against a snapshot of an older schema, not just a fresh install) would prevent the next one.

Happy to open a PR for whichever approach you prefer.

title: v0.42.58.0 fix(ai): provider-agnostic gateway — env clobber, base-URL /v1, embedding dims (#1249 #1250 #1292 #2271 #2209)
body:
## Summary

Provider-agnostic plumbing wave: gbrain stops silently degrading or hard-failing on non-OpenAI/Anthropic stacks (local Ollama, LiteLLM proxy, llama-server, Claude Code MCP subprocess). Scope was set by a code-verified triage of the open backlog, then corrected by `/plan-eng-review` + a Codex outside-voice pass (decision trail D1–D7 in the plan).

**Gateway env + base URLs**
- `#1249` — empty-string `process.env` values no longer clobber valid config-plane API keys (Claude Code injects `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=''`; every gateway op then failed). Filter drops `''`/undefined only; `'0'`/`'false'` preserved. (`build-gateway-config.ts`)
- `#1250` — new shared `resolveNativeBaseUrl` normalizes env-injected `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` to carry `/v1`, applied at all 5 native `createAnthropic`/`createOpenAI` sites; unset → SDK default untouched. Google deferred until its native suffix is verified (TODO).

**Embedding availability + dimensions**
- `#1292`/`#2295` — the `user_provided_model_unset` guard was structurally unreachable as a no-model check (`parseModelId` throws on a bare provider) and only ever false-positived for `litellm:<model>`, silently disabling vector search ("No results."). Replaced with a real dims-presence check (`user_provided_dims_unset`) that fails closed with an actionable message; dead branches removed from both consumers; `configureGateway` no longer fabricates a default `embedding_dimensions`.
- `#2271` — new `EmbeddingTouchpoint.trust_custom_dims` passthrough tier lets ollama/llama-server/litellm accept a user-declared `--embedding-dimensions`; runs after recipe `dims_options` + Matryoshka allowlists so openai/voyage/zeroentropy/openrouter stay fail-closed (pinned by regression tests). Modern Ollama embed model names registered.
- `#2209` — LiteLLM `setup_hint` states the `/v1` path convention; stale doc pointer fixed.

**Review-driven fix (pre-landing adversarial)**
- The new dims-unset messages originally pointed at `gbrain config set embedding_dimensions`, which `config.ts` hard-rejects (schema-sizing field). Both now point at `gbrain init --embedding-dimensions <N>`, pinned by test.

**Docs**
- `KEY_FILES.md` current-state (gateway, build-gateway-config, types), `ENGINES.md` embedding note, `embedding-providers.md` (base-URL normalization, litellm multimodal, dedupe), llms bundle regenerated.

## Test Coverage

Coverage audit (subagent): **92% → gaps closed** — every changed branch now tested.

```
build-gateway-config: '' no-clobber / env-wins / '0'-'false' preserved ........ 3 tests
resolveNativeBaseUrl: bare→/v1, /v1→unchanged, slash, unset→omitted [REG],
  openai symmetry, per-provider isolation ..................................... 6 tests
diagnoseEmbedding: litellm+dims→ok (#1292 fix), no-dims→clear fail,
  fixed-dim ok, backfill invariant (getEmbeddingDimensions defaults) .......... 4 tests
embedding-dim-check: ollama/litellm/llama-server passthrough,
  openrouter fail-closed [REG], pgvector cap not bypassed [REG] ............... 6 tests
embed-preflight: dims-unset message points at accepted remediation ............ 1 test
```
Tests: 3 new test files + 3 extended (+~20 new cases). Regression paths all pinned.

## Pre-Landing Review

title: v0.42.58.1 fix: pre-v121 PGLite brains crash migrating to v0.42.x
body:
## Summary

Fixes a crash that blocks any pre-v121 PGLite brain from upgrading to v0.42.x.

**The bug.** A brain built on an older schema has a `timeline_entries` table without the `event_page_id` column (added in migration v121). On upgrade, `initSchema()` replays `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL`, which builds `idx_timeline_event_page` and `idx_timeline_event_dedup` on that column. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timeline_entries` is a no-op against the already-present table, so the column never appears and the `CREATE INDEX` aborts with `column "event_page_id" does not exist`. That wedges every migration entry point: `gbrain init --migrate-only`, `gbrain apply-migrations`, and the post-upgrade chain.

**The fix.** `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap()` exists precisely to add forward-referenced columns before the schema replay, but the v121 column was never registered with it. This adds `timeline_entries.event_page_id` to the probe set and the ALTER block, matching every sibling forward-reference (a plain `INTEGER`; migration v121 still owns the foreign key and both indexes, and stays idempotent). The matching `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_COVERAGE` entry is added so the coverage test guards it — a future forward-referenced column that skips the bootstrap now fails CI instead of a user's upgrade.

Verified end-to-end on a real brain: the jump from schema v24 to v122 went from a hard crash to 97 migrations applied in a single pass.

Commits:
- `fix:` pre-v121 PGLite brains crash migrating to v0.42.x (bootstrap coverage for `timeline_entries.event_page_id`)
- `docs:` note the column in the KEY_FILES bootstrap-coverage list

## Test Coverage

`test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts` gains the `timeline_entries.event_page_id` entry. That suite runs all 122 migrations against an in-memory PGLite brain and asserts the bootstrap covers every declared forward reference, so it exercises the new branch directly.

Directly-relevant suites: **270 pass, 0 fail** (`test/pglite-engine.test.ts`, `test/schema-bootstrap-coverage.test.ts`, `test/migrate.test.ts`).

ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER`; probes are read-only `information_schema` queries with static literals (no injection surface); the guard fires only when the table exists but the column does not, so fresh installs and modern brains both no-op.
