body:
## Bug / safety issue

`gbrain dream --phase lint` appears to run the lint core in fix mode and can write back to the source tree. For agent-managed workspaces this is a surprising side effect: most dream phases are DB-only/read-only, but `lint` can mutate markdown files.

## Expected behavior

One of:

- `dream --phase lint` defaults to read-only and reports proposed fixes, or
- expose an explicit `--fix` / `--no-fix` flag, with non-mutating behavior available for scheduled maintenance, or
- document prominently that `lint` is filesystem-mutating and should be excluded from read-only dream cycles.

## Why this matters

Users may schedule dream/maintenance cycles expecting brain/index updates, not source rewrites. Agents also need a safe mode they can run without risking unreviewed edits in a synced/git-managed workspace.

## Current workaround

Exclude `lint` from scheduled dream loops and run other phases only.

title: init --migrate-only fails on real Postgres for v121/v122 chronicle migrations: "column event_page_id does not exist"
body:
## Summary

On the real PostgreSQL engine, `gbrain init --migrate-only` deterministically fails to apply the v0.42.56.0 (Life Chronicle) schema migrations **v121** (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`) and **v122** (`facts_ontology_dimension`) with:

```
column "event_page_id" does not exist
```

The migration transaction rolls back cleanly (no partial state), so the brain stays at the pre-migration version. **PGLite is unaffected** (it tolerates the pattern), which is likely why the chronicle test-suite (PGLite-based) didn't catch it — same class as the v0.42.55.0 `#1385` fix where "PGLite tolerated it" but real PG rejected it.

## Environment

- gbrain v0.42.57.0 (introduced in v0.42.56.0 with migrations v121/v122)
- Engine: PostgreSQL + pgvector, direct connection (port 5432)
- Repro: `gbrain init --migrate-only` on a brain sitting below schema v121

## Root cause

Each migration's whole multi-statement `sql` block is sent to the engine in one call: `runMigrationSQL` (`src/core/migrate.ts`) → `tx.runMigration(version, sql)` / `conn.executeRaw(sql)` → `PostgresEngine.runUnsafe` → **`conn.unsafe(sql)`** (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts`, postgres.js).

On real PostgreSQL that path **parse-analyzes the entire multi-statement batch before executing any statement**. v121's block is:

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (...) THEN ALTER TABLE timeline_entries
  ADD CONSTRAINT timeline_entries_event_page_id_fkey
  FOREIGN KEY (event_page_id) REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; END IF; END $$;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
```

So `CREATE INDEX ... (event_page_id)` is validated **before** the preceding `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN event_page_id` has executed → "column does not exist". v122 has the same shape (`ALTER TABLE facts ADD COLUMN dimension/value/value_hash/dim_status`, then `CREATE INDEX ... (dimension, ...)`).

The **exact same SQL applies cleanly via `psql`** (the simple query protocol executes statement-by-statement), verified in a `BEGIN; … ROLLBACK;` transaction against a live brain.

## Notes

- `GBRAIN_PREPARE=false` does **not** fix it — that toggles prepared-statement caching, not simple-vs-extended protocol. `runUnsafe` calls `conn.unsafe()` (not `.simple()`), so it still batch-parses. Confirmed: re-running with `GBRAIN_PREPARE=false` ("Prepared statements disabled" logged) fails identically.
- The daemon's `initSchema` path (on `gbrain serve` startup) **does** apply these migrations successfully on the same real-Postgres brain — so the CLI `--migrate-only` path and the daemon path diverge in how they execute migration SQL. Worth reconciling the two.

## Suggested fix

Execute each migration's `sql` **statement-by-statement** (a `DO $$…$$`-aware splitter, or postgres.js `.simple()` for the batch) so an `ADD COLUMN` commits its catalog change before a later `CREATE INDEX` in the same migration is parse-analyzed — matching PGLite, `psql`, and the daemon's initSchema behavior. (Alternatively split each add-column-then-index migration into two ordered entries, but the executor fix protects every future migration of this shape.)

## Workaround

Pre-create the columns via `psql`, then re-run `gbrain init --migrate-only` (the `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` becomes a no-op and the `CREATE INDEX` then parse-validates fine):

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE facts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS dimension  TEXT;
ALTER TABLE facts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS value      TEXT;
ALTER TABLE facts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS value_hash TEXT;
ALTER TABLE facts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS dim_status TEXT;
```

title: fix(gateway): use providerOptions[recipe.id] for thinking disable + add retry loop
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2577 — the thinking disable feature for openai-compatible providers was using the wrong key in `providerOptions`, causing DeepSeek V4's thinking mode to silently remain ON.

## Root Cause

`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` reads `providerOptions[recipe.id]` (e.g. `providerOptions['deepseek']`), NOT `providerOptions.openaiCompatible`. This is because `createOpenAICompatible({ name })` sets `this.providerOptionsName = name`, where `name` is the recipe id.

Using `providerOptions.openaiCompatible` as a literal key silently drops the `thinking: { type: 'disabled' }` parameter before it reaches the wire → DeepSeek V4 defaults to thinking mode ON → reasoning tokens consume `max_tokens` quota → `content` is empty → AI SDK `generateText()` hangs until 300s timeout.

## Changes

1. **Fix providerOptions key**: `providerOptions.openaiCompatible` → `providerOptions[recipe.id]` so thinking disable reaches the API.
2. **Retry loop** for openai-compatible providers: 3 retries with exponential backoff (2s → 4s → 8s) and 30s per-attempt timeout, so transient failures do not fail the entire operation.

## Testing

- Verified `chat(deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash)` completes in ~835ms (was timing out at 300s before).
- Verified `propose_takes` cycle phase processes 100 pages and inserts 47 proposals with zero warnings (was failing all 100 extracts before).
- See issue #2577 for detailed diagnosis and timeline.

title: Migration wedge: v0.11.0 (Minions) Phase A references event_page_id, a column created by a later v0.42.x migration (old-brain upgrade 0.18.2 -> 0.42.57)
body:
### Summary

Upgrading an old brain (created around v0.17/v0.18, PGLite engine) from v0.18.2 straight to v0.42.57.0 fails on the very first pending migration: `v0.11.0 (GBrain Minions)` aborts with `column "event_page_id" does not exist`.

### Root cause (as far as I can tell)

Migration `v0.11.0` "Phase A (schema)" replays the current embedded schema, which includes the Life Chronicle indexes introduced much later:

```
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
```

But the column `event_page_id` itself is added by a v0.42.x migration (`timeline_entries_event_page_id`, src/core/migrate.ts) that runs AFTER v0.11.0 in the ledger order. On a brain whose ledger still has v0.11.0 pending (mine was "MINIONS HALF-INSTALLED (partial migration: 0.11.0)" per doctor), the old migration references a column created by a newer one: chicken-and-egg, and `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` aborts.

### Workaround that unblocked me

Manually adding the column first (same definition as the upstream migration, additive and idempotent):

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
```

then re-running `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` (multiple passes until the PARTIAL backfills drained). Everything completed cleanly afterwards: doctor reports 0 failed checks on a 14 GB / ~14.8k pages PGLite brain.

### Suggested fix

Either make v0.11.0 Phase A tolerant of forward-referenced columns (skip index creation when the column is missing: the later migration recreates it), or have the schema replay apply the guarded column additions before index creation.

### Environment

- gbrain v0.42.57.0 (git 058f448b), upgraded from v0.18.2 (git 08b3698e)
- PGLite engine, brain ~14 GB, ~14 800 pages
- bun on Linux x64

Thanks for #2348 by the way: we hit the live-lock steal corruption in production the very same day, and the new never-steal behavior plus the recovery hints are exactly right.

title: v119 to v122 migration failure: column "event_page_id" does not exist
body:
## Summary

On an existing Postgres brain, `initSchema()` (and therefore `gbrain init --migrate-only`, `apply-migrations`, and any command that brings up the schema) crashes with:

```
column "event_page_id" does not exist
```

The schema stays stuck at v119 and migrations v120–v122 never apply. `gbrain sources status` also prints `Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist` on every run.

## Root cause

`initSchema()` runs `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap(conn)` and then replays the embedded schema (`SCHEMA_SQL`) *before* running incremental migrations:

- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:327` → `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap(conn)`
- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:329` → `conn.unsafe(sqlText)` (SCHEMA_SQL replay)
- `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:332` → `runMigrations(this)`

The embedded schema now references `timeline_entries.event_page_id` (added by migration **v121** `timeline_entries_event_page_id`):

- `src/core/schema-embedded.ts:549` → `event_page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `src/core/schema-embedded.ts:561-562` → `CREATE INDEX ... ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) ...`

On an existing brain `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timeline_entries` is a no-op, so the column is **not** added, and the subsequent `CREATE INDEX ... (event_page_id)` in the SCHEMA_SQL replay throws. Because this happens before `runMigrations`, v121 (which would add the column) never gets a chance to run — the transaction rolls back and the version stays at 119.

`applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` exists precisely to add columns the embedded schema forward-references but old brains lack. Every other such reference has a bootstrap entry — e.g. v79 `pages.last_retrieved_at` at `src/core/postgres-engine.ts:802` (`ALTER TABLE pages ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_retrieved_at ...`). The `event_page_id` case is missing its equivalent.

## Fix

Add an `event_page_id` bootstrap entry to `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` (both the Postgres and PGLite mirrors), matching the v79 pattern:

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
```

(guarded by a `timeline_entries` existence probe, like the others) so the SCHEMA_SQL index creation succeeds and `runMigrations` can then apply v121's FK + indexes idempotently.

## Repro

1. A Postgres brain stamped at schema v119 (pre-v121).
2. Upgrade to >= the version that introduced v121 / the embedded `event_page_id` index.
3. `gbrain init --migrate-only` → prints `column "event_page_id" does not exist`, schema stays 119.

## Workaround

Manually apply v121's DDL (`ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;` plus its FK/indexes), then re-run `gbrain init --migrate-only` — migrations then advance 120→122 cleanly.

Seen on v0.42.57.0 (commit 058f448), Postgres backend.

title: user_provided_models recipes (llama-server, litellm): init is a catch-22 — requires --embedding-dimensions, then rejects every value
body:
**Version:** 0.42.57.0, PGLite engine, Linux ARM64, bun 1.3.14

**Repro:**

Point the llama-server recipe at any OpenAI-compatible local embedding server (mine serves BAAI/bge-m3, native 1024-dim, at `http://127.0.0.1:8889/v1` — `/v1/models` and `/v1/embeddings` both implemented):

```
$ gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model llama-server:bge-m3
Provider llama-server requires --embedding-dimensions <N> when using --embedding-model llama-server:bge-m3.

$ gbrain init --pglite --embedding-model llama-server:bge-m3 --embedding-dimensions 1024
Refusing to init: Provider "llama-server" model "bge-m3" does not support custom dimensions 1024 (this model only emits its default vector size). Either drop --embedding-dimensions or pick a Matryoshka-aware model.
```

Every path is rejected, so the recipe is unusable for embeddings as shipped.

**Cause:** `validateDimAgainstTouchpoint` (src/core/embedding-dim-check.ts) treats any `requestedDims !== defaultDims` as a Matryoshka truncation request and walks the custom-dim allow-lists. For user-provided-model recipes the touchpoint declares `default_dims: 0` ("forces explicit --embedding-dimensions" per the recipe comment), so the explicit value can never equal the default and always falls through to the tier-3 rejection.

**Suggested fix:** when `default_dims === 0` (user-provided-model recipes), treat the explicit dims as the declared native size and skip the custom-dim validation:

```ts
if (requestedDims !== undefined && requestedDims !== defaultDims && defaultDims !== 0) {
  // ... existing precedence walk
}
```

Locally patched this way and the recipe works end-to-end (init → import → query) against a llama-server-wire embedding endpoint.

title: embed preflight rejects user_provided_models recipes even when the config string names a model ("requires a specific model name to be configured")
body:
**Version:** 0.42.57.0, PGLite engine, Linux ARM64, bun 1.3.14. Companion to #2675 — hit immediately after working around it.

**Repro:**

`~/.gbrain/config.json`:
```json
{
  "embedding_model": "llama-server:bge-m3",
  "embedding_dimensions": 1024,
  "provider_base_urls": { "llama-server": "http://127.0.0.1:8889/v1" }
}
```

```
$ gbrain import .
Provider "llama-server" requires a specific model name to be configured.

  Set one: gbrain config set embedding_model llama-server:<model-name>
  Or run with --no-embed to import-only and embed later.
```

The config string plainly carries a model (`bge-m3`), and `gbrain config get embedding_model` echoes it back — but every embed path refuses with the "unset" error, telling you to set the thing that is already set.

**Cause:** the preflight in src/core/ai/gateway.ts checks the recipe's *static* touchpoint model list, which is empty **by design** for user-provided recipes, without ever consulting the parsed model id from the config string:

```ts
if (
  Array.isArray(tp.models) &&
  tp.models.length === 0 &&
  (recipe.id === 'litellm' || isUserProvided)
) {
  return { ok: false, reason: 'user_provided_model_unset', ... };
}
```

So `user_provided_model_unset` fires for every valid config, and (with #2675) the llama-server/litellm embedding recipes can never be used.

**Suggested fix:** only reject when the parsed config string itself lacks a model id:

```ts
  (recipe.id === 'litellm' || isUserProvided) &&
  !(parsed.modelId && String(parsed.modelId).trim())
```

With both this and #2675 patched locally, llama-server-recipe embeddings work end-to-end (85-page import, 166 chunks, hybrid query) against a local OpenAI-compatible embedding server.

title: migrate --to does not copy the sources table — FK failure on any multi-source brain (+ resume manifest is not target-aware)
body:
Two related migrate-engine issues found migrating a 4,750-page multi-source brain (pglite → postgres), gbrain 0.42.44.0:

**1. `migrate --to` never copies `sources` rows.** On a brain with a registered source (`gbrain sources add …`), `copy_pages` fails on the very first page with `insert or update on table "pages" violates foreign key constraint "pages_source_id_fkey"` — the target only has the `default` source. Workaround: manually `INSERT` the source row on the target before migrating. Suggested fix: copy `sources` before `copy_pages`.

**2. `migrate-manifest.json` resume checkpoint is not target-aware.** After an interrupted migration to target A (remote postgres), re-running against target B (local postgres) reported `4032 already done` and skipped those pages — the manifest records slugs but not the target, so a different target inherits a bogus completion set (and then hits issue 1 on the remainder). Suggested fix: key the manifest by target URL hash, or clear it when `--url` differs.

Also hit (minor, documented behaviors worth a docs note): schema migration [24] requires the target role to have BYPASSRLS, and [35] (`auto_rls_event_trigger`) requires superuser — a least-privilege dedicated role needs a temporary elevation dance.

Happy to provide full logs.

title: fix(sources): audit walker inverts pruneDir — nested sources report 0 files scanned
body:
## Bug

`gbrain sources audit <source>` reports **"Files scanned: 0 markdown files"** for any source whose `local_path` organizes content in subdirectories. Flat sources audit fine.

## Root cause

The audit walk in `src/commands/sources.ts` (~line 1137):

```ts
if (stat.isDirectory()) {
  if (pruneDir(entry, dir)) continue;   // inverted
  walk(full);
}
```

`pruneDir()` in `core/sync.ts` returns **`true` = descend, `false` = prune** ("Should this directory be descended into?"). The audit walker treats it as the opposite, so it:

- **skips every legitimate subdirectory** → any nested source audits 0 files, and
- **descends into exactly the trees it should skip** (`node_modules/`, `.git/`, `vendor/`, `dist/`, `.raw/` sidecars) — the inverse harm, if any of those happen to contain `.md` files they get audited.

The walker's own comment says *"Mirror gbrain sync's descent rules so the file set we audit matches the file set that would actually be ingested"* — the inversion makes it do precisely the opposite: the audited set and the ingested set are disjoint for nested sources.

## Reproduction (real brain, v0.42.56/0.42.57)

A comms source with per-contact subdirectories (`<root>/<contact>/<YYYY-MM>.md`, ~1.1k files, all ingested and searchable by sync):

```
$ gbrain sources audit comms-imessage
Files scanned: 0 markdown files
```

A flat source in the same brain:

```
$ gbrain sources audit comms-gcal
Files scanned: 4 markdown files
```

Related but distinct from #2607 (sync --full git fast path bypassing pruneDir) — this one is the audit command's walker.

## Fix

One-line inversion (plus a comment pinning the contract at the callsite). Happy to add a regression test if you can point at the preferred harness for command-level walkers — the `walk` closure is currently inline in the command, so unit-testing it needs either extraction or the serial CLI harness.

title: Fix/autopilot setup agent cron
CLI take-writes resolve pages by slug only (getPageId has no source filter) - cross-source writes when a slug exists in multiple sources
body:
**Version:** 0.42.52.0 (SHA `bb2e88c`), Postgres engine, multi-source brain.

## Summary
Every CLI take-write (`takes add`, `takes update`, `takes supersede`) resolves its target page via
`getPageId` (`src/commands/takes.ts:86`):

```ts
const rows = await engine.executeRaw<{ id: number }>(
  `SELECT id FROM pages WHERE slug = $1 LIMIT 1`, [slug]);
```

No `source_id` filter, no `ORDER BY`. When the **same slug exists in more than one source**, the
pick is arbitrary — neither `GBRAIN_SOURCE` nor `--source` participates (verified: `--source` on
`takes add`/`takes supersede` lands in the take's provenance `source` column; it does not scope the
page resolution).

## Repro (two sources, same slug)
1. `put_page` the same slug into source A and source B (e.g. a dept source and a shared/canon source).
2. Under `GBRAIN_SOURCE=<source A>`, run
   `gbrain takes supersede <slug> --row 1 --claim "x" --who someone --source <source A> --dir /tmp`.
3. Observed: the supersede resolved the **source B** page — struck source B's take row 1 and
   appended the replacement take onto source B's page. Source A's take was untouched. (In our case
   this silently struck a `world`-held take in the shared source while the command was scoped to a
   dept source.)

`takes add` has the same exposure via the same helper (call sites ~198/226/271/350): a scoped add
can attach a take to another source's page that happens to share the slug.

## Expected
Page resolution for take-writes should be scoped to the resolved source (`GBRAIN_SOURCE` / ctx
source), like `delete_page` already is — `softDeletePage(slug, { sourceId })` threads the source
and behaves correctly in the same setup. The asymmetry between the takes commands and the page ops
is the trap.

## Workarounds we use meanwhile
- Never let a slug exist in two sources (namespace shared-source copies, e.g. `canon/<slug>`).
- A post-condition guard around supersede: re-list the page's active takes under the scope and
  verify the requested take id actually flipped `active=false`; treat "still active" as a hard
  failure.

Related: the `takes supersede` active-take lookup bug (listTakes({active:false}) at takes.ts:274,
which we patch locally) — same file; a `getPageId` fix could land together.

title: fix(db): chunk-row model label falls back to live gateway model, not build-time constant
body:
## Problem

Closes #1717.

`content_chunks.model` records `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` (currently `'zeroentropyai:zembed-1'`) for every chunk of a brain configured with any other embedding provider. No `ChunkInput` builder sets `model` — `embed.ts` (3 call sites), `embed-stale.ts`, and `import-file.ts` all leave it undefined — so the `chunk.model || DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` fallback in both engines' `_upsertChunksOnce` always wins, stamping provenance for a model that never produced the vectors.

Meanwhile the two *page-level* mechanisms resolved from the gateway are correct (`pages.embedding_signature` and the column DEFAULT baked by `initSchema`), so the row label silently contradicts them. Nothing reads the column for decisions today (stale detection is `embedding IS NULL`; model-swap detection is `pages.embedding_signature`), but any operator inspecting the DB — or any future feature that trusts the column — gets the wrong provider.

This is the recurrence of the v0.37 Lane A.7 fix: that pass replaced the hard-coded `'text-embedding-3-large'` literal with the `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` constant, but a build-time constant still isn't *this brain's* configured model.

## Relationship to #1803

#1803 fixes the same mislabel (#1717) at the `embed` command layer, so it covers `gbrain embed` only. This PR closes the class at the seam every path converges on — `upsertChunks` in both engines — so `put`, `import`, worker `embed-backfill`, and contextual re-index get the correct label too, including any future ChunkInput builder that forgets to set `model`.

## Change (2 files, same seam in both engines)

`_upsertChunksOnce` resolves the fallback from the live gateway (`getEmbeddingModel()`) at upsert time — the same pattern `initSchema` uses to bake the column DEFAULT. The constant remains only when the gateway is unconfigured (unit tests).

## Tests

`test/v0_37_gap_fill.serial.test.ts` Lane A.7 updated to pin both branches: configured gateway model wins; unconfigured gateway falls back to `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL`. 13 tests / 0 fail; `tsc --noEmit` clean on top of current master.

title: fix(db): bootstrap timeline_entries.event_page_id before schema-blob index replay
body:
## Problem

Fixes #2626, #2673.

Upgrading any pre-v121 brain wedges at `initSchema`: the schema blob's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timeline_entries` is a no-op on an existing table (it won't add the v121 column), so the blob's partial indexes `idx_timeline_event_page` + `idx_timeline_event_dedup` crash with `column "event_page_id" does not exist` **before** `runMigrations` can ever apply v121. The version stays stamped at the old number and every retry hits the same wall. Reproduced on a real v119 postgres brain upgrading to v0.42.57.0 (`gbrain init --migrate-only` dies with that one-line error).

Same wedge family as #239/#266/#357/#366/#374/#375/#378/#396: a column-with-index added to the schema blob without a corresponding `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` entry.

## Relationship to #2548 / #2623

Both open PRs address the same wedge — offered here as an alternative in case either stalls; happy to close this if one of them lands. What this one adds:

- Bootstrap entry follows the exact house pattern in **both** engines (single-round-trip probe extension + guarded `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for the bare column only — FK and indexes land via the blob and v121, both idempotent).
- A red/green regression in `test/bootstrap.test.ts`: down-mutate a fresh brain to pre-v121 shape (drop indexes + FK + column, stamp version 119) and assert `initSchema` reaches `LATEST_VERSION` with the column restored. Verified the test fails on master without the fix and passes with it.
- Verified end-to-end against a real v119 → v122 postgres upgrade (migrations 120–122 apply, doctor reports latest).

## Tests

`bun test test/bootstrap.test.ts test/migration-v120.test.ts`: 9 tests / 0 fail; `tsc --noEmit` clean on top of current master.

title: Schema replay throws on v0.42.x upgrade: CREATE INDEX on `timeline_entries(event_page_id)` runs before migration 121 adds the column
body:
## Summary

On a Postgres brain at schema `version=119`, running `gbrain init --migrate-only` (or any path that calls `PostgresEngine.initSchema`) throws:

```
column "event_page_id" does not exist
```

with exit 1, and the migration array never runs. Schema stays wedged at 119.

## Environment

- gbrain `0.42.57.0` (latest master, `058f448b`)
- Postgres brain (local dev pool)
- Starting schema version: **119** (op_checkpoints CHECK constraint)
- Target schema version: **122**

## Repro

Fresh brain at v119. Any of these paths triggers the failure:

```bash
gbrain init --migrate-only      # exit 1
gbrain apply-migrations --yes   # silently succeeds ("All migrations up to date") but schema stays at 119
gbrain doctor                   # reports Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist
```

## Root cause

`PostgresEngine.initSchema` (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts:277-363`) runs, in order:

1. `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap(conn)` — probes for forward-referenced columns and pre-creates them (`pages.deleted_at`, `links.link_source`, `content_chunks.language`, etc.).
2. `conn.unsafe(sqlText)` — replays the full embedded schema.
3. `runMigrations(this)` — applies pending migrations.

The embedded schema (`src/core/schema-embedded.ts:561-562`) contains:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
```

On a pre-121 brain, `timeline_entries` exists but `event_page_id` does not. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` protects against "index already exists" — not against "column does not exist." Step 2 throws → step 3 never runs → the migration that would have created the column (`migrations/[121] timeline_entries_event_page_id`, `src/core/migrate.ts:5442-5477`) never fires. Wedge is permanent until manually resolved.

This is the same forward-reference class that `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` was built to handle. `event_page_id` is just missing from the probe list.

## Verification the migration SQL itself is fine

Ran migration 121's SQL in isolation on a v119 brain via psql (with `BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK`): clean. Same for migrations 120 and 122. All three succeed when driven directly.

## Proposed fix

Extend `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` (`src/core/postgres-engine.ts:389-...`) with an `event_page_id_exists` probe + guarded add, mirroring the existing pattern for `pages.deleted_at` etc.

Sketch (~10 lines):

```typescript
// Add to the probe SELECT (single round-trip):
event_page_id_exists: boolean;  // add to the type
// SELECT clause:
EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
   WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
     AND table_name = 'timeline_entries'
     AND column_name = 'event_page_id'
) AS event_page_id_exists

// Then in the bootstrap step, after the existing probes:
if (probe.pages_exists && !probe.event_page_id_exists) {
  await conn`ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER`;
}
```

The migration 121 body remains as-is; on a bootstrapped v119 brain, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` in the migration is now a no-op but the FK-constraint DO block and the two indexes still land through the migration path (the migration's own DDL is idempotent by design).

Alternative sketch: wrap the two `CREATE INDEX` statements in `schema-embedded.ts:561-562` in a `DO $$ IF column_exists ... $$` block. Slightly less invasive but doesn't add the column so the migration must still land — same net effect, just a different placement.

## Workaround for users hitting this now

Manual DDL (matches migration 121's exact shape), then re-run `gbrain init --migrate-only`:

```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conname = 'timeline_entries_event_page_id_fkey'
       AND conrelid = 'timeline_entries'::regclass
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE timeline_entries
      ADD CONSTRAINT timeline_entries_event_page_id_fkey
      FOREIGN KEY (event_page_id) REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;
  END IF;
END $$;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_dedup
  ON timeline_entries(event_page_id, date) WHERE event_page_id IS NOT NULL;
COMMIT;
```

Then:

```bash
gbrain init --migrate-only
# ✓ Schema version 119 → 122 (3 migration(s) pending)
# ✓ [120] schema_lint_hardening_search_path_security_invoker
# ✓ [121] timeline_entries_event_page_id
# ✓ [122] facts_ontology_dimension
```

## Impact

Any brain at v119 attempting to reach v122 via the standard `gbrain init --migrate-only` or auto-migrate paths. `gbrain apply-migrations --yes` silently reports "up to date" without applying — that's a separate warning-quality issue (should surface the failed schema replay rather than reporting success).

## Not filing a PR

Filing the issue for triage — happy to leave the fix implementation to maintainers to keep the forward-reference bootstrap pattern consistent.

title: One md file >1MB overflows page-level tsvector and blocks the entire source sync at checkpoint
body:
## Bug

Keyword indexing builds one `tsvector` over the whole page, and Postgres hard-caps a tsvector at 1,048,575 bytes. A single markdown file over that size fails with `string is too long for tsvector` — and instead of failing just that file, the **whole source sync reports `Sync BLOCKED`** and the checkpoint cannot advance until the file is fixed or skipped.

## Evidence from v0.42.56.0 (macOS, Postgres 17)

Sync-failures ledger entries for a mailing-list feed source containing large exported Google-Docs markdown (1.1–7.5 MB):

```
"error":"string is too long for tsvector (1888898 bytes, max 1048575 bytes)"
"error":"string is too long for tsvector (3547984 bytes, max 1048575 bytes)"
```

Sync output:

```
Sync BLOCKED at 0e1313a1: 5 file(s) failed to parse.
  See ~/.gbrain/sync-failures.jsonl for details, or run 'gbrain doctor'.
```

- Other files in the same run DID import, but the checkpoint stays pinned.
- With `--retry-failed` the same files re-fail every run.
- The 3-consecutive-failure auto-skip eventually moves past them, but for a scheduled collector that means hours of blocked cycles per oversized file, per source.

Notably, **embeddings are already chunk-level** — only the keyword tsvector is whole-page, so this limit looks like an implementation artifact rather than inherent.

## Why this matters

Sources fed by automated exporters (Drive docs, email archives, large tables) routinely produce multi-MB markdown. One such file silently degrades an entire source's freshness, and the failure mode ("Sync BLOCKED") reads like a sync-infrastructure problem rather than "one file is too big for the keyword index".

## Expected fix

Any of:

- Build `search_vector` per chunk (matching the embedding granularity), or
- Truncate/cap the tsvector input for oversized pages (index the first ~1MB, warn, keep full text in the page body), or
- At minimum: treat tsvector overflow as a per-file ledger entry that does NOT block the source checkpoint.

## Workaround

Cap markdown exports at the collection layer (we truncate to ≤900KB with a marker before gbrain ever sees the file).

title: Image pages are created with source_id='default' regardless of the syncing source
body:
## Bug

Image pages are created with `source_id='default'` regardless of which registered source's sync imported them. Sibling markdown pages from the same sync get the correct `source_id`; only image-asset pages misroute.

## Evidence from v0.42.56.0 (macOS, Postgres 17)

After `gbrain sync --source <feed-id> --full --parallel 1` across ~10 registered feed sources containing ~35k images total:

```sql
SELECT source_id, count(*) FROM pages
WHERE slug ~ '\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$'
GROUP BY source_id;
-- every row lands under 'default'; zero under the syncing source ids
```

Markdown pages from the same syncs carry the right `source_id`.

## Why this matters

- **Per-source fidelity accounting is impossible**: you cannot compare images-on-disk vs images-in-brain per source (we had to fall back to a single global disk-vs-DB count).
- **Search scoping**: `search --source <feed-id>` excludes that source's own images.
- **`sources status` page counts** exclude the images a source actually contributed.

Related to the broader source-isolation efforts in #929 and #753 — this is the image-import corner of the same problem.

## Expected fix

`importImageFile` (and whatever creates the image page row) should inherit the `source_id` of the sync run that imported it, same as markdown imports.

## Workaround

Global (cross-source) disk-vs-DB image accounting only; per-source scoped searches must be repeated against `default` to pick up that source's images.

title: sources add accepts non-git dirs that can never sync; stale last_commit after re-init dies on raw 'git cat-file' fatal with no self-heal or reset CLI
body:
## Bug (two related UX gaps around the git-repo requirement)

**(a) `sources add` accepts a non-git directory that can never sync.** Registering a plain directory succeeds; every subsequent sync then fails with:

```
Not a git repository: <local_path>. GBrain sync requires a git-initialized repo.
```

Nothing at registration time validates or hints at the requirement, so in an automated pipeline the source just goes silently stale (`last_sync_at` frozen) until an operator reads the sync logs. In our case an email-archive source sat unsyncable for 3 days while its markdown looked healthy from the earlier import.

**(b) After `git init` + commit in that directory, sync dies on a stale anchor with a raw git fatal.** `sources.last_commit` still held a SHA from the pre-git era, and `gbrain sync --source <id> --full` failed with:

```
fatal: git cat-file: could not get object info
```

No message names the stale anchor, and there is no CLI to reset it — we recovered by NULL-ing the `sources.last_commit` column in the database by hand, after which the full sync ran perfectly.

Worth noting: #1205 shows autopilot HAS a graceful path for this exact condition ("Sync anchor commit <sha> missing (force push?). Running full reimport."). CLI `sync --full` in this shape did not take that path — it surfaced the raw fatal instead.

**(c) Docs gap:** `git init` + an empty commit is NOT sufficient — the walker reads files through git objects, so untracked working-tree files are invisible. Files must actually be committed. This is discoverable only by experiment.

## Why this matters

The git requirement is reasonable, but its failure modes are all silent-or-cryptic: a source that never syncs, a fatal with no remediation hint, and a recovery that requires editing the database. Each one costs an operator a debugging session.

## Expected fix

- Validate (or at least warn) at `sources add` when `local_path` is not a git repo.
- When the anchor commit is missing from the repo, treat it as a first sync / full reimport (reusing the recovery that autopilot already has per #1205) instead of surfacing `git cat-file` fatals.
- Provide `gbrain sources reset-anchor <id>` (or document the supported way to clear `last_commit`).
- Document the "files must be committed, not just present" requirement.

Related: #1205 (anchor invalidation under autopilot), #753 (git-root discovery for subdir sources).

## Workaround

`git init && git add -A && git commit` in the source dir, then manually `UPDATE sources SET last_commit=NULL WHERE id='<id>'` and re-run `gbrain sync --source <id> --full`.

title: fix(gbrain): source-scoping + facts-fence + calibration + migration-honesty correctness fixes
body:
Batch of correctness + reliability fixes from a personal fork, offered upstream. Each commit is independently reviewable; all are test-covered. typecheck: 0 errors.

## Fixes
1. **`get_page`/`resolve_slugs` per-call source scoping** — a scoped `query` could surface a page from a non-default source a follow-up `get_page` on the same connection couldn't resolve. Adds a `source_id` param mirroring `query`. Also stops `schema sync` calling a prefix "dead" when pages exist under it.
2. **`list_pages` honors per-call `source_id`** — same gap; it silently scoped to the caller's ambient default. Routed through the grant-checked `resolveRequestedScope`; omitted → prior behavior (the #861 leak seal holds).
3. **`extract_facts` guard ignores structurally-unfenceable legacy rows** — the guard blocked the cycle on any `row_num IS NULL` fact, but v0.32.2 can never fence a row whose source has NULL `local_path`, so the phase wedged forever. Excludes NULL-local_path rows, mirroring the NULL-entity_slug exclusion.
4. **v0.32.2 reports unfenceable rows instead of silently self-certifying** — Phase B returned `complete` having fenced 0 of a non-empty backlog. Keeps `complete` (permanently unfenceable; `partial` would re-run forever) but reports the backlog in the detail + a `console.warn`.
5. **calibration: honor holder env + reject leaked scaffolding** — the phase was always invoked with `{}` (generated for the default holder regardless of `GBRAIN_CALIBRATION_HOLDER`); and a thin scorecard leaked clarifying-question chain-of-thought into `pattern_statements`. Reads the env now, and filters scaffolding shapes.
6. **`takes_list` holder fallback + BigInt-safe calibration serialization** — `get_calibration_profile` threw "cannot serialize BigInt"; `takes_list` returned `[]` for a valid holder.
7. **concept synthesis attributes to dominant atom source, not `default`** — stranded concept pages in the unbacked `default` source.
8. **chat: retry the provider call on the default-timeout abort** — the wall-clock backstop aborts a slow provider call and the SDK doesn't retry an abort, so a transient slow moment killed the call (timed out 10/21 pages in a dream run). Bounded retry (≤3, 0.75s→1.5s), fresh deadline per attempt, fires ONLY on default-timeout aborts — caller aborts never retried.
9. **voice-gate judge uses the configured chat model, not a hardcoded bare id** — `defaultJudge` hardcoded `model: 'claude-haiku-4-5'` (no provider prefix → rejected by model resolution; also anthropic-only, unreachable on a proxy-only setup). Latent because the calibration cold-brain branch short-circuits before the gate runs for <5-take holders. Drops the hardcoded model so `chat()` resolves `opts.model ?? getChatModel()`.

Note #5, #8, #9 form a chain: fixing the holder (#5) made the phase reach the LLM path for a real holder, which surfaced the abort-not-retried behavior (#8) and the hardcoded judge model (#9) — both previously masked by the 0-take short-circuit.

title: extract_facts entity resolution misattributes at scale — bare first names (102/102 to the wrong person) and shared-token company names (8/8 to one wrong company) land on confident wrong entities
body:
## Summary

`extract_facts` entity resolution misattributes facts at scale when names share tokens. In a ~10-day window on one brain (v0.42.53.0):

- **Bare "Victor" resolved to the wrong person 102 consecutive times.** The vault has `10-people/victor-fteha` (the brain owner, `user_holder=victor`) and `10-people/victor-braca` (a contact). Every bare-first-name mention landed on `victor-braca`; the holder's page received **zero** facts over the same window.
- **"* Capital" company facts landed on one unrelated company 8/8 times**: facts about Capital on Tap, Elson Capital, and Ruby Capital Group all resolved to `11-companies/cast-capital`.

`page_aliases` / `slug_aliases` are empty for the affected entities — this is the resolver's own scoring (`resolveEntitySlug`'s pg_trgm + prefix-expansion path, per the comment at fence-write.ts ~183), not user-configured aliasing.

## Why it matters

Wrong-entity facts are silent: writes succeed, fences render, and recall/timeline/enrichment then serve confident wrong answers about both entities (queries about the real Victor returned the contact's page). Repair is expensive — SQL reattribution honoring the `(source_id, source_markdown_slug, row_num)` fence key plus fence re-renders on every touched page — and re-pollutes on the next extraction run, since the resolver behavior is unchanged.

## Ask

- **Bare first names should never fuzzy-match one of several candidates sharing that token** — require a full-name/alias-grade match, and when the brain has a `user_holder`, give the holder's own page priority for its bare first name (the single most common bare-name referent in any personal brain).
- **Shared-suffix company tokens ("Capital", "Group", "LLC") should be down-weighted** in trigram scoring so "Elson Capital" can't land on "Cast Capital" on the strength of the shared suffix.
- When no candidate clears a confidence threshold, prefer an unresolved/holding bucket over the best-scoring wrong match — a skipped fact is recoverable; a misattributed one is invisible.

title: Postgres brains stuck at schema v119: startup probe queries event_page_id before migration v121 can create it
body:
## Summary

After updating code to v0.42.58.0, a Postgres brain at schema version 119 can't migrate to 122. A startup schema probe queries `timeline_entries.event_page_id` (added by migration v121, Life Chronicle #2390) and fails, and that failure blocks the migration runners that would create the column. Chicken and egg: the tool that adds the column dies because the column is missing.

## Repro

1. Postgres brain at schema version 119 (pre Life Chronicle).
2. Update code to v0.42.58.0.
3. Every CLI invocation now prints:
   ```
   Schema probe failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist
   Re-run: `gbrain apply-migrations --yes`
   ```
4. Following that instruction:
   ```
   $ gbrain apply-migrations --yes
   === Applying migration v0.11.0: GBrain Minions ===
   Phase A (schema) failed: column "event_page_id" does not exist. Aborting; re-run after fixing.
   Migration v0.11.0 reported status=failed.
   ```
5. The other entrypoint fails too:
   ```
   $ gbrain init --migrate-only
   column "event_page_id" does not exist
   ```
6. `gbrain doctor` confirms: `schema_version → Version 119, latest is 122`.

## Impact

Core reads/writes/search keep working, but every upgrading Postgres user below v121 is wedged out of migrations 120-122, Chronicle and advisor paths error, and the probe warning prints on every command. No path forward through the shipped tooling; the workaround is hand-applying migrations 120-122 from `src/core/migrate.ts` and stamping the version.

## Suspected cause

The always-run probe added with Chronicle (the one in doctor.ts that keys off the real schema, `event_page_id`) runs before the migration path, and its failure aborts rather than downgrades. Migrations 120-122 themselves look fine: additive and idempotent.

## Suggested fix

Either run the probe after `runMigrations`, or make it tolerate the missing column (skip with a warn) so the runners can reach v121. Happy to test a fix against a wedged v119 brain, and can PR if you'd like.

title: facts-fence pipe escaping is asymmetric: renderFactsTable writes \| but parseRowCells splits on every pipe — facts with literal pipes are silently deleted on the next reconcile
body:
## Summary

`renderFactsTable` escapes literal pipes in cell text as `\|` (`escapeFenceCell`, fence-shared.ts:86), but `parseRowCells` (fence-shared.ts:36) splits rows on **every** `|` without honoring the escape — its own comment says "does NOT unescape `\|`" and assumes fact text never contains pipes ("currently neither takes nor facts do at the LLM-extract layer"). That assumption doesn't hold: LLM-extracted facts DO contain pipes (ours: "replies resolve them with correct|incorrect|partial|unresolvable scores"), and any such fact breaks the fence round-trip.

## Failure

1. A fact whose claim contains `a|b|c` is inserted; any fence render (`upsertFactRow` append, forget re-render, a manual DB→fence backfill) writes the cell as `a\|b\|c`.
2. The next fence→DB reconcile (`extract_facts` cycle phase) calls `parseFactsFence` → `parseRowCells`, which splits the row into 13 cells instead of 10.
3. The row fails column validation and is **silently dropped from the DB** (the phase's wipe-then-reinsert means the fact is deleted; only a per-page warning counter hints at it).

Observed live on v0.42.53.0: a 7-row fence reconciled to 6 DB rows; the dropped row was exactly the one with escaped pipes.

## Ask

Make the round-trip symmetric: either have `parseRowCells` split on unescaped pipes only (e.g. split on `/(?<!\\)\|/` then unescape `\|` → `|` in cell text), or sanitize pipes out of claim text at extract/insert time so render never needs to escape. The silent-drop should also be louder — a row that parses to the wrong cell count is data loss, worth a named warning with the row text, not just a counter.

title: providers command bypasses canonical gateway config
body:
## Summary

`gbrain providers` builds gateway configuration separately from the rest of the CLI instead of using `buildGatewayConfig()`. On v0.42.58.0 this means provider diagnostics can ignore file-plane API keys and can behave differently from the real configured gateway path. The explicit `providers test --model` override also drops configured provider base URLs.

This is especially visible when a launcher injects an empty provider environment variable: `buildGatewayConfig()` correctly filters the empty value and preserves the configured key, while the providers command does not use that ownership seam.

## Affected version

- `v0.42.58.0`
- commit `a25209bbb2bacf1b88e06fd5282b27f1bf4a3e7a`

## Reproduction

1. Put a valid Anthropic key and native base URL in the GBrain config plane.
2. Run from an environment where `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset or injected as an empty string.
3. Run:

```bash
gbrain providers test --touchpoint chat --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
```

`src/commands/providers.ts` currently constructs gateway config manually:

- `configureFromEnv()` copies model/base URL fields plus raw `process.env`, but does not map file-plane API keys.
- The `--model` test override passes only the model/dimensions plus raw `process.env`, dropping the configured key and configured base URL.

The result can disagree with the real CLI path that uses `buildGatewayConfig()`.

## Expected behavior

Provider listing/testing should use the same gateway configuration ownership seam as normal CLI execution. `providers test --model` should override only the requested model and embedding dimensions; credentials, base URLs, fallback config, and empty-env handling should continue to come from `buildGatewayConfig()`.

## Proposed fix

- Route `configureFromEnv()` through `buildGatewayConfig(loadConfig() ?? { engine: 'pglite' })` so the command still works before `gbrain init`.
- Add a pure `buildProviderTestGatewayConfig()` helper that starts from the canonical config and changes only the tested model/dimensions.
- Add a regression test using the repository's `withEnv()` helper to prove an empty `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` does not clobber the configured key and that configured base URLs survive the override.

## Verification

On a clean branch based directly on v0.42.58.0:

```text
bun test test/providers.test.ts test/ai/build-gateway-config.test.ts
21 pass, 0 fail
```

The repository verification suite is 30/31 on the untouched baseline and on the patch. The one pre-existing failure is unrelated: `test/e2e/openclaw-plugin-load-real.test.ts:281` resolves an undeclared parent `openclaw/plugin-sdk` type that lacks `registerContextEngine`.

An apply-ready two-file patch/commit is available.

title: fix(#1745): atomic module-singleton rebuild — no null window on reconnect; loud cycle stamp
body:
Fixes #1745 ("connect() has not been called" — concurrent minion-worker path not covered by the #1570 fix).

## Root cause
Two callers invoke `PostgresEngine.reconnect()` while a dream cycle is in flight: the minion supervisor's 3-strikes health loop and `batchRetry`'s reconnect hook.  For **module-style** engines (`poolSize` unset), `reconnect()` ran `disconnect()` + `connect()` on the **process-shared db.ts singleton**.  That opens a null window (every concurrent `getConnection()` throws the #1745 error) and `sql.end()` kills in-flight sibling queries.  The #1570 fix protected the three batch primitives after the fact, but plain phase queries (sync, synthesize bookkeeping) have no retry coverage, so the cycle's phases die.

A second defect then hides the damage: the `last_full_cycle_at` stamp ignores `updateSourceConfig`'s boolean return, so a zero-row UPDATE skips the stamp silently and the run exits 0 — `cycle_freshness` reads stale for weeks with no visible failure.  (Note: `reconnect()`'s old docstring claimed module mode no-ops; it never did — `connect()` saves config unconditionally, so the destructive path was live.)

## Fix
- **`db.rebuildConnection()`** (new): build + verify the NEW client first, swap the singleton reference, then drain the old pool in the background (`end({timeout: 5})`).  No null window, ever; in-flight queries get a graceful drain.  Fail-loud: if the fresh client cannot be built, the error propagates and the old pool is left untouched.
- **`PostgresEngine.reconnect()`**: module-style engines route through `rebuildConnection()`; instance pools keep the existing teardown+rebuild (engine-private, safe).
- **`cycle.ts` stamp**: checks the return value and warns loudly on a zero-row UPDATE instead of silently skipping.

## Proof
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; 45/45 nearest unit tests pass (cycle-last-full-cycle-at, autopilot-reconnect-classifier, retry-matcher, doctor-batch-retry).
- Live concurrency test against a real Supabase Postgres: 6 concurrent workers through 8 singleton rebuilds → **444 queries, 0 connect-class errors, 0 other errors** on the fixed path.  Negative control (old disconnect+connect sequence, same load) → **547 "connect() has not been called" errors + 83 in-flight query kills**, reproducing #1745 on demand.

## Repro pedigree
Independently reproduced on three seats (three machines, one shared brain) on 0.41.28 and 0.42.1.0; diagnostics in the #1745 thread.  Real-world impact on our fleet: a source's dream cycle silently dead for ~30 days while recall stayed healthy — the silent-stamp defect made it invisible.

title: Cache growing conversation history in Anthropic subagent tool loops
body:
**What problem does this solve?**

The native Anthropic subagent loop currently places explicit 5-minute cache breakpoints on the last tool definition and the system prompt (`src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts`). Those static prefixes cache correctly, but the growing `messages` history is not marked for caching.

On every multi-turn tool loop, prior user messages, assistant responses, tool-use blocks, and tool results are therefore sent again as ordinary input tokens. This leaves the largest growing prefix uncached even when every previous block is byte-identical.

A content-free audit of one recent production week found approximately:

- 2.26M uncached input tokens
- 179K cache-read tokens
- 33K cache-write tokens
- 60K output tokens
- cache-hit share of total input: about 7.2%

The existing system/tool caching works, but these figures suggest that conversation history dominates the remaining input cost in tool-heavy jobs.

This is separate from #2490 / #2442. Those address correct placement of static system and tool cache markers in `gateway.chat()`. They do not add a moving conversation-history breakpoint.

**What does the solution look like?**

For Anthropic subagent tool loops, cache the growing conversation prefix as well as the existing static prefixes. Two possible implementations:

1. Add Anthropic automatic caching at the request level while retaining explicit breakpoints for tools and system; or
2. Add an explicit ephemeral breakpoint to the final eligible message content block on each turn, allowing Anthropic's lookback to hit the previous turn's write.

The implementation should preserve these constraints:

- Keep tool definitions and the deterministic system prompt independently cacheable.
- Use the default 5-minute TTL initially. A 1-hour TTL should be a separate, evidence-led decision because cache writes cost more.
- Stay within Anthropic's four-breakpoint limit when static and moving breakpoints are combined.
- Apply only to providers/routes that genuinely support the relevant cache-control shape.
- Persist and expose `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` per turn and per job.
- Add request-shape tests plus a live/manual verification that turn 2 produces non-zero cache reads for turn 1's message history.
- Preserve crash replay and tool-result ordering exactly.

An acceptance test could run a two- or three-turn Anthropic tool loop with a cacheable message history and assert:

- turn 1 writes the eligible conversation prefix;
- turn 2 reads the unchanged prior history from cache;
- only the newly appended turn is processed as fresh input/cache creation;
- output and tool behaviour are unchanged.

**Alternatives considered**

- Keep caching only tools and system prompts. This leaves accumulated conversation and tool-result history at full input price.
- Use a 1-hour TTL for the current static breakpoints. This may improve reuse between separate jobs, but it does not solve uncached history within a multi-turn job and can cost more when prefixes are not reused enough.
- Implement this as a downstream patch. This belongs upstream because it is generic Anthropic tool-loop cost control and touches an active request-construction seam.

title: Upgrade-path failure: initSchema replays schema blob before migrations — chronicle index on timeline_entries(event_page_id) fails on existing brains
body:
## Summary

Upgrading an existing (v0.42.36-era) Postgres brain to v0.42.58 fails during schema bring-up with:

```
column "event_page_id" does not exist
```

Fresh installs are unaffected — only brains upgraded in place hit this.

## Root cause

`PostgresEngine.initSchema()` replays the embedded schema blob (`conn.unsafe(sqlText)`) **before** calling `runMigrations()`:

- On an existing brain, the blob's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS timeline_entries (...)` is a no-op, so the table keeps its pre-chronicle shape (no `event_page_id`).
- The blob then runs `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_timeline_event_page ON timeline_entries(event_page_id) ...` (and the partial unique dedup index), which fails because the column only arrives with migration `timeline_entries_event_page_id` (v121) — which never gets to run.

`applyForwardReferenceBootstrap` exists for exactly this class ("add forward-referenced state the embedded schema blob requires but that older brains don't have yet") but wasn't taught the chronicle wave's column.

All fresh-DB test paths pass (the blob creates the full new table), which is why this class only surfaces on real upgraded brains. Migration 122 (`facts_ontology_dimension`) is immune by design — its comment notes `facts` is migration-created and absent from the static schema, which seems like the right general convention.

## Repro

1. Any Postgres brain at schema version ≤120 (e.g. created around v0.42.36).
2. Upgrade the checkout to v0.42.58.
3. `gbrain init --migrate-only` (or any command that reaches `initSchema`) → `column "event_page_id" does not exist`.

## Workaround (clean, idempotent)

Pre-apply migration 121's own first statement, then rerun:

```sql
ALTER TABLE timeline_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_page_id INTEGER;
```

After that, `gbrain init --migrate-only` applies the pending migrations normally (verified: 115 → 122, all green, chronicle indexes created).

## Suggested fix

Either add `event_page_id` to `applyForwardReferenceBootstrap`, or adopt migration 122's convention for future waves (new tables/columns referenced by blob indexes stay migration-owned and out of the static blob until the floor version includes them).

Happy to provide more environment details if useful. Found while updating a long-lived fork to v0.42.58; the upgrade otherwise went smoothly.

title: resolveGbrainCliPath() fails inside managed-worker spawn when engine=postgres, silently blocking embed jobs
body:
## Environment
- gbrain 0.42.38.0
- 
- Host: Linux x64 VPS (Debian-based), not macOS
- 
- Engine: postgres (migrated from pglite via `gbrain migrate --to supabase --url ...`)
- 
- Runtime: reproduced identically under both Bun 1.3.14 and Node 20.20.2
- 
- Install method: git clone + bun install (documented/blessed path, not `bun install -g github:...`)
- 

## Summary
After migrating from PGLite to Postgres, running `gbrain autopilot` triggers the managed-worker dispatch path, since `useMinionsDispatch` requires `engineType === 'postgres'`. This path calls `resolveGbrainCliPath()` (src/commands/autopilot.ts), which throws:

```
Could not resolve the gbrain CLI path. Install gbrain so it is on $PATH (e.g. /usr/local/bin/gbrain), or run autopilot from the compiled binary directly.
```

...even though `gbrain` is confirmed on $PATH at the time of the crash. Manually reproducing the exact same call (`execSync('which gbrain')`) in the same shell/process context, with the same inherited env, succeeds and returns a valid path (`/usr/local/bin/gbrain` symlink -> `~/.bun/bin/gbrain` -> `src/cli.ts`). So `which gbrain` works standalone but fails specifically inside the autopilot worker-spawn code path.

## Impact
Since this only fires when `spawnManagedWorker` is true (postgres engine + minion_mode enabled), autopilot's dispatch loop still submits jobs, but no worker process ever picks them up — including embed jobs. This silently accumulates stale/missing embeddings over time with no error surfaced to the operator; `gbrain doctor` just shows a growing 'N stale chunks' warning that looks like a normal backlog, not a broken worker.

## Workaround
Running with `gbrain autopilot --no-worker` avoids the crash (dispatch-loop-only mode), but this also means embed jobs never get worked automatically — they queue but nothing processes them. Not a real fix, just avoids the loud failure.

## Suspected cause
`resolveGbrainCliPath()` (src/commands/autopilot.ts) resolution order is:
1. `execSync('which gbrain')`
2. 
2. `process.execPath` ends with `/gbrain`
3. 
3. `process.argv[1]` ends with `/gbrain`
4. 
4. throw
5. 

Worth checking whether the managed-worker spawn path runs this resolution in a context with a different/sanitized `env` (e.g. via `ChildWorkerSupervisor` passing an explicit `env` object that doesn't fully match the parent's inherited PATH at the exact moment of the `execSync` call), since a direct, identical `execSync('which gbrain')` call outside that path succeeds every time in the same shell, same PATH.

## Reproduction
1. `gbrain init --url <postgres-connection-string>` (or `gbrain migrate --to supabase --url ...` from an existing pglite brain)
2. 
2. Confirm `gbrain` resolves via `which gbrain` standalone
3. 
3. `gbrain autopilot --repo <path>` (no `--no-worker`)
4. 
4. Observe immediate throw on first cycle needing a managed worker
5. 

Also worth noting separately: the generic 'PGlite failed to initialize its WASM runtime... Most common cause: the macOS 26.3 WASM bug' wrapper message (from #223) fires on any PGLite abort regardless of host OS — it fired identically on this Linux x64 box during a genuine WAL-corruption crash unrelated to macOS. Might be worth softening that message to not assume macOS when the host is detectably something else.

title: Advance timeline, salience, and schema materialization
body:
## Header links

Local artifacts: `.humanlayer/tasks/advance-gbrain-knowledge-system/` · Local walkthrough: `.humanlayer/tasks/advance-gbrain-knowledge-system/pr-walkthrough.html`

## What problems was I solving

GBrain had three generic contract gaps that kept a well-indexed brain from materializing trustworthy structured knowledge:

1. Filesystem timeline extraction used a narrower parser than DB, stale-extraction, and trusted `put_page` paths. A readable canonical bullet such as `- YYYY-MM-DD — event` was ignored, and an incremental sync could stamp a page even though another extraction path would derive different rows.
2. Salience did not filter soft-deleted pages or distinguish routine future-effective pages from meaningful future pages. Recency-biased scoring could also feed negative age into its denominator.
3. Schema stats treated every nonempty stored type as covered, even if the active pack did not declare it. `schema_review_orphans` described active-pack conformance but returned only empty types.

This PR makes the timeline contract deterministic, makes future salience safe and explicit, and adds truthful active-pack conformance without breaking existing response fields.

## What user-facing changes did I ship

- [`src/core/link-extraction.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-15e35b73f5c590e8975e1d28807fad726eacc71c48357f09ebccff84fa173d6f) recognizes the existing bold-date forms, canonical plain-date bullets, and dated level-three headings through one validated parser.
- [`src/commands/extract.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-ae76a68f8c95649890a583b2626af1c33ab651513ab9fc31b413862aea94a8e6) routes filesystem, DB, incremental, and stale timeline extraction through that shared representation while preserving provenance and source scoping.
- [`src/commands/salience.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-24b81ca46d77f4808ac81ce6746d40e39d626f4f7d15b835021d787f77a196a7) adds `--recency-bias flat|on` and `--include-future`, with equivalent thin-client payloads.
- [`src/core/postgres-engine.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-16f634ce7f5d182a5954636ce79698778f823d3cfb05dd799f4b7ff8e08cd1c6) and [`src/core/pglite-engine.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-6bac3a1062787d9a706dede51b5bb7cc364ce09b7f1e627f2a0efb351632b5c3) exclude deleted pages and suppress future zero-signal pages unless explicitly included.
- [`src/core/schema-pack/stats.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-efbd9acdcefb96cce573545e1e9fd7df9a41914af209bd23607c7467d2c9613a) adds declared/undeclared page counts, declared coverage, and bounded undeclared-type aggregates alongside the legacy typed/untyped fields.
- [`src/core/schema-pack/review.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-6c9a8c38633101ee9a55672874225738332b0bc4ec0075e1c403a9a61be013d5) makes CLI and MCP orphan review agree on `untyped` versus `undeclared_type`, including federated source scope.
- [`src/core/advisor/collect-schema-pack.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2749/files#diff-f6031817d21c2313196eaec5614f668707b02c1a2fbac4b428813c3286c5cc3c) surfaces material active-pack drift without auto-mutation.

## How I implemented it

### Timeline materialization

`parseTimelineEntries` is now the only deterministic legacy timeline parser. `extractTimelineFromContent` is a filesystem adapter over it, and every projection maps the optional parsed source or defaults it to `markdown`. Dry-run dedup keys include provenance, so two otherwise identical events from different sources are not silently collapsed. Chronicle remains a separate event-page pipeline for eligible meetings, conversations, and calendar pages.

### Salience safety and parity

The engine contract adds an optional `includeFuture` flag; MCP exposes `include_future`. Both engines apply the same eligibility predicate:

- soft-deleted pages are always excluded;
- past/present/no-effective-date pages remain eligible even with zero structured signal;
- future pages remain eligible when they carry emotional weight or an active take;
- routine future pages require explicit opt-in.

The shared SQL ranking helper clamps age with `GREATEST(0.0, ...)`, keeping future recency finite.

### Schema conformance

The stable stored-typing metric remains unchanged. The new additive invariant is:

```text
declared_pages + undeclared_pages + untyped_pages = total_pages
```

Schema reads resolve the DB-backed active-pack tiers before classifying stored types. The shared review core returns bounded slugs, stored types, and reasons—never page bodies. Advisor findings are thresholded to avoid noise and recommend preview/read operations.

## Deviations from the plan

### Implemented as planned

- Shared parser and canonical timeline syntax, source/default behavior, Chronicle separation, source scoping, and idempotency.
- CLI/MCP future controls, deleted/future eligibility, nonnegative recency, and Postgres/PGLite parity code.
- Additive schema conformance, shared orphan-review semantics, advisor findings, public documentation, and synthetic privacy-safe tests.

### Deviations and surprises

- Advisor is whole-brain because `AdvisorContext` has no source-scope field; CLI/MCP schema stats and orphan review remain source-aware.
- No extraction-lag advisor was added because `getHealth` does not currently expose that value. Doctor remains its canonical surface.
- Low entity link/timeline findings use a ten-entity minimum to avoid noisy advice on tiny brains.
- Timeline dry-run dedup now includes provenance, a contract-consistent addition discovered while unifying parsers.

### Planned but not part of this public PR

- Private schema packs, private health content, deployment configuration, production backfills, and worker scheduling remain deliberately separate.
- Real-Postgres salience parity is encoded in `test/e2e/engine-parity-salience.test.ts`; the local Mac had no Docker/Postgres runtime, so CI is the authoritative execution lane.

## How to verify it

```bash
git fetch origin pull/2749/head:pr-2749
git worktree add ../gbrain-pr-2749 pr-2749
cd ../gbrain-pr-2749
bun install --frozen-lockfile

bun test test/link-extraction.test.ts test/extract.test.ts \
  test/extract-incremental.test.ts test/chronicle-backfill.test.ts
bun test test/salience-controls.test.ts test/recency-decay.test.ts \
  test/e2e/salience-pglite.test.ts test/e2e/v0_29-mcp-dispatch-pglite.test.ts
bun test test/schema-pack-stats.test.ts test/operations-schema-pack.test.ts \
  test/e2e/schema-cathedral.test.ts test/advisor-core.test.ts
bun run verify
```

With `DATABASE_URL` pointing at a disposable pgvector-enabled Postgres database:

```bash
bun test test/e2e/engine-parity-salience.test.ts
```

Manual checks:

- Run filesystem extraction over a page containing `- 2026-07-11 — event`; confirm one `source=markdown` timeline candidate.
- Compare `gbrain salience --json` with and without `--include-future`.
- Compare `gbrain schema stats --json` with `schema_review_orphans` over declared, undeclared, and empty-type fixtures.

## Description for the changelog

Unify timeline extraction, make future salience safe and explicit, and report active-pack schema conformance without breaking legacy metrics.

title: fix(sync): refresh freshness on no-op sync
body:
## Summary

Successful no-op syncs currently return `up_to_date` without updating `sources.last_sync_at`. That makes daily Dream/autopilot cycles that correctly find no changes look stale to `doctor sync_freshness` after the freshness window elapses.

This adds a small `markSyncChecked` helper and calls it on the pure HEAD-equality no-op path. It refreshes `last_sync_at` for source-scoped syncs without advancing `last_commit` or touching `newest_content_at`, preserving the blocked/partial-sync safety invariants.

## Test plan

- `bun test test/sync-resumable-import.serial.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

## Notes

Validated against a dogfood source where nightly Dream had been running daily with `syncStatus: up_to_date`, while `doctor` reported the source as stale because `last_sync_at` had not changed since the last content-bearing sync.

title: conversation-facts cannot run on iMessage exports: type allowlist omits imessage, 12h time-only pattern missing, multi-day date headers not anchored
body:
## Summary `extract-conversation-facts` can never run on iMessage exports, even though gbrain's own imessage-sync integration produces them. Three independent gaps stack up: 1. **Type allowlist omits iMessage.** `ALLOWED_TYPES` in `src/commands/extract-conversation-facts.ts` is `['conversation', 'meeting', 'slack', 'email']` — the `imessage` / `imessage-daily` types the integration writes are excluded, so extraction never considers those pages at all. 2. **No pattern for the time-only 12-hour message shape.** iMessage exports produce `**Speaker** (9:04 AM): text` — bold speaker, paren-wrapped 12h wall-clock time **without a date**, colon outside the bold. This falls in the gap between the `imessage-slack` builtin (requires a full `YYYY-MM-DD` inside the parens) and `bold-paren-time` (24h only, rejects an AM/PM suffix). Result: `no_match` on every line. 3. **Multi-day exports anchor every message to one fallback date.** iMessage pages commonly carry a frontmatter `date_range` plus per-day `## YYYY-MM-DD` section headers. The parser ignores markdown date headers, so every message in a multi-day page gets the single frontmatter fallback date — and facts inherit extraction-time `valid_from` instead of the conversation's real time. ## Why it matters iMessage is a first-party source (imessage-sync ships with gbrain), and conversation-facts is the feature that makes conversational sources queryable. Together these gaps mean the entire iMessage corpus silently contributes zero facts — no error, no warning, just `no_match`/skip. ## Tested fix (running in production since 2026-06-01) We've been running the three patches below on a ~43K-page Postgres brain since June 1 (currently v0.42.58.0), reapplied across every upgrade. Conversation-facts extraction on iMessage pages works end-to-end with them; the new pattern's test_negative fixtures pin the non-shadowing guarantees (24h shapes still fall through to `bold-paren-time`, full-date shapes to `imessage-slack`). (Test fixtures below are sanitized — phone numbers and message text are placeholders.)
Patch 1 — builtins.ts: bold-paren-time-12h PatternEntry ```diff --- a/src/core/conversation-parser/builtins.ts +++ b/src/core/conversation-parser/builtins.ts @@ -176,6 +176,54 @@ ], source_doc: 'OpenClaw meeting-ingestion pipeline reformat of Circleback transcripts (see your OpenClaw skills/meeting-ingestion/SKILL.md)', + }, + + { + // time-only 12-hour AM/PM variant of bold-paren-time. Matches the shape + // imessage-sync exports produce: `**Me** (9:04 AM): text` — bold speaker, + // paren-wrapped 12-hour wall-clock time WITHOUT a date, colon outside the + // bold. Falls in the gap between imessage-slack (requires a full + // `YYYY-MM-DD` date inside the parens) and bold-paren-time (24h only, + // rejects an AM/PM suffix before the closing paren). + // + // NON-SHADOW GUARANTEE: the (AM|PM) group is REQUIRED, so 24h shapes + // `(00:00)` still fall through to bold-paren-time, and imessage-slack's + // full-date shape never matches here (the leading date digits break the + // `(\d{1,2}):` anchor right after the open paren). + id: 'bold-paren-time-12h', + origin: 'builtin', + regex: /^\*\*(.+?)\*\*\s*\((\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*(AM|PM|am|pm)\)\s*:\s*(.*)$/, + captures: { + speaker_group: 1, + hour_group: 2, + minute_group: 3, + ampm_group: 4, + text_group: 5, + }, + date_source: 'frontmatter', + time_format: '12h_ampm', + timezone_policy: 'utc_assumed_with_warn', + multi_line: false, + quick_reject: /^\*\*/, + test_positive: [ + '**Me** (9:04 AM): sounds good, see you then', + '**+15555550135** (9:39 AM): Will do', + '**Alice Example** (12:00 PM): noon message', + '**Bob Example** (5:38 pm): lowercase ampm', + ], + test_negative: [ + // bold-paren-time 24h shape MUST fall through to bold-paren-time: + '**Alice** (00:00): 24h shape', + // imessage-slack full-date shape MUST fall through to imessage-slack: + '**Alice Example** (2024-03-15 9:00 AM): full-date iMessage shape', + // telegram-bracket shape: + '**[18:37] G T:** telegram bracket', + // No bold markers: + 'Alice (9:00 AM): missing the bold', + ], + source_doc: + 'Time-only 12h AM/PM iMessage export shape: `**Speaker** (H:MM AM): text` (no date in parens; date from frontmatter)', }, { ```
Patch 2 — parse.ts: ## YYYY-MM-DD section headers update the running date anchor ```diff --- a/src/core/conversation-parser/parse.ts +++ b/src/core/conversation-parser/parse.ts @@ -321,10 +321,26 @@ if (!body) return []; const out: MatchedMessage[] = []; const lines = body.split(/\r?\n/); + // markdown date headers (`## 2020-03-25`) update the running date anchor so + // multi-day exports (e.g. iMessage pages with a frontmatter date_range and + // per-day `## YYYY-MM-DD` sections) get per-day timestamps instead of + // anchoring every message to one fallback date. The running context is a + // local copy so candidate-scoring passes never mutate the caller's ctx. + const runningCtx: DateContext = { ...dateCtx }; + const DATE_HEADER_RE = /^#{1,4}\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$/; for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) { const rawLine = lines[i]; const line = rawLine.trim(); if (!line) continue; + + // date-header lines update the running anchor and are + // consumed (never treated as message continuations). + const dateHeader = DATE_HEADER_RE.exec(line); + if (dateHeader) { + runningCtx.fallbackDate = dateHeader[1]; + continue; + } // Quick-reject fast path. if (entry.quick_reject && !entry.quick_reject.test(line)) { @@ -339,7 +355,7 @@ const m = entry.regex.exec(line); if (m) { - const iso = buildIso(m, entry, dateCtx); + const iso = buildIso(m, entry, runningCtx); if (iso === null) continue; // reconstruction failed; skip line const rawSpeaker = m[entry.captures.speaker_group] ?? ''; const speaker = cleanSpeaker(rawSpeaker, entry.speaker_clean); ```
Patch 3 — extract-conversation-facts.ts: allow imessage types + anchor valid_from to segment time ```diff --- a/src/commands/extract-conversation-facts.ts +++ b/src/commands/extract-conversation-facts.ts @@ -140,7 +140,11 @@ * `--types` flag is an explicit per-run override; cycle config is * the single source of truth. */ -export const ALLOWED_TYPES = ['conversation', 'meeting', 'slack', 'email'] as const; +// upstream's allowlist omits the 'imessage' / 'imessage-daily' types that +// gbrain's own imessage-sync integration produces, so conversation-facts +// extraction can never run on iMessage pages without this. +export const ALLOWED_TYPES = ['conversation', 'meeting', 'slack', 'email', 'imessage', 'imessage-daily'] as const; export type AllowedType = (typeof ALLOWED_TYPES)[number]; /** @@ -765,6 +769,14 @@ source_markdown_slug: page.slug, source: PER_SEGMENT_SOURCE_PREFIX, source_session: sessionId, + // anchor the fact's valid_from to the segment's real conversation time + // instead of letting insertFacts default to extraction-time (now()). + // Skipped for epoch-anchored segments (parser had no real date) so those + // keep the pre-patch fallback behavior. + ...(seg.startIso && !seg.startIso.startsWith('1970-') + ? { valid_from: new Date(seg.startIso) } + : {}), context: fact.context ?? `from ${page.slug} segment ${seg.startIso}..${seg.endIso}`, })); ```
Happy to turn these into a PR if the approach looks right — the three changes are independent and could land separately (the `ALLOWED_TYPES` one-liner is the minimum to stop the silent skip).
