title: feat(dream): process BirdClaw bookmarks through OpenCode
body:
## Summary

GBrain can now process BirdClaw X bookmarks through its normal creator-pack dream lifecycle using ChatGPT OAuth through a persistent OpenCode server. BirdClaw remains a deterministic collector; GBrain owns atom extraction, evidence-backed concept synthesis, indexing, and the later graph/fact pass.

This ships the provider and dream changes together because bookmark reasoning must follow the same configured gateway, budget, receipts, and lifecycle controls as every other native GBrain workload.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  X[X bookmarks] --> B[BirdClaw collector]
  B --> M[Marked media pages]
  M --> S[gbrain sync]
  S --> E[Dream: extract_atoms]
  E --> A[Source-aware atoms]
  A --> C[Dream: synthesize_concepts]
  C --> W[Evidence-linked concepts]
  W --> D[Next normal dream pass]
  D --> G[Graph, facts, embeddings, search]
  O[OpenCode OAuth server] --> E
  O --> C
```

## Design decisions

- Media eligibility requires all 3 BirdClaw markers, so unrelated media cannot enter the extraction backlog.
- Research concepts require 2 distinct original sources. Multiple atoms from one bookmark cannot manufacture support.
- Concept pages persist bounded, source-qualified links to both original bookmarks and supporting atoms. Identical slugs in different sources remain unambiguous.
- Atom identities include a stable source digest and response ordinal, preventing same-titled insights from overwriting one another.
- Deterministic support ordering and semantic no-op detection prevent duplicate links, page rewrites, and false extraction receipts on reruns.
- Legacy transcript concepts retain count-based promotion, including mixed legacy/research groups.
- OpenCode remains behind GBrain's provider-agnostic gateway, keeping OAuth reuse, budgets, diagnostics, and fallback behavior native.

## Validation

- `bun run verify` (31 checks passed)
- 53 focused bookmark/dream tests passed
- 156 synthesis and link-extraction tests passed during autofix re-review
- BirdClaw collector-only shell and Node tests passed in the integration repository
- TypeScript typecheck passed
- Postgres dream E2E coverage was added and is gated by `DATABASE_URL`; the PGLite suite always covers the critical collision and rerun paths
- Browser testing was not applicable because the diff has no web routes or UI surface

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **Window and owner:** first 24 hours after activation; brain operator owns validation.
- **Logs:** watch for `extract_atoms`, `synthesize_concepts`, `not_in_active_pack`, `provider_unavailable`, and `cycle_already_running`.
- **Healthy signals:** extract backlog falls; native atom/concept receipts advance; concept pages have at least 2 distinct `supporting_sources`; OpenCode diagnostics show the configured `opencode-server:*` route; search resolves qualified evidence links.
- **Failure signals:** unrelated media is admitted, backlog is flat across 2 scheduled cycles, provider warnings persist, evidence links are unresolved, or legacy `build-research-wiki` commands continue after collector-only cutover.
- **Rollback trigger:** on any failure signal, restore the prior BirdClaw combined invocation, switch the active pack back to `gbrain-base-v2`, and stop native bookmark admission until diagnosed.

title: fix(minions): restore rolling conversation prompt-cache on the direct SDK path
body:
## Summary

Regression since v0.42.51 (`@ai-sdk` bump): on the direct/native subagent path (`agent.use_gateway_loop=false`), `cache_control` is only marked on the static system-prompt and last-tool-def blocks (~5.2K tokens). The `anthroMessages` array — the part of the request that actually grows every turn — carries no cache marker at all, so Anthropic re-bills the full conversation as fresh input on every turn instead of reading it from cache.

Before the regression, `cache_read_input_tokens` grew with the conversation (4.6K → 125K across a session, healthy period ≤ 2026-06-18). Since the regression, `cache_read_input_tokens` is pinned at the ~5.2K static prefix regardless of conversation length — this run alone cost ~$20 with `cacheR/in=0.000`.

## Fix

Mark the last content block of the last message with `cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'}` on every turn, keeping the immediately-preceding rolling marker in place (not stripping down to a single marker — see below) and stripping anything older. Anthropic caches everything up to the last breakpoint, so this turns the trailing marker into a rolling window over the growing conversation, staying within the 4-breakpoint limit (system + last-tool + 2 rolling = 4).

Two rolling markers, not one: Anthropic's automatic cache lookup only walks back up to 20 content blocks from a breakpoint to find a prior cached prefix ([prompt-caching docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), "20-block lookback window"). A turn that adds more than 20 blocks since the last marker (e.g. a large parallel `tool_use`/`tool_result` round) would make a freshly-placed single marker miss the previous cache entirely. Keeping the immediately-preceding rolling marker guarantees at least that marker's prefix remains a valid, already-cached read even when the new marker's own lookback comes up empty.

A fresh job's seed message is initialized with string `content` (`[{ role: 'user', content: data.prompt }]`), not a content-block array — the array-only breakpoint check would otherwise silently skip the very first API call, leaving the common single-tool round-trip (seed prompt → tool_use → tool_result → done) with zero conversation-cache benefit. Content is normalized to a one-block array before the check so the first call gets the same treatment as every later one.

## Measured impact

Forced dream run on the native path: `cacheR/in` 0.000 → 32–61 across 23 calls (cache_read grows 0 → 122K as the conversation grows; `input_tokens` drops to 1 after turn 1 — the whole conversation is read from cache). Actual cost $1.71 vs. ~$8.5 no-cache-equivalent for the same run (~80% reduction), zero dead-letter jobs.

## Why not the gateway path

Neither the gateway path (`cache_control` placed at the top level, which `@ai-sdk` 3.x silently ignores — #2490) nor #2442 (system + last-tool only) restores this; both leave the conversation body unrecovered. This fix targets the native/direct path specifically (`agent.use_gateway_loop=false`).

## Test plan
- [x] Syntax-checked via `bun build --target=bun` and `tsc --noEmit` (0 errors)
- [x] Reviewed via `codex review` (gpt-5.6-sol, high effort) across 3 iterations — both real findings (seed-message string content, 20-block lookback) fixed; final pass clean
- [x] Verified on a real dream synthesize run (cacheR/in 0.000 → 32-61, ~80% cost reduction, 0 dead-letter — see measured impact above)
- [x] Running in production on this fork's install since 2026-07-04 (v1) / 2026-07-13 (this v2 fix)

title: bug(cli): book-mirror dispatcher is unreachable in v0.42.58.0
body:
## Reproduction

On macOS with the current upstream HEAD (`a25209bbb2bacf1b88e06fd5282b27f1bf4a3e7a`, `gbrain 0.42.58.0`):

```bash
gbrain --version
# gbrain 0.42.58.0

gbrain book-mirror --help
# Usage: gbrain book-mirror
#
# gbrain book-mirror - run gbrain --help for the full command list.
```

The same result occurs when invoking the installed entrypoint directly with `bun run src/cli.ts book-mirror --help`.

## Expected

The Book Mirror help text from `src/commands/book-mirror.ts`, then normal execution via:

```bash
gbrain book-mirror --chapters-dir <path> --context-file <path> --slug <slug>
```

This matches the v0.25.1 changelog and the bundled `skills/book-mirror/SKILL.md`.

## Diagnosis

The implementation and downstream switch both exist:

- `src/commands/book-mirror.ts` exports the command implementation.
- `src/cli.ts` has `case 'book-mirror'` at ~1654.

But top-level dispatch checks `CLI_ONLY`, then `cliOps`/`cliAliases`, before reaching that later switch. `book-mirror` is not registered in `CLI_ONLY`, `cliOps`, or `cliAliases`, so it exits through the generic unknown-command path and the handler is unreachable.

`gbrain skillpack scaffold book-mirror --dry-run` copies the skill and shared conventions only (`pairedSourcesWritten: 0`), so scaffolding does not provide an alternate runnable command.

## Requested fix

Route `book-mirror` through the engine-backed command dispatcher before the shared-operation lookup, add a regression test for `gbrain book-mirror --help`, and release a tagged fix.

I am deliberately avoiding a local edit to the global install so that upgrades remain reproducible.

This matches the v0.25.1 changelog and the bundled `skills/book-mirror/SKILL.md`.

## Diagnosis

The implementation and downstream switch both exist:

- `src/commands/book-mirror.ts` exports the command implementation.
- `src/cli.ts` has `case 'book-mirror'` at ~1654.

But top-level dispatch checks `CLI_ONLY`, then `cliOps`/`cliAliases`, before reaching that later switch. `book-mirror` is not registered in `CLI_ONLY`, `cliOps`, or `cliAliases`, so it exits through the generic unknown-command path and the handler is unreachable.

`gbrain skillpack scaffold book-mirror --dry-run` copies the skill and shared conventions only (`pairedSourcesWritten: 0`), so scaffolding does not provide an alternate runnable command.

## Requested fix

Route `book-mirror` through the engine-backed command dispatcher before the shared-operation lookup, add a regression test for `gbrain book-mirror --help`, and release a tagged fix.

I am deliberately avoiding a local edit to the global install so that upgrades remain reproducible.

title: bug(subagent): fenced allowlist omits add_timeline_entry (the canonical timeline op); 4096-token turn cap + unrecovered tool_use truncation make pages >~12KB unwritable
body:
**What happened?**

> Deployment context (applies to a batch of reports filed today, all from the same production operation): ~1 week of intensive operation (2026-07-06 → 2026-07-12) of a ~7,000-page brain (6,907 indexed pages / 8,945 chunks / 100% embedded, single source) on a Mac mini against Supabase Postgres (PgBouncer transaction mode). Full native surface plus a thin custom layer: `gbrain autopilot` (launchd, KeepAlive), Minions with five sense collectors dispatching idempotency-keyed jobs, fenced triage/apply subagents from plugin defs, remote MCP over a cloudflared tunnel, hourly git backup lane. Every report was hit in real operation, has receipts (job numbers, log lines, source line numbers), and most have a local workaround deployed whose retirement is the point of filing. All source references verified against v0.42.58.0 (a25209bb).

Three interacting defects in the fenced subagent write path make it impossible for a fenced subagent to update any page beyond ~12KB:

1. **The allowlist omits gbrain's own canonical timeline op.** `BRAIN_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` (`src/core/minions/tools/brain-allowlist.ts:48-71`) includes `put_page` but not `add_timeline_entry` — with no justifying comment (the only write-exclusion comment in the file, lines 57-59, argues for excluding LINK writes specifically). Yet the compiled-truth guide (`docs/guides/compiled-truth.md:71-88`) prescribes `add_timeline_entry` for ALL timeline appends ("timeline is NOT passed" to put — put is for compiled-truth rewrites only), and `engine.addTimelineEntry` is an O(entry) idempotent insert — `ON CONFLICT (page_id, date, summary, source) DO NOTHING` (`postgres-engine.ts:3387-3392`) — that works at any page size. The allowlist blocks the canonical surface and leaves full-page-echo `put_page` as the only write path.

2. **The default subagent loop caps every turn at `max_tokens: 4096`** (`src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts:483`, the default/legacy path — the gateway loop is opt-in per lines 186-187).

3. **Truncated tool_use is not recovered.** The loop never reads `stop_reason`; tool_use blocks from a turn cut off at max_tokens are dispatched anyway (`toolDef.execute(use.input, ...)`, subagent.ts:648), so tools receive undefined/partial args silently. The file header acknowledges this: `NOT in v0.15: refusal detection, stop_reason=max_tokens partial` (subagent.ts:20).

Consequence, with receipts: job #22761 burned **26 turns / 2.8M input tokens** on 15 `put_page` calls that ALL arrived with `content` undefined against 18–21KB pages (body-append + full-page echo cannot fit a >12KB page inside a 4096-token turn). Second face of the same cap: a newer model's thinking blocks overflow the turn and return EMPTY verdicts (job #23357), forcing an older-model pin on the fenced lane. The "~12KB page cap" operators may report is not a page limit — it is the emergent artifact of these three defects.

**What did you expect?**

1. `add_timeline_entry` allowlisted for fenced subagents — it is the doctrine-prescribed append op and strictly safer than the full-echo `put_page` that IS allowlisted (idempotent, O(entry), no page-size exposure).
2. The per-turn `max_tokens` raised or made configurable.
3. Truncated tool_use to fail loudly instead of silently passing undefined args to tools.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run any fenced subagent def against a page >12KB and instruct it to record a dated update.
2. Observe it cannot use `add_timeline_entry` (not allowlisted) and falls back to `put_page`, echoing the full page.
3. Observe the 4096-token turn truncate mid-tool-call and the tool execute anyway with `content` undefined — no error raised, turn burned; the loop retries into the same wall.

**Environment**
- gbrain version: 0.42.57.0 (all source refs re-verified unchanged at 0.42.58.0 / a25209bb)
- OS: macOS 26.3.1 (Mac mini)
- Bun version: 1.3.13
- Database: Supabase Postgres (PgBouncer, transaction mode)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**
Not relevant to this defect (verified in source + job transcripts); excerpts of the burned jobs available on request.

---

Related: #1974 (subagent tool registry too narrow), #1594 (hardcoded subagent timeout silently drops output), #2606 (output truncated at maxTokens silently recorded as empty — same fail-loud class as defect 3).

Local workarounds deployed, all of which retire on a fix: LARGE-PAGE LIMIT rules in plugin subagent defs (report blocked writes instead of retrying against physics), a daily sweep surfacing blocked writes for hand-application, a truncation-retry lane, and the older-model pin.

title: bug(cycle): patterns phase reports status:ok with child_outcome:timeout and writes nothing when no subagent-capable worker slot is free — silent no-op for days; doctor's fan-out check can't see cycle-spawned subagent capacity
body:
**What happened?**

Deployment context for this batch of reports: see #2778 (same production operation, environment, and receipts discipline).

In the stock topology, the autopilot's embedded child worker is the only subagent-capable worker and runs at **concurrency 1**: `jobs work` defaults to `'1'` (`src/commands/jobs.ts:83` — `parseFlag(args, '--concurrency') ?? env.GBRAIN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY ?? '1'`), and autopilot spawns it with no `--concurrency` flag (`autopilot.ts:396`). A running autopilot-cycle therefore occupies the sole slot — **the cycle's own patterns subagent can never be claimed.**

The phase then hides the failure. In `src/core/cycle/patterns.ts`, a child `TimeoutError` sets `outcome = 'timeout'` without throwing (lines 99-102), and the phase returns `ok(...)` — which hardcodes `status: 'ok'` (patterns.ts:324-325) — with `child_outcome: 'timeout'`, `patterns_written: 0`. Every "completed" cycle's patterns phase reported ok while producing nothing, for days. Verified on jobs #23745/#23747; live-reproduced: subagent job #24262 sat WAITING through the entirety of cycle #24261.

Doctor cannot see it either: `computeAutopilotFanoutConcurrencyCheck` (`doctor.ts:1604-1637`) compares the autopilot per-source cycle fan-out against worker concurrency, reserving one slot (`effectiveSlots = max(1, concurrency - 1)`), but does not model that each RUNNING cycle additionally needs a free slot for its patterns subagent. At concurrency 1 with fan-out 1: `1 > max(1, 0)` is false → reports ok — the exact starvation case. (And when no supervisor audit event exists, the check skips entirely.)

**What did you expect?**

1. A subagent-awaiting phase should **fail loudly or run inline** when no free subagent-capable worker slot exists — never report `status: ok` on a timed-out child that wrote nothing. Silent no-op phases are the worst outage class: everything looks green while a whole judgment layer is dead.
2. The doctor fan-out check should account for **cycle-spawned subagent capacity** — including the autopilot's own embedded worker concurrency — not just cycle fan-out with a single reserved slot.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Default install (embedded worker at concurrency 1) on a brain where cycles run for minutes.
2. Let autopilot dispatch a cycle; watch the patterns child job sit WAITING while its parent occupies the only slot.
3. Observe the cycle complete with `status: ok`, `child_outcome: timeout`, `patterns_written: 0`, and `gbrain doctor` fan-out check green.

**Environment**
- gbrain version: 0.42.57.0 (source refs re-verified unchanged at 0.42.58.0 / a25209bb)
- OS: macOS 26.3.1 · Bun 1.3.13 · Supabase Postgres (PgBouncer, transaction mode)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**
Fan-out check reports ok in the failing topology (that's defect 2); excerpts on request.

---

Related: #1737 (long-job starvation family), #2278 (patterns silent skip), #2194 (fan-out clamp + doctor check, v0.42.52), #2781 (cycle budget — the two interact: short budgets kill cycles that DO get a slot; slot starvation silently no-ops the ones that survive).

Local workaround: `GBRAIN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=2` exported in the autopilot run script so the cycle's judgment child can run — an interim value pending guidance on weighing the native supervisor default against the DB connection budget.

title: bug(jobs): retry never resets started_at/attempts — the wall-clock sweep dead-letters any retry issued past the original window in under a second
body:
**What happened?**

Deployment context for this batch of reports: see #2778 (same production operation, environment, and receipts discipline).

`gbrain jobs retry` re-queues a dead job but never resets its wall-clock anchor, so any retry issued after the original window is claimed and instantly dead-lettered:

- `retryJob` (`src/core/minions/queue.ts:474-485`) resets `status/error_text/locks/delay/finished_at` — but **not** `started_at`, `attempts_made`, or `attempts_started`.
- On re-claim, `claim()` preserves the original first-claim time: `started_at = COALESCE(started_at, now())` (`queue.ts:620`) — the retry re-stamps `timeout_at` but inherits the old `started_at`.
- The wall-clock sweep `handleWallClockTimeouts()` (`queue.ts:729-749`) anchors on `started_at`: a retry claimed more than `timeout_ms * 2` after the ORIGINAL first claim immediately trips the check and is dead-lettered with `wall-clock timeout exceeded`, with `attempts_made` incrementing past max.

Observed 2026-07-11 on jobs #23954 / #24020 / #24042 / #24085 / #23990 — jobs killed by an API-credit outage, retried after the outage cleared: every retry died in **under 1 second**, displaying `attempt 4/3`. Retry is therefore useless for exactly the case it exists for: recovering work after an outage that lasted longer than the job's timeout.

**What did you expect?**

On explicit `jobs retry`: clear `started_at` (so re-claim re-stamps it) and reset `attempts_made`/`attempts_started`. An operator explicitly retrying a dead job is asserting "run this fresh."

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a job with `timeout_ms` T; let it die (e.g. worker down / provider outage).
2. Wait > 2×T.
3. `gbrain jobs retry <id>` → job is claimed, then dead-lettered `wall-clock timeout exceeded` in <1s with the attempt counter past max.

**Environment**
- gbrain version: 0.42.57.0 (source refs re-verified unchanged at 0.42.58.0 / a25209bb)
- OS: macOS 26.3.1 · Bun 1.3.13 · Supabase Postgres (PgBouncer, transaction mode)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**
Not relevant (jobs-engine defect; job rows available on request).

---

Related: #1737 (wall-clock attempt accounting — this is the retry-side gap in the same machinery), #1014 (wall-clock cap tuning).

Operational note for anyone hitting this today: for slot-keyed collector work, do NOT hand-retry — the next slot's sweep with unburned idempotency keys re-covers the missed window naturally (verified here: missed digests self-covered on later slots).

title: feat(jobs): plugin-registered job handlers loadable by jobs work — plugins ship subagent defs only, forcing two-worker topologies
body:
**What problem does this solve?**

Deployment context for this batch of reports: see #2778 (same production operation, environment, and receipts discipline).

`GBRAIN_PLUGIN_PATH` plugins can ship **subagent defs only**. Verified at HEAD (a25209bb): the plugin manifest has no handler field (`src/core/minions/plugin-loader.ts:39-45` — `name, version, plugin_version, subagents?, description?`), `loadSinglePlugin` reads only `subagents/*.md` (lines 155-229), and the trust-policy docstring is explicit (lines 21-26): plugins "cannot declare new tools." The job-handler registry is an in-process `Map` populated exclusively by hardcoded `worker.register(...)` calls (`worker.ts:153,230-236`; `src/commands/jobs.ts:1323-2114`).

Consequence: any deployment with deterministic collector/apply job handlers is forced into a **two-worker topology** — a custom worker process for site-local handlers, plus the autopilot's embedded child for builtins (including `subagent`). That means two supervised processes, two concurrency stories, ~2× the DB connections, and it is the exact seam where the subagent-capacity starvation lived (#2782 — the patterns silent no-op). An independent from-scratch design exercise against v0.42.57's native surfaces converged on the same forced shape: the one-worker design is foreclosed purely by this gap, not by anything architectural.

**What does the solution look like?**

Let plugins register custom job handlers that `gbrain jobs work` loads — the same conformance/trust pattern as subagent defs (manifest-declared, path-loaded, name-spaced). One worker then runs builtins + site-local handlers, with one concurrency budget and one supervision story.

**Alternatives considered**

A standing custom worker process (launchd, KeepAlive) registering collector/apply handlers, with its own test harness — deployed here and working, but it is a whole second supervised process that exists only because handlers can't ride the native worker. Consolidates to one worker the day handler plugins ship.

---

Environment: gbrain 0.42.57.0 (verified unchanged at 0.42.58.0 / a25209bb) · macOS 26.3.1 · Bun 1.3.13 · Supabase Postgres (PgBouncer transaction mode).

title: bug(sources): archive collapses already-archived into a reasonless "Failed to archive" — not idempotent, no diagnostic, pushes operators toward destructive remove
body:
**What happened?**

Deployment context for this batch of reports: see #2778 (same production operation, environment, and receipts discipline).

`gbrain sources archive <id>` failed twice in a row with no reason printed (just `Failed to archive source "<id>".`) on an isolated code source; `sources remove --confirm-destructive` then worked. Reproduced 2026-07-08 on v0.42.57.

From source at HEAD (a25209bb), the silent path — and a correction to our own first diagnosis (it is NOT a code-source type check; archive is fully type-agnostic):

- `runArchive` (`src/commands/sources.ts:484-510`): after the existence check passes, the only non-throwing failure is `softDeleteSource` returning null, which `runArchive` collapses into the generic reason-free error at `:505`.
- `softDeleteSource` (`src/core/destructive-guard.ts:180-198`) is a guarded UPDATE — `WHERE id = $1 AND archived = false` (`:194`) — returning null on 0 rows (`:198`). So the null means precisely **"the source is already archived"**, and the error message discards that: it doesn't say "already archived", doesn't distinguish it from anything else, and exits 4. Repeated attempts produce the identical opaque failure (archive is not idempotent), which is exactly what pushes an operator to the destructive `remove` instead — trading a soft archive for a hard cascade delete just to get an operation that reports what it did.

**What did you expect?**

`archive` on an already-archived source should say so — and arguably exit 0 (idempotent: the desired state holds). Any other 0-row outcome should be distinguished from it. The one-line shape: have `softDeleteSource` (or `runArchive`) check `archived` state when the guarded UPDATE hits 0 rows and report it.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `gbrain sources archive <id>` on any source → succeeds.
2. Run the same command again → `Failed to archive source "<id>".`, exit 4, no reason. (Matches the field observation where the first archive's outcome wasn't visible to the operator.)

**Environment**
- gbrain version: 0.42.57.0 (source refs re-verified unchanged at 0.42.58.0 / a25209bb)
- OS: macOS 26.3.1 · Bun 1.3.13 · Supabase Postgres (PgBouncer, transaction mode)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**
Not relevant (CLI diagnostics defect).

title: bug(cli): sync --install-cron exists only in help text — no handler; it silently runs an ordinary sync instead of installing anything
body:
**What happened?**

Deployment context for this batch of reports: see #2778 (same production operation, environment, and receipts discipline).

The top-level help advertises a sync daemon installer:

```
sync --install-cron                Install persistent sync daemon
```
(`src/cli.ts:2231`)

No handler exists. A whole-tree grep finds `install-cron` nowhere else; `runSync` (`src/commands/sync.ts:3281`, flag parsing `:3351-3372`) never references it, the `sync --help` usage block doesn't list it, and unknown flags aren't validated — so `gbrain sync --install-cron` **silently performs an ordinary one-off incremental sync**. An operator now believes scheduled syncing is installed; nothing is.

That's worse than dead surface area: it manufactures false confidence in the exact durability layer (freshness syncs) operators reach for it to secure.

**What did you expect?**

Either implement it or delete the help line. Observation from production in favor of deletion: autopilot already owns freshness syncs (44 sync jobs/24h observed on this deployment) — a separate sync cron may be a competing scheduler rather than a missing feature. If deleted, a `--help` pointer at autopilot's role closes the loop; if implemented, unknown-flag validation in `runSync` would have caught this class from the start.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `gbrain --help` → note the `sync --install-cron` line.
2. `gbrain sync --install-cron` → observe a normal sync run; no cron/launchd/systemd artifact created anywhere.

**Environment**
- gbrain version: 0.42.57.0 (source refs re-verified unchanged at 0.42.58.0 / a25209bb)

title: fix(gateway,subagent): persist tool results per turn, drop null-text blocks on conversion
body:
> **Final update (2026-07-13):** PR description rewritten after thorough investigation + 3 rounds of batch testing totaling ~60 test submissions. See [#2803](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/2803) and [vercel/ai#17144](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/17144) for upstream bug reports.

---

## Summary

Fixes two distinct subagent bugs that together caused ~85-92% subagent job failure in nightly dream-cycle batch processing. Both bugs live in the AI SDK tool-loop and message-conversion code paths (`src/core/ai/gateway.ts`, `src/core/minions/handlers/subagent.ts`).

After this PR: **MissingToolResultsError → 0 cases. InvalidPromptError → retry recovery at ~97.5%**. Expected production success rate is now ~97.5% (with the remaining ~2.5% transient failures recoverable on retry).

---

## Bug A: InvalidPromptError (~85-92% of failures)

### Root Cause

A dual interface mismatch between gbrain's `ChatBlock` (internal) and AI SDK v6's `ModelMessage` (SDK layer):

1. **`modelMessageSchema` (Zod validation, AI SDK core):** expects tool-call content parts to have field name **`args`**
2. **Wire converter (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` v2.x):** reads tool-call content parts using field name **`input`**

gbrain's `toModelMessages` function (the translation seam from `ChatBlock` → `ModelMessage`) was sending only `input`. This caused:

- **Any job ≥ 2 turns:** Zod rejection at `standardizePrompt()` because `args` was missing → 100% deterministic failure
- **Fresh 1-turn jobs:** passed through (no tool-call blocks in messages yet), so ~8-13% of jobs randomly succeeded

The Zod v4 `discriminatedUnion` lazy initialization in the AI SDK **also** has a mild race condition (~50% first-call failure), which compounded the problem but was not the primary cause.

### Fix (gateway.ts:2422)

Dual-field emission for tool-call blocks, satisfying both consumers:

```typescript
// BEFORE (missing args → Zod rejects):
{ type: 'tool-call', toolCallId, toolName, input: b.input }

// AFTER (both args for Zod + input for wire converter):
{ type: 'tool-call', toolCallId, toolName, args: b.input, input: b.input }
```

### Additional Defensive Changes (gateway.ts)

1. **User text-only content → string** (line 2408): `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` rejects `{type:'text', text:'...'}` in user content arrays. When retry loads messages from DB (stored as block arrays), flatten to bare string.
2. **Null-text block filtering** (line 2411, inherited from prior InvalidPrompt fix for reasoning models)
3. **`bun update ai`** (6.0.174 → 6.0.224): picks up Zod v4 compatibility fixes

---

## Bug B: MissingToolResultsError (~15% of failures, DETERMINISTIC CRASH)

### Root Cause

gbrain's `toolLoop` (gateway.ts) calls `generateText()` with tool-call blocks in the assistant's response, then the model provider validates that every tool-call has a matching tool-result in the messages. The original code **did not persist** tool results between `chat()` calls — they were reconstructed from ephemeral in-memory state.

On subagent retry (which reloads conversation from DB), the reloaded messages contained assistant tool-call blocks but **no matching tool-result blocks**, causing `convertToLanguageModelPrompt` to throw `MissingToolResultsError`. This was **deterministic**: every multi-turn job that crashed and retried would die on the next turn.

### Fix (subagent.ts, gateway.ts)

1. **`onTurnComplete` callback** (subagent.ts): persists each toolLoop iteration's assistant (tool-calls) + matching user (tool-results) messages to `subagent_messages` table
2. **Message reconstruction** (subagent.ts `runSubagentViaGateway`): on retry, loads persisted tool-call/tool-result pairs from DB. `toolLoop` receives `replayState` with complete prior messages including tool results.
3. **`toModelMessages` tool-role conversion**: user messages with tool-result blocks are converted to `{role:'tool', content:[...]}` for AI SDK's three-role (user/assistant/tool) message schema

---

## Testing Results

Clean single-job test (20632, 3 turns with brain_search tools, dual-field + onTurnComplete fixes active):
```
Status:     completed
Attempts:   1/3 (started: 2 — attempt 1 InvalidPrompt, retry succeeded)
Turns:      3
Tokens:     41,729 in / 1,856 out
Output:     Full synthesis page with 7 sections, 10 cross-links to existing brain pages
MissingToolResults:  0
InvalidPrompt:      triggered on attempt 1, recovered on retry
```

---

## Related

- Closes #2273 (MissingToolResultsError)
- Closes #2609 (subagent crash-replay)
- Closes #2488 (InvalidPrompt from reasoning model null-text)
- References #2803 (remaining InvalidPrompt from AI SDK Zod race condition)
- References vercel/ai#17144 (upstream AI SDK bug report)

---

## Remaining Issue

~50% of first `generateText()` calls in a process hit a Zod v4 `discriminatedUnion` race in AI SDK v6's `modelMessageSchema`. This is an **AI SDK internal bug** — retry with freshTools + backoff recovers it. The fix for this requires waiting for an AI SDK v7 upgrade (breaking API changes) or an upstream Zod v4 patch. Current recovery rate: **~97.5%** on retry.

title: subagent: InvalidPrompt (ModelMessage[] schema) from AI SDK v6 Zod discriminator race — 87% failure
body:
## Problem

Subagent jobs using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider (`deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash`) fail with `Invalid prompt: The messages do not match the ModelMessage[] schema` at ~85-92% rate.

## Root Cause

AI SDK v6.0.174's `standardizePrompt()` caches an internal Zod v4 `modelMessageSchema` (a `discriminatedUnion('role', ...)`). This schema has a race condition during lazy initialization on the first `generateText()` call — ~50% of calls reach an inconsistent discriminator-key state, rejecting structurally valid messages.

## Evidence

- 16 test jobs: 2 completed, 14 dead (87.5%)
- All dead: identical InvalidPrompt error
- Zod cause chain: discriminator resolves to wrong branch, `text` claimed as `undefined` when actual value is valid string
- Retry with 2s backoff recovers ~50%, proving non-deterministic (not a data issue)
- Error persists across all 3 retry attempts for jobs that die

## Affected

- `ai` v6.0.174, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` v2.0.45, Zod v4
- `MissingToolResultsError` is fully resolved (PR #2802) — this is the sole remaining failure

## Workarounds Applied (Partial)

title: fix(think): give thinking-default Claude 5 models output-token headroom
body:
## Problem

`gbrain think` returns an empty answer with `synthesisOk: false` (warning `LLM_OUTPUT_NOT_JSON`) on harder questions when `models.think` is set to a Claude 5 family model such as `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5`, even though retrieval succeeds (pages gathered fine). The nightly auto-think path hits the same failure (`status: partial`).

## Root cause

On Claude Sonnet 5 (and the rest of the Claude 5 family), adaptive thinking runs **by default** when the `thinking` parameter is omitted, and `max_tokens` is a hard cap on **thinking + response text combined**. `runThink` calls the LLM with `max_tokens: 4000` (`DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) and no thinking config, so on hard questions the model spends the entire 4000-token budget on thinking and returns zero text blocks. `chat()` extracts only text parts, `tryParseJSON("")` fails, and think degrades to an empty answer.

## Repro / verification

- `models.think = anthropic:claude-sonnet-5`, two multi-page synthesis questions → ~50s of generation, then `answer: ""`, `warnings: [LLM_OUTPUT_NOT_JSON, CITATIONS_REGEX_FALLBACK]`, `synthesisOk: false` (pagesGathered 20/24, so retrieval was healthy).
- With the headroom, the exact same questions return full cited answers. Simple questions were unaffected before and after (little thinking needed).

## Change

Resolve the max_tokens default per model in `runThink`:

- **16000** for thinking-by-default Claude 5 family models (`/^anthropic[:\/]claude-[a-z0-9]+-5(?:[.-]|$)/`) — their output ceilings are ≥ 64K, so the higher request is always valid.
- **4000 (unchanged)** for everything else, so models and providers with lower output ceilings (local Ollama models, older small models) are not regressed by an unconditionally higher request.

Gate behavior verified: `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-fable-5` → 16000; `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `ollama:*`, `claude-3-haiku` → 4000. Note the request stays within the 300s `AI_CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS` for realistic generation speeds.

A nicer follow-up could source per-model output ceilings from the provider recipes and/or make this configurable (e.g. `models.think_max_tokens`), but this restores correctness for thinking-default models without touching other paths.

title: putPage defaults chunker_version to 1 on INSERT, causing perpetual doctor warning
body:
`postgres-engine.ts:990` uses `COALESCE(${chunkerVersion}::smallint, 1)` in the INSERT. When callers don't supply `chunker_version` (which no MCP/subagent caller does — it's internal metadata), new pages land at version 1.

The `importFromFile` path correctly stamps `MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION` (currently 3), but dream subagents write through `putPage` directly — their pages get v1. Doctor then flags them as "older chunker_version" in the `contextual_retrieval_coverage` check forever.

The pages are actually chunked and embedded correctly at write time (embedding coverage stays 100%). Only the metadata column is wrong.

**Impact:** On an active brain with dream running twice daily, doctor fires `contextual_retrieval_coverage: warn` continuously. Running `reindex --markdown` clears it, but it recurs the next cycle.

**Fix (one line):**

```diff
- COALESCE(${chunkerVersion}::smallint, 1)
+ COALESCE(${chunkerVersion}::smallint, ${MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION})
```

Import `MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION` from `../core/chunkers/recursive.ts` (already imported elsewhere in the codebase).

The COALESCE-preserve on UPDATE is correct (don't regress pages already at a higher version). Only the INSERT default needs the bump.

title: `extract_atoms` slug (`slice(0,60)`) can end in a hyphen; import's `slugifyPath` strips it → duplicate atom on export→sync round-trip
body:
**Type:** bug · **Area:** cycle/extract-atoms slug vs sync slugifyPath

### Summary
`extract_atoms` builds atom slugs as `atoms/<date>/<slugify(title)>` where
`slugify` (`src/core/cycle/extract-atoms.ts`) ends with `.slice(0, 60)` and does
**not** strip a trailing hyphen left by the truncation. So a long title can
yield a DB slug like `…-maturity-is-`.

`gbrain export --type atom` writes that page to `…-maturity-is-.md`. On the next
`gbrain sync`, the importer derives the slug via `slugifyPath` →
`slugifySegment` (`src/core/sync.ts`), which **does** strip the trailing hyphen
→ `…-maturity-is`. The stripped slug doesn't match the original, so sync creates
a **new** page and orphans the original — a duplicate atom (same content, same
`source_hash`, two slugs differing only by a trailing `-`).

### Reproduce
1. Get an atom whose 60-char-truncated title-slug ends on a hyphen (observed 4
   of 23 in one run).
2. `gbrain export --type atom --dir <repo>` then `gbrain sync`.
3. Observe `+N added` where N = number of trailing-hyphen atoms, and two atoms
   per affected `source_hash` (one file-backed stripped slug, one db-only
   `…-`).

### Fix
Make the two slug functions agree: have `extract_atoms`' `slugify` strip
trailing/leading hyphens after the `slice(0,60)` (i.e. `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g,'')`
post-slice), matching `slugifySegment`. Then extract-time and import-time slugs
round-trip.

### Workaround (in use downstream)
After export, rename `atoms/**/*-.md` → `*.md` and prune db-only atoms whose
slug has no backing file.

title: `synthesize_concepts` produces 0 concepts because `extract_atoms` never writes the `concepts:` field it clusters on (structural)
body:
**Type:** bug · **Area:** cycle / lens packs (extract_atoms + synthesize_concepts)

### Summary
On a brain running the creator/everything lens (or any pack that declares the
`extract_atoms` + `synthesize_concepts` phases), `extract_atoms` produces good
atoms, but `synthesize_concepts` **always yields 0 concepts** — regardless of
corpus size. Root cause: the two phases disagree on the join key.

- `synthesize_concepts` groups atoms **exclusively** by each atom's
  `frontmatter.concepts` array (`src/core/cycle/synthesize-concepts.ts`, the
  `SELECT … WHERE frontmatter->>'concepts' …` filter + the group-by over
  `atom.concept_refs`). If no atom has that field it returns early:
  `status:'skipped', summary:'synthesize_concepts: no atoms with concept refs'`.
- `extract_atoms`' `EXTRACT_PROMPT` (`src/core/cycle/extract-atoms.ts`) asks the
  model for `{title, atom_type, body, source_quote, lesson, virality_score,
  emotional_register}` — **there is no `concepts` (or `tags`) field in the
  schema**, so the written atom pages never carry `frontmatter.concepts`.

There is no fallback clustering (no tag-based, no embedding/topic clustering),
so the concept tier (T1–T4) can never populate from a fresh extraction.

### Reproduce
1. Activate a pack that declares both phases.
2. Feed a corpus (transcripts via `dream.synthesize.session_corpus_dir`, or
   `meeting`-typed pages) and run `gbrain dream --phase extract_atoms`.
3. Confirm atoms exist but none has a `concepts` field:
   `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE frontmatter ? 'concepts') FROM pages WHERE type='atom';`
   → **0** (observed: 0 of 26 atoms).
4. Run `gbrain dream --phase synthesize_concepts` →
   `synthesize_concepts: no atoms with concept refs` in ~0.1s, **0 concepts**.

### Expected
Either (a) `extract_atoms` emits a `concepts:` array (topic/theme tags) per
atom, or (b) `synthesize_concepts` clusters by an available signal (tags,
embeddings, or title/lesson similarity) when `concepts:` is absent. Today the
producer and consumer are wired to different fields, so the concept half of the
lens is a guaranteed no-op.

### Note: the intended writer appears to have been dropped
`synthesize-concepts.ts` (top-of-file comment) states the field is populated
"when the Haiku 3-check from extract_atoms decides 'this atom is about concept
X', it stamps the field" — but no such step exists in the current
`extract-atoms.ts` (the prompt and the whitelist parser have no `concepts`
field). So the producer was assumed to live inside `extract_atoms` but was never
implemented (or removed). Meanwhile the ingest-side skills (signal-detector,
idea-ingest, voice-note-ingest) write concept **pages** directly, bypassing
atoms — so there are effectively two disjoint concept paths, and the
atom-frontmatter one has no writer.

### Impact
`dream` becomes an atom/Take layer only; the advertised "atoms → tier-promoted
concepts" pipeline never completes without manual `concepts:` tagging.

title: No tick-level (whole-cycle) budget cap; a full `dream` tick's cost is the unbounded sum of ~19 per-phase budgets
body:
**Type:** enhancement · **Area:** cycle / budget-meter

> **Author's correction (for honesty):** an earlier internal note claimed a
> single phase blew past its cap ("$8+ in propose_takes past a $5 cap"). That
> was a measurement error — the `dream-budget-YYYY-Www.jsonl` ledger is
> **weekly** and `cumulative_cost_usd` **resets per run**; summing
> `estimated_cost_usd` across a whole week's rows conflated ~7 separate runs.
> Re-checked: **max per-run cumulative was $1.20, well under the $5 cap.** The
> per-phase gate works. The real, narrower observation is below.

### Summary
Each cycle phase enforces its own budget cap via `BaseCyclePhase` +
`src/core/cycle/budget-meter.ts` (`budgetUsdKey`/`budgetUsdDefault`, e.g.
`cycle.propose_takes.budget_usd=5`, `cycle.extract_atoms.budget_usd=0.3`,
`cycle.calibration_profile.budget_usd=0.5`, …). These **work**: the meter
refuses the next submit once a phase's cumulative estimate exceeds that phase's
cap.

What's missing is a **cycle-level aggregate cap**. A full `dream` tick runs ~19
phases; several are LLM-backed, each with its own independent budget. The tick's
total spend is therefore the **sum** of all per-phase caps (order of $10–20+
depending on config), with no single knob bounding a whole tick. The only
effective backstop for total tick spend is the workspace/provider credit limit.

### Suggestion
Add an optional `cycle.budget_usd` (whole-tick) cap that the budget meter
threads across phases and that halts the remaining phases once the tick total is
reached — analogous to the per-phase caps but at the cycle level. Even a
`--max-cost` flag on `gbrain dream` would let operators bound an unattended tick.

### Why it matters
For unattended/cron `dream` on metered API credits, operators reason about
"what can one nightly tick cost me" — today that answer requires summing every
phase's cap by hand, and nothing enforces the sum.

title: `grade_takes` ships a placeholder evidence retriever + `calibration_profile` defaults to a hardcoded holder name
body:
**Type:** bug · **Area:** cycle / hindsight calibration (grade_takes + calibration_profile)

### Summary
Two coupled gaps make the take-calibration half of the cycle a near-no-op on a
stock brain:

1. **`grade_takes` evidence retriever is a stub.** `defaultEvidenceRetriever`
   (`src/core/cycle/grade-takes.ts`, ~L294-305) returns only the take's own
   claim text as "evidence" — it is explicitly documented as not-yet-wired to
   real hybrid-search retrieval. With no external evidence, the judge has
   nothing to grade against, so most verdicts land `unresolvable`. The phase
   runs, spends (Sonnet), and writes cache rows, but produces no usable
   resolutions.
2. **`calibration_profile` holder defaults to a hardcoded name.** The phase
   scores `opts.holder ?? '<hardcoded-default-name>'` (`calibration-profile.ts`),
   and the nightly cycle dispatch (`cycle.ts`, the `runPhaseCalibrationProfile`
   call site) passes `{}` — so on every operator's brain it computes the profile
   for the maintainer's default holder name, not the actual brain owner, unless
   a caller threads `opts.holder`. Combined with (1) rarely reaching ≥5 resolved
   takes, the profile stays empty/mis-attributed.

### Reproduce
1. Accumulate takes with `since_date` ≥6 months old; run
   `gbrain dream --phase grade_takes`. Observe verdicts dominated by
   `unresolvable` and no real evidence in `take_grade_cache`.
2. Run `gbrain dream --phase calibration_profile` on a brain whose owner is not
   the hardcoded default holder; observe the profile row is keyed to the default
   holder name, not the owner.

### Expected
(a) Wire `grade_takes` evidence retrieval to the real hybrid-search/graph path
so verdicts can resolve; (b) derive `calibration_profile`'s default holder from
the brain owner/identity config instead of a hardcoded literal, or thread
`opts.holder` from the cycle dispatch.

### Impact
The "surfaces conflicts between takes + facts / brain-consistency" value
advertised for the daily cycle does not materialize on a default install: takes
are proposed and stored but effectively never graded or calibrated.

title: fix(gateway): consolidate tool-loop resume + provider fixes — fix-wave A (supersedes 15 PRs)
body:
Fix-wave A — consolidates the **gateway tool-loop duplicate cluster + adjacent provider fixes** into one content-deduped, tested change. Re-implemented from the best of each PR (deduped by content, not file overlap); every fix carries test coverage.

## Supersedes 15 PRs (from 11 contributors)

**Gateway tool-loop resume** (10 + test): #1934, #2062, #2065, #2112, #2274, #2487, #2336, #2257, #2499, #2491, test #2063
**Adjacent provider fixes** (4): #2614, #2806 (max-output-tokens), #2617 (DeepSeek `reasoning_content`), #2572 (OpenRouter key + `KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS`)

## What it does

- **Tool-loop resume:** `toolLoop` persists the tool-result user turn per round, so a resumed subagent reloads a *balanced* transcript instead of dangling assistant tool-calls that non-Anthropic providers reject (`AI_MissingToolResultsError`). `runSubagentViaGateway` reconciles an already-corrupted transcript on resume — heals every dangling turn from settled `subagent_tool_executions`, re-dispatches idempotent-pending tools, throws on non-idempotent; terminal early-return once the transcript reached `end_turn`.
- **`repairToolPairing()`** last-resort normalization at the `chat()` boundary — back-fills error stubs for any unanswered assistant tool-call (partial turns, provider-duplicated/dropped IDs on local models, truncated batches). No-op on balanced input.
- **`toModelMessages` is Date-safe** — Postgres `timestamptz` → ISO via a JSON round-trip at the SDK boundary, **never a `::jsonb` cast**; drops non-string reasoning blocks AI SDK v6 rejects.
- **Model-aware default max output tokens** — thinking-by-default Claude 5 models get headroom (gateway 32000 / think 16000), everything else stays 4096/4000 so DeepSeek/OpenAI subagents don't exceed provider caps.
- **DeepSeek:** promote `reasoning_content` into `content` when content is empty (fail-open recipe shim).
- **OpenRouter:** map `openrouter_api_key` (config + env) into `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`; register `agent.use_gateway_loop`, zeroentropy, openrouter keys in `KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS`.

## Invariants preserved
JSONB (no `JSON.stringify` into `::jsonb`), engine parity (PGLite ⇄ Postgres), source isolation, trust boundary.

## Verification
- **`gbrain-pr-test-env` consumer matrix:** clawlancer/Postgres, gstack + hivemindos/PGLite — baseline-FAIL → candidate-PASS on the same repro.
- **`bun run verify` 31/31** · **439 targeted unit + e2e tests.**
- Scope: 15 files, +1,143 / −27.

## ⚠️ Pre-merge todos (not done — raw fix per fix-wave convention)
- [ ] **VERSION + CHANGELOG bump** (currently `0.42.59.0` == master → version-gate red until bumped). Land via `/ship`.
- [ ] Rebase if master moves before merge.
- [ ] On merge: close the 15 superseded PRs with contributor thank-you comments.

Contributor attribution preserved via `Co-Authored-By:` trailers on the commit.

title: query_cache ignores hard-exclude config — cached results leak GBRAIN_SEARCH_EXCLUDE'd slugs across processes
body:
**Version**: 0.42.59.0, postgres engine

**Summary**: `knobsHash` (`src/core/search/mode.ts`) does not include the resolved hard-exclude configuration (`GBRAIN_SEARCH_EXCLUDE` env / per-call `exclude_slug_prefixes`). Since the cache row id is `(query, source, knobsHash)`, two processes with *different* exclude configs share the same cache row — whichever runs first poisons the other.

**Repro**:
1. Have pages under a prefix you exclude, e.g. `GBRAIN_SEARCH_EXCLUDE="private/"` on your serve daemon.
2. From a shell **without** the env (e.g. a non-interactive script shell), run `gbrain query "..."` — results legitimately include `private/` pages, and the row is cached.
3. From a process **with** the env, run the same query — it returns the cached row, `private/` pages included. The hard exclude is silently bypassed.
4. The reverse also holds: an env-set query caches filtered results, so a deliberate opt-out query (`GBRAIN_SEARCH_EXCLUDE= gbrain query ...`) silently gets pre-filtered results.

**Impact**: hard excludes act as a privacy/scoping control (the docs position them as such), but the cache makes them nondeterministic across processes. In our deployment (serve daemon with env + occasional CLI shells without), we found **82 poisoned cache rows** in production before noticing.

**Suggested fix**: include the resolved hard-exclude list (sorted, comma-joined) in the `knobsHash` parts and bump `KNOBS_HASH_VERSION` (the code comment there already mandates the bump when adding a knob). Per-call `exclude_slug_prefixes`/`include_slug_prefixes` likely need the same treatment.

**Workaround we're using**: guarantee identical env for every process (moved the export to `~/.zshenv`) and purge poisoned rows: `DELETE FROM query_cache WHERE results::text LIKE '%<excluded-prefix>%'`.

title: sync --full reconcile deletes every subdirectory page on Windows (source_path separator mismatch) — total source data loss
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `gbrain sync --full` deletes **every page whose `source_path` contains a directory separator** when those pages were written with forward-slash paths (e.g. by capture/write-through operations). In our case the full-sync reconcile hard-deleted 1,215 of 1,224 pages in a capture-origin source. Root-level pages (`readme`, `schema`, etc. — no separator in the path) survive, which is the diagnostic fingerprint.

Version: 0.42.59.0, Postgres engine, Windows 11 host (Postgres in WSL2, CLI via bun on Windows).

## Root cause

`src/commands/sync.ts`, full-sync reconcile (~line 3104 in 0.42.59):

```ts
const current = new Set(
  collectSyncableFiles(repoPath, { strategy: opts.strategy ?? 'markdown' })
    .map(abs => relative(repoPath, abs)),
);
```

On Windows, Node's `relative()` returns **backslash** paths (`processes\2026\07\file.md`). But `pages.source_path` can be stored with **forward slashes** — in our brain, every page created by the capture op had `processes/2026/07/file.md`. The membership test

```ts
&& !current.has(r.source_path)
```

then fails for every subdirectory page, so the reconcile classifies the entire corpus as "backing file removed" and deletes it, while the import phase in the same run happily reports those very files as `skipped (unchanged)` (its comparison normalizes differently).

The comment above the reconcile explicitly worries about this class ("otherwise every page looks stale and the reconcile would wrongly delete live pages") — the separator dimension is the missed case.

## Reproduction

1. Windows host, Postgres engine.
2. Create pages in a source via a write path that stores forward-slash `source_path` values under subdirectories (capture ops do this), with matching files in the repo working tree.
3. `gbrain sync --source <id> --repo <path> --full --no-pull --yes`
4. Observe: `Reconciled N stale page(s) whose source file was removed.` where N ≈ every subdirectory page; import phase in the same run reported the same files as unchanged.

## Suggested fix

Normalize separators on **both** sides of the membership test (e.g. `.replace(/\\/g, '/')`), the same way other path-handling in the codebase does. A belt-and-braces addition: refuse to reconcile-delete more than some fraction (e.g. >50%) of a source's pages in one run without an explicit flag — a mass delete of an entire live source is almost always a comparison bug, and this failure mode is total data loss for users without backups.

## Impact

Total loss of a source's pages (recoverable only from backups). Incremental syncs are unaffected (the reconcile runs on the `--full` path).

title: fix(sync): normalize path separators + mass-delete safety valve in full-sync reconcile (#2828)
body:
Fixes #2828 (Windows reconcile mass-delete).

## What was happening

On a full sync (`gbrain sync --full`), after re-importing the tree the reconcile step deletes pages whose backing file is gone: it builds a set of the working tree's repo-relative paths and deletes any file-backed page whose stored `source_path` is not in that set.

The membership test compared paths without normalizing separators. On a Windows checkout `path.relative` yields backslash-separated paths (`topics\foo.md`), while a page's stored `source_path` can hold forward slashes (`topics/foo.md`) — e.g. when it was written from a git-derived path. Every file-backed page then failed the membership test, looked stale, and the reconcile deleted the entire source.

## The fix

1. **Separator normalization on both sides of the membership test.** The working-tree set entries and each `source_path` are compared through a shared `.replace(/\\/g, '/')`, so a page written with either separator matches on any OS.

2. **Mass-delete safety valve.** A reconcile that would sweep more than 50% of the file-backed pages a sync strategy manages, on a source that holds more than 20 of them, is almost always a path-comparison bug or the wrong repo path — not a genuine bulk deletion. In that case the reconcile now skips the delete and prints a loud warning instead of silently wiping the brain. The escape hatch `GBRAIN_ALLOW_MASS_RECONCILE=1` restores the old behavior for the rare intentional bulk removal.

The decision is factored into pure, exported helpers (`planReconcileDeletes`, `massReconcileAllowed`) so the separator matching, the valve threshold, and the env override are unit-testable without a live engine or a Windows host. `massReconcileAllowed` mirrors the existing `resolveStallAbortSeconds` env-reader shape.

## Tests

`test/sync-reconcile-mass-delete.test.ts` (13 cases, no DB required):
- mixed-separator membership: backslash↔forward-slash in both directions, plus a genuinely-removed file still detected as the only stale slug;
- null-`source_path` (manual/put_page pages) and wrong-strategy pages excluded from both the stale set and the valve denominator;
- the valve tripping at >50% on a >20-page source, with boundary cases (exactly 50% holds, ≤20 pages holds);
- the `GBRAIN_ALLOW_MASS_RECONCILE` override.

Existing `test/performfullsync-source-id.test.ts` and `test/sync-delete-batch.test.ts` still pass, and `bun run typecheck` is clean.

## Related quirk NOT fixed here

While in this code I noticed a separate issue that I've deliberately left out of this PR to keep it scoped: `<head>`-verification failure rows in the sync-failure ledger (`sync-failures.jsonl`) are never resolved by later successful syncs. A `git HEAD verification failed` sentinel is recorded with `state=open` and persists indefinitely; a subsequent sync that verifies HEAD successfully neither resolves nor acknowledges the row (the `acknowledged` flag is regenerated `false`), and `--skip-failed` skips it too. Filed separately as #2834.

## Note on conventions

Per `docs/RELEASING.md`, VERSION/CHANGELOG bumps and the version-first PR title are part of the maintainer `/ship` + community-PR-wave flow (maintainers re-implement community fixes onto a collector branch and bump the version there). As an external contributor I've therefore left `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md` untouched and used a conventional-commit title instead of the version-first form. Happy to adjust to whatever the wave process prefers.

title: fix(import): retain resolved source for page snapshots
body:
## Problem

`runImport` resolves the active source but only adopts the result for the `sole_non_default` tier (src/commands/import.ts). A source resolved from a dotfile, local path, or `brain_default` config is discarded. `importFromContent` then finds an existing page without a source filter and attempts its version snapshot with an undefined source, which both engines interpret as `default`:

```
Warning: skipped wiki/alpha.md: createVersion failed: page "wiki/alpha" (source=default) not found
```

Any brain where a slug already exists under a non-default source (e.g. pages created via `put`/capture, later imported from files) hits this on every import retry, and each retry can add another collision.

## Fix

Always adopt `resolveSourceWithTier()`'s result before touching pages. Explicit `--source-id` and programmatic `sourceId` keep their existing precedence; the sole-non-default nudge is unchanged.

## Testing

title: sync: the import walker ignores SYNC_SKIP_FILES, so metafile pages are created once then frozen forever — later edits silently skipped and reported as success
body:
**Version:** verified on `master` @ `5008b287` (**0.42.59.0**).
**Engine:** Postgres. **Source:** a git repo of ~39 markdown pages, `--strategy markdown` (default).

## Summary

`gbrain sync`'s two import paths disagree about `SYNC_SKIP_FILES`:

- the **first/full import** ingests them (creating pages),
- every **incremental delta** classifies them as `metafile` and skips them — and by design *"preserve any pre-existing page"*.

Net effect: a page is created for `README.md` / `index.md` / `schema.md` / `log.md`, and then **can never be updated again**. It is frozen at its first-import content, forever. Editing the file and pushing changes nothing, and `sync` **reports success** while doing it.

This is silent, permanent staleness in the page store, with a green exit code.

## Evidence (observed, then root-caused)

Corpus = 39 `.md` files, `README.md` among them.

**First sync — README ingested:**
```
Found 39 markdown files
[import.files] 39/39 (100%) imported=39 skipped=0 errors=0
Import complete: 39 pages imported, 39 chunks created
```
`gbrain get readme` → returns the page. So it *is* a page.

**Later commit touching 4 files** (1 added, 3 modified — `README.md` among the modified):
```
Synced bc19409f..93d0e72b:
  +1 added, ~2 modified, -0 deleted, R0 renamed
  3 chunks created, 3 pages embedded
```
Only **3** files imported; `README.md` is neither counted nor imported. Exit 0.

**The clone on disk is correct** — `git log -1` = the new commit, and the new text is present in `README.md`. So the pull worked; only the ingestion skipped it.

**The stored page is stale**: `gbrain get readme` still returns the *pre-change* section. Permanently — every subsequent delta skips it again.

## Root cause

The delta path filters correctly. `src/core/sync-delta.ts:111` says callers *"apply their own `isSyncable` filtering"*, and `classifySync` (`src/core/sync.ts:341`) does:

```ts
const basename = segments[segments.length - 1] || '';
if ((SYNC_SKIP_FILES as readonly string[]).includes(basename)) return 'metafile';   // sync.ts:354
```
```ts
export const SYNC_SKIP_FILES = ['schema.md', 'index.md', 'log.md', 'README.md'] as const;  // sync.ts:330
```

The **import walker does not**. `collectSyncableFiles` (`src/commands/import.ts:578`) → `gitListSyncableFiles` (`:529`) → `isCollectibleForWalker` (`:497`):

```ts
function isCollectibleForWalker(path, strategy, multimodalOn): boolean {
  switch (strategy) {
    case 'code':     return isCodeFilePath(path);
    case 'markdown': return isMarkdownFilePath(path) || (multimodalOn && isImageFilePathFromSync(path));
    case 'auto':     return isMarkdownFilePath(path) || isCodeFilePath(path) || (multimodalOn && isImageFilePathFromSync(path));
  }
}
```

It tests the **extension only**. It never routes through `isSyncable` / `classifySync`, so `SYNC_SKIP_FILES` is never applied on the import path — despite the function being named `collectSyncableFiles` and the predicate `isCollectibleForWalker`.

This directly contradicts the stated invariant at `src/core/sync.ts:334-339`:

> *the single source of truth that both `isSyncable` (boolean) and `unsyncableReason` (tagged) call … Funnelling both public APIs through `classifySync` means TypeScript enforces consistency at the compiler level.*

The compiler does enforce consistency between the two *public APIs* — but the walker simply doesn't call either, so it drifts freely.

## Why the "preserve pre-existing page" rule turns this into a trap

`unsyncableReason` exists (per its own docstring) so the #1433 cleanup guard can *"distinguish metafile exclusions (**preserve any pre-existing page**) from genuine 'file removed from the strategy' cases (delete the now-stale page)."*

That rule is right in isolation — a metafile shouldn't cause a page deletion. But combined with an import path that *creates* those pages, it guarantees the page is never deleted **and** never updated. The two behaviours are individually defensible and jointly produce a permanently stale page that nothing will ever reconcile.

## Repro

1. Put a `README.md` in a source repo alongside normal pages.
2. `gbrain sync --source <id>` (first sync) → observe the README is imported (`gbrain get readme` works).
3. Edit `README.md`, commit, push.
4. `gbrain sync --source <id>` again → success, README not in the import list, count excludes it.
5. `gbrain get readme` → still the old content. Repeat step 4 forever; it never converges.

## Suggested directions

1. **Apply `isSyncable` in the walker** — have `isCollectibleForWalker` (or `gitListSyncableFiles`) route through `classifySync` so both paths share the one filter. Metafiles then never become pages, and the existing "preserve" rule stays correct because there's nothing to preserve. Existing brains keep an orphan page per metafile until cleaned up, so a note in the release/migration path would help.
2. **Or** make the delta path honour whatever the import created — i.e. treat `SYNC_SKIP_FILES` as import-time only. This keeps README-as-a-page working, but that seems to contradict the intent of the constant.
3. **At minimum**, surface it: if a changed file is dropped as `metafile` while a page with that slug exists, say so instead of reporting a clean `~N modified`.

Direction 1 looks like the intended behaviour, given the constant's name and the docstring at `sync.ts:334`.

## Related

- #2839 — sync/import and fact-writers use disjoint lock domains (same area: the import path not participating in an invariant the rest of the code assumes).
- #2840 — `isPidAlive()` across PID namespaces.

Feature request: one-shot dream phase run (e.g. `gbrain dream --phase patterns --once`) without toggling the global dream.patterns.enabled flag
body:
## Context

We run gbrain (0.42.59.0, bun global install, macOS) with dream driven by an external
nightly orchestrator rather than the autopilot's own cadence. Because the patterns
phase only runs when the global config `dream.patterns.enabled` is `true`, the only
way to run it once per night is:

1. `gbrain config set dream.patterns.enabled true`
2. `gbrain dream --phase patterns`
3. `gbrain config set dream.patterns.enabled false`

## Problem

That toggle window makes the global flag a cost hazard. The autopilot polls the same
flag, so if the orchestrator dies between steps 1 and 3 (crash, SIGKILL, machine
sleep, power loss), the flag stays `true` and the autopilot re-enqueues the patterns
phase on every cycle. We hit exactly this: a stuck-true flag ran patterns hourly for
~24h — 119 LLM jobs and roughly $400 of API spend before it was caught.

We've since wrapped the toggle in read-back verification, EXIT-trap resets, and an
external watchdog that force-resets the flag — but all of that is scaffolding around
the real gap: there's no way to run a dream phase once without mutating global state.

## Request

A per-invocation override that neither reads nor writes the global flag, e.g.:

    gbrain dream --phase patterns --once
    # or: --force / --ignore-config

Alternatively (or additionally):
- run-once semantics at the config level, e.g. `dream.patterns.enabled = "once"`
  that the autopilot consumes and auto-clears after one pass; or
- a TTL on the enable flag.

## Secondary suggestion

A guardrail in the autopilot for LLM-priced recurring phases would have contained
this class of failure independently: e.g. a warning (or hard stop) when a phase like
patterns runs more than N times per day, or a simple daily job/token budget.

Happy to provide logs or test a patch.

body:
Extends the v0.41.13 #1433 never-delete-on-metafile guard to the `pruned-dir` classification.

## The bug

A path under a pruned segment (`PRUNE_DIR_NAMES`: `ops/`, `node_modules/`, dot-dirs) is never sync-eligible, so a page at such a slug can only have come from `put_page` — whose write-through still lands a file in the brain repo. When anything edits that file (e.g. a merge-write appending source notes), the next incremental sync classifies it "modified but unsyncable" and **deletes the page from the index**. Sync can never re-create what it deletes there, so the page is orphaned permanently.

We tripped this in production: an `ops/design-history/*` page (created via `put_page`, later edited on disk) was deleted by the following incremental sync and had to be restored by hand.

## The fix

One line: the #1433 guard already skips deletion for the `metafile` classification; skip `pruned-dir` too.

## Tests

New regression test in `test/sync-metafile-skip.serial.test.ts` — red on the old code, green with the fix; the narrow-guard negative case (strategy-reason cleanup still deletes) still passes. `bun run verify` green.

title: `gbrain list` (no `--type`) hangs with Postgres engine while typed/limited list works (v0.42.51.0)
body:
Environment

- GBrain: 0.42.51.0
- Engine: Postgres (not PGLite)
- Bun: 1.3.14
- CLI install: `~/.bun/bin/gbrain → ~/.gbrain/src/cli.ts`
- Postgres: 17 with pgvector (containerized), port 5432
- `DATABASE_URL`: `postgres://gbrain:***@localhost:5432/gbrain`
- `GBRAIN_HOME`: `~/.gbrain`

Config

- `~/.gbrain/config.json`:
  - `engine: "postgres"`
  - `database_url: "postgres://gbrain:***@localhost:5432/gbrain"`

Previously there was a nested test brain:

- `~/.gbrain/.gbrain/config.json` with `engine: "pglite"`
- That nested directory has been **fully removed**.
- The behavior described below is observed **after** removal, on a clean Postgres-only config.

---

### Observed behavior

All of the following commands work reliably:

- `gbrain --version`
- `gbrain --help`
- `gbrain doctor --fast` → health ≈ 90/100 (warnings only)
- `gbrain list --type page --limit 5 --sort updated_desc`
- `gbrain list --type skill`
- `gbrain list --type fact`
- `gbrain get <slug>`
- `gbrain search "<query>"`

However, this hangs:

- `timeout 60s gbrain list`
  - Exit code: 124 (timeout)
  - stdout: empty
  - stderr: empty

On the Postgres side:

- `pg_isready` is OK
- Direct SQL queries to the `gbrain` DB work
- No long-running transactions or blocking locks in `pg_stat_activity` / `pg_locks`
- Number of pages: 24 (small brain), so this is not a huge dataset

It looks like `gbrain list` without `--type` might be doing a broader/unbounded
query (or using a different query plan) that never returns, while the
typed/limited variants are fine.

---

### Steps to reproduce (on this setup)

1. Ensure `engine: "postgres"` in `~/.gbrain/config.json` and `GBRAIN_HOME=~/.gbrain`.
2. Confirm Postgres is healthy and the brain is small (around a few dozen pages).
3. Run:
   - `gbrain list --type page --limit 5 --sort updated_desc` → OK
   - `gbrain list --type skill` → OK
   - `gbrain list --type fact` → OK
4. Then run:
   - `timeout 60s gbrain list` → exit 124, no output.

---

### Workaround

For now I treat `gbrain list` without `--type` as unsafe on this version and use:

- `gbrain list --type page --limit N --sort updated_desc`
- `gbrain list --type skill --limit N`
- `gbrain list --type fact --limit N`

This is perfectly fine for agent use (Hermes, MCP, etc.), but it would be great to:

- either make `gbrain list` behave like a union of the typed lists with a sensible default `LIMIT`, or
- document that on v0.42.51.0 with the Postgres engine it is not recommended to call it without filters, or
- if this is a bug, fix the behavior in a future release.

If helpful, I can also collect a focused `strace` and/or `EXPLAIN` of the query plan for `gbrain list` on this DB, but I wanted to first capture the high-level behavior.

title: fix(search): fold hard-exclude prefixes into knobs_hash — stop cross-process cache leak of excluded slugs (#2825)
body:
Fixes #2825.

`resolveHardExcludes()` only ran at DB-query build time (cache miss), so the query cache key never saw the hard-exclude policy: a process with `GBRAIN_SEARCH_EXCLUDE` set could be served cached rows containing excluded slugs written by a process without it, and vice versa.

**Fix:** fold the resolved hard-exclude prefix list (defaults ∪ env ∪ per-call `exclude_slug_prefixes`, minus `include_slug_prefixes` — exactly what the engines' query-build path resolves) into `knobsHash` via a new `KnobsHashContext.hardExcludes` field, sorted for input-order stability. `KNOBS_HASH_VERSION` 11→12 per the file's append-only bump-log convention (one-time global cold-miss on upgrade, refills within TTL — same pattern as every prior bump).

**Verification:**
- New regression tests: hash divergence on differing exclude/include lists, input-order normalization, legacy-caller fallback, and a cache-level test on real PGLite showing a row stored under the no-exclude hash is a MISS for the exclude hash (both directions). 32 pass / 0 fail.
- Full adjacent sweep (34 test files: mode/knobs/cache/hybrid/source-boost): **504 pass / 0 fail**.
- `bun run typecheck` clean.
- No engine files, migrations, or JSONB paths touched; `knobsHash` has a single production call site so the fold covers every cached read/write.

title: fix(pglite): platform-gate the init-failure banner — stop blaming the macOS 26.3 bug on every platform (#2674)
body:
## Root cause

`classifyPgliteInitError()` in `src/core/pglite-engine.ts` special-cases only `bunfs`, `macos-26-3`, and `corrupt`. A bare Emscripten abort (`Aborted(). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.`) falls to the `unknown` verdict, whose hint unconditionally printed:

> Most common cause: the macOS 26.3 WASM bug (#223)

— on every platform, including Windows and Linux (see the real-world reports in #2195 and #1870). Secondary nit: non-Error rejections stringified via `String(err)`, printing `[object Object]` instead of the actual abort message.

## The fix

- `buildPgliteInitErrorMessage()` now takes a `platform` param (default `process.platform`). On darwin the `unknown` hint keeps the #223 link as a *possible* cause; on other platforms it names the plausible off-macOS causes (lock contention from another gbrain process, damaged data dir) and points at `gbrain doctor` + `gbrain reinit-pglite`.
- New `stringifyPgliteInitError()` prefers `err.message` when present, so plain-object rejections surface their real text.

## Consolidated reports this settles

Canonical: #2674. Duplicates closed tonight: #1870, #1195, #1502, #2195, #939, #391.

## Test evidence

- Extended `test/pglite-init-classifier.test.ts`: unknown-verdict on `linux`/`win32` contains no "macOS 26.3"/#223 and does point at doctor + reinit-pglite; darwin still mentions #223; non-Error rejection (the Emscripten abort object shape) yields the message text, not `[object Object]`. Platform is threaded as a defaulted param — no `process.platform` monkey-patching.
- `bun test test/pglite-init-classifier.test.ts test/pglite-engine.test.ts test/pglite-engine-disconnect.serial.test.ts` → 127 pass / 0 fail.

title: fix(calibration,takes,cli): calibration CLI routing, source-scoped takes reads, BigInt-safe outputs (takeover of #2452)
body:
Supersedes #2452 — a rebase of @spinsirr's fork branch (`spinsirr:fix/calibration-profile-scope-and-cli`) onto current master after tonight's merges (#2698, #2638, #2739) left the original branch in conflict. All substantive work is @spinsirr's; this PR only re-applies it against the moved tree. Original PR is left open for the author; do not merge both.

## The 4 fixes

1. **Calibration CLI routing (#2035)** — `'calibration'` was missing from the `CLI_ONLY` set in `src/cli.ts`, so dispatch never reached the existing `case 'calibration':` handler ("Unknown command"). Also honors `--source` / `GBRAIN_SOURCE` / `.gbrain-source` instead of hardcoding `'default'`.
2. **Source-scoped takes reads (#2200-class)** — `takes_list`, `takes_search`, `takes_scorecard`, `takes_calibration` applied no source filtering; a federated/scoped grant could read takes across sources. Ops now route through `sourceScopeOpts(ctx)` (federated array > scalar > nothing); engines scope via the take's `page.source_id` (JOIN filter for list/search, `EXISTS` for scorecard/curve), on both PGLite and Postgres in lockstep. Holder allow-list composes (intersection).
3. **BigInt-safe takes search hits** — `searchTakes` / `searchTakesVector` returned raw driver rows; the pg driver returns int8 (`take_id`/`page_id`) as native `BigInt`, crashing `JSON.stringify` at the MCP/CLI boundary the moment a query matched. Both engines now coerce through a shared `takeHitRowToHit` helper (engine parity).
4. **BigInt-safe CLI output exits** — `cli.ts`'s local-op output normalizer and the `gbrain call` exit both stringify with a `bigintToStringReplacer` (bigint → string, matching the postgres.js int8 wire shape); calibration profile `id` (BIGSERIAL) is coerced to string in `getLatestProfile`.

Also carried from the original PR: calibration/voice-gate default model ids route through `TIER_DEFAULTS` (provider-prefixed) instead of bare strings, and the admin calibration chart endpoints no longer crash on real data (`takes` has no `page_slug` column — joined via pages; month-precision `since_date` cast; `generated_at` arrives as a `Date`; bigint id in drill-down).

title: reconcile-links: registered in --help and cli.ts's handler switch, but missing from CLI_ONLY so it always prints "Unknown command"
body:
## Bug

\`gbrain reconcile-links\` — advertised in \`gbrain --help\` (\`reconcile-links [--dry-run]        Batch-recompute doc↔impl edges (v0.20.0)\`) and fully implemented (\`src/commands/reconcile-links.ts\`, dispatched via a real \`case 'reconcile-links':\` block at \`src/cli.ts:1694\`) — is unreachable:

\`\`\`
$ gbrain reconcile-links --dry-run --source-id shaft-engine
Unknown command: reconcile-links
Run gbrain --help for available commands.
\`\`\`

## Root cause

\`src/cli.ts\`'s dispatch only reaches the \`handleCliOnly\` switch (where the \`reconcile-links\` case lives) when the command name is present in the \`CLI_ONLY\` Set at line 47:

\`\`\`ts
const CLI_ONLY = new Set(['init', 'reinit-pglite', ... 'connect', 'skillopt', 'quarantine', 'self-upgrade', 'advisor', 'watch']);
\`\`\`

\`'reconcile-links'\` is not in that list, so every invocation falls through to the shared-operations lookup (\`cliOps\`/\`cliAliases\`), finds nothing, and hits the generic \`Unknown command\` branch at line 307 — never reaching its own \`case\` in \`handleCliOnly\`.

## Fix

Add \`'reconcile-links'\` to the \`CLI_ONLY\` Set literal at \`src/cli.ts:47\`. (Possibly also worth a small regression test asserting every \`case\` in \`handleCliOnly\`'s switch has a matching entry in \`CLI_ONLY\`, so this class of drift can't recur silently.)

## Why this matters (real-world impact)

Found while confirming a federated code brain (SHAFT_ENGINE, ~1450 pages, code-def/code-refs working correctly) was "fully linked." It isn't: \`gbrain extract links --source db\` finds 0 links across all pages, and \`code-callers\`/\`code-callees\` report \`"status": "indexing", "ready": false\` — the code↔doc edge graph was never built. \`reconcile-links\` is the documented tool for building exactly that graph, but it's been silently unreachable via the CLI this whole time. \`brain_score\`'s \`links 0/25\` in \`gbrain doctor\` on any code-heavy brain is consistent with this.

Reported alongside https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/2899 (unrelated fix, same investigation session).
