title: ci(security): OSV dependency scan, release artifact attestations, Semgrep CE SAST (#2182 #2142 #2272)
body:
Fix-wave D: three additive security CI workflows. No existing workflow is restructured; every action is pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment (repo convention), and the Semgrep container image is pinned by digest.

## OSV-Scanner dependency scan (#2182)

New `.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml` calling Google's official reusable workflow (`google/osv-scanner-action` v2.3.8, SHA-pinned).

- **When:** weekly (Mon 06:30 UTC), on PRs touching `bun.lock` / `package.json`, and manual dispatch.
- **Permissions:** read-only (`contents: read`, `actions: read`). `upload-sarif: false` — findings land in the job log and as a SARIF run artifact, deliberately skipping the code-scanning upload so the workflow needs no `security-events: write`.
- **Secrets:** none.

## Release artifact attestations (#2142)

`.github/workflows/release.yml`, additive only: the `build` matrix job gains `id-token: write` + `attestations: write` (plus explicit `contents: read`), and an `actions/attest-build-provenance` (v4.1.1, SHA-pinned) step attests `bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}` right after `bun build --compile` — the same paths the upload/release steps use. The `release` job is untouched and keeps the workflow-level `contents: write`.

Note: this repo does not currently push `v*` tags, so `release.yml` never fires today — the attestation is correct-but-dormant and will take effect on the first tagged release.

## Semgrep CE SAST (#2272)

New `.github/workflows/semgrep.yml` running Semgrep Community Edition tokenless in the official container (version + digest pinned), with the default + TypeScript registry rulesets (`p/default`, `p/typescript`).

- **When:** every PR, weekly (Mon 07:30 UTC), and manual dispatch.
- **Permissions:** `contents: read` only. Findings print in the job log; no code-scanning/SARIF upload by design (keeps the surface and permissions minimal).
- **Non-blocking initially:** the scan step has `continue-on-error: true` so a fresh baseline doesn't fail unrelated PRs. Graduation path (documented in the workflow): triage the baseline (fix or `# nosemgrep`), then remove `continue-on-error` so new findings block.

## Validation

- `actionlint` v1.7.11 (the exact pin the repo's `actionlint.yml` CI uses) run repo-wide: exit 0.
- All `uses:` references SHA-pinned with version comments, matching existing workflow style.

Fixes #2182, Fixes #2142, Fixes #2272

title: fix(cli,config,doctor): CLI/config UX wave — config-get file plane, idempotent archive, honest help + doctor text (#2120 #2792 #1175 #1123 #2451)
body:
Fix-wave B: five verified-open CLI/config UX bugs, one minimal root-cause fix + one regression test each.

## Fixes

### #2120 — `config get` reads only the DB plane
`src/commands/config.ts` `get` called only `engine.getConfig(key)`, so a runtime-effective key in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (or env) reported not-found while the runtime used it. `get` now resolves the way the runtime does — env/file plane wins over DB (`loadConfig()` already overlays env onto the file) — falling back to the DB plane, and prints provenance on stderr (`[config] source: file/env plane ...` / `db plane`, including a shadowed-DB-value note). stdout stays a bare value for scripts; DB-only dotted keys (`search.mode`) are unregressed.
**Test:** `test/config-get-plane.test.ts` (4 tests: file-plane found, file-over-DB precedence + shadow note, DB-only fallback, neither-plane exit 1).

### #2792 — `sources archive` not idempotent
`runArchive` collapsed "already archived" into the same reasonless `Failed to archive` exit-4 as a real failure (`softDeleteSource` returns null when the `archived = false` UPDATE matches no row). Already-archived is now a friendly no-op (exit 0) pointing at `sources archived` / `sources restore`; not-found keeps the clear exit-4 error.
**Test:** `test/sources-archive-idempotent.test.ts` (PGLite, mirrors `destructive-guard.test.ts` conventions).

### #1175 — `sources archive` missing from `--help`
The top-level SOURCES help block listed only `list`/`add`/`remove`. It now lists the soft-delete lifecycle (`archive`, `restore`, `archived`, `purge`) plus `status`, and points at `sources --help` (which already documents the full 20-subcommand set) for the long tail.
**Test:** new describe block in `test/cli-help-discoverability.test.ts` (spawns the real CLI).

### #1123 — doctor recommends CLI surfaces that don't exist
The `multi_source_drift` recommendation referenced `gbrain sources rehome` (never built) and `gbrain delete <slug>` without noting delete targets the ACTIVE source — following it literally on a multi-source brain deletes the correctly-routed row. The message (extracted to exported `multiSourceDriftAdvice` in `src/commands/doctor.ts`) now leads with the re-sync path that reconciles drift without deletions and pins any residual delete to `GBRAIN_SOURCE=default gbrain delete <slug>`. No new surfaces built (issue's Option A).
**Test:** `test/doctor-drift-advice.test.ts`.

### #2451 — bare model ids crash parseModelId
Re-verified on current master: already fixed by #2892 (26d2f8ab, merged last night) — calibration-profile and voice-gate defaults now route through provider-prefixed `TIER_DEFAULTS`, with regression tests at `test/calibration-profile.test.ts:255-267`. No change in this PR; listed here so the still-open issue gets closed.

title: fix(extract,ingest,cycle): source-provenance wave — thread source identity through ingest_capture, fs-walk links, and cycle extract (#1522 #1747 #1503)
body:
## Summary

Fix-wave C: three verified-open issues in the same invariant class — **source identity silently dropped on a write path, collapsing to the `default` source**. One PR because the fixes share a seam (`ExtractOpts.sourceId` → batch-row stamping) and one test vocabulary (multi-source PGLite fixtures proving rows land in the right source).

## Per-fix evidence

### 1. #1522 — `ingest_capture` drops IngestionEvent provenance

`src/core/minions/handlers/ingest-capture.ts` validated `source_id` / `source_kind` / `source_uri` (required by `validateIngestionEvent`) and then called `importFromContent(engine, slug, event.content, { noEmbed })` — dropping all three, even though `importFromContent` fully supports provenance write-through.

**Fix:** the handler now threads `source_kind`, `source_uri`, and `ingested_via: 'ingest_capture'` into the write, and routes the page under `event.source_id` when **both** hold:
- the event is trusted (`untrusted_payload !== true`) — fail-closed, because the webhook path builds `event.source_id` from a caller-controlled `x-gbrain-source-id` header, and an untrusted network payload must not get to choose its write source, and
- the id names a registered `sources` row — the webhook's fabricated `webhook-<clientId>` ids are not registered, so that path keeps its pre-fix default-source routing instead of FK-failing every webhook ingest.

**Tests** (`test/ingestion/ingest-capture.test.ts`, real PGLite): registered+trusted routes to the source with all provenance columns persisted; unregistered emitter id keeps default routing but persists provenance; untrusted+registered stays in `default` (fail-closed). All three fail on unfixed master.

### 2. #1747 — 0 wikilink edges on non-default sources (fs-walk extract)

The fs-walk extractors (`extractLinksFromDir` / `extractTimelineFromDir` / `extractForSlugs` in `src/commands/extract.ts`) built `LinkBatchInput` / `TimelineBatchInput` rows with no `source_id`, so `addLinksBatch` / `addTimelineEntriesBatch` mapped missing → literal `'default'` and their `JOIN pages ON (slug, source_id)` dropped **every** row on a brain populated via `import --source-id X` — the silent `Links: created 0 from N pages` no-op.

**Fix:** `ExtractOpts` gains `sourceId`; the CLI fs path resolves it through the standard 6-tier `resolveSourceId` chain (`--source-id` > `GBRAIN_SOURCE` > `.gbrain-source` > registered-path match > sole-non-default > `default`) and every fs-walk batch row is stamped `from/to/origin_source_id` (links) / `source_id` (timeline). When unresolved, behavior is byte-identical to before.

**Tests** (`test/extract-fs-source-id.test.ts`): CLI `extract all --source-id wiki` and the no-flag auto-resolution both land edges + timeline under `wiki`; a negative control pins the pre-fix JOIN-drop shape (`created 0`). Red on unfixed master, green here.

### 3. #1503 — cycle extract phase writes links/timeline to `default` on federated brains

`runPhaseExtract` (`src/core/cycle.ts`) called `runExtractCore` with no source, so nightly dream/autopilot cycles on federated brains persisted nothing (`created 0` every cycle) while the source-aware CLI path worked.

**Fix:** `runPhaseExtract` now receives `cycleSourceId` — the cycle's already-resolved per-source scope (explicit `--source` wins, else `resolveSourceForDir(brainDir)`, the same seam `runPhaseSync` uses) — and threads it into `runExtractCore` for both the incremental (changed-slugs) and full-walk paths.

**Tests** (`test/cycle-extract-source.test.ts`): `runCycle(phases: ['extract'])` on a federated PGLite brain resolves the source from the registered brain dir and lands links + timeline under it; explicit `opts.sourceId` path also pinned. Both fail on unfixed master.

## Relationship to PR #1719

#1719 (@seungsu-kr) attacked defect 1 of this class by threading `sourceId` through `ExtractOpts` at v0.42.1.0. This PR reuses that approach (credited via `Co-authored-by`), rebased onto the current signal-aware fs-walk signatures, and extends it to the timeline batch, the cycle phase (#1503 defect 2), and the ingest handler. **#1719 is superseded by this PR and can be closed with credit once this merges.**

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- New/changed suites: 24/24 pass (`ingest-capture`, `extract-fs-source-id`, `cycle-extract-source`)
- Adjacent suites: `test/ingestion/` + `test/extract-source-aware.test.ts` (225 pass), full `extract`-named sweep (610 tests, 47 files): all pass except one pre-existing hook-timeout flake in `test/extract/receipt-writer.test.ts` that reproduces identically on clean master under the same 47-file load (passes in isolation on both)
- Ownership triage: running the new test files against **unfixed** master → 5 failures (the regression pins are real); with the fix → 0
- CI guards: `check-test-isolation.sh`, `check-jsonb-pattern.sh`, `check-jsonb-params.mjs`, `test/build-llms.test.ts` all green; no doc/engine-SQL changes (engine parity untouched)

Fixes #1522, Fixes #1747, Fixes #1503

title: fix(facts): make dream extract_facts idempotent so fence rows don't duplicate each cycle (#1781)
body:
Supersedes #1837 by @mvanhorn — that PR's fix and tests are correct, but it went stale against master (conflicts with #1972's abort-signal threading and #1928's cli:-exclusion on the wipe). This is a rebase/port of the same fix onto current master, with full credit to the original author (Co-authored-by on the commit).

Fixes #1781

## Summary

Re-running a `gbrain dream` cycle on unchanged content no longer accumulates duplicate facts. The `extract_facts` phase in `src/core/cycle/extract-facts.ts` previously wipe-and-reinserted every page's fence-owned DB rows on every run; it now de-duplicates extracted facts by the canonical `(claim, source)` content key and reconciles the page-scoped DB index — no-op when already in sync, insert-only for genuinely new keys, wipe/reinsert only when stale DB rows need cleanup. A no-change cycle is a true no-op (`factsInserted: 0`, `factsDeleted: 0`).

## Adjustments over #1837 (master moved underneath it)

- **#1972 abort-signal threading preserved**: the batch `embed()` call keeps `{ abortSignal: opts.signal }` (this was the merge conflict that stalled the original PR).
- **#1928 `cli:` conversation-fact protection preserved and extended**: every wipe keeps `excludeSourcePrefixes: ['cli:']`, and `cli:`-origin rows are also excluded from the existing-row set used for reconciliation — otherwise a page carrying conversation facts would count them as "stale" and fall back to wipe/reinsert every cycle, defeating the idempotency this PR adds. Pinned by a new test.
- Checked against #2104's durable facts-absorb path: `writeFactsToFence` writes fence rows and DB rows together (fence-owned), so the reconcile stays consistent with it.

- `bun test test/extract-facts-phase.test.ts test/facts-reconcile-protect-cli.test.ts` — 19 pass (new cases: duplicate fence rows dedupe without rewriting the fence, same-claim-different-source is not a duplicate, new fence fact inserts exactly once, `cli:` facts neither break idempotency nor get wiped; plus tightened no-op counter assertions on the existing idempotency test).

title: fix(retry): reconnect on null instance pool in all non-batch config accessors (takeover of #1891)
body:
Verify-and-salvage takeover of #1891 (by @jalagrange), whose territory was partially covered by later merges:

**Covered on master:** `getConfig` gained retry-with-reconnect via #1603 (inline `withRetry` + `reconnect`), and #1906 / #2025 fixed the reconnect machinery itself (build-then-swap; worker reconnect after promote loss).

**Genuine remnant (this PR):** `setConfig`, `unsetConfig`, and `listConfigKeys` still touched `this.sql` bare. After a mid-cycle instance-pool teardown the getter throws the retryable "No database connection" (#1678) *by design* so a withRetry+reconnect caller can self-heal — but these three had no such wrapper, so the first config write/list after a disconnect threw unhandled.

What's ported (rebased onto master's shape):
- #1891's `connRetry` private helper — same retry+reconnect posture as `batchRetry`, but no batch-audit JSONL (a config accessor is not a sized batch; routing it through `batchRetry` would inflate the `batch_retry_health` doctor metric and demand a bogus `BatchAuditSite` member).
- `getConfig` refactored onto the helper (behavior unchanged — one posture, no drift); `setConfig` / `unsetConfig` / `listConfigKeys` wrapped. Writes are retry-safe: `withRetry` only retries connection-class failures (statement never committed) and both writes are idempotent (upsert / delete).
- `test/postgres-engine-config-reconnect.test.ts` (adapted from #1891): all four accessors reconnect+retry a null instance pool exactly once; non-retryable errors surface without any reconnect (no masking). Pure — no real DB.

- Capture the `gbrain import <dir>` target once at import start as an absolute real path (`resolveImportTargetDir` = `resolve` + `realpathSync`), and use that canonical value for file collection, checkpoint load/save, and resume filtering. A checkpoint left behind by an interrupted run (e.g. SIGTERM) can no longer carry `.` or a symlink alias whose meaning depends on the next consumer's CWD.
- Write self-describing checkpoints (`schema_version: 1`, `owner: "gbrain"`, `kind: "import"`). `loadCheckpoint` tolerates absent metadata (legacy path-based checkpoints keep resuming) but rejects present-and-wrong metadata and any relative `dir`.
- Document the checkpoint contract in `docs/guides/live-sync.md` (llms bundle regenerated — the guide is inlined in `llms-full.txt`).

## Changes vs. #1731

- Dropped the unrelated `.env.testing.example` Gemini-key hunk and the `docs/reference/gbrain-1728-submission-package.md` process artifact — the shipped diff is just the fix, its tests, and the contract doc.
- `test/import-resume.test.ts` fixture now realpaths its mkdtemp brain dir: on macOS `tmpdir()` is a `/var` → `/private/var` symlink, so the planted checkpoint's `dir` must match the canonicalized identity runImport now persists (this is the fix working as intended, exercised end-to-end by the existing resume tests).
- Added a small negative test: `resolveImportTargetDir` throws on a nonexistent target (runImport turns that into a clean usage error instead of a checkpoint with a phantom dir).

## Testing

- `bun test test/import-checkpoint.test.ts test/import-resume.test.ts test/import-source-id.test.ts test/sync-walker-symlink.test.ts test/import-metafile-skip.test.ts` — 41 pass.

- `bun test test/build-llms.test.ts` — 12 pass (bundle freshness after the docs edit).
- `bun run typecheck` — clean.
- `bun run check:test-isolation` — OK (984 files scanned).

Original fix, contract design, and tests by @diazMelgarejo in #1731 (credited via Co-authored-by).

title: fix(dream): gate patterns phase on gateway provider reachability, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (takeover of #2279)
body:
Verify-and-salvage takeover of #2279 (by @brettdavies; issue #2278 was closed as its dup).

**Why not merge #2279 as-is:** it removes the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` gate with *no replacement*, which (a) breaks the two tests that pin the skip path (`test/cycle-patterns.test.ts` structural check + `test/e2e/dream-patterns-pglite.test.ts` E2E), and (b) on an Anthropic-default install with no key, would submit a subagent job doomed to fail instead of skipping cheaply.

**The correct end-state (this PR), post-#2208:** the patterns phase should run when ANY capable provider is configured, gateway-routed — not gate on the Anthropic env var. The gate now probes the RESOLVED patterns model via `probeChatModel(normalizeModelId(config.model))`, the exact shared predicate `think/index.ts` and synthesize's `makeJudgeClient` already use (one predicate, no drift). This fixes both misclassifications of the old gate:

- Non-Anthropic stacks (litellm, deepseek, openrouter, ...) were skipped as "no upstream" even though the subagent routes them through the gateway (`agent.use_gateway_loop`). They now pass; their auth is checked lazily at dispatch and surfaces in the job outcome — the deliberate degrade contract the probe was built for.
- Anthropic keys set via `gbrain config set anthropic_api_key` (stdio MCP launches without shell env) were treated as missing; `hasAnthropicKey` inside the probe reads both sources.

Skip reason: `no_api_key` → `no_provider` (carries the probe's detail string). No other consumer of the old reason exists in src/docs/skills.

**Tests updated to pin the new behavior:**
- `test/cycle-patterns.test.ts`: asserts `probeChatModel` + `normalizeModelId` + `no_provider` wiring, and that `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is gone from the phase.
- `test/e2e/dream-patterns-pglite.test.ts`: expects `no_provider`; also swaps its local env-only helper for the shared hermetic `test/helpers/no-anthropic-key.ts` (neuters env AND config-file key), so the test can't flip to a live LLM call on a dev machine whose `~/.gbrain/config.json` carries a real key.

Verified: both pinning suites + `test/cycle*` + `dream-synthesize-pglite` E2E — 240 pass / 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` clean; `check-test-isolation` OK.

Credit: @brettdavies (Co-authored-by on the commit). Recommend closing #2279 as superseded by this PR.

title: fix(subagent): orchestration fix-wave G — configurable timeouts/caps, honest child outcomes, fenced timeline writes
body:
One PR fixing the verified-open subagent-orchestration family. All four issues re-verified open against current master (`3aeb622d`) before work started.

Fixes #1594, Fixes #2778, Fixes #2782, Fixes #2113.

## Per-fix summary + evidence

### #1594 — synthesize.ts hardcoded 30/35-min subagent timeouts
`dream.synthesize.subagent_timeout_ms` / `dream.synthesize.subagent_wait_timeout_ms` config keys (defaults preserve 30/35 min), threaded through `loadSynthConfig` into the per-chunk `queue.add` and `waitForCompletion` calls, plus the `loadConfigWithEngine` DB-plane merge and `KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS`.

**Supersedes #1596 with credit:** open PR #1596 by @ai920wisco implemented this correctly but went stale (conflicts). Its config.ts + synthesize.ts approach and test are ported here essentially verbatim (test restructured to the shared-engine isolation pattern the `check:test-isolation` gate now enforces). Commit carries `Co-authored-by: ai920wisco`.

Evidence: `test/cycle-synthesize-subagent-timeout.test.ts` (config value lands on the submitted `minion_jobs.timeout_ms`), `test/loadConfig-merge.test.ts`, `test/config-set.test.ts`.

### #2778 — fenced allowlist omits add_timeline_entry; hardcoded 4096-token turn cap; silent tool_use truncation
- `add_timeline_entry` (the canonical timeline op) joins `BRAIN_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` (+ usage hint). **Trust fail-closed:** the put_page inline namespace check is extracted into a shared `enforceSubagentSlugFence(ctx, slug, opName)` in operations.ts and applied to `add_timeline_entry` too — a subagent can only append timeline entries to pages it could have written (trusted-workspace allow-list, else `wiki/agents/<id>/` namespace, rejecting outright when `subagentId` is missing). put_page behavior is unchanged (its full namespace test suite still passes).
- Per-turn output cap: `resolveMaxOutputTokens(data.max_tokens, config)` — per-job `max_tokens` → `agent.max_output_tokens` config → 8192 default (was hardcoded 4096, which made pages >~12KB unwritable). Threaded into both the legacy Anthropic path and the gateway `toolLoop` path.
- `stop_reason=max_tokens` is no longer silent: a capped final turn returns the new `SubagentStopReason 'max_tokens'` (previously reported as a clean `end_turn` with truncated text); a capped tool round injects a `[system]` truncation note into the tool-result turn so the model re-issues the dropped call instead of assuming the write happened.

Evidence: `test/timeline-entry-subagent-fence.test.ts` (9 cases: non-subagent callers unchanged, namespace + allow-list accept/reject, fail-closed), `test/brain-allowlist.serial.test.ts` (size pin 14→15), `test/subagent-handler.test.ts` (+8 cases: resolver tiers, SDK call carries the resolved cap, max_tokens surfaced, truncation-note round-trip with recovery).

### #2782 — patterns phase returns status:ok on child timeout with nothing written
The phase status now reflects the child outcome: non-`complete` outcome (timeout / failed / dead) with zero pattern pages written → `status: 'fail'` with error `PATTERNS_CHILD_<OUTCOME>` (Timeout class + a worker-capacity hint for the no-free-slot case); non-`complete` with partial writes → `status: 'warn'`. `details` keeps `child_outcome` / `job_id` / counts in every branch. The patterns timeouts also get the #1594-family config pair (`dream.patterns.subagent_timeout_ms` / `dream.patterns.subagent_wait_timeout_ms`), which is also what makes the fix testable without a 35-minute wait.

Evidence: `test/cycle-patterns-child-outcome.test.ts` — drives the real phase on PGLite with wait timeout 1ms and no worker: asserts `fail` + `PATTERNS_CHILD_TIMEOUT` (this returned `ok` pre-fix), and that the timeout config lands on the submitted job.

Scope note: the issue's second ask (doctor fan-out visibility into cycle-spawned subagent capacity) is a separate doctor-surface feature, not taken here — the silent-ok bug is the fix; a failing phase now surfaces through the normal cycle-report path.

### #2113 — facts extraction never checks finish_reason; hardcoded maxTokens:1500
`facts.extraction_max_tokens` config key (default raised 1500→4000, headroom for mandatory-reasoning models whose thinking tokens share the cap). `stopReason: 'length'` is now checked: one retry at 2× the cap, and a loud stderr warning (with the paste-ready `gbrain config set` fix) if still truncated — never a silent zero-fact extraction.

Evidence: `test/facts-extract-truncation.test.ts` (config resolution + invalid-value fallback; default call carries 4000; truncated first call retries once at double and recovers the facts; retry bounded at one). Uses the gateway chat-transport seam — no API key, no network.

## Verification

- `bun test` over all 4 new + 17 adjacent files (subagent/cycle/patterns/facts/config/operations): **414 pass / 0 fail** (output captured to file, `EXIT=0`)
- `bun run typecheck`: clean
- `bun run check:all` (includes `check:test-isolation`, jsonb guards, key-files current-state): clean
- `bun test test/build-llms.test.ts`: clean (llms bundle regenerated after the KEY_FILES.md current-state updates)
- No SQL/schema changes → engine parity untouched

## Scope-outs

- #2782's doctor fan-out check (see above).
- Auto-continuation on `max_tokens` final turns (re-prompting to finish truncated text) — surfacing via `stop_reason` is the honest minimal fix; continuation is a behavior change callers should opt into.
- No VERSION/CHANGELOG bump — release bookkeeping left to the maintainer's /ship flow.

title: fix(sync): sync data-loss family — ops/ prune-kill, DB-only write-through deletion, full-sync gate drift (#2404 #2426 #2607)
body:
Fix-wave E: one PR for the verified-open sync data-loss family (two P0s + the full-sync divergence face of the same class). Every defect was re-verified on current master before coding, and every regression test was run against master `src/` to confirm it fails there.

## #2404 (P0) — `ops/` hardcoded in PRUNE_DIR_NAMES

**Root cause:** `'ops'` sat in `PRUNE_DIR_NAMES` (traced to the v0.2.0 `path.startsWith('ops/')` carve-out; comment said only "Skip ops/ directory"). `classifySync` marks any path with an `ops` segment `'pruned-dir'`, so committed `ops/*.md` never imported, and a modified `ops/*` file fell into the `unsyncableModified` delete loop — whose #1433 guard only spared `'metafile'` — silently deleting put-created pages (including `ops/tasks`, which the bundled daily-task-manager skill prescribes as its canonical store) on every sync.

**Fix (the issue's preferred direction, option 1 + hardening 3):**
- Removed `'ops'` from `PRUNE_DIR_NAMES` (`src/core/sync.ts`), with a do-not-re-add note. The noise entries the list exists for (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `venv`, `.raw`, dot-dirs) are untouched — `ops/` was never generated/vendored noise.
- Hardened the delete loop (`src/commands/sync.ts`) to also skip `'pruned-dir'` classifications: a page under a pruned dir can only exist via a deliberate `put_page` (sync never imports those paths), so a file edit is not evidence the page is stale. This protects the whole class for any future pruned dir, per the issue comment's data point.

**Evidence:** `test/sync-ops-pages.serial.test.ts` — committed `ops/tasks.md` imports; an edit updates (pre-fix: "Deleted un-syncable page: ops/tasks" kill-loop); a put-created page under still-pruned `node_modules/` survives a file edit. 2 of 3 fail on master (the third documents that master's `--full` imported ops only via the #2607 bug — the two modes cycled content in and out, exactly as #2607 reports).

## #2426 (P0) — write-through stays DB-only and `sync --full` deletes it

All **three** compounding bugs from the issue are fixed:

1. **Write-through never committed** — `writePageThrough` (`src/core/write-through.ts`) now best-effort commits the artifact after a successful atomic write, gated on `isDurabilityHardened(repo)` (the gbrain post-commit hook is installed, i.e. the user opted into durability via `gbrain sources harden`); the hook then background-pushes. The commit is path-limited (`git commit -- <file>`) so unrelated dirty edits are never swept in. Unhardened repos keep the existing write-only behavior. This also unfreezes the `sync_freshness` symptom from the issue comment (HEAD advances again). Result carries `committed?: boolean` for observability.
2. **`brain-commit-push.sh` pulled before staging** — the helper template (`src/core/brain-repo-durability.ts`) now stages + commits BEFORE any pull. The old fetch + `pull --rebase`-first order aborted on any dirty tree ("cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes", exit 3), so it could only ever commit untracked-NEW files, never modifications — exactly the write-through shape. The shared `brain_push` retry already handles an advanced remote (push → rejected → `pull --rebase` → push), which is the issue's requested ordering. Already-hardened repos pick up the fixed helper on their next `gbrain sources harden` (content-diff refresh).
3. **Delete-reconcile deletes DB-only pages** — `performFullSync`'s reconcile now partitions stale slugs by git history via the new exported `listEverCommittedPaths(repoPath)` (one `git log --all --no-renames --diff-filter=A --name-only` pass, run only when there are stale pages; `null` on non-git dirs → unchanged behavior). A stale path that ever existed in history was genuinely deleted → reconciled as before. A path with NO history is DB-only write-through → the page is **kept** and its markdown **re-exported** to the working tree via the existing `writePageThrough`, with a stderr hint to commit it. Builds on (does not duplicate) the #2828 mass-delete valve — this covers the below-valve cases the ratio check can't see, and follows the responsible-disclosure rule (mechanism described, no exposure quantification).

**Evidence:** `test/write-through-commit.serial.test.ts` (hardened → committed path-limited, unrelated dirty edit stays uncommitted; unhardened → unchanged behavior), the new `#2426` helper test in `test/brain-durability-hook.serial.test.ts` (dirty MODIFIED tracked file + remote advanced from a second clone → helper commits AND pushes; pre-fix exit 3), `test/sync-reconcile-db-only.serial.test.ts` (genuinely-deleted page reconciles; never-committed page survives `--full` and its file is re-exported; plus `listEverCommittedPaths` unit incl. later-deleted paths and the non-git `null` arm). All fail against master src.

## #2607 — `sync --full` git fast path bypasses pruneDir

**Root cause:** `gitListSyncableFiles` (`git ls-files` fast path) filtered only by strategy/extension + .gitignore; `isCollectibleForWalker` had the metafile exclusion but no `pruneDir`, so a full pass imported — and resurrected previously-soft-deleted — pages under dot-dirs/vendored trees that incremental sync excludes.

**Fix:** `isCollectibleForWalker` (`src/commands/import.ts`) now applies the same segment-level `pruneDir` gate as `classifySync`, so full and incremental enumeration agree on the exclusion set (whatever that set is — orthogonal to #2404, exactly as the issue frames it). No behavior change on the FS-walk route (it already pruned at descent + emit).

**Evidence:** `test/import-git-fastpath-prune.test.ts` — tracked files under `.obsidian/`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `*.raw/` are not collected; plus the contract test that every collected file passes incremental `isSyncable`. Both fail on master.

## Scoped out

- **#2607 include/exclude globs:** per-source include/exclude globs still don't reach the full-path enumerator (they're `SyncableOptions`, not `CollectOpts`). The issue's named divergence (pruneDir + metafiles) is fully covered; the glob seam is the #2082-adjacent follow-up.
- **#2426 doctor `sync_freshness` copy:** the issue-comment's suggestion to reword the doctor remediation is mooted for hardened repos by fix 1 (HEAD advances) and left as a copy-level follow-up otherwise.

## Verification

- New tests: 12 pass on branch; 6 verified failing when run against master `src/` (plus the reconcile suite failing to load on master's missing export).
- Adjacent suites green: `sync*`, `import*`, `write-through*`, `put-page*`, `performfullsync`, `storage-sync`, `brain-repo-durability` / `brain-durability-hook` / `git-remote-durable` / `durability-cron`, `brain-writer-walk-prune`, `core/cycle` — 500+ tests, 0 fail attributable to this branch. (`brain-durability-hook`'s pre-existing "LOCAL-ONLY line" test is timing-flaky on this machine — fails identically on unmodified master, 3/3 runs.)
- Updated pre-existing pins that asserted the old ops behavior (`test/sync.test.ts`, `test/sync-strategy.test.ts`, `test/sync-isSyncable-shape.test.ts`, `test/brain-writer-walk-prune.test.ts`, `test/e2e/sync.test.ts`) — each preserves its original intent with `vendor/`/`node_modules` now carrying the pruned-dir case.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run check:test-isolation` OK (985 files); jsonb pattern + positional guards and progress-to-stdout guard clean; `docs/architecture/KEY_FILES.md` updated to current state, `bun run build:llms` run (bundles unchanged), `check-key-files-current-state.sh` + `test/build-llms.test.ts` green.
- No SQL changes → engine parity untouched; reconcile guard reuses the existing source-scoped rows query.

Fixes #2404
Fixes #2426
Fixes #2607

title: fix(dream,chronicle): synthesize output family — source scope, output root, retrieval reach, durable provenance, honest judge failures (#1586 #2415 #2163 #2569 #2606)
body:
## Fix wave F — dream/synthesize output family

Five verified-open issues (re-checked against tonight's master before each fix), one PR because they share the same code family (`src/core/cycle/synthesize*.ts`, `patterns.ts`, chronicle judge) and the fixes compose.

### #1586 — synthesize writes landed in the 'default' source

**Evidence:** `src/core/cycle/synthesize.ts` `collectChildPutPageSlugs` hardcoded `source_id: 'default'`, and the subagent tool registry (`src/core/minions/tools/brain-allowlist.ts:buildOpContext`) hardcoded `sourceId: 'default'` — so both the write AND the collection ignored the cycle's resolved source.

**Fix (reuses the #2920 `cycleSourceId` seam):** `cycle.ts` threads `sourceId: cycleSourceId` into `runPhaseSynthesize`; the phase forwards it as `SubagentHandlerData.source_id` (new trusted field, same PROTECTED_JOB_NAMES trust story as `allowed_slug_prefixes`, `validateSourceId`-checked at registry build); `buildOpContext` scopes every child tool call to it, so put_page writes land in the right source. Collected refs, the provenance stamp, reverse-writes, and the summary page all carry the same source. Reverse-writes for the cycle's own source stay at `brainDir/<slug>.md` (brainDir IS that source's checkout); foreign sources keep the `.sources/<id>/` layout. Unset → `'default'`, byte-identical legacy behavior.

### #2415 — hardcoded `wiki/` output namespace

**Evidence:** `synthesize.ts` prompt slug templates (`wiki/personal/reflections/…`, `wiki/originals/ideas/…`), `patterns.ts` reflection lookup (`slug LIKE 'wiki/personal/reflections/%'`) + prompt, and the `wiki/`-rooted allow-list globs in `skills/_brain-filing-rules.json`.

**Fix:** new config knob `dream.synthesize.output_root` (default `wiki`, registered in `KNOWN_CONFIG_KEYS` per the #2632 pattern; slug-grammar-validated with loud fallback). It drives (1) both prompt slug templates, (2) the patterns lookup (now a bound LIKE parameter), (3) the patterns prompt, and (4) `loadAllowedSlugPrefixes(outputRoot)` remaps the `wiki/`-rooted globs (non-wiki globs like `dream-cycle-summaries/*` pass through). The duplicated `loadAllowedSlugPrefixes` copy in `patterns.ts` was deleted — both phases now share the synthesize implementation, so they can't disagree. Zero behavior change unless the key is set.

### #2163 — concept pages invisible to retrieval

**Evidence:** `synthesize-concepts.ts` called bare `engine.putPage()` — no chunking, no embedding — while `source-boost.ts` weights `concepts/` at 1.3×.

**Fix:** concept writes route through `importFromContent` (the exact parse→chunk→embed pipeline `put_page` uses — reused, not hand-rolled), with put_page's `isAvailable('embedding')` → `noEmbed` gate. Concept pages now land with `content_chunks` (+ embeddings when a provider is configured).

### #2569 — `dream_generated` provenance was render-time only

**Evidence:** `renderPageToMarkdown` stamped the marker via `frontmatterOverrides` only — the markdown file got it, the `pages.frontmatter` JSONB row didn't, so DB consumers couldn't enumerate generated pages and a later put_page write-through (which re-renders from the DB row) silently erased the file's marker.

**Fix:** new `stampDreamProvenance` persists `dream_generated: true` + `dream_cycle_date` into the DB row for every child-written ref BEFORE reverse-rendering (JSONB merge via `executeRawJsonb` — raw object bound to `$N::jsonb`, never `JSON.stringify` into a cast; plain UPDATE, engine-parity safe, no new engine method). Render-time overrides stay as belt-and-braces. Best-effort per row — a stamp failure never kills the phase.

### #2606 — chronicle judge truncation misrecorded as `no_events`

**Evidence:** `extract-events.ts` capped the judge at `maxTokens: 1500`, only checked `refusal`/`content_filter` stopReasons, and `parseJudgeJson` returned `[]` for both parse failure and a legitimate empty array — so a token-cap-truncated JSON array was recorded as a terminal-looking `no_events`.

**Fix:** `stopReason === 'length'` → `failure: 'truncated'` (the cut-off text is never fed to the parser); `parseJudgeJson` now returns `null` on parse failure (`[]` only for a real empty array); `runChronicleExtract` records these as `status: 'skipped'` with distinct reasons `judge_truncated` / `judge_parse_failed`. Default cap raised 1500 → 4000, configurable via `chronicle.judge_max_tokens` (prefix `chronicle.` already registered; key also added explicitly).

## Tests

New/updated (all green):
- `test/brain-allowlist.serial.test.ts` — put_page tool executes into the configured `sourceId`; malformed sourceId rejected at build time (#1586)
- `test/cycle-synthesize-slug-collection.test.ts` — refs stamped with the cycle sourceId; legacy default preserved (#1586); `stampDreamProvenance` merges into DB frontmatter (queryable values, pre-existing keys survive) + idempotent/missing-page safe (#2569)
- `test/cycle-dream-output-root.test.ts` (new) — prompt templates default vs custom root, allow-list remap, `loadOutputRoot` validation, patterns phase gathers only under the configured root (#2415)
- `test/cycle-patterns.test.ts` — source pin updated preserving intent (scope filter now a bound parameter)
- `test/cycle/extract-atoms-synthesize-concepts.test.ts` — concept pages have `content_chunks` rows; type + frontmatter survive the importFromContent round-trip (#2163)
- `test/chronicle-extract.test.ts` — `judge_truncated` / `judge_parse_failed` skipped outcomes; `parseJudgeJson` null-vs-empty-array contract (#2606)

Verification (redirect-to-file, real exit codes):
- `bun run typecheck` → EXIT=0
- `bun run check:test-isolation` → OK (985 files)
- jsonb guards (`check-jsonb-pattern.sh` + `check-jsonb-params.mjs`) → clean
- `scripts/check-key-files-current-state.sh` → ok; `bun run build:llms` + `bun test test/build-llms.test.ts` → green (KEY_FILES entries updated to current behavior)
- Adjacent suites all green: cycle-synthesize* (5 files), dream.test, dream-cli-flags, e2e dream-synthesize/patterns/chunking/allow-list, chronicle-* (7 files), subagent-handler, synthesize-gateway-adapter, regression-pr-wave-r1-r2-r4, minions, operations-descriptions, brain-allowlist.

**Pre-existing failure (not this PR):** `test/e2e/dream-cycle-phase-order-pglite.test.ts` fails identically on clean master (`willEmbedSynchronously` missing from the test's embedding-module mock) — verified by stash-run against the base commit.

## Scope notes (honest)

- The patterns phase's put_page collection still stamps `'default'` (patterns is not per-source-scoped in cycle.ts today); #1586 as filed targets synthesize. The shared seam (`SubagentHandlerData.source_id`) is in place, so scoping patterns later is a two-line change.
- `defaultJudge`'s gateway call isn't integration-tested (the judge is injectable by design; the config read + stopReason branch are covered via the injectable contract and unit tests on the parser).

Fixes #1586, Fixes #2415, Fixes #2163, Fixes #2569, Fixes #2606

title: feat(engine): opt-in Postgres RLS source-scope binding (lands #2387)
body:
Supersedes #2387 (with credit) — takeover PR landing @harrisali0101's opt-in Postgres RLS source-scope binding with the security review's required fixes applied. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Harris <79081645+harrisali0101@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Security-review summary

Verdict on #2387 was **MERGE-AFTER-FIXES**: no malice found — flag-off SQL verified byte-identical to master, `set_config` value is a bound parameter, zero DDL shipped — but concrete gaps around flag-off overhead and missing test/doc coverage.

## What it does

With `GBRAIN_RLS_SCOPE_BINDING=1`, source-scoped Postgres read methods wrap their queries in a transaction that binds `SELECT set_config('app.scopes', $1, true)` (federated `sourceIds` CSV > scalar `sourceId` > `'*'`), so operator-managed RLS policies can filter rows at the SQL layer. Defense-in-depth layer 2; the app-layer source filters (`sourceScopeOpts`) remain layer 1 and mandatory. Default off; zero behavior change for existing operators.

## Review fixes applied on top of #2387

1. **Flag-off true pass-through.** The original helper always opened a transaction (one pool-hold per read — the #1794 PgBouncer-exhaustion class). Now: flag off → `callback(this.sql)` exactly as master; flag on → scoped `set_config` transaction. The three search methods pass `alwaysTransaction: true` so their pre-existing `sql.begin()` + `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` wrap is preserved byte-identically in both modes.
2. **Shape tests updated** (`test/postgres-engine.test.ts`): the two "wraps its query in sql.begin()" tests now pin the new invariant — search methods route through `withScopedReadTransaction` with `alwaysTransaction: true`; the helper owns the `sql.begin()`; the flag-off non-search path is a true pass-through.
3. **New behavioral tests** (`test/postgres-engine-rls-scope.test.ts`, 9 tests): flag-off pass-through (no begin, no set_config, callback receives the pool handle), flag-off `alwaysTransaction` (begin, no set_config), flag-on `set_config` emission before the callback, federated-array > scalar > `'*'` precedence, and the CSV as a bound parameter (exact literal-segment shape asserted against a hostile value).
4. **Fixed the stale helper header comment** ("pass-through, no transaction wrap") to match the actual branching behavior.
5. **Operator docs** (`docs/ENGINES.md`, PostgresEngine section): the env var, the `CREATE POLICY` SQL, the required `ALTER ROLE ... SET app.scopes = '*'` default, the `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` note for table-owner roles, and the honest caveat that unwrapped paths run under the role default (layer 2 only where wrapped). llms bundles regenerated.

title: feat(search): configurable FTS language + reindex command (lands #580/#581/#582)
body:
Squashed superset takeover of the FTS-language trilogy by @rafaelreis-r, rebased onto current master with the security review's required fixes applied. #582's tree is the superset (582 ⊇ 581 ⊇ 580), so this lands all three as one commit.

Closes #580, Closes #581, Closes #582. Context issue: #584 (left open for the contributor — not auto-closed).

## What lands

- **`GBRAIN_FTS_LANGUAGE`** (default `english`): configures the Postgres text-search configuration on both the query side (`websearch_to_tsquery` in both engines) and the write side (the `update_page_search_vector` / `update_chunk_search_vector` trigger functions), via the new `src/core/fts-language.ts` helper.
- **Migration `configurable_fts_language`**: handler-based (config names can't be bound as parameters), recreates the two trigger functions in the configured language; backfills existing rows when non-english.
- **`gbrain reindex-search-vector [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]`**: escape hatch for changing language after the migration has run — recreates triggers + backfills in place.
- `docs/guides/multi-language-fts.md` (README referenced it; no PR in the trilogy added it) with the `unaccent`+portuguese `pt_br` recipe.

## Security-review summary

- **Allowlist verdict: sound, kept exactly as authored.** Config names can't be parameterized in `to_tsvector`/`websearch_to_tsquery`, so the value is interpolated — gated by `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/` with warn-and-fall-back-to-english on violation. The injection tests (including the `'; DROP TABLE pages; --'` case) are ported verbatim and pass.
- **search_path hardening restored.** Master's trigger functions carry `SET search_path = pg_catalog, public` (v120 / #1647). `CREATE OR REPLACE` resets proconfig, so the trilogy's original function recreations would have silently stripped that hardening from every upgraded install. All four recreation sites (migration handler + reindex command, pages + chunks) now mirror master's hardened bodies; pinned by test assertions and verified live (`pg_proc.proconfig = ["search_path=pg_catalog, public"]` after both the migration and the reindex command).
- **Migration renumbered v116 → v123.** Master's v116 was already claimed (`code_edges_source_backfill_and_callee_index`); master is at v122. The trilogy's own test looks the migration up by name and asserts `version === LATEST_VERSION`, so it survives the renumber.

## Review-convention fixes applied to the reindex command

- Shared progress reporter (`src/core/progress.ts`), phases `reindex_search_vector.pages` / `.chunks`, stderr only (`check-progress-to-stdout.sh` green).
- The two whole-table `UPDATE`s are now id-keyset batched (5000 rows per statement via `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … ORDER BY id LIMIT n) RETURNING id`) so a large brain never holds one giant row lock.
- `--json` no longer bypasses confirmation: non-TTY without `--yes` refuses with a `ConfirmationRequired` envelope, exit 2 (mirrors `reindex-code`, #1784).
- Stale `v33`/`v116` comments swept; llms bundles regenerated with `bun run build:llms` (the original PR hand-edited `llms-full.txt`).
- Trilogy tests quarantined as `*.serial.test.ts` (they mutate `process.env`, per `check-test-isolation`).

- All 27 trilogy tests pass (`fts-language` 14, `fts-language-migration` 7, `reindex-search-vector` 6), including search_path pin assertions.
- Adjacent suites green: `migrate`, `migrations-registry`, `schema-bootstrap-coverage`, `migration-v120`, `chunk-grain-fts`, `migrate-retry`, `migration-in-process` (213 pass), CLI dispatch + search suites (50 pass).

title: feat(sync): --src-subpath + --exclude for monorepo subdir-source support (#753, supersedes #774)
body:
## Summary

Rebased, verified port of #774 (by @jeremyknows — thank you, the design and the NAV guard framing are theirs) onto current master. Supersedes #774, which had gone ~2 months stale against heavy `sync.ts`/`import.ts` churn. Fixes #753.

A single git repo can hold N logical sources at subdirectories (`wiki/`, `memory/`, ...):

- **`--src-subpath <dir>`** — git operations (pull, rev-parse, diff, cat-file) run at the discovered repo root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so worktrees + submodules resolve natively); file walking, imports, deletes and renames are scoped to the subdir. Passing the subdirectory directly as `--repo` / source `local_path` (auto-discovery) works through the same code path — so `gbrain sources add wiki --path ~/mono/wiki` followed by plain `gbrain sync --source wiki` just works.
- **`--exclude <glob>`** (repeatable) — filters scope-relative paths in both the full-sync and incremental paths. Exclusion never deletes previously-imported pages (conservative, matching the metafile posture from #1433).

## Security guards (NAV-1..4)

| Guard | What it blocks | Where |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| NAV-1 scope entry | `--src-subpath ../escape` | realpath containment check before any git op |
| NAV-2 | symlinked subdir pointing outside the repo | same realpath check (git root is realpathed too) |
| NAV-1 TOCTOU | committed symlink file whose target escapes the repo | per-file `isPathSafe` realpath re-validation in the incremental import drain AND the rename reimport; recorded as a failure, i.e. **fail-closed — the bookmark cannot advance past a symlink escape** |
| NAV-4 | `--exclude` set that filters out everything (mistyped pattern) | loud warning in both full and incremental paths |

The existing walker hardening (`collectSyncableFiles` lstat symlink skip, inode-cycle detection, depth cap, git-ls-files fast path) is untouched — `test/sync-walker-symlink.test.ts` and `test/sync-walker-submodule.test.ts` pass unchanged.

## What needed substantive re-porting (vs the original diff)

`sync.ts` grew ~4x since the #774 branch point; the port preserves all of it:

- **#2828 mass-delete safety valve**: the full-sync reconcile now relativizes the walk against the slug base and is scope-restricted (a scoped full sync never treats out-of-scope pages as stale), so a healthy scoped source can't trip — or bypass — the valve.
- **#1794 resumable sync (pinned targets + op_checkpoint banking)**: the scope/exclude filters apply to the deterministic pinned-diff manifest; checkpoints, resume filtering, and the pin-reachability gate are unchanged.
- **#1950 stall watchdog, #2335 heartbeat bump, #2402 crash-safe renames, #1970 bookmark reachability + rename-to-unsyncable folding**: all preserved; the rename-source fold gains a scope test (a rename whose destination leaves the scope deletes the old page).
- **git-ls-files walker (#2315/#2462/#2678)**: `runImport` applies `--exclude` after the walker, so `.gitignore` semantics and symlink policy are unchanged.
- **Slug consistency fix over the original**: #774 (commit b4bfb70) gated git-root-relative slugs on the explicit flag only, which made the auto-discovery flow produce subdir-relative slugs on full sync but git-root-relative slugs on incremental sync — duplicate pages on the first modify. This port uses git-root-relative slugs whenever the scope is a strict subdir (both spellings, both paths), which is what the original PR body actually promised.
- **Checkpoint contract**: `runImport`'s resume checkpoint stays dir-relative (per `resumeFilter`'s contract); only the slug/`source_path` base moves with `slugRoot`.
- `--src-subpath`/`--exclude` are rejected with `--all` (loudly, instead of the original's silent ignore); for `--all` runs, register the subdir as the source's `local_path`.
- `.gitignore` management resolves to the git root at every call site (`manageGitignoreAtGitRoot`) so a subdir source doesn't grow a stray subdir `.gitignore`.

## Interaction with .gbrainignore (#449)

`--exclude` is a per-invocation CLI knob layered on the existing `isSyncable`/`matchesAnyGlob` machinery; a future `.gbrainignore` (#449) would be a per-repo persistent layer feeding the same glob matcher. Nothing here paints it into a corner: patterns are matched scope-relative (what a `.gbrainignore` living in the scope root would naturally use), the matcher (`matchesAnyGlob`) is now exported from `core/sync.ts` for reuse, and exclusion semantics (never delete on exclude) are the ones #449 will want to inherit.

## Tests

`test/sync-monorepo.test.ts` — 13 tests (10 ported from #774 + 3 new):

```
✓ back-compat: sync at git root without srcSubpath imports all files
✓ auto-discovery: repoPath is a git subdir — discoverGitRoot succeeds
✓ --src-subpath wiki: only wiki/ files are imported
✓ --src-subpath memory: only memory/ files are imported
✓ 2 sources in 1 repo: sync each scope independently, no cross-contamination
✓ incremental --src-subpath: only in-scope diff paths are processed   (NEW — the gap #774 flagged as untested)
✓ path-traversal: --src-subpath ../escape is rejected before any git op
✓ path-traversal: symlink subdir pointing outside repo is rejected (NAV-1 TOCTOU)
✓ path-traversal: absolute/deep ..-traversal subpath is rejected      (NEW)
✓ --exclude: single pattern excludes matching files from full sync
✓ --exclude: glob pattern with wildcard
✓ --exclude applies to the incremental path too                        (NEW)
✓ --exclude **/* emits warning when all files are excluded (NAV-4)
```

Verification (all EXIT=0, output captured to files per repo iron rule):

```
bun test test/sync-monorepo.test.ts                       13 pass / 0 fail
adjacent suites batch 1 (sync, walker-symlink, walker-submodule,
  import-walker, sync-strategy, performfullsync-source-id,
  import-resume, import-checkpoint, metafile-skip x2, redos,
  reconcile-mass-delete, sync-delta)                     165 pass / 0 fail
adjacent suites batch 2 (resumable-import, timeout, failures,
  ledger, rename-batch, delete-batch, all-parallel, parallel,
  classifier, isSyncable-shape, cost x2, import-file,
  import-source-id, dedup, storage-sync, inline-extract,
  nudge, resync-recovery, schema-pack-sync)              307 pass / 0 fail
adjacent suites batch 3 (hard-deadline, trigger-cli,
  break-lock-all, concurrency, doctor-consolidation,
  distribution-boundary, image, content-sanity, code-edges,
  signature-stamp, delete-batch.slow, cost-gate.serial)  110 pass / 0 fail
bun run typecheck                                         clean
bun run check:test-isolation                              OK (991 files)
bun run check:jsonb + check-jsonb-params.mjs              clean
scripts/check-key-files-current-state.sh                  ok
bun run build:llms + bun test test/build-llms.test.ts     12 pass / 0 fail
```

One test-message pin updated intent-preserved: `sync.test.ts`'s detached-HEAD stderr assertion pins the caller's repoPath spelling; the message keeps printing `repoPath` while the git op itself runs against the discovered root.

Docs: `docs/architecture/KEY_FILES.md` entries for `sync.ts` + `import.ts` updated to current behavior; llms bundles regenerated.

title: fix(brain-writer): deadline-race verdict from the sentinel, not the clock the timer raced
body:
## Summary

Part of #2946. The hung-COUNT deadline race in `scanBrainSources` derived its verdict from a post-await wall-clock re-check — which races the timer's own drift. On loaded CI runners `setTimeout` callbacks fire measurably EARLY relative to `Date.now()`, so each prior adjustment (the `>=` boundary, then the `+1ms` pad) only moved which wrong status the partial-scan test received: first `'scanned'`, and once the fixture walk grew long enough to straddle the boundary, `'partial'` (the occurrence in #2946: an unrelated doctor PR, `Expected "skipped" / Received "partial"` at 554ms against the 500ms deadline; same commit re-pushed → green).

Fix — take the verdict from the race itself, not the clock the race was against:
- The timeout arm resolves a **module-private sentinel** (`unique symbol`) instead of `null`. The sentinel winning IS the deadline verdict: it sets `deadlineHit`, which the post-await skip-check consults without re-reading `Date.now()`. Timer drift becomes irrelevant for the hung path — early or late, the timeout winning means the budget is spent.
- A COUNT that legitimately resolves `null` (failed/absent count) is now structurally distinguishable from a deadline hit: the source still scans, with `db_page_count` simply unavailable (previously both arms resolved `null` and only the clock re-check told them apart).
- The wall-clock re-check (`>=`) is retained for the case it still owns: a COUNT that RESOLVES slowly enough to eat the budget without the timer winning, plus the pre-existing `remainingMs <= 0` early-out now also sets `deadlineHit` explicitly.
- The `+1ms` pad is removed — it existed only to out-pad the drift this change makes irrelevant.

## Test Coverage

- Existing partial-scan suite unchanged and green — the "hanging COUNT" test that flaked in three guises now exercises a deterministic path (sentinel wins → skipped), verified over 8 consecutive local runs.
- New test pins the null-vs-sentinel distinction: a COUNT resolving `null` before a generous deadline is NOT treated as a deadline verdict — the source still reports `'scanned'` with `db_page_count` unavailable.

Local gates: 9/9 partial-scan tests (×8 repeats), `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun run verify` 31/31 green.

title: `remote ping` reads `job.state` but MinionJob's lifecycle field is `status` — ping never observes completion, always times out with exit 1
body:
## What happened

`gbrain remote ping` from a thin-client install against a healthy host (v0.42.61.0, Postgres engine, worker consuming the queue) always runs to its full `--timeout` and exits 1, printing:

```
Submitted autopilot-cycle (job #11751). Polling...

ping timed out after 900s. Job #11751 is still undefined.
Run `gbrain jobs get 11751` on the host to inspect.
```

— even when the autopilot-cycle it submitted completed successfully minutes earlier. Note the `still undefined`.

## Root cause

`src/commands/remote.ts` (runRemotePing) types and reads a `state` field on the objects returned by `submit_job` / `get_job`:

- `let submitted: { id: number; name: string; state: string }`
- `job = unpackToolResult<{ id: number; state: string; ... }>(res)`
- `if (terminal.includes(job.state)) { ... }`

But both operations return the `MinionJob` row verbatim (`src/core/operations.ts` — `get_job` returns `queue.getJob(...)`, `submit_job` returns `queue.add(...)`), and `MinionJob`'s lifecycle field is **`status`** (`src/core/minions/types.ts`). So every poll sees `job.state === undefined`, the terminal check never matches, the state-transition log line never fires, and the loop exhausts the timeout unconditionally.

## Impact

- Every `remote ping` invocation burns its full timeout (default 15 min) and exits 1 — success is indistinguishable from failure at the call site.
- Anything scheduled on `remote ping` (cron/launchd autopilot triggers, the documented thin-client "trigger a cycle" path) reports perpetual failure while the host is actually fine, and wastes a 15-minute poll per fire.
- The timeout message prints `still undefined`, which sends the operator debugging the queue instead of the client.

## Repro

Thin-client install pointed at any live host with a working queue consumer:

```
gbrain remote ping --timeout 2m
```

Watch the submitted job complete on the host (`gbrain jobs get <id>`, status `completed`) while the ping still times out and exits 1.

## Fix

PR incoming: reads switched to `status` (the ping's own JSON output keys `state`/`last_state` kept as-is for consumers), plus a source-audit regression test in the `thin-client-routing-audit.test.ts` idiom pinning the field reads.

title: Thin-client `jobs` and `config` fabricate a scratch local PGLite (full migration replay on every invocation) instead of routing or refusing
body:
## What happened

On a thin-client install (`~/.gbrain/config.json` with `remote_mcp` set, `engine: pglite`), every `gbrain jobs get <id>` / `gbrain jobs list` invocation prints the entire migration chain before doing anything:

```
  Schema version 1 → 122 (117 migration(s) pending)
  [2] slugify_existing_pages...
  [2] ✓ slugify_existing_pages
  ...
  117 migration(s) applied
Job #11751: autopilot-cycle (WAITING)
```

The job data itself is correct (it comes over MCP via the v0.32 routing branches) — but the CLI first **creates and migrates an empty scratch PGLite** in the thin-client `GBRAIN_HOME`, on **every single invocation**. A stray `gbrain config …` on a thin client does the same, and then reads/writes config rows in a scratch DB nobody will ever see.

## Root cause

`handleCliOnly` in `src/cli.ts` checks `THIN_CLIENT_REFUSED_COMMANDS`, then unconditionally runs `const engine = await connectEngine()` for everything that survives. `jobs` and `config` aren't in the refused set:

- `jobs list|get` have thin-client MCP routing *inside* `runJobs` (v0.32, `callRemoteTool('list_jobs'/'get_job')`) — but the scratch engine is connected before dispatch ever reaches them.
- All other `jobs` subcommands (`work`, `supervisor`, `submit`, `stats`, …) are host-queue-bound and should refuse with a pinpoint hint, per the existing v0.31.1/#734 pattern — instead they run against the empty scratch DB (e.g. `jobs stats` happily reports an empty queue for a busy host).
- `config get/set` operates on the host brain's config plane; on a thin client it silently targets the scratch store.

## Impact

- Seconds of migration replay + a phantom `brain.pglite` store fabricated in the thin-client home per invocation.
- Misleading output: commands appear to succeed against an empty brain (the v0.31.1 "silent-empty-results" bug class this table exists to prevent).
- The phantom store shadows real debugging — a thin-client home accumulates a full-schema DB that looks like a real brain.

## Fix

PR incoming, following the existing dispatch patterns:

- `cli.ts`: dispatch thin-client `jobs list|get` engine-free (`runJobs(null, …)`) before `connectEngine()`; refuse the other `jobs` subcommands via `refuseThinClient` with a hint; add `config` to `THIN_CLIENT_REFUSED_COMMANDS` + hint.
- `jobs.ts`: `runJobs` accepts `BrainEngine | null`, guarded so null can only reach the MCP-routed `list`/`get` branches.
- Tests: behavioral (no scratch store created, no migration replay, refusals carry hints — `cli-dispatch-thin-client.test.ts` idiom) + source-audit pins (`thin-client-routing-audit.test.ts` idiom).

Related: #2948 (found in the same debugging session — `remote ping` polling the wrong field).

title: fix(remote): poll MinionJob.status, not .state — ping now sees completion (#2948)

title: fix(cli): stop thin-client jobs/config from fabricating a scratch PGLite (#2949)
body:
Fixes #2949.

## Problem

`jobs list|get` have had remote MCP routing since v0.32, but the CLI shell still ran `connectEngine()` before dispatch. On a thin-client install that fabricates an empty scratch PGLite in the thin-client `GBRAIN_HOME` and replays the entire migration chain (`Schema version 1 → 122, 117 migration(s) pending…`) on **every invocation**, before the remote call even runs. The host-only `jobs` subcommands (`work`, `supervisor`, `submit`, `stats`, …) and `config` did the same instead of refusing — `jobs stats` happily reports an empty queue for a busy host, and `config set` writes rows nobody will ever read (the v0.31.1 silent-empty-results bug class).

## Change

Follows the existing dispatch patterns:

- **`src/cli.ts`**: thin-client `jobs list|get` dispatch engine-free (`runJobs(null, args)`) before `connectEngine()`; every other `jobs` subcommand refuses via `refuseThinClient` with a pinpoint hint (naming the routable subcommands and the `submit_job`/`list_jobs`/`get_job` MCP tools); `config` joins `THIN_CLIENT_REFUSED_COMMANDS` with a hint pointing at the host's file-plane config. `jobs` is deliberately NOT in the refused set — the partial dispatch owns it (noted in a comment at the set).
- **`src/commands/jobs.ts`**: `runJobs` accepts `BrainEngine | null`, guarded at entry so null can only reach the MCP-routed `list`/`get` branches (which never touch the engine); narrowed once so the host-only cases typecheck unchanged.
- **Tests**: behavioral additions to `cli-dispatch-thin-client.test.ts` (refusals carry hints + exit 1; `jobs get`/`jobs list` create **no** scratch store and print **no** migration replay) and source-audit pins in `thin-client-routing-audit.test.ts` (the new dispatch block, the `config` entry + hint, `jobs`'s deliberate absence from the set, the null-engine guard).

## Verification

title: search stats cache hit rate is structurally 0/0: telemetry records only from bare hybridSearch, which never knows the cache outcome (and cache hits skip telemetry entirely)
body:
## Environment

gbrain 0.42.62.0, Postgres engine, `search.mode` balanced (default), cache enabled (bundle default), OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` 1536d. Single-user brain in daily agent-driven use.

## Observed

`gbrain search stats --days 14` on a brain with real search volume:

```
Total searches:        244
Cache hit rate:        0.0%  (0 hit / 0 miss)
```

Not "0% hit rate" — **zero hits AND zero misses** across 244 searches. Yet the cache itself is demonstrably alive: `SELECT count(*) FROM query_cache` returns 455 rows with `max(created_at)` advancing daily, so the writeback path fires constantly. Raw `search_telemetry` rows confirm it is not an aggregation artifact — every daily bucket has `cache_hit = 0, cache_miss = 0` while `count` and `sum_budget_dropped` accumulate normally.

## Root cause (traced in v0.42.62.0 source)

Telemetry recording and cache classification live in two functions that never exchange the cache outcome:

1. `recordSearchTelemetry` is called from exactly one place: the `emitMeta` helper inside **bare `hybridSearch`** (`src/core/search/hybrid.ts:946`). The meta objects built at all three of its return paths carry no `cache` field — bare `hybridSearch` never consults the cache, so it can't.
2. **`hybridSearchCached`** is the only place that knows the cache outcome (`cacheStatus: 'hit' | 'miss' | 'disabled'`). On miss/disabled it delegates to inner `hybridSearch`, whose telemetry record then classifies the search as *neither* hit nor miss. The cache-aware `finalMeta` it builds is emitted to `onMeta` consumers only — never recorded.
3. On a cache **hit**, `hybridSearchCached` returns early without ever reaching inner `hybridSearch` — so a hit search is not recorded **at all**: it is missing from `count`, `sum_results`, `sum_tokens`, and the rank-1 drift signal, not just from the hit counter.

So `TelemetryWriter.record`'s `if (meta.cache?.status === 'hit') b.cache_hit += 1;` branches (`telemetry.ts:114-115`) are structurally unreachable from the production `query` op path.

## Impact

- The cache-observability third of `gbrain search stats` is permanently dead for every operator: it can never distinguish "cache is working great" from "cache never serves a row". The cost anchors in CLAUDE.md/docs lean on "cache hits cut all numbers ~50%" — this is the surface meant to verify that, and it can't.
- `search tune`'s recommendations run on the same telemetry, so any future cache-tuning heuristic (e.g. "hit rate low → lower similarity threshold") would silently never fire.
- Hit-path searches vanishing from `count` also skews avg results / avg tokens / rank-1 telemetry once a brain's cache does start serving (the more the cache works, the more the stats undercount).

Found via long-horizon dogfooding: it takes a couple of weeks of real usage plus cross-checking `search stats` against the `query_cache` table to notice that 0/0 is impossible rather than merely unlucky.

## Fix sketch

Single-record-per-search invariant, held at the layer that knows the outcome:

- Thread the cache outcome into the one existing record call: `hybridSearchCached` passes an internal `_telemetryCacheStatus: 'miss' | 'disabled'` down to inner `hybridSearch` (same internal-opt pattern as `_queryEmbedDeadline`), which folds it into the *recorded* meta only — `onMeta` payloads unchanged, `count`/`sum_tokens`/`budget_dropped`/rank-1 behavior byte-identical.
- On the hit path, record once from `hybridSearchCached` itself with the already-built `cachedMeta` (which carries `cache.status='hit'`), the post-slice/budget result count, and the same rank-1 rule the inner paths use.
- Bare `hybridSearch` callers (think/gather, brainstorm, enrich, evals, …) keep recording exactly as today, with no cache classification — they never consulted the cache.

Happy to submit a PR with a wiring test that drives a real store→hit roundtrip through `hybridSearchCached` (mocked `embedQuery`, real PGLite cache) and pins hit/miss/disabled/bare-call telemetry classification.

title: fix(search): classify cache hit/miss in telemetry — hits were invisible, misses unclassified
body:
## Summary

Part of #2952. `gbrain search stats` reports `0 hit / 0 miss` forever on every brain, because telemetry recording and cache classification live in functions that never exchange the outcome: `recordSearchTelemetry` fires only from bare `hybridSearch` (whose meta never carries a `cache` field), while `hybridSearchCached` — the only place that knows `cacheStatus` — returns from a HIT before any record at all. So misses count as unclassified searches, and hit searches vanish from stats entirely (count, results, tokens, rank-1 — not just the hit counter). Found on a live brain where `query_cache` held 455 growing rows while every telemetry bucket read `0/0`.

Design — one record per search, classified at the layer that knows the outcome:

- **`HybridSearchOpts._telemetryCacheStatus`** (internal, same threading pattern as `_queryEmbedDeadline`): `hybridSearchCached` passes `'miss'` or `'disabled'` down to the inner `hybridSearch`, which folds it into the **recorded meta only**. `onMeta` payloads are byte-identical to before on every path, and the miss/disabled records keep their existing count/results/tokens/budget-drop/rank-1 values exactly — the fold adds classification, nothing else.
- **Hit path** records once from `hybridSearchCached` itself with the already-built `cachedMeta` (`cache.status='hit'`), the post-slice/budget result count, and the same rank-1 rule the inner return paths use. Tokens are gated on the **mode-resolved** budget, mirroring the inner paths' `resolvedMode.tokenBudget > 0` meta condition — otherwise a tokenmax (budget-off) brain would record real tokens on hits but 0 on misses, inflating avg-tokens as the hit rate rises (codex review).
- **Bare `hybridSearch` direct callers** (think/gather, brainstorm, enrich, evals, diagnose, …) record exactly as before, with no cache classification — they never consulted the cache.

Double-count is structurally impossible: miss/disabled are recorded by the inner function (once), hit by the wrapper (once, and the inner never runs on a hit).

Two boundaries verified during review and left as-is deliberately: `SemanticQueryCache.lookup` converts every error to a miss inside its own try/catch (the "lookup rejects and skips both record sites" path cannot occur), and searches that throw before completing were never recorded pre-fix either — telemetry counts completed searches; changing that would be a separate, behavior-widening decision.

## Test Coverage

`test/search-telemetry-cache-wiring.serial.test.ts` (serial: `mock.module` + gateway/env mutation) drives the real pipeline — PGLite brain, real `SemanticQueryCache` store→lookup roundtrip, mocked `embedQuery` for a deterministic vector — and pins the decision matrix:

- consulted + no row → recorded once with `cache_miss`, then the identical query is served from cache and recorded once with `cache_hit`, contributing results/rank-1/tokens (with an **exact token-delta parity** assertion: the hit's token contribution equals the miss's, since it serves the same stored set)
- consult skipped (`useCache:false`) → recorded once, neither counter
- consult degraded (embed-provider failure → catch → disabled; keyword fallback serves) → recorded once, neither counter
- bare `hybridSearch` → recorded once, no cache field in the caller-visible meta (pins the recorded-only fold)

Revert-checked: on pre-fix source the matrix test goes red exactly at the miss classification (`miss=0`), reproducing the reported symptom; the contract-pinning cases stay green pre-fix as expected (those paths' counters were already correct).

Local gates: wiring test 8 consecutive green runs, cache/telemetry-related suites 74 tests green, `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun run verify` 31/31 green.

title: fix(search): per-call token-budget meta masked the real cut on both cache paths; restore vacuous search-lite coverage
body:
## Summary

While building the wiring test for #2953 I found that `test/hybrid-search-lite.serial.test.ts` — the integration coverage for the search-lite token-budget feature — has been **structurally vacuous since it was written**: `putPage` never creates chunks, `searchKeyword` joins `content_chunks`, so every fixture query returned zero rows on every machine. The tight-budget cut test's defensive skip (`if (unbounded.length < 2) return;`, rationalized in a comment as "keyword search may dedupe by page") silently returned before its assertions had ever executed anywhere, and the two budget-meta tests ran against empty result sets where `kept === results.length` passes trivially at `0 === 0`.

Restoring the fixture immediately made the suite catch a **real meta bug** — which is the strongest possible argument that the coverage was worth restoring:

**With a per-call `tokenBudget`, the caller-visible budget meta always reported `dropped: 0`, masking the real cut.** The inner `hybridSearch` enforces the resolved budget (per-call wins in `resolveSearchMode`) and its meta carries the true dropped count — but `hybridSearchCached` re-applied the budget to the already-cut set and published *that* no-op pass's meta on both paths:

- **Miss path**: `finalMeta` used the outer `budgetMeta` (`dropped: 0`) instead of `innerMeta.token_budget`. Telemetry — recorded from the inner meta — disagreed with what `onMeta` consumers and `--explain` saw.
- **Hit path** (found by review): the stored row holds an already-trimmed set, so the read-time re-application also reads `dropped: 0`, while the miss that produced the *same* result set reported the real cut.

Fix, both paths, prefer the record that witnessed the actual cut:

- miss: `finalMeta.token_budget = innerMeta.token_budget ?? budgetMeta` (gated on a per-call budget, so the "no per-call budget → no token_budget meta" contract is untouched);
- hit: `cachedMeta.token_budget = hit.meta.token_budget ?? budgetMeta`. Safe unconditionally: `tokenBudget` is folded into `knobsHash` (`tb=`), so a hit only ever serves a lookup with the identical resolved budget as the write — the outer pass can never cut further, and the stored record's budget always matches the caller's. `budgetMeta` stays as the fallback for legacy rows stored without a budget record, and the outer enforcement itself stays (it is the only enforcement on the hit path).

Inner and outer budgets cannot diverge on the miss path either: a positive per-call value wins both resolutions (review confirmed the same).

## Test Coverage

- `test/hybrid-search-lite.serial.test.ts`: fixture pages now carry explicit chunks (pattern: `test/chunk-grain-fts.test.ts`) with **mixed page types** (person/company/note) so dedup's Layer-3 type-diversity cap no longer shapes the test; the defensive skip is replaced with a hard `>= 2` precondition; the cut assertions now execute and are exact — `dropped === unbounded.length - results.length` and `0 < used <= budget` (increase-only/upper-bound-only forms accept wrong positive counts and bogus zeros); budget-meta tests assert non-empty result sets.
- `test/hybrid-cached-hit-budget-meta.serial.test.ts` (new): drives a real store→hit roundtrip (mocked `embedQuery` for a deterministic vector, real PGLite `SemanticQueryCache`) and pins `hit.token_budget == miss.token_budget` for the identical query+knobs.
- Both fixes revert-checked red: with the meta changes stashed, the lite cut test fails at `dropped` (received 0) and the hit test fails at `dropped` (received 0); restored, both green.

Local gates: both serial files 5 consecutive green runs, budget/meta/cache-related suites (`commands-search`, `search-telemetry`, `token-budget`, `hybrid-meta.serial`, `query-cache`, `query-cache-knobs-hash.serial`) green, `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun run verify` 31/31 green.

Independent of #2953 (adjacent hunks in `hybrid.ts`, no overlap; either lands cleanly in any order).
