title: fix(cli): register reconcile-links in CLI_ONLY so it is reachable (#2900)
body:
## Summary

`gbrain reconcile-links` is advertised in `gbrain --help` and fully implemented (`src/commands/reconcile-links.ts`, dispatched via a real `case 'reconcile-links':` block in `handleCliOnly`), but it was **unreachable**:

```
$ gbrain reconcile-links --dry-run
Unknown command: reconcile-links
```

## Root cause

Dispatch only enters `handleCliOnly` when the command name is present in the `CLI_ONLY` Set (`src/cli.ts:320`). `'reconcile-links'` was missing from that set, so every invocation fell through to the shared-operations lookup, found nothing, and hit the generic `Unknown command` branch — never reaching its own `case`.

This is the same class of drift as #2035 (`calibration`).

## Fix

- Add `'reconcile-links'` to the `CLI_ONLY` Set, grouped with the other code-edge commands (`code-callers`, `code-callees`).
- Add a focused reachability regression test (`test/reconcile-links-cli-reachability.test.ts`) mirroring the existing #2035 guard in `test/cli-bigint-normalize.test.ts`.

Closes #2900.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test test/reconcile-links-cli-reachability.test.ts` — asserts `CLI_ONLY.has('reconcile-links')`.
- [ ] `bun test test/reconcile-links.serial.test.ts` — existing behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Manual: `gbrain reconcile-links --dry-run` no longer prints "Unknown command".

> Note: I was unable to run the test suite locally (this environment has no `bun` runtime or installed dependencies). The change is a single Set-membership addition plus a static-membership test mirroring an existing passing guard; CI will validate.

title: fix(pages): default chunker_version to MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION on INSERT (#2807)
body:
## Summary

`putPage`'s INSERT defaulted `chunker_version` to the literal `1`:

```ts
COALESCE(${chunkerVersion}::smallint, 1)
```

Callers that don't supply `chunker_version` (no MCP/subagent caller does — it's internal metadata) landed new pages at **v1**. Dream subagents write through `putPage` directly, so their pages got v1 and `doctor`'s `contextual_retrieval_coverage` check flagged them as "older chunker_version" **forever** — even though the pages were actually chunked and embedded with the current chunker (embedding coverage stays 100%). `reindex --markdown` clears it, but the next dream cycle brings it back.

## Fix

Default the INSERT to `MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION` (currently 3) on **both** engines (`postgres-engine.ts`, `pglite-engine.ts`), importing the constant from `core/chunkers/recursive.ts`. The `ON CONFLICT ... UPDATE` COALESCE-preserve is left untouched, so an explicitly supplied version is still honored and never lowered below the current version.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test test/chunker-version-insert-default.test.ts`
  - page written without `chunker_version` → lands at `MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION`, not 1
  - explicit `chunker_version` honored on INSERT
  - re-put without `chunker_version` does not lower an already-current version
- [ ] `bun test test/pglite-engine.test.ts` — existing putPage behavior unchanged.

> Note: I could not run the suite locally (this environment has no `bun` runtime or installed deps). The change is a two-line INSERT-default swap mirrored across both engines plus an engine-level regression test; CI will validate.

Closes #2807.

title: fix: add GBrain autopilot cost guardrails
body:
## Summary

- enforce a hard two-hour minimum between autopilot cycles across launchd, systemd, and cron installs
- make autonomous jobs single-attempt with two-hour-to-one-day failure cooldowns and zero SDK retries by default
- add an atomic, database-backed daily AI budget governor covering gateway chat, embeddings, expansion/OCR, and reranking
- charge crashed or expired reservations pessimistically so failures cannot restore budget headroom
- remove provider credentials from generated launchd configuration and make fatal exits stay stopped

## Why

The previous controls could amplify costs in several layers at once: low health shortened the autopilot interval, service managers relaunched failed processes, autonomous jobs retried, and the provider SDK also retried. Budget reservations were not fully atomic and expired reservations restored their estimated headroom, so crashes could weaken the cap.

This change treats cadence, retries, and spend accounting as independent safety boundaries. When `ai.daily_budget_usd` is configured, every priced gateway call reserves shared daily headroom before transport and fails closed if pricing or the ledger is unavailable.

## Impact

- generated autopilot installs use `--interval 7200 --min-interval 7200`
- launchd uses `KeepAlive=false`; systemd uses bounded failure-only restarts
- autonomous jobs use one attempt and provider SDK calls default to zero retries
- `ai.daily_budget_usd` is a registered configuration key; absent or zero preserves backward compatibility
- daily accounting is shared across GBrain processes and uses pessimistic settlement on provider or process failure

## Validation

- focused guardrail and gateway suite: 101 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run verify`: 31/31 checks green
- `git diff --check`
- four parallel embedding-dimension failures from the broad suite passed in isolation (21/21)
- three remaining legacy fixture failures reproduce unchanged on the `origin/master` baseline (`hybrid-meta.serial` and `worker-registry.serial`)

title: chronicle last-seen returns future-dated events → days_ago always 0 ("seen today")
body:
**What happened?**

`gbrain last-seen <person>` returns a *future*-dated chronicle event as the "last seen" date and reports `days_ago: 0` ("seen today"). On a brain with `auto_chronicle` on:

```
$ gbrain last-seen people/jane-doe
{ "entity_slug": "people/jane-doe",
  "last_date": "2026-08-01", "last_event_slug": "life/events/2026-08-01-<id>",
  "days_ago": 0 }          # today is 2026-07-15 — the event is 17 days in the FUTURE
```

`life/events/2026-08-01-<id>` is a real `auto_chronicle` event correctly dated in the future (a planned engagement/milestone), wrongly surfaced as a "last seen." Sweeping all 100 person pages: **8 returned a future `last_date`, every one `days_ago: 0`** — worst ~4 months out (a future-dated conference `calendar-event`, whose attendees all read as "seen today").

**What did you expect?**

"Last seen" is a *past* relation — it should return the most recent event **on or before today** (or `--asof`), never a scheduled/future one. Note `--asof <today>` does **not** currently help: it only reaches `finalizeLastSeen`, never the query's WHERE clause.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Brain with `auto_chronicle` on and any meeting / `calendar-event` whose `when` is in the future (a scheduled conference, a planned end-date).
2. `gbrain last-seen people/<someone in that event's who>`
3. → returns `last_date` = the future date, `days_ago: 0`.


**Environment**
- gbrain: `0.42.62.0` (current; also reproduced on 0.42.56)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS · Bun `1.3.14`
- DB: self-hosted Postgres — **and** the PGLite engine (same missing bound in both)

**`gbrain doctor --json` output**
healthy apart from the known chronicle-orphan ratio (#2264), which is unrelated to this read bug.

---

## Root cause

A **reader** bug, not an extractor bug — recording future events is by design (`src/core/chronicle/eligibility.ts` `ELIGIBLE_TYPES` includes `calendar-event`, which is inherently often future). Two spots:

1. `getLastSeen` (in `postgres-engine.ts` and its PGLite twin) has **no upper date bound**. Its sibling `getOnThisDay`, a few methods away, *does* bound (`AND te.date < ${target}`) — the guard was just never added here.
2. `chronicle/last-seen.ts` `finalizeLastSeen`: `days_ago = Math.max(0, …)` clamps the negative delta to `0`, which is what disguises a future date as "today" instead of surfacing it as obviously wrong.

## Why it's invisible in CI

No test covers the future case (`grep -r future src/core/chronicle test/chronicle-*` = 0). The gold eval (`src/eval/chronicle/harness.ts`) asserts only a *past* last-seen, so `gbrain eval chronicle` stays 6/6 with the bug live.

## Fix

Bound the query to `te.date <= COALESCE(asof, current_date)` in both engines (mirrors the existing `getOnThisDay` bound). A fix is ready and I'll open a PR that closes this — it adds a future-event regression in `test/chronicle-timeline-reads.test.ts` (PGLite) plus a live-Postgres e2e in `test/e2e/`, fail-before / pass-after on both engines. Happy to adjust the approach if you'd prefer a different bound.

title: fix(chronicle): bound last-seen to <= asof/today so future events don't read as "seen today"
body:
**Impact:** any entity with a scheduled *future* event — a `calendar-event`, a planned milestone — reads as **last-seen = today** (`days_ago: 0`), even if you last actually saw them months ago. That silently corrupts every recency / staleness signal built on last-seen (e.g. "haven't spoken to X in N days" prompts, relationship-radar surfacing).

**Root cause:** `getLastSeen` had no upper date bound, so a future-dated chronicle event became the entity's "last seen" date; `finalizeLastSeen`'s `Math.max(0, …)` then clamped the negative delta to `days_ago: 0`. Recording future events is intended (`eligibility.ts` `ELIGIBLE_TYPES` includes `calendar-event`); the reader just needs to stop counting them as "seen."

**Fix:** bound the query to `te.date <= COALESCE(asof, current_date)` in both engines, mirroring the existing `getOnThisDay` bound (`te.date < target`).

**One behavior change to flag:** `asof` now filters rows (in the WHERE), not just the `days_ago` math in `finalizeLastSeen`. Before, a time-travel read (`asof` in the past) returned the latest event *regardless* of `asof`, and the `Math.max(0, …)` clamp reported it as `days_ago: 0` — unusable output. The `chronicle_last_seen` op does expose `asof`, but no *correct* behavior depended on that clamped-to-0 result. The new path is the correct as-of semantics and matches `getOnThisDay`.

Regression test in `test/chronicle-timeline-reads.test.ts`: an entity with past events plus a future event → last-seen returns the most recent PAST event, not the future one; and `asof` after the future date lets it through.

**Fails before, passes after.**

Verified on **both engines**, fail-before/pass-after:
- **PGLite** — `bun test test/chronicle-timeline-reads.test.ts` (8/8); the new case fails on unpatched code with `Received: "2026-08-01"`, passes with the fix.
- **Postgres** — `bun test test/e2e/chronicle-last-seen-postgres.test.ts` against a live PG16 + pgvector database (DATABASE_URL-gated, skips when unset). Unpatched:`getLastSeen` returns the future event `2026-08-01`; patched: returns the most recent past event `2026-06-20`, and `asof` after the future date lets it through.
- `bun run verify` 31/31 (typecheck + full check suite).

Both engines get the identical bound (the same `getOnThisDay` pattern already used in that file). Not a retrieval/ranking change (chronicle read, no search path), so no `eval replay` delta.

Fixes #2991.

## Known nuance (called out for the reviewer)
The query filters `te.date` but ORDERs BY `COALESCE(ep.effective_date, te.date)`.
Both derive from the event's `when`, so for any real event they're the same day and the bound is exact. Bounding `te.date` (not `effective_date`) is deliberate — it mirrors `getOnThisDay`, keeping the two chronicle reads consistent.

`finalizeLastSeen`'s `Math.max(0, …)` clamp is left in place: with the SQL bound it's a no-op (last_date ≤ base ⇒ days_ago ≥ 0), kept as defense-in-depth. Flagged so the leftover clamp isn't read as an oversight.

title: fix(extract): --dry-run must not write the extract_rollup_7d cache row
body:
**Impact:** `extract-conversation-facts --dry-run` documents *"no DB writes, no checkpoint advance"* (help text), but a dry run **UPSERTs a row into `extract_rollup_7d`** — so a "preview" mutates the DB (bumps `round_completed_count` / `updated_at` for `kind='facts.conversation'`, which feeds doctor's `extract_health`). Anyone using `--dry-run` to safely preview extraction is silently writing cache state.

**Root cause:** `writeRunReceiptAndRollup` is called unconditionally at both exit paths (`extract-conversation-facts.ts` — budget-exhausted and normal). Inside it, the receipt-page write is already gated on `facts_inserted > 0` (always 0 in dry-run), but the rollup `upsertExtractRollup` fires **unconditionally** (commented "ALWAYS fire so doctor's extract_health sees the cycle ran"). Every other side-effect — fact INSERTs, orphan delete, checkpoint advance, audit row — is correctly `!dryRun`-gated; this one write path was missed.

**Fix:** gate both `writeRunReceiptAndRollup` call sites on `!dryRun`. The writer returns void and its only non-rollup action (the receipt page) is already suppressed in dry-run, so gating at the call site skips nothing else — and it mirrors the existing `!dryRun` guards already used on the insert / checkpoint / audit paths.

**Not changed (called out):** `--dry-run` still calls the extractor (LLM) — `facts_extracted` is the reported "would extract N" preview count, a designed dry-run signal that requires the model call. Left as-is; happy to add a segmentation-only / `--no-llm` mode separately if that's wanted.

**Verified** — fail-before / pass-after, fully hermetic:
- Extended `test/extract-conversation-facts.test.ts` (in-memory PGLite + stubbed chat/embed transports — no live LLM, no live brain): a dry run leaves `extract_rollup_7d` empty. **Fails on unpatched code (`Received: 1`), passes with the fix.**
- Full test file 29/29; `bun run verify` 31/31.

Blast radius: 2 gated call sites + 1 regression test (+ a `DELETE FROM extract_rollup_7d` in the test's `beforeEach` for isolation). No schema, no API, no signature change.

**Scope note:** this is about the *persistent* cache write. A dry run still briefly acquires the per-page advisory lock (`gbrain_cycle_locks` INSERT on acquire / DELETE on release) — transient, net-zero, and pre-existing — so it's not literally zero-DML; that's out of scope here. This PR stops the one write that leaves durable state (the `extract_rollup_7d` cache row feeding doctor's `extract_health`).

title: bug: synthesize_concepts skips edge reconciliation for fingerprint-unchanged pages
body:
**What happened?**

`runPhaseSynthesizeConcepts` skips a concept group entirely when its stored
`synthesis_input_hash` matches the current input hash:

```ts
const existing = existingConcepts.get(outputSlug);
if (existing?.inputHash === inputHash) {
  conceptsSkippedUnchanged++;
  await maybeYield();
  continue;
}
```

This correctly avoids unnecessary narrative regeneration and LLM work, but it
also bypasses the later `importFromContent` path that imports the rendered
markdown and reconciles its links.

As a result, a synthesized concept page can have:

- an unchanged and valid `synthesis_input_hash`;
- supporting-atom wikilinks already present in its markdown body;
- missing or stale graph edges;

and subsequent `synthesize_concepts` runs will never repair those edges because
the fingerprint optimization exits before reconciliation.

Relevant code:

- `src/core/cycle/synthesize-concepts.ts:300–308`
- `src/core/cycle/synthesize-concepts.ts:354–372`
- `src/core/cycle/synthesize-concepts.ts:579–594`

**What did you expect?**

An unchanged synthesis input should skip narrative regeneration and avoid an LLM
call, while still allowing deterministic graph reconciliation.

A rerun should be able to restore missing edges from the existing concept
markdown without rewriting the page or changing its synthesis fingerprint.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create or select a synthesized concept page whose stored
   `synthesis_input_hash` matches its current atom-group input.
2. Confirm that the page body contains supporting-atom wikilinks.
3. Remove or omit the corresponding graph edges while leaving the page content
   and synthesis fingerprint unchanged.
4. Run:

   ```bash
   gbrain dream --phase synthesize_concepts
   ```

5. Observe that:
   - `concepts_skipped_unchanged` increments;
   - the page is not passed through `importFromContent`;
   - the missing graph edges remain missing.

**Suggested direction**

Separate the two concerns:

1. skip narrative synthesis/page rewriting when the input fingerprint is
   unchanged;
2. still run deterministic link reconciliation, either:
   - through a dedicated generated-link materializer; or
   - through a reconciliation path that does not rewrite or re-embed the page.

The fix should not require an LLM call.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A concept with an unchanged fingerprint and missing supporting-atom edges
      has those edges restored on the next phase run.
- [ ] The repair does not invoke the synthesis model.
- [ ] The repair does not rewrite unchanged page content.
- [ ] Existing correct edges are not duplicated.
- [ ] Source scoping remains correct.
- [ ] A regression test covers the unchanged-fingerprint/missing-edge case.
- [ ] The phase receipt reports repaired/reconciled edges separately from
      concepts written.

**Environment**

- gbrain: `0.42.62.0`
- commit: `c125e8b0`
- branch: `master`
- Bun: `1.3.13`
- OS: macOS `26.5.2`
- Database: Postgres
- schema migration: `130`

**Doctor context**

The local brain reports high aggregate graph coverage but also a material
link-extraction lag. Full doctor output contains private brain slugs and is not
included in this public report. The defect is independently reproducible from
the control flow above.

title: feat(cli): GBRAIN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS env override for the per-sink teardown drain budget
body:
## Problem

`finishCliTeardown` drains fire-and-forget background sinks with a hardcoded 2s per-sink budget (`DEFAULT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` in `src/core/cli-force-exit.ts`). That budget is tuned for sub-second cloud chat providers. On a self-hosted provider — e.g. an ollama model at 10–20s per completion — a `facts:absorb` extraction can never finish inside it, so every one-shot CLI exit (sync timers especially) aborts the in-flight chat:

```
facts:absorb → <page>
  pipeline_error: [chat(ollama:<model>)] The operation was aborted.
```

Because the page is re-touched on the next timed `gbrain sync`, the absorb re-enqueues and re-aborts every run — facts from those pages silently never land, and `doctor`'s `facts_extraction_health` warns permanently. Observed live on a Postgres brain with a 5-min sync timer + local ollama extraction model: the same two churning pages aborted ~17×/day, always at ~2.0s (client-side cancel visible in the ollama server log), while the identical extraction succeeds in one shot when run through the long-lived MCP server (no teardown).

## Fix

`resolveDrainTimeoutMs()`: `GBRAIN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` env override — the same env-only escape-hatch pattern as `GBRAIN_TEARDOWN_DEADLINE_MS` and `GBRAIN_FLUSH_GRACE_MS` — over the 2000ms default.

- An explicit `drainTimeoutMs` from a call site still wins; the env replaces only the default.
- `computeTeardownDeadlineMs` already takes the resolved value as input, so the backstop deadline scales automatically with it.
- Garbage / zero / negative env values fall back to the default (matching the existing knobs' posture).

## Tests

Added to `test/cli-finish-teardown.test.ts` (house `withEnv` pattern): default value, env override, garbage/zero/negative fallback, `finishCliTeardown` draining with the env-resolved budget, and explicit opts winning over env. Suite: 26 pass / 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` clean.

title: fix(takes): default takes extraction to the configured chat_model instead of hardcoded cloud Haiku
body:
## Problem

`extract-takes-from-pages.ts` hardcodes `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5` as the takes-extraction model. On an OAuth/local-only install (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; chat routed through a local gateway model), every takes extraction dies with `llm_unavailable` — the takes layer silently never populates and the `takes_count` health check stays red, even though the brain has a perfectly good configured `chat_model`.

## Fix

Default the takes-extraction model to the configured `chat_model` (resolved through the existing model-config chain), keeping `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5` as the final fallback when no chat model is configured. Explicit `opts.model` still wins. One file, 6 lines.

Verified live on a Postgres brain with an ollama-gateway chat model: 586 takes generated where extraction previously failed 100% of the time; `takes_count` health check now OK.

## Tests

No behavior change for cloud-key installs (fallback preserved). Suite: 304 takes-related tests pass; `bun run verify` all 31 checks green; typecheck clean.

title: fix(providers): route diagnostics through buildGatewayConfig so file-plane keys are visible (closes #2728)
body:
## Summary

`gbrain providers list` / `gbrain providers test` build their own `AIGatewayConfig` in `configureFromEnv()` instead of using `buildGatewayConfig()` — the single ownership seam that folds file-plane API keys (`openrouter_api_key`, `zeroentropy_api_key`, ...) into the gateway env. Result: the diagnostics command can report a provider as `✗ missing <ENV_VAR>` even when it's correctly configured via `~/.gbrain/config.json` and the real runtime gateway path resolves it fine. Closes #2728.

## The fix

- `configureFromEnv()`: when `loadConfig()` returns a config, call `configureGateway(buildGatewayConfig(config))` instead of hand-assembling the gateway config field-by-field. Falls back to a bare `configureGateway({ env: { ...process.env } })` when there is no file-plane config yet (pre-`gbrain init`), so the command keeps working before init.
- `runList()`: pass `buildGatewayConfig(cfg).env` into `formatRecipeTable(recipes, env)` — an existing optional parameter already used by `init-provider-picker.ts` (no new API). Keeps the `list` table's `env_ready` column honest with what `providers test` (and the real gateway) would actually see.

## Note on the alternate shape in #2728

The issue's proposed fix suggests `buildGatewayConfig(loadConfig() ?? { engine: 'pglite' })` so the pre-init path still runs through `buildGatewayConfig`. This patch instead falls back to a bare env-only `configureGateway()` call pre-init, which is simpler but skips base-URL threading in the pre-init case. Open question for review: is the pre-init base-URL case worth the synthetic `{ engine: 'pglite' }` config object, or is bare env-passthrough fine there since `gbrain providers` pre-init is mostly used to check *whether* to run init in the first place?

Out of scope (per #2728's own comment thread): `providers test --model` base-URL-override behavior, and adding config.json slots for google/voyage keys.

## Tests

Existing `test/providers.test.ts` behavior for the `process.env`-only case is preserved — this only adds visibility for the previously-invisible file-plane case. Happy to add a case asserting `providers list` reflects a `config.json`-only key if maintainers want it in this PR. `bun test test/providers.test.ts` passes (10/10), as does `test/init-provider-picker.test.ts` (7/7, shares `formatRecipeTable`), and `bun run typecheck` is clean.

title: feat(ai): add Mistral provider recipe
body:
Adds a Mistral recipe so a brain can run embedding, expansion and chat on a single EU-hosted provider. Mistral exposes an OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.mistral.ai/v1`, so this is a recipe plus registration, no new adapter.

The motivation is jurisdictional rather than performance: a brain that has to stay inside the EU currently has no single provider covering all three touchpoints, and mixing providers per touchpoint means a US hop for at least one of them.

Same shape as the Moonshot recipe (#2378), including the `supports_subagent_loop: false` call: ordinary tool calls work, but the subagent loop stays Anthropic-pinned for stable `tool_use_id` behavior across crashes and replays.

## Measured against the live API, not taken from docs

Every non-obvious field was verified on 2026-07-19:

| Field | Value | How it was established |
|---|---|---|
| `mistral-embed` native dimension | 1024 | live embed call, vector length counted |
| `dimensions` parameter | rejected | HTTP 400 `extra_forbidden` |
| `output_dimension` parameter | rejected | HTTP 400 "does not support output_dimension" |
| `max_batch_tokens` | 65536 | 65,286 tokens accepted, 66,960 returns 400 code 3210 |
| price | $0.10 per 1M | mistral.ai/pricing/api |

Two of these are load-bearing.

**No dimension parameter may be emitted.** Both spellings 400. The generic `openai-compatible` branch of `dimsProviderOptions()` already falls through to `return undefined` for these model ids, so the current behavior is correct by default. The risk is a future change adding `mistral-embed` to one of the flexible-dim allowlists in `dims.ts`, which would then 400 on every embed call. That is the same contract `voyage-4-nano` has, and the test pins it the same way, with a negative assertion.

**`chars_per_token` is set to 2, not left at the default.** The value is a divisor in `splitByTokenBudget()` (`estTokens = text.length / charsPerToken`), so a lower number is the conservative direction and a higher one is optimistic. The module default of 4 encodes an English-prose assumption. A German-language corpus measured 3.58 chars/token, so the default underestimates real token count by roughly 12 percent, in the overflow direction. With `safety_factor: 0.5` the pre-split budget lands at 32,768 estimated tokens, which even at a worst-case density near 1.5 chars/token stays clear of the 64K ceiling.

`codestral-embed` and `codestral-embed-2505` are deliberately not listed. They return 1536 dims, and a touchpoint carries a single `default_dims`, so listing them under a 1024 declaration is exactly the mixed-dim case `embedding-dim-check.ts` exists to catch. They are code-retrieval models anyway.

## One thing worth flagging, not a claim on this PR

While verifying dimensions I noticed `takes.embedding` is hardcoded `VECTOR(1536)` in `migrate.ts` (two sites, around lines 1211 and 1273), whereas `content_chunks.embedding` takes its dimension from the configured `embeddingDim`. On a 1024-dim brain the two therefore disagree. It is inert unless takes are enabled, and I have not exercised that path, so I am flagging it rather than touching it. Happy to open a separate issue if useful.

## Testing

`test/ai/recipe-mistral.test.ts`, 8 tests, modeled on `test/ai/recipe-moonshot.test.ts`. Covers registration shape, the pinned embedding constants, the negative dimension assertion, price resolution (an unknown price makes the embedding spend cap fail closed), touchpoint acceptance, the deliberate codestral absence, and both auth paths.

Verified locally on this branch:

- `bun test test/ai/recipe-mistral.test.ts` : 8 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test test/ai/ test/parity.test.ts` : 385 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck` : clean
- `scripts/check-privacy.sh` : clean

I could not get `bun run verify` to report meaningfully in my environment: every individual check prints OK but each subprocess ends with rc=143, and an unmodified `master` checkout produces the identical `pass=0 fail=31`, so it looks like the backgrounded jobs in `run-verify-parallel.sh` are being signalled by my sandbox rather than anything in this diff. I ran the checks individually instead. Worth a second look in CI.

No `VERSION`, `package.json` or `CHANGELOG.md` changes, following the external-contribution pattern in #2378, #2857 and #2836, so the version bump stays with the release ship.

title: v0.42.63.0 fix(autopilot): keep Postgres brains operational checkoutless
body:
## Problem  Long-running Postgres brains could inherit a checkout path written by another host, making a valid VPS install look dependent on that machine. One-shot capture enrichment also left historical `facts:absorb` failures without a bounded recovery path, doctor counted already-recovered history, and 30-minute cycle deaths did not identify the phase that consumed the budget.  ## What this fixes  1. **Checkoutless Postgres autopilot** — ignores a missing database-configured checkout as stale host-local metadata, keeps explicit missing `--repo` fail-closed, preserves PGLite's checkout requirement, and fans out database-only sources with `repoPath: null`. 2. **Durable fact enrichment** — includes the durable Minion capture path already landed upstream and hardens conversation extraction with intra-page checkpoints, an in-flight deadline, and stale terminal-row cleanup. 3. **Bounded backlog recovery** — adds one global, default-on `realtime_absorb_recovery` phase with page, cost, and wall-clock caps; it records recovery only after confirmed success. 4. **Truthful health** — doctor counts only unresolved source refs, so later recovery removes historical failures from the unhealthy total. 5. **Phase-aware timeouts** — serializes persisted cycle progress and includes the last `cycle.<phase>` in timeout/dead-letter errors.  ## Outcome  A Postgres/Supabase worker can run entirely on its current host without a checkout when its sources are database-only. Interrupted enrichment is resumable and drainable without unbounded spend, recovered history stops producing false alarms, and a future 30-minute death points to the phase that stalled.  ## Safety and validation  - Explicit checkout paths still fail closed. - Recovery is single-flight/global under autopilot fan-out and bounded by config. - Appended conversation tails remove the prior completion marker before retry. - `bun run typecheck` passed. - 380/381 broad focused tests passed on the first combined run; the sole failure was an existing Unix-only PID-1 fixture, made cross-platform and then verified green. - 221 audit-focused tests passed, including new concurrency, deadline, terminal cleanup, and ordered-progress regressions. - Staged public privacy scan passed. - The repository's all-in-one Bash verify wrapper is not executable cleanly from this Windows checkout; direct TypeScript and focused Bun suites were used. One unrelated existing Bun E2E dynamic-import case reports a false missing named export even though the export exists and typecheck passes.  ## Deployment  PR only. Nothing is merged or deployed. 

## Coordinated operator PR

The exact candidate is pinned and operationally gated by danwiggins/org-brain#89. Both remain review-only; neither has been deployed.

title: fix(cli): keep doctor --json stdout clean — v123 migration handler printed to stdout
body:
## Root cause

Nightly Heavy Tests run [29731426470](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/actions/runs/29731426470) failed in the `fm_wallclock` step: `gbrain doctor --json` exited 0 but jq died with `Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 7`.

The polluter is the **v123 configurable-FTS migration handler** added by #2941 (`src/core/migrate.ts`), which printed its completion notice via `console.log`:

```
  v123: trigger functions recreated with language='english' (default — no backfill needed)
```

That line reproduces jq's error byte-for-byte (2 spaces + `v123` = 6 chars, the `:` at column 7). Migrations run lazily inside **any** command's first DB connect — the heavy workflow sets `DATABASE_URL` to a fresh Postgres service DB, `doctor` is the first command to touch it, so the migration ran mid-`doctor --json` and its notice became line 1 of stdout. `runMigrations` already documents the contract ("Progress messages route to stderr so callers parsing stdout … aren't polluted"); the new handler violated it.

## Fix

- `src/core/migrate.ts`: route the two v123 prints (and the pre-existing v2 slug-rename print, same class) to `process.stderr.write`, matching every other migration progress message.
- Swept all other stdout prints added by Friday's merges (#2918/#2937/#2939/#2941/#2942 diffs): the rest are command-level data/human output on non-shared paths — the migration handler was the only shared-path polluter.

## Harness repair (discovered during triage)

The fm_wallclock register-source step was silently vacuous: `bun run -e` makes bun dump its usage/script listing with **exit 0** instead of running the snippet, and `connect({})` is in-memory — so the source was never registered and doctor scanned zero files. The step now resolves the engine exactly like the CLI (`loadConfig` + `toEngineConfig` + `createEngine`), so the source lands in the DB doctor actually reads (Postgres in CI, the PGLite brain locally) and the 60K-file wall-clock assertion is real again.

## Test evidence

- Repro: brain at schema v122 + `doctor --json` → stdout line 1 was the v123 notice, jq failed with the exact CI error. Post-fix: stdout is pure JSON (`jq -r '.status'` → `warnings`), notice on stderr.
- New regression test `test/migrate-stdout-clean.test.ts`: re-runs migrations from v122 asserting zero stdout writes + a guard that `migrate.ts` contains no `console.log`. **Fails on unfixed master (2 fail), passes post-fix (2 pass).**
- Harness: `bash scripts/run-heavy.sh 'frontmatter_scan_wallclock.sh'` → `PASS (doctor=2194ms < 15s budget, frontmatter_integrity=ok)` with `1 source(s) clean` (real scan) and the jq parse succeeding.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; adjacent suites (`migrate`, `migration-v120`, `bootstrap`, `timeline-dedup-repair`) 177 pass / 0 fail; `check:test-isolation` OK; `check-progress-to-stdout` OK.

title: fix(code-edges): per-row $n::text::jsonb binds in addCodeEdges — Bun SQL mis-encodes jsonb[] arrays (takeover of #2968)
body:
## Summary

Takeover of #2968 by @zsimovanforgeops (credited via Co-authored-by) — the fix is correct as submitted; this branch ports it onto current master and adds the regression test the fix was missing.

**The bug:** on the Postgres engine, `addCodeEdges` bound `edge_metadata` through `${metas}::jsonb[]` array binds. Bun SQL mis-encodes jsonb array binds — each element arrives double-encoded (`jsonb_typeof = 'string'`, never `object`). The symbol resolver's `edge_metadata || jsonb_build_object(...)` UPDATE then concatenates onto a string scalar and produces a jsonb *array*, so `resolved_chunk_id` is never readable: the resolver logs `edges_resolved > 0` while `code_callers` / `code_callees` / `code_blast` return nothing on Postgres-engine brains. PGLite is unaffected (its `addCodeEdges` already used per-row placeholders) — which is exactly why this class needs a Postgres-gated test.

**The fix (unchanged from #2968):** rewrite both inserts (`code_edges_chunk`, `code_edges_symbol`) to per-row `$n::text::jsonb` placeholders via `sql.unsafe` — the same shape `executeRawJsonb` and the PGLite engine use, per the repo's JSONB iron rule (`docs/ENGINES.md`).

**Added on top of the original PR:** `test/e2e/code-edges-jsonb-postgres.test.ts`, DATABASE_URL-gated per the engine-parity convention:
- resolved insert → `jsonb_typeof(edge_metadata) = 'object'` + field round-trip
- unresolved inserts (explicit metadata and defaulted `{}`) → `object`
- resolver-style `|| jsonb_build_object(...)` UPDATE keeps object shape and `resolved_chunk_id` reads back

## Test evidence

Against real Postgres (pgvector/pgvector:pg16 via docker-compose.test.yml):

- Regression test vs **pre-fix** engine code: `0 pass / 3 fail` (bug reproduces)
- Regression test + `test/code-edges.test.ts` + `test/edge-extractor.test.ts` with fix: `23 pass / 0 fail`
- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- `scripts/check-jsonb-pattern.sh` + `scripts/check-jsonb-params.mjs` — clean

## Credit

All fix logic by @zsimovanforgeops in #2968, including the affected-brain diagnosis (`SELECT jsonb_typeof(edge_metadata), count(*) FROM code_edges_symbol GROUP BY 1`) and the one-time repair UPDATE for corrupted rows documented there.

**The bug (from #2997):** `extract-takes-from-pages.ts` hardcoded `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5`. - gateway-configured `chat_model` is used when `opts.model` is unset

title: fix(test): reset AI gateway after adaptive-embed-batch suite (unbreaks master shard 6)
body:
## Summary
Master's push CI for #3022 failed twice in shard 6: `synthesize_concepts progress wiring (T4)` attempted a **live Google embedding call** and got `API key not valid`.

Root cause: `test/ai/adaptive-embed-batch.test.ts`'s last test configures the gateway (`configureGoogle()`) with a fake key, and its `afterEach` only clears the mock transport — there is no `afterAll`. The configured-but-stale global gateway survives the file boundary, and the legacy-embedding preload deliberately re-applies defaults only when the slot is EMPTY, so the first downstream file that triggers an embed makes a real HTTP call. #3022 is innocent — adding its new test file merely reshuffled shard composition so the pre-existing leak finally landed upstream of an embed-triggering test.

Fix: `afterAll(() => resetGateway())` at the leaker, with a comment explaining the failure mode.
